title: Broken SLS 1508 fiber optic connection
body_text: Broken SLS 1508 fiber optic connection In this example, the fiber optic cable from the Secondary SISNet Repeater on CTLR3 to the SISNet Repeater on CTLR4 has been disconnected or broken. All SISNet Repeaters on the secondary ring have an integrity error of SISNet Broken. In addition, the secondary SISNet Repeater on CTLR4 shows the red X, as it is not receiving any communications. This is indicated by the Pred_Sa value of 00-00-00-00-00-00, indicating that this repeater has no predecessor (the receiver connection is not connected or the cable is disconnected or broken between the preceding repeater on the ring and this repeater).

title: DeltaV OPC History Server browser
body_text: DeltaV OPC History Server browser The DeltaV OPC History Server has a browser that exposes all parameters stored in the DeltaV Continuous Historian. The browser supports the use of "wild cards" for string filters to assist in finding the stored parameters. A single character may be filtered using the question mark character (?). For example, requesting TIC-100?/PID1/PV.CV will return TIC-1000/PID1/PV.CV, TIC-1001/PID1/PV.CV, etc. Multiple characters may be filtered by the asterisk character (*). For example, requesting TIC-1001/PID1/*.CV will return TIC-1001/PID1/OUT.CV, TIC-1001/PID1/PV.CV, and TIC-1001/PID1/SP.CV. In addition, the logical operators equal to (=) and not equal to (!=) may be used with the wild card filters to further refine the parameter search.

title: Browsing
body_text: Browsing In Recipe Studio, you can perform a structured search for different objects. This is referred to as browsing. The objects you can browse for include; procedures, unit procedures, operations, units, parameters, resources and phase classes. Browse Dialog All Browse dialogs appear the same, but each one only allows browsing for those types of objects (recipe level, units, unit parameters, etc.) that are relevant to what you are doing. For example, if you are writing an expression for a transition in a recipe and click the Insert Parameter button, you can only browse for objects that can be used in an expression. When creating a new step in an operation, the Browse dialog lets you select only phase classes. To browse, select the correct Object Type: from the list. Set the Look in: field to the correct location based on the list available. Select the name of the object needed.

title: Connect the BS-420 to the DeltaV system
main_heading: Connect the BS-420 to the DeltaV system
body_text: Connect the BS-420 to the DeltaV system The LSNG connects to both the BS-420 panel and the Local Safety Network from ports on the Dual Universal Safety Carrier that houses the LSNG. The carrier must be connected to the panel's two devices using separate network segments. There should be no common switches or routers between them. While these are not redundant connections, they are dual simplex and must be independent. Important: The network routing is critical to achieve the SIL2 rating. The figure shows the Dual Universal Carrier with Ethernet Isolation Ports installed. The upper ports, labeled Modbus Port 1 and Modbus Port 2 , connect to the panel. The two lower ports, labeled Primary LSN Port and Secondary LSN Port , are the Local Safety Network connections. Dual Universal Safety Carrier port connections for LSNG Connect the BS-420 Ethernet 2 (J2) connection on the panel to Modbus Port 1 on the carrier and connect the BC-420 Ethernet 2 (J2) connection to Modbus Port 2. Verify that the BS-420 Ethernet 1 (J1) is connected directly to the BC-420 Ethernet 1 (J1). Note that these connections must match the configuration in the AS Configuration Tool.

title: The Autronica BS-420 in a DeltaV system
main_heading: The Autronica BS-420 in a DeltaV system
body_text: The Autronica BS-420 in a DeltaV system This section describes how to use signal information from the Autronica BS-420 (and BC-420) with the Local Safety Network Gateway (LSNG) in DeltaV configurations, including fire and gas alarm detection and control of the BS-420 and connected detection devices. The use includes an example configuration that processes the BS-420 signals into DeltaV parameters for use in configuration logic. Note: The LSNG and DeltaV software support detection devices only. This section assumes the following: You have performed the basic configuration of the LSNG in DeltaV Explorer. The BS-420 is configured and connected to the LSNG Modbus ports. Subtopics: Connect the BS-420 to the DeltaV system Configure the BS-420 Configure BS-420 devices in DeltaV Explorer Export the BS-420 configuration Import the BS-420 configuration into DeltaV Explorer Example DeltaV configuration using data from the BS-420

title: Example DeltaV configuration using data from the BS-420
main_heading:
Example DeltaV configuration using data from the 
	 BS-420
body_text: Example DeltaV configuration using data from the BS-420 This section outlines a simple configuration example to show how to create a module to provide limited control of the Autronica panel in a DeltaV configuration. The example processes information from the BS-420 and sends commands to it. The following figure shows an SIS Module running in any CSLS on the same Local Safety Network as the LSNG, or in a CSLS on a different LSN that is connected by a Logic Solver Network Bridges. Example BS-420 module In the figure: COMMAND and PARAM1 are internal read parameters that are 32-bit unsigned integers with status and they are used together to command the panel. CMD1 is a Non-Boolean Secure Parameter of type 32-bit unsigned integer with status. CMDREADY0 is a Boolean Secure Parameter Reference to the LSNG that is used as a handshake mechanism for writing commands to the device. The command ready logic is active low - a one means that the device is not ready to accept a command while a zero means that the device is ready to accept the next command. The LSCALC1 expression is: IF (('^/COMMAND' != 0) AND ('^/CMDREADY0' = 0)) THEN '^/CMD1' := '^/COMMAND' + (ROL('^/PARAM1' ,16)); ELSE '^/CMD1' := 0; '^/COMMAND' := 0; ENDIF; You can now use the PARAM1 and COMMAND parameters for limited control of the panel and detection units. Controlling the BS-420 panel To command the BS-420 panel, only the COMMAND parameter is required. The following table lists the command values supported BS-420 Panel command values Value Action 0 No Action 1 Silence 2 Reset Controlling Units BS-420 units are controlled by first writing the Modbus Index of the unit (not the Modbus Address) to PARAM1 and then writing the appropriate value to COMMAND. Note that Modbus Indexes can be found in the AS Configuration Tool or in the exported Modbus Index file (.csv). The following table lists the command values supported. BS-420 unit command values Value Action 4 Unit Disable 5 Unit Enable 8 Unit Inhibit Actions 9 Unit Allow Actions

title: Configure BS-420 devices in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading: Configure BS-420 devices in DeltaV Explorer
body_text: Configure BS-420 devices in DeltaV Explorer In DeltaV Explorer, navigate to the Modbus ports of an LSNG. Select Modbus Port 1 and from the context menu, select Device . The Properties dialog for the device on the selected port opens. Configure both the General and Advanced tabs for both devices. On the General tab Configure the following: Name You can accept the default name or enter a name that is unique in the configuration. Description Enter information about the device, if desired. Manufacturer This read-only field contains Autronica. Device Model This read-only field contains BS-420/BC-420. Comparison Partner This read-only field contains the configured name of the device connected to the other Modbus port of this LSNG. On the Advanced tab Configure the following: IP Address IP address for the device Note: This IP address should be the same as that configured in the AS tool. Ports The device's TCP/IP ports that the left and right cards the LSNG redundant pair use. Use the default values. Poll Period This read-only field is set to 1 second. The Modbus poll period does not affect the Secure Parameter Publisher broadcast period on the LSN which is always 50 msec. Timeout This is a required field. If no response is received after this time elapses, the status is set to Bad. The recommended value is 500 msec. System Status Register It is recommended that you enter a value in this field. This field is the Modbus Address of the status register for the device. An address of zero means disabled (status defaults to Good). Watchdog Register This is a required field. The Modbus Address of the device's watchdog register. This register increments every poll period. If it does not, all data from the device is marked bad status. Unit Status Block This is a required field. The block of contiguous Modbus registers within the device that hold the detector data. The AutroSafe register start address must be 30011 or greater. There is a maximum of 382 registers due to the publisher limit of 766 Boolean values. Modbus Registers Start - The first register for the block. Modbus Registers End - The last register in the block. Number of Registers Allocated - This read-only field contains the number of registers the block contains. Device Commands It is recommended that you use these fields. This area maps a 32-bit unsigned Secure Parameter in a CSLS on the LSN that can write Parameter 1 and the command word to the BS-420. Parameter 2 is not supported. Configure logic in DeltaV software to build these parameters. The Cmd and Param 1 fields are summarized below and described in more detail in the Autronica documentation. Modbus Registers Cmd Word - The Modbus address of the register that holds the command word. Modbus Registers Param 1 - The Modbus address of the register that holds Parameter 1. Secure Parameter Reference - Browse to the Secure Parameter that contains the command word and Parameter 1. Command Ready Secure Parameter It is recommended that you use these fields. This parameter is a feedback to the command logic signals that the device is ready to accept another command. Name - The configured name of the secure parameter. Type - This read-only field is Boolean with status, the only type the supported by the device. A value of 0 (zero) indicates that the device is ready for a command and a value of 1 (one) indicates that it is not ready. Note: These are Boolean with status parameters and count against the number of Booleans that are published by the LSNG. If these parameters are configured for both ports then only 766 signals can be published. Now configure the device on Modbus Port 2. Note: Because the two devices are paired, only a few fields on the Modbus Port 2 device are configurable. Many of the fields in the second device (Port 2) must match exactly with the fields in the first device (Port 1) because the LSNG is comparing the data received between them. The Device Command data will be unique because the devices can be commanded separately (if necessary). Note that with interconnected devices, this is not always necessary.

title: Built-in DeltaV groups
body_text: Built-in DeltaV groups DeltaV groups are similar in function to Windows groups. They allow you to define a set of keys to DeltaV locks that can be easily assigned to a number of users. For example, you can define a group that has the keys for several locks, then make your users members of that group rather than assigning several locks to each user. The DeltaV groups created during installation are: Maintenance OEM Engineering Operate SIS Engineering (supports DeltaV SIS) SIS OEM Engineering (supports DeltaV SIS) SIS Operate (supports DeltaV SIS) SIS Smart Commissioning (supports DeltaV SIS) SIS Supervise (supports DeltaV SIS) Smart Commissioning Supervise Tune Each of these has default keys assigned and can have default users assigned. From the DeltaV User Manager you can see the default members of each group and the default keys assigned to each group. You can create your own groups, if necessary. Related information DeltaV locks

title: Built-in Windows groups
body_text: Built-in Windows groups This topic is concerned only with the default groups created by DeltaV software. It is possible to create additional Windows groups, but this is not necessary and not recommended for use with DeltaV software. When you select File > New > User the New User dialog opens. DeltaV User Manager New User dialog By default, the Operating System (Windows) Account and DeltaV Database Account check boxes are selected. Once a user account exists, you can modify the account type in DeltaV User Manager by double-clicking the account name to access the user account properties. Note: To ensure proper tracking of security events, the software creates a record in the Windows Events Viewer's Application log when a user is added or deleted with the DeltaV User Manager application. You do not assign DeltaV users to Windows groups directly. When you create a user in the DeltaV User Manager the selections you make for each user determine the Windows groups to which the user is assigned. The following tables show how the New User dialog selections put users in Windows groups that standard DeltaV software created during DeltaV software installation. Note: The DeltaV installation creates other groups to support Emerson software that can be purchased and installed separately. New User dialog check box... Adds user to this Windows group in a workgroup environment Adds user to this Windows group in a domain environment These users... The following Windows account sub-type check boxes each assign a user to an additional Windows group Operating System (Windows) Account and DeltaV Database Account DeltaV Domain DeltaV Can log on to Windows and the DeltaV system. Have no access to Windows Desktop. Have no access to DeltaV privileges unless specifically assigned. DeltaV Administrator DeltaV Admins Domain DeltaV Admins Can perform privileged DeltaV operations and have access to the Windows Desktop. They are also added to the local Windows Administrators group on domain member workstations and, therefore, are allowed access to Windows System utilities. DeltaV Batch Historian Administrator DVBHisAdmin Domain DVBHisAdmin Have unrestricted access to DeltaV Batch Historian data. DeltaV Batch Historian User DVBHisUser Domain DVBHisUser Have restricted, read-only access to DeltaV Batch Historian data. DeltaV Event Chronicle Administrator DVECAdmin Domain DVECAdmin Have access to the Event Chronicle Administration tool. Windows Desktop Access DeltaV Access Domain DeltaV Ax S Have access to the Windows Desktop. Windows Administrator Administrators Domain Admins Are allowed access to Windows System utilities. Allow Remote Desktop Logon Remote Desktop Users Domain DeltaV TSUsers Are allowed to log in remotely. DeltaV Database Account DeltaV Domain Deltav Are given a DeltaV account allowing the user to log on to the DeltaV system. DeltaV privileges are assigned with DeltaV Locks. DeltaV User Roles In addition to the check boxes, the New User dialog has a Role drop-down field that contains two options. The following table lists the options and the Windows group associated with them. Selecting this role… Adds user to this Windows group in a workgroup environment Adds user to this Windows group in a domain environment These users... Basic Configuration DeltaV Basic Configuration Domain DeltaV Basic Configuration Have restricted access to DeltaV applications and their folders. In workgroup settings, access to Windows features is controlled by New Technology File System (NTFS) security settings. In domain systems, access to Windows features for users in this group is controlled by NTFS security settings and further limited by the DeltaV Basic Configuration Group Policy Object (GPO). Basic Operator DeltaV Basic Operator Domain DeltaV Basic Operator Have restricted access to DeltaV applications and their folders. In workgroup settings, access to Windows features is controlled by NTFS security settings. In domain systems, access to Windows features for users in this group is controlled by NTFS security settings and further limited by the DeltaV Basic Operator Group Policy Object (GPO). Note: Be aware that NTFS permissions and Group Policies can disallow privileges granted through DeltaV keys. For example, if a user is granted the Can Configure or Can Download key but is prevented from accessing the DeltaV Explorer because of NTFS permissions associated with that user's role, downloading and configuring privileges are disallowed. Related information DeltaV locks DeltaV security using Organizational Units, Group Policies, and file permissions

title: Bulk editing AS-i discrete I/O
body_text: Bulk editing AS-i discrete I/O AS-i devices must be defined before you can import AS-i discrete I/O configurations. Create a format specification file or use ASI_Disc_IO.fmt and export the discrete I/O objects that were created when you created the devices in DeltaV Explorer. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name, card_slot, and asi_dev_type field values are consistent with the nodes, AS-i cards, and AS-i devices in your database. You must also make sure that the asi_disc_io_name field values are correct for the device you are importing them to.

title: Bulk editing DeviceNet devices
body_text: Bulk editing DeviceNet devices DeviceNet ports must be defined in the database before you can import DeviceNet device configurations. In DeltaV Explorer, create one DeviceNet device of each type you want to bulk edit. (This also creates DeviceNet signals.) Create a format specification file or use DevNet_Device.fmt, then export the devices. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name and card_slot field values are consistent with the nodes and DeviceNet cards in your database.

title: DeltaV Legacy Bulk Power Supplies
body_text: DeltaV Legacy Bulk Power Supplies Bulk power supplies supply power to the system or to field devices. Power to the system is isolated from power to field devices. The following figure shows one method of providing system power and bussed field power with Legacy Bulk Power Supplies. System Power and Bussed Field Power Example with Legacy Bulk Power Supplies You can use DeltaV Legacy Bulk Power Supplies, DeltaV Bulk Power Supplies, or third-party bulk power supplies. There are three types of DeltaV Legacy Bulk Power Supplies: Legacy Bulk AC to 24 VDC Power Supply (Panel and DIN-rail mounted) – Accepts 120/230 VAC power and supplies 24 VDC power to field devices and System Power Supplies (Dual DC/DC). Legacy Bulk AC to 12 VDC Power Supply (Panel and DIN-rail mounted) – Accepts 120/230 VAC power and supplies 12 VDC power to System Power Supplies (DC/DC) and System Power Supplies (Dual DC/DC). Legacy Bulk 24 VDC to 12 VDC Power Supply – Accepts 24 VDC power and supplies 12 VDC power to System Power Supplies (DC/DC). This power supply is no longer available from Emerson Process Management. Note: Refer to the DeltaV™ S-series and CHARMs Hardware Reference manual for information on the DeltaV Bulk Power supplies. Subtopics: Legacy DIN Rail-Mounted Bulk AC to 24 VDC and Bulk AC to 12 VDC Power Supplies Legacy Panel-Mounted Bulk AC to 24 VDC and Bulk AC to 12 VDC Legacy Bulk 24 VDC to 12 VDC Related information System Power Guidelines

title: The bulk edit add in
body_text: The bulk edit add in User-defined exports and imports transfer configuration data to and from text files. DeltaV provides a Bulk Edit Excel add-in you can use to edit the configuration in a spreadsheet. With bulk editing you can easily create or modify large amounts of configuration data, such as I/O channels. Note: The Bulk Edit add-in requires Excel 2013 software and Visual Basic for Applications. The remainder of this section explains how to install the software and provides an overview of using bulk edit. Subtopics: Add Visual Basic for applications Install the Bulk Edit Excel Add-in Bulk editing with the add-in Bulk editing expressions

title: Bulk editing alarms
body_text: Bulk editing alarms The Module_Alarm.fmt provides a way to capture all alarms from a control module using a single format specification file template, independent of the module itself. This explanation is based on the assumption that your configuration exists and that all you need to do is create or modify alarm help information for existing alarm containers. The general procedure to bulk edit alarms is: Export the alarms using the Module_Alarm format specification file. Open the file in MS Excel. Edit the file as required. Import the edited file. Subtopics: Alarms syntax table

title: Bulk editing alarm help
body_text: Bulk editing alarm help This section outlines how to bulk edit DeltaV alarm help. Most items in a DeltaV system that have alarms support alarm help. This explanation is based on the assumption that your configuration exists and that all you need to do is create or modify alarm help information for existing alarm containers. The general procedure to bulk edit alarm help is: Export the alarm containers using an appropriate format file. Open the file in MS Excel. Edit the file as required. Import the edited file. Subtopics: Supported alarm containers and format files Using DeltaV format specification files Create alarm help format specification files Alarm help bulk edit considerations

title: Bulk editing aliases
body_text: Bulk editing aliases The general procedure to bulk edit aliases is: Configure one or more aliases. Use the sample format specification file or create your own and export data from the existing configuration. Edit the aliases in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the edited aliases. Note: You cannot create new aliases with the bulk edit add-in. You can only edit existing aliases.

title: Bulk editing aliases and formulas
body_text: Bulk editing aliases and formulas Use the same techniques and tools to bulk edit batch object that you used for other DeltaV configuration objects. There are a few differences and a couple of objects that are unique to batch configurations, but generally, bulk editing batch objects is no different. Batch hierarchies can be as complex as module hierarchies. Use the complex module bulk edit procedures to bulk edit complex batch hierarchies. Both the process cell and unit module objects must be based on classes in batch configuration to be able to use the Batch Executive. You must correctly specify the proc_cell_class field values when editing process cell data and correctly specify unit_mod_class when editing unit module data. Subtopics: Bulk editing aliases Bulk editing formulas Alias and formula syntax tables Related information Bulk editing complex module hierarchies

title: Using DeltaV format specification files
body_text: Using DeltaV format specification files In most cases using the format specification files provided with the DeltaV software is straightforward. The files generally contain the minimum number of fields necessary to bulk edit alarm help-related information. The Module_AlmHlp.fmt file supports all alarms that appear in non-SIS modules created from DeltaV library module templates. Each of the alarms has several fields associated with it. The format file has more than 100 fields. In export files, a large number of these fields contain <NULL> because the fields do not apply to a module. The SIS_Module_AlmHlp.fmt file supports the alarms that appear in the SIS_DEFAULT DeltaV library module template. If your configuration contains a small subset of modules based on library module templates, you may want to create one or more of your own format specification files. If your configuration contains modules that are not based on library module templates, you must create format specification files for alarm help as explained in the following section.

title: Bulk editing AS-Interface ports, devices, and discrete I/O
main_heading: Bulk editing AS-Interface ports, devices, and discrete I/O
body_text: Bulk editing AS-Interface ports, devices, and discrete I/O This section outlines how to bulk edit AS-interface ports, devices, and discrete I/O. The general procedure to bulk edit AS-Interface objects is: Create an AS-i card. Configure the card's ports. Under one of the ports, create and configure an AS-i device of the type you want to bulk edit. Configure the AS-i discrete I/O that appears under the device. For each level ( AS-i port, device, and discrete I/O) use the sample format specification files or create your own and export data from the existing configuration. Edit the ports in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Edit the devices in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Edit the discrete I/O in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the ports. Import the devices. Import the discrete I/O. Subtopics: Bulk editing AS-i ports Bulk editing AS-i devices Bulk editing AS-i discrete I/O AS-i syntax tables

title: Bulk editing AS-i devices
body_text: Bulk editing AS-i devices AS-i ports must be defined in the database before you can import AS-i device configurations. In DeltaV Explorer, create one AS-i device of each type you want to bulk edit. (This also creates AS-i discrete I/O.) Create a format specification file or use ASI_Dev.fmt, then export the devices. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name and card_slot field values are consistent with the nodes and AS-i cards in your database.

title: Bulk editing AS-i ports
body_text: Bulk editing AS-i ports Nodes and cards must be defined in the database before you can import AS-i port configurations. Create and configure a port in DeltaV Explorer. Create a format specification file or use ASI_Port.fmt then export the port. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name and card_slot field values are consistent with the nodes and AS-i cards in your database.

title: Bulk editing batch equipment trains
body_text: Bulk editing batch equipment trains Batch Equipment Trains represent the collection of units, equipment, and modules used in a batch process recipe. Several of the items (unit_alias, unit_class, batch_equipment_train_class, and selectable_units) must already exist for an import to succeed. Subtopics: Batch equipment train syntax table Related information Format Specification files

title: Bulk editing CHARM I/O cards and CHARMs
main_heading: Bulk editing CHARM I/O cards and CHARMs
body_text: Bulk editing CHARM I/O cards and CHARMs This section outlines how to bulk edit DeltaV CHARM-related configuration objects. One general procedure to bulk edit CHARM objects (both CHARM I/O cards and CHARMs combined) is: Create a CHARM I/O card (CIOC). Configure at least one of each type of CHARM you want to bulk edit. Use the charmIO.fmt format specification file to export the CIOC or create your own format specification file. The export file contains one line for each of the 96 CHARM slots in the CIOC. Edit the file in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the file. You can also bulk edit CHARM I/O cards and CHARMs separately, using the cioc.fmt and charms.fmt format files respectively (or create your own format files). Subtopics: Combined CIOC and CHARMs syntax table CIOC syntax table CHARMs syntax table Non-SIS CHARM HART device syntax table List of CHARM classes and types

title: Bulk editing class-based modules containing class-based modules
main_heading: Bulk editing class-based modules containing class-based modules
body_text: Bulk editing class-based modules containing class-based modules This example builds on the information contained in Bulk Editing Class-based Modules. Read that topic before beginning this example. This example is based on the Equipment Module Classes example in the Batch Tutorial. Because this section is about bulk editing, the example does not go into all the detail the Batch Tutorial contains. The example steps through the tasks required to create a class-based equipment module that contains two class-based control modules, then uses Bulk Edit to create copies of the class-based module. Most of the information in this section applies to other combinations of containership, class-based and classless. The methods explained here apply generally to other types of containing and contained objects. The steps necessary to complete this example are: Create and combine classes for the containing module and contained modules. Create a template from the class and instantiate the template. Create format specification files for the containing module and the contained modules. Export the contained (lower level) modules. Export the containing (top level) module. Create new modules using Bulk Edit. Import the contained modules. Import the containing module. Note: Throughout the example objects are renamed. This is done to improve the clarity of the example. You do not need to rename objects you create Subtopics: Create and combine example module classes Create and instantiate an example template Create format specification files for the example Export the contained and containing modules Editing contained and containing module data Import contained and containing module data Related information Class-based module Creating a command-driven equipment module (TOTALIZER) Bulk editing classless module containing classless module

title: Edit class-based module data
body_text: Edit class-based module data Properties dialogs of parameters that are children of class-based control modules include a Use default value from library object check box. If this box is checked on a parameter of the item you exported, the parameter's value is enclosed in angle brackets in the exported file in the Bulk Edit add-in. Changing a value inside brackets has no effect. On import, the default value from the library object is assigned to the parameter. To change a value, remove the brackets and enter the desired value. When the file is imported the check box is no longer selected and the new value is assigned to the parameter in the imported object. Adding angle brackets to a parameter value selects the check box. To cause the check box to be selected for a parameter with multiple fields, you must enclose all the fields' values in angle brackets before importing the file. Edit the exported file in Excel using the Bulk Edit add-in: Start Excel. Open TEMPS.TXT using the Bulk Edit Open Data File command. The add-in converts the file from Unicode to ASCII and creates the ASCII version of the file TEMPS_ASCII.TXT. Note that the fields in the exported file include only those parameters that can be edited. In Excel, copy the first data row (row 2, TEMP-101) and paste it to an empty row. In the module_name column of the new row, rename the module to TEMP-102. Make other changes desired, including entering I/O references for AI1$IO_IN.REF. Use the Bulk Edit menu to save the file. Close the file.

title: Class-based module
body_text: Class-based module This example shows how to use Bulk Edit to configure copies of a class-based module. This example module consists of an Analog Input function block and a Calculation function block. The module's output is temperature both in degrees Celsius and degrees Fahrenheit. The example starts with creating one class-based module and proceeds through creating a template from the class, then exporting, editing, and importing of data. Note that successful import and export of a class-based module requires that you create a module template that the import/export format file can reference. The module template and the module must have the same SubType (as defined in the module and template Properties dialogs) and this SubType field must be the name of the module template. Following the steps in the example ensures this. The tasks covered in the example are: Create the class. Save the class both as a template and a module. Create a format specification. Export the module. Create new modules using Bulk Edit. Import the new modules. Subtopics: Create the class-based module example Create the example format specification file Export the example module Edit class-based module data Import class-based module data Class-based parameter option shortcuts

title: Class-based parameter option shortcuts
body_text: Class-based parameter option shortcuts Parameter option shortcuts in class-based modules (for parameters such as CONTROL_OPTS) appear in the heading column of the export file with generic option names. For example, PID1$CONTROL_OPTS.OPTION5. To see the descriptive term for the options you can do either of two things: Refer to DeltaV\bin\BitstringTranslations.txt Rename the parameter shortcut. BitstringTranslations.txt DeltaV\bin\BitstringTranslations.txt contains a list of parameter options and the corresponding descriptive strings for the options. For example, the line for CONTROL_OPTS.OPTION5 looks like: CONTROL_OPTS.OPTION5 CONTROL_OPTS.ActOnIR If you encounter generic option names in your export files you can refer to the file to find the parameter and the option to see the descriptive term for the option. Note: The DeltaV software uses BitstringTranslations.txt during configuration and operation. Do not modify BitstringTranslations.txt in any way. Doing so may cause unpredictable results. Renaming Parameter Shortcuts You can make the descriptive terms appear in the export file by renaming the parameter shortcut in the control module class to the actual parameter name before you export a module. For example, to rename PID1$CONTROL_OPTS: Select Advanced Definitions > Control Module Classes > General > module_name . Right-click and select Configure . Select the Parameters tab of the module Configuration dialog. Select PID1$CONTROL_OPTS and click Rename . Rename the parameter shortcut CONTROL_OPTS. When you export the file will contain the descriptive strings in the headings for the CONTROL_OPTS options. If you rename the parameter shortcut to anything other than CONTROL_OPTS, the generic option names appear.

title: Bulk editing classless module containing classless module
main_heading:
Bulk editing classless module containing classless
    module
body_text: Bulk editing classless module containing classless module This example explains how to create and bulk edit classless modules that contain other classless modules. This example is similar to the CASCADE_MASTER and CASCADE_SLAVE module templates which consist of a control module template containing another control module template. The methods explained here apply generally to other types of containing and contained objects. The steps necessary to complete this example are: Create a template and instantiate the template. Create format specification files for the containing and contained modules. Export the contained (lower level) modules. Export the containing (top level) module. Create new modules using Bulk Edit. Import the contained modules. Import the containing module. Subtopics: Creating an example template and instantiating it Create format specification files for the example Export modules Edit the exported data Import the edited data

title: Edit the exported data
body_text: Edit the exported data To create two new modules you must edit both exported files. Editing the containing module is slightly different than editing the contained module so both are detailed below. To bulk edit a contained module: Use the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu to open SLAVE_CAS.TXT. Click OK on the Unicode Detected popup. The file opens. Note that only the fields you specified in the format file appear as columns in the spreadsheet. Copy line 2 of the spreadsheet and paste it back into the spreadsheet into line 3. In the area column, remove /MASTER_CAS from both lines, leaving only AREA_A. In the module_name field, rename the two modules to SLAVE_CAS2 and SLAVE_CAS3. Edit any other parameters you exported as you require. Save the file using the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu. If SLAVE_CAS_ASCII.TXT is not already selected, select it. Click Save . Click Yes to replace the existing copy of the file. Close the spreadsheet but leave Excel and the Bulk Edit Add-in open. To bulk edit a containing module: Use the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu to open MASTER_CAS.TXT. Click OK on the Unicode Detected popup. The file opens. Note that only the fields you specified in the format file appear as columns in the spreadsheet. Copy line 2 of the spreadsheet and paste it back into the spreadsheet into line 3 of the spreadsheet. In the module_name column, rename the two modules to MASTER_CAS_2 and MASTER_CAS_3. In the SLAVE_CAS/MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME column, change the two rows to ~SLAVE_CAS2 and SLAVE_CAS3. The spreadsheet should look like the following figure. This step binds each the MASTER_CAS modules to specific instances of SLAVE_CAS created when you import the edited files. The tildes (~) at the beginning of each module name cause the bulk edit software to discard extra modules created during import. If you do not use the tildes an extra copy of all the contained modules remain in the hierarchy after import. Edit other parameters if necessary. Save the file using the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu. If MASTER_CAS_ASCII.TXT is not already selected, select it. Click Save . Click Yes to replace the existing copy of the file. Close the spreadsheet and close Excel unless you have more files to bulk edit. Note: You can also use Bulk Edit to move existing containing and contained modules, with some limitations. Related information Moving modules using bulk edit

title: Create format specification files for the example
main_heading: Create format specification files for the example
body_text: Create format specification files for the example To successfully bulk edit modules containing other modules, you must create format files for each individual module. The example requires format files for MASTER_CAS_1 and SLAVE_CAS1. The steps to create format files for a contained module are slightly different than the steps to create a containing module so both are detailed below. To create a format file for a contained module: In DeltaV Explorer, select File > Format Specification > New . In the Filename field, enter SLAVE_CAS to create a format file for the SLAVE_CAS module. Select Include Column Headers . Specify the Object type as Module . Click the Apply Filter button and make sure the appropriate filters are selected for your purpose. Click the Browse button for the Subtype field. In the Object Type field of the Browse dialog, select Module Templates . Browse to and select the module template SLAVE_CAS. In the Select fields dialog, select module parameters you want to bulk edit. You must at least include area , module_name , and module_subtype . Open the Parameter List and include block parameters you want to bulk edit, if any. Select items in the Format specification - Must exist dialog, if desired. Click Finish to save the format specification file and close the dialog. To create a format file for a containing module: In DeltaV Explorer, select File > Format Specification > New . In the Filename field, enter MASTER_CAS to create a format file for the MASTER_CAS module. Select Include Column Headers . Specify the Object type as Module . Click the Apply Filter button and make sure the appropriate filters are selected for your purpose. Click the Browse button for the Subtype field. In the Object Type field of the Browse dialog, select Module Templates . Browse to and select the module template MASTER_CAS. In the Select fields dialog, select module parameters you want to bulk edit. You must at least include area , module_name , and module_subtype . Open the Parameter List in the Select fields dialog. Select the SLAVE_CAS/MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME field. Select any block parameters you want to bulk edit. Select items in the Format specification - Must exist dialog, if desired. Click Finish to save the format specification file and close the dialog. Related information Format Specification files

title: Editing object data for each level
main_heading: Editing object data for each level
body_text: Editing object data for each level The following lists the tasks required to create two copies of the example hierarchy. You do not have to perform these tasks in a specific order, but doing them from the top down may help you keep track of the object names you are creating. In the process cell data: Change the values in the proc_cell_name field for the two new process cells to PROC_CELL_1 and PROC_CELL_2. In the unit module data: Edit the area field values to include the process cell names you created -- AREA_A/PROC_CELL_1 and AREA_A/PROC_CELL_2. Change the values for the unit_mod_name field to UNIT_MOD_1 and UNIT_MOD_2. In the equipment module data: Edit the area field values to include the names of the parent process cells and unit modules. Change the module_name field values to EQUIP_MOD_1 and EQUIP_MOD_2. Because the equipment module contains two control modules the data has two binding name fields. Change the CNT_MOD_LVL_1A binding name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_1A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1A2. Change the CNT_MOD_LVL_1B binding name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_1B1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1B2. Prepend the binding name field values with a tilde (~). In the CNT_MOD_LVL_1A data: Edit the area field values to include the names of the parent process cells, unit modules, and equipment modules. Change the module_name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_1A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1A2. Change the CNT_MOD_LVL_2A binding name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_2A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_2A2. Change the CNT_MOD_LVL_2B binding name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_2B1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_2B2. Prepend the binding name field values with a tilde (~). In the CNT_MOD_LVL1B data: Edit the area field values to include the names of the parent process cells, unit modules, and equipment modules. Change the module_name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_1B1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1B2. In the CNT_MOD_LVL_2A data: Edit the area field values to include the names of the parent process cells, unit modules, equipment modules, and control modules. Change the module_name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_2A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_2A2. In the CNT_MOD_LVL_2B data: Edit the area field values to include the names of the parent process cells, unit modules, equipment modules, and control modules. Change the module_name field values to CNT_MOD_LVL_2B1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_2B2.

title: Bulk editing complex module hierarchies
body_text: Bulk editing complex module hierarchies You can bulk edit more complex module hierarchies than those shown in previous sections. For example, a configuration may contain a module hierarchy that looks like: The procedure to bulk edit this hierarchy is: If the modules are not based on a template, create a template for every unique equipment and control module in the hierarchy. Create format specification files for each module based on a unique template. Be sure to specify the correct template as the Subtype for each specification file. Create format specification files for the process cell and unit module. Export items at each level. Edit the exported items as required. Import the edited data in the correct order. The first four steps have been explained in detail elsewhere. The remainder of this topic explains how to perform the last two steps. Subtopics: Editing object data for each level Importing complex module hierarchy data

title: Create the class-based module example
body_text: Create the class-based module example The following steps explain how to create and instance a simple class-based module. In DeltaV Explorer, drag the ANALOG monitoring template in the library to the Example category under Control Module Classes to create a class. Name the class F_C. Open F_C in Control Studio. Set the following parameters on the AI block as indicated: L_TYPE properties: Named state: Direct OUT_SCALE properties: Engineering unit descriptor: °F Add a Calculation function block to the class and connect the output of the AI block to the input of the Calc block. The class should look similar to the following: Select the Calc block, and then select Expressions from the context menu. Enter the following in the Expression Editor: REM Two outputs: degrees F and C 'OUT1.CV' := 'IN1.CV'; 'OUT2.CV' := ( 'IN1.CV' - 32 ) * 5 / 9; Note: It is a good idea to always start an expression with a remark (REM). If the first line of the expression starts with a quote mark, the User-Defined export and import may not interpret the expression correctly. In the module's properties change the SubType to TEMPS_F_C. Note: The SubType must be entered in all capital letters. The user-defined import uses the Subtype to identify the module templates when it creates modules. In DeltaV Explorer, drag the class F_C to a category under Module Templates. Rename the resulting module template to TEMPS_F_C. Create a module by dragging the TEMPS_F_C template to AREA_A. Rename the module to TEMP-101. Related information Module classes

title: Create and combine example module classes
main_heading: Create and combine example module classes
body_text: Create and combine example module classes This class-based example consists of an equipment module class (TOTALIZER) that contains two control module classes (FLO_CTRL, and TTL_FLO). Note that successful import and export of a class-based module requires that you create a module template that the import/export format file can reference. The module template and the class-based module must have the same SubType (as defined in the module template Properties dialogs) and this SubType field must be the name of the module template. The following steps explain how to create the TOTALIZER class by creating its component parts, then combining them. Create the totalizer named set as explained in the Batch Tutorial topic Creating a Command-Driven Equipment Module Class (TOTALIZER). In DeltaV Explorer, navigate to Library/Advanced Definitions/Equipment Module Classes/General . (You can create a new category if you want.) Right-click and select New Equipment Module Class . In the New dialog, name the class TTLZER_CL (for class ), select Command Driven in the Algorithm Type field, and browse to the totalizer named set in the Named Set Name field. Click OK . Navigate to the General category of Control Module Classes. Right-click and select New Control Module Class . In the New dialog name the class FLO_CTRL_CL. Click OK . Open the class in Control Studio and add a PID block to it. Save the class and close Control Studio. Right-click again and create another control module class. In the New dialog, name the class TTL_FLO_CL. Click OK . Open the class in Control Studio and add an INT block to it. Save the class and close Control Studio. For this example you do not need to fully configure the classes, but at least put the blocks in the classes so you can see how to bulk edit parameters of contained blocks. Drag FLO_CTRL_CL and TTL_FLO_CL and drop them onto TTLZER_CL. The Advanced Definitions hierarchy should now look like the following. Rename FLO_CTRL_CL_1 to FLO_CTRL_CNT (for contained module) Rename TTL_FLO_CL_1 to TTL_FLO_CNT. Related information Creating a command-driven equipment module (TOTALIZER)

title: Create the example format specification file
main_heading: Create the example format specification file
body_text: Create the example format specification file From DeltaV Explorer: Select File > Format Specification > New . Enter TEMPS.FMT in the Filename field. Select Include Column Headers . Specify the Object type as Module . In the SubType field, browse to the module template TEMPS_F_C. In the Select fields dialog, select module parameters you want to bulk edit. You must at least include area, module_name, and module_subtype. Also include any parameter shortcuts you want to bulk edit. Parameter shortcuts consist of the contained block name and block parameter name separated by a dollar sign ($). You must at least include AI1$IO_IN.REF so you can specify the input to the AI block when creating modules during bulk edit. You can use parameter option shortcuts when bulk editing parameters with multiple options. Select items in the Which fields must already exist in the database dialog, if desired. Click Finish to save the format specification file and close the dialog. Related information Create a format specification file Class-based parameter option shortcuts

title: Create format specification files for the example
main_heading: Create format specification files for the example
body_text: Create format specification files for the example To successfully bulk edit class-based modules containing other class-based modules, you must create format files for each individual module. The example requires format files for TOTALIZER, FLOW_CONTROL, and TOTAL_FLOW. The steps to create format files for a contained module are slightly different than the steps to create a containing module so both are detailed below. To create a format file for a contained module: In DeltaV Explorer, select File > Format Specification > New . In the Filename field, enter FLOW_CONTROL to create a format file for the FLOW_CONTROL module. Select Include Column Headers . Specify the Object type as Module . Click the Apply Filter button and make sure the appropriate filters are selected for your use. Click the Browse button for the Subtype field. In the Object Type field of the Browse dialog, select Module Templates . Browse to and select the module template FLO_CTRL_TMP. In the Select fields dialog, select module parameters you want to bulk edit. You must at least include area , module_name , and module_subtype . Open the Parameter List and include parameter shortcuts for block parameters you want to bulk edit, if any. Note: Parameter shortcuts consist of the contained block name and block parameter name separated by a dollar sign ($). For example, PID1$GAIN is a shortcut to the GAIN parameter of the PID block that FLOW_CONTROL contains. The column heading for the parameter shortcut in the export file is PID1$GAIN. Parameter shortcuts for parameters that have multiple options use generic terms for the options. Select items in the Format specification - Must exist dialog, if desired. Click Finish to save the format specification file and close the dialog. Repeat steps 1 through 12 for the module TOTAL_FLOW, giving the format file a unique name and browsing to TTL_FLO_TMP for the Subtype field. To create a format file for a containing module: In DeltaV Explorer, select File > Format Specification > New . In the Filename field, enter TOTALIZER.FMT to create a format file for the TOTALIZER equipment module. Select Include Column Headers . Specify the Object type as Module . Click the Apply Filter button and make sure the appropriate filters are selected for your use. Click the Browse button for the Subtype field. In the Object Type field of the Browse dialog, select Module Templates . Browse to and select the module template TTLZER_TMP. In the Select fields dialog, select module parameters you want to bulk edit. You must at least include area , module_name , and module_subtype . Open the Parameter List in the Select fields dialog. Select the MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME field for both FLO_CTRL_CNT and TTL_FLO_CNT. The Selected fields area of the Select fields dialog now looks like the following. If the equipment module contains function blocks, include parameter shortcuts for block parameters you want to bulk edit. Select items in the Format specification - Must exist dialog, if desired. Click Finish to save the format specification file and close the dialog. Related information Class-based parameter option shortcuts Format Specification files

title: Create and instantiate an example template
main_heading: Create and instantiate an example template
body_text: Create and instantiate an example template Follow these steps to create a template from the class, then create an instance of the module from the template. Drag the TTLZER_CL equipment module class to a category under Module Templates. The Module Templates hierarchy should look similar to the following figure. Note that the text in the parentheses next to the contained modules' name is the name of the contained modules in the TTLZER_CL class. To determine the class a module or template is based on, right-click the module or template and select Properties . The Class name field contains the class the module or template is based on. Rename the module template TTLZER_CL_1 to TTLZER_TMP (for template ). Select TTLZER_TMP. Select File > Properties and change the SubType to TTLZER_TMP. Note: The Subtype must be entered in all capital letters. The user-defined import uses the Subtype to identify the module templates when it creates modules. Rename FLO_CTRL_CNT1 to FLO_CTRL_TMP. Set the FLO_CTRL_TMP module SubType to FLO_CTRL_TMP. Rename TTL_FLO_CNT1 to TTL_FLO_TMP. Set the TTL_FLO_TMP module SubType to TTL_FLO_TMP. Create an instance of the template by dragging TTLZER_TMP to AREA_A. The AREA_A hierarchy now includes the instance: Rename the module instances: Rename TTLZER_TMP_1 to TOTALIZER. Rename FLO_CTRL_CNT1 to FLOW_CONTROL. Rename TTL_FLO_CNT1 to TOTAL_FLOW.

title: Bulk editing CHARMs Smart Logic Solver objects
main_heading: Bulk editing CHARMs Smart Logic Solver objects
body_text: Bulk editing CHARMs Smart Logic Solver objects The DeltaV Bulk Edit Excel Template supports editing several CHARMs Smart Logic Solver objects. Subtopics: Bulk edit CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers Bulk edit LS CHARMs Bulk edit CHARMs Smart Logic Solver plus LS CHARMs Bulk edit SIS Controller Modbus Port register mapping Bulk edit Local Safety Network Bridges Bulk edit Local Safety Network Gateways Bulk edit Local Safety Network Gateway signals Related information User-defined export, import, and bulk editing

title: Bulk editing DeviceNet ports, devices, and signals
main_heading: Bulk editing DeviceNet ports, devices, and signals
body_text: Bulk editing DeviceNet ports, devices, and signals This section outlines how to bulk edit DeviceNet ports, devices, and signals. The general procedure to bulk edit DeviceNet objects is: Create a DeviceNet. Configure the card's port. Under one of the ports, create and configure a DeviceNet device of the type you want to bulk edit. Configure the DeviceNet signals that appear under the device. For each level (DeviceNet port, device, and signals) use the sample format specification files or create your own and export data from the existing configuration. Edit the ports in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Edit the devices in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Edit the signals in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the ports. Import the devices. Import the signals. Subtopics: Bulk editing DeviceNet ports Bulk editing DeviceNet devices Bulk editing DeviceNet signals DeviceNet port syntax table DeviceNet device syntax table DeviceNet signals syntax table

title: Bulk editing DeviceNet ports
body_text: Bulk editing DeviceNet ports Nodes and cards must be defined in the database before you can import DeviceNet port configurations. Create and configure a port in DeltaV Explorer. Create a format specification file or use DevNet_Port.fmt then export the port. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name and card_slot field values are consistent with the nodes and DeviceNet cards in your database.

title: Bulk editing DeviceNet signals
body_text: Bulk editing DeviceNet signals DeviceNet devices must be defined in the database before you can import DeviceNet signal configurations. Create a format specification file or use DevNet_Signal.fmt and export the signal objects that were created when you created the devices in DeltaV Explorer. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name and card_slot field values are consistent with the nodes, DeviceNet cards, and DeviceNet devices in your database. You must also make sure that other field values are correct for the device you are importing them to.

title: Bulk editing Ethernet I/O Cards (EIOC)
body_text: Bulk editing Ethernet I/O Cards (EIOC) This section outlines how to bulk edit EIOC nodes, ports, physical and logical devices, and signals. The general procedure to bulk edit EIOC objects is: Create an EIOC card. Configure the card's ports. Under the port create and configure a physical device of the type you want to bulk edit. Under the physical device create and configure a logical device of the type you want to bulk edit. Under the logical device configure the signals. For each level (EIOC, logical device, physical device, signal) use the sample format specification files or create your own and export data from the existing configuration. Note: The EIOC port is bulk edited with the EIOC. In DeltaV Explorer, select the EIOC object that you want to export and select File > Export > User Defined to create a text file for import. Edit the text file for the EIOC object in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the text file for the EIOC object into the DeltaV Explorer. Subtopics: Bulk editing EIOCs Bulk editing EIOC physical devices Bulk editing EIOC logical devices Bulk editing EIOC signals Ethernet I/O Card syntax table Ethernet/IP physical device syntax table Ethernet/IP Class 1 Implicit logical device syntax table Ethernet/IP Class 3 Explicit logical device syntax table Ethernet/IP Class 3 with PCCC logical device syntax table Ethernet/IP UCMM with Logix Tags logical device syntax table Ethernet/IP Class 1 Implicit signal syntax table Ethernet/IP Class 3 Explicit signal syntax table Ethernet/IP Class 3 with PCCC signal syntax table Ethernet/IP UCMM with Logix Tags signal syntax table IEC 61850 physical device syntax table IEC 61850 logical device syntax table IEC 61850 signal syntax table Modbus TCP physical device syntax table Modbus TCP logical device syntax table Modbus TCP signal syntax table Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration physical device syntax table Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration logical device syntax table Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration control tag syntax table Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration signal syntax table OPC UA physical device syntax table OPC UA logical device syntax table OPC UA signal syntax table

title: Bulk editing EIOCs
body_text: Bulk editing EIOCs The EIOC card and port must be defined in the database before you can import EIOC configurations. Configure the EIOC port in DeltaV Explorer. Create a format specification file or use EIOC.fmt and then export the EIOC. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the values are consistent with those in the database.

title: Bulk editing EIOC logical devices
body_text: Bulk editing EIOC logical devices The EIOC card, port, and physical device must be defined in the database before you can import EIOC logical devices. Create a format specification file or use the appropriate EIOC logical device FMT file and export the logical devices that were created when you configured the EIOC physical devices in DeltaV Explorer. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the values are consistent with those in the database. The EIOC logical device FMT files are: Logical_Device_CTA.fmt Logical_Device_EIP_Class1.fmt Logical_Device_EIP_Class3.fmt Logical_Device_EIP_Class3PCCC.fmt Logical_Device_EIP_UCMM.fmt Logical_Device_IEC_61850.fmt Logical_Device_Modbus.fmt Logical_Device_OpcUa.fmt

title: Bulk editing EIOC physical devices
body_text: Bulk editing EIOC physical devices The EIOC card and port must be defined in the database before you can import EIOC physical devices. Create a format specification file or use the appropriate EIOC physical device FMT file and export the physical devices that were created when you configured the EIOC port in DeltaV Explorer. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the values are consistent with those in the database. The EIOC physical device FMT files are: Physical_Device_CTA.fmt Physical_Device_EIP.fmt Physical_Device_IEC_61850.fmt Physical_Device_Modbus.fmt Physical_Device_OpcUa.fmt

title: Bulk editing EIOC signals
body_text: Bulk editing EIOC signals The EIOC card, port, physical devices, and logical devices must be defined in the database before you can import EIOC signals. Create a format specification file or use the appropriate EIOC signal FMT file and export the EIOC signals that were created when you configured the logical devices in DeltaV Explorer. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the values are consistent with those in the database. The EIOC signal FMT files are: Signal_CTA.fmt Signal_EIP_Class1.fmt Signal_EIP_Class3.fmt Signal_EIP_Class3PCCC.fmt Signal_EIP_UCMM.fmt Signal_IEC.fmt Signal_Modbus.fmt Signal_OpcUa.fmt

title: Bulk editing equipment and control modules
main_heading: Bulk editing equipment and control modules
body_text: Bulk editing equipment and control modules This example shows how you can use Bulk Edit to configure copies of a module. The example module is a control module that consists of an Analog Input function block and a Calculation function block. The module provides temperature both in degrees Celsius and degrees Fahrenheit. The information in this section applies to equipment modules as well. The example starts with the creation of the custom module and then outlines the requirements for successfully creating the format specification file and editing the exported data. Note that successful import and export of a module requires the module be template based. The template and the module must have the same SubType (as defined in the module and template Properties dialogs). Following the steps in the example ensures this. Subtopics: Creating the example module Creating the format specification file Creating modules within a container Equipment and control module syntax table

title: Editing contained and containing module data
main_heading: Editing contained and containing module data
body_text: Editing contained and containing module data To create two new modules you must edit all three exported files. Editing the containing module is slightly different than editing the contained module so both are detailed below. To bulk edit a contained module: Use the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu to open FLOW_CONTROL.TXT. Click OK on the Unicode Detected popup. The file opens. Note that only the fields you specified in the format file appear as columns in the spreadsheet. Copy line 2 of the spreadsheet and paste two copies back into the spreadsheet into lines 3 and 4. In the area column, remove /TOTALIZER from all three copies, leaving only AREA_A. In the module_name field, rename the three modules to FLOW_CONTROL-1, -2, and -3 respectively. Edit any other parameters you exported as you require. Use the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu to save FLOW_CONTROL_ASCII.TXT. Click Save . Click Yes to replace the existing copy of the file. Close the spreadsheet but leave Excel and the Bulk Edit Add-in open. Repeat steps 1 through 12 for TOTAL_FLOW.TXT, naming the three modules TOTAL_FLOW-1, -2, and -3. To bulk edit a containing module: Use the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu to open TOTALIZER.TXT. Click OK on the Unicode Detected popup. The file opens. Note that only the fields you specified in the format file appear as columns in the spreadsheet. Copy line 2 of the spreadsheet and paste two copies back into the spreadsheet into lines 3 and 4 of the spreadsheet. In the module_name column, rename the three modules to TOTALIZER-1, -2, and -3. In the FLO_CTRL_CNT/MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME column, change the three rows to ~FLOW_CONTROL-1, -2, and -3. In the TTL_FLO_CNTB/MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME column, change the three rows to ~TOTAL_FLOW-1, -2, and -3. The spreadsheet should look like the following figure. Steps 6 and 7 bind each of the TOTALIZER modules to specific instances of FLOW_CONTROL and TOTAL_FLOW created when you import the edited files. The tildes (~) at the beginning of each module name cause the bulk edit software to discard extra modules created during import. If you do not use the tildes an extra copy of all the contained modules remain in the hierarchy after import. Edit other parameters if necessary. Save TOTALIZER_ASCII.TXT from the DeltaV Bulk Edit menu. Click Save . Click Yes to replace the existing copy of the file. Close the spreadsheet and close Excel unless you have more files to bulk edit. Note: You can also use Bulk Edit to move existing containing and contained modules, with some limitations. Related information Moving modules using bulk edit

title: Export the example module
body_text: Export the example module Note that you can export only an instance of the class-based module. You cannot export the class definition or the module template. Export the module TEMP-101 to a .txt file: From DeltaV Explorer, select the TEMP-101 module in AREA_A. Select File > Export > User Defined . Select the TEMPS.FMT format specification file. Specify the target data file as TEMPS.TXT. Export the data.

title: Export modules
body_text: Export modules You must export each module in the hierarchy individually. To export the modules: From DeltaV Explorer, select the SLAVE_CAS1 module under MASTER_CAS_1. Select File > Export > User Defined . Click Next . Click Next to acknowledge that you are exporting children of SLAVE_CAS1. Select the check box by SLAVE_CAS1. Click Next . Browse to the SLAVE_CAS.FMT format specification file. Specify the target data file as SLAVE_CAS. Export the data. Repeat steps 1 through 9 for MASTER_CAS. When you export MASTER_CAS select only the MASTER_CAS_1 module in the hierarchy diagram of the User Defined Export dialog. Do not select anything else.

title: Export the contained and containing modules
main_heading: Export the contained and containing modules
body_text: Export the contained and containing modules You must export each module in the hierarchy individually. To export a class-based module: From DeltaV Explorer, select the FLOW_CONTROL module under TOTALIZER. Select File > Export > User Defined . Click Next . Click Next to acknowledge that you are exporting children of FLOW_CONTROL. Select the check box by FLOW_CONTROL. Click Next . Browse to the FLOW_CONTROL.FMT format specification file. Specify the target data file as FLOW_CONTROL. Export the data. Repeat steps 1 through 9 for TOTAL_FLOW and TOTALIZER. When you export TOTALIZER select only the TOTALIZER module in the hierarchy diagram of the User Defined Export dialog as shown in the following figure.

title: Bulk editing fieldbus devices
body_text: Bulk editing fieldbus devices Fieldbus ports must be defined in the database before you can import fieldbus device configurations. In DeltaV Explorer, create one fieldbus device of each type you want to bulk edit. Create a format specification file or use FF_Device.fmt (or FF_Device with Device Alarms.fmt), then export the devices. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name, card_slot, and card_type field values match the nodes and fieldbus cards in your database.

title: Bulk editing fieldbus ports
body_text: Bulk editing fieldbus ports Nodes and fieldbus cards must be defined in the database before you can import fieldbus port configurations. Create and configure a port in DeltaV Explorer. Create a format specification file or use FF_Port.fmt then export the port. Edit the exported data as required, making sure that the node_name, card_slot, and card_type field values match the nodes and fieldbus cards in your database.

title: Bulk editing fieldbus ports and devices
main_heading: Bulk editing fieldbus ports and devices
body_text: Bulk editing fieldbus ports and devices This section outlines how to bulk edit fieldbus ports and devices. The general procedure to bulk edit fieldbus objects for a single fieldbus card is: Create a fieldbus card. Configure the card's ports. Under one of the ports, create and configure a fieldbus device of the type you want to bulk edit. For each level (fieldbus port and device) use the sample format specification files or create your own and export data from the existing configuration. Use the Format Specification file Must Exist dialog to prevent existing card configurations from being overwritten in the database. Edit the ports in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Edit the devices in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the ports. Import the devices. You can extend this method to configure the ports and devices for multiple fieldbus cards with one bulk edit text file. Subtopics: Bulk editing fieldbus ports Bulk editing fieldbus devices fieldbus port syntax table Fieldbus device syntax table Related information The Must Exist dialog

title: Bulk editing formulas
body_text: Bulk editing formulas The general procedure to bulk edit formulas is: Configure one or more formulas. Create a format specification file (specify the formula as the subtype) and export data from the existing configuration. Edit the formulas in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the newly created formulas.

title: Bulk editing system hardware alarms
body_text: Bulk editing system hardware alarms This section contains information on bulk editing system hardware alarms. Use the Excel Bulk Edit template to edit the exported data. Subtopics: System hardware alarm syntax table Related information Format Specification files

title: Bulk editing HART devices
body_text: Bulk editing HART devices The main uses of Bulk Edit for HART devices are: Creating HART devices on channels from a template or definition using Bulk Edit import Comparing the parameter values of multiple devices by exporting devices having a common template or definition to check for differences This section outlines how to bulk edit HART devices and SIS HART devices. Subtopics: Bulk editing HART devices HART device syntax table

title: Bulk editing HART devices
body_text: Bulk editing HART devices One way to bulk edit HART objects is: Create a HART-capable card. Set one of the card's channels to be a HART channel The device tag changes to a HART device tag. From the HART device tag, open the Properties dialog. Fill in the fields with the information for a HART device. Use the sample format specification file or create your own and export the HART device. Edit the device in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the devices. Note: Even though the condition masks are exported, it is not practical to edit the masks using Bulk Edit because it is not easy to determine how the bits map to conditions. If you need to change condition masks create a new template after configuring the conditions as desired. Controllers and HART enabled cards must be defined in the database before you can import HART device configurations. When you create a format specification file for a HART device you must select a subtype to specify whether you are editing SIS or non-SIS devices.

title: Bulk editing history data points
body_text: Bulk editing history data points This section outlines how to bulk edit history data points (history collection configuration). The general procedure to bulk edit history data points is: Configure history data points of the types you want to bulk edit. Use the sample format specification file or create your own and export data from the existing configuration. Edit the history data points in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the history data points. Note: To bulk edit history data points for all modules in an area, select only the area in the User Defined Export dialog. Do not click the Select All button. If you select the area and click Select All , all history data points are duplicated in the export file. Subtopics: Paths in the value_recorded field History data points in class-based modules History data points syntax table

title: Import class-based module data
body_text: Import class-based module data Import the modules you edited in Excel. From DeltaV Explorer, select File > Import > User Defined Format . Select the TEMPS.FMT format specification file. Select the TEMPS_ASCII.TXT data file. Import the data. The Import dialog indicates the progress and notifies you when the import is complete. From DeltaV Explorer, you can see the module you imported, TEMP-102. You may need to refresh the view in DeltaV Explorer.

title: Import the edited data
body_text: Import the edited data To create the new modules you must import the edited files. Note: You must import the files for the contained modules before you import the file for the containing module. The steps for importing are the same for all modules: From DeltaV Explorer, select File > Import > User Defined . In the Format source dialog, browse to and open SLAVE_CAS.FMT. Click Next . In the Import data sourcef dialog, browse to and open SLAVE_CAS_ASCII.TXT. Click Next . On the Import results dialog, click Import . After a moment the Import complete dialog appears. It has a log of the import actions. If errors are reported scroll through the log or open DeltaV\DVData\ImportExportProgress.log to determine the cause. If the import was successful, click Close . The AREA_A hierarchy now looks like the following figure. Note that the SLAVE_CAS modules were imported to the AREA_A level. Repeat steps 1 through 6, opening MASTER_CAS.FMT and MASTER_CAS_ASCII.TXT. The import does not disturb MASTER_CAS_1 and creates MASTER_CAS_2 and MASTER_CAS_3 and replaces the contained modules created by importing the MASTER_CAS modules with copies of the contained modules you created. The hierarchy under AREA_A now looks similar to the following figure. Note that the MASTER_CAS_ n modules are populated with SLAVE_CAS n modules. Importing MASTER_CAS_ASCII.TXT moved the SLAVE_CAS modules created by importing SLAVE_CAS_ASCII.TXT under the MASTER_CAS modules. The tildes you prepended the MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME values in the MASTER_CAS_ASCII.TXT file caused the import to remove the extra modules created when MASTER_CAS_ASCII.TXT was imported.

title: Importing complex module hierarchy data
body_text: Importing complex module hierarchy data You must import the data in a specific order to successfully create copies of the example hierarchy. Generally, import process cells and unit modules from the top down, import equipment and control modules from the bottom up. After you import each level you may want to refresh DeltaV Explorer to make sure the changes appear. Import the process cell data. PROC_CELL_1 and PROC_CELL_2 appear below AREA_A. Import the unit module data. UNIT_MOD_1 and UNIT_MOD_2 appear under PROC_CELL_1 and PROC_CELL_2 respectively. Import the CNT_MOD_LVL_2A data. CNT_MOD_LVL_2A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL2A2 appear below AREA_A. Import the CNT_MOD_LVL_2B data. CNT_MOD_LVL_2B1 and CNT_MOD_LVL2B2 appear below AREA_A. Import the CNT_MOD_LVL_1A data. CNT_MOD_LVL_1A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1A2 appear below AREA_A. CNT_MOD_LVL_2A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL2B1 move below CNT_MOD_LVL_1A1. CNT_MOD_LVL_2A2 and CNT_MOD_LVL2B2 move below CNT_MOD_LVL_1A2. Import the CNT_LVL_1B data. CNT_MOD_LVL_1B1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1B2 appear below AREA_A. Import the equipment module data. EQUIP_MOD_1 and EQUIP_MOD_2 appear below UNIT_MOD_1 and UNIT_MOD_2 respectively. CNT_MOD_LVL_1A1 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1B1 move under EQUIP_MOD_1. CNT_MOD_LVL_1A2 and CNT_MOD_LVL_1B2 move under EQUIP_MOD_2. If all the imports were successful, the hierarchy under AREA_A should look like the figure.

title: Import contained and containing module data
main_heading: Import contained and containing module data
body_text: Import contained and containing module data To create the new modules you must import the edited files. Note: You must import the files for the contained modules before you import the file for the containing module. The steps for importing are the same for all modules: From DeltaV Explorer, select File > Import > User Defined . In the Format source dialog, browse to and open FLOW_CONTROL.FMT. Click Next . In the Import data source dialog, browse to and open FLOW_CONTROL_ASCII.TXT. Click Next . On the Import results dialog, click Import . After a moment the Import complete dialog appears. It has a log of the import actions. If errors are reported scroll through the log or open DeltaV\DVData\ImportExportProgress.log to determine the cause. If the import was successful, click Close . Repeat steps 1 through 7, opening TOTAL_FLOW.FMT and TOTAL_FLOW_ASCII.TXT. The AREA_A hierarchy now looks like the following figure. Note that the FLOW_CONTROL and TOTAL_FLOW modules were imported to the AREA_A level. Repeat steps 1 through 6, opening TOTALIZER.FMT and TOTALIZER_ASCII.TXT. The import replaces the contained modules created by importing the TOTALIZER modules with copies of the contained modules you created. The hierarchy under AREA_A now looks similar to the following figure. Note that the TOTALIZER- n modules are populated with FLOW_CONTROL- n and TOTAL_FLOW- n modules. Importing TOTALIZER_ASCII.TXT moved the FLOW_CONTROL and TOTAL_FLOW modules under the TOTALIZER modules. The tildes you prepended the MODULE_BLOCK_BINDING.MNAME values in the TOTALIZER_ASCII.TXT file caused the import to remove the extra modules created when TOTALIZER_ASCII.TXT was imported.

title: Bulk editing local cards
body_text: Bulk editing local cards All of the field values for cards are similar. Only a few cards have card-level parameters and these cards have only a few parameters. Unless you want to bulk edit card-level parameters you can use the Card.fmt format specification file included with the DeltaV software to export and import local I/O card data. If you need to bulk edit a large number of cards that have card-level parameters, you can create the format specification files for each of the card types you want to bulk edit. To include card-level parameters in format specification files you must correctly specify the Subtype (browse to the location of the card you want to bulk edit).

title: Bulk editing local channels
body_text: Bulk editing local channels Though the DeltaV software includes some format specification files for channels, it is more likely that you will create your own format specification files so you can define exactly the information you want to bulk edit. Channels have a number of channel-level parameters so if you need to bulk edit these parameters you should create format specification files for each channel type you want to bulk edit.

title: Bulk editing local I/O cards and channels
main_heading: Bulk editing local I/O cards and channels
body_text: Bulk editing local I/O cards and channels This section outlines one way to bulk edit local I/O cards and channels. This section does not explain how to bulk edit remote I/O cards. To successfully import bulk edited cards, the controller to which you are assigning the cards must already be in the database. Similarly, to import bulk edited channels, the cards must already be in the database. The general procedure to bulk edit local I/O cards and channels is: Create one card of a type you want to edit. Configure the card's channels. Use the Card.fmt format specification file to export the card or create your own format specification file. Use one of the channel format specification files or create your own and export a channel of the type you want to bulk edit. Format Specification files can allow existing card configurations to be overwritten in the database. Edit the cards in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Edit the channels in the bulk edit Excel add-in. Import the cards. Import the channels.
