title: Editing rules for the Campaign Manager API
main_heading: Editing rules for the Campaign Manager API
body_text: Editing rules for the Campaign Manager API Campaign States and Edit Rules The possible states for a campaign to be in are as follows: dvbcmCampaignStateDefining dvbcmCampaignStateDefined dvbcmCampaignStateActive dvbcmCampaignStateComplete dvbcmCampaignStateClosed dvbcmCampaignStateTerminated dvbcmCampaignStateUnknown Campaign States and Edit Rules Chart A campaign in the Defining or Defined state can have any of its properties edited as long as it has never been in the Active state. Once the campaign has gone to the Active state, the Recipe Edit object of that campaign can no longer be edited. Any call to the recipe edit object of a campaign that has ever been in the Active state will fail. Once in the Active state, any property that is not part of the recipe edit object can be edited. Batches can be added to a campaign in any state except the Terminated state, as long as the campaign is in manual mode. If a batch is added to a campaign in the Complete state the campaign will automatically be placed into the Active state. Batch States and Edit Rules The possible states for a batch to be in are as follows: dvbcmBatchStateDefined dvbcmBatchStateDefining dvbcmBatchStateReleasing dvbcmBatchStateReleaseFailed dvbcmBatchStateReleased dvbcmBatchStateStarting dvbcmBatchStateActiveAborted dvbcmBatchStateActiveAborting dvbcmBatchStateActiveComplete dvbcmBatchStateActiveHeld dvbcmBatchStateActiveHolding dvbcmBatchStateActiveIdle dvbcmBatchStateActiveReady dvbcmBatchStateActiveRestarting dvbcmBatchStateActiveRunning dvbcmBatchStateActiveStarting dvbcmBatchStateActiveStopped dvbcmBatchStateActiveStopping dvbcmBatchStateCompleteNoError dvbcmBatchStateCompleteNotStarted dvbcmBatchStateCompleteWithError dvbcmBatchStateRemoving dvbcmBatchStateClosed dvbcmBatchStateUnknown dvbcmBatchStateLoadFailed dvbcmBatchStateRecovering dvbcmBatchStateRecoverFailed dvbcmBatchStateLost Campaign Manager Batch States and Edit Rules Note: The ReleaseFailed state is when a batch fails to be released to the Batch Executive. The comment in the status field of the Campaign Manager Operator Interface displays the reason for this failure. A batch that is in the Defining or Defined state can have any of its properties edited. Once the batch has been released to the Batch Executive, it can no longer be edited in any way by the Campaign Manager server. If the batch goes into the ReleasedFailed state it can be put back into the Defining state by the Campaign Manager server and then edited.

title: Editing a module copied from a module template
main_heading: Editing a module copied from a module template
body_text: Editing a module copied from a module template After you create a module from a module template and give the module the name you want, you can customize it using either Control Studio or DeltaV Explorer. If you edit the module in Control Studio, there are comments (configuration tips) on the function block diagram to step you through the procedure. For certain module templates, however, you might prefer to edit the copied module from DeltaV Explorer. Subtopics: Editing the module in Control Studio Editing the module in DeltaV Explorer Related information Module naming conventions

title: Editing the NC_VALVE control module class
main_heading: Editing the NC_VALVE control module class
body_text: Editing the NC_VALVE control module class Use Control Studio to make changes to the NC_VALVE control module class. The changes to be made include adding a Deadtime block, an input parameter for the valve setpoint, and an output parameter for the PV. We will also change the mode properties for the DC1 block to allow Cascade as a permitted mode and to change the normal and target modes to Cascade. (The reason for making these changes to the mode properties is that the phases will write to the CAS setpoint. Later, during testing, you will have to put some of the valves in AUTO mode to change the setpoint.) The Deadtime block will be used to simulate the valve opening and closing. The valve setpoint and PV parameters will be used later when the control module is added to an equipment module. After configuring the logic for the module, we will open the Properties dialog and select Process as the primary control display for this module. Selecting the display at the class level eliminates the need to set the display for all the individual control module instances created from the class. (In a real process system, it may well be that many process graphics are available, but in this tutorial, only one process graphic is used.) Subtopics: Edit the NC_VALVE control module class

title: Editing parameters in module classes and module instances
main_heading: Editing parameters in module classes and module instances
body_text: Editing parameters in module classes and module instances In a module class the parameter Properties dialog (including dialogs for the parameters of contained function blocks) contains a check box labeled Allow instance value to be configured . When this check box is selected you can edit the value of the parameter in any instance of the class. When the check box is selected, the link to instances of the class for that parameter are broken — subsequent changes at the class level do not propagate to the instances unless the Use default value from library check box is selected in the instance. Editing configurable parameters in a module instance has no effect on the module class. At the module class level, the Allow instance value to be configured check box is in one of the following: Selectable (not grayed out) — Select this check box to allow the value of this parameter to be changed in a module instance. In the Instance dialog, the Use default value from library object check box appears and is selectable. The Allow instance value to be configured check box is selected by default for function block parameters with the Common Configuration filter. You can make other parameters editable in the instance by selecting the Allow instance value to be configured check box in the class. Selected and grayed out — The parameter value is configurable in a module instance. The parameters are in this category include: Function block Parameters with the I/O References filter Module VERSION parameter User-defined external reference parameters Not selected and grayed out — The parameter value is not configurable in a module instance. The parameters in this category include: User-defined internal reference parameters Module VERSION_CLASS parameter User-defined dynamic reference parameters are configurable in the class or the instance. Block scan rates are not editable in module instances. There are two ways to configure parameters in module classes and module instances: The Configuration dialog The Parameter Instances dialog

title: Editing the module in Control Studio
main_heading: Editing the module in Control Studio
body_text: Editing the module in Control Studio To launch Control Studio from DeltaV Explorer, select and right-click the copied module, and then select Edit from the context menu. The module appears to be nearly identical to the template from which it was created. Only the name in the title bar is different. Give the module unique parameter values, I/O references, and so on, to differentiate it from other modules. Note: In Control Studio, a module initially looks like the module template from which it was created. When you are customizing a module, be sure that you are editing the module and not the module template. Follow the procedure in the configuration tips. A common step to all module templates is filtering the parameter list to display the Quick Config parameters. These are the parameters that you edit to make the module unique. However, it is not necessary to change every Quick Config parameter, and you might want to change other parameters that are not in the Quick Confg view. The Quick Config parameters are those that are commonly configured when a module is created from a module template. You can add or remove parameters from the Quick Confg view for a given module or module template. Click the Filter button in the parameter list window to set the view in the list. The default view is for Common configuration. Clear the Common configuration check box and select the Quick config check box, as shown in the following figure. Parameter Filtering dialog to set the view for the parameter list The scope for the parameter list can be either Track Selection or All Levels. Use the combo box to set the scope in the parameter list window. Consider the scope suggested in the configuration tips. When Track Selection is needed, select the function block named in the configuration tips to view the appropriate list of parameters. To add or remove a parameter in the Quick Confg view, use the parameter's Edit dialog. Click the Filter button on the parameter's Edit dialog to open the dialog shown below. Note that the System options are not active. Select the Quick config option to add the parameter to the module's Quick Confg viewor clear it to remove the parameter from the Quick Confg view. Parameter Filtering dialog to change a User category for a parameter All of the module templates include one or more module alarm parameters. In some cases, the alarms are not enabled by default. These alarms can be enabled, and other alarms can be disabled. The priority of each alarm has a default value that can be changed as necessary. Another step common to all modules is editing the module properties. The Module Properties dialog, shown below, can be accessed by clicking its toolbar icon or by selecting Properties from the File menu. If the module was created from a DeltaV module template, the text you enter in the Description box appears on the faceplate display and the detail display. Note that the description can be as long as 48 characters, but it is truncated to 24 on the pop-up displays. The execution rate for the module can be changed using the combo box. Enter the name of the primary control display without the file extension. Data links for this module can appear on more than one display. With this primary display name, you can access the module from the alarm banner. If the module was not created from a DeltaV module template or if you want to change the name of a faceplate or detail display, enter the display names without their extensions. Note: If you change the name of the faceplate display for the module, you must create a chart for Process History View to use when launched from this faceplate. The standard faceplate displays already have charts with the same name for Process History View to use. You can copy the existing chart and rename it or create a completely new chart. Refer to the Process History View help for information on creating and editing charts. Module Properties dialog CAUTION: When customizing a module created from a DeltaV module template, do not change any function block usage name. Doing so changes the path to the block's parameters and results in a loss of communication in DeltaV Operate for parameters with data links on the dynamos, faceplates, and detail displays.

title: Editing the module in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading: Editing the module in DeltaV Explorer
body_text: Editing the module in DeltaV Explorer A module that has been created from a module template can also be customized from DeltaV Explorer. After you have customized modules a few times using Control Studio, you might find it quicker to accomplish this from DeltaV Explorer. Although you cannot view the function block diagram or configuration tips from DeltaV Explorer, you do have access to the other views, including the module properties and the Quick Confg view of the parameters. From the left pane of DeltaV Explorer, select and right-click the module, and then select Filtered Parameter List from the context menu. This is the Quick Confg viewfor the module with the scope set at All Levels . While the module is selected, right-click, and then click Properties from the context menu to access the Module Properties dialog. Note: If you change the name of the faceplate display for the module, you must create a chart for Process History View to use when launched from this faceplate. The standard faceplate displays already have charts with the same name for Process History View to use. You can copy the existing chart and rename it or create a completely new chart. Refer to the Process History View help for information on creating and editing charts. The Alarm Properties dialog can be opened from DeltaV Explorer by selecting and right-clicking the alarm parameter in the right pane, and then selecting Properties . Expressions, such as those found in the Condition function block, can also be edited from DeltaV Explorer. Click the Condition function block under the module in the left pane. In the right pane, select and right-click T_EXPRESSION, and then select Properties from the context menu to edit the expression.

title: Edit the campaign's recipe object
body_text: Edit the campaign's recipe object In order to set up a campaign or batch recipe edit object, the user must be presented with recipe information so that selections can be made. For example, if a recipe has multiple steps that require unit binding selections, the user needs to make those selections. All of the recipe information to be presented to the user can be accessed from the DeltaV software using the DVBCMExecRecipeInfo object. This object exposes many properties and methods that return various pieces of information consistent with how the recipe has been configured in Recipe Studio. To retrieve the DVBCMExecRecipeInfo object, first get the list of recipes available. The DVBCMExecInfo object keeps this list. The following code shows an example. Private Sub GetBaseRecipe() Dim objExecOnfo As DVBCMExecInfo Dim objExecRecipeInfo As DVBCMExecRecipeInfo Dim strExecNode As String ' Get the executive node name strExecNode = DVBCMClient.ExecutiveNode 'Set the Executive info object Set objExecInfo = DVBCMClient.ExecutiveInfo(strExecNode) Call UseExecInfo(objExecInfo) End Sub Once an executive recipe object is retrieved, a list of all recipes on the executive can be retrieved for the user to select the new campaign's base recipe and to obtain an executive recipe information object. Private Sub UseExecInfo(objExecInfo) Dim vRecipes() As String Dim strRecipeName As String Dim objExecRecipeInfo As DVBCMExecRecipeInfo ' Get list of recipes vRecipe = objExecInfo.ExecutiveRecipeList ' User Selects base recipe from list of recipes Call UserSelectsRecipe(vRecipes, strRecipeName) ' Retrieve executive recipe object objExecRecipeInfo = objExecInfo.ExecutiveRecipeInfo(strRecipeName) Call UseExecRecipeInfo(objExecRecipeInfo, objExecInfo) End Sub As the recipe is selected, specific information about that recipe such as formulas and bound units, can be retrieved from the DVBCMExecRecipeInfo and DVBCMExecParamInfo objects. As the formula and bound unit information is retrieved from the executive, it can be presented to the user for selection. Private Sub UseExecRecipeInfo(objExecRecipeInfo, objExecInfo) Dim vFormulas() As String Dim vStepNames() As String Dim vUnitClasses() As String Dim vUnitNames() As String Dim vIsClassBased() As Boolean Dim lUnitIDs() As Long Dim vAreaNames() As String Dim lAreaIDs() As Long ' Get a list of each recipe step along with its associated unit class Call objExecRecipeInfo.GetStepsAndBoundUnits(vStepNames, _ vUnitClasses, vIsClassBased) ' Get the bound units for each step Call SetBoundUnits(vStepNAmes, vUnitClasses, vIsClassBased, _ vUnitNames, lUnitIDs, vAreaNames, lAreaIDs, objExecInfo) 'Get a list of formulas for this recipe vFormulas = objExecRecipeInfo.FormulaList Call SetFormulaAndParameters(vFormulas) End Sub A bound unit must be selected for each step of the recipe. A list of units for each unit class can be retrieved from a DVBCMExecInfo object using the GetExecutiveUnitInfo method. The user must be presented with a list of possible units for each step. As the list of unit names is being presented, a list of unit IDs, area names and area IDs is also retrieved and presented for selection. If the recipe is not unit class based and the GetExecutiveUnitInfo method is passed a unit name instead of a unit class name, the method will just return the unit passed in. To determine if a step is associated with an individual unit or a unit class, check the vIsClassBased parameter passed to GetStepsAndBoundUnits above. Each entry in this array will be true if the corresponding step is based off a unit class. Private SetBoundUnits(vStepNames, vUnitClasses, vIsClassBased, vUnitNames, lUnitIDs, vAreaNames, lAreaIDs, objExecInfo) Dim strBoundUnit As String Dim iSteps As Long Dim iCount As Long iSteps = Ubound(vStepNames) for iCount = 1 to iSteps if vIsClassBased(iCount) then Call ObjExecInfo.GetExecutiveUnitInfo(strBoundUnit, _ vUnitNames, 1UnitIDs, vAreaNames, 1AreaIDs) Call PromptUserForBoundUnit(strBoundUnit, vUnitNames) Else strBoundUnit = vUnitClasses(iCount) End if next iCount End Sub Once a list of formulas is retrieved the user can be prompted for a formula name. With the formula name the GetFormulaInfo method can be called from DVBCMExecRecipeInfo object to retrieve the description, version, parameter names and parameter values of the formula. These can all be used to display information to the user about the formula or to allow the user to enter a custom formula with custom parameter values. With a specific parameter name, a DVBCMExecParamInfo object can be retrieved to display information about a parameter such as default value, high scale and low scale, as well as to tell if it can be edited or scaled. If custom parameter values are entered, the user must provide a unique formula name to be added to the server. If no formula is selected for the new campaign, the default values of all the parameters will be used. Note: When calling one custom formula to replace another custom formula, the first custom formula must assign all recipe parameters. Any unassigned recipe parameters will be reset to the default parameter value before the new custom formula is loaded. Private Sub SetFormulaAndParameters(vFormulas) Dim strFormulaName As String Call PromptUserForFormula(vFormulas, strFormulaName) End Sub Once all the recipe information has been selected and maintained in variables, a recipe edit object can be retrieved to set all the properties of the campaign's recipe edit object. The only other property the user needs to enter is the recipe's scale. Private Sub SetCampaignRecipeObject(ByRef objCampaignEdit As _ IDVBCMCampaignEdit4, vStepNames As Variant, vUnitNames As Variant, _ lUnitIDs As Variant, vParameterNames As Variant, vParameterValues As _ Variant, strFormula As String, strExecNode As String) Dim fScale As float Dim objRecipeEdit As DVBCMRecipeEdit ' Prompt user for recipe's scale Call GetScaleFromUSer(fScale) ' Get the campaign's recipe edit object objRecipeEdit = objCampaignEdit.RecipeEdit Call objRecipeEdit.SetScale(fScale) objRecipeEdit.Formula = strFormula Call objRecipeEdit.SetUnitBindings(vStepNames, vUnitNames, _ lUnitIDs) Call objRecipeEdit.SetParameters(vParameterNames, _ vParameterValues) End Sub SetUnitBindings must be sent a valid list of step names along with a list of valid bound units for each step. If either list is incorrect, then when DVBCMCampaignEdit.SetupComplete is called for the campaign, the call will fail due to invalid unit selections for the base recipe of the campaign. The function SetUnitBinding can be used in instead to set one unit at a time but this is mainly used to change bound units after the campaign has been created. For the initial setup of a campaign all unit bindings are usually set. SetParameters must be sent a valid list of parameter names and valid parameter types or, as with the unit bindings, the DVBCMCampaignEdit.SetupComplete call will fail. The function SetParameter can be used to set one parameter at a time but SetParameters is used at the initial setup of the campaign to set all parameters at once.

title: Effects of configuration changes
body_text: Effects of configuration changes The Area Model defines the physical equipment and the batch components to be used by batch recipes. There are several configuration changes that alter the Area Model (see below). When an Area Model change is made, the Batch Executive does not have to be stopped and restarted; however, the Batch Executive needs to be downloaded (either a complete download or equipment only) for the changes to take effect. The following are considered Area Model changes: Adding, deleting, or modifying a process cell Adding, deleting, or modifying a unit module (including downstream units) Adding, deleting, or modifying a phase class (altering composite logic within the phase does not impact the Area Model) including input parameter modifications including report parameter modifications including batch message parameter modifications Changing the "Phase Type" or "Simulate" properties for a Unit Phase or a Phase Logic Module (PLM) Changing the associations between areas and process cells, between process cells and units/unit modules, units and phase logic modules, and unit modules and unit phases Changing area assignments to the Batch Executive Changes to unit aliases in equipment trains and equipment train classes Changes to unit selection policies Adding or deleting equipment trains When the Batch Executive is processing a download the following functions are not available through the Batch Operator Interface, Campaign Manager or the DeltaV Operate Batch control: Adding a batch to the batch list. Creating a manual phase batch. Creating a campaign. Releasing a batch via the Campaign Manager. For changes made to the controller (for example, unit module assignments) to be effective with new batches added to the Batch List, the changes, that is the changed unit modules, must be downloaded to the controller. The Batch Executive must also be downloaded (equipment download at a minimum). When downloading both the controller and the Batch Executive, download the controller first, then the Batch Executive. To be able to select new equipment for recipes already on the batch list, you must resynchronized the recipe after downloading the controller and Batch Executive. Note: If you have already downloaded the Batch Executive and then change the unit module's controller assignment, you will have to make a change to the Area Model as well and re-download the Batch Executive for the Batch Executive to be current. Changes to recipes do not impact recipes already on the Batch List. A snapshot of the recipe and equipment configuration is stored by the batch runner when the batch is added to the Batch List.New batches will use the modified recipe. The following recipe changes can take effect after a download without restarting the Batch Executive. Recipes may be added or deleted or modified (provided that you have not added new input or report parameters to any phase classes that are referenced in the recipe). Creating, altering, or deleting formulas Creating, altering, or deleting operations Creating, altering, or deleting unit procedures Creating, altering, or deleting procedures Modifying what equipment trains the procedure uses CAUTION: Downloading a modified recipe used as a base recipe in a campaign requires you to resync the campaign's (or its constituent batches') recipes. The following changes should not be downloaded while a recipe is running or on the batch list. Doing so can cause undesirable results. Deleting process cells or units that are being used by batches currently in the Batch List Renaming equipment, phase classes, unit class parameters, or phase class parameters Modifying unit class or phase class parameters Changing equipment arbitration ID's Adding or deleting phase class input or report parameters If you make changes online, such as adding or deleting a phase parameter, while recipes are running that involve those parameters, your phase logic must be able to handle those kinds of changes. For example, if a recipe gets to a phase where a parameter has been deleted, there may be a mismatch. (The Batch Executive knows of the parameter, but the controller is not aware of it.) In this case an operator prompt will appear notifying you of the mismatch and asking for confirmation of whether to continue. On the other hand, if you add a phase parameter and download the phase, the Batch Executive will not be aware of it, but the controller will be. Your phase/recipe logic must be able to handle this kind of mismatch. CAUTION: Never download a phase logic module (PLM) that is being used by an active batch as this will cause all phases that are being executed on the phase logic module to be terminated. The unexpected termination of a phase will cause the recipe that was executing the phase to fail. Related information Batch Executive configuration settings Resync the base recipe

title: Effect of HART error conditions on the channel integrity parameter (Classic I/O)
main_heading: Effect of HART error conditions on the channel integrity parameter (Classic I/O)
body_text: Effect of HART error conditions on the channel integrity parameter (Classic I/O) The channel integrity parameter (OINTEG) is True (1) when one or more of the following conditions are True: HART card detects a problem with itself. An open or short is detected on a HART channel input. An analog NAMUR high or low level is detected (AI only). DEV_MALFUNC is True and not ignored via the HART_ERRORS parameter. PV_FIXED is True and not ignored via the HART_ERRORS parameter. There has been a problem configuring the HART instrument during initialization. If any of the conditions below exist, OINTEG will be True (1) except for Good and Good - No Installed Config.

title: Install and power Ethernet I/O cards
main_heading: Install and power Ethernet I/O cards
body_text: Install and power Ethernet I/O cards The Ethernet I/O Card (EIOC) is used to easily and securely integrate TCP/IP-based data into a DeltaV system. Simplex or redundant EIOCs mount in the Dual Universal Carrier. A simplex EIOC can install in either slot of the carrier. Cover the open slot with a protective cover if installing a simplex EIOC. title: Adding and configuring EIOCs in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading: Adding and configuring EIOCs in DeltaV Explorer
body_text: Adding and configuring EIOCs in DeltaV Explorer Ethernet I/O Cards are added to the I/O Network in DeltaV Explorer. The properties for the EIOC port, physical device, logical device, and signals are configured in the DeltaV Explorer. Refer to the help for the EIOC properties dialogs in DeltaV Explorer for configuration information. Refer also to the device documentation when configuring the device in DeltaV Explorer. Related information Ethernet I/O Card license demand guidelines DNS and EIOC as an OPC UA client

title: Ethernet-based device control write confirmation time guidelines
main_heading:
Ethernet-based device control write confirmation time
	 guidelines
body_text: Ethernet-based device control write confirmation time guidelines The following are things to consider when configuring write confirmation: Each protocol behaves differently. The scan times vary based on each of the following, the impact of which varies based on the selected protocol. The number of logical devices on a specific physical device. Note that different physical devices can have different scan times. The total number of physical and logical devices configured on the controller or EIOC affects communication time. The frequency of output changes. Outputs are typically only driven on demand which increases the time of a scan that includes a write. With the 61850 protocol, the configuration of an SBO or SBOw output affects communication time. In this case, two messages are required to drive the output which increases the total time needed. All communications occur over Ethernet which can have time delays causing a retransmission of the packet. Any timeouts associated with retries impacts the scan time. Confirmation times must allow for these normal retry delays. Do not make the write confirmation time unrealistic for your scenario.

title: Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration interface
body_text: Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration interface The Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration interface is a tag-based protocol for accessing PLC data. DeltaV software includes control tag definitions that correspond to Rockwell Logix tag data. Subtopics: Accessing Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration data Configuring Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration devices and signals with tag definitions Configuring custom or array PLC tag definitions

title: Accessing Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration data
main_heading: Accessing Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration data
body_text: Accessing Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration data The Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration interface monitors Rockwell PLC tags data. The EIOC supports Rockwell ControlLogix and CompactLogix PLC integration. You can create custom tags or use the tag definitions provided with DeltaV software. The tag definitions provided with DeltaV software monitor the following Rockwell Logix Add-On instructions: P_AIn (Basic Analog Input) P_AOn (Basic Analog Output) P_DIn (Basic Discrete Input) P_DOn (Basic Discrete Output) The tag definitions listed above work with DeltaV TAG function blocks. You can design a custom tag definition to work with wide variety of Rockwell PLC tag data as long as it is an Add-On instruction or structure. This protocol reads or writes PLC tags that are base data types (such as BOOL, INT, SINT, DINT, REAL, and STRING as input only).

title: Configuring Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration devices and signals with tag definitions
main_heading:
Configuring Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration devices and signals
	 with tag definitions
body_text: Configuring Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration devices and signals with tag definitions The EIOC port defines the protocol used in the device network. Physical devices, their logical devices and device signals are configured under the port. The following sections provide a high-level description of the tasks required to integrate PLC data through Control Tags using the standard tag definitions that are included with DeltaV software. Refer to the PLC documentation for device information. Refer to DeltaV Explorer help information on the EIOC dialogs and for specific configuration tasks. Set preferences to support control tag integration In the System Preferences application under Networking , select Ethernet I/P Integration with Tags . Export control tag definitions from your PLC Export control tag definitions from the PLC. For Rockwell devices, this is a .L5X file. Copy the control tag definitions file to the ProfessionalPLUS workstation Copy the file you exported from the PLC to the ProfessionalPLUS. You can place the file anywhere on the workstation. When you configure the physical device later in the configuration process, the software copies it to the DeltaV\DVData\ControlTags folder. Set the port protocol for the EIOC port to Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration In the Ethernet I/O Port Preferences Properties dialog, on the Advanced tab, click Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration under the Protocol drop-down list. Create a physical device on the EIOC port to communicate with the PLC Right-click the port and click New Ethernet I/O Physical Device . Specify a control tags file for the physical device On the physical device properties dialog, under the Advanced tab, click Browse to specify the Control Tag File that you exported previously. Create a logical device under the physical device for specific groups of control tag information On the Properties dialog for the logical device, specify the rack number, slot number and other properties of the device. Add Ethernet I/O control tags to the EIOC logical device Under the logical device, add new Ethernet I/O control tags. This links a device tag from the PLC export file to a DeltaV tag definition. Tag definitions are part of the DeltaV library templates (Library\PLC Tag Definitions). The table shows the standard tag definitions included with DeltaV software and the Rockwell Logix Add-On instructions to which they correspond. The standard tag definitions are read-only. Writing values requires a custom tag. DeltaV PLC Tag Definition Rockwell Logix Add-On Instruction TAGAI_Monitor P_AIn TAGAO_Monitor P_AOn TAGDI_Monitor P_DIn TAGDO_Monitor P_DOn If the tag definitions included with DeltaV software are not sufficient for your control strategy, you can create your own custom or array tag definition. You can do this in one of two ways: by creating a library definition in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy and choosing it when you add a control tag to the EIOC logical device (custom and array tag definitions are included in the drop-down list along with standard tag definitions), or by creating it new when you add a control tag to the logical device. You create a custom or array tag definition using a PLC export file, or you can enter the data manually. If you use an export file, it must be on your workstation. The New Control Tag Definition dialog enables you to select the export file ( Definition File ). Once you select the file, you can browse for a specific Add-On instruction. If you want to use a tag in the export file that is not an Add-On instruction, you must type it in manually. Using control tag data in your control strategy You can assign a signal DST to a parameter in an EIOC-resident control module. The DSTs and the control module parameters (or function block parameters) must be associated with the same EIOC. Non-Boolean input signal DSTs can be referenced as a FIELD_VAL parameter. Boolean input signal DSTs can be referenced as a FIELD_VAL_D parameter. String input signal DSTs can be referenced as a FIELD_VAL_S parameter. Similarly, output signal DSTs can be referenced as an OUT parameter for non-Boolean and an OUT_D parameter for Boolean. Using Tag I/O blocks and TagIntegration module templates in your control strategy The DeltaV Explorer library contains four TagIntegration module templates that use the TAG I/O blocks and alarm blocks to form the basis or a working monitoring module. You assign the tag block to an Ethernet I/O control tag (of the appropriate type) you created under the logical device. Control Studio includes TAG I/O blocks on the IO palette (TAGAI, TAGAO, TAGDI, TAGDO). In addition, there is a TAGIO block that converts to the appropriate TAG block when you assign it to specific EIOC control tag signal. You can build your own module using these blocks if you do not use a template. Connect the PLC to the EIOC device network port Physically connect the PLC to the EIOC port.

title: EIOC device network redundancy
body_text: EIOC device network redundancy The EIOC supports redundant device network connections through its carrier. With redundant networks, the EIOC attempts communications with a device on the device's primary address first. If the primary address fails, it attempts communications on the device's secondary address (must be configured to be a redundant network). Additionally, primary and secondary device networks connected to an EIOC support two types of redundancy: the redundancy inherent in the device network protocol (the default), or Parallel Redundancy Protocol (PRP). In the case of the IEC 61850 protocol, PRP is the only option because PRP is the inherent method used for redundancy. Subnets for redundant device networks Redundant device networks require that you configure the primary and secondary device networks to be on separate subnets. Additionally, all devices that are connected to the EIOC must have IP addresses that match the subnets of the network to which the devices are connected. Note: Understanding IP addressing and the subnet mask is key to creating separate subnets. The basic rule is that the sum of the IP address and the subnet mask define the subnets. IPv4 addresses are grouped into 4 octets, where each octet represents a very large binary number. Depending on the subnet mask, you will need to change the appropriate octet to create the different subnets for your primary and secondary device networks. For example, if the primary device network is 192.168.1.100 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0, you must change the third octet to create a different secondary subnet (192.168. 2 .101 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0). Contact Emerson support for assistance in designing the device network IP addressing. Parallel Redundancy Protocol (PRP) PRP is a high-availability protocol that provides uninterrupted data communication in the event of a device network failure. It does this by duplicating outgoing packets and transmitting them on both device networks. Duplicate communications are discarded by the receiving node. If one network fails, the nodes use the data from the remaining network which is already operational. You enable PRP on the Ethernet I/O Port Properties dialog (Advanced tab) by selecting the Parallel Redundancy Protocol checkbox. PRP-enabled devices can connect to both networks. Devices that are not PRP-enabled must connect to a redundancy box (RedBox) before connecting to the network. The RedBox adapts simplex devices for primary and secondary PRP device networks. If you connect a device that is not PRP-enabled to only one network (no RedBox), the DeltaV system generates alarms until a RedBox and a connection to each network is added. Related information DNS and EIOC as an OPC UA client

title: EIOC download options
body_text: EIOC download options There are several download options for EIOCs. Downloading the: EIOC results in a total download of the card. Individual modules results in a partial download of the selected modules. Port results in a partial download of the port and all devices and signals configured under the port; only devices with configuration changes are affected by the port download. Physical device results in a partial download of the device and all its logical devices and signals. For the Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration protocol, control tags are included. The following lists how a download affects a running process. The Effects of the EIOC Download Options Type of download Modbus, Ethernet/IP, and Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration IEC 61850 OPC UA EIOC (total) All devices on the card are affected. The download replaces all information in the EIOC and reinitializes communication with the device. All devices on the card are affected. The download replaces all information in the EIOC and reinitializes communication with the device. All devices on the card are affected. The download replaces all information in the EIOC and reinitializes communication with the device. Individual module This is the same behavior as the DeltaV controller. Refer to the Downloading Data topic's Partial Download section for details. This is the same behavior as the DeltaV controller. Refer to the Downloading Data topic's Partial Download section for details. Port A port download with any of the following changes results in communication to the device being reestablished (an interruption in communication occurs): a changed port number a changed IP address a changed subnet mask A port download with changed device configuration only affects those devices. If none of the above changes were made, a port download has no affect on communications with the attached devices. A change to the IP address results in communications being stopped and reestablished using the new IP address. This is similar to a total download. Note: A port number change (which is fixed on 61850) has a similar impact, as does changing the protocol. A port download with changed device configuration only affects those devices. If none of the above changes were made, a port download has no affect on communications with the attached devices. A port download with any of the following changes results in communication to the device being reestablished (an interruption in communication occurs): a changed IP address a changed subnet mask a change on a certificate a change on issuers a change on the revocation list A port download with changed device configuration only affects those devices. Physical device A physical device download with logical device and/or signal changes causes the physical device to reestablish communications. If no changes were made, a physical device download has no affect on communications with the attached devices. A change to the IP address results in communications being stopped and reestablished using the new IP address. This is similar to a total download. Note: A port number change (which is fixed on 61850) has a similar impact, as does changing the protocol. Additional changes and their affect are as follows: Changing either a logical device and/or the signals underneath only affects those specific items. Device communications are not affected. Any changes to the logical device affects all underlying signals. Changes to individual signals will only affect that signal. If none of the above changes were made, a physical device download has no affect on communications with the attached devices. A port download with changed device configuration only affects those devices. Note: Critical function block parameters are preserved during a partial EIOC download for any function block supported in the EIOC that is also in the Critical function block parameters preserved during partial download table (refer to the Downloading data topic). Related information Downloading data

title: Ethernet/IP interface
body_text: Ethernet/IP interface The EtherNet/IP interface is an I/O scanner that reads and writes data from and to Ethernet/IP I/O adapters and other scanners. Subtopics: Accessing Ethernet/IP data Configuring Ethernet/IP devices and signals

title: Accessing Ethernet/IP data
body_text: Accessing Ethernet/IP data The Ethernet/IP interface supports the following types of messaging connections: Implicit messages (Class 1) Explicit messages (Class 3) Class 3 with PCCC UCMM with Logix Tags

title: Configuring Ethernet/IP devices and signals
body_text: Configuring Ethernet/IP devices and signals Ethernet/IP physical devices, their logical devices, and device signals are configured under the port. Ethernet/IP physical device configuration consists of specifying the physical device's primary and secondary IP addresses. Ethernet/IP logical devices are groups of functions for the physical device. Ethernet/IP logical device configuration in DeltaV Explorer involves defining the characteristics of the device data represented by the logical device. Among the items configured in a logical device that uses the Ethernet/IP protocol is the messaging class (Class 1 Implicit, Class 3 Explicit, Class 3 with PCCC, and UCMM with Logix Tags), and the input and output sizes. Refer to the device documentation for the specific values to use to configure the logical device and to the context sensitive help in DeltaV Explorer. The device signals are used to access the device data. Many Ethernet/IP signal values are populated with information from the logical device. Note: To reduce the risk of I/O output failures and output transfer failures when using the EtherNet/IP protocol, Emerson recommends configuring one module to write to all output signals configured within a single LDT.

title: IEC 61850 (MMS) interface
body_text: IEC 61850 (MMS) interface The IEC 61850 Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS) interface is a client that reads and writes data from and to Intelligent Electronic Device servers. Subtopics: Accessing IEC 61850 data Configuring IEC 61850 devices and signals

title: Accessing IEC 61850 data
body_text: Accessing IEC 61850 data Inputs are periodic or by exception based on the signal configuration and outputs are sent when they are written at a rate limited by the execution rate of the module that is writing the outputs. IEC 61850 defines specific names to identify data. Data is contained in Intelligent Electronic Devices within logical devices and logical nodes. The logical devices and signals defined under the IEC 61850 Intelligent Electronic Devices include the information needed to identify which data element within a logical node of a logical device is to be accessed.

title: Configuring IEC 61850 devices and signals
body_text: Configuring IEC 61850 devices and signals IEC 61850 physical devices, their logical devices, and device signals are configured under the port. IEC 61850 physical device configuration consists of specifying the physical device's primary and secondary IP addresses. IEC 61850 defines specific names to identify data. Data is contained in Intelligent Electronic Devices within logical devices in logical nodes. The logical devices and signals defined under IEC 61850 devices include the information needed to identify which data element within a logical node of a logical device is to be accessed. Among the items configured for logical devices that use the IEC 61850 protocol are the logical device name and logical node name. The logical device name identifies the logical device within the Intelligent Electronic Device that contains the logical nodes holding data to be accessed by the logical device's signals. The logical node name defines the container that holds the attribute data to be accessed by the logical device's signals. Refer to the device documentation for the strings to use for the logical device name and the logical node name and refer to the context sensitive help in DeltaV Explorer for configuration information. The device signals are used to access the device data. IEC 61850 signals make use of common properties such as signal direction, data type, byte order and offset and so on. Note: Make sure the parameter name is correct. Incorrect names can result in a Reject PDU message from the server in the MMS response rather than bad status on the signal itself.

title: EIOC licensing
body_text: EIOC licensing There are three license types associated with the EIOC: an interface (protocol) license, one or more DST licenses, and a system-wide license to support the total number of EIOC physical devices in the DeltaV system. Follow the Related information link for more information on EIOC licensing. Related information Ethernet I/O Card license demand guidelines

title: Ethernet I/O Card license demand guidelines
main_heading: Ethernet I/O Card license demand guidelines
body_text: Ethernet I/O Card license demand guidelines There are three license types associated with the Ethernet I/O Card (EIOC): an interface license, a system-wide (physical device) license, and one or more DST licenses. Interface license An interface license is available for each of the protocols supported by the EIOC: Ethernet/IP Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration IEC 61850 Modbus TCP OPC UA Only one interface license can be assigned to an EIOC. Ethernet I/O physical device licenses A physical device EIOC license is required to support the total number of EIOC physical devices (PDTs) in a single DeltaV system. Several license levels are available. EIOC system-wide licenses are assigned to the ProfessionalPlus workstation. They cannot be unassigned. Note: PK controller physical devices also consume licenses from the EIOC system-wide license. DST licenses The table describes the DST license consumption. For the Ethernet/IP, IEC 61850, Modbus TCP, and OPC UA protocols, the DST license type consumed is determined by the most expensive type of signal configured for the logical device. For the Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration protocol, the DST license type consumed is determined by the most expensive type of signal configured for the Control Tag. The DST license demand from the logical devices configured for an EIOC are counted against the system-wide AO DST, AI DST, DO DST, and DI DST license capacities assigned to the system. DST license demand for EIOCs Protocol DST licenses consumed Ethernet/IP One per logical device Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration One per Control Tag IEC 61850 One per logical device Modbus TCP One per logical device OPC UA One per logical device Signal-bearing parameters and license demand requirements Parameter name I/O license type used FIELD_VAL AI FIELD_VAL_D DI FIELD_VAL_S 1 DI OUT AO OUT_D DO Ethernet I/O physical device licenses A system-wide EIOC license is required to support the total number of EIOC physical devices in a single DeltaV system. Several license levels are available. EIOC system-wide licenses are assigned to the ProfessionalPlus workstation. They cannot be unassigned. Placeholder EIOC devices do not count against the system-wide license. However, placeholders do impact download performance. Note: PK controller physical devices also consume licenses from the EIOC system-wide license. 1 This parameter is only supported by the Ethernet /IP Control Tag Integration and OPC UA protocols.

title: Modbus TCP/IP interface
body_text: Modbus TCP/IP interface The Modbus TCP interface is a Modbus client (master) that reads and writes data from and to Modbus servers (slave devices). The Modbus server devices can be direct Modbus TCP devices or Modbus serial devices under a Modbus TCP gateway. Subtopics: Accessing Modbus TCP data Configuring Modbus TCP devices and signals Related information Modbus register ranges

title: Accessing Modbus TCP data
body_text: Accessing Modbus TCP data The EIOC supports only the Modbus TCP standard protocol; the RTU via TCP and RTU via UDP are not supported in the EIOC. The EIOC uses MODICON (PLC) based addressing (Modbus absolute addressing is not supported). The Modbus TCP interface supports the following types of data access using the Modbus TCP protocol: Input data is read from Modbus Coils, Discrete Input, Holding Registers, and Input Registers. Input data is read in multiple mode for the best performance. Output data is written to Coils and Holding Registers. Output data is written one at a time or in multiple mode. All reads are performed periodically and outputs are sent at a rate that is limited by the execution rate of the module writing the outputs. The logical devices and signals defined under the Modbus device include the information needed to identify the specific Modbus device (for serial devices under a Modbus TCP gateway) and the register being accessed.

title: Configuring Modbus TCP devices and signals
main_heading: Configuring Modbus TCP devices and signals
body_text: Configuring Modbus TCP devices and signals The port defines the protocol that is used in the device network. Physical devices, their logical devices, and device signals are configured under the port. Refer to the device documentation and the context sensitive help for all EIOC dialogs in DeltaV Explorer for configuration information. Modbus physical device configuration consists of specifying the physical device's primary and secondary IP addresses. Modbus logical devices are groups of functions for the physical device. Logical device configuration involves defining the characteristics of the device data represented by the logical device. Among the items configured in the logical device is the Number of values which defines how many contiguous registers are accessed in this logical device's data grouping. Refer to the device documentation for the specific values to use to configure the device. The device signals are used to access the device data. The proper number of signals is automatically created under the logical device when it is initially saved based on the "Number of values" that is specified for the logical device. The signals are automatically populated with the appropriate configuration information included in the logical device.

title: DeltaV Ethernet I/O Card
body_text: DeltaV Ethernet I/O Card The Ethernet I/O Card (EIOC) provides an interface to Ethernet device networks and to devices that use one of the following protocols: Modbus TCP/IP Ethernet/Industrial Protocol (Ethernet/IP) IEC 61850 Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS) OPC UA Ethernet/IP Control Tag Integration interface The EIOC accesses data for history collection, alarming, and limited control. The EIOC is not a DeltaV controller. Unlike a DeltaV controller, the EIOC: Supports a subset of function blocks that are used for motor control and supervisory control. References device data only, it does not reference other I/O such as CHARMs I/O. Only references data from devices on the network to which it is connected and external module data. It does not support externally referenced device data directly. The EIOC mounts on a carrier that houses a dual port for connections to the DeltaV Area Control Network and to the intelligent device network. The EIOC can communicate with M and S-series controllers using the standard inter-controller communications. The EIOC's port defines the protocol used, the physical devices, their logical devices, and device signals. Logical devices are groups of functions for the physical device. The device signals are used to access the device data, OPC UA data and Ethernet/IP control tag data. title: EIOC node redundancy
body_text: EIOC node redundancy EIOC nodes can be configured for redundancy. Switchovers occur with no bumps in device data values or status. Redundant EIOC nodes operate as an Active/Standby pair. The active EIOC configures and updates the standby to keep it synchronized with the active. The standby EIOC in a redundant pair monitors the health of the active EIOC and becomes the active when: The currently active EIOC fails to communicate with the standby over the redundancy link The currently active EIOC fails to communicate with all configured Ethernet devices Redundant EIOC nodes are two paired EIOCs having either a simplex device network or redundant device networks (the EIOC supports redundant device network connections through its carrier). With redundant EIOC nodes, if the active node fails the pair can switchover to the standby for communication to the devices. Once switched over to the standby, if the previous node is still not communicating, you are operating in a simplex EIOC mode. Note: When creating physical devices on redundant EIOCs, be aware that the system assigns the primary and secondary IP addresses of the standby by adding 1 to the existing address. Therefore, when the EIOC primary port has a network IP address of 192.168.1.1; the standby EIOC primary port is given the primary network IP address of 192.168.1.2.

title: Electronic signatures
body_text: Electronic signatures Electronic signatures are user names and passwords that provide accountability for operator writes to certain module parameters and fields from DeltaV Operate and Control Studio online. Electronic Signatures do not apply to writes to OPC and to the DeltaV Excel Add-in application. Electronic signatures is a DeltaV system preference that can be disabled (hidden) if not required or enabled selectively on an area-by-area, module-by-module basis. Electronic signatures does not change the existing DeltaV security feature that controls who is able to make changes to parameters. Rather, it uses a signature to authenticate the operator's identity. That is, the signature is used as an additional check to ensure that the operator is who he claims to be. The operator must have a valid user name and password and the required privileges to perform the action in the area in which the module resides. The write is not allowed if the operator fails to enter a valid username and password and if the operator does not have the required privileges in the area in which the module resides. Depending upon the criticality of a module to the process, no signature, one signature (confirmer), or two signatures (confirmer and verifier) can be configured. It is possible to allow the same person to be both the confirmer and verifier of an operator write. Typically, the verifier is a higher-level employee whose signature approves the change the confirmer is making. The verifier must hold the key to the ACTION_VERIFY function lock. To allow the same person to be both Confirmer and Verifier, select Properties from the Electronic Signatures context menu and select the check box. If the electronic signature succeeds, the date and time the electronic signature authentication occurred, the node from which the change occurred, a description of the action, and the confirmer and verifier names are recorded in the Event Chronicle and can be seen through the Process History View application. Similarly, failed attempts at confirming or verifying an action are also recorded and visible through the Process History View. In addition to the Process History View application, failed confirm or verify attempts are also recorded in the Batch Historian if it is collecting Event Chronicle events and can be viewed through the Batch History View application. Operator comments The operator has the option of entering a comment about the parameter change. Operator comments are recorded in the Desc2 field in the Process History View application. This field is truncated at 240 characters. By default, the system adds the string VALUE SIGNED FOR = xxxxx before the comment. That is, the system adds additional characters to your comment and these additional characters are counted in the 240 character limit. So for example if you changed a value to 365 and entered the comment "changed value for tank1" the Desc2 field will total 48 characters and read: VALUE SIGNED FOR = 365 (changed value for tank1) The system calculates the length of the string VALUE SIGNED FOR = xxxxx plus the length of the comment. If the comment will cause Desc2 to exceed 240 characters, the system posts a message asking that the comment be shortened. The length of the comment is limited to the lesser of: 200 characters or what fits in the Desc2 field. If VALUE SIGNED FOR is a string that exceeds that 240 characters, the value is truncated at 240 characters in the Desc2 field in Process History View and no comment is saved with the value. The DeltaV system does not enforce the use of operator comments; this decision is left to plant managers. Note: Do not use the ENTER key to create a line break in the Comment field. Pressing the ENTER key in the Comment field is the same as selecting the OK button; it dismisses the dialog and performs the command. Subtopics: Configuring electronic signatures Using signature policies with contained modules Electronic signatures at run time Using electronic signatures when acknowledging alarms on pictures

title: Signature Policies preference
body_text: Signature Policies preference Note: Disabling the Signature Policies option in the System Properties dialog does not disable electronic signatures on modules. To disable electronic signatures on modules you must remove the signature policy on each module before disabling the Signature Policies option in the System Properties dialog. This preference enables or disables the following features of electronic signature policies: DeltaV Explorer An Electronic Signatures container under the Security object. Dialogs for creating signature policies and assigning polices to modules. Control Studio (online) and DeltaV Operate Dialogs that allow operators to enter an electronic signature before writing to parameters and fields listed in signature policies. Note: To enable electronic signatures system-wide you must: Enable the Signature Policies option in System Preferences . Enable electronic signatures in the Electronic Signatures Properties dialog for ElectronicSignatures under the Security container in DeltaV Explorer. You can also enable electronic signatures in DeltaV Operate and DeltaV Control Studio in the Electronic Signatures Properties dialog. Enable the Enable Electronic Signature option in the Properties dialog for the Area in DeltaV Explorer. For example, if the modules requiring electronic signatures are in Area_A, enable the Enable Electronic Signature option in the Area_A Properties dialog.

title: Electronic signatures at run time
body_text: Electronic signatures at run time In Control Studio online, dialogs that are used to modify parameters, such as the Mode Properties dialog, automatically launch the Electronic Signature dialog when electronic signatures are configured for the parameter. However, in DeltaV Operate only objects inserted with the following tools launch the Electronic Signatures dialog: Datalink Stamper Datalink Formatter DeltaV Data Entry Expert SIS Data Entry Expert When an operator clicks a button or presses ENTER after writing to a parameter that is subject to an electronic signature, the Electronic Signature dialog opens. The parameter is not written until the required signature is provided. The following image shows the Electronic Signature dialog that opens in Control Studio online when a Confirm and Verify signature is required for a parameter write. The appearance of this dialog varies depending upon the signature requirement. Electronic Signature dialog for confirm and verify signature requirement

title: Electronic Signature Properties
body_text: Electronic Signature Properties Use the Electronic Signatures Properties dialog to enable electronic signature support in DeltaV Operate and Control Studio online and to allow the confirmer and verifier to be the same person. Electronic Signatures Properties dialog Enabling electronic signatures from this dialog enables the electronic signature capability in DeltaV Operate and Control Studio online. If electronic signatures are not enabled here, no signatures are required for any write. Before electronic signatures can be used, you must enable electronic signatures for the process areas in which the modules reside and define a signature policy for the modules. If electronic signatures is not enabled for an area, no signatures will be required for writes to modules in that area. To enable electronic signatures in a process area, select Properties from the area's context menu and select Enable Electronic Signature . It is necessary to download the Setup data after making a change to electronic signature properties. When the change affects either the Batch Executive or the Campaign Manager, those subsystems must be downloaded.

title: Embedded composites
body_text: Embedded composites When you use an embedded composite, both the structural and the parameter data are stored as part of the module (refer to the previous figure). When you edit the module in the offline view, both types of information can be modified. Double-click an embedded composite (or right-click, and then select Edit Object ) to open the composite for modification. Like in any control diagram within the DeltaV system, you can edit the parameter information when in the online view. If you created the embedded composite from a library composite, an exact copy of the library composite is made and placed within the control module. From that point forward, all links back to the original library composite are broken. If your purpose is to create a composite that you can modify without affecting the original block or any other composite blocks that are linked to the original, embed the composite. An embedded composite is a separate, standalone object; modifying it does not change the source block, and modifying the source block does not change the new composite.

title: Embedded OSIsoft PI Server architecture
body_text: Embedded OSIsoft PI Server architecture You can install OSIsoft PI Server on an Application Station to function as the historian on your DeltaV system. The embedded PI Server historian is used to configure, collect, store, and retrieve historical data from DeltaV. You can use PI Server instead of or in addition to using the DeltaV Continuous Historian or the Advanced Continuous Historian. The embedded PI Server historian requires the DeltaV Smart Connector, as well as a DeltaV OPC Data Access Server and an Enterprise Historian Configuration Interface license from Emerson. The DeltaV Smart Connector includes the DeltaV Asset Connector and the PI OPC Data Access (DA) Interface. The following diagram illustrates the basic configuration of a DeltaV system with PI Server installed on an Application Station: Related information Integrated OSIsoft PI Server architecture

title: Emergency Repair Disk
body_text: Emergency Repair Disk The Windows Repair Disk utility protects Windows system settings by creating an Emergency Repair Disk (ERD) from which to restore a workstation's configuration and security settings in case of a system failure. Create and update the ERD after making any significant changes to the hardware or software setup or adding Windows accounts. Note: Installing DeltaV software, running Workstation Configuration, or running the DeltaV User Manager can change software settings or add Windows accounts. Also, most of the Windows programs located in Control Panel as well as the Windows User Manager program in Administrative tools can change the workstation's software settings. It is recommended that you create a new ERD after running any of these applications. Note: The ERD does not create a system backup or a DeltaV backup. Do not use the Repair Disk utility in place of a backup tool. Online Windows documentation steps you through the creation of an ERD. To view these instructions, click Start > Help and enter ERD under the Find or Index tab.

title: Enabling the Campaign Manager Server
body_text: Enabling the Campaign Manager Server To run campaigns, you must enable the Campaign Manager subsystem. Once the Campaign Manager subsystem is enabled and configured (from the subsystem Properties dialog), you must download the workstation for the change to take effect. You must also start the Campaign Manager server for this node using the Batch Application Manager. Each Campaign Manager server can be enabled for only one Batch Executive. That is, with multiple Batch Executives, you have multiple Campaign Managers. It is a one-to-one relationship. You must select a Batch Executive node for this Campaign Manager from the list (or click Browse and browse to the Batch Executive node).

title: The enable auto switchback parameter
body_text: The enable auto switchback parameter Redundant Series 2 cards have an enable automatic switchback (ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK) parameter that controls whether or not the active and standby cards switch over more than one time when faults are detected. The default is enabled (True). Note: ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK cannot be disabled for Redundant Series 2 Serial and H1 cards. For these cards, it is always True. To enable or disable the parameter, select the redundant card in DeltaV Explorer, right-click ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK, and then select Properties . When ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK is True and: a fault occurs, the active card switches over. the same fault occurs, the new active card does not switch over. (If both cards detect the same problem, it is probably a field error.) a different fault occurs, the new active card switches over. When ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK is False and: a fault occurs, the active card switches over. a subsequent fault occurs, the cards do not switch over until the saved fault information command is issued. Note: If ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK is False and the controller detects a new card in the redundant pair, a switchover will be allowed to the new card if the active card has a fault. For example, if you replace the standby card or if communications is lost and then reestablished with the standby card, a switchover can occur even if ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK is False. The decision to enable or disable automatic switchback depends on the requirements of your process and the importance of the card. Disabling ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK requires manual intervention for switchovers to occur but prevents cards from frequently switching over. On the other hand, enabling ENABLE_AUTO_SWBK causes cards to switch over but, under certain circumstances, can result in frequent switchovers. Related information Identifying and troubleshooting Series 2 redundant cards

title: Enabling and disabling a transition
body_text: Enabling and disabling a transition You can disable and (re-) enable transitions from the Procedure as PFC screen. Disabling (or enabling) the transition allows the recipe to continue and the transition evaluates to False. You can re-enable a disabled transition and it will execute the next time the recipe is run (or if the recipe loops back to that location). Related information Displaying transition status

title: Enabling the Batch Executive
body_text: Enabling the Batch Executive In order to run a batch either in Recipe Simulator or real time, you must first enable the Batch Executive on a machine that will run the Batch Executive application. This lets the DeltaV database know which machine has the responsibility for processing the recipes, arbitrating equipment, handling messages, coordinating phase link groups, and recording events. A maximum of four Batch Executives can be enabled on a DeltaV network. General Properties of the Batch Executive Once the Batch Executive subsystem is enabled (from the subsystem Properties dialog), you must download the workstation for the change to take effect. When downloading the Batch Executive, the following functions are not available through the Batch Operator Interface or the DeltaV Operate Batch controls: Add a batch to the batch list. Create a manual phase batch. Create a campaign. Release a batch. When importing a workstation, be sure to correctly answer which components you want to overwrite during the download. Individually select 'No' on any items that are not to be imported. Then, you can answer 'Yes' to overwrite the existing Batch Server object (BATCH_AREA). This imports the Batch Executive configuration changes. Related information Downloading data

title: Enabling the Batch Historian
body_text: Enabling the Batch Historian To collect data from the DeltaV system and store that data in a Batch Historian database, you must first enable a Batch Historian on the machine that will run the Batch Historian application. This lets the DeltaV database know which machine has the responsibility for identifying the data sources and storage databases. Up to four Batch Historians can be enabled on a DeltaV system The Batch Historian can only be enabled on an Application Station . General Properties of the Batch Historian Once the Batch Historian subsystem is enabled and configured (from the subsystem Properties dialog), you must download the workstation for the change to take effect. If you disable the Batch Historian while it is storing batch data, it is recommended that you re-enable it before the time configured for removing event files as determined in the Batch Executive properties. The Batch Historian can retrieve and store data from any batch event files that were generated before the Batch Historian was enabled, provided the files have not been removed or deleted while the Batch Historian was disabled. Therefore, in order to maintain a continuous and complete batch history, the Batch Historian should be re-enabled and started before the event files are removed.

title: Enabling device alarms
body_text: Enabling device alarms Fieldbus and HART device alarms are enabled by default when you add a new device to the control network from the Explorer library. You can change the enabled/disabled status of the alarms for the device as a whole and for each individual alarm. The enable/disable setting for the device is on the Alarms & Displays tab of the device Properties dialog. To access the setting: Right-click the device. Click Properties . Click the Enable Device Alarms check box. The figure below shows the Fieldbus Device Properties dialog. The HART Device Properties dialog is similar. The Enable Device Alarms option determines whether the alarms are available within the DeltaV system. If this check box is not checked, the alarms will not be available through parameter browsers. In addition, the individual alarms do not appear in the Explorer and device alarm communications will not be attempted with the device. If you disable device alarms for a device, any configurable properties of the individual alarms (alarm enable and priority) are discarded. If the device alarms for a device are subsequently enabled again, the configurable properties are set to their default values. You enable or disable individual alarms as follows: Right-click the alarm. Click Properties . Click the Enabled check box. The enabled/disabled property for the individual alarms corresponds to the .ENAB field for the alarm. Control modules, OPC client applications and Operators using displays can change the .ENAB field for the alarm. Note: For fieldbus devices, changing the .ENAB field for a device alarm does not change the corresponding alarm enable status in the field device. Also note that when you download the field device (along with the device alarms), the corresponding enable is set to be consistent with the setting in the field device. In general, it is possible to read and write the parameter fields of device alarms from control modules that run in the same node. This type of reading and writing is typically limited to enabling or disabling certain device alarms based on the operating state of the module. For example, you might want to disable advisory alarms, which depend on the process to be active to work properly, when the unit is idle.

title: Enabling hardware alarms
body_text: Enabling hardware alarms Hardware alarms appear as a subsystem under the node in DeltaV Explorer. This subsystem must be enabled for the system to detect the alarm condition and categorize it into one of the four types of hardware alarm: Advisory (ADVISE_ALM), Failed (FAILED_ALM), Maintenance (MAINT_ALM), and Not Communicating (COMM_ALM). The Hardware Alarms subsystem is enabled from the node's Properties dialog by selecting the Enable System Hardware Alarms option. Hardware alarms for I/O cards are enabled with the controller under which they reside. Once hardware alarms are enabled, the hierarchy view displays the Hardware Alarm subsystem. Configuring the Hardware Alarm's Properties Once enabled, you can select the Hardware Alarms subsystem and configure the hardware alarm's properties. Access the alarm's Properties dialog by expanding the node, selecting the Hardware Alarms subsystem, and, in the right pane, right-clicking the alarm (ADVISE_ALM, for example). Then, select Properties from the context menu. Note: Hardware alarms are not supported on remote workstations. From the Alarm Properties dialog, the following can be configured: enable/disable the alarm change the default priority (this changes how operators see the alarm in the alarm banner. configure the alarm shelving timeout (except on COMM_ALM) set the functional classification enable/disable alarm help. Note: Setting the three alarm shelving timeout fields to zero (0) disables alarm shelving. Hardware alarm messages For a list of hardware alarm messages, including descriptions of the specific error conditions that trigger each message, refer to Hardware Alarm Messages. Downloads, switchovers and hardware alarms Hardware alarm state is retained through most partial downloads to the node. Condition state is reset on total downloads to the node; thus, after a total download, all hardware conditions become unsuppressed and the active timestamps are re-established (if the conditions are redetected). Note: There are exceptions to what is retained during a partial download to the node. For example, I/O cards undergoing major changes (number of channels, card type changes and so on) will have the hardware condition reset. Cards not undergoing such changes will have their condition preserved during the partial download. The alarm's properties settings are downloaded to the node when performing a total download, setup data download, or changed setup data download. The hardware alarm can be enabled/disabled by writing to the alarm's ENAB field (that is, <node>/FAILED_ALM.ENAB). This value cannot be uploaded. Hardware alarm condition suppression state survives redundant node switchovers; that is, all suppressed conditions do not unsuppress themselves because of a switchover. Related information Alarm priorities Alarm help overview Hardware alarm messages
