title: DeltaV system hardware
body_text: DeltaV system hardware The DeltaV hardware installation and reference manuals, available in DeltaV™ Books Online , describe the DeltaV system hardware and provide instructions for installing and powering up the system. The system hardware consists of the following: One or more DeltaV workstations A control network (optionally redundant) for communication between system nodes Power supplies One or more DeltaV controllers (optionally redundant) that perform local control and manage data and communications between the I/O subsystem and the control network At least one I/O subsystem per controller that processes information from field devices System Identifier The System Identifier, shipped in the License Pack, is a connector that plugs into a Universal Serial Bus (USB) port of the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. It gives each DeltaV system a unique identification that allows you to download changes to the system. Install the System Identifier on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation before you power up your system. Online, running DeltaV systems require a User System Identifier. Development System Identifiers are used to engineer and configure DeltaV systems before the systems go online. Multi-Node Simulate System Identifiers are used for training and simulation with DeltaV systems. Development System Identifiers and Multi-Node Simulate System Identifiers cannot be used with online, running systems. For information about converting a system based on a Development or Multi-Node System Identifier to one based on a User System Identifier, contact the Global Support Center or your local sales representative or sales office.

title: Hardware alarms overview
body_text: Hardware alarms overview Workstations, logic solvers, and controllers have a variety of conditions that indicate potential integrity problems. When detected, these conditions set OINTEG to BAD on the subsystem where that condition was detected, as well as for that node. This is shown in DeltaV Diagnostics. When a node is not communicating, it is shown in DeltaV Diagnostics as The conditions that set OINTEG to BAD and the detection of no communication can also generate DeltaV hardware alarms. For hardware alarms, each condition is defined by the system in either one of the following alarms (or defined to not generate an alarm): Not Communicating (COMM_ALM) - The node or card appears to not be communicating. This means that no other conditions can be detected. This also means any displays associated with this node or card cannot be opened for the operator. Failed (FAILED_ALM)- The node or card is communicating but important functions are not operable or there is a loss of control functions. Maintenance (MAINT_ALM) - All functions are working, but attention is required; for example, a redundant partner is not available. Advisory (ADVISE_ALM) - A single condition on the hardware is detected, such as an I/O channel's OINTEG is set to BAD is detected. Note: Control module conditions that set OINTEG do not generate a hardware alarm. Certain active conditions can encompass other conditions This is done to reduce the number of conditions being reported. For example, if an I/O card stops communicating to the controller, that alarm condition is reported and any other previously active conditions on that card, such as a bad I/O channel condition, are cleared. All active hardware conditions for a node are displayed in the Conditions Summary application. Any active condition that should not cause a hardware alarm can be suppressed in this application. Suppressed alarms (either shelved, out of service or both) are also displayed in the Conditions Summary application. The Conditions Summary application can be accessed from either DeltaV Diagnostics or DeltaV Operate (from the hardware alarm list or node faceplate). Loss of communications is detected by the workstation expecting the communication. When a workstation determines it has lost communications with another node, it sets the COMM_ALM alarm. This alarm is displayed on that workstation. Suppressing the COMM_ALM is only suppressing it on that specific workstation. Therefore, if you suppress a COMM_ALM for a controller on one workstation, the alarm is unchanged on any other workstation. All workstations include the ProfessionalPLUS’ COMM_ALM. Any node detected as having a communication failure problem with the ProfessionalPLUS will annunciate on that workstation, regardless of the alarm scope of the current DeltaV user. In order to acknowledge or suppress this alarm on a workstation that doesn’t include the ProfessionalPLUS’ Associate Alarms & Events with Area field: The workstation must have Restrict on-line changes to areas assigned to the Alarms & Events subsystem of this station disabled The user must have the “Alarms” lock for the area specified in the ProfessionalPLUS’ Associate Alarms & Events with Area field. Enabling DeltaV hardware alarms on a node or suppressing a hardware condition does not impact the OINTEG status or presentation. DeltaV applications such as DeltaV Operate (depending on configuration settings), DeltaV Diagnostics, and DeltaV Explorer present the OINTEG status. Each node's Associate Alarms & Events with Area is defined in its Properties dialog. The default association is Area_A. As with all alarms, nodes report hardware alarms to all workstations which have the nodes' areas assigned to them. Of the nodes assigned due to their area association, any node detected as having a communication problem will annunciate on that workstation, regardless of the alarm scope of the current DeltaV user. Related information Hardware alarm messages

title: Hardware alarm condition parameters (Smart Switch)
body_text: Hardware alarm condition parameters (Smart Switch) Except for changing the value of the alarm level (ignore, maint, advise or fail) we strongly recommend that you do not adjust other default parameters in the switch module unless instructed to do so by Emerson to solve a specific issue. A number of parameters hold information that determine how hardware alarm condition information in the switch is transformed into one of the PlantWeb-style hardware alarms. For floating-point array parameters that hold information specific to a switch port (expressed as m.p where m = module number and p = port number in the module), the mapping of port m.p to port number (array index) n follows the rule: Array index n = (switch module m - 1) * PPM + (switch module port p) where PPM (Ports per Module): Is 8 for FP20 and RM100 switches. Is 4 for MD20 and MD30 switches. Is 24 for RM104 switch Thus for an RM100: Port 1.1 information goes into HAC_XXXXXXXX_PRT[1] (1 - 1) * 1 = 1 Port 4.8 information (if present) goes into HAC_XXXXXXXX_PRT[32] (4 - 1) * 8 = 32 For an MD30: Port 7.4 information (if present) goes into HAC_XXXXXXXX_PRT[28] (7 - 1) * 4 = 28 For an RM104: Port 1.1 information goes into HAC_XXXXXXXX_PRT[1] (1 - 1) * 1 = 1 Port 1.24 information (if present) goes into HAC_XXXXXXXX_PRT[24] (1 - 1) * 24 = 24 Information for installed ports is not necessarily contiguous in the array. The parameter information that follows is arranged in the order the parameters appear in the switch module class function block diagram. Switch Not Communicating This condition is reported when the node hosting the switch module cannot communicate with the switch using the IP address in the MGMT_IP_ADDR parameter. Failure to communicate with the switch overrides all other switch conditions that may be configured causing them to become inactive: It is not possible to configure the switch module to ignore the NOCOMM condition. If there are any failures in reading information from the switch the raw NOCOMM condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_NOCOMM_OND and HAC_NOCOMM_OFFD. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_NOCOMM_OND Float 0 On delay (seconds). HAC_NOCOMM_OFD Float 0 Off delay (seconds). There is no HAC_NOCOMM_PWA parameter supported because the not communicating condition is always mapped to the COMM_ALM for the switch. Switch Is Unlocked If HAC_UNLOCKED_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for lockdown status and the time remaining on the lockdown timer If the lockdown status is Unlocked and there is no time remaining on the lockdown timer the raw UNLOCKED condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_UNLOCKED_OND and HAC_UNLOCKED_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the UNLOCKED condition, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Switch Message: DeltaV network switch unlocked Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_UNLOCKED_PWA Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_UNLOCKED_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_UNLOCKED_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_UNLOCKED_OFD Float 0 Off delay (seconds). Power Supply Unavailable DeltaV Smart Switches support redundant power supply connections (and in the case of the RM100, an option for redundant power conversion electronics). Reporting the loss of one of the power sources allows repairs before both power sources fail. If HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for the status of the power supply connections. If either power supply connection is bad, the raw PSNAVAIL condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_PSNAVAIL_OND and HAC_PSNAVAIL_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the PSNAVAIL condtion, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Switch Message: Power supply n unavailable (where n is either 1 or 2 to reflect the power supply that is unavailable). Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA When the switch power supply is not redundant you should either: Make the (non-redundant) power connections to both Power supply 1 and Power supply 2, or Configure HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA as Ignore (0) to disable checking this condition. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA Named Set MAINT_ALM This condition should trigger the MAINT alarm. HAC_PSNAVAIL_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_PSNAVAIL_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). Switch Chassis High Temperature DeltaV Smart Switches can detect and report their chassis temperature. Operating above their rated temperature range can result in deteriorating switch behavior. If HAC_HITEMP_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for its chassis temperature and writes the value to the HAC_HITEMP_VAL parameter. If the value in HAC_HITEMP_VAL becomes greater than the value in HAC_HITEMP_LIM the raw HITEMP condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_HITEMP_OND and HAC_HITEMP_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the HITEMP condition, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Switch Message: Switch temperature too high. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_HITEMP_PWA If DeltaV Smart Switches with different temperature ranges are employed, adjust HAC_HITEMP_LIM as desired in each switch module. If historical data on switch temperature is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_HITEMP_VAL. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_HITEMP_PWA Named Set MAINT_ALM This condition should trigger the MAINT alarm. HAC_HITEMP_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_HITEMP_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_HITEMP_LIM Float 50 Configurable high temperature limit for the switch, in degrees C. HAC_HITEMP_VAL Float 0 Receives the chassis temperature read from the switch (available for history capture). Switch Signal Relay Activated You can use advanced switch management tools to configure the conditions that cause the signaling relay on the switch to activate. The signaling relay can then be used to drive local indication of the problems detected by the switch. If HAC_SIGRACT_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for the status of the signal relay contacts. The value returned (1 = signal relay is activated; 2 = otherwise) is written to the HAC_SIGRACT_VAL parameter. If HAC_SIGRACT_VAL has a value other than 2 the raw SIGRACT condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_SIGRACT_OND and HAC_SIGRACT_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM HAC is active. The result is reported as the SIGRACT condition visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Switch Message: Switch signal relay activated. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_SIGRACT_PWA If historical data on the state of the signal relay is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_SIGRACT_VAL. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_SIGRACT_PWA Named Set Ignored This condition should be ignored by default. HAC_SIGRACT_OND Float 0 On delay (seconds). HAC_SIGRACT_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_SIGRACT_VAL Float 2 Receives the status of the signal relay read from the switch (available for history capture). 1 = signal relay is activated; 2 = inactive. Port Expected Communications Absent When locking a DeltaV Smart Switch, ports that have been communicating remain enabled, and all other ports are disabled (do not permit communications while the switch is locked). Given the nature of communications between nodes on the DeltaV control network, regular communications is expected on all enabled ports on locked switches (including switch to switch communications.) If HAC_COMABSNT_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for: The list of all ports installed on the switch. The switch lock status Whether each port is enabled or disabled Information about bytes received in the last 60 seconds on each installed port. If the switch is locked each enabled port is examined. If there have been 0 bytes of (unblocked) data received from any device or switch connected to a port in the last 60 seconds the raw COMABSNT condition is true for that port. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_COMABSNT_OND and HAC_COMABSNT_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the COMABSNT condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: Expected communications absent on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_COMABSNT_PWA Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_COMABSNT_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_COMABSNT_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_COMABSNT_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). Excessive Packets Discarded On Port Unusually high levels of packets discarded (due to CRC errors, packets too small (runts) or packets too large (giants) can be an indicator of loose or deteriorating network cable connections, damaged network cables, or failing network interface electronics. If HAC_DISCPKTS_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for: The list of all ports installed on the switch. Whether each port is enabled or disabled. Information about packets discarded (due to CRC errors, runts, and giants) in the last 60 seconds on each installed port. For each enabled port, the number of packets discarded in the last 60 seconds is written to the corresponding array element in HAC_DISCPKTS_PRT[n]. 0 is written for ports that are not installed or that are disabled. The sum from all ports of the packets discarded in the last 60 seconds is written to HAC_DISCPKTS_VAL. If the port is enabled, and if the number of discarded packets on this port in the last 60 seconds is greater than HAC_DISCPKTS_LIM the raw DISCPKTS condition is true for that port. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_DISCPKTS_OND and HAC_DISCPKTS_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM HAC is active. The result is reported as the DISCPKTS condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: Excessive packets discarded on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_DISCPKTS_PWA If historical data on packet discard rates for this switch is desired, users should configure continuous history recording on HAC_DISCPKTS_VAL. Per port history could be captured by configuring history collection on individual elements of HAC_DISCPKTS_PRT[x]. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_DISCPKTS_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_DISCPKTS_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_DISCPKTS_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_DISCPKTS_LIM Float 10 Configurable limit for packet discards on a port. HAC_DISCPKTS_VAL Float 0 Receives total number of packets discarded from all enabled ports in the last 60 seconds. HAC_DISCPKTS_PRT[ n ] Float Array 32 rows 1 column 0 For each enabled port, receives number of packets discarded in the last 60 seconds. 0 for disabled ports. Excessive Packet Collisions On Port If HAC_COLLIDES_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for: The list of all ports installed on the switch. Whether each port is enabled or disabled Information about packet collisions (including late collisions) in the last 60 seconds on each installed port. For each enabled port, the number of packet collisions in the last 60 seconds is written to the corresponding array element in HAC_COLLIDES_PRT[n]. 0 is written for ports that are disabled or not installed. The sum from all ports of the packet collisions in the last 60 seconds is written to HAC_COLLIDES_VAL. If the port is enabled, and if the number of packet collisions on this port in the last 60 seconds is greater than HAC_COLLIDES_LIM the raw COLLIDES condition is true for that port. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_COLLIDES_OND and HAC_COLLIDES_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the COLLIDES condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: Excessive packet collisions on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_COLLIDES_PWA If historical data on packet collision rates for this switch is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_COLLIDES_VAL. Per port history can be captured by configuring history collection on individual elements of HAC_COLLIDES_PRT[n]. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_COLLIDES_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_COLLIDES_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_COLLIDES_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_COLLIDES_LIM Float 10 Configurable limit for packet collisions on a port. HAC_COLLIDES_VAL Float 0 Receives total number of packet collisions from all enabled ports in the last 60 seconds. HAC_COLLIDES_PRT[ n ] Float Array 32 rows 1 column 0 For each enabled port, receives number of packet collisions in the last 60 seconds. 0 for disabled ports. High Link Utilization On Port If HAC_HIUTIL_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates for: The list of all ports installed on the switch. Whether each port is enabled or disabled Information about the link utilization in the last 30 seconds on each installed port. Note: Link utilization information is for inbound communication on the ports. It does not include outbound communication. For each enabled port, link utilization is written to the corresponding array element in HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[n]. 0 is written for ports that are disabled or not installed. The maximum value from all elements of HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[n] elements is written to HAC_HIUTIL_VAL. If the port is enabled and the link utilization on this port in the last 30 seconds is greater than HAC_HIUTIL_LIM the raw HIUTIL condition is true for that port. Note: A common utilization limit as a percent of port speed is applied to all ports (connected to controllers, workstations and other switches), making the condition detection most sensitive to high traffic levels on ports connected to DeltaV workstations. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_HIUTIL_OND and HAC_HIUTIL_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the HIUTIL condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: High link utilization on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_HIUTIL_PWA If historical data on link utilization for this switch is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_HIUTIL_VAL. Per port history can be captured by configuring history collection on individual elements of HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[n]. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_HIUTIL_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_HIUTIL_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_HIUTIL_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_HIUTIL_LIM Float 30 (percent) Configurable limit for packet link utilization on a port. HAC_HIUTIL_VAL Float 0 Receives the maximum link utilization value (0 to 100 in percent) from all enabled ports in the last 60 seconds. HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[ n ] Float Array 32 rows 1 column 0 For each enabled port, receives link utilization value (0 to 100 in percent) over the last 30 seconds. 0 for disabled ports. Locking Violation On Port When DeltaV Smart Switches are locked, ports with no communications activity are disabled. The other ports remain enabled, and the switch stores the MAC addresses of devices connected to these ports at the time the switch was locked. This is typically one MAC address for most ports and multiple MAC addresses for ports connected to other switches. While locked, the switch communicates only with the device (MAC address) stored for each port, blocking communications with any other device (MAC address). When the switch detects (and blocks) communications with any device other than the one stored for that port, it is considered a port locking violation. Switches also detect devices attempting to communicate on disabled ports. These are also considered port locking violations. Port locking violations indicate attempts to attach an unauthorized device, or replace an expected device with an unauthorized device using the enabled port. Multiple port locking violations could indicate that network cables were disconnected and inadvertently reconnected to different ports on a locked switch. If HAC_BLOCKING_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the switch for: The list of all ports installed on the switch. The switch lock status. Information about the presence of blocked communications in the last 60 seconds due to port locking (on enabled and disabled ports) If the switch is locked and one or more packets received on the (enabled or disabled) port in the last 60 seconds were blocked due to port locking the raw BLOCKING condition is true for that port. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_BLOCKING_OND and HAC_BLOCKING_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the BLOCKING condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: Port locking violation on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_BLOCKING_PWA In some cases, the removal of a violating device does not clear the information in the switch about the presence of the violating device. The switch module periodically commands the switch to clear information about (old) violating devices if the switch module is configured to detect port violations (HAC_BLOCKING_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3). Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_BLOCKING_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_BLOCKING_OND Float 0 On delay (seconds). HAC_BLOCKING_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). Switch Port Communications Status Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description LINK_STATUS_PRT[ n ] Float Array 0 For each enabled port, the link status value: 0 — link is down (idle) or not connected < 0 — the number of violating devices (blocked) (on a locked port) > 0 — the number of devices communicating through this port. Switch Management Password The HAC_MGINFO_* and HAC_MGINFOREM_* parameters are defined for the switch management password change reminder. For all the following parameters: The parameter category is either Configuration or Operating Restore parameter value after restart is false (unchecked) The "Allow named set changes for new instances" is false (unchecked), when applicable. The parameter filter is either Common Configuration or Advanced Configuration Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_MGINFOREM_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. If absent, a value of "(Ignored)" is assumed. HAC_MGINFOREM_LIM Float 0 Configurable limit for password reminder in days. Default of 0 means there is no reminder. Set value to >0 to create reminder. HAC_MGINFO_TM String empty The UTC time when the management password was last changed.

title: Hardware alarm messages
body_text: Hardware alarm messages There are four types of hardware alarms: Advisory (ADVISE_ALM), Failed (FAILED_ALM), Maintenance (MAINT_ALM), and Not Communicating (COMM_ALM). When a hardware condition occurs that triggers a hardware alarm, a message appears in one or more of the following places: The Message column of the Alarm Summary screen in DeltaV Operate A Hardware Alarms or Logic Solver faceplate The Condition Summary Viewer The Event Chronicle In the case of a hardware error that triggers a COMM_ALM alarm, the message Not Communicating appears in the alarm summary and faceplate. Because communications have been lost with that node, any previous hardware alarm messages for that node are replaced with the Not Communicating message and no hardware alarm messages appear in the Condition Summary Viewer. Some hardware alarm messages identify an I/O card by its type, as card_type Card. When the same alarm type (MAINT_ALM, for example) occurs for multiple condition, the condition listed is preceded with [MULT]. The condition listed is the last one that occurred; however, the date/time stamp listed is of the first condition. To see all currently active conditions for the [MULT] alarm, open the Condition Summary Viewer (from either the alarm faceplate or the right-click context menu of the alarm). Subtopics: Advisory (ADVISE_ALM) hardware alarms Failed (FAILED_ALM) hardware alarms Maintenance (MAINT_ALM) hardware alarms I/O card types Related information I/O card types

title: Hardware repairs and additions
body_text: Hardware repairs and additions The following sections provide information on how to install hardware peripherals on DeltaV systems. They also contain details about DeltaV equipment repair and warranty. Subtopics: Equipment repair Equipment additions

title: HART communication with the DeltaV system
main_heading: HART communication with the DeltaV system
body_text: HART communication with the DeltaV system The HART information is communicated digitally and is very helpful for device diagnostics. This information can be used in the DeltaV system to affect control strategy or to alert operators to a transmitter malfunction. The DeltaV system communicates with HART devices through the following channels: HART analog input HART analog output The HART analog input channel communicates the following values: Analog - raw 4 to 20 mA signal, Card and channel status are applied, no HART status is applied. Field value, in percent (FIELD_VAL_PCT) Hybrid - 4 to 20 mA signal, Card, Channel, and HART status are applied. Field value, in engineering units (HART_FIELD_VAL) HART Dynamic Variables - digital signal, Card, Channel, and HART status are applied. Primary Variable, in engineering units (HART_PV) Secondary Variable, in engineering units (HART_SV) Tertiary Variable, in engineering units (HART_TV) Fourth Variable, in engineering units (HART_FV) The HART analog output channel communicates the following values: Hybrid - 4 to 20 mA signal, Card, Channel, and HART status are applied. Field value, in engineering units (OUT) HART Dynamic Variables - digital signal, Card, Channel, and HART status are applied. Primary Variable, in engineering units (HART_PV) Secondary Variable, in engineering units (HART_SV) Tertiary Variable, in engineering units (HART_TV) Fourth Variable, in engineering units (HART_FV) HART Device Variables - digital signal, Card, Channel, and HART status are applied. Slot 0 device variable, in engineering units (HART DV SLOT0) Slot 1 device variable, in engineering units (HART DV SLOT1) Slot 2 device variable, in engineering units (HART DV SLOT2) Slot 3 device variable, in engineering units (HART DV SLOT3) Some multivariable devices have a predefined set of Dynamic Variables; in others, you can assign process values to the Dynamic Variables through an external device or application. Refer to the vendor's documentation for your HART device for specific information. Link initialization contains information on setting up the devices to communicate correctly with the DeltaV system. Related information Link initialization

title: HART devices and the DeltaV System
main_heading: HART devices and the DeltaV System
body_text: HART devices and the DeltaV System The DeltaV system provides the capability to interface to HART devices. This topic provides information about how HART devices communicate with the DeltaV system and how you can manage your device configuration through the use of device templates and definitions. Subtopics: HART communication with the DeltaV system HART device configuration HART device definitions HART device templates Scaling HART Values Smart Commissioning for HART devices HART error conditions for Classic I/O HART error conditions for CHARMs I/O Using HART error conditions for control strategy Link initialization Access AMS Device Manager

title: HART device configuration
body_text: HART device configuration A HART device configuration defines a specific device associated with a device tag. The configuration contains information about the device manufacturer, type and revision, as well as information about the device's alarms. You can view devices and their properties through the DeltaV Explorer Control Network and SIS Network. Related information Configuring device alarms

title: HART device definitions
body_text: HART device definitions DeltaV Explorer Library contains many device definitions. A device definition contains information for a specific HART device type and revision. The device definitions are available in the DeltaV Explorer under Library/HART Devices . When you autosense a HART device, the system attempts to match the device with a device definition in the library. If you want to use HART devices that are not part of the DeltaV install image, you can install a set of device description files on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. Refer to DeltaV Explorer help for information on how to use the Add Device Type command. If there is no definition available in the library for your device, you can also use the conventional manufacturer definition that most closely matches the function of the device. Conventional manufacturer definitions enable devices to be used in your control system but these devices many have limitations with regard to device alerts until a specific device definition is available. The conventional manufacturer definitions are available under the HART Devices in the DeltaV Explorer library. You cannot delete a HART device definition if your configuration includes a device that uses that definition.

title: HART device templates
body_text: HART device templates Device templates enable you to create device configurations for reuse. You can create a HART device template from a device description, another HART device template, or a device using the drag and drop feature in DeltaV Explorer. You modify the properties of the template and use it to create device configurations for your control system. Device templates are ideal for defining and creating multiple devices with the same configuration. Refer to DeltaV Explorer help for instructions on creating HART device templates.

title: SIS HART device proof testing
body_text: SIS HART device proof testing Proof testing HART device in a SIS system is an important function to keep the system operating correctly. The DeltaV software does not perform proof tests on HART devices, but does include some functionality to assist in scheduling proof tests. The DeltaV software contains several internal parameters that keep track of HART device proof tests. Parameter Name Parameter Writeable Description Test Interval DEV_PT_TIME Yes Number of days between proof tests. Reminder Interval DEV_PT_REMINDER Yes Number of days before proof test to send alert. Reset DEV_PT_RESET Yes Writing a value of 1 to this parameter sets the Time since parameter to zero. Time since DEV_PT_TIME_SINCE No Time elapsed since last reset. Last Test Time DEV_PT_LAST No Absolute time when the last proof test was run displayed in ISO 8601 format. This is set to Unknown after a full download and until the next proof test of the device is complete. The general order of events to configure and respond to proof test alerts is the following: Note: if you suppress device alarm conditions they remain suppressed until they are manually unsuppressed from the detail display. The suppressed conditions are not unsuppressed automatically even by the subsequent timeout and reset of the proof test and acknowledgment of proof test alarms. On the device's property dialog In DeltaV Explorer configure the device's proof test alert interval and proof test reminder alert. This sets the internal parameters DEV_PT_TIME and DV_PT_REMINDER respectively. Download the configuration. The absolute time of the last proof test (DEV_PT_LAST) is set on initial full download to Unknown until the next proof test for the device. The time since the last test (DV_PT_TIME_SINCE) is set to zero on initial full download. Both values are reset when the reset button on the device faceplate is clicked. The values of both parameters are preserved during subsequent partial downloads to preserve the proof test schedule. Operate the plant until the proof test reminder alarm condition becomes active. If the alarm condition contributes to a device alarm, acknowledge or suppress the alarm as desired. Perform the proof test on the device when plant operations allow. If you wait until the proof test alarm condition becomes active DeltaV software triggers a device alarm. DeltaV software does not perform the device proof test. Refer to the device manufacturer's documentation for the proof test procedures required for your use of the device. After you have completed the proof test, open the device faceplate and reset the days since the last test. The Days since last test field on the faceplate begins counting up from zero. If you have not done so previously, acknowledge the proof test alarm and reminder alarm to clear them.

title: HART error conditions for Classic I/O
main_heading: HART error conditions for Classic I/O
body_text: HART error conditions for Classic I/O HART field devices report internal self-test status information and indications of signal integrity. This information is sent in a status byte that is sent with each HART message. The error conditions affect the status associated with channel data, the channel integrity parameter (OINTEG), and the status text visible in the diagnostics application (STATUS).
