title: CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) SIS hardware overview
main_heading: CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) SIS hardware overview
body_text: CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) SIS hardware overview CSLS SIS hardware consists of: CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS) CSLS process LS CHARM signals and run the SIS modules that contain the safety system logic. Redundant CSLS can support up to 96 LS CHARMs. The maximum number of LS CHARMs (96) are organized in eight banks of 12 LS CHARMs. Each bank of 12 LS CHARMs is held by a CHARM Baseplate. CSLS mount on CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carriers and connect to the Local Safety Network through connectors on the carriers. SZ Controllers SZ Controllers mount on either the SZ Controller Carrier or the Dual Universal Safety Carrier and connect to the Area Control Network and the Local Safety Network through ports on the carrier. SZ Controllers isolate CSLS from the rest of the system. SZ controllers receive redundant 24 VDC input through the carrier. Redundant Modbus TCP ports on the carrier enable an SZ controller to support standalone SIS installations. Local Safety Network Bridges Local Safety Network Bridges (LSNB) connect Local Safety Networks under different SZ Controllers so that secure parameters can be passed between CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers on different Local Safety Networks. Local Safety Network Bridges mount on Dual Universal Safety Carriers that house redundant connections to the Local Safety Network and to the Global Safety Network . CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carriers CSLS Carriers are vertical DIN rail-mounted carriers that hold redundant CSLS and Power Modules. The CSLS Carrier provides 24 VDC input to the CSLS and to the Power Modules. The Power Modules provide 6.3 VDC to the LS CHARMs. The CSLS Carrier houses primary and secondary Safety Network Ports for connections to the Local Safety Network and a keylock switch that restricts how and when the CSLS can be unlocked for downloads and upgrades. Dual Universal Safety Carriers Dual Universal Safety Carriers are horizontal DIN rail-mounted carriers that hold redundant Local Safety Network Bridges or SZ Controllers. The Dual Universal Safety Carrier houses primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports for connections to the Global Safety Network and Local Safety Network when used with Local Safety Network Bridges and connections to the DeltaV Area Control Network and the Local Safety Network when used with SZ Controllers. SZ Controller Carriers SZ Controller Carriers are vertical DIN rail-mounted carriers that hold redundant SZ Controllers. The SZ Controller Carrier houses primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports for connections to the DeltaV Area Control Network and to the Local Safety Network. Baseplates CHARM Baseplates hold Logic Solver CHARMs (LS CHARMs) and I.S. Baseplates hold LS Intrinsically Safe CHARMs. The baseplates connect to the CSLS Carrier and to other baseplates through connectors on the baseplates. Each baseplate holds up to 12 terminal blocks that hold LS CHARMs, and an Address Plug that determines the address of the baseplate and the CHARMs installed on the baseplate. Logic Solver (LS) CHARMs LS CHARMs are single I/O channels that plug into the CHARM Terminal Blocks on the CHARM Baseplate. The DeltaV system supports analog input, discrete input, discrete output (including LS DO redundant DTA and LS DO redundant ETA CHARMs), LS DVC HART simplex and redundant DTA, LS power output, LS thermocouple input, LS RTD / Resistance Input, and LS voltage CHARMs as well as LS Intrinsically Safe analog input, discrete input, RTD/ Resistance input, and Thermocouple / mV input CHARMs.

title: CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) SIS hardware overview
main_heading: CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) SIS hardware overview
body_text: CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) SIS hardware overview CSLS SIS hardware consists of: CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS) CSLS process LS CHARM signals and run the SIS modules that contain the safety system logic. Redundant CSLS can support up to 96 LS CHARMs. The maximum number of LS CHARMs (96) are organized in eight banks of 12 LS CHARMs. Each bank of 12 LS CHARMs is held by a CHARM Baseplate. CSLS mount on CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carriers and connect to the Local Safety Network through connectors on the carriers. SZ Controllers SZ Controllers mount on either the SZ Controller Carrier or the Dual Universal Safety Carrier and connect to the Area Control Network and the Local Safety Network through ports on the carrier. SZ Controllers isolate CSLS from the rest of the system. SZ controllers receive redundant 24 VDC input through the carrier. Redundant Modbus TCP ports on the carrier enable an SZ controller to support standalone SIS installations. Local Safety Network Bridges Local Safety Network Bridges (LSNB) connect Local Safety Networks under different SZ Controllers so that secure parameters can be passed between CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers on different Local Safety Networks. Local Safety Network Bridges mount on Dual Universal Safety Carriers that house redundant connections to the Local Safety Network and to the Global Safety Network . CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carriers CSLS Carriers are vertical DIN rail-mounted carriers that hold redundant CSLS and Power Modules. The CSLS Carrier provides 24 VDC input to the CSLS and to the Power Modules. The Power Modules provide 6.3 VDC to the LS CHARMs. The CSLS Carrier houses primary and secondary Safety Network Ports for connections to the Local Safety Network and a keylock switch that restricts how and when the CSLS can be unlocked for downloads and upgrades. Dual Universal Safety Carriers Dual Universal Safety Carriers are horizontal DIN rail-mounted carriers that hold redundant Local Safety Network Bridges or SZ Controllers. The Dual Universal Safety Carrier houses primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports for connections to the Global Safety Network and Local Safety Network when used with Local Safety Network Bridges and connections to the DeltaV Area Control Network and the Local Safety Network when used with SZ Controllers. SZ Controller Carriers SZ Controller Carriers are vertical DIN rail-mounted carriers that hold redundant SZ Controllers. The SZ Controller Carrier houses primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports for connections to the DeltaV Area Control Network and to the Local Safety Network. Baseplates CHARM Baseplates hold Logic Solver CHARMs (LS CHARMs) and I.S. Baseplates hold LS Intrinsically Safe CHARMs. The baseplates connect to the CSLS Carrier and to other baseplates through connectors on the baseplates. Each baseplate holds up to 12 terminal blocks that hold LS CHARMs, and an Address Plug that determines the address of the baseplate and the CHARMs installed on the baseplate. Logic Solver (LS) CHARMs LS CHARMs are single I/O channels that plug into the CHARM Terminal Blocks on the CHARM Baseplate. The DeltaV system supports analog input, discrete input, discrete output (including LS DO redundant DTA and LS DO redundant ETA CHARMs), LS DVC HART simplex and redundant DTA, LS power output, LS thermocouple input, LS RTD / Resistance Input, and LS voltage CHARMs as well as LS Intrinsically Safe analog input, discrete input, RTD/ Resistance input, and Thermocouple / mV input CHARMs.

title: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains
body_text: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains As SLS 1508 SIS applications grow larger, your configuration may need to span across multiple DeltaV SIS nodes. SIS Network rings and multiple SIS Network domains provide this capability. The following table contains some terminology used in the remainder of SIS Network domain documentation. SLS 1508 terms and definitions Term Meaning node The DeltaV I/O Interface Carrier and Logic Solver cards. SIS Local Peer Bus A two-channel bus within the DeltaV I/O Interface Carrier. SISNet Repeater The device that connects a DeltaV I/O Interface Carrier to another DeltaV I/O Interface Carrier using fiber optic cables. The repeater collects data from Logic Solvers on its node and forwards it around the fiber optic ring. The repeater also takes data off the ring and forwards it to the Logic Solvers on its node. Redundant Remote Peer Bus (SIS Network ring) A fiber optic ring that connects DeltaV SIS nodes through SISNet Repeaters. The ring allows Logic Solvers on different nodes to share Secure Parameter data. A DeltaV SIS installation can contain one or more SIS Network rings. You can configure one or more SIS Network domains in a SIS Network ring. functional group A set of Logic Solvers used for a single purpose. For example, controlling a single boiler. You define the functional groups in your installation. The DeltaV software does not indicate functional groups within the DeltaV system. SIS Network domain A collection of Logic Solvers configured in DeltaV Explorer that can share domain global variables. A SIS Network domain can contain multiple functional groups. Logic Solvers that communicate with each other within a domain must be on the same SIS Network ring. A DeltaV SIS system can have 15 SIS Network domains. Secure Parameter This is a Boolean with Status value published by a Logic Solver that can be referenced by another Logic Solver. Local Publisher By default, all Logic Solvers are Local Publishers on their node. That is, any Logic Solver module can reference a secure parameter published by any Logic Solver on the same node. Domain Global Publisher A Logic Solver whose Secure Parameters can be referenced by another Logic Solver on a different node within the same SIS Network domain, if the Logic Solvers are on the same SIS Network ring. Logic Solvers that are in a different domain cannot reference parameters published by a Domain Global Publisher in another domain even if they are on the same SIS Network ring. Each SIS Network domain can have as many as 32 Logic Solvers configured as Domain Global Publishers. SIS Network bridge An Ethernet connection between two SISNet Repeaters in different SIS Network rings. System Global Publisher A Logic Solver whose Secure Parameters can be seen by all Logic Solvers in the SIS Network independent of which SIS Network domain they are in. System Global data is sent on the SIS Local Peer Bus, the SIS Network ring, and over the SIS Network bridges to other rings. System Global data is forwarded only from one ring to another so two rings that share data must be connected by a single SIS Network bridge. The entire SIS Network can contain as many as 16 Logic Solvers configured as System Global Publishers. The following sections show three different ways SIS Network domains and SIS Network rings can be implemented. There are certainly several other ways to configure domains and SIS Network rings, but these three layouts are the most likely you will need. The figures are for illustration only and are not intended to be example configurations. The SIS networks shown are greatly simplified. Actual SIS networks can be much larger. Using SIS Network domains provides flexibility when configuring large SIS networks. Each domain can have 32 Logic Solvers configured as Domain Global Publishers. That is, any Logic Solver within the domain can potentially receive secure parameter data from these global publishers (subject to the conditions listed below). In addition, the entire DeltaV SIS Network can have 16 Logic Solvers defined as System Global Publishers. Any Logic Solver in the SIS Network can potentially receive secure parameter data from these system global publishers (again, subject to the conditions listed below). There must be a physical path between the Logic Solver publishing a secure parameter and the Logic Solver referencing the secure parameter. This path required depends on the publisher type: Local Publisher — All Logic Solvers publish locally on the DeltaV SIS node. Both the publisher and the referencing Logic Solvers must reside on the same DeltaV SIS node. Domain Global Publisher — Both publishing and referencing Logic Solvers must be on the same DeltaV SIS node or on different nodes connected by SISNet Repeaters on a SIS Network ring. The nodes containing the publishing and referencing Logic Solvers must be in the same SIS Network domain. System Global Publisher — Both Logic Solvers must be on the same node, or connected by SISNet Repeaters on a SIS Network ring, or in separate SIS Network rings connected by a single SIS Network bridge connection. The physical layout you decide to use will depend on the physical layout of your plant (cable runs for fiber optic cable, for example) and process requirements (the possible need to shut down the hardware in one domain without affecting other domains, for example). There are certainly several ways to configure domains and SIS Network rings, but these three layouts are the most likely you will need. Your SIS Network configuration will depend on the physical layout of your plant and your process requirements. Subtopics: Single SLS 1508 SIS Network ring, single domain Single SLS 1508 SIS Network ring, multiple domains Multiple SLS 1508 SIS Network rings, multiple domains SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Explorer

title: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Diagnostics
main_heading: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Diagnostics
body_text: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Diagnostics The following figure shows how the SIS Network portion of the example layout appears in the left pane of DeltaV Diagnostics. The SIS Network of the Example Layout in DeltaV Diagnostics DOMAIN_1 is shown fully expanded, except for the logic solvers. DOMAIN_2 and DOMAIN_3 are shown collapsed. The structure not shown in these domains is very similar to that of DOMAIN_1. The physical rings do not appear in the hierarchy, but SISNet Repeaters associated with controllers appear. SISNet Repeaters are always named REPEATER01 and REPEATER02. You cannot rename them. REPEATER01 is the primary (left hand) repeater and REPEATER02 is the secondary (right hand) repeater. Each SIS Network domain folder contains the folders Logic Solvers and Repeaters. As you select items in the hierarchy, diagnostic parameters and values for the item appear in the right pane. Many items in the SIS Network hierarchy have a context menu. The options on the menu depend on the item selected. The UNDEFINED domain contains SISNet Repeaters that are not assigned to a domain. Repeaters can appear in UNDEFINED if their controllers are not downloaded or if there are no commissioned Logic Solvers. Duplicate Global Publishers It is unlikely but possible under some circumstances for two different Logic Solvers that are configured as Global Publisher to be assigned to the same System Global slot. This is not allowed and is reported in the Diagnostics as follows: The MaintAlerts parameter on both Logic Solver reports SISNet Error. The P2PStatus on both Logic Solver cards reports Duplicate Global Publisher Detected. All Secure Parameter references to the affected Logic Solvers have a status of BadConfigErr until the issue is corrected. Two ways in which these errors can appear are: Two DeltaV SIS systems exist in a plant. Some of the logic solvers in each system are configured as global publishers. The fiber optic rings of the two DeltaV systems are inadvertently connected resulting in duplicate global publisher slots assigned. The standby logic solver of a redundant pair is powered down and the primary logic solver's configuration is changed to clear the Publish secure parameters globally check box. Another logic solver in the system is configured as a global publisher and it is assigned the slot that the redundant pair's primary logic solver had been assigned. At some later time the primary logic solver is powered down and the standby is powered back up with old configuration resulting in two logic solvers assigned the same global slot. There may be other ways this can occur. If the MaintAlerts and P2PStatus errors listed above appear, correct your configuration as required. To further diagnose the SIS Network, open the Repeater Connection List from the SIS Network context menu.

title: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Explorer
body_text: SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Explorer In DeltaV SIS networks, Logic Solvers are configured in SIS Network domains. These are not physical groupings, but there will usually be some correspondence between SIS Network domains and SIS Network rings. By default, the SIS Network contains one SIS Network domain that cannot be deleted (it can be renamed). You can create an additional 14 domains. Nothing in the DeltaV Explorer view of SIS Network domains indicates anything about the physical connections between Logic Solvers or domains. Because publishing and referencing of secure parameters depends on physical connections between Logic Solvers, you must know the physical connections between Logic Solvers before you can configure SIS Network domains and your safety logic. The following figure shows how two SIS Network domains under the SIS Network, BOILER1 and BOILER2, appear in DeltaV Explorer. SIS Network domain Configuration Example Logic Solvers in SIS Network domain folders are associated on a one to one correspondence with Logic Solver cards on DeltaV I/O Interface Carriers. For example, Logic Solver SLS1 is associated with the Logic Solver card in controller CTLR1 in card slot C01. After one Logic Solver card on a node has been associated with a SIS Network domain, none of the other Logic Solver cards on that node can be associated with another SIS Network domain.

title: SIS alarm types
body_text: SIS alarm types Plant areas, alarm priorities, alarm types, and alarm states all affect the way the system manages individual alarms. Understanding these concepts is key to developing a good system alarm strategy. An SIS alarm type defines a set of characteristics that determines how an alarm appears on displays, in the SIS alarm banner and in the Process History View. Each alarm used in an SIS module must be associated with an SIS alarm type. You can assign a single alarm type to several alarms to give the alarms the same display characteristics. The DeltaV system provides several predefined SIS alarm types. The SIS alarm types are uniquely identified to separate them from the non-SIS DeltaV alarm types. This separation provides a mechanism for displaying, recording and managing SIS alarms apart from all other DeltaV alarms. For example, in Process History View, the SIS alarms are identified as the Event Type, SIS_ALARM. However, all other aspects of alarm configuration (priority, sounds, logging, and so on) are the same as a non-SIS DeltaV system. Note: SIS alarms share alarm priority definitions with DeltaV alarms. Only a user with the Configure key can create, modify, and delete alarm priority definitions, giving process engineers a way to tailor alarm behavior to plant conditions. You can use the predefined SIS alarm types as they are, modify them, or create additional types. DeltaV SIS alarms must be created in the DeltaV SIS Alarm Types category of DeltaV Explorer under System Configuration\Setup\Alarm Preferences\SIS Alarm Types. An example of needing a new alarm type is when an alarm requires a message that is different from the available alarm type messages. Note: Alarm type names are case sensitive. Additionally, alarm types must exist in the DeltaV system before you can assign an alarm using that alarm type to a module. Subtopics: Alarm type properties Related information Alarms and events

title: SIS alarm groups
body_text: SIS alarm groups SIS alarm groups help you identify alarms associated with either physical devices or logical elements within a single module. You can create several alarm groups for a module and assign the blocks and user-defined parameters within the module to an appropriate alarm group. For example, you might create an alarm group that includes all the function blocks associated with a voter (such as an analog voter block and its analog input blocks). You might also create a different alarm group for all the function blocks associated with a valve (for example, a discrete output block for the solenoid and a DVC block for the positioner). For each alarm group, you specify a set of displays (primary control, detail and faceplate). Both the CSLS and SLS1508 support alarm groups. Related information Configure SIS alarm groups

title: SIS Alarm List display
body_text: SIS Alarm List display The SIS Alarm List display contains unacknowledged or suppressed (either shelved, out of service or both) SIS-related alarms. SIS-related alarms include SIS module alarms, Logic Solver hardware alarms, and HART device alarms for devices connected to a Logic Solver. Access the SIS Alarm List from the button on the toolbar window in the DeltaV operator workspace. The button is visible when there is at least one active, unacknowledged or suppressed SIS-related alarm. The SIS Alarm List display has two alarm lists, one for active SIS-related alarms and one for suppressed SIS-related alarms. In addition to appearing on this display, SIS-related alarms also appear on the standard Alarm List display and the standard Suppressed Alarm display. The following shows an example of the SIS Alarm List picture in run mode. This picture shows the total number of active alarms, the number of unacknowledged and suppressed alarms for the current area, and lists active alarms by: Ack - the acknowledged status. Time In - the time at which the alarm went active. If the alarm is active when a controller switchover occurs, the alarm is regenerated with a new Time Last value. The value of Time In is maintained. Unit - the name of the unit that owns the module that is in alarm. Module/Parameter - the name of the SIS module that contains the alarm and the active alarm. Description - a description of the module. Alarm - the alarm word for this alarm. Message - a message associated with the alarm. The format of the alarm message is determined by the alarm type. Priority - a word, such as Critical, Warning, Advisory, or any user-configured priority that indicates the importance of an event to the operator and the priority of the alarm at the workstation. The priority affects the order in which the alarm appears in this picture and in the Alarm Banner.

title: Common DeltaV SIS system information
body_text: Common DeltaV SIS system information This section of the document contains information that is mostly identical for both SLS 1508 and CHARMs Smart Logic Solver SIS systems. There may be some information which is slightly different between the two systems. Those differences are explicitly noted within the text.

title: SIS Composite Blocks
body_text: SIS Composite Blocks The only valid SIS composite block type is embedded. Linked composites are not supported. From Control Studio you can create templates for SIS composites in the library for reuse or you can create individual SIS composites while editing an SIS module. You can protect templates to prevent unauthorized changes to the logic of embedded composites. Because SIS composites are embedded, an embedded composite does not change if you subsequently modify the template it was created from. The embedded composites are separate, standalone blocks. Use composite blocks to encapsulate portions of logic that are used multiple times in a configuration. SIS composite blocks cannot be nested and can contain only SIS function blocks and items from the Special Items palette. Subtopics: SIS composite strategy SIS composite definitions Create an SIS composite template Add an SIS composite to a module

title: SIS composite block
body_text: SIS composite block Use an SIS composite block to hold an algorithm, or a portion of an algorithm, that you want to use multiple times. You can think of a composite block as a subroutine that you can call more than once. You specify the number of inputs and outputs and define the algorithm for the composite. SIS composite blocks can contain only SIS function blocks and items from the SIS Special Items palette. You cannot nest SIS composite blocks.

title: SIS composite blocks
body_text: SIS composite blocks DeltaV SIS composite blocks can contain DeltaV SIS function blocks and user-defined parameters. Nesting is not allowed. Composite block execution is synchronous with other function blocks in the module. DeltaV SIS Composite blocks are always embedded and not linked. An embedded composite does not change if you modify the template you used to create the block. Embedded blocks are separate, standalone blocks. If you edit the structure of an embedded block, other copies of the composite block remain unchanged. You cannot associate alarm definitions with a composite. You can assign a composite to an alarm group. When you assign a composite to an alarm group, the system assigns all the components in the composite to the same alarm group. If you are creating objects for reuse and want to save alarm definitions with the objects, you must create module templates.

title: SIS composite definitions
body_text: SIS composite definitions Connect multiple function blocks to form a composite block. If you create an SIS composite template in the Library you can reuse it multiple times. You can also create individual composite blocks using the Composite Block assistant in the Special Items palette. You cannot copy or reuse composite blocks created with the Composite Block assistant. After you put a composite block in a function block diagram, you can view the composite block in the diagram and drill down in the composite to see and modify its structure. You can also step into a composite block when you are viewing a downloaded module online. Like in any diagram within the DeltaV system, you can edit the parameter information when in the online view unless the composite was created from a protected template. Because all SIS composites are embedded, an exact copy of the library composite is made and placed within the module. From that point forward, all links back to the original library composite are broken.

title: SIS composite strategy
body_text: SIS composite strategy There are several ways that composites help to create SIS modules. In addition to their manageability, composites can perform the following functions: improve readability of a large SIS module by allowing you to group the elements into logical tasks allow SIS logic to be reused provide a mechanism to develop SIS logic segments one time, store them in the library, maintain them in a single location, and still use that logic in a number of different modules In addition, SIS Composite Templates can be protected to prevent unauthorized modification after they are in use. Related information Protected SIS composite templates

title: SIS Composite template run-time behavior
body_text: SIS Composite template run-time behavior Online parameter changes to internal parameters of Embedded Composites created from protected SIS Composite Templates are not allowed, either by secure writes or Calculation/Logic block writes. A Calculation/Logic block within a protected composite can write to parameters within that protected composite. Writes are not allowed to protected parameters or parameters of a block within a protected composite. If a user attempts to write a value an error message appears. If a Calc block attempts the write, the Output Failure bit in the Calc blocks BLOCK_ERR parameter is set. If users need to change parameter values of a block within a protected SIS Composite Template from DeltaV Operate, promote the parameters to composite-level parameters. Make sure the input parameters are included in SIS Parameter Security and assigned an appropriate lock or change the default lock for SIS parameters. Use the SIS Data Entry Expert to create DeltaV Operate objects so users can change composite block values.

title: DeltaV SIS configuration
body_text: DeltaV SIS configuration The configuration for both SLS 1508 SIS systems and CSLS SIS systems is similar. Use DeltaV Explorer to create the hierarchy of system components and use Control Studio to create the safety logic. In a DeltaV SIS system, safety instrumented functions are implemented in SIS modules that run in SLS 1508 Logic Solvers or CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers. The number of modules a logic solver can run depends on the type. SIS modules communicate through secure parameters and secure parameter references. This is true whether the communicating modules are in the same logic solver or in different logic solvers. The modules in all logic solvers on a node can reference a secure parameter configured in any module in any logic solver on the same node.

title: SIS Controller configuration
body_text: SIS Controller configuration DeltaV SIS Controllers appear in DeltaV Explorer under the Control Network. DeltaV SIS Controller (SISCTLR1) in DeltaV Explorer With the exception that SIS Controllers do not support local I/O, SIS Controllers have the same properties as other DeltaV controllers, including redundancy. The Assigned Modules subsystem supports the same options as the DeltaV Controller except the only module type that can be added is a control module or template. Class-based and classless unit and equipment modules as well as phase logic modules are not supported. The Assigned I/O subsystem holds the remote I/O assignments from CIOCs and Zone1/Zone2 Remote I/O . The Assigned Wireless I/O subsystem holds the I/O assignments from WIOCs and wireless gateways .

title: SIS Controller Modbus port
body_text: SIS Controller Modbus port For standalone safety systems, the DeltaV SIS controller can communicate to a third-party control system through Modbus TCP with the DeltaV SIS controller acting as a slave device. The DeltaV SIS controller supports both simplex and redundant Modbus communication. For simplex mode, connect one of the top ports of the DeltaV SIS controller to the DeltaV ACN and the other top port to the Modbus master. You must also enable network redundancy for the controller. To enable redundancy, check the Enable network redundancy for this node check box on the SIS Controller properties dialog. For redundant Modbus communication, connect the top ports of the DeltaV SIS controller to the Modbus master and to the DeltaV ACN. On a SIS standalone system, the DeltaV ACN enables connectivity to the SIS engineering station (a DeltaV ProfessionalPLUS station). The top ports on the SIS controller handle DeltaV communications and Modbus simultaneously using different IP addresses for Modbus communication. Configure the IP address for Modbus TCP through the Modbus Port Properties dialog. You also define Modbus TCP registers and mappings through this dialog. The figure below shows an example system. Connections to third-party control system through Modbus TCP The following table shows the register types and their data types and the number of values and register addresses that can be configured. Modbus Port data configuration Register type Data type Description Number of values Base register address (read-only and fixed) coil Boolean For discrete output parameter read/writes 0 to 1000 R1 input status Boolean For discrete input and status parameter reads 0 to 1000 R10001 float input floating point Floating point for analog input parameter reads 0 to 3000 R30001 integer input 8- or 16-bit unsigned Integer for integer value input parameter reads 0 to 3999 (restricted by the last register being 39999) R36001 float holding floating point Floating point for analog parameters 0 to 3000 R40001 integer holding 8- or 16-bit unsigned Integer for integer value parameters 0 to 3999 (restricted by the last register being 49999) R46001 Note: There is only one data set for each register type and the data set must be sized large enough for registers of that type that will be used. The register offset is always 0. Each data set starts at the base address for that register type. You can map parameters to Modbus port registers from the Register mapping and Map Register dialogs. However, because of the possible large number of parameters to map, using Bulk Edit is easier for initial configuration. Only function block and module parameters can be mapped. There is one mapping table for the SIS Controller. Supported Modbus TCP Function commands The following function codes are supported from the Modbus interface. Function commands Description 1 Read multiple coils (1 bit per coil) 2 Read multiple input statuses (1 bit per status) 3 Read holding registers 4 Read multiple input registers (2 bytes per register) 5 Write single coil (0x0000 = OFF, 0xFF00 = ON) 6 Write single holding register (2 bytes) 15 Write multiple coils (1 bit per coil) 16 Write multiple holding registers (2 bytes per register) Subtopics: SIS Controller Modbus port write support Related information Bulk edit SIS Controller Modbus Port register mapping Configure SIS Controller Modbus port Data set mapping Modbus register ranges

title: SIS module and function block custom faceplates
main_heading: SIS module and function block custom faceplates
body_text: SIS module and function block custom faceplates The procedure for creating custom faceplates for SIS modules is similar to that for creating custom faceplates for DeltaV modules. To open the SIS module faceplate template, double-click SIS_Faceplate template in the Templates folder. SIS module faceplates are opened in run mode using the alarm banner or the Open Faceplate toolbar button. The SIS_ faceplate template consists of an empty main display area, a "close picture" button, a pushpin button, the SIS module tag and description, and command buttons. The pushpin button appears when multiple faceplate capability has been enabled in UserSettings.grf. When multiple monitor capability has been enabled, a display selector appears to the right of the pushpin. The command buttons from left to right include "open detail display," "open control display," "open CSOnline," "open PHV," and "Ack All Alarms." The procedure for creating custom faceplates for SIS function blocks is similar to that for creating custom faceplates for DeltaV function blocks. for more information. For SIS function blocks, use the Any_SIS_Block dynamo in the dynamo set named frsSIS on the display. To open the SIS module faceplate template, double-click SIS_FaceplateFB template in the Templates folder. The SIS_FaceplateFB template consists of an empty main display area, a "close picture" button, a pushpin button, an "open module faceplate" button, and the function block path. The pushpin button appears when multiple faceplate capability has been enabled in UserSettings.grf. When multiple monitor capability has been enabled, a display selector appears to the right of the pushpin. Note: Any writeable datalinks on the custom faceplates must be added using the SIS Data Entry Expert. Related information Create new faceplates and detail displays for modules Create new faceplates and detail displays for function blocks The Secure Write Mechanism

title: The SIS Data Entry Expert
body_text: The SIS Data Entry Expert DeltaV Operate uses the secure write mechanism for all changes to parameters in SIS modules. You can create writeable datalinks using the SIS Data Entry Expert. The button for the SIS Data Entry Expert is on the DeltaV Operating Experts toolbar; it is similar to the button for the DeltaV Data Entry Expert, but it has a yellow background. The SIS Data Entry Expert creates one of three graphical objects: labeled button, toggle value, and write value (numeric) datalink. To create an SIS datalink, click the SIS Data Entry Expert to open the configuration dialog, which is shown below. Use the dialog to configure the data source and appearance of the data on the picture. The dialog has three tabs (Labeled Button, Toggle Value, and Write Value) that are described further in this topic. If any non-SIS object is selected when the SIS Data Entry Expert is invoked, only the Write Value tab is available; if an SIS object is selected, the appropriate tab is made available and the two others are disabled. Subtopics: Configure Labeled Button tab Configure Toggle Value tab Configure Write Value tab

title: Diagnose SLS 1508 SIS systems
body_text: Diagnose SLS 1508 SIS systems Use DeltaV Diagnostics to diagnose and view status for SIS Network domains, Logic Solvers, Logic Solver cards and channels, SISNet Repeaters, and assigned SIS modules. The SIS Network in the left pane of the Diagnostics application contains the Domains, Logic Solvers, Logic Solver I/O, Assigned SIS Modules, and SISNet Repeaters. Select an item under the SIS Network in the left pane and view diagnostic and status parameters for that item in the right pane. Use a parameter's help for more information on the parameter. Context menu commands are available for most items in the SIS Network. Access the context menu commands by selecting an item and clicking the right-mouse button. Related information SLS 1508 SIS diagnostics DeltaV Diagnostics

title: SLS 1508 SIS diagnostics
body_text: SLS 1508 SIS diagnostics Use DeltaV Diagnostics to view status information for SIS Network domains, Logic Solvers, Logic Solver cards and channels, SISNet Repeaters, and assigned SIS modules. The SIS Network in the left pane of the Diagnostics application contains the Domains, Logic Solvers, Logic Solver I/O, Assigned SIS Modules, and SISNet Repeaters. Diagnostics for the SIS Network is similar to diagnostics for the control network. However, there are some additional tools available to diagnose SIS Network domains and physical rings. Most of this section explores an example SIS installation, starting with the physical layout, progressing through the configuration in DeltaV Explorer, and ending with an examination of the installation in DeltaV Diagnostics. Note: This section uses the convention of describing communication in the SIS Network as if it were between controllers instead of repeaters, logic solvers, or SIS modules. Subtopics: SLS 1508 example SIS Network physical layout SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Explorer SLS 1508 SIS Network domains in DeltaV Diagnostics SLS 1508 Repeater Connection List Diagnose SLS 1508 SISNet Repeater connection problems Logic solver diagnostic parameters Related information DeltaV Diagnostics SLS 1508 SIS Network domains

title: SLS 1508 Logic Solver downloads
body_text: SLS 1508 Logic Solver downloads Note: Downloading a logic solver may result in a value and/or status change of non-secure parameters. The effect on production depends on what the references for the non-secure parameters are used for. Initiate a Logic Solver download from the Logic Solver under SIS Network. Downloading a Logic Solver sends the configuration information from this Logic Solver to the Logic Solver card (physical or simulated) that the Logic Solver is assigned to. All downloads to a Logic Solver are total downloads. Partial downloads are not allowed. A Logic Solver card cannot be downloaded independent of the Logic Solver. You can download a Logic Solver only by selecting it under the SIS Network. You cannot download multiple Logic Solvers at the same time. The steps to download are the same whether the Logic Solver is assigned to a physical Logic Solver card or to the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. Downloads to Logic Solvers are matching downloads. Values of certain parameters are preserved on download to prevent process disruptions. The download states for Logic Solvers differ from other DeltaV system downloadable items in the following ways: Blue triangle - The configuration has changed from the configuration currently in the Logic Solver. Note that blue triangles on Logic Solvers do not roll up to the SIS Network because you cannot download the SIS Network. You can only download individual Logic Solvers. Yellow triangle overlay - The Logic Solver does not have a configuration.

title: SIS function block dynamos
body_text: SIS function block dynamos In DeltaV Operate configure mode, the SIS dynamos are available and visible regardless of whether or not SIS has been enabled as a system preference. The frsSIS dynamo sets, named frsSIS and frsSIS_Theme, are in the Dynamo Sets folder. Some of the SIS function blocks have multiple dynamos from which to choose. The dynamos are textual in nature and are designed for use on a picture depicting a single SIS interlock (one or more SIS modules that include safety instrumented functions, SIFs, with common final elements). SIS dynamos are not meant for SIS blocks that are inside a composite block. After an SIS function block dynamo has been created on a picture, it cannot be edited. The frsSIS_Theme dynamo set uses a color set that is themed to a color palette (Silver) to help you coordinate the use of colors on your graphic. The frsSIS_Theme dynamo set has slightly different behavior from the frsSIS dynamo set. title: Expressions in DeltaV SIS Software
body_text: Expressions in DeltaV SIS Software The Logic Solver is capable of executing Structured Text Language expressions. Expressions represent calculations and logic and have a specific syntax. Expressions for the Logic Solver are created in the Logic Solver Calculation/Logic (LSCALC) function block. To facilitate the writing of expressions, use the Expression Editor. For specific help on using the Expression Editor, click on the help button in the Expression Editor dialog. CAUTION: When writing expressions using an external editor, only use a plain ASCII text editor (Notepad is recommended). Using other editors can cause the expression to change during the load and save process. The expression functionality of the Logic Solver is a subset of the capabilities that are available in the DeltaV controller. The following functions and features are not supported in expressions in the Logic Solver: References to I/O DSTs References to external parameters (outside the module containing the LSCALC block) Writing to an OUT parameter of another LSCALC block Reading or writing .CST and .AWST fields for any parameter String functions Array declarations Looping constructs While-Do-End_While Goto Label Exit Subtopics: Syntax Rules in Logic Solver Expressions Variables in Logic Solver Expressions Operands in Logic Solver Expressions Constants in Logic Solver Expression Operators in Logic Solver Expression Functions in Logic Solver Expressions Comments in Logic Solver Expressions

title: SIS HART device detail display
body_text: SIS HART device detail display The DeltaV System provides detail displays for HART devices connected to a Logic Solver. These detail displays enable you to view and manage HART device alarms. HART devices that use standard status information for their alarms use SIS_HARTGENERIC_DT. Some Emerson HART devices have device-specific detail displays. Subtopics: Generic SIS HART device alarm detail display (SIS_HARTGENERIC_DT) Device-specific SIS HART device alarm detail display

title: SIS HART device faceplate
body_text: SIS HART device faceplate The SIS HART Device faceplate, SIS_HARTDEV_fp contains active and suppressed alarm lists. The following shows an example of the SIS HART Device faceplate in run mode. You can open the SIS HART Device faceplate in DeltaV Operate run mode by clicking a HART Device alarm button in the Alarm Banner or by clicking the Device Faceplate button on the Toolbar and typing the HART Device tag. The following items are contained in the SIS HART Device faceplate: Active or unacknowledged alarms – Contains the currently active or unacknowledged alarms along with the alarm message and an indicator that shows if the alarm has been acknowledged. You can right-click on an alarm to acknowledge or suppress it. Suppressed Alarms list – Contains the alarms that are currently suppressed (either shelved, out of service or both) along with the time they were suppressed. You can right-click on an alarm to unshelve it or restore it to service. Configured module faceplate button – Opens the module configured for this faceplate's area association. (Configured in DeltaV Explorer, in the SIS HART Device Properties dialog/ Alarms and Displays tab.) Proof Test area – Contains the following fields and controls: Test interval (days): The configured number of days between scheduled proof tests. Days since last test: The number of days since the last test was performed. Click here to reset time since last test button: resets the Days since last test counter and the internal parameter that contains the absolute time of the last proof test. title: SIS input parameter
body_text: SIS input parameter Input parameters are available only in composite templates and composite blocks. Input parameters appear automatically as input connectors when you create a composite block. The input parameter provides an input connection that allows you to bring in signals from other modules or from the field. An Input Parameter can be one of the following types: Floating point with status — a floating point value with a status indicator. Boolean with status — a True or False value with status indicator. 32-bit unsigned integer with status — a whole number without a positive or negative sign associated with it with a status indicator. Named Set — a value from 0 to 255 that displays an assigned text message. When you create this parameter you configure whether its characteristic is Restore parameter value after restart or Preserve parameter value on download .

title: SIS internal read parameter
body_text: SIS internal read parameter An Internal Read Parameter provides a connector from which you can wire on a function block diagram. The parameter connector is not visible outside of the block or module by default. You can use the Show Parameter function to make an Internal Read Parameter appear as an input connector on a composite block. An Internal Read Parameter can be one of the following types: Floating point with status — a floating point value with a status indicator. Boolean with status — a True or False value with status indicator. 32-bit unsigned integer with status — a whole number without a positive or negative sign associated with it with a status indicator. Named Set — a value from 0 to 255 that displays an assigned text message. You configure the restart characteristic for this parameter. The options are Restore parameter value after restart or Preserve parameter value on download . For major revision 2 and later CSLSs, you configure the write access characteristic for this parameter. The options are Not Writeable , Writeable or Not Operator Writeable When Locked . The Writeable option enables an LSCALC block to write to the internal read parameter. The Not Operator Writeable When Locked enables an operator to write to the internal read parameter if the CSLS is unlocked. Using an internal read parameter to write to a function block For example, the user needs to write to the NUM_TO_TRIP parameter on a discrete voter block. First, the user exposes the NUM_TO_TRIP parameter using the Show context command on the block. Then, the user adds an internal read parameter to the module with write access configured as Writeable or Not Operator Writeable When Locked .

title: SIS internal write parameter
body_text: SIS internal write parameter An Internal Write Parameter provides a connector to which you can wire on a function block diagram so that you can write a particular parameter. The parameter connector is not visible outside of the block or module by default. You can use the Show Parameter function to make an Internal Read parameter appear as an output connector on a composite block. An Internal Write Parameter can be one of the following types: Floating point with status — a floating point value with a status indicator. Boolean with status — a True or False value with status indicator. 32-bit unsigned integer with status — a whole number without a positive or negative sign associated with it with a status indicator. Named Set — a value from 0 to 255 that displays an assigned text message. When you create this parameter you configure whether its characteristic is Restore parameter value after restart or Preserve parameter value on download .

title: SIS locks assigned to parameters and fields
main_heading: SIS locks assigned to parameters and fields
body_text: SIS locks assigned to parameters and fields All writeable SIS function block parameters and fields have assigned locks that determine who can access the parameters and fields. In DeltaV Explorer you can change the lock assignments made by the system using the Modify button on the Properties dialogs for SIS Parameter Security and SIS Field Security. The default locks assigned to SIS function block parameters are either SIS Control or SIS Restricted Control. The default locks assigned to SIS fields are either SIS Alarms or SIS Restricted Control. Note: SIS module-level parameters (including user-defined parameters) do not appear in the parameter list and are therefore assigned the default lock. The default lock is SIS No Access. Users cannot write to these parameters unless you change the default lock or add the parameters to the parameter list and assign them a lock that users have the key for.

body_text: About CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Migration Panels CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Migration Panels are used to replace legacy safety system hardware installed in existing cabinets with LS CHARM I/O. title: SIS modules
body_text: SIS modules DeltaV SIS modules contain DeltaV SIS module parameters, DeltaV SIS alarm parameters, and DeltaV SIS function blocks. In addition, SIS modules can contain user-defined parameters, composite function blocks (one level deep, no nesting) and alarm groups.. DeltaV SIS modules hold the logic for performing the actions required in a safety instrumented system and can be downloaded only to Logic Solvers. A Logic Solver has locked and unlocked modes. When the Logic Solver is unlocked and an SIS module is being viewed in debug mode of Control Studio, forced inputs are allowed. When the Logic Solver is locked, Control Studio exits debug mode and any forced inputs are removed. DeltaV SIS modules cannot contain other SIS modules and can contain only user-defined parameters, SIS function blocks, and SIS composite blocks (which can contain only SIS function blocks and user-defined parameters). The only algorithm type supported for DeltaV SIS modules is the function block diagram. DeltaV SIS software does not support class-based modules. Your application may require many modules that are similar or identical. Use DeltaV SIS module templates to reduce engineering time and promote reuse of engineering work. DeltaV SIS module history collection works the same as DeltaV module history collection. History is not collected from the Logic Solver so you cannot keep histories of I/O or diagnostic information. title: SIS module faceplate

The SIS module faceplate opens in runtime using the same techniques as those for control modules. The following shows an example of the SIS module faceplate in run mode. The SIS module faceplate consists of a main display area, a "close picture" button, a pushpin button, the SIS module tag and description, and command buttons. The pushpin button appears when multiple faceplate capability has been enabled in UserSettings.grf. When multiple monitor capability has been enabled, a position button appears to the left of the pushpin. The main display area of the SIS module faceplate contains an active alarm list and suppressed alarm list, and a tabbed control with two tabs, Errors and Alerts. The Errors tab lists text strings associated with active bits in SIF_ERRORS. The Alerts tab lists text strings associated with active bits in SIF_ALERTS. An indicator bar is visible under the word Errors or Alerts when one or more applicable bits are active. You can open the SIS module faceplate in DeltaV Operate run mode by clicking an SLS alarm button in the Alarm Banner or clicking the Open Faceplate button on the Toolbar and typing the SIS module name. The following items are contained in the SIS module faceplate: Active Alarms list – Contains the currently active or unacknowledged alarms along with the alarm message and an indicator that shows if the alarm has been acknowledged. Errors and Alerts lists – Lists text strings associated with SIF_ERRORS or SIF_ALERTS. title: SIS module blocks
body_text: SIS module blocks DeltaV SIS modules cannot contain module blocks. However, you can create module blocks in DeltaV equipment modules and assign them to SIS modules. You can refer to the same SIS module from multiple module blocks if you select Shared as the Ownership type. If you select Private, the SIS module moves under the equipment module and cannot be referred to from another module block. You can also create module blocks by dragging SIS modules to DeltaV equipment modules. This creates blocks with Private ownership (the SIS module moves under the equipment module), but you can select the SIS module, then select Module Block Properties from the context menu and change the ownership to Shared.

title: SIS module templates
body_text: SIS module templates Your implementation of a DeltaV SIS system may require multiple identical modules. Rather than create each module from scratch during configuration, you can create one or more module templates that capture the logic you require. You can then copy these templates, modify the copies as required, then save and download the copies. The DeltaV SIS software includes one SIS module template, SIS_DEFAULT. It is located in Deltav_System\Library\SIS Module Templates\General . The template contains two alarms based on SIF_ERRORS and SIF_ALERTS, to show the recommended way to handle SIF alarm detection. The template contains no function blocks or logic. You can modify the template to suit your needs or create your own templates as required and save them in the template library.

title: SLS 1508 module processing and communication
body_text: SLS 1508 module processing and communication The SLS 1508 Logic Solver processes DeltaV SIS modules differently than the DeltaV controller processes other DeltaV modules. All SIS modules in a Logic Solver run at the same scan rate. The scan rate is configurable from 50 to 200 milliseconds in 50 millisecond increments. On download, the Logic Solver estimates the maximum possible execution time for the SIS modules based on their complexity (number of inputs, expressions, and so on). Note that the estimated maximum execution time can be much greater than the actual ExecTime reported in DeltaV Diagnostics. The estimated maximum execution time is not reported. If the configured scan rate is less than the estimated maximum execution time, the Logic Solver sets the scan rate to the next slower scan rate. The Logic Solver also sets the Module not executing at configured scan rate bit in the module parameter SIF_ERRORS and activates the standard Logic Solver alarm MAINT_ALM. DeltaV Diagnostics Explorer shows the actual scan rate in the ActualScanTime parameter at the Logic Solver (SLS) level. To clear the alarm, change the configured scan rate to the actual scan rate and re-download. If the total estimated SIS module execution time exceeds 200 milliseconds, the Logic Solver does not apply the downloaded script and the download fails. The order of Logic Solver I/O and module processing is also different compared to DeltaV controllers and other DeltaV modules: Prior to running the SIS modules, every Logic Solver stores a snapshot of all input data in an internal database. Every Logic Solver executes its contained modules and transmits any secure parameter data. Secure parameters to be published globally are forwarded to the SISNet repeaters. Every Logic Solver transmits its I/O data to other Logic Solvers on the SIS Local Peer Bus. The SISNet Repeater forwards any secure parameters generated on the SIS Local Peer Bus. The SISNet Repeater transmits secure parameters to other SIS Local Peer Busses.

title: SIS non-secure parameter reference
body_text: SIS non-secure parameter reference Use a non-secure parameter reference to bring data from other SIS modules or DeltaV modules into an SIS module. Because these references are communicated over the local bus, do not use non-secure parameter references for safety-critical data. The number of SIS non-secure parameter references allowed per logic solver depend on the logic solver type: Logic solver type Number of non-secure parameter references allowed SLS 1508 24 CSLS 96 Only data of the following types can be referenced by non-secure parameter references: Floating Point Floating Point with status Boolean Bool with status Discrete with status 8-bit unsigned integer 16-bit unsigned integer 32-bit unsigned integer 32-bit unsigned integer with status Named Set When you create a non-secure parameter reference use the Parameter type field to convert the input to one of the three types allowed in a Logic Solver Convert to float with status Convert to boolean with status Convert to UInt32 with status When used with a CSLS, SIS non-secure parameter references support status handling. You enable status handling through the SIS non-secure parameter reference Properties dialog. The dialog enables you to specify how the parameter reference manages bad status for communications and device (non-communication) statuses. For each type of status, you specify whether the parameter reference passes the status values, ignores the values or temporarily ignores the values based on the user-specified suppression time. If a non-secure parameter reference obtains its value from another controller (or from a logic solver hosted in another controller), and the reference source stops sending new data, the system implements a 30-second time-out by default before the non-secure parameter reference is marked BAD. This is to help prevent issues if, for example, there is a failure in communication during a host controller switchover. For Convert to boolean with status non-secure parameter references, you can also configure the value to True or False along with status masking. If a non-secure parameter references is obtaining its data from another controller (or from a logic solver hosted in another controller), the system applies a 30-second timeout by default before the non-secure parameter reference is marked Bad when the reference source stops sending new data (for example, due to failure in communication during a switchover). This times out the chance of problems when the host controller switches over. The path to the control module must begin with a control module tag. The control module reference is a read-only input parameter for an SIS module. Create one by dragging the non-secure parameter reference icon from the Special Items palette. Note: The runtime data type of the non-secure parameter reference is that of the referenced parameter. title: SIS output parameter
body_text: SIS output parameter Output parameters appear automatically as output connector when you create composite blocks. The output parameter provides an output connection that allows you to send signals to other blocks, modules, or displays. In an SIS composite template or SIS module an Output Parameter can be one of the following types: Floating point with status — a floating point value with a status indicator. Boolean with status — a True or False value with status indicator. 32-bit unsigned integer with status — a whole number without a positive or negative sign associated with it with a status indicator. Named Set — a value from 0 to 255 that displays an assigned text message. When you create this parameter you configure whether its characteristic is Restore parameter value after restart or Preserve parameter value on download .

title: SIS parameter, field, and function security
main_heading: SIS parameter, field, and function security
body_text: SIS parameter, field, and function security Through the use of SIS locks and keys, DeltaV provides security mechanisms at the SIS parameter, SIS parameter field, and SIS function levels. At the parameter and field levels, the DeltaV system allows you to control which users can write to specific parameters and parameter fields at runtime. At the function level, the DeltaV system allows you to control which users can perform certain functions, for example, downloading the configuration. SIS fields, SIS parameters, and SIS functions are assigned to locks through DeltaV Explorer (under System Configuration\Setup\Security ). To be able to write to the field or parameter or perform the function, the logged-on user must have been assigned the key to the lock. Key assignments are configured in DeltaV User Manager. User span of control and access privilege is further defined by the plant area assignments. SIS modules can coexist with control modules in an area. Related information Parameter, field, and function security SIS locks SIS locks assigned to parameters and fields SIS locks assigned to functions

title: The Secure Write Mechanism
body_text: The Secure Write Mechanism The values of certain SIS module parameters may be changed, via messages, from several workstation applications. In addition, commands (such as Unlock) may be sent to a Logic Solver via messages from several workstation applications. These messages travel through several layers of communications before arriving at the destination. It is necessary to have a mechanism that validates these messages before they are acted on by the safety system. The Secure Write Mechanism, which is TUV-certified software, provides the validation of messages. The purpose of the Secure Write Mechanism is to substantially reduce the risk of sending an invalid message to the safety system from workstation applications. Secure writes are the only way that you can send write requests from workstations to SIS modules and Logic Solvers with the exception of writeable SIS alarm fields and SIS function block parameters of the string data type. Writeable SIS alarm fields and SIS function block string parameters accept standard writes. This Secure Write mechanism: Checks for security privilege to make the change Provides a confirm dialog to allow you to verify the change request Checks for message corruption Checks that the message arrives at the intended destination Prevents a spuriously generated message from causing a change Four DeltaV applications (DeltaV Explorer, DeltaV Operate, Diagnostics, and Control Studio) are able to use the Secure Write Mechanism. No other applications, including the OPC Server, have the ability to use the Secure Write Mechanism. Secure writes are not applicable to DeltaV controllers or BPCS modules. Note: You must confirm that a change request is correct. You may press the Confirm button to continue with the change, press the Cancel button to cancel the change, or do nothing and allow a timeout to cancel the change. Subtopics: Secure writes from DeltaV Explorer Secure writes from DeltaV Diagnostics Secure writes from Control Studio Secure writes from DeltaV Operate Changing the value of a Named Set parameter from DeltaV Operate Secure write behavior

title: SIS secure parameter
body_text: SIS secure parameter Use SIS secure parameters and SIS secure parameter references to transfer data between SIS modules. This pair (parameter and parameter reference) is required whether the SIS modules are assigned to the same logic solver or different logic solvers. The number of secure parameters a module can contain depends on the number of parameters available in the logic solver the module is assigned to.

title: SIS secure parameter reference
body_text: SIS secure parameter reference Use SIS secure parameters and SIS secure parameter references to transfer data between SIS modules. This pair (parameter and parameter reference) is required whether the SIS modules are assigned to the same logic solver or different logic solvers. When used with a CSLS, SIS secure parameter references support status handling. You enable status handling through the SIS secure parameter reference Properties dialog. The dialog enables you to specify how the parameter reference manages bad status for both communications and device (non-communication) statuses. For each type of status, you specify whether the parameter reference passes the status values, ignores the values or temporarily ignores the values based on the user-specified suppression time. For Boolean-type secure parameter references, you can also configure the value to True or False along with status masking. You can have any number of Secure Parameter References in a configuration.

title: SIS secure parameter status propagation
body_text: SIS secure parameter status propagation Status propagation from a secure parameter to a secure parameter reference works in the following ways: In SLS 1508 systems Non high density parameters: All Good and Uncertain incoming statuses are seen in the secure parameter reference as GoodNonCascade NonSpecific NotLimited (128) All Bad incoming statuses (except Bad NotConnected NotLimited) are seen in the secure parameter reference as Bad NonSpecific NotLimited (0) Bad NotConnected NotLimited status is seen in the secure parameter reference as Bad NotConnected NotLimited (8) High density parameters: All Good and Uncertain incoming statuses are seen in the secure parameter reference as GoodNonCascade NonSpecific NotLimited (128) All Bad incoming statuses are seen in the secure parameter reference as Bad NonSpecific NotLimited (0) Communication between logic solvers can affect secure reference parameters in SLS 1508 systems: If the receiving logic solver isn't receiving valid messages the secure parameter reference status is set to Bad NoCommLUV NotLimited (20) and the last value is retained. If the receiving logic solver receives a valid message but the revision information doesn't match the secure parameter references revision information the parameter reference status is set to Bad ConfigErr NotLimited (4) and the last value is retained. In CSLS systems All Good and Uncertain statuses are seen in the secure parameter reference as GoodNonCascade NonSpecific NotLimited (128) All Bad incoming statuses (except Bad NotConnected NotLimited) are seen in the secure parameter reference as Bad NonSpecific NotLimited (0) Bad NotConnected NotLimited status is seen in the reference as Bad NotConnected NotLimited (8) In CSLS systems if the receiving logic solver is not receiving valid messages the secure parameter reference status is set to Bad NoCommLUV NotLimited (20) and the last value is retained. This occurs if the secure parameter or reference is modified (the secure parameter name is changed, for example) and both source and destination are not redownloaded. This behavior is different compared to SLS 1508 systems.

title: SLS 1508 SIS Simulate
body_text: SLS 1508 SIS Simulate DeltaV SIS Simulate is a complete simulation environment you can use to design and test an SLS 1508 safety instrumented system. Most aspects of an SIS simulation system are identical in look and feel to a physical system. This includes configuration (including graphics configuration), diagnostics, and operating (if you have the OPC license and have configured a process simulation with a third-party application). The ability to simulate operation makes SIS Simulate useful for operator training. You can configure a simulated SIS system only on workstations with the appropriate simulation licenses. There are licenses available that allow different levels of use. You cannot commission or run simulated logic solvers in an online system. Because DeltaV SIS Simulate is an add-on to DeltaV Simulate, this document explains only the differences and enhancements seen when using DeltaV SIS Simulate. Note: DeltaV SIS Simulate does not affect the operation of DeltaV Simulate. DeltaV SIS Simulate adds the ability to simulate safety instrumented system configuration and operation to the DeltaV Simulate environment. DeltaV SIS Simulate features include the ability to configure: The ProfessionalPLUS workstation as a simulated controller with as many as 32 simulated logic solver cards. Configure Application Stations as additional simulated controllers, each with 32 simulated logic solver cards. Communication between simulated logic solver cards in the same workstation using secure parameter references. Communication between simulated logic solvers in different workstation using global secure parameter references (simulated SISNet Repeaters) Writing simulated process inputs to SIS modules. Reading process outputs from SIS modules. OPC (OLE for process control) to write values to SIS inputs. The general steps to use DeltaV SIS Simulate are: Configure a complete simulated safety instrumented system or import a runtime SIS configuration into the simulation system. Configure operator graphics. Perform operator training. Perform a functional test on the simulation system. Record the CRC checksums. Export the configuration from the simulation system. Import the configuration to the runtime system. Verify that the CRC checksums have not changed. Copy the operator graphics from the simulation system to the real system. You do not need to make any changes to the graphics. Perform a functional test on the physical system. Begin operating. body_text: Creating an SLS 1508 SIS simulation system You can configure an SIS Simulation system from scratch or you can import an existing SLS 1508 SIS configuration. There are a few differences compared to configuring a physical SIS system, but these differences are minor and do not affect your ability to export a configuration from a simulated system and then import it into a physical system. This section explains the configuration tasks that are unique or different for SIS Simulation systems. Because you are simulating a physical system, before you begin the configuration determine the types of Logic Solver cards (simplex or redundant) and their slot locations within each controller in the physical system. If you create your simulated system with this information, when you export your simulated system and import it into the physical system, all of the Logic Solver card assignments are correct. Note: If your simulated logic solver card assignments do not match your real system, you will not be able to import the simulation system into the real system without affecting the CRCs. title: DeltaV SIS Version Control
body_text: DeltaV SIS Version Control Version Control and Audit Trail (VCAT) in DeltaV SIS systems is similar to version control for non-SIS DeltaV items. VCAT can be enabled for SIS items only, if desired. You can enable VCAT for SIS only if SIS is enabled in DeltaV System Preferences. When DeltaV SIS software is enabled in the DeltaV System Preferences, the Version Control Configuration dialog that opens from Database Administration contains controls to enable version control for DeltaV SIS Module Authorization and SIS Module Function Test Recording. VCAT security for DeltaV SIS software uses the following functions and locks that parallel existing VCAT functions. This ensures that you can configure your installation so that only qualified users can perform SIS-related VCAT activities. SIS_VC_CHECKOUT_CHECKIN (default lock = Can Configure SIS) SIS_VC_DOWNLOAD_CHECKEDOUT (default lock = SIS Version Control) SIS_VC_DOWNLOAD_UNAUTHORIZED (default lock = SIS Version Control) SIS_VC_PURGE_RECOVER_ITEMS (default lock = SIS Version Control) SIS_VC_ROLLBACK_ITEMS (default lock = SIS Version Control) The tasks you perform using VCAT for DeltaV SIS items are nearly identical to the tasks used required to use DeltaV VCAT. The remainder of this section contains information specific to using VCAT with DeltaV SIS objects. Subtopics: VCAT for SIS module authorization approval VCAT for SIS module function test approval

title: Site Preparation
body_text: Site Preparation Properly designed and installed power distribution, ground networks, and signal wiring are part of site preparation and are extremely important for optimum DeltaV system operation. Even the best control system can only perform as well as the electrical foundation on which it is built. Clean input power, single-point grounding, and adequate shielding from outside electrical interference are a must. Power distribution, ground networks, and signal wiring should be installed before the system is installed. Use the manual, DeltaV Power and Grounding , as your resource for proper site preparation. Note: Some images in this manual show bullet style wiring connections. This style is used for reference only and splicing wires into wires to emulate bullet connections is never recommended by Emerson. Always use terminal-to-terminal wiring.
