title: General parameters (Smart Firewall)
body_text: General parameters (Smart Firewall) A number of parameters hold information written to the Smart Firewall during the adding of the firewall. These parameters are configured and downloaded to the firewall using the Network Device Command Center (NDCC). The firewall uses these values to customize its behavior for your DeltaV system. For all the following parameters: The parameter category is Configuration Restore parameter value after restart is false (unchecked) The parameter filter is either Common Configuration or Advanced Configuration Changes to these parameters in the module class are not automatically propagated to the firewall. Parameter settings must be modified in BOTH the module class and to the firewall directly. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Allow instance value to be configured - Default Value Description BCK_TIME_IP_ADDR String (empty string) No A computer to be used as a backup NTP time server. LOC_DESCRIPTION String (empty string) Yes DeltaV description (typically location) for the firewall. MGINFO String (empty string) Yes The encrypted firewall management password. This parameter is written to when the user sets the firewall management password in NDCC. DO NOT write to this parameter other than through NDCC. DO NOT delete the MGINFO parameter. Doing either of these things will cause DeltaV to fail to communicate to the firewall. MGMT_IP_ADDR String (empty string) Yes The management IP address for this firewall. (During firewall replacement, the same IP address is assigned to the replacement firewall.) NETWORK 8-bit unsigned integer 0 Yes The network to which this firewall is connected. This parameter is written to during the adding of the firewall and is used to determine where to display the firewall in the NDCC application. The values are 0 - Unknown Network 1 - ACN Primary 2 - ACN Secondary 3 - Remote Primary 4 - Remote Secondary 5 - Other network (for example, the Thin Client network or the Level 2.5 network) PRI_TIME_IP_ADDR String (empty string) No A computer to be used as the primary NTP time server. SYSLOG_IP_ADDR* String (empty string) No A computer hosting a syslog server which should receive firewall event log records. * These parameters exist to allow experienced users (or your Information Technology group) to use third party tools such as a Syslog Server or third party SNMP package to collect this information. Typical DeltaV users will not need to set these addresses.

title: Guardian registration parameters (Smart Firewall)
body_text: Guardian registration parameters (Smart Firewall) The Guardian registration information parameters are manually entered with information from the firewall. Once configured, you can use these parameters in custom displays showing the Emerson Smart Firewall. For all the following parameters: The parameter category is Misc Allow instance value to be configured is false (unchecked) Restore parameter value after restart is false (unchecked) The parameter filter is On-line XINFO_MODEL XINFO_HWREV XINFO_SWREV XINFO_SERIAL

title: Hardware alarm condition parameters (Smart Firewall)
body_text: Hardware alarm condition parameters (Smart Firewall) *Except for changing the value of the alarm level (ignore, maint, advise or fail) it is strongly recommend that you do not adjust other default parameters in the firewall module unless instructed to do so by Emerson to solve a specific issue. *A number of parameters hold information that determine how hardware alarm condition information in the firewall is transformed into one of the PlantWeb-style hardware alarms. For all the following parameters: The parameter category is either Configuration or Operating Restore parameter value after restart is false (unchecked) Allow named set changes for new instances is false (unchecked), when applicable The parameter filter is one of Common Configuration, Advanced Configuration or On-line The Smart Firewall has two ports; one port connects to the external LAN and another port connects to the DeltaV. The float array parameters used to hold information specific to a firewall port are size 2 arrays: Index 1 for the port connecting to the external LAN Index 2 for the port connecting to the DeltaV The parameter information that follows is arranged in the order the parameters appear in the firewall module class function block diagram. Firewall Not Communicating This condition is reported when the node hosting the firewall module cannot communicate with the firewall using the IP address in the MGMT_IP_ADDR parameter. Failure to communicate with the firewall overrides all other firewall conditions that may be configured, causing them to become inactive: It is not possible to configure the firewall module to ignore the NOCOMM condition. If there are any failures in reading information from the firewall, the raw NOCOMM condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_NOCOMM_OND and HAC_NOCOMM_OFFD. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_NOCOMM_OND Float 0 On delay (seconds). HAC_NOCOMM_OFD Float 0 Off delay (seconds). There is no HAC_NOCOMM_PWA parameter supported because the not communicating condition is always mapped to the COMM_ALM for the firewall. Power Supply Unavailable Emerson Smart Firewalls support redundant power supply connections. Reporting the loss of one of the power sources allows repairs before both power sources fail. If HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the firewall for the status of the power supply connections. If either power supply connection is bad, the raw PSNAVAIL condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_PSNAVAIL_OND and HAC_PSNAVAIL_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the PSNAVAIL condtion, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Firewall Message: Power supply n unavailable (where n is either 1 or 2 to reflect the power supply that is unavailable). Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA When the firewall power supply is not redundant you should either: Make the (non-redundant) power connections to both Power supply 1 and Power supply 2, or Configure HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA as Ignore (0) to disable checking this condition. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_PSNAVAIL_PWA Named Set MAINT_ALM This condition should trigger the MAINT alarm. HAC_PSNAVAIL_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_PSNAVAIL_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). Firewall Chassis High Temperature Emerson Smart Firewalls can detect and report their chassis temperature. Operating above their rated temperature range can result in deteriorating firewall behavior. If HAC_HITEMP_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the firewall for its chassis temperature and writes the value to the HAC_HITEMP_VAL parameter. If the value in HAC_HITEMP_VAL becomes greater than the value in HAC_HITEMP_LIM the raw HITEMP condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_HITEMP_OND and HAC_HITEMP_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the HITEMP condition, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Firewall Message: Firewall temperature too high. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_HITEMP_PWA If an Emerson Smart Firewall with a different temperature range is employed, adjust HAC_HITEMP_LIM as desired in the firewall. If historical data on firewall temperature is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_HITEMP_VAL. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_HITEMP_PWA Named Set MAINT_ALM This condition should trigger the MAINT alarm. HAC_HITEMP_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_HITEMP_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_HITEMP_LIM Float 50 Configurable high temperature limit for the firewall, in degrees C. HAC_HITEMP_VAL Float 0 Receives the chassis temperature read from the firewall (available for history capture). Firewall Digital Signal Activated You can use advanced firewall management tools to configure the conditions that cause the digital signal on the firewall to activate. The digital signal can then be used to drive local indication of the problems detected by the firewall. If HAC_SIGACT_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the firewall for the status of the digital signal contacts. The value returned (1 = digital signal is activated; 0 = otherwise) is written to the HAC_SIGACT_VAL parameter. If HAC_SIGACT_VAL has a value other than 0 the raw SIGACT condition is true. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_SIGACT_OND and HAC_SIGACT_OFFD. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM HAC is active. The result is reported as the SIGACT condition visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Firewall Message: Firewall digital signal activated. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_SIGACT_PWA If historical data on the state of the digital signal is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_SIGACT_VAL. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_SIGACT_PWA Named Set Ignored This condition should be ignored by default. HAC_SIGACT_OND Float 0 On delay (seconds). HAC_SIGACT_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_SIGACT_VAL Float 0 Receives the status of the digital signal read from the firewall (available for history capture). 1 = digital signal is activated; 0 = otherwise. Excessive Packets Discarded On Port Unusually high levels of packets discarded (due to CRC errors, packets too small (runts), or packets too large (giants) can be an indicator of loose or deteriorating network cable connections, damaged network cables, or failing network interface electronics. If HAC_DISCPKTS_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3, the workstation interrogates the firewall for: The list of all ports installed on the firewall. Whether each port is enabled or disabled. Information about packets discarded (due to CRC errors, runts, and giants) in the last 60 seconds on each installed port. For each enabled port, the number of packets discarded in the last 60 seconds is written to the corresponding array element in HAC_DISCPKTS_PRT[n]. 0 is written for ports that are not installed or that are disabled. The sum from all ports of the packets discarded in the last 60 seconds is written to HAC_DISCPKTS_VAL. If the port is enabled, and if the number of discarded packets on this port in the last 60 seconds is greater than HAC_DISCPKTS_LIM the raw DISCPKTS condition is true for that port. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_DISCPKTS_OND and HAC_DISCPKTS_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM HAC is active. The result is reported as the DISCPKTS condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: Excessive packets discarded on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_DISCPKTS_PWA If historical data on packet discard rates for this firewall is desired, users should configure continuous history recording on HAC_DISCPKTS_VAL. Per port history could be captured by configuring history collection on individual elements of HAC_DISCPKTS_PRT[x]. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_DISCPKTS_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_DISCPKTS_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_DISCPKTS_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_DISCPKTS_LIM Float Array 32 rows , 1 column 10 For the two ports, configurable limit for packet discards on the port. HAC_DISCPKTS_VAL Float 0 Receives total number of packets discarded from all enabled ports in the last 60 seconds. HAC_DISCPKTS_PRT[ n ] Float Array 32 rows , 1 column 0 For each enabled port, receives number of packets discarded in the last 60 seconds. 0 for disabled ports. High Link Utilization On Port If HAC_HIUTIL_PWA.CVI has the value 1, 2, or 3 the workstation interrogates the firewall for: The list of all ports installed on the firewall. Whether each port is enabled or disabled Information about the link utilization in the last 30 seconds on each installed port. Note: Link utilization information is for inbound communication on the ports. It does not include outbound communication. For each enabled port, link utilization is written to the corresponding array element in HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[n]. 0 is written for ports that are disabled or not installed. The maximum value from all elements of HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[n] elements is written to HAC_HIUTIL_VAL. If the port is enabled and the link utilization on this port in the last 30 seconds is greater than HAC_HIUTIL_LIM the raw HIUTIL condition is true for that port. Note: A common utilization limit as a percent of port speed is applied to all ports (connected to controllers, workstations and other firewalls), making the condition detection most sensitive to high traffic levels on ports connected to DeltaV workstations. On/off delay logic is applied using the values in HAC_HIUTIL_OND and HAC_HIUTIL_OFFD. The configurable on/off delay times are applied to all ports. Independent on/off delay timers are used for each port. The result from the on/off delay logic is forced inactive if the current NOCOMM condition is active. The result is reported as the HIUTIL condition for that port, visible in the Condition Summary application: Subsystem: Port Message: High link utilization on port m.p. Alarm: Determined by value in HAC_HIUTIL_PWA If historical data on link utilization for this firewall is required, configure continuous history recording on HAC_HIUTIL_VAL. Per port history can be captured by configuring history collection on individual elements of HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[n]. Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_HIUTIL_PWA Named Set ADVISE_ALM This condition should trigger the ADVISE alarm. HAC_HIUTIL_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_HIUTIL_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_HIUTIL_LIM Float Array 2 rows , 1 column 30 (percent) For the two ports, configurable limit for packet link utilization on the port. HAC_HIUTIL_VAL Float 0 Receives the maximum link utilization value (0 to 100 in percent) from all enabled ports in the last 60 seconds. HAC_HIUTIL_PRT[ n ] Float Array 2 rows , 1 column 0 For each enabled port, receives link utilization value (0 to 100 in percent) over the last 30 seconds. 0 for disabled ports. CPU usage too high Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_HICPU_PWA Named Set MAINT_ALM This condition should trigger the MAINT alarm. HAC_HICPU_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_HICPU_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_HICPU_LIM Float 50 Configurable high CPU usage limit for the firewall. HAC_HICPU_VAL Float 0 Receives the CPU usage (0 to 100 in percent) read from the firewall (available for history capture). Memory usage too high Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description HAC_HIMEM_PWA Named Set MAINT_ALM This condition should trigger the MAINT alarm. HAC_HIMEM_OND Float 60 On delay (seconds). HAC_HIMEM_OFD Float 600 Off delay (seconds). HAC_HIMEM_LIM Float 80 Configurable high memory usage limit for the firewall. HAC_HIMEM_VAL Float 0 Receives the memory usage (0 to 100 in percent) read from the firewall (available for history capture).

title: Hardware alarm parameters (Smart Firewall)
body_text: Hardware alarm parameters (Smart Firewall) A number of parameters hold information that determine how to report hardware alarms for the firewall. Note: The alarm parameter properties listed in the tables are the only properties you should change. COMM_ALM Parameter Reports that communications with the firewall have been lost. Property Default value Priority 15 (CRITICAL) Enabled Yes Shelving Timeout 999d 0h 0m FAILED_ALM Parameter Reports that one or more conditions indicating a failure exist in the firewall. Property Default value Priority 15 (CRITICAL) Enabled Yes ShelvingTimeout 999d 0h 0m MAINT_ALM Parameter Reports that one or more conditions exist indicating maintenance needed by the firewall. Property Default value Priority 11 (WARNING) Enabled Yes Shelving Timeout 999d 0h 0m ADVISE_ALM Alarm to advise users about one or more conditions reported by the firewall. Property Default value Priority 7 (ADVISORY) Enabled Yes Shelving Timeout 999d 0h 0m

title: Information needed to configure the internal network
main_heading: Information needed to configure the internal network
body_text: Information needed to configure the internal network There is a network on the DeltaV workstations connected to the DeltaV port on the firewall whether you have one or many workstations connected to the port. In a DeltaV system, the network between the Emerson Smart Firewall and the DeltaV workstations is called the 2.5 LAN. It is important that the network addresses used for the DeltaV workstations' Network Interface Cards (NICs) connected to the 2.5 LAN do not conflict with existing network addresses in other networks in the facility. Your IT department can provide guidance in what addresses are available for use in the 2.5 network. The firewall's internal network (the 2.5 LAN) can be configured with either static or dynamic IP addressing. Emerson recommends static IP addressing with no DNS server entries. If dynamic IP addressing is used, ensure the firewall's external interface address is created statically with no DNS servers. With dynamic IP addressing using DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol), the firewall serves the IP addresses to the workstations in the internal network. If dynamic IP addressing is used, the internal workstations' NICs must be set to Obtain an IP address automatically . Also when dynamic IP addressing is used, the firewall administrator must know the maximum number of internal IP addresses that will be generated. Emerson suggests that you set the DeltaV workstations' third NIC to Use the following DNS server addresses and leave the addresses blank so the DNS server does not create the DNS information in the NIC. With static IP addressing, the workstations are assigned an IP address by the administrator; not served an IP address by the firewall. If static IP addressing is used, the internal workstations' NICs must be set to Use the following IP address and the firewall administrator must enter the required information (IP address, Subnet mask, and Default gateway) at each workstation. Emerson suggests that you set the DeltaV workstations' third NIC to Use the following DNS server addresses and leave the addresses blank so the DNS server does not create the DNS information in the NIC. Important: If the DeltaV workstations' third NICs are connected to an existing network, you should understand the network architecture and how the DeltaV workstations' network addresses have been assigned before setting up the network. It is highly recommended that you consult with your IT department or with those responsible for the existing network to determine how to install and configure the firewall in the existing network. It is possible that the existing network architecture will require modifications before the Smart Firewall can be installed. Questions to ask when configuring the internal network for static IP addressing Consult with your IT department and obtain the following information required to configure the firewall's internal network for static IP addressing where the firewall administrator assigns the network addresses. We recommend that you record this information on the Worksheet for internal workstation names and IP addresses . What is the range of IP addresses for the internal network? An example range is 192.168.1.100 to 192.168.1.200. What is the subnet mask for the network? An example subnet mask is 255.255.255.0. What IP address will be configured as the firewall's gateway address. This address becomes the network address of the firewall's web UI. This address should be selected from the range of addresses assigned to the internal network. Typically it is the first address in the range. Be sure that no DNS information is configured for the NICs. Questions to ask when configuring the internal network for dynamic IP addressing Consult with your IT department and obtain the following information required to configure the firewall's internal network for dynamic IP addressing where the firewall assigns the network addresses. We recommend that you record this information on the Worksheet for internal workstation names and IP addresses . If the firewall serves the IP addresses to the internal workstations (DHCP), what is the starting address that is used to generate the network addresses for the DeltaV workstations? This must be the first address in the subnet; typically xxx.xxx.1.1. What is the subnet mask for the address? How many workstations will have network addresses assigned? To prevent unauthorized connections this number should be the exact number of DeltaV workstations. When you have gathered all the necessary information and completed the worksheets, you are ready to configure the internal network. Related information Configure the internal network Configure static addressing on DeltaV workstations Worksheet for internal workstation names and IP addresses What is the 2.5 network?

title: Logging menu - initial configuration settings
body_text: Logging menu - initial configuration settings Leave the general logging parameters at their default settings for the initial setup. The logging settings will be made during the protection phase of firewall configuration. Firewall events can be written to a log that is saved temporarily on the firewall. In addition, firewall events can be saved to a remote server as historical data. If firewall events are saved to a remote server, you must know the server's IP address. The logging information is saved in a standard reporting format and can be sent to a remote syslog server. A syslog server application must be installed on the server or workstation to accept the logging information. Any internal workstation can act as the syslog server. There are many types of syslog server software available, from no cost, open source versions to more costly private versions. If your IT department does not have a syslog server preference, we suggest that you install a simple syslog server and use it to collect and archive firewall logs for security analysis. Note: Users are responsible for acquiring the syslog daemon and must install and run the syslog daemon per the manufacturer's instructions. Emerson provides no support or warranty for any syslog daemon. The KIWI Syslog Server has been tested to work with the DeltaV system and the Emerson Smart Firewall. The free KIWI Syslog Server for Windows is available at http://www.kiwisyslog.com/ . Consult with your IT department and obtain the following information required to configure a remote syslog server. We recommend that you record this information on the Worksheet for Smart Firewall configuration . If firewall events are logged to a remote syslog server, what is the server's address? This address can be entered during initial configuration even if the remote syslog server software is not yet installed. This address must be a workstation on the internal LAN. Emerson recommends that a third party syslog server is installed on a DeltaV application station or a non-DeltaV computer. Related information Basic firewall setup Worksheet for Smart Firewall configuration Configure Emerson Smart Firewall remote logging using its WebUI

title: Modifying the Hosts file
body_text: Modifying the Hosts file The Hosts file can be modified when an application needs to use a computer name rather than the network address to access the computer. The Hosts files is easy to modify as the file is a text file that you can edit in Notepad. Because your Hosts file is a system file, you must run Notepad as an administrator when you edit it. To run Notepad as an administrator, find Notepad in your start menu, right click it, and select Run as administrator . Not all versions of Windows store the Hosts file in the same location. It is usually located in c:\windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts . You can search the hard drive for the filename. We recommend that you make a backup of the Hosts file before modifying it. An open Hosts file in Notepad should look similar to the following: # Copyright (c) 1993-2009 Microsoft Corp. # # This is a sample HOSTS file used by Microsoft TCP/IP for Windows. # # This file contains the mappings of IP addresses to host names. Each # entry should be kept on an individual line. The IP address should # be placed in the first column followed by the corresponding host name. # The IP address and the host name should be separated by at least one # space. # # Additionally, comments (such as these) may be inserted on individual # lines or following the machine name denoted by a '#' symbol. # # For example: # # 102.54.94.97 rhino.acme.com # source server # 38.25.63.10 x.acme.com # x client host # localhost name resolution is handled within DNS itself. # 127.0.0.1 localhost # ::1 localhost

title: Smart Firewall module class
body_text: Smart Firewall module class You want all of your Emerson Smart Firewalls to have consistent behavior. To assist that goal, DeltaV software includes a control module class from which firewall modules are created: FW_STDCFG_$W. The firewall module class holds common firewall setup information and hardware alarm behavior configuration for Smart Firewalls on the DeltaV 2.5 network. The 2.5 network is a simplex network, so a secondary firewall module is not needed. You can modify parameter settings of the class to tailor it to your needs, but modifications made in the module class are not automatically propagated to the firewall. Parameter settings must be modified in BOTH the module class and to the firewall directly. Important: Modifications to the class should be done prior to adding the firewall. It is recommended that you do not add any other parameters or logic in this module class. Any additions to the class may not be preserved when upgrading to future versions of DeltaV software. The control module class is located in the configuration library at: DeltaV _System/Library/Advanced Definitions/Control Module Classes/Firewalls . If the module class is deleted or renamed, you cannot add firewalls. Subtopics: General parameters (Smart Firewall) Hardware alarm condition parameters (Smart Firewall) Hardware alarm parameters (Smart Firewall) Guardian registration parameters (Smart Firewall) State information parameters (Smart Firewall)

title: Resolving workstation names
body_text: Resolving workstation names If an external application is not connecting with an application on a DeltaV workstation you may need to modify the Windows Hosts file. Some applications require the use of a Windows Hosts file to resolve a host name to an IP address in order to communicate with internal workstations through the firewall. Name resolution cannot be configured on the firewall; it must be configured on some or all of the external workstations. We recommend that you create a Hosts file for each workstation that will communicate through the firewall. This is a simple text file that is used to associate a computer name with a network IP address. Some applications use computer names rather than network IP addresses to access computers and the Hosts file is needed to provide the name for network address resolution. Related information Modifying the Hosts file Adding Hosts file entries Testing modifications to the Hosts file

title: SNMP menu - initial configuration settings
body_text: SNMP menu - initial configuration settings No initial configuration settings are required. SNMP settings are made during the protection phase of firewall configuration. The firewall's SNMP server must be enabled so that DeltaV's Network Device Command Center (NDCC) can obtain information from the firewall.

title: State information parameters (Smart Firewall)
body_text: State information parameters (Smart Firewall) A number of parameters hold state information in the firewall module. These parameters are not intended to be configurable. For all the following parameters: The parameter category is one of Alarm, Operating, Misc or none Allow instance value to be configured is false (unchecked) Restore parameter value after restart is false (unchecked) The parameter filter is On-line Parameter Name Parameter Type Default Value Description COMM_ACT 32-bit unsigned integer 1 0 When non-zero, indicates that the COMM_ALM is active. FAILED_ACT 32-bit unsigned integer 0 When non-zero, indicates that the FAILED_ALM is active. MAINT_ACT 32-bit unsigned integer 0 When non-zero, indicates that the MAINT_ALM is active. ADVISE_ACT 32-bit unsigned integer 0 When non-zero, indicates that the ADVISE_ALM is active. COMM_P1 String (empty string) Reserved for use by DeltaV software. FAILED_P1 String (empty string) Reserved for use by DeltaV software. MAINT_P1 String (empty string) Reserved for use by DeltaV software. ADVISE_P1 String (empty string) Reserved for use by DeltaV software. HACACTCNT 32-bit unsigned integer 0 The number of (unsuppressed) active hardware alarm conditions in the firewall. (The number of active conditions shown in the Condition Summary application for this firewall.) HACSUPCNT 32-bit unsigned integer 0 The number of suppressed hardware alarm conditions in the firewall. (The number of suppressed conditions shown in the Condition Summary application for this firewall.)

title: System time menu - initial configuration settings
main_heading: System time menu - initial configuration settings
body_text: System time menu - initial configuration settings If a GPS network time server is in use, obtain the IP address of the network time server. The IP address can be on the internal or external network. If it is on the external network, ensure that the computer can access the firewall. If a GPS network time server is not in use, you can synchronize system time for all workstations and controllers on the DeltaV Control Network in the DeltaV System Time dialog by running deltav\bin\SystemTime.exe . CAUTION: Do not attempt to change system time by using the Windows Date and Time utility, accessed from the Control Panel or the Taskbar clock. The Windows Date and Time utility does not synchronize system time on all workstations and controllers in the DeltaV Control Network. Use the Windows Date and Time utility only to specify the local time zone and to enable the Automatically adjust clock for Daylight Saving Time option. Related information Basic firewall setup System time

title: Testing modifications to the Hosts file
main_heading: Testing modifications to the Hosts file
body_text: Testing modifications to the Hosts file To test the modifications to the Hosts file, ping the internal computer (the DeltaV Workstation) using the computer name instead of the IP address, for example: C:\Users\username>ping batch_manager_server If the Hosts file is correct you will get a reply from the internal computer. If you get a reply from the computer that you pinged, the Hosts file is working correctly. If you do not get a reply by pinging with the computer name, ping the computer's IP address directly. If the IP address ping is successful, recheck the Hosts file. Another option is to use the ipconfig/displaydns command and ensure that the Hosts file entries are correct.

title: Troubleshooting the Smart Firewall's initial setup
main_heading: Troubleshooting the Smart Firewall's initial setup
body_text: Troubleshooting the Smart Firewall's initial setup LEDs for Ethernet communications link status and speed - 10/100 MB/s auto-sensing When the Ethernet cables are plugged into the Smart Firewall ports from powered devices, the LEDs adjacent to the network ports are lit. The following image shows the location of the LEDs on the Smart Firewall. LED Meaning Connection status indicator (LED on the left side of each network port) Steady green or blinking: good link. Unlit: the device on the other end of the cable is not powered up or the cable is bad, or over 100 meters long. You can confirm the quality of the cable by verifying the LEDs on the adjacent port work with the same cable and end device or by testing the cable. Link rate indicator (LED on the right side of each network port) Steady amber: a 100 MB/s link is established. Unlit: a 10 MB/s link is established. LEDs for power and errors Refer to the preceding image for the location of the power and error LEDs on the Smart Firewall. LED Meaning Error indication: Steady = Power Supply Unit (PSU) Error red and power green: only one power cord is connected. The alarm contact TTL output goes to a Low state under these conditions. Refer to The alarm contact for more information. Power indication Steady green: the firewall is powered by either or both AC inputs. Power green and error red: only one power cord is connected. The alarm contact TTL output goes to a Low state under this conditions. Refer to The alarm contact for more information. Troubleshooting Ethernet communications - duplex operation The Configuration Summary page in the firewall's web UI provides information about the external (plant LAN) and internal (DeltaV workstations) Ethernet communications. Refer to the web UI's online help for information on the Configuration Summary page. The following image shows the type of information displayed on the Configuration Summary page. Troubleshooting Ethernet communications - bandwidth usage The Dashboard Summary page in the firewall's web UI provides information on bandwidth usage (network loading). The Port 1 and Port 2 bandwidth displays use averaging and do not indicate brief spikes in bandwidth. These measurements are intended to show longer term trends in network bandwidth utilization that should normally be much lower than the 100 MB/s theoretical maximum. For more precise bandwidth measurements use an external network monitor, or if the Smart Firewall is connected to a managed switch, use the switch port diagnostics. The alarm contact The alarm contact is used to monitor the Smart Firewall. It contains two screw terminals for 16-30 AWG wires. The left hand screw terminal is the High Side of a +5V TTL output and the right hand screw terminal is the Low Side or ground connection for the TTL output. Apply no more than 2 inch-pounds of torque to these screw terminals after the wires are installed or damage may result. It is not necessary to remove the terminal block from the Smart Firewall front panel in order to install the alarm contact wiring. If you need to replace the firewall, you can unscrew the two screws on the front panel that hold the terminal block in place and remove the terminal block with the existing wires. This way the terminal block can be reused on the new firewall with the wires already attached. USB port The USB port on the back panel is used to save user configuration.

title: Smart Switch module classes
body_text: Smart Switch module classes You want all of your DeltaV Smart Switches to have consistent behavior. To assist that goal, DeltaV software includes two control module classes from which switch modules are created: SWITCH_STDCFG_$X — Class for switches on the primary network. SWITCH_SECCFG_$X — Class for switches on the secondary network. The switch module classes hold common switch setup information and hardware alarm behavior configuration for Smart Switches. You can modify parameter settings of the classes to tailor them to your needs. The Network Device Command Center detects which DeltaV ACN or DeltaV Remote network a switch is on and creates a switch module instance named the same as the switch from the appropriate module class when commissioning a switch. Note: During commissioning of a switch, Network Device Command Center (NDCC) only detects the primary and secondary network for the DeltaV ACN and DeltaV Remote networks. For all other networks, it uses the SWITCH_STDCFG_$X module. Classes are provided for both primary and secondary networks because you may need to have different values for the following parameters: TRAP_IP_ADDR SYSLOG_IP_ADDR PRI_TIME_IP_ADDR BCK_TIME_IP_ADDR Note: It is recommended that you set these addresses in the switch module class or make the class configurable at the instance. Important: NDCC only detects the primary and secondary network for the DeltaV ACN and DeltaV Remote networks. For all other networks, it uses the SWITCH_STDCFG_$X module. Therefore, if you need to have any parameters set for these other networks, you must set the module class to allow for the instance to be configured, and you must set the correct IP addresses for things such as the SYSLOG or NTP servers for those networks (that is, the subnets must be appropriate for the switch's network). It is recommended that you do not add any other parameters or logic in these module classes. Any additions to the classes may not be preserved when upgrading to future versions of DeltaV software. The control module classes are in the configuration library at: DeltaV _System/Library/Advanced Definitions/Control Module Classes/Switches . If the module classes have been deleted or renamed, you cannot commission switches. Note: It is not recommended to assign the smart switch module to a member of an Application Station pair because the standby Application Station is not communicating with the switch, it is getting all updates from the active Application Station. The smart switch module (in the active Application Station) is communicating to the switch through Network Device Command Center SNMP processes that are not redundant. Networks monitored by NDCC Network Device Command Center (NDCC) is capable of discovering (and therefore, commissioning, monitoring, and managing) DeltaV Smart Switches from the following networks (provided there is no routing or redirecting of the network traffic): DeltaV Area Control Network (the ACN), primary and secondary DeltaV Remote Network, primary and secondary DeltaV level 2.5 network Thin Client network (for virtual DeltaV workstations), primary and secondary Subtopics: General parameters (Smart Switch) Hardware alarm condition parameters (Smart Switch) Hardware alarm parameters (Smart Switch) Guardian registration parameters (Smart Switch) State information parameters (Smart Switch) Related information Commissioning and monitoring DeltaV Smart Switches Module classes

title: Web service APIs
body_text: Web service APIs Each of the web services has an application programming interface (API). Every web service (except Mynah Mimic) supports both WSHttp and NetTcp bindings. WSHttp binding is based on SOAP messages and supports interoperability so that client programs on any operating system that conform to Web Service standards (WS-*) work with the DeltaV web services. The NetTcp binding is supported only by .NET client programs. NetTcp binding uses binary-based messaging and provides faster communications than WSHttp binding using SOAP-based messaging. Note: The Mynah Integration web service supports the Mynah Mimic application. You cannot access the Mynah API to write your own client programs. You can set some properties for the web service from the Gateway administration tool but only from within the DeltaV network. Subtopics: Recipe Exchange API Campaign Manager API Mynah Integration Web Service API

title: Campaign Manager API
body_text: Campaign Manager API The Campaign Manager Web Service application programming interface (API) provides a programmatic interface for DeltaV batch configuration data exchange. The API includes data contracts and methods you use to access information in the DeltaV database. Use the API to define recipes in text leveraging your existing tools. You can also save and exchange recipes in XML files. The foundation of the API is the existing DeltaV Campaign Manager control. The API is an interface to the control that supports Windows Communication Foundation (WCF) Service Oriented Architecture (SOA). The endpoint address for the Campaign Manager web service is http://localhost:49202/CampaignManager/CMService If you have changed the port number for the service, use the new port number. The schemas and other supporting files for the API are located in the directory: \DeltaV\bin\SOASchema\ How you access the APIs depends on your development environment and the programming language you are using. Subtopics: Campaign Manager sample client Campaign Manager data contracts Campaign Manager errors

title: SOA Web Services Introduction
body_text: SOA Web Services Introduction DeltaV software uses Services Oriented Architecture (SOA) web services to provide access to DeltaV functionality such as Campaign Manager and Recipe Exchange from client applications outside of the DeltaV system. The web services are built with the Windows Communication Foundation (WCF) programming framework. Use the web services to integrate Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems with the process control system in conjunction with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES). The web services are Recipe Exchange, Campaign Manager, Mynah Integration, and Monitor. The Monitor service is used internally and has no interface. The Mynah Integration service exists solely to support the Mynah Mimic application. You cannot write applications that access this service. Client applications access these services and communicate with the underlying DeltaV functionality through an application station configured as an SOA Gateway. Subtopics: Supported network configurations Gateway Administration utility

title: Mynah Integration Web Service API
body_text: Mynah Integration Web Service API The Mynah Integration web service exists solely to support the Mynah Mimic application. You cannot write applications that access this service. The only interaction you can have is to set some service properties from the gateway administration tool if this becomes necessary. You can set Mynah Integration service properties only from within the DeltaV system.

title: Recipe Exchange API
body_text: Recipe Exchange API The Recipe Exchange Web Service application programming interface (API) provides a programmatic interface for DeltaV batch configuration data exchange. The API includes data contracts and methods you use to access information in the DeltaV database. Use the API to define recipes in text to leverage your existing tools. You can also save and exchange recipes in XML files. The foundation of the API is the existing DeltaV Recipe Exchange control. The API is an interface to the control that supports Windows Communication Foundation (WCF) Service Oriented Architecture (SOA). The endpoint address for the Recipe Exchange web service is http://localhost:49200/RecipeExchange/REService If you have changed the port number for the service, use the new port number. The schemas and other supporting files for the APIs are located in the directory: \DeltaV\bin\SOASchema\ How you access the APIs depends on your development environment and the programming language you are using. Subtopics: Recipe Exchange sample client Recipe Exchange data contracts

title: Security
body_text: Security The web services are fully integrated into the standard DeltaV security system. All web service interactions with the underlying DeltaV control systems occur under an authenticated user account and are checked against any applicable DeltaV security function keys and locks using the username and password arguments. All passwords are encrypted and are passed using secure means. The web services impersonate the caller of any of its web methods and therefore ensures that it is this caller's identity against which all Operating System-level security checks are authenticated. For this reason, any web service client application must run as a valid and known Windows account from the perspective of the DeltaV node hosting the service. At the same time, some web methods (in Campaign Manager) take a confirmer name and password. The confirmer's account is checked against the DeltaV security function locks. For example to modify a campaign, the DeltaV Campaign Manager enforces that the confirmer account has the CAMPAIGN_MODIFY function key in the DeltaV security system. First, the Campaign Manager node authenticates the confirmer name and password to ensure it is a valid account and if so, ensures that the user has the appropriate key for the DeltaV security function lock. The node performs the requested operation only after both of these checks have passed. The web services support both Basic authentication and Integrated Windows authentication. If Integrated Windows authentication is used Impersonation must be enabled to ensure communication. Subtopics: Using Web Services between domains

title: Using PerformOperations
body_text: Using PerformOperations This topic includes general information for using the PerformOperations method to access any SOA web service. General Usage Information The XML passed to the PerformOperations method must be well-formed XML. Declare the required namespaces in the root (PerformOperations) node: For example, to use the Campaign Manager PerformOperations method the namespace declarations would be similar to: <PerformOperations xmlns="http://EmersonProcess.WebServices/PerformOperations" xmlns:dc="http://EmersonProcess.WebServices/CampaignManager/DataContracts" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Note: Always set the namespace xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance". Customizing PerformOperations You can add XML nodes that are not defined by the web service schema. To use this feature, you must supply a stylesheet (XSL file) to transform the custom XML node/data to web service-compliant XML. You can optionally provide a schema to validate the custom XML node: You can add custom schemas and stylesheets by setting the customSchema, customXslt attributes and/or CustomSchema, CustomXslt node. Add these attributes and nodes under the PerformOperations node or Operation node. When using a custom schema and/or stylesheet, set the useCustom attribute of the Operation node to be transformed to True. CustomSchema and CustomXslt elements must contain the schema or stylesheet inside a CDATA node. Set the customSchema and customXslt attributes to the path of the schema or stylesheet. Combinations of attribute and node are allowed. For example: CustomSchema and CustomXslt nodes <CustomSchema> <![CDATA[ ...insert schema here... ]]> </CustomSchema> <CustomXslt> <![CDATA[ ...insert stylesheet here... ]]> </CustomXslt> CustomSchema and CustomXslt attributes <Operation xsi:type="GetListOfAssignedBatchExecutives" customSchema="\\soa12\xsd\CustomRecipeinfo.xsd" customXslt="D:\xsl\CustomRecipeinfo.xslt" useCustomXslt="true" > Combination <Operation xsi:type="GetListOfAssignedBatchExecutives" customXslt="\\soa12\xsl\CustomRecipeinfo.xslt" useCustomXslt="true" > <CustomSchema> <![CDATA[ ...insert schema here... ]]> </CustomSchema> When inserting XML inside a CDATA tag, omit the XML declaration: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> This applies to custom schemas and stylesheets and Recipe Exchange import. If you set the schema or stylesheet under the PerformOperations node, they can be applied to any Operation node (global). If you set the schema or stylesheet under the Operation node, they apply only to that Operation node (local) and override any global schema or stylesheet. The custom schema validates only the child nodes of the Operation node. Additional attributes to the Operation node are not allowed. See the examples. The custom stylesheet transforms the entire Operation node. Make sure that the resulting XML's root node is Operation and that it retains the xsi namespace alias and declaration as well as the xsi:type attribute. Also, make sure the resulting XML passes the web service schema validation. See the examples. Examples CustomRecipeInfo.xml <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <!-- Note: Sample XML for custom transformation. This XML file will not run if used directly in the Recipe Exchange Web service. --> <Operation xsi:type="GetBatchExecutive" useCustom="true" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" > <rs:recipeInfo recipeType="Procedure" recipeName="PRC_PAINT" xmlns:rs="http://tempuri.org/RecipeSchema.xsd"/> </Operation> CustomRecipeInfo.xsd <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <xs:schema id="recipeInfo" targetNamespace="http://tempuri.org/RecipeSchema.xsd" elementFormDefault="qualified" xmlns="http://tempuri.org/RecipeSchema.xsd" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <xs:complexType name="recipeInfoType"> <xs:sequence> </xs:sequence> <xs:attribute name="recipeType" type="xs:string" /> <xs:attribute name="recipeName" type="xs:string" /> </xs:complexType> <xs:element name="recipeInfo" type="recipeInfoType"> </xs:element> </xs:schema> CustomRecipeInfo.xslt <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" xmlns="http://EmersonProcess.WebServices/PerformOperations" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" > <xsl:output method="xml" encoding="UTF-8" indent="yes" omit-xml-declaration="yes"/> <xsl:template match="Operation"> <xsl:element name="{local-name()}"> <xsl:apply-templates select="@type | @xsi:type" mode="xsi" /> <xsl:apply-templates select="@useCustom" mode="attribute" /> <!-- add other Operation attributes that will be retained or added here--> <!-- do custom transformations here --> <xsl:apply-templates select="*"/> </xsl:element> </xsl:template> <!-- ignore CustomSchema and CustomXslt elements --> <xsl:template match="CustomSchema | CustomXslt"/> <xsl:template match="@*" mode="attribute"> <xsl:attribute name="{name()}" > <xsl:value-of select="."/> </xsl:attribute> </xsl:template> <xsl:template match="@*" mode="xsi"> <xsl:attribute name="xsi:{local-name()}"> <xsl:value-of select="."/> </xsl:attribute> </xsl:template> <xsl:template match="@*"> <xsl:element name="{local-name()}"> <xsl:value-of select="."/> </xsl:element> <xsl:apply-templates/> </xsl:template> <xsl:namespace-alias result-prefix="xsi" stylesheet-prefix="xsi"/> <xsl:template match="*"> <xsl:element name="{local-name()}"> <xsl:apply-templates select="@*|node()"/> </xsl:element> </xsl:template> </xsl:stylesheet>

title: Soft phase application example
body_text: Soft phase application example The following is an example of how you can use Soft Phases in your batch process. This is only an example and learning tool. Soft phases are programs running on the PC that behave like controller based phases. Soft phases can be included in recipes just like any other phase in the DeltaV system. These phases are configured using predefined Visual Basic (version 6), VB .NET, Visual C++ (version 6) and VC .NET shells that include predefined function calls for common needs. The example soft phase issues a series of prompts to the operator. These prompts request the lot number and amount of color stabilizer to add to the batch. The sample code checks the color stabilizer file (an XML file, color_stabilizer_db.xml) to determine if the material exists, if there is enough of the requested lot number available, and verifies that the material's expiration date has not been exceeded. If all conditions are met, the soft phase allows the recipe to continue. If even one condition is not met, then the soft phase relays this information back to the operator. At this point the operator can choose to proceed with entered information (lot number and quantity) or can enter another selection. Note: You must create the color_stabilizer_db.xml file for use with the sample soft phase application. This application shows interaction with external control (the operator and a soft phase) and an information system (a text file). You can expand this example to show interaction with other external controls and information systems, such as the following: Material and inventory databases Barcode readers LIMS systems This might also include manual processing steps required by the batch, which means you can easily capture historical data, electronic signatures and operator comments for these types of activities and have them included in the electronic batch record. Subtopics: Soft phase application example code The color_stabilizer_db.xml file Related information DeltaV Soft Phases Writing soft phases The color_stabilizer_db.xml file

title: DeltaV Soft Phases
body_text: DeltaV Soft Phases The DeltaV Soft Phase is an executable that can exist on a DeltaV or a non-DeltaV node. In order to create a DeltaV Soft Phase, you must install the DeltaV Soft Phase environment. This environment consists of 3 elements, the Soft Phase Broker, the Soft Phase DLL and the user written Soft Phase application (the executable file). The Soft Phase Server (which is automatically installed on the DeltaV Batch Executive) is launched by the Batch Executive to execute the soft phase. Soft phases are written in any of the following: Visual C++ VC .NET Visual Basic VB.NET (single threaded) VB.NET (Multithreaded) Note: You must compile the soft phase as a 32-bit application as DeltaV is currently a 32-bit application, even when it is running on a 64-bit operating system. Templates are supplied when using the CreateSoftPhase.exe application to create your soft phase. A DeltaV Soft Phase can run on any node that can communicate on the DeltaV network, as a DeltaV or a non-DeltaV node. When configuring the soft phase in DeltaV Explorer, on the External Phase Properties dialog, you will select SoftPhase as the external phase server and enter the name of the workstation where the soft phase will run. This information is downloaded to the Batch Executive through the association of the soft phase to a phase class. Important: DeltaV Soft Phase executables are not redundant, even when the batch executing the soft phase is being controlled by a Batch Executive on a Redundant Batch pair. The supported machine to run a DeltaV Soft Phase executable is on a simplex node. The node can be the Batch Executive node provided it is a simplex Batch Executive ; or, the node can be another DeltaV workstation or a non-DeltaV workstation. The soft phase executable should not reside on any workstation that is part of a DeltaV redundant subsystem pair, either Redundant Batch or Redundant OPC. The redundant subsystem pair must be dedicated to running the redundant subsystem and no other executables should be run on this pair. Because the soft phase executable is not redundant, the soft phase cannot switch over in the event of a switchover of the redundant subsystem and the soft phase would cease executing forcing the batch into HELD. The batch might not be recoverable at this point. Keeping the soft phase on a simplex node ensures the continued execution of the soft phase in a Redundant Batch system in the event of a Batch Executive switchover. Subtopics: Install the Soft Phase environment The Soft Phase Server The Soft Phase Broker The Soft Phase DLL The Soft Phase application The Soft Phase Tester Soft phase application example Related information Running Soft Phases on a non-DeltaV node

title: Soft phase test parameters
body_text: Soft phase test parameters You can configure the parameters needed for the soft phase once you have opened or created a new test file. Download parameters are those parameters configured in the recipe that are normally downloaded to the controller. When using the Soft Phase Tester, you do not have access to any of the recipe parameters. If you require data from one of these parameters, you need to configure that parameter as a download parameter and enter the value. You can change the value when running the soft phase by entering a new value in the editable field in the list of parameters. The report parameter is configured in the soft phase and can be tested by including it in the Report Parameters. This tracks the value of the parameter as would be reported when using the Batch Executive. You can add new parameters or modify existing parameters. To add a parameter, click Add from the parameter dialog. Enter the name of the parameter, select the type from the list, and, if valid, enter the default value. If you are modifying an existing parameter, select the parameter from the parameter dialog list and click Modify . Change the values as required and click OK .

title: Software updates
body_text: Software updates The DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility upgrades DeltaV controllers, remote I/O nodes, I/O modules, CHARMs, DeltaV SIS components, and H1 fieldbus device firmware , as well as RS3 and PROVOX interfaces, by downloading a new software image to specific controller cards and devices in the DeltaV system. Refer to the online help for information on using the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility. Important: The upgrade process can have serious negative effects if it is not performed properly. Only qualified personnel should attempt device upgrades. The best practice is to upgrade the controller before upgrading the I/O (including CIOCs and CHARMs) rather than upgrading the controller and the I/O at the same time. Unpredictable behavior can result if you upgrade the controller and I/O at the same time (including CIOCs and CHARMs). To run the utility, click Start > DeltaV Installation > Controller Upgrade Utility . Upgrading Controllers and Remote I/O Nodes To successfully upgrade controllers, including SIS (SZ) controllers, and remote I/O nodes, you must know the controller name as well as the name and location of the controller upgrade file (filename.udf). The upgrade file contains all the information you need to perform the upgrade successfully. Run the utility to view controller and I/O card revision information and to identify the controller visually before upgrading. For more information, refer to the online help for the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility. Upgrading I/O Modules To upgrade I/O modules successfully, you must know the controller name and the name and location of the I/O module upgrade file (filename.idf). In addition, the Passthrough Message Server (PTM) must be installed and running. Contact your system administrator to be sure the PTM server is available. Refer to the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility's online help for more information. Note: All cards except the Series 1 Discrete cards can be upgraded. Upgrading Fieldbus H1 Device Firmware The DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility supports upgrading the firmware in one or more H1 fieldbus devices. Only devices that are commissioned or in standby are available for upgrading. H1 fieldbus devices with a Download class of "1" may be upgraded while they are commissioned; it is not necessary for them to be in Standby mode. These devices are frequently referred to as "Class 1 devices." Class 2 and Class 3 devices, however, must be put in Standby before upgrading. To upgrade an H1 fieldbus device, you must know the port to which the device is connected and the name and location of the upgrade file (filename.ffd). Software upgrade files are supplied by the device manufacturer and should not be modified or renamed. You have the option of downloading and immediately activating the upgrade software or downloading and then activating at a later time. You can also revert to a previous version of the software still saved in the device. When you want to download new software to a device, the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility gives you the option to select an upgrade file and let the system find the devices that can be upgraded with it or to select the devices and then select an upgrade file for each device. Refer to the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility's online help for more information on upgrading H1 fieldbus devices. Upgrading SIS Components To upgrade Logic Solvers, SISNet Repeaters, CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers, and LS CHARMs select the DeltaV SIS Components option from the drop-down list on the opening window of the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility program. Be sure that the Logic Solver is decommissioned and the controller with which it is communicating is commissioned before starting the upgrade process. For more information, refer to the online help for the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility. SIS Controllers (SZ model) are not upgraded under SIS components but are upgraded under controllers.

title: Sounding the horn with alarms
body_text: Sounding the horn with alarms Each alarm banner, alarm picture (AlarmList.grf for example), and node status object is capable of sounding a horn for any of the alarms that are displayed. Each alarm display has its own way of being configured for having the alarm horn sound or not sound. DeltaV Operate provides you with flexibility in configuring when and which alarms will sound the horn. You will need to be familiar with alarm priorities, User_Ref/UserSettings file and the various alarm banners and pictures to configure sounding the horn. Alarm Banners (AlarmBan.grf, AlarmBan_HAC.grf and so on) all have a Silence Horn button. The operator can silence the horn for an alarm at runtime. Alarm banners also have a Disable Horn and Enable Horn buttons. Again, this allows the operator to silence the horns at runtime. You can also turn off the alarm horn for all operators at all workstations by configuring the User_Ref (UserSettings.grf) file. Uncomment the line: frsVariables.gs_ab_hornEnabled.currentValue = "hornDisabled" or frsVariables.gs_ab_hornEnabled.currentValue = "hornEnabled", depending on whether you want the horn on or off for all alarm banners. Embedded Alarm Summary Control on AlarmBan_HAC.grf has the alarm sound turned on by default. This control sounds the alarm horn for the hardware alarms. To enable/disable the sound, select the control on the alarm banner picture in configure mode. Right-click and select Properties . Select the Layout tab and select/deselect the Sound Horn option. Node Status object embedded on the AlarmBan.grf can have the alarm horn sound turned on or off. You can also set which alarm priorities sound the alarm. In the UserSettings.grf file, The "frswritevalue "0", "DVSYS.THISUSER/NODES[1].A_HPRI" setting will turn off all node status alarm sounds. Change the "0" value to any alarm priority number (4 through 15) and the horn will sound for the specified priority. Alarm Pictures (AlarmList, AlarmSum, AlarmFilter, AlmSupp) have a configuration option to turn on/off the sound for alarms. Each picture can be configured differently so that you can have the horn sound for the AlarmList picture, but not the AlarmFilter picture. To enable/disable the sound, open the picture in configure mode. Right-click and select Properties . Select the Layout tab and select/deselect the Sound Horn option.

title: Source linkage and Batch Historian administration
main_heading: Source linkage and Batch Historian administration
body_text: Source linkage and Batch Historian administration Within the DeltaV system, process history data and batch history data are collected and stored in different databases. However, the ability to view process trend and alarm and event data with respect to a batch is a common request. For example, when a batch report is generated, it is useful to have the report include trends, alarms, and other events that are relevant to that batch. Source Linkages are the key to creating this type of report. Source Linkages link data stored in the Continuous Historian database (process history) to data stored in the Batch Historian database (batch history) and are typically used by Batch Historian clients to retrieve process history data related to one or more batches. Each Source Linkage defines a relationship between equipment used by a batch (such as a tank) and any modules used to control the process (such as a level indicator on the tank). Source Linkages allow users or applications to view how process history relates to batch history. You can use Source Linkages to retrieve two types of process history data: alarm and event data and continuous (trend) data. Process alarm and event data can be stored in the Batch Historian database along with batch event data. To store alarm and event data in the Batch Historian database, configure the Batch Historian to use the alarms and events collected on a workstation as an input source. (Refer to The Batch Historian Properties topic for information on configuring the Batch Historian). Once the alarm and event data has been stored, use Source Linkages to retrieve the relevant alarms and events for any batch. Continuous (trend) data is stored in a separate database from alarm and event data and batch data. Like alarm and event data, you can use Sources Linkages to retrieve the relevant continuous data for any batch. Note: Batch History View does not require Source Linkage data. The Process Trend , Process Events , or Process Trend Comparison menu option can be used to display data for any DeltaV module, regardless of whether or not a Source Linkage has been created for that module. Related information The Batch Historian properties

title: Specifying which events and alarms are recorded
main_heading: Specifying which events and alarms are recorded
body_text: Specifying which events and alarms are recorded A workstation records alarms and events for the areas listed under the Alarms and Events subsystem. It is practical to record alarms and events for the areas that match the operator span of control. If an operator on Op_Station_1 has control of Areas 1, 2 and 3, these areas should probably be included in the Alarms and Events Subsystem on Op_Station_1 . This allows the operator to view and query events records quickly on the local machine, without having to see records from other areas or connect to another system to view records. At the same time, it may also be helpful to set up the ProfessionalPLUS workstation to record the alarms and events for the entire system. This enables operators to query records across all areas when necessary. Note: In order for alarms and events to be recorded for the entire system, AREA_A must be assigned to the ProfessionalPLUS, all Operator stations, and any Remote Client sessions configured on these workstations. A configuration like the one shown below enables operators to view and query records within their span of control on their local machine while enabling anyone to view or query all records by connecting to the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. title: Specifying conditions with the Expression Assistant
main_heading: Specifying conditions with the Expression Assistant
body_text: Specifying conditions with the Expression Assistant The motor should shut off if any of the following three conditions occurs: The block valve is closed. The tank level is less than 100 gallons. The regulatory valve is less than 5 percent open. Now we need a way to specify these requirements. The condition blocks serve this purpose. Each condition will have associated with it an expression that identifies the condition precisely in mathematical or logical terms. Expressions are made up of operands, operators, functions, constants, and keywords. Two guidelines for writing an expression for a condition are: The expression must end with a semi-colon (;). Parameter values must be enclosed by single quotes ('). The DeltaV system provides an Expression Assistant to help you define expressions. After you enter an expression, the Expression Assistant checks the syntax, indicates any problems, and identifies any unresolved parameters. You can access the Expression Assistant using either the Object menu or the right-click context menu for Action, Calculation/Logic, and Condition function blocks. The Expression Assistant inserts the characters shown in the following table when constructing expressions. If you type the expressions without using the Expression Assistant, you need to use these characters in the same way. Characters Use Example / Precedes a reference to an internal parameter (one within the current module). Use the Insert Internal Parameter button to browse for these parameters. ^/ Precedes a reference to an internal parameter up one block level. Use the Insert Internal Parameter button to browse for these parameters. // Precedes a reference to an external parameter (one within another module). Use the Insert External Parameter button to browse for these parameters. '//XV-101/DC1/PV_D.CV' # # In Batch processing, used to enclose an alias. : Used to separate a named set from the named set value. 'vlvnc-sp:OPEN' := Used to assign values. Step actions use this operator. The value of the right operand is assigned to the left operand. 'SP':='SFCCTRL:IDLE' = Used to compare values. Similar operators include >, <, >=, <=,!= (not equal to), <> (not equal to). Transitions use these operators. 'SP'='SFCCTRL:START' + Used to add numeric values or to concatenate strings. ' ' Single quotes are used to enclose parameters. " " Double quotes are used to enclose strings. ; Used to continue action statements on subsequent lines of the Expression Assistant. Subtopics: What are parameter tagnames? Specify interlock conditions on condition blocks Specify the DSTs for MTR-101

title: Specify interlock conditions on condition blocks
main_heading: Specify interlock conditions on condition blocks
body_text: Specify interlock conditions on condition blocks In this procedure, we will use the Expression Assistant to specify the interlock conditions on the three condition blocks. On the View tab, in the Windows group, click Arrange so that you can see all the views again. Select the CND1 block, right-click it, and then select Expression from the context menu to open the Expression Assistant. . Highlight and delete the entire first line of the expression. (The default first line is "FALSE". ) Click the External Parameter button. This button browses for parameters that are external to the current parameter. The Browse dialog opens. Open the TANK-101 area. Double-click these items in each succeeding level: XV-101, DC1, PV_D and CV. The Expression Assistant assembles the tagname and puts it in the Expression box. Click or type "=". Click Named State , double-click the named set vlvnc-pv, select the state CLOSED , and then click OK . Type a semicolon at the end of the expression. The completed expression now reads as follows: '//XV-101/DC1/PV_D.CV' = 'vlvnc-pv:CLOSED'; XV-101 is the module for the block valve; DC1 is the function block; PV_D.CV is the current value for the process value; and CLOSED is one of the states in the named set, vlvnc-pv. The expression indicates that an interlock should occur (the motor should shut off) if the block valve is closed. (A named set is simply a way to define names and equate them to integer values. Named sets are defined in DeltaV Explorer under System Configuration > Setup .) Click Parse . The Expression Assistant checks the syntax. If there are any errors, correct them. Click OK . Select the CND2 block and use the Expression Assistant to specify the second interlock condition as: '//LI-101/AI1/PV.CV'< 100; LI-101 is the control module for the level indicator. AI1 is the analog input function block. PV.CV is the parameter for the analog input current value. The expression indicates that an interlock should occur (the motor should shut off) if the tank level goes below 100 gallons. Click Parse , correct any errors, and then click OK . Select the CND3 block and use the Expression Assistant to specify the third interlock condition (the regulatory valve is less than 5 percent open) as: '//FIC-101/PID1/PV.CV' < 5; FIC-101 is the module for controlling the outlet flow (regulatory) valve. PID1 is the loop function block. PV.CV is the parameter indicating the current state of the valve (percent open). The expression indicates that an interlock should occur if the valve is less than 5 percent open. Click Parse , correct any errors, and then click OK .

title: Specifying unit parameter values
body_text: Specifying unit parameter values When we defined the COLOR unit class, we set up a unit parameter to define the capacity of the color tanks and gave it a default value of 500. Now that we have individual color unit modules, we can specify a different value for each tank's capacity by editing the unit parameter properties for the unit module.
