title: Prompting for a parameter reference substitution string for Process History View
main_heading:
Prompting for a parameter reference substitution string for Process
    History View
body_text: Prompting for a parameter reference substitution string for Process History View Parameter: /prompt The prompt parameter is identical to the sub parameter, except that it starts the DeltaV Browser to select a module. Then, like the sub parameter, it replaces modules existing in the chart with the module selected in the browser. The string following the prompt parameter is the starting location for the browser. This can be any string but is typically the area where the expected module resides (for example, AREA_A). If the area is unknown, enter any string that does not match an existing area (for example, /prompt NONE ). It is also a good idea to put a default value with the prompt parameter. If the user presses the Cancel button while browsing, the default value is used in the substitution. Applies to: Chart and E+Chart Value: A single character string. If the string contains a hyphen (-) or a forward slash (/), enclose the entire string in parentheses or double quotes.

title: Pulse Input function block parameters
body_text: Pulse Input function block parameters The following table lists the system parameters for the Pulse Input function block: Pulse Input function block system parameters Parameter Units Description ABNORM_ACTIVE None The indication that a block error condition not selected in BAD_MASK (on the function block level) is True (active) or the indication that an error condition (at the module level) not selected in MERROR_MASK is True (Active) or a module status not selected in MSTATUS_MASK is True (Active). ALARM_HYS Percent or Percent of PV_SCALE The amount the alarm value must return within the alarm limit before the associated active alarm condition clears. ALARM_HYS is limited to 50% of scale. BAD_ACTIVE None The indication that a block error condition selected in BAD_MASK (at the function block level) is True (Active) or the indication that an error condition (at the module level) selected in MERROR_MASK is True (Active) or a module status selected in MSTATUS_MASK is True (Active). BAD_MASK None The set of active error conditions that triggers a user-defined Bad condition. The user selects a subset of block error (BLOCK_ERR) conditions in the BAD_MASK parameter. When any of these conditions are True, the BAD_ACTIVE parameter becomes True. When any of the BLOCK_ERR conditions that are not included in BAD_MASK are True, ABNORM_ACTIVE becomes True. BLOCK_ERR None The summary of active error conditions associated with the block. The possible block errors for the Pulse Input function block are Out of Service Input Failure/Bad PV Simulate Active FIELD_VAL Percent The value and status from the I/O card or from the simulated input when simulation is enabled. In the PIN function block, FIELD_VAL is the percent value of PV within the range defined by OUT_SCALE. HI_ACT None The result of alarm detection associated with HI_LIM. If HI_ACT equals True, HI_LIM has been exceeded. HI_HI_ACT None The result of alarm detection associated with HI_HI_LIM. If HI_HI_ACT equals True, HI_HI_LIM has been exceeded. HI_HI_LIM EU of PV The setting for the alarm limit used to detect the high high alarm condition. HI_LIM EU of PV The setting for the alarm limit used to detect the high alarm condition. INSPECT_ACT None Indicates if Inspect is enabled and one or more of the limits for the block have been exceeded. The normal value is 0. This parameter is set to 1 only if both of the following conditions are true: The Write To Inspect Alarm context menu item has been selected from Inspect for this block. With the Current Hour filter selected, Inspect indicates that an abnormal condition exists for Mode, Control, Input, or Variability. (Note that an abnormal condition exists for Variability only if both the Variability Index and the Standard Deviation have exceeded their defined limits.) IO_IN None Defines the input DST for the I/O channel used for the PV. LO_ACT None The result of alarm detection associated with LO_LIM. If LO_ACT equals True, LO_LIM has been exceeded. LO_LIM EU of PV The setting for the alarm limit used to detect the low alarm condition. LO_LO_ACT None The result of alarm detection associated with LO_LO_LIM. If LO_LO_ACT equals True, LO_LO_LIM has been exceeded. LO_LO_LIM EU of PV The setting for the alarm limit used to detect the low low alarm condition. MODE None Parameter used to request and show the source of the output used by the block. OUT EU of OUT_SCALE The primary value and status calculated by the block in Auto mode. OUT can be set manually in Man mode. OUT_SCALE None The high and low scale values, engineering units code, and number of digits to the right of the decimal point associated with OUT. In the PIN function block, it is used to back-calculate FIELD_VAL from PV. The configurer enters EU0 and EU100 fields of OUT_SCALE as the minimum and maximum values in engineering units per time units defined by TIME_UNITS PULSE_VAL None The number of engineering units per pulse. The block calculates PV from the frequency of pulses using PULSE_VAL and TIME_UNITS. PV EU of OUT Calculated using the RATE channel value (counts/sec) defined by the IO_IN parameter, the PULSE_VAL parameter value to convert to EU/sec, and the TIME_UNITS parameter to convert to EU per time units. PV_FTIME Seconds The time constant of the first-order PV filter. It is the time required for a 63% change in the FIELD_VAL to be reflected in the PV. SIMULATE EU of XD_SCALE Enables simulation and allows you to enter an input value and status. The SIMULATE value is used by the block only when SIMULATE_IN is not connected. SIMULATE_IN EU of XD_SCALE The input connector value and status used by the block instead of the analog measurement when simulation is enabled. If SIMULATE_IN is connected or has a manually entered value, SIMULATE_IN always overrides SIMULATE. Note: When SIMULATE_IN is wired from an input source on the function block diagram, it always overrides a manually entered value. STATUS_OPTS None Status options allow you to select options for status handling and processing. The supported status option for the Pulse Input function block is: Uncertain if Man mode. STDEV_CAP EU of OUT_SCALE or EU of PV_SCALE (reports in percent to Inspect) The estimated capability standard deviation (measurement of short term variation). An estimate of the least standard deviation the process could achieve ideally. STDEV_TIME Seconds The time frame over which STDEV and STDEV_CAP are performed. The default value of zero is good for most processes where the scan rate is no more than approximately 10 times faster than the time to steady state. If the process is relatively much slower, it is recommended that you enter the approximate time it takes for the process to return to steady state after a change. This ensures that the STDEV and STDEV_CAP calculations accurately consider the actual time constant of the process. STDEV EU of OUT_SCALE or EU of PV_SCALE (reports in percent to Inspect) The standard deviation of PV. For analog control blocks in AUTO, mean is assumed to be the SP. TIME_UNITS Selectable Time Unit - seconds, minutes, hours, or days Determines the factor used to convert EU/sec to the desired units of time in the PV calculation. Note: Default values and data type information for the parameters are available by expanding the Parameter View window. Related information Status options Inspect with InSight

title: Ramp function block parameters

ENABLE None The discrete input value and status that activates ramp calculation. The discrete input value and status that enables/ disables the ramp state machine and may activate ramping or alarm calculations. END_VALUE EU of IN The ramp endpoint input value and status. PAUSE None The discrete input value and status that stops ramp calculation. OUT and TIME_REMAIN are held at their last values. RAMP_RATE EU of IN per second The increase or decrease rate of ramp calculation. RAMP_TIME Seconds The time period for the output to ramp from IN to END_VALUE. title: Rate Limit function block parameters
body_text: Rate Limit function block parameters The following table lists the system parameters for the Rate Limit function block: Rate Limit function block system parameters Parameter Units Description DECR_LIMITED None When 1, indicates that OUT is not equal to IN due to a decreasing rate of change exceeding (being less than) DECREASE_MAX. Otherwise, the value is 0. DECREASE_MAX EU of IN per TIME_UNITS The maximum decreasing rate of change allowed for OUT. DECREASE_MAX must be a negative number. ENABLE None The discrete input that activates rate limiting. IN Determined by source The analog input value and status. INCR_LIMITED None When 1, indicates that OUT is not equal to IN due to an increasing rate of change exceeding (being greater than) INCREASE_MAX. Otherwise, the value is 0. INCREASE_MAX EU of IN per TIME_UNITS The maximum increasing rate of change allowed for OUT. INCREASE_MAX must be a positive number. LIMITED None When 1, indicates that OUT is not equal to IN due to an excessive rate of change. Is the logical OR of DECR_LIMITED and INCR_LIMITED. Otherwise, the value is 0. OUT EU of IN The analog output value and status. ROC EU of IN per TIME_UNITS The filtered rate of change of the IN parameter. ROC is an indication that is independent of the scan-to-scan rate of change used by the block algorithm to determine OUT. TIMECONST Seconds The time constant of the first order filter applied to the scan-to-scan rate of change calculation for the ROC parameter. TIME_UNITS Selectable time unit - seconds, minutes, hours, or days Determines the time units for the ROC parameter. Also used to convert INCREASE_MAX and DECREASE_MAX to units of EU/sec. title: Raw Data function (DvCHRaw)
body_text: Raw Data function (DvCHRaw) This worksheet function can be used to retrieve available samples for a single tag within a specified time period. The function must be entered as an array formula in a range that has the appropriate number of rows and columns. You can use the Configure Raw Data Function dialog in DeltaV Reporter to set up a call to this function. Syntax DvCHRaw(connection, tag, show_header, columns, time_mode, period_start, period_end, start_boundary, end_boundary, max_num_values) Example Array Formula =DvCHRaw("localhost","DeltaV=MAIN_WORKSTATION CHS250_1S/SGGN1/OUT.CV",TRUE,"Value;Timestamp,Local;Parameter Status,IsGood;Collection Status,Text","GMT","10/11/08 3:02:05 PM","10/12/08 3:02:05 PM",1,1,50) Function Arguments connection The node name of the DeltaV Continuous Historian server. tag The DeltaV tag for which you want to retrieve data. The tag can be text, such as FIC101.PV, or a cell reference. In the case of a cell reference (such as $A$1), the contents of the referenced cell must contain a valid tag. show_header A Boolean (TRUE or FALSE) that indicates whether or not you want the returned data to have a column header row. columns A string that defines the columns to be included in the worksheet. Column definitions are separated by semicolons. Each column definition comprises the column name and, optionally, various attributes relating to that specific column. Column attributes are separated by commas. The following columns and attributes are supported: Column name: Timestamp Mode attribute: Local, GMT, or GMT ±hh:mm Column name: Value For Int32, UInt32, and Float data types, the value stored by Excel is a Variant Double. For strings, the value stored by Excel is a Variant String. For enumerations, the value stored by Excel is the state name in a Variant String. Column name: Parameter Status (that is, FfStatus) Mode attribute. Valid modes are: Text – which yields a descriptive string, such as GoodNonCascade NonSpecific NotLimited IsGood – which yields a Boolean: TRUE if the parameter status is good, or FALSE if it is not good (that is, bad or uncertain) Number – which yields the raw value as an integer Column name: Collection Status (that is, DvCHStatus) Mode attribute. Valid modes are: Text – which yields a descriptive string IsGood – which yields a Boolean: TRUE if the collection status is good (that is, 0) or FALSE if it is not good (not zero) Number – which yields the raw value as an integer time_mode Indicates how the time stamp argument should be interpreted. The DeltaV Continuous Historian database records all times in GMT; the time_mode argument specifies what conversion, if any, should be applied to the supplied time stamp in order to convert to GMT. Local – the time stamp is treated as being in the time zone of the client PC. Conversion to GMT takes into consideration whether the time stamp falls within daylight saving time. GMT – no conversion is necessary GMT ±hh:mm – the time is adjusted by the specified hh:mm; daylight saving time has no effect. period_start The time stamp of the start of the period. Specify period_start as text or a cell reference. period_end The time stamp of the end of the period. Specify period_end as text or a cell reference. Note: If period_start is a later time than period_end, samples are retrieved in reverse chronological order from the (later) start time toward the (earlier) end time. If you specify the period_start or period_end argument as a cell reference, the cell must contain a valid date and time in standard Excel format, not exceeding millisecond precision—for example, "10/12/2008 21:06:40.676". start_boundary Defines how the start boundary is handled: If 0 (inside), the first sample returned is the first sample after (or at exactly the same time as) the period_start. If 1 (outside), the first sample returned is the first sample before (or at exactly the same time as) the period_start. If 2 (interpolated), an interpolated sample is created for the period_start time. end_boundary Defines how the end boundary is handled: If 0 (inside), the last sample returned is the first sample before (or at exactly the same time as) the period_end. If 1 (outside), the last sample returned is the first sample after (or at exactly the same time as) the period_end. If 2 (interpolated), an interpolated sample is created for the period_end time. max_num_values The maximum number of values you wish to retrieve. Any samples in the database within the time period in excess of this number are not retrieved. If max_num_values is set to –1, all samples within the time period are retrieved.

title: LS Redundant Terminal Block specifications
body_text: LS Redundant Terminal Block specifications Installation notes Each LS Redundant Terminal Block holds two LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant ETA) or LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant DTA) CHARMs. It provides the keying and field wiring connections for the LS CHARMs. Both LS CHARMs installed in the terminal block must be of the same type: either two LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant DTA) CHARMs or two LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant ETA) CHARMs The LS Redundant Terminal Block's keying mechanism sets itself to match the inserted LS CHARMs. Install the terminal block in an odd and even numbered slot on the baseplate. The lower slot number must be odd and the even slot number must be the next higher number (for example, slots 1 and 2 or slots 3 and 4). main_heading:
LS Redundant DTA Fused Injected Power Relay Terminal Block
	 specifications
body_text: LS Redundant DTA Fused Injected Power Relay Terminal Block specifications Installation notes Each LS Redundant DTA Fused Injected Power Relay Terminal Block holds two LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant DTA) CHARMs. It provides the keying and field wiring connections for the CHARMs and bussed power connections to implement high-side outputs. Bussed power is wired to the CHARM Address Terminal. The LS Redundant DTA Fused Injected Power Relay Terminal Block has a built-in relay. The LS Redundant DTA Fused Injected Power Relay Terminal Block has a replaceable fuse that protects the field wiring from short circuits. The fuse cannot be replaced when the terminal block is under power in a hazardous environment. The LS Redundant DTA Fused Injected Power Relay Terminal Block's keying is fixed to allow only LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant DTA) CHARMs. Install the terminal block in an odd and even numbered slot on the baseplate. The lower slot number must be odd and the even slot number must be the next higher number (for example, slots 1 and 2 or slots 3 and 4). This terminal block is used by a LS DO 24 VDC (Redundant DTA) CHARM when driving a final element that requires more than 500 mA and the baseplate's injected power bus rather than system power is required to power the field circuit. The test point is used to verify each contact individually. To verify one relay, place probes between the positive (+) on the CHARM Address Terminal and the test point. To verify the other relay, place probes between screw terminal 1 and the test point. title: Remote Interface Unit
body_text: Remote Interface Unit The Remote Interface Unit allows standard DeltaV I/O cards to be installed remotely from the controller. The remote subsystem, consisting of the Remote Interface Unit, system power supply, carriers, and I/O cards, can be located in Zone 2. The Remote Interface Unit communicates with the controller over redundant, Control Network (ethernet) connections. Specifications The following table shows specifications for the Remote Interface Unit. Item Specification Power requirement (supplied by system power supply through 2-wide power/controller carrier) +3.3 VDC at 500 mA maximum +5 VDC at 200 mA maximum Fuse protection 3.0 A, non-replaceable fuses Power dissipation 3.0 W maximum Mounting On right slot of power/controller carrier Connections and Dimensions The Remote Interface Unit mounts in the controller slot of a 2-wide carrier and has redundant ethernet connections to the DeltaV Control Network switch or hub. Connect the primary port to the primary switch or hub and the secondary port to the secondary switch or hub. The primary Control Network connection is capable of 10/100Mbit ethernet while the secondary connection is limited to 10Mbit ethernet. Remote Interface Unit Dimensions

title: Remote Desktop Gateway firewall ports to configure
main_heading: Remote Desktop Gateway firewall ports to configure
body_text: Remote Desktop Gateway firewall ports to configure The following ports must be configured on any firewalls between the Remote Desktop Client computer, the Remote Desktop Gateway (RD Gateway) computer, and the DeltaV workstation. Keep in mind the direction is relative to the originating computer. HTTPS on port 443 - Bidirectional between the RD Gateway and the DeltaV node. RDP on port 3389 - outbound from the RD Client and inbound to the RD Gateway computer. When using the Emerson Smart Firewall (such as between the RD Gateway and the DeltaV node) and when configuring the Windows Firewall on the DeltaV node, you can use the predefined rules that match the ports and direction.

title: Report parameter resynchronization
body_text: Report parameter resynchronization The following lists how changes to recipe report parameters affect warm and cold restarts with resynchronization. Modifying Active Steps, Warm Restart Modifying recipe report parameters on active steps causes warm restart with resynchronization to fail. Changing the recipe report parameter type (integer, real, named set or string) causes warm and cold restart with resynchronization to fail. Modifying Active Steps, Cold Restart Changing the recipe report parameter type (integer, real, named set or string) causes warm and cold restart with resynchronization to fail. Modifying recipe report parameters on active steps succeeds with cold restart with resynchronization, except in the case of changing the parameter type (integer, real, named set, or string), which fails resynchronization. Inactive Steps, Value Not Uploaded, Warm and Cold Restart Changing the recipe report parameter type (integer, real, named set or string) causes warm and cold restart with resynchronization to fail. Modifying recipe report parameters on inactive steps succeeds with warm and cold restart with resynchronization, except in the case of changing the parameter type (integer, real, named set, or string), which always fails resynchronization. Inactive Steps, Value Uploaded, Warm and Cold Restart Changing the recipe report parameter type (integer, real, named set or string) causes warm and cold restart with resynchronization to fail. Changing recipe report parameters causes warm and cold restart with resynchronization to fail except in the following two conditions: Changing an input parameter's origin from Value or Operator to Defer and deferring it to a report parameter succeeds Changing an input parameter to a report parameter (that is, deleting the input parameter and adding a report parameter of the same name).

title: Parameter values resynchronization chart
body_text: Parameter values resynchronization chart The following table defines the default recipe resynchronization behavior with changed parameters. Important: Modifying active steps will cause warm restart with resynchronization to fail. Formula Type Cold Restart with Resync (Resolve = Yes) Warm Restart with Resync (Resolve = Yes) Cold Restart with Resync (Resolve = No) Warm Restart with Resync (Resolve = No) <defaults> Formula existing parameters uses default value uses persisted value uses batch create value uses persisted value new parameters uses default value uses default value uses default value uses default value Custom Formula existing parameters uses batch create value uses persisted value uses batch create value uses persisted value new parameters uses default value uses default value uses default value uses default value Configured Formula existing parameters uses formula value uses persisted value uses batch create value uses persisted value new parameters uses formula value uses formula value uses default value uses default value Key Legend <defaults> Formula - The formula uses the parameter's default value. That is, either the formula parameter values were not configured prior to running the batch or the formula parameter values were not set by the operator when the batch was created. Custom Formula - The formula as created at runtime by the operator setting the formula parameter values. Configured Formula - The formula as created at configuration time; that is, the formula parameter values were configured using Recipe Studio or DeltaV Explorer. Batch create value - The initial parameter values when the batch is initially created. These can be different from the default values; for example, if the operator scaled the batch when creating it. Persisted value -The current runtime value of the parameter. Formula value - The value of the parameter from when it was created. This is only valid when the formula parameter value has been configured in Recipe Studio or DeltaV Explorer (Configured Formula).

title: Retentive Timer function block parameters
body_text: Retentive Timer function block parameters The following table lists the system parameters for the Retentive Timer function block: Retentive Timer function block system parameters Parameter Units Description ELAPSED_TIMER Seconds The elapsed time IN_D has been True (1). IN_D None The discrete input value and status. OUT_D None The discrete output value and status. RESET_IN None The reset discrete input value and status. TIME_DURATION Seconds Specifies the time duration IN_D must be True before OUT_D is set True. This value must be greater than the scan rate of the parent module. Note: Default values and data type information for the parameters are available by expanding the Parameter View window.

title: Recipe Exchange data contracts
body_text: Recipe Exchange data contracts Data contracts define complex data that can be exchanged with the service. Data contracts contain information required by the service to process the method invoked by the client. Recipe Exchange Web Service includes the following data contracts. tagRecipeType This data contract is an enumeration used as input to recipeType member in the data contracts. The values in this enumeration set contains a subset of what is defined in the API to limit the choices to those valid as recipe types. The following are the types valid as input to recipeType: OPERATION UNITPROCEDURE PROCEDURE tagExportType Recipe Exchange supports exporting of more than recipe types. This enumeration set lists all items that can be exported by Recipe Exchange that are valid as input to exportType: AREA AREAS CONTROL_MODULE CONTROL_MODULE_CLASS CONTROL_MODULE_CLASSES ENGINEERING_UNITS ENUMSETS EQUIPMENT_MODULE EQUIPMENT_MODULE_CLASS EQUIPMENT_MODULE_CLASSES EQUIPMENT_TRAIN EQUIPMENT_TRAIN_CLASS EQUIPMENT_TRAIN_CLASSES EQUIPMENT_TRAINS FORMULA NODE NODES NONE OPERATION OPERATIONS PHASECLASS PHASECLASSES PROCEDURE PROCEDURES PROCESSCELL PROCESSCELLCLASS PROCESSCELLCLASSES RECIPES SYSTEM UNIT_SELECTION_POLICIES UNIT_SELECTION_POLICY UNITCLASS UNITCLASSES UNITMODULE UNITPROCEDURE UNITPROCEDURES RecipeInfo RecipeInfo contains the basic information for recipe, recipe type and recipe name. This contract is used by methods requiring information about the recipe being processed. Member Purpose Type Required Input From Client recipeType The type of the specified recipe to be assigned to the batch executives of the specified workstations. tagRecipeType Yes recipeName The name of the recipe assigned to the batch executives of the specified workstations. If the recipe is in a category, this name should include the category. For example, operationFolder1/op1 and procedure1/formula1. string Yes ExportInfo The Export method uses this contract as an input parameter. The contract contains the export type and export name of the items requested by the client. Member Purpose Type Required Input From Client exportType The type of item/s to be exported. tagExportType Yes exportName The name of the specified item to be exported. string Yes ExportData The Export method uses this contract to return requested data to the client application. The contract contains a log string and the exported DeltaV XML configuration. Member Purpose Type Required Input From Client Log String containing information about the export string No exportedXMLConfig A string containing the XML that defines the exported item string No

title: Ethernet Isolation Ports specifications
body_text: Ethernet Isolation Ports specifications Installation notes The Dual Universal Safety Carrier and SZ Controller Carrier house a primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Port (EIP). When the Dual Universal Safety Carrier holds a Local Safety Network Bridge, each EIP consists of a Global Safety Network Port for connections to the Global Safety Network and a Safety Network port for connections to the Local Safety Network. When the Dual Universal Safety Carrier holds an SZ Controller, each EIP consists of an Area Control Network port for connections to the DeltaV Area Control Network and a Safety Network Port for connections to the Local Safety Network. When the Dual Universal Safety Carrier holds an SZ Controller for standalone safety applications, each EIP consists of a Modbus TCP port and a Safety Network Port for connections to the Local Safety Network. The EIPs are removable. To remove an EIP, depress the button next to the EIP and push it out of the carrier. Specifications Ethernet Isolation Port specifications Item Specification Redundant Ethernet connections (primary and secondary) Copper twisted pair: 10/100BASE-TX with RJ45 connectors; full duplex operation. Input power provided by installed component +5 VDC at 200 mA maximum Heat dissipation 1 W Image Ethernet Isolation Port Related information SZ Controller Carrier specifications Ethernet Isolation Port LEDs

title: Twisted pair network with DeltaV safety switches
main_heading: Twisted pair network with DeltaV safety switches
body_text: Twisted pair network with DeltaV safety switches Example safety network Callout Description 100 meter (maximum) straight-through or crossover cable. To prevent ground loops, build this cable assembly with a shielded, metal-enclosed RJ45 connector on one end and an isolated, plastic-enclosed RJ45 connector on the other end. The metal connector end of this cable assembly must be placed on the switch and not on the PC. 100 m (maximum) straight-through or crossover cable. The shield on the SZ controller's RJ45 connector connects only to a Faraday cage in the controller; not to the controller's DC ground. Therefore, the RJ45 connectors are floating and the single point of ground is made at the switch to which the controller is connected. Build this cable assembly with a shielded, metal-enclosed RJ45 connector on both ends. 100 m (maximum) straight-through or crossover cable. The shield on the CSLS RJ45 connector connects only to a Faraday cage in the CSLS; not to the CSLS DC ground. Therefore, the RJ45 connectors are floating and the single point of ground is made at the switch to which the CSLS is connected. Build this cable assembly with a shielded, metal-enclosed RJ45 connector on both ends. The SZ Controller completely isolates communications between the DeltaV Control Network and the Safety Network. External cabling should never be used to connect these two independent systems together. The RM100 Smart Switches are managed through the DeltaV console using the Network Device Command Center. The LSN20 safety switches cannot be managed through the Network Device Command Center. For network diagnostics for these switches, you must attach an optional serial cable to the serial port of the safety switch and use an application such as Hyper-terminal to access the switch information. No configuration of the safety switch is possible though the serial port. The switches are plug and play. Attach the ground screw of the switch to a suitable ground for the cable shields. Up to 16 CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS) can be connected within the Safety System architecture. In this example, the LSN20 switches, which have a low port count, are used but an SRM100 rack mounted safety switch with optional twisted pair port modules could be used so that the maximum of 16 CSLS can be attached. Related information Building twisted pair cable assemblies

title: Alarm information displayed
body_text: Alarm information displayed The following table describes the alarm information shown by the System Alarm Management application. Item Description Alarm name The name of the alarm as it appears on operator displays that reference it. For example, HI_HI_ALM. Type A set of characteristics that determine how the alarm appears in operator displays and in the Event Chronicle. Parameter The name of the module that contains the alarm and the parameter value that triggers the alarm. Limit value The value at which the alarm condition is true. Enable True - the alarm is eligible to become active. False - the alarm is ineligible to become active. Inverted True - the alarm characteristics are inverted. False - the alarm characteristics are not inverted. Priority A word such as critical, warning, or advisory, or any user-defined priority that indicates the importance of the event to the operator and the priority of the alarm at the workstation. %P1 Parameter Represents the first parameter value that appears in the alarm message. (This parameter is optional.) % P2 Parameter Represents the second parameter value that appears in the alarm message. (This parameter is optional.) Enable Delay Shows the time (in seconds) that is delayed before alarm processing begins. Processing begins immediately after the alarm is enabled (alarm_ENAB becomes true). The alarm_ACT parameter is forced to 0 for the time specified (in seconds). The timer resets whenever alarm_ENAB goes from zero to 1. On Delay The time (in seconds) that is delayed before alarm_ACT is set to true (1) after the alarm condition is detected. If the alarm condition clears before the delay time is reached, the alarm_ACT parameter remains false (0) and the timer is reset. Every time the alarm condition clears, the timer resets. Off Delay The time (in seconds) that is delayed before alarm_ACT is set to 0 (false) after the alarm condition clears. If the alarm condition reoccurs before the delay time is reached, the alarm_ACT parameter remains true (1) and the timer is reset. Every time the alarm condition is detected, the timer resets. Hysteresis Used as a deadband when resetting base alarm conditions for analog values. The block uses the value of alarm_HYS instead of the standard ALARM_HYS. When conditional alarm detection is enabled, the block uses ALARM_HYS as the deadband for deviation alarm conditions only. Days Timeout The days component of the alarm shelving timeout. The days, hours and minutes values are combined. Alarm shelving timeout resets this alarm to unshelved if it has been shelved for the specified timeout period. The days, hours and minutes values are totaled. Hours Timeout The hours component of the alarm shelving timeout. The days, hours and minutes values are combined. Alarm shelving timeout resets this alarm to shelved if it has been shelved for the specified timeout period. The days, hours and minutes values are totaled. Minutes Timeout The minutes component of the alarm shelving timeout. The days, hours and minutes values are combined. Alarm shelving timeout resets this alarm to unshelved if it has been shelved for the specified timeout period. The days, hours and minutes values are totaled. Functional Classification The functional classification assigned to this alarm. Alarm Help Whether or not help has been configured for this alarm.

title: abs function
body_text: abs function The abs function returns the absolute value of x . Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The absolute value of the given number. Syntax Math.abs( x ) Examples Example Result Assuming you have a module parameter, U012-FICA-5625-C/DELTA.CV, with a value of 1.2: var FlowChange = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DELTA.CV"]; this.Label = Math.abs(FlowChange); Returns "1.2". function difference(a, b) { return Math.abs(a - b) } Dsp.Button6.Label = difference(3, 5) Returns "2".

title: acos function
body_text: acos function The acos function returns the arc cosine of x as a value between 0 and pi radians. Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The arccosine (in radians) of the given number, if the given number is between -1 and 1. Otherwise, NaN. Syntax Math.acos( x ) Examples Example Result Assuming you have a module parameter, U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV, with a value of 0.5: var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.acos(Num); Returns "1.047". This script calculates the angle of a right-angle triangle, in radians: function calcAngle(adjacent, hypotenuse) { return Math.acos(adjacent / hypotenuse) } Dsp.Button8.Label = calcAngle(8, 10) Returns "0.6435011087932843".

title: ActiveAlarms function
body_text: ActiveAlarms function ActiveAlarms() returns the count of active alarms that are associated with the designated display and, optionally, within the specified priority level range. Arguments 1–4, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description DisplayName A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a display. ChildDisplays A literal or graphics expression whose value is interpreted as true or false. When evaluated to: True, the return count includes active alarms for the specified display, as well as from all direct and indirect child displays of the specified display in the display set. False, the return count includes active alarms in only modules, nodes, and devices whose primary control display is the specified display. If this argument is omitted or undefined, the assumed value is false. MinPriority A literal or graphics expression whose value is interpreted as a minimum priority level number. When this argument is present, the count returned includes only active alarms whose priority level is greater than or equal to this value. If this argument is omitted or undefined, the assumed value is the minimum active alarm priority. MaxPriority A literal or graphics expression whose value is interpreted as a maximum priority level number. When this argument is present, the count returned includes only active alarms whose priority level is less than or equal to this value. If this argument is omitted or undefined, the assumed value is the maximum active alarm priority. Return values (number) The number of active alarms that satisfy the argument criteria. 0, if DisplayName is not a primary control display for some module, node, or device in this DeltaV system. 0 with a bad data quality status, if DisplayName cannot be resolved. Syntax DARU.ActiveAlarms( DisplayName , ChildDisplays , MinPriority , MaxPriority ) Examples Example Result DARU.ActiveAlarms(DL.DN("Reactor1")) Shows the number of active alarms on the Reactor1 display. DARU.ActiveAlarms(Gem.DisplayName, true, 12,15); Shows the number of active alarms with a priority of 12 through 15 for all modules, nodes, and devices associated with the ??? display and its child displays.

title: AddSessionStoreItem function
body_text: AddSessionStoreItem function AddSessionStoreItem() stores data (JavaScript primitive values or objects) in a memory storage area for the duration of that DeltaV Live session. These data remain available in the storage area throughout the DeltaV Live session, even after the configuration is refreshed or reset. Normally, layout variables return to their configured initial values when a Deltav Live user performs a Refresh Configuration online. However, by calling AddSessionStoreItem() in a layout's "OnClose" event handling script and GetSessionStoreItem() in a layout's "OnOpen" event handling script, any layout-scope data that was called by AddSessionStoreItem() when the layout was closed is retrieved again by GetSessionStoreItem() when the refreshed layout reopens. Note: Calling AddSessionStoreItem() replaces any existing stored data having an identical key string. Arguments 2 Argument Description key string The unique name of the data item to be stored for retrieval by GetStoreItem(), within the scope of this instance of DeltaV Live. The key string is case sensitive. data item Any JavaScript primitive value or object. Return values None Syntax .AddSessionStoreItem( key string , data item ) Examples Example Result If you want the layout-scope variable, MyVar, to be added to the storage area for retrieval during a Refresh Configuration action, you could add the following expression to the layout's "OnClose" event handling script: DL.AddStoreItem("Lyt.MyVar", Lyt.MyVar) When the layout closes in DeltaV live, the value of the layout-scope variable, MyVar, is added to the storage area.

title: asin function
body_text: asin function The asin function returns the arc sine of x as a value between -pi/2 and pi/2 radians. Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The arcsine (in radians) of the given number, if it is between -1 and 1. Otherwise, NaN. Syntax Math.asin( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.asin(Num); Returns "0.523...". This script calculates the angle of a right-angle triangle, in radians: function calcAngle(opposite, hypotenuse) { return Math.asin(opposite / hypotenuse); } Dsp.Text1.Label = calcAngle(6, 10); Returns "0.6435011087932844".

title: atan2 function
body_text: atan2 function The atan2 function returns the arc tangent of the quotient ( y / x ) of its arguments, y and x , where the signs of y and x are used to determine the quadrant of the result. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from -pi to +pi. Arguments 2 Argument Description y First number. x Second number. Return value The arctangent of the quotient of the given arguments. Syntax Math.atan2( y , x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.atan2(8, Num); Returns "1.508...". Math.atan2(90, 15) Returns "1.4056476493802699". function calcAngleDegrees(x, y) { return Math.atan2(y, x) * 180 / Math.PI; } Dsp.Text2.Label = calcAngleDegrees(5, 5) Returns "45".

body_text: atan function The atan function returns the arc tangent of x as a numeric value between -pi/2 and pi/2 radians. Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The arctangent (in radians) of the given number. Syntax Math.atan( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.atan(Num); Returns "0.463...". This script calculates the angle of a right-angle triangle, in radians: function calcAngle(opposite, adjacent) { return Math.atan(opposite / adjacent) } Dsp.Text1.Label = calcAngle(8, 10) Returns "0.6747409422235527".

title: BlockName function
body_text: BlockName function BlockName() returns the name of the lowest-level block in the path, assuming the path argument also contains a parameter name. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A full or partial DeltaV parameter path. Return values (string) The substring between the second to last and last delimiter, when multiple block/parameter delimiters (/) are present. An empty string, otherwise. Syntax DLPATH.BlockName( path string ) Examples Example Result DLPATH.BlockName("ZONE1%FIC101/PID1/MODE.ACTUAL.STR") Returns "PID1" as a string. DLPATH.BlockName("THISUSER/ALMCNT[12][15].CV") Returns "". DLPATH.BlockName("TIC200/BLK1/BLK2/OUT") Returns "BLK2" as a string.

title: BlockPath function
body_text: BlockPath function BlockPath() returns the full path through the lowest-level block in the path, assuming the path argument also contains a parameter name. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A full or partial DeltaV parameter path. Return values (string) The substring preceding the last delimiter, when multiple block/parameter delimiters (/) are present. An empty string, otherwise. Syntax DLPATH.BlockPath( path string ) Examples Example Result DLPATH.BlockPath("ZONE1%FIC101/PID1/MODE.ACTUAL.STR") Returns "ZONE1%FIC101/PID1" as a string. DLPATH.BlockPath("THISUSER/ALMCNT[12][15].CV") Returns "". DLPATH.BlockPath("TIC200/BLK1/BLK2/OUT") Returns "TIC200/BLK1/BLK2" as a string.

title: Boolean function
body_text: Boolean function The Boolean function determines whether an expression or variable is true or false. Arguments 1, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description value? The initial value of the Boolean object. Return values (Boolean) True, if value? is true. Otherwise, false. Syntax Boolean( value? ) Examples Example Result Assuming that you have a module parameter, U012-FICA-5625-C/PID1/PV.CV, with a value of "20": var PV = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/PID1/PV.CV"]; this.Label = Boolean(PV > 45); Returns "false". Boolean(10 > 9) Returns "true".

title: Boolean object
body_text: Boolean object The following Boolean object function is supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopic under Boolean object for more details about this function. Function Description Syntax Boolean() Converts a value to a Boolean value. Boolean( value? ) Subtopics: Boolean function

title: ceil function
body_text: ceil function The ceil function returns x , rounded up to the nearest integer. Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The smallest integer greater than or equal to the given number. Syntax Math.ceil( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.ceil(Num); Returns "1". Math.ceil(.95) Returns "1". Math.ceil(7.004) Returns "8".

title: ClearSessionStore function
body_text: ClearSessionStore function ClearSessionStore() removes from the storage area all data retrieved by the AddSessionStoreItem() during this DeltaV Live session. Arguments 0 Return values None Syntax .ClearSessionStore() Examples Example Result Configure a click event on a button with the following expression: DL.ClearSessionStore() When the DeltaV Live user clicks the button, all data retrieved by the AddSessionStoreItem function during this DeltaV Live session is removed from the storage area.

title: concat function
body_text: concat function The concat function combines the characters in two or more strings and returns them as one new string. Arguments 0-n, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description str .concat( string1? , string2? , … , stringN? ) The strings to combine. Return values (string) A new string containing the combined text of the strings provided. Syntax str .concat( string1? , string2? , … , stringN? ) Examples Example Result var str1 = DLSYS["CONTROL1/VALUEPLUSEU.CV"]; this.Label = str1.concat(" avg"); Returns “105 g/liter avg”. var hello = 'Hello, '; Dsp.Text3.Label = hello.concat('Kevin', '. Have a nice day.'); Returns "Hello, Kevin. Have a nice day." on Text3's label.

title: CondRead function
body_text: CondRead function CondRead() reads a parameter path and returns either the parameter value or a specified fallback value (if the path fails the Exists() test). Arguments 2 Argument Description path string A literal or graphics expression that resolves to a DeltaV parameter path. fallback value The value to return if the path string does not exist (fails the Exists() test). Return values (string) The value of the specified path, if Exists() returns True. The specified fallback value, if Exists() returns False. Syntax DLSYS.CondRead( path string , fallback value ) Examples The examples in this table demonstrate how to use CondRead() to replace data that cannot be read (has 'bad' data quality) with a designated fallback value. Example Result DLSYS.condRead("MOD1/PID1/SP",DLSYS["MOD1/PID2/SP") The set point of MOD1's PID2 block. DLSYS.condRead("MOD1/PARAM1",DLSYS("MOD1/PARAM2") MOD2's PARAM2 This example demonstrates how to use CondRead() to extract bit-level data from data values that hold bit-packed information. Example Result Assume you have a running module that contains a Boolean Fan Output function block with four outputs. On a display, add a data link that allows online changes and whose expression is DLSYS["MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT.CV"] . Add a second data link with the following expression: DLSYS.WriteAsync("MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT", 16)Dsp.Text1.Label = DLSYS.condReadBit('MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT', 1, 1,'GoodNonCascade')Dsp.Text2.Label = DLSYS.condReadBit("MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT", 2,0)Dsp.Text3.Label = DLSYS.condReadBit("MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT",3,0)Dsp.Text4.Label = DLSYS.condReadBit("MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT",4,0)Dsp.Text5.Label = DLSYS.condReadBit("MOD2/BFO1/IN_INT",5,0) When the DeltaV Live user modifies the input value of the Boolean Fan Output block, the data link's label shows the bit-level data.

title: cos function
body_text: cos function The cos function returns the cosine of x in radians. Arguments 1 Argument Description x The angle in radians for which to return the cosine. Return value The cosine of the given number. Syntax Math.cos( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.cos(Num); Returns "0.877..." function getCircleX(radians, radius) { return Math.cos(radians) * radius; } Dsp.Text2.Label = getCircleX(1, 10) Returns "5.403023058681398". Math.cos(Math.PI) Returns "-1".

title: DARU (Display Alarm Roll-up) object
body_text: DARU (Display Alarm Roll-up) object The DARU object provides functions related to accessing information about alarms related to displays. The DARU object accesses this information through the a module's primary control display. The following DARU object functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopics under the DARU object for more details about each function. Functions for the DARU object Function Description Syntax ActiveAlarms() Returns the count of active alarms that are associated with the designated display and, optionally, within the specified priority level range. DARU.ActiveAlarms( DisplayName , ChildDisplays , MinPriority , MaxPriority ) SuppressedAlarms() Returns the count of suppressed alarms that are associated with the designated display and within the specified priority level range. DARU.SuppressedAlarms( DisplayName , ChildDisplays , MinPriority , MaxPriority ) TopAlarmPriority() Returns the priority level of the top active or unacknowledged alarms that are associated with the designated display. DARU.TopAlarmPriority( DisplayName , ChildDisplays ) TopAlarmState() Returns the alarm state (as a number) of the top active or unacknowledged alarms that are associated with the designated display. DARU.TopAlarmState( DisplayName , ChildDisplays ) UnackedAlarms() Returns the count of unacknowledged alarms that are associated with the designated display and within the specified priority level range. DARU.UnackedAlarms( DisplayName , ChildDisplays , MinPriority , MaxPriority ) Subtopics: ActiveAlarms function SuppressedAlarms function TopAlarmPriority function TopAlarmState function UnackedAlarms function

title: Date object
body_text: Date object The Date object can be used to represent arbitrary dates and times, get the current system date, and calculate differences between dates. The following Date object functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. Date object functions Date object syntax: new Date(); new Date( value ); new Date( dateString ); new Date( year , month? , day? , hours? , minutes? , seconds? , milliseconds? ); Function Description Syntax now () Returns the time value (as a number) designating the UTC date and time from the occurrence of the call to now. Date.now() parse() Parses a date string and returns the number of milliseconds since January 1, 1970. Date.parse( date string ) UTC() Returns the number of milliseconds in a date since midnight of January 1, 1970, according to Universal time. Date.UTC( year , month , day? , hour? , minute? , second? , millisecond? ) Subtopics: now function parse function UTC function

between UTC time and local time, in minutes. dateObj .getTimezoneOffset() getUTCDate() Returns the day of the month (1–31) for the specified date, according to universal time. dateObj .getUTCDate() getUTCDay() Returns the day of the week (0–6) for the specified date, according to universal time. dateObj .getUTCDay() getUTCFullYear() Returns the year (four digits for dates between year 1000 and .getUTCMonth() getUTCSeconds() Returns the seconds (0–59) for the specified date and time, according to universal time. dateObj .getUTCSeconds() Set functions setDate() Sets the day of the month (0-31) for a Date object, according to local time. dateObj .setDate( day ) setFullYear() Sets the full year (four digits for dates between year 1000 and 9999) for a specified date, according to local time. dateObj .setFullYear( year , month? , day? ) setHours() Sets the hours for a specified date, according to local time. dateObj .setHours( hour , min? , sec? , millisec? ) setMilliseconds() Sets body_text: toString function Converts a Date object into a string, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return value (string) A string representing the date and time of the Date object. Syntax Date .toString() Examples

title: toTimeString function
body_text: toTimeString function Converts the time portion of a Date object into a string, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (string) A string, representing the time portion of the Date object. Syntax dateObj .toTimeString() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.toTimeString(); Returns "13:45:55 GMT-0600 (Central Standard Time)” on the element's label. (The return value is adjusted for current local time.) With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var event = new Date('August 19, 1975 23:15:30'); Gem.Button2.Label = event.toTimeString(); Returns "23:15:30 GMT+0200 (CEST)" on Button2's label (Your time zone may vary.) With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var d = new Date(1993, 6, 28, 14, 39, 7); Dsp.Button1.Label = d.toTimeString(); Returns "14:39:07 GMT-0600 (PDT)" on Button1's label.

title: toUTCString function
body_text: toUTCString function Converts a Date object into a string, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return value (string) A string, representing the date and time of the Date object. Syntax dateObj .toUTCString() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.toUTCString(); Returns ”Wed Feb 28 2018 19:45:55 GMT” on the element's label. (The return value is adjusted for current date, in UTC.)

title: valueOf function
body_text: valueOf function Returns the primitive value of a Date object. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number, representing the number of milliseconds between the Date object and midnight January 1, 1970 UTC. Syntax Date .valueOf() Examples

title: DLPATH object
body_text: DLPATH object The DLPATH object provides functions for extracting tags, names, and sub-paths from typical DeltaV parameter/field addressing paths. Note: These functions operate only on the path string provided as an argument. They do not employ understanding of DeltaV configuration that may be present in the system. For example, the DLPATH object functions does not recognize whether names in the argument path are block names or parameter names, unless a field delimiter is present. Functions for the DLPATH object Function Description Syntax ZoneName() Returns the DeltaV Zone name, if one exists, from the path argument. DLPATH.ZoneName( path string ) TagName() Returns the name of the top-level block/parameter container (typically a module, node, or device name) from the path argument. DLPATH.TagName( path string ) BlockName() Returns the name of the lowest-level block in the path, assuming the path argument contains a parameter name. DLPATH.BlockName( path string ) ParameterName() Returns the name of the parameter in the path, assuming the path contains a parameter name. DLPATH.ParameterName( path string ) FieldName() Returns the parameter field name, if one exists. DLPATH.FieldName( path string ) TagPath() Returns the full path through the name of the top-level block/parameter container. The path also includes the DeltaV Zone name, if one exists. DLPATH.TagPath( path string ) BlockPath() Returns the full path through the of the lowest-level block in the path, assuming the path argument contains a parameter name. DLPATH.BlockPath( path string ) ParameterPath() Returns the full path of the specified parameter name from a DeltaV parameter path string. DLPATH.ParameterPath( path string ) Subtopics: BlockName function BlockPath function FieldName function ParameterName function ParameterPath function TagName function TagPath function ZoneName function

title: DLSYS object
body_text: DLSYS object The DLSYS object provides functions related to reading and writing DeltaV parameters that use the DeltaV Live parameter field path syntax, and that are accessible in or from this DeltaV system. Restriction: The DLSYS object works only with parameters using the DeltaV Live parameter field path syntax. For graphics configurations that have been migrated from DeltaV Operate and contain parameters using the DeltaV Operate syntax, use the DVSYS object and its functions. The following DLSYS object functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopics under DLSYS object for more details about each function. DLSYS object functions Function Description Syntax Exists() Determines if the parameter (and field) can be resolved and read, and then returns a Boolean value. DLSYS.Exists( path string ) CondRead() Reads a parameter path and returns either the parameter value or a specified fallback value (if the path fails the Exists() test). DLSYS.CondRead( path string , fallback value ) GetBit() Extracts the value of the specified bit from the test value. DLSYS.GetBit( test value , bit number ) Read() Reads the specified DeltaV parameter path and immediately returns the status of the read attempt, and if successful, the requested value. DLSYS.Read( path string ) ReadAsync() Reads the specified DeltaV Operate-style parameter path and immediately returns the status of the read attempt. DLSYS.ReadAsync( path string ) Subtopics: CondRead function Exists function GetBit function Read function ReadAsync function

In the table below, < CP > stands for the additional context or placement information. Functions for the DL object Function Description Syntax DN() Evaluates and returns the argument as a string. title: DN function
body_text: DN function DN() evaluates and returns the argument as a string. When the argument is a literal string, the DN() authorizes display rename tracking to automatically update the string argument to match the new name. If the argument is anything other than a single literal string, it does not participate in display rename tracking. Arguments 1 Argument Description DisplayName A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a display or contextual display. Return values (string) The name of a display or contextual display. Syntax DL.DN( display name ) Examples Example Result DL.DN("Reactor1") Shows the string, Reactor1. DL.OpenContextDisplay(DL.DN("Loop_fp"), "FIC-101") Opens the contextual display with the name Loop_fp, and with FIC-101 as the module name on the faceplate.

title: DVSYS object
body_text: DVSYS object The DVSYS object provides a means to use legacy DeltaV Operate syntax for parameter paths and path modifiers in DeltaV Live. It is recommended that you use the DVSYS Object and its functions only on graphics configurations that have been migrated from DeltaV Operate to DeltaV Live, and that you use the DLSYS object and its functions for graphics configurations created in DeltaV Live. DVSYS object functions Function Description Syntax Read() Reads the specified DeltaV parameter path and immediately returns the status of the read attempt, and if successful, the requested value. DVSYS.Read( path string ) ReadAsync() Reads the specified DeltaV Operate-style parameter path and immediately returns the status of the read attempt. DVSYS.ReadAsync( path string )

title: ENV object
body_text: ENV object The ENV object provides functions related to accessing information about the online environment (DeltaV system/workstation/session) within 'this' instance of DeltaV Live. The following EVN object functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopics under EVN object for more details about each function. Functions for the ENV object Function Description Syntax ZoneName() Returns the zone name for the local DeltaV system. ENV.ZoneName() NodeName() Returns the DeltaV workstation name hosting this instance of DeltaV Live. ENV.NodeName() UserName() Returns the user name for the currently logged on DeltaV user. ENV.UserName() FullUserName() Returns the full domain\user id for the currently logged on DeltaV user. ENV.FullUserName() IsBatchSystem() Returns True if Batch is enabled in this DeltaV system.
