title: Exists function
body_text: Exists function Exists() determines if the parameter (and field) can be resolved and read, and then returns a Boolean value. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A full or partial DeltaV parameter path Return values (Boolean) True, if the parameter path can be resolved and the parameter is read as a string. False, otherwise. Syntax DLSYS.Exists( path string ) Examples Example Result DLSYS.Exists("FIC101/CALC1/OUT3") True, if "FIC101/CALC1/OUT3" exists in this system. False, if "FIC101/CALC1/OUT3" does not exist in this system. DLSYS.Exists(Grp.Mod + "/OPT1") && DLSYS.Exists(Grp.Mod + "/OPT2") True, if both Grp.Mod + "/OPT1" and Grp.Mod + "/OPT1" exist in this system. False, if either Grp.Mod + "/OPT1" or Grp.Mod + "/OPT1" do not exist in this system.

title: exp function
body_text: exp function The exp function commands DeltaV Live to return the value of E to the power of x . Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value A number representing e x , where e is Euler's number. Syntax Math.exp( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.exp(Num); Returns "1.648...". Math.exp(-1) Returns "0.36787944117144233".

title: FieldName function
body_text: FieldName function FieldName() extracts and returns a specified parameter field name, if one exists, from a DeltaV parameter path string. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A full or partial DeltaV parameter path. Return values (string) The substring following the first field delimiter, when a field delimiter (.) is present. If any <read-as suffix> suffixes are included in the path, they are removed from the returned result. An empty string, otherwise. Syntax DLPATH.FieldName( path string ) Examples The following examples demonstrate how to extract a parameter field name from a DeltaV parameter path string and show it as the label on a text element. Example Result DLSYS.Text1.Label = DLPATH.FieldName("ZONE1%FIC101/PID1/MODE.ACTUAL.STR") Returns "ACTUAL" as the label text. DLSYS.Text2.Label = DLPATH.FieldName("THISUSER/ALMCNT[12][15].CV") Returns "CV" as the label text. DLSYS.Text3.Label = DLPATH.FieldName("TIC200/BLK1/BLK2/OUT") Returns "". DLSYS.Text4.Label = DLPATH.FieldName("ALARMS[1].PRI") Returns "PRI" as the label text. DLSYS.Text5.Label = DLPATH.FieldName("LIC330") Returns "".

title: floor function
body_text: floor function The floor function returns x , rounded down to the nearest integer. Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value A number representing the largest integer less than or equal to the specified number. Syntax Math.floor( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.floor(Num); Returns "0". Math.floor(5.95) Returns "5". Math.floor10(59, 1) Returns "50".

title: FullUserName function
body_text: FullUserName function FullUserName() returns the full domain\user id for the currently logged on DeltaV user. Note: FullUserName() returns the same string as the DeltaV Operate data link path, THISUSER/FULLUSERNAME.A_CV . Arguments 0 Return values (string) The domain (or workgroup) and user name for the DeltaV user currently logged on to the workstation/session where this instance of DeltaV Live is running. An empty string, when a DeltaV user is not currently logged on to the workstation/session. Syntax ENV.FullUserName()

title: GetBit function
body_text: GetBit function GetBit() extracts the value of the specified bit from the numeric value. Arguments 2 Argument Description test value A numeric value that holds bit-encoded information. bit number A number identifying the bit to be extracted from the < test value > . The < bit number > is rounded to an integer from 0 to 31, with 0 representing the least significant bit of the < test value > . Return values (Boolean) 0 or 1, the specified bit of the < test value > . The return value is equivalent to the JavaScript shift and bit mask operators, ( test value >>> bit number ) & 1 . Syntax DLSYS.GetBit( test value , bit number ) Examples Example Result DLSYS.GetBit(DLSYS["FIC101/PID1/BAD_ACTIVE.CV"],7) Bit 7 of FIC101/PID1/BAD_ACTIVE.CV DLSYS.GetBit(DLSYS.CondRead (DLSYS["MOD1/PID1/IO_OPTS.CV"],0),5)

title: getDate function
body_text: getDate function Returns the day of the month for the specified date, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–31), representing the day of the month. Syntax dateObj.getDate() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getDate(); Assuming the current date, local time, is March 7: Returns "7" on the element's label. This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var birthday = new Date("August 19, 1975 23:15:30"); this.Label = birthday.getDate(); Returns "19" on the element's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script on a Button1 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = Xmas95.getDate(); Returns "25" on Button1's label.

title: getDay function
body_text: getDay function Returns the day of the week for the specified date, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–6), representing the day of the week (where 0 represents Sunday). Syntax dateObj.getDay() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getDay(); // Sunday - Saturday: 0 - 6 Assuming the current date, local time, is Wednesday: Returns "3" on the element's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script on a Button1 action. var birthday = new Date("August 19, 1975 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = birthday.getDay(); // Sunday - Saturday : 0 - 6 Returns "2" on Button1's label. With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Gem.Button2.Label = Xmas95.getDay(); // Sunday - Saturday : 0 - 6 Returns "1" (represents Monday).

title: getFullYear function
body_text: getFullYear function Returns the year for the specified date, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (four digits for dates between year 1000 and 9999), representing the year of the specified date. Syntax dateObj.getFullYear() Example Example Result With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script on a Button1 action. var today = new Date(); Dsp.Button1.Label = today.getFullYear(); Assuming the current year, local time, is 2018: Returns "2018". This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var moonLanding = new Date("July 20, 69 00:20:18"); this.Label = moonLanding.getFullYear(); Returns "1969".

title: getHours function
body_text: getHours function Returns the hour for the specified date and time, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–23), representing the hour. Syntax dateObj.getHours() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getHours(); Assuming the current local time is 12:40: Returns "12". With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var birthday = new Date("March 13, 08 04:20"); Gem.Button2.Label = birthday.getHours(); Returns "4" on Button2's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = Xmas95.getHours(); Returns "23" on Button1's label.

title: getMilliseconds function
body_text: getMilliseconds function Returns the milliseconds for the specified date and time, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–999), representing milliseconds. Syntax dateObj.getMilliseconds() Example Example Result With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var today = new Date(); Dsp.Button1.Label = today.getMilliseconds(); Assuming the current local time is 12:39:18.789: Returns "789". With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var moonLanding = new Date("July 20, 69 00:20:18"); moonLanding.setMilliseconds(123); Gem.Button2.Label = moonLanding.getMilliseconds(); Returns "123" on Button2's label.

title: getMinutes function
body_text: getMinutes function Returns the minutes for the specified date and time, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–59), representing minutes. Syntax dateObj.getMinutes() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getMinutes(); Assuming the current local time is 12:39:18.789: Returns "39". With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var birthday = new Date("March 13, 08 04:20"); Gem.Button2.Label = birthday.getMinutes(); Returns "20" on Button2's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = Xmas95.getMinutes(); Returns "15" on Button1's label.

title: getMonth function
body_text: getMonth function Returns the month for the specified date, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–11), representing the month. Syntax dateObj.getMonth() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getMonth(); // (January = 0) Assuming the current month, local time, is February: Returns "1". With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var moonLanding = new Date("July 20, 69 00:20:18"); Gem.Button2.Label = moonLanding.getMonth(); // January = 0 Returns "6" on Button2's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = Xmas95.getMonth(); // January = 0 Returns "11" on Button1's label.

title: getSeconds function
body_text: getSeconds function Returns the seconds for the specified date and time, according to local time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–59), representing the seconds. Syntax dateObj.getSeconds() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getSeconds(); Assuming the current local time is 12:39:18.789: Returns "18". With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var moonLanding = new Date("July 20, 69 00:20:18"); Gem.Button2.Label = moonLanding.getSeconds(); Returns "18" on Button2's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = Xmas95.getSeconds(); Returns "30" on Button1's label.

title: GetSessionStoreItem function
body_text: GetSessionStoreItem function GetSessionStoreItem() retrieves data that has been stored, using AddSessionStoreItem(), during this DeltaV Live session. The data is retrieved when a DeltaV Live user performs a Refresh Configuration action. Normally, layout variables return to their configured initial values when a Deltav Live user performs a Refresh Configuration online. However, by calling AddSessionStoreItem() in a layout's "OnClose" event handling script and GetSessionStoreItem() in a layout's "OnOpen" event handling script, any layout-scope data that was called by AddSessionStoreItem() when the layout was closed is retrieved again by GetSessionStoreItem() when the refreshed layout reopens. Arguments 1 Argument Description key string The unique name of the data item to be retrieved from the storage area. The key string is case sensitive. Return values (any) If a data item with a matching key string supplied by an previous AddSessionStoreItem() is present, returns the primitive value or object that was stored. Otherwise, the configured default value. Syntax .GetSessionStoreItem( key string ) Examples Example Result If you want to retrieve the value for the layout-scope variable, MyVar, when the layout configuration is refreshed, you could use the following expression in the layout's "OnOpen" event handling script. let temp = DL.GetStoreItem("Lyt.MyVar"); if (temp !== undefined) Lyt.MyVar = temp; // recover it if in the store // else keep the initial value configured for my variable When the DeltaV Live user clicks the Refresh Configuration button, the variable, MyVar, retrieves the value stored by AddSessionStoreItem().

title: getTimezoneOffset function
body_text: getTimezoneOffset function Returns the time difference between UTC time and local time, in minutes. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number, representing the time difference between UTC and Local Time, in minutes. Syntax dateObj.getTimezoneOffset() Example Example Result With Text1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Text1 action. var d = new Date(); Dsp.Text1.Label = d.getTimeZoneOffset(); Returns "360" on Text1's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. // Get timezone offset for International Labour Day (May 1) in 2016 // January = 0 var labourDay = new Date(2016, 4, 1) Dsp.Button1.Label = labourDay.getTimezoneOffset() / 60;

title: getTime function
body_text: getTime function Returns the number of milliseconds between midnight of January 1, 1970, and the specified date. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number, representing the number of milliseconds since midnight January 1, 1970. Syntax dateObj.getTime() Example Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getTime(); Returns "1518028231579" on the element's label. With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var moonLanding = new Date("July 20, 69 00:20:18 GMT+00:00"); // milliseconds since Jan 1, 1970, 00:00:00.000 GMT Gem.Button2.Label = moonLanding.getTime(); Returns "-14254782000" on Button2's label.

title: getUTCDate function
body_text: getUTCDate function Returns the day of the month for the specified date, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–31), representing the day of the month. Syntax dateObj.getUTCDate() Examples Example Result With Text1 and Text2 on a display, this script is added to the display's "OnOpen" event handling script. var date1 = new Date("August 19, 1975 23:15:30 GMT+11:00"); var date2 = new Date("August 19, 1975 23:15:30 GMT-11:00"); Dsp.Text1.Label = date1.getUTCDate(); Dsp.Text2.Label = date2.getUTCDate(); Returns "19" on the Text1 label. Returns "20" on the Text2 label. This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCDate(); Assuming the current date, UTC time, is March 7: Returns "7" on the element's label.

title: getUTCDay function
body_text: getUTCDay function Returns the day of the week for the specified date, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–6), representing the day of the week. Syntax dateObj.getUTCDay() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCDay(); // Sunday = 0 Assuming the current day is Wednesday, UTC time: Returns "3" on the element's label. With Button1 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Button1 action. var Xmas95 = new Date("December 25, 1995 23:15:30"); Dsp.Button1.Label = Xmas95.getDate(); Returns "25" on Button1's label.

title: getUTCFullYear function
body_text: getUTCFullYear function Returns the year for the specified date, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (four digits for dates between year 1000 and 9999), representing the year. Syntax dateObj.getUTCFullYear() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCFullYear(); Assuming the current year, UTC time, is 2018: Returns "2018" on the element's label. With Text1 and Text2 on a display, this script is added to the display's "OnOpen" event handling script. var date1 = new Date("December 31, 1975, 23:15:30 GMT+11:00"); var date2 = new Date("December 31, 1975, 23:15:30 GMT-11:00"); Dsp.Text1.Label = date1.getUTCFullYear(); Dsp.Text2.Label = date2.getUTCFullYear(); Returns "1975" on the Text1 label. Returns "1976" on the Text2 label.

title: getUTCHours function
body_text: getUTCHours function Returns the hour for the specified date and time, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–23), representing the hour. Syntax dateObj.getUTCHours() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCHours(); Assuming the current UTC time is 12:40 p.m.: Returns "12" on the element's label. With Text3 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Text3 action. var today = new Date(); var year = today.getUTCFullYear(); Dsp.Text3.Label = year Assuming the current UTC time is 4:12 p.m.: Returns "16" on Text1's label.

title: getUTCMilliseconds function
body_text: getUTCMilliseconds function Returns the milliseconds for the specified date and time, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return value (number) A number (0–999) representing the milliseconds. Syntax dateObj.getUTCMilliseconds() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCMilliseconds(); Assuming the current UTC time is 12:39:18.789: Returns "789" on the element's label. With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var exampleDate = new Date('2018-01-02T03:04:05.678Z'); Gem.Button2.Label = exampleDate.getUTCMilliseconds(); Or, you can write the script this way: var exampleDate = new Date('2 January 2018, 03:04:05.678 (UTC'); // 2 January 2018, 03:04:05.678 (UTC) Gem.Button2.Label = exampleDate.getUTCMilliseconds(); Returns "678" on Button2's label.

title: getUTCMinutes function
body_text: getUTCMinutes function Returns the minutes for the specified date and time, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–59) representing the minutes. Syntax dateObj.getUTCMinutes() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCMinutes(); Assuming the current UTC time is 12:39:18.789: Returns "39" on the element's label. With Text1 and Text2 on a display, this script is added to the display's "OnOpen" event handling script. var date1 = new Date('1 January 2000 03:15:30 GMT+07:00'); var date2 = new Date('1 January 2000 03:15:30 GMT+03:30'); Dsp.Text1.Label = date1.getUTCMinutes(); Dsp.Text2.Label = date2.getUTCMinutes(); Or, you can write the script this way: var date1 = new Date('31 Dec 1999 20:15:30 GMT'); var date2 = new Date('31 Dec 1999 23:45:30 GMT'); Dsp.Text1.Label = date1.getUTCMinutes(); Dsp.Text2.Label = date2.getUTCMinutes(); Returns "15" on Text1's label. Returns "45" on Text2's label.

title: getUTCMonth function
body_text: getUTCMonth function Returns the month for the specified date, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number ((0–11), representing the month. Syntax dateObj.getUTCMonth() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCMonth(); Assuming the current month, UTC time, is February: Returns "1" on the element's label. With Text3 on a display, this script is added as a custom script to a Text3 action.s var today = new Date(); var month = today.getUTCMonth(); Dsp.Text3.Label = month Assuming the current month, UTC time, is November: Returns "12" on Text3's label.

title: getUTCSeconds function
body_text: getUTCSeconds function Returns the seconds for the specified date and time, according to universal time. Arguments 0 Return values (number) A number (0–59), representing the seconds. Syntax dateObj.getUTCSeconds() Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); this.Label = d.getUTCSeconds(); Assuming the current UTC time is 12:39:18.789: Returns "18" on the element's label. With Button2 nested inside a GEM, this script is added as a custom script on a Button2 action. var OpSwitch = new Date('July 20, 1969, 20:18:04 UTC'); Gem.Button2.Label = OpSwitch.getUTCSeconds(); Returns "4" on the Button2's label.

title: Global object
body_text: Global object The following Global object values and functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopics under the Global object for more details about each function. Global object values Name Description NaN Represents a "Not-a-Number" value and indicates that a value is not a legal number. Infinity A numeric value that represents positive infinity. Global object function Name Description Syntax parseInt() Parses a string argument and returns an integer of the specified radix (the base in mathematical numeral systems). parseInt( string , radix ) parseFloat() Parses a string and returns a floating point number parseFloat( string ) isNaN() Determines whether a value is an illegal number. isNaN( number ) isFinite() Determines whether a value is a finite, legal number. Number.isFinite( value ) Subtopics: isFinite function isNaN function parseFloat function parseInt function

title: indexOf function
body_text: indexOf function The indexOf function returns the position of the first found occurrence of a specified value in a string. Arguments 1–2, Optional arguments indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description search string A string representing the value to search for. position An integer specifying the position at which to start the search. If this argument is not present, 0 is assumed, and the entire string is searched. Return values (number) The position of the first occurrence of search string -1 , if the value to search for never occurs. If search string appears as a substring of the result of converting this object to a string, at one or more positions that are greater than or equal to position : Returns the index of the smallest such position. Syntax str .indexOf( search string , position? ) Examples Example Result var str1 = DLSYS["CONTROL1/VALUEPLUSEU.CV"]; this.Label = str1.indexOf("g"); Returns "4". 'Blue Whale'.indexOf('Whale', 0) Returns "5".

title: IsAdminUser function
body_text: IsAdminUser function IsAdminUser() returns True if the currently logged on DeltaV user is considered an administrator. Note: The .IsAdminUser function returns the same string as the DeltaV Operate data link path, THISUSER/IS_ADMIN_USER.B_CV . Arguments 0 Return values (Boolean) True, if the DeltaV user currently logged on to the workstation/session where this instance of DeltaV Live is running is an administrator. False, otherwise. Syntax ENV.IsAdminUserName() Examples Example Result if (ENV.IsAdminUser()) { // code to execute for administrators } If the currently logged on DeltaV user is an administrator on this machine, the "code to execute for administrators" is executed.

title: IsBatchSystem function
body_text: IsBatchSystem function IsBatchSystem() determines whether Batch is or is not enabled in this DeltaV system. Note: In DeltaV Live, the .IsBatchSystem function is comparable to the DeltaV Operate data link path, THISUSER/IS_BATCH.B_CV . Arguments 0 Return values (Boolean) True, if Batch is enabled in this DeltaV system. False, if Batch is not enabled in this DeltaV system. Syntax ENV.IsBatchSystem() Examples Example Result Add a data link and a button on a display. Configure an action for the button using the following custom script: let e = await ENV.IsBatchSystemAsync() If (e) { // yes for sure it is batch system, let’s do something with it } Write the Boolean value (True/False) to the button's label. On the data link, enter the expression, ENV.IsBatchSystem() If Batch is enabled on this system, the button label shows True . If Batch is not enabled on this system, the button label shows False .

title: isFinite function
body_text: isFinite function The isFinite function determines whether a value is a finite, legal number. Arguments 1 Argument Description string The string to be tested Return values (Boolean) False, if the value is +infinity, -infinity, or NaN . True, otherwise. Syntax Number.isFinite( value ) Examples Example Result isFinite("123") Returns "true" because 123 is a finite, legal number. isFinite("Hello") Returns 'false" because Hello is not a finite, legal number.

title: isNaN function
body_text: isNaN function The isNaN function determines whether a value is an illegal number. Arguments 1 Argument Description string The string to be tested. Return values (Boolean) True, if the value equates to NaN . False, otherwise. Syntax isNaN( string ) Examples Example Result isNaN('123ABC') Returns "true" because 123ABC is an illegal number. isNaN('123ABC') Returns "false" because parseInt converts 123ABC to a number; therefore, 123ABC is not an illegal number. isNaN("37,5") Returns "true" because 37,5 is an illegal number. isNaN('Hello') Returns "true" because Hello is an illegal number.

title: lastIndexOf function
body_text: lastIndexOf function The lastIndexOf function returns the position of the last found occurrence of a specified value in a string. Arguments 1–2, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. argument Description search string A string representing the value to search for. position? Specifies the position at which to start the search (searching backwards). If this argument is not present, 0 is assumed, and the entire string is searched. Return values (number) A number indicating the position of the last occurrence of search string . -1 , if the value to search for never occurs If search string appears as a substring of the result of converting this object to a string, at one or more positions that are smaller than or equal to position : Returns the index of the greatest such position. Syntax str .lastIndexOf( search string , position? ) Examples Example Result Assuming that you have a module parameter, CONTROL1/VALUE1AND2.CV, with a value of “T1=47 T2=67”. var str1 = DLSYS["CONTROL1/VALUE1AND2.CV"]; this.Label = str1.lastIndexOf("T"); Returns "6". 'canal'.lastIndexOf('a') Returns "3".

title: log function
body_text: log function The log function returns the natural logarithm (base E) of x . Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The natural logarithm (base e) of the given number. If the number is negative, NaN. Syntax Math.log( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.log(Num); Returns "-0.693". function getBaseLog(x, y) { return Math.log(y) / Math.log(x); } // 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 Dsp.Text3.Label = getBaseLog(2, 8); Returns "3" Math.log(10) Returns "2.302585092994046".

title: Math object
body_text: Math object The following Math object values and functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopics under Math Object for more details about each function. Math object values Value Description .E Returns the number value for e, the base of the natural logarithms (approximately 2.718). .LN10 Returns the number value for the natural logarithm of 10 (approximately 2.302). .LN2 Returns the number value for the natural logarithm of 2 (approximately 0.693). .LOG2E Returns the number value for the base-2 logarithm of e, the base of the natural logarithms (approximately 1.442). .LOG10E Returns the number value for the base-10 logarithm of e, the base of the natural logarithms (approximately 0.434). .PI Returns the number value for pi, the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter (approximately 3.14). .SQRT1_2 Returns the number value for the square root of ½ (approximately 0.707). .SQRT2 Returns the number value for the square root of 2 (approximately 1.414). Math object functions Function Description Syntax abs() Returns the absolute value of x . Math.abs( x ) acos() Returns the arc cosine of x as a value between 0 and pi radians. Math.acos( x ) asin() Returns the arc sine of x as a value between -pi/2 and pi/2 radians. Math.asin( x ) atan() Returns the arc tangent of x as a numeric value between -pi/2 and pi/2 radians. Math.atan( x ) atan2() Returns the arc tangent of the quotient ( y / x ) of its arguments, y and x , where the signs of y and x are used to determine the quadrant of the result. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from -pi to +pi. Math.atan2( y , x ) ceil() Returns x , rounded up to the nearest integer. Math.ceil( x ) cos() Returns the cosine of x in radians. Math.cos( x ) exp() Returns the value of E to the power of x . Math.exp( x ) floor() Returns x , rounded down to the nearest integer. Math.floor( x ) log() Returns the natural logarithm (base E) of x . Math.log( x ) max() Given zero or more arguments, returns the number with the highest value. Math.max( x? , y? , z? , n? ) min() Given zero or more arguments, returns the number with the lowest value. Math.min( x? , y? , z? , n? ) pow() Returns the value of x to the power of y . Math.pow( x , y ) random() Returns a random number between 0 and 1. Math.random() round() Returns x rounded to the nearest integer. Math.round( x ) sin() Returns the sine of x in radians. Math.sin( x ) sqrt() Returns the square root of x . Math.sqrt( x ) tan() Returns the tangent of x in radians. Math.tan( x ) Subtopics: abs function acos function asin function atan function atan2 function ceil function cos function exp function floor function log function max function min function pow function random function round function sin function sqrt function tan function

title: max function
body_text: max function The max function compares zero or more values and returns the number with the largest value. Arguments 0- n, Optional arguments are indicated by a question mark following the argument name. Argument Description x? through n? One or more numbers to compare Syntax Math.max( x? , y? , z? , n? ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.max(Num, 1); Returns "1". Math.max(10, 20) Returns "20". Math.max(-10, -20) Returns "-10".

title: min function
body_text: min function The min function compares zero or more values and returns the number with the lowest value. Arguments 0–n, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description x? through n? One or more numbers to compare. Syntax Math.min( x? , y? , z? , n? ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.min(Num, 1); Returns "0.5". Math.min(2, 3, 1) Returns "1". var x = 10, y = -20 var z = Math.min(x, y) Dsp.Button9.Label = z Returns "-20" on Button9's label.

title: NodeName function
body_text: NodeName function NodeName() returns the DeltaV workstation name hosting this instance of DeltaV Live. Note: In DeltaV Live, the NodeName function is comparable to the DeltaV Operate data link path, THISUSER/NODENAME.A_CV . Arguments 0 Return values (string) The DeltaV workstation name hosting this instance of DeltaV Live. Syntax ENV.NodeName() Examples DLSYS[ENV.NodeName() + "/COMM/PRI/CONBAD.CV"]

title: now function
body_text: now function The now function returns the time value (as a number) designating the UTC date and time from the occurrence of the call to now. Arguments 0 Return Values (number) The time value designating the UTC date and time from the occurrence of the call to now. Syntax Date.now(); Examples Example Result this.Label = Date.now() Returns 1518023657912 (adjusted for current date – number of milliseconds since January 1, 1970).

title: Number function
body_text: Number function The Number function converts a value to a number. Arguments 0–1, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description value? The value to be converted to a number. Return values (number) A number representing the given value. NaN , if the value cannot be converted to a legal number. 0 , if no argument is provided. Syntax Number( value ) Examples Example Result Assuming you have: the module parameter, CONTROL1/VALUEPLUSEU.CV a button (Button1) on a display the following script added as a custom script to a Button1 action Number(DLSYS.["CONTROL1/VALUEPLUSEU.CV"]) Returns "NaN" on Button1's label. Assuming you have: the module parameter, U012-FICA-5625-C/PID1/PV.CV, with a value of 20 a button (Button1) on a display the following script added as a custom script to a Button1 action Number(DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/PID1/PV.CV"]) Returns "20" on Button1's label.

title: Number object
body_text: Number object The following Number object values and functions are supported in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. See the subtopics under Number object for more details about each function. Number object values Value Description .MAX_VALUE Returns he largest positive representable number. .MIN_VALUE Returns the smallest positive representable number. Number object functions Function Description Syntax Number() Converts a value to a number. Number( value ) toString() Returns a string representing the specified Number object. numObj .toString( radix? ) toFixed() Returns a string representing the given number and using fixed-point notation. numObj .toFixed( fractionDigits? ) toExponential() Returns a string representing the Number object in exponential notation. numObj .toExponential( fractionDigits? ) toPrecision() Returns a string representing a given number and written with a specified length. numObj .toPrecision( precision? ) Subtopics: Number function toExponential function toFixed function toPrecision function toString function

title: OpenContextDisplayAsTooltip function
body_text: OpenContextDisplayAsTooltip function OpenContextDisplayAsTooltip() opens the specified contextual display in a tooltip-style window, providing it with the primary context information (tag), optional additional context information, and optional initial placement rules. Arguments 3–9, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description display element CDisplayName A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a contextual display. tag A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Tag Description property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. context 1? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 1 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 1? value is not present in the expression, the contextual display's Context 1 Default Value is used. context 2? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 2 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 2? value is not present, the contextual display's Context 2 Default Value is used. context 3? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 3 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 3? value is not present, the contextual display's Context 3 Default Value is used. context 4? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 4 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 4? value is not present, the contextual display's Context 4 Default Value is used. X? A number indicating the X coordinates for the contextual display's trigger point. Y? A number indicating the Y coordinates for the contextual display's trigger point. Return values True, if CDisplayName (case-insensitive) matches a published contextual display available to be opened by this instance of DeltaV Live. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.OpenContextDisplayAsTooltip( DisplayElement , cDisplayName , tag , context1? , context2? , context3? , context4? , X? , Y? ) Examples Example Result DL.OpenContextDisplayAsTooltip("loop_tip",Dsp.Context); Note: Tooltip-style pop-up windows in DeltaV Live have a distinctive appearance and automatic closing behavior, as compared to normal pop-up windows. Tooltip-style pop-up windows in DeltaV Live do not support minimization.

title: OpenContextDisplayAsync function
body_text: OpenContextDisplayAsync function OpenContextDisplayAsync() opens the specified contextual display, providing it with the primary context information (tag), optional additional context information, and optional initial placement rules. Arguments 2–9, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description CDisplayName A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a contextual display. tag A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Tag Description property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. placement? A Placement object or array of Placement objects whose values define the initial placement of the contextual display when it opens. The Placement objects override the default pop-up window placement rules. context 1? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 1 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 1? value is not present in the expression, the contextual display's Context 1 Default Value is used. context 2? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 2 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 2? value is not present, the contextual display's Context 2 Default Value is used. context 3? context 1? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 3 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 3? value is not present, the contextual display's Context 3 Default Value is used. context 4? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the contextual display's Context 4 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 4? value is not present, the contextual display's Context 4 Default Value is used. X? A number indicating the X coordinates for the contextual display's trigger point. Y? A number indicating the Y coordinates for the contextual display's trigger point. Return values (Boolean) True, if CDisplayName (case-insensitive) matches a published contextual display available to be opened by this instance of DeltaV Live. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.OpenContextDisplayAsync( cDisplayName , tag , placement? [], context1? , context2? , context3? , context4? , X? , Y? ) Examples Example Result DL.OpenContextDisplay("loop_fp", "FIC-101", "1") Opens the contextual display with the name Loop_fp, with FIC-101 as the module tag on the faceplate, and ??? DL.OpenContextDisplay(DL.DN("LOOP_DT"), Dsp.Context) Opens the contextual display with the name LOOP_DT and ??? as the tag name. Note: If contextual displays use this function to open as pop-up windows in DeltaV Live, then when minimized, they appear in a group on a layout's menu bar. Faceplate and detail displays each appears in its own group in the menu bar.

title: OpenDetailAsync function
body_text: OpenDetailAsync function OpenDetailAsync() opens the detail display configured for the specified module, device, or node name, (tag), optional additional context information, and optional initial placement rules. Arguments 1–8, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description tag A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a DeltaV module, node, or device, if the detail display name configured for that module, node, or device matches the Name of a contextual display. placement? A Placement object or array of Placement objects whose values define the initial placement of the detail display when it opens. The Placement objects override the default pop-up window placement rules. context 1? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the detail display's Context 1 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 1? value is not present in the expression, the detail display's Context 1 Default Value is used. context 2? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the detail display's Context 2 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 2? value is not present, the detail display's Context 2 Default Value is used. context 3? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the detail display's Context 3 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 3? value is not present, the detail display's Context 3 Default Value is used. context 4? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the detail display's Context 4 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 4? value is not present, the detail display's Context 4 Default Value is used. X? A number indicating the X coordinates for the detail display's trigger point. Y? A number indicating the Y coordinates for the detail display's trigger point. Return values (Promise object, that when resolved, returns a Boolean) True, if tag (case-insensitive) matches a running DeltaV module, node, or device name, AND the detail display name (case-insensitive) configured for that DeltaV module, node, or device matches the name of a published contextual display available to be opened by this instance of DeltaV Live. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.OpenDetailAsync( tag , placement? [], context1? , context2? , context3? , context4? , X? , Y? ) Examples Example Result DL.OpenDetailAsync("FIC-101") Opens the detail display configured for the FIC-101 module. DL.OpenDetailAsync(Dsp.Context, "2", "HI_ALM") Opens the detail display configured for the ??? Context property and ??????. if (!await DL.OpenDetailAsync("FIC-101")) { // do something dealing with the display not being found } DL.OpenDetailAsync(Dsp.Context, null, "2", "HI_ALM"); Note: If detail displays use this function to open as pop-up windows in DeltaV Live, then when minimized, they appear in a group on a layout's menu bar. Faceplate displays and other contextual displays each appears in its own group in the menu bar.

title: OpenDisplayAsync function
body_text: OpenDisplayAsync function OpenDisplayAsync() opens the specified display, optional additional context information, and optional initial placement rules. Arguments 1-4, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description DisplayName A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a display. placement? A Placement object or array of Placement objects whose values define the initial placement of the faceplate's when it opens. The Placement objects override the default pop-up window placement rules. X? A number indicating the X coordinates for the display's trigger point. Y? A number indicating the Y coordinates for the display's trigger point. Return values (Promise object, that when resolved, returns a Boolean) True, if < DisplayName > (case-insensitive) matches a published display available to be opened by this instance of DeltaV Live. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.OpenDisplayAsync( displayName , placement? [], X? , Y? ) Examples Example Result if (!await DL.OpenDisplayAsync(DL.DN("Reactor4"))) { // do something dealing with the display not being found } // direct display to open at bottom-center of the "OVVW" Screen // for Layouts that have it let pos = new Placement(PlacementOption.Screen, "OVVW"); pos.UseCachedPosition = false; pos.Alignment = PlacementAlignment.Bottom | PlacementAlignment.Center; DL.OpenDisplayAsync(DL.DN("EnergyUse”), [pos]); Note: It is recommended that you use the DL.DN() function for the display name to enable display and display frame rename tracking.

title: OpenFaceplateAsync function
body_text: OpenFaceplateAsync function OpenFaceplateAsync() opens the faceplate display configured for the specified module, device, or node name (tag), optional additional context information, and optional initial placement rules. Arguments 1–8, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description tag A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a DeltaV module, node, or device, if the faceplate's name configured for that module, node, or device matches the Name of a contextual display. placement? A Placement object or array of Placement objects whose values define the initial placement of the faceplate's when it opens. The Placement objects override the default pop-up window placement rules. context 1? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the faceplate's Context 1 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 1? value is not present in the expression, the faceplate's Context 1 Default Value is used. context 2? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the faceplate's Context 2 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 2? value is not present, the faceplate's Context 2 Default Value is used. context 3? context 1? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the faceplate's Context 3 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 3? value is not present, the faceplate's Context 3 Default Value is used. context 4? A literal or graphics expression whose value is placed in the faceplate's Context 4 property immediately before starting to run in DeltaV Live. If a context 4? value is not present, the faceplate's Context 4 Default Value is used. X? A number indicating the X coordinates for the faceplate's trigger point. Y? A number indicating the Y coordinates for the faceplate's trigger point. Return values (Promise object, that when resolved, returns a Boolean) True, if tag (case-insensitive) matches a running DeltaV module, node, or device name, AND the faceplate name (case-insensitive) configured for that DeltaV module, node, or device matches the name of a published contextual display available to be opened by this instance of DeltaV Live. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.OpenFaceplateAsync( tag , placement? [], context1? , context2? , context3? , context4? , X? , Y? ) Examples Example Result DL.OpenFaceplateAsync("FIC-101") Opens the faceplate configured for the FIC-101 module. DL.OpenFaceplateAsync(Dsp.Context, "true") Opens the faceplate configured for the ??? Context property and ??????. if (!await DL.OpenFaceplateAsync("FIC-101")) { // do something dealing with the display not being found } DL.OpenFaceplateAsync(Dsp.Context, null, "true") Note: If faceplate displays use this function to open as pop-up windows in DeltaV Live, then when minimized, they appear in a group on a layout's menu bar. Detail displays and other contextual displays each appears in its own group in the menu bar.

title: OpenPrimaryDisplayAsync function
body_text: OpenPrimaryDisplayAsync function OpenPrimaryDisplayAsync() opens the primary control display configured for the specified module, device, or node name. Arguments 1–4, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description module name A literal or graphics expression that resolves to the name of a DeltaV module, node, or device, if the primary control display name configured for that module, node, or device matches the name of a display. placement? A Placement object or array of Placement objects whose values define the initial placement of the primary display when it opens. The Placement objects override the default pop-up window placement rules. X? A number indicating the X coordinates for the primary display's trigger point. Y? A number indicating the Y coordinates for the primary display's trigger point. Return values (Promise object, that when resolved, returns a Boolean) True, if module name (case-insensitive) matches a running DeltaV module, node, or device name, AND the primary control display name (case-insensitive) configured for that DeltaV module, node, or device matches the name of a published display available to be opened by this instance of DeltaV Live. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.OpenPrimaryDisplayAsync( moduleName , placement? [], X? , Y? ) Examples Example Result if (!await DL.OpenPrimaryDisplay(Dsp.Context)) { // do something dealing with the display not being found } // direct display to open in specific Display Frame let pos = new Placement( PlacementOption.FullDisplayFrame, "ParkIt_1"); DL.OpenPrimaryDisplayAsync(DL.DN("FIC-101"), [pos]); // direct display to open in pop-up centered on specific Screen2 // in Layouts that have it, falling back to centered on Screen1 let posPrefs = []; let pref1 = new Placement(PlacementOption.Screen, "Screen2"); pref1.Alignment = PlacementAlignment.Centered; pref1.UseCachedPosition = false; posPrefs.push(pref1); let pref2 = new Placement(PlacementOption.Screen, "Screen1"); pref2.Alignment = PlacementAlignment.Centered; pref1.UseCachedPosition = false; posPrefs.push(pref2); DL.OpenPrimaryDisplayAsync(DL.DN("FIC-101"), posPrefs); Note: This function has no effect if a primary control display cannot be resolved for the module name argument, or if that display is not available for this workstation/session because it is not included in the active display set. It is recommended that you use the DL.DN function fro the module name to enable display and display frame rename tracking.

title: ParameterName function
body_text: ParameterName function ParameterName() extracts the name of a specified parameter from a DeltaV parameter path string. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A full or partial DeltaV parameter path. Return values (string) The substring preceding the first field delimiter, when only a field delimiter (.) is present. The substring following the last block/parameter delimiter, when one or more block/parameter delimiters (/) are present. The substring between the last block/parameter delimiter and the first field delimiter, when one or more block/parameter delimiters (/) and a field delimiter (.) are present. An empty string, otherwise. Syntax DLPATH.ParameterName( path string ) Examples The following examples demonstrate how to extract a parameter name and show it as the label on a text element. Example Result DLSYS.Text1.Label = DLPATH.ParameterName("ZONE1%FIC101/PID1/MODE.ACTUAL.STR") Returns "MODE" as the label text. DLSYS.Text2.Label = DLPATH.ParameterName("THISUSER/ALMCNT[12][15].CV") Returns "ALMCNT[12][15]" as the label text. DLSYS.Text3.Label = DLPATH.ParameterName("TIC200/BLK1/BLK2/OUT") Returns "OUT" as the label text. DLSYS.Text4.Label = DLPATH.ParameterName("ALARMS[1].PRI") Returns "ALARMS[1]" as the label text. DLSYS.Text5.Label = DLPATH.ParameterName("LIC330") Returns "". Note: If the argument path is an ambiguous partial path, a block name may be returned. If the argument path includes array parameter syntax, that syntax is included in the result to specify the parameter element.

title: ParameterPath function
body_text: ParameterPath function ParameterPath() extracts and returns the full path of the specified parameter name from a DeltaV parameter path string. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A full or partial DeltaV parameter path. Return values (string) The substring preceding the first field delimiter, when a field delimiter (.) is present. The full argument string, otherwise. Syntax DLPATH.ParameterPath( path string ) Examples The following examples demonstrate how to extract the full path of a parameter name and show it as the label on a text element. Example Result DLSYS.Text1.Label = DLPATH.ParameterPath ("ZONE1%FIC101/PID1/MODE.ACTUAL.STR") Returns "ZONE1%FIC101/PID1/MODE" as the label text. DLSYS.Text2.Label = DLPATH.ParameterPath("THISUSER/ALMCNT[12][15].CV") Returns "THISUSER/ALMCNT[12][15]]" as the label text. DLSYS.Text3.Label = DLPATH.ParameterPath("TIC200/BLK1/BLK2/OUT") Returns "TIC200/BLK1/BLK2/OUT" as the label text. DLSYS.Text4.Label = DLPATH.ParameterPath("ALARMS[1].PRI") Returns "ALARMS[1]" as the label text. Note: If the argument path includes array parameter syntax, that syntax is included in the returned parameter path.

title: parseFloat function
body_text: parseFloat function The parseFloat function parses a string and returns a floating point number. Arguments 1 Arguments Description string The value to be parsed. Return values (number) A floating point number. NaN , if the string cannot be converted to a number. Syntax parseFloat( string ) Examples Example Result parseFloat('0.0314E+2'); Returns "3.14". var foo = Object.create(null); foo.toString = function () { return "100"; }; Dsp.Button4.Label = parseFloat(foo); Returns "100" on Button4's label. parseFloat("10.33 g/liter") Returns "10.33".

title: parseInt function
body_text: parseInt function The parseInt function parses a string argument and returns an integer of the specified radix (the base in mathematical numeral systems). Arguments 2 Argument Description string The string to be parsed. radix A number (from 2 through 36) that represents the numeral system to be used. If this argument is omitted or undefined, it assumes the value of 10. Return values (number) An integer of the specified radix. If the first character cannot be converted to a number, NaN is returned. Syntax parseInt( string , radix ) Examples Example Result parseInt('15 * 3', 10) Returns "15". parseInt('Hello', 8); Returns NaN. Assuming that you have the module param, CONTROL1/VALUEPLUSEU.CV, with a value of “105 g/liter". var str1 = DLSYS["CONTROL1/VALUEPLUSEU.CV"]; this.Label = parseInt(str1); parseInt("10", 8) Returns "105". Returns "8".

title: parse function
body_text: parse function The parse function parses a date string and returns the number of milliseconds since January 1, 1970. Arguments 1 Argument Description date string A string representing a date. Return value (number) A number representing the milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC and the date obtained by parsing the given string representation of a date. NaN , if the argument does not represent a valid date. Syntax Date.parse( date string ) Examples Example Result this.Label = Date.parse(“February 1, 2018”) -Returns 1517464800000 (number of milliseconds between specified date and January 1, 1970).

title: PlacementAlignment enum
body_text: PlacementAlignment enum The PlacementAlignment enum is recommended as the means for using descriptive names for the alignment options in a Placement object. The PlacementOption enum includes the following values: enum PlacmentAlignment { Right = 0B0001, Left = 0B0010, Center = 0B0011, Bottom = 0B0100, Top = 0B1000, Middle = 0B1100, Centered = 0B1111, // both Horz. Center and Vert. Middle }

title: PlacementOption enum
body_text: PlacementOption enum The PlacementOption enum is recommended as the means for using descriptive names when testing condition bits in the .Status values of a RtValue object. The PlacementOption enum includes the following values: enum PlacementOption { Default = 0, // built-in Display placement in Layout rules TriggerPoint, DisplayFrame, // opens pop-up within a Display Frame Screen, NearRegion, AboveRegion, BelowRegion, LeftOfRegion, RightOfRegion, FullDisplayFrame, // replaces current Display in Display Frame // designated by Placement.ReferenceName }

title: Placement object
body_text: Placement object The Placement object holds information that is used as arguments in functions to define the preferred initial placement of a newly opened pop-up window in DeltaV Live. Functions that accept Placement object(s) as arguments generally accept an array of Placement objects, which define the preferred placement alternatives in decreasing preference order. You may want to define placement alternatives (an array of Placement objects) in case DeltaV Live is unable to use the information in the first, second, and so forth array element. For example, it may happen that the name of a display frame cannot be resolved in 'this' layout, or a placement alternative would cause the pop-up windows to not be entirely within a layout screen. If DeltaV Live cannot use the information in the first array element, it attempts to use the next Placement array element, then the next, and so on, until it finds one that works. If the array of preferred placements is exhausted, DeltaV Live minimally adjusts placement for the 'last resort' Placement object to open the pop-up window within a screen's boundaries. If this adjustment does not work, Deltav Live uses the default placement rules. Placement object values Value type Name Description enum (see PlacementOption enum) .Option Determines the use of the other Placement object properties. string .ReferenceName When .Option is .DisplayFrame or .FullDisplayFrame, this value is the name of the target display frame in the layout. If undefined or empty, this value refers to the display frame where the script is running. The .FullDisplayFrame PlacementOption supports a comma delimited list of display names. region (see Region object) .Region Used with the .Option and .xxxRegion choices to designate the rectangular area that the pop-up is adjacent to but does not obscure. enum (see PlacementAlignment enum) .Alignment Used with the .Option choices to specify the preferred position of pop-up windows relative to the display frame, screen, or region. measurement .HorzOffset Holds the final horizontal (X) offset applied to the preferred pop-up window placement. If undefined or null, 0 is assumed. May be a negative number. measurement .VertOffset This value is typically a measurement. Holds the final vertical (Y) offset applied to the preferred pop-up window placement. If undefined or null, 0 is assumed. May be a negative number. Boolean .UseCachedPosition When false, this value participates in determining the pop-up window's preferred position and causes any cached position information to be ignored. When true, this value is ignored when applicable cached position information is present in this instance of DeltaV Live. constructor .Placement Creates a new Placement object. Subtopics: PlacementOption enum PlacementAlignment enum

title: PopupClose function
body_text: PopupClose function PopupClose() closes 'this' display, if it is running in a pop-up window. Arguments 0 Return values (Boolean) True, if the display or contextual display containing the script calling this function is running in a pop-up window and is closed by the user. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.PopupClose() Examples Example Result Add a button to a display that is configured to open as a popup display. Configure an action on the button using this expression: DL.PopupClose() When the user clicks the button, the popup display closes. Note: This function closes pop-up displays and contextual displays in either their visible (restored) or minimized state. It also force closes contextual displays running in tooltip-style pop-up windows.

title: PopupMinimize function
body_text: PopupMinimize function PopupMinimize() closes 'this' display, if it is running and visible in a pop-up window. Arguments 0 Return values (Boolean) True, if the display or contextual display containing the script calling this function is running in a pop-up window that is in the visible (restored) state and is minimized by the user. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.PopupMinimize() Examples Example Result Add a button to a display that is configured to open as a popup display. Configure an action on the button using this expression: DL.PopupMinimize() When the user clicks the button, the popup display is minimized. Note: PopupMinimize() has no effect if the display or contextual display is already in the minimized state, or if the contextual display is running in a tooltip-style pop-up window.

title: PopupRestore function
body_text: PopupRestore function PopupRestore() restores 'this' display to its visible state, if 'this' display is running and minimized in a pop-up window. This display's pop-up window is stacked on top of any other visible pop-up windows. Arguments 0 Return values (Boolean) True, if the display or contextual display containing the script calling this function is running in a pop-up window that is in the minimized state and is restored to the visible state by the user. False, otherwise. Syntax DL.PopupRestore() Examples Example Result Add a button to a display that is configured to open as a popup display. Configure an action on the button using this expression: DL.PopupRestore() When the user clicks the button, the minimized popup display is restored.

title: pow function
body_text: pow function The pow function returns the value of x to the power of y . Arguments 2 Argument Description x The base number. y The exponent used to rase the base. Return value (number) A number representing the given base, x , taken to the power of the given exponent, y . Syntax Math.pow( x , y ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.pow(Num, 2); Returns "0.25". (Math.pow(7, 3) Returns "343". Math.pow(2, 10) Returns "1024" on Button9's label.

title: random function
body_text: random function The random function returns a random number between 0 and 1. Arguments 0 Return value (float) A floating-point, pseudo-random number, ranging from 0 (inclusive) up to, but not including, 1. You can scale this number to your desired range. Syntax Math.random() Examples Example Result this.Label = Math.random() Returns a random float number between 0 and 1. function getRandomInt(max) { return Math.floor(Math.random() * Math.floor(max)); } Dsp.Button1.Label = getRandomInt(3); Returns "0, 1, or 2". function getRandomArbitrary(min, max) { return Math.random() * (max - min) + min; } Returns a random number between the specified values.

title: ReadAsync function
body_text: ReadAsync function ReadAsync() reads the specified DeltaV Operate-style parameter path and immediately returns the status of the read attempt. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A literal or graphics expression that resolves to a DeltaV parameter. Return value (Boolean) Syntax DLSYS.ReadAsync( path string ) Examples Example Result const x = (await DLSYS.ReadASync('MOD1/SGGN1/Bias')).Value const y = (await DLSYS.ReadASync['MOD1/SGGN2/Bias')).Value Dsp.Text1.Label = x Dsp.Text2.Label = y const x = (await DLSYS.ReadASync('MOD1/SGGN1/Bias')).Value const y = (await DLSYS.ReadASync['MOD1/SGGN2/Bias')).Value Dsp.Text1.Label = x Dsp.Text2.Label = y

title: Read function
body_text: Read function Read() reads the specified DeltaV parameter path and immediately returns the status of the read attempt, and if successful, the requested value. The Read function is useful with scripts that execute periodically because once data is available, calls to .Read() perform successfully. Arguments 1 Argument Description path string A literal or graphics expression that resolves to a DeltaV parameter. Return values (RtValue object) A number representing the status of the read attempt. 0 represents a successful read; ?? represents an unsuccessful read. The value read. The data type returned is determined by the < read-as suffix > . Syntax DLSYS.Read( path string ) Examples Example Result let pv = DLSYS.Read("FIC101/PID1/PV.CV"); A successful read: a status of 0, and the PV of FIC101's PID1 block. An unsuccessful read: ?? let actModeName = DLSYS.Read("FIC101/PID1/MODE.ACTUAL.STR"); const x = DLSYS.Read('MOD1/SGGN1/OUT.CV').Status.Text const y = DLSYS.Read('MOD1/SGGN2/OUT.CV').Status.Text Dsp.Text1.Label = x Dsp.Text2.Label = y A successful read: a status of 0, and the OUT value of SGGN1 on the Text1 label and the OUT value of SGGN2 on the Text2 label. An unsuccessful read: ??

title: Region object
body_text: Region object The Region object holds information that determines the rectangular region in a display frame. Region object values Value Description .X Relative to the display frame, the horizontal position of the upper-left corner rectangular region as measured from the left boundary of the display frame. .Y Relative to the display frame, the vertical position of the upper left-corner rectangular region as measured from the top boundary of the display frame. .Width The width of the rectangular region. .Height The height of the rectangular region.

title: RemoveSessionStoreItem function
body_text: RemoveSessionStoreItem function RemoveSessionStoreItem() discards data retrieved by AddSessionStoreItem() during this DeltaV Live session. Arguments 1 Argument Description key string The unique name of the data item to be discarded from the storage area. The key string is case sensitive. Return values None Syntax .RemoveSessionStoreItem( key string ) Examples Example Result If you want the layout-scope variable, MyVar, to revert to its configured default value when the layout configuration is refreshed, you could use the following expression: // next time we open, revert to the configured default value DL.RemoveStoreItem("Lyt.MyVar") When the DeltaV Live user clicks the Refresh Configuration button, the variable, MyVar, reverts to its configured default value.

title: round function
body_text: round function The round function returns x rounded to the nearest integer. Arguments 1 Argument Description x A number. Return value The value of the given number rounded to the nearest integer. Syntax Math.round( x ) Examples Example Result var Num = DLSYS["U012-FICA-5625-C/DIFF.CV"]; this.Label = Math.round(Num); ->returns 1 Returns "1". Math.round(0.45) Returns "0". function precisionRound(number, precision) { var factor = Math.pow(10, precision); return Math.round(number * factor) / factor; } Dsp.Button1.Label = precisionRound(1234.5678, 1); Returns "1234.6".

title: RtValue object
body_text: RtValue object The RtValue object holds the 'value with status' results of the Read and ReadAsync function calls for the DLSYS and DVSYS objects. The following values are supported for the RtValue object in DeltaV Live graphics expressions and scripting. RtValue object values Value Description .Value Returns the value determined by the <read-as suffix> . This value is typically a string or number, but can be any type. .Status Returns the status, as a number, of the parameter's read attempt. 0: Indicates the .Value is usable and "good" in all respects. The least significant 32 bits are treated as bit-wise indicators of the zero or more 'abnormal' status conditions present for this RtValue. Note: It is recommended that you use the ValueStatus Enum Object to mask or test conditions reflected in a . Status value. Usage example let modOption = DLSYS["FIC101/OPTION.CV”]; let groupVisibility = (modOption.Status == ValueStatus.Good) && modOption.Value >= 1 && modOption.Value <= 3)

title: setDate function
body_text: setDate function Sets the day of the month for a specified date object, according to local time. Arguments 1 Argument Description day An integer representing the day of a month. 1–31 are the expected values, but 0, -1, or 32 can also be used. Return value (number) A number representing the number of milliseconds between the date object and midnight January 1 1970. If the argument is 0, returns the last day of the previous month. If the argument is -1, returns the day before the last day of the previous month. If the argument is 32, and the month has 31 days, returns the first day of the next month. If the argument is 32, and the month has 3o days, returns the second day of the next month. Syntax dateObj.setDate( day ) Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); d.setDate(15); this.Label = d.getDate(); Returns 15 (the day of the month) on the element's label, replacing the current day.

title: setFullYear function
body_text: setFullYear function Sets the full year (four digits for dates between year 1000 and 9999) for a specified date, according to local time. Arguments 1–3, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description year A value representing the year. Negative values are allowed. month? An integer representing the month. 0–11 are the expected values, but -1, 12, or 13 can also be used. day? An integer representing the day of month. 1–31 are the expected values, but 0, -1, or 32 can also be used. Return value (number) A number representing the number of milliseconds between the date object and midnight January 1 1970. If month? is -1, returns the last month of the previous year. If month? is 12, returns the first month of the next year. If month? is 13, returns the second month of the next year. If day? is 0, returns the last day of the previous month. If day? is -1, returns the day before the last day of the previous month. If day? is 32 and the month has 31 days, returns the first day of the next month. If day? is 32 and the month has 30 days, returns the second day of the next month. Syntax dateObj.setFullYear( year , month? , day? ) Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); d.setFullYear(2020); this.Label = d.getFullYear(); Returns 2020 on the element's label.

title: setHours function
body_text: setHours function Sets the hours for a specified date object, according to local time. Arguments 1–4, Optional arguments are indicated by a ? following the argument name. Argument Description hour An integer representing the hour. 0–23 are the expected values, but -1, or 24 can also be used. min? An integer representing the minutes. 0–59 are the expected values, but -1, or 60 can also be used. sec? An integer representing the seconds. 0–59 are the expected values, but -1, or 60 can also be used. millisec? An integer representing the milliseconds. 0–999 are the expected values, but -1, or 1000 can also be used. Return value (number) A number representing the number of milliseconds between the date object and midnight January 1 1970. If hour is -1, returns the last hour of the previous day. If hour is 24, returns the first hour of the next day. If [ min? ] is -1, returns the last minute of the previous hour. If [ min? ] is 60, returns the first minute of the next hour. If [ sec? ] is -1, returns the last second of the previous minute. If [ sec? ] is 60, returns the first second of the next minute. If [ millisec? ] is -1, returns the last millisecond of the previous second. If [ millisec? ] is 1000, returns the first millisecond of the next second. Syntax dateObj.setHours( hour , min? , sec? , millisec? ) Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); d.setHours(11); this.Label = d.getHours(); Returns 11 on the element's label.

title: setMilliseconds function
body_text: setMilliseconds function Sets the milliseconds for a specified date object, according to local time. Arguments 1 Argument Description millisec An integer representing the milliseconds. 0–999 are the expected values, but -1, 1000, or 1001 can also be used. Return value (number) A number representing the number of milliseconds between the date object and midnight January 1 1970. If millisec is -1, returns the last millisecond of the previous second. If millisec is 1000, returns the first millisecond of the next second. If millisec is 1001, returns the second millisecond of the next second. Syntax dateObj.setMilliseconds( millisec ) Examples Example Result This script is added, as a custom script on an action, to any element with a Label property, such as a button. var d = new Date(); d.setMilliseconds(987); this.Label = d.getMilliseconds(); Returns 987 on the element's label.

Return value (number) A number representing the number of milliseconds between the date object and midnight January 1 1970. If min is -1, returns the last minute of the previous hour. If min is 60, returns the first minute of the next hour. If sec? is -1, returns the last second of the previous minute. If sec? is 60, returns the first second of the next minute. title: setMonth function
