Therefore, limit unit names in the Autronica Configuration tool to nine characters in length to allow for the renaming to unique Secure Parameter names.

title: Export the BS-420 configuration

title: Create alarm help format specification files
main_heading: Create alarm help format specification files
body_text: Create alarm help format specification files If the existing format specification files do not meet your needs, or if you have modules that contain alarms that are different from the alarms supported in Module_AlmHlp.fmt, you can create your own format specification files. The following is an example of how to create a format specification file for custom modules in a configuration. In this example, the configuration has a ModuleTemplates category named Local that contains two module templates, MODULE_1 and MODULE_2. MODULE_1 has alarms ALARM_1 and ALARM_2 defined. MODULE_2 has alarms ALARM_A and ALARM_B defined. You can create an alarm help format specification file for each module, but if you want to be able to bulk edit alarms for both types of modules in one text file you can create a format file that includes alarm information for both modules: Open the Format specification dialog (in DeltaV Explorer select File > Format Specification > New ). Enter a meaningful name for the file and click Next . In the Object type field select Module . Click the Browse button next to the Subtype field and navigate to the Local ModuleTemplates folder. Select one of the module templates and click OK . Note: You can also browse to a module created from the template. In the Field names area select the module_name field. Because you are editing only alarm-related information and are not creating new modules, this is the only field that is required to exist in the format file. You can add other fields if you want. In the Field names area select the alarm parameters under Alarms . Click the Browse button next to the Subtype field and navigate to the Local ModuleTemplates folder. Select the other module template and click OK . In the Field names area select the alarm parameters under Alarms . Click Next . Click Next to accept the field order. Click Finish . In DeltaV Explorer you can now navigate to an area that contains instances of these modules and export the alarm information for them.

title: Create an ODBC data source
body_text: Create an ODBC data source The procedure you use to create an ODBC data source depends on whether you are on a 32-bit or 64-bit operating system. Note: The 32-bit version of Microsoft Access must already be installed (DeltaV software does not support 64-bit versions of Microsoft Office) and the database must exist prior to completing the ODBC data source connection. The ODBC Data Source Name is needed to connect User-Defined Export and Import with the Access database and table you created. How you begin depends on your operating system. On a 32-bit operating system: Go to Control Panel > Administrative Tools . Double-click Data Sources (ODBC) . On a 64-bit operating system: Navigate to the \Windows\SysWoW64 folder. Double-click Odbcad32.exe The ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog opens. Click the File DSN tab. Note: File DSN is the only valid choice when creating an ODBC source for a user-defined import or export. Click Add . On the Create New Data Source dialog select the appropriate driver: Microsoft Access Driver (*.mdb, *.accdb) . Click Next . Browse to a location in which to save the .dsn data source file and give it a name. Click Save . Verify the name and location for the .dsn data source file. Click Next . Click Finish to create the data source. On the ODBC Microsoft Access Setup dialog, click Select . In the Select Database dialog select the previously-created Microsoft database to be associated with your .dsn Data Source File. Click OK . Click OK on the ODBC Microsoft Access Setup dialog . Click OK on the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog.

title: Create the Access database for the custom module example
main_heading: Create the Access database for the custom module example
body_text: Create the Access database for the custom module example This topic outlines the procedure to create an Access database for the custom module example. The actual sequence of commands you use to create the database depend on the version of Access you are using. Adjust the following steps as required for the version you are using. From MS Access, create a database. Create a table in the database. Change to Design View. The view of the table changes so that the first column is a list of table fields. Delete the Primary key row. Create a row for each field in the format specification you will be using. The number of fields required in the table equals the number of is_a_string_parameter fields (T or F) in the module's format file. For example, there are 43 is_a_string_parameter fields (any field with a T or F) in the custom module example TEMPS.FMT file. For each row designate a Field Name (this does not have to match the header names in the format files). Note: Some of the characters in the labels might not be valid in Access (for example, a period, an exclamation point, brackets, leading spaces, or non-printable characters such as a carriage return). You will need to remove them or change them to valid characters. Assign the column Data Type to be Text . The default field size is adequate for all fields except for the CALC block's expression (field 23). Change that field's size to 200. Accept the default values for all other field parameters in the table. Save the table and database. Verify that none of the rows in table view is designated as the Primary key. Close the database Next, you must create an ODBC Data Source Name to connect User-Defined Export and Import with the Access database and table you created. Related information Bulk editing equipment and control modules

title: Bulk edit SIS Controller Modbus Port register mapping
main_heading: Bulk edit SIS Controller Modbus Port register mapping
body_text: Bulk edit SIS Controller Modbus Port register mapping This section outlines how to bulk edit DeltaV SIS Controller Modbus port registers mappings to module. There are a few conditions that must be met to bulk edit register mapping: Each register_type value must be correct for the corresponding register_name. For example, register_names between R10001 and R11000 must be register_type Input status . Importing more register mappings than the allowed number of registers for a particular type imports only the registers up to the maximum allowed value. The register_name for Float input and Float holding register types must end with an odd number. If the bulk edit file contains gaps in the register_name list (for example R1 and R3 exist in the file but R2 does not), the omitted registers are created on import but are not mapped. Note: Bulk edit can add or modify registers but cannot remove registers. The only way to remove registers is from the Modbus Port Properties dialog Data sets tab. The general procedure to bulk edit is: Create and configure one register of each type to be configured. Use the Modbus_Port.fmt format specification file to export the data or create your own format specification file. Copy and edit the exported file in the bulk edit Excel template as required. Import the edited data. Subtopics: SIS Controller Modbus Port mapping object syntax table

title: Bypassing the firewall IPD
body_text: Bypassing the firewall IPD In order to send an unlock command to a logic solver such as a CSLS or SLS 1508, you must first bypass the firewall IPD. You can use either the front-panel pushbutton or a set of discrete input contacts on the front panel to bypass the firewall IPD. This topic explains how to use the front-panel pushbutton to bypass the firewall IPD. Refer to KBA NK-1600-0290 for information on using the discrete input contacts. Press the pushbutton on the primary firewall IPD, release the pushbutton, and wait for two seconds. Press the pushbutton again, release it, and wait for two seconds. Press the pushbutton a third time and release it. After about 10 seconds, the relay contacts open and the Status LED flashes on and off red. The firewall IPD remains bypassed for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, the firewall IPD returns to the blocking state, the Status LED turns off, and the relay contacts close. When the firewall IPD is in the blocking state, the logic solver can receive lock commands but cannot receive unlock commands.

title: Change the phase type and download the controller
main_heading: Change the phase type and download the controller

title: Change the OPC UA server's port
main_heading: Change the OPC UA server's port
body_text: Change the OPC UA server's port You can modify the default port on the workstation OPC UA server using this procedure. From DeltaV Explorer, select the OPC UA server node. Right click and select Properties from the context menu. Select the OPC UA Server subsystem. In the right pane, select the endpoint URL. Right click and select Properties . Edit the port number in the Port field. Note: This changes the Endpoint Url field after downloading. Click OK to save the change. Download the OPC UA server. To copy the new endpoint URL for your OPC UA clients, go back to the endpoint's Properties dialog. For workstation servers using HTTPS endpoint URL, get the following information about the existing bound certificate using the netsh command. Certificate Hash Application ID From the Start menu, open a command prompt. Type netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:[PORT] and press Enter. The port is 9408 by default. Highlight the number needed and press Ctrl C to copy it. In a text editor, paste the number (label it for use later). Repeat for the other number. For workstation servers using HTTPS endpoint URL, delete the existing certificate binding (the old port): netsh http delete sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:[PORT] The port is 9408 by default. For workstation servers using HTTPS endpoint URL, bind the certificate to the new port: netsh http add sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:[PORT] certhash=[CERTHASH] certstorename=Root appid=[APPGUID] When using a self-signed certificate, the certstorename parameter is set to my . For workstation servers using HTTPS endpoint URL, verify that the SSL certificate has been bound to the new port: netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:[PORT] The software displays the SSL certificate bindings. Open the new port on any firewalls (including Windows firewalls) between the OPC UA server and its clients for all protocols that you are using (HTTP, HTTPS, OPC.TCP). Related information The Windows firewall and a DeltaV workstation

title: Change the data source for historical data
main_heading: Change the data source for historical data
body_text: Change the data source for historical data To change the connection to a historical data server where the DeltaV Continuous Historian , the Advanced Continuous Historian, or OSIsoft PI Server is running, complete the following steps: Click File > Set Default Data Servers to open the Set Default Data Servers dialog. In the Historical Data Server field on the Continuous Historian tab: Select a source for historical data from the drop-down list for the process data (parameter references) displayed for historical data in the events grid or trended on charts. To connect to the machine where you are running Process History View, select localhost . If the node where the historian is running does not appear on the drop-down list—for example, in a DeltaV Zones environment or when the historian is installed on a non-DeltaV workstation—you can enter the node name in the Historical Data Server field explicitly. If you clear the Historical Data Server field, leaving it blank, Process History View connects only to the DeltaV OPC Server for real-time data, not to any historical data server. To set the specified historical data server as the default data source to be used whenever you start Process History View, enable the Save as my Application Startup Data Server option. Tip: To improve performance when collecting historical data with the Advanced Continuous Historian or with a PI Server enterprise historian, enable the Connect to Advance Continuous Historian Server option. Click OK to close the dialog and save your changes.

title: Clear recipe authorization signatures
body_text: Clear recipe authorization signatures You cannot clear a signature on a recipe that has been downloaded to a Batch Executive. To clear an approval or rejection signature, perform the following steps: Open the Recipe Authorization dialog, select the Signer Description for which you have the key, and click the Clear button. title: Clearing COMM_ALM alarms when a fieldbus device is removed from the segment
main_heading:
Clearing COMM_ALM alarms when a fieldbus device is removed from the
	 segment
body_text: Clearing COMM_ALM alarms when a fieldbus device is removed from the segment When a commissioned fieldbus device is permanently removed from the segment physically, it may generate a COMM_ALM alarm. In applications where the device is no longer needed, the device placeholder may also be deleted. Despite the physical removal of the device and the deletion of the placeholder, the alarm is not automatically removed from DeltaV Operate and attempts to acknowledge the alarm generate an Item Not Found error. Follow these steps to clear the COMM_ALM alarm that is generated when a fieldbus device is removed from the segment: Reattach the fieldbus device to the segment and then recreate the alarm to acknowledge the COMM alarm, if possible. If the process permits, perform a total download of the controller where the device was previously assigned. If the fieldbus device can no longer be reattached to the segment and a total download of the controller is not possible, perform the following steps: Open the fieldbus device's Properties dialog in DeltaV Explorer and select the Alarms and Display tab. Take note of the area indicated in the All device alarms associated with area: field. Decommission and delete the fieldbus device placeholder. Create a control module under the area seen in the All device alarms associated with area: field. Name the new control module with the same tag as the device that was just deleted. Create an alarm in the control module and name it COMM_ALM. Assign the control module to the controller where the fieldbus device was previously assigned. Save and download the control module. Acknowledge the alarm and delete the newly configured control module.

title: Commission the SLS 1508 logic solver
body_text: Commission the SLS 1508 logic solver A logic solver under the SIS Network must be assigned to a physical logic solver card under the Physical Network or to a ProfessionalPLUS workstation before it can be commissioned. If the logic solver is not assigned, the Commission menu item is disabled. Navigate to the logic solver to commission under SIS Network. Right-click and select Commission . Note that you use the Decommission selection on the same context menu to decommission a logic solver. Click Yes on the dialog asking if you want to commission the logic solver. Click Confirm on the Confirmation dialog. After commissioning, the Logic Solver can accept a download. The Logic Solver icon appears yellow, rather than grayed-out. After a logic solver has been commissioned, it cannot be renamed, unassigned, or upgraded until it is decommissioned. In addition, the card slot and redundancy of a physical logic solver card cannot be changed if the logic solver is commissioned.

title: Commission a CSLS
body_text: Commission a CSLS Right click a CSLS placeholder in the Local Safety Network and select Commission . On the confirmation dialog that appears, click Yes . The Secure Write confirm dialog appears. Click Confirm to commission the CSLS. The CSLS icon turns yellow to show that it has been commissioned.

title: Commission Wireless Gateway nodes
body_text: Commission Wireless Gateway nodes When the system is powered up, any Wireless Gateway nodes that are physically connected are listed under Decommissioned Nodes in DeltaV Explorer. To commission a Wireless Gateway node, you can drag-and-drop a decommissioned Wireless Gateway to the Wireless I/O Network or to a placeholder under the network that you configured in advance. It is recommended that you commission one Gateway at a time as it is difficult to distinguish one Gateway from another when commissioning multiple Gateways simultaneously. When you commission a Wireless Gateway, you are prompted to autosense it. If you choose to autosense the Gateway, the wireless Reconcile I/O dialog opens. During the commissioning process, a red X can temporarily appear on the Wireless Gateway node until the commissioning process completes. If you notice a loss of communication with a Wireless Gateway after commissioning it (a red X persists on the Wireless Gateway node in the DeltaV Explorer and DeltaV Diagnostics hierarchies), it is possible that some security protocols have not been enabled. Follow these steps to enable the protocols. Select the Wireless Gateway under the Wireless I/O Network in DeltaV Explorer and use the context menu commands to log onto the Wireless Gateway's web interface using the admin account (user=admin). Refer to the Quick Installation Guide that ships with the 1420 for the default password. Navigate to Setup/Security/Protocols and enable the DeltaV Commissioner and HART UDP Port protocols. If these items are already enabled, exit the web interface and use DeltaV Diagnostics along with the troubleshooting information provided in the Wireless Gateway documentation to troubleshoot the communication problems. After enabling the DeltaV Commissioner and HART UDP Port protocols, exit the web interface, and decommission the Wireless Gateway. Open DeltaV Diagnostics, navigate to the Wireless Gateway node under Decommissioned Nodes, and use the context menu commands to log onto the Wireless Gateway's web interface using the admin account. Navigate to Setup/Security/User Accounts , select the Enable factory support accounts option, and click the Submit button. Click OK on the dialog that appears. Click the Restart Apps button, click Yes in response to the prompts to restart the application software, wait for the restart to complete, and close the web interface. From DeltaV Diagnostics, log onto the Gateway's web interface using the factory account (user=factory) and click Cancel on the dialog that appears. Navigate to Setup/Security/Protocols in the Wireless Gateway's web interface and confirm that the DeltaV Commissioner and HART UDP Port protocols are enabled. Navigate to Setup/Factory Settings , select the Save the settings as factory defaults option, and click the Submit button. Click the Restart Apps button. Click Yes to the Restart the application software now prompt and wait for the restart to complete. Close the web interface when the restart is complete. Note: It is expected that decommissioning a functional Wireless Gateway node would be a rare occurrence. However, if you should decommission a functional Wireless Gateway node with a redundant network in DeltaV Explorer, first open DeltaV Diagnostics and check the status of the node's Primary and Secondary communication links. Be sure that at least one of the communication links is Good. The Wireless Gateway node does not lose its IP address when both communication links are Bad and will not appear under the Decommissioned nodes list in DeltaV Explorer. For firmware version 3.xx, the only way to recommission the Wireless Gateway node when both communication links are Bad is to open the Gateway's housing, install a jumper to restore the factory settings, and then commission the Gateway. For firmware version 4.0 and higher, the only way to recommission the Wireless Gate node when both communication links are Bad is to open the Gateway's housing, move DIP switch 2 on the center circuit board to the ON position (left) to restore the factory settings and then commission the Gateway. For a simplex network, be sure that the Primary communication link is Good. Refer to the device documentation for information on how to restore the factory settings. Tip: After you decommission a Wireless Gateway node, a routine delay is normal before it appears in the list of Decommissioned Nodes in DeltaV Explorer. Also, you may need to wait for up to five minutes before recommissioning a recently decommissioned Wireless Gateway node or decommissioning a recently commissioned Wireless Gateway node. Related information Wireless devices: autosensing and assigning

title: Commission with DeltaV Explorer and the device commissioning wizard
main_heading:
Commission with DeltaV Explorer and the device commissioning
    wizard
body_text: Commission with DeltaV Explorer and the device commissioning wizard Attach the device to the segment. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > DeltaV Explorer to open the DeltaV Explorer. The device should appear under Decommissioned fieldbus Devices. It may take a minute for the device to appear. Tip : Press the F5 key to update the list. The device must be in the Standby state before you can commission it. To determine if a device is in Standby, select Decommissioned Devices, click View > Details from the menu bar, and be sure that the words "Standby fieldbus Device" appear under Type in the right pane. If the device is not in Standby, right-click the device in the right pane and select Standby . It may take a minute or so for the device to transition to Standby. Now be sure that the decommissioned device's properties, Device Type, Manufacturer, and Device Revision, match the placeholder properties. To check the properties, right-click the item and select Properties . If necessary, edit the placeholder properties to match the device properties. Select the device from the Decommissioned fieldbus Devices list and drag it to the placeholder. The Device Commissioning Wizard - Start opens. Read the information on the Device Commissioning Wizard - Start dialog and click Next to open the Device Commissioning Wizard – Reconcile Device dialog. Use this dialog to reconcile any differences between the placeholder and the device. Click the Reconcile Device button. (If you do not click this button and click Next instead, the parameters in the device will remain as they are and will overwrite the parameters in the placeholder when you commission the device.) The Reconcile Device dialog shows two sets of fieldbus device configuration parameters: parameters in the placeholder and parameters in the device. This dialog allows you to transfer parameters from a placeholder to a device and edit parameters in the device. Click the Help button and read about reconciling device parameters. Click the Transducer block in the upper left corner of the Reconcile dialog to reconcile the transducer block parameters. Read the device documentation before reconciling transducer block parameters. Click OK when you are finished reconciling parameters and then click Finish to commission the device. It may take a little while to commission the device. Several factors contribute to the time it takes to commission. Among these are the number of function blocks and devices and the time it takes for devices to move through the various device states. Related information Create a device placeholder

title: Communication failure due to open or bent pin
main_heading: Communication failure due to open or bent pin
body_text: Communication failure due to open or bent pin Some of the pins that connect the card to the carrier can become bent or broken during installation or through improper handling. An open or bent pin shorts to the adjacent pin and causes the redundant cards to stop communicating and a switchover to occur. To correct this issue: Remove the redundant cards and check for bent or broken pins. Straighten any bent pins and re-insert the card into its slot on the carrier. Replace the card if a pin is broken or bent beyond repair. Open DeltaV Diagnostics (click Start > DeltaV Operator > Diagnostics ). For each card, right-click the card, and then select Clear Saved Fault Information .

title: Complete the firewall configuration
body_text: Complete the firewall configuration It is assumed that all communications rules have been created and tested. On the firewall's web UI navigate to the Protection tab Inbound connections and Outbound connections and delete the ping rules that were created as part of the configuration procedure. Go to Administration > Backup/Restore and create a new backup of the configuration. This saves the configuration locally on the firewall. On the Backup/Restore page, click copy to local PC (listed under Actions ) and save the configuration in case you need to restore it later. Note: The backup cannot be used to make configuration changes from outside the firewall; it is only used to restore a configuration. Go to Administration > Configuration audit and print the configuration. For audit purposes this should be signed and dated and stored as part of the firewall change management process. If possible it should also be printed to a file and stored with the configuration backup. Navigate to the Dashboard tab and ensure that all of the ping rules are disconnected and only valid communications are listed. Go to Administration > Restart page and restart the firewall (if possible). This ensures that the firewall is properly configured and if at a later time, the firewall restarts, you will know it allows the communications to successfully restart. It also ensures the ping communications and any other communications created in which the rules are deleted or disabled are completely terminated. Ensure that the rules are working as expected.

title: Complete the Sequential Function Chart diagram
main_heading: Complete the Sequential Function Chart diagram
body_text: Complete the Sequential Function Chart diagram Repeat the procedures for adding steps and transitions using the information in the following table. (Drag Step and Transition icons from the palette or use the Sequence item on the palette to automatically add multiple steps and transitions in one operation. Use a Termination icon for the last transition.) Tip: On the View tab, in the Diagram group, click Diagram Preferences , and then check Display Grid and Snap to Grid to help you line up the SFC objects on the diagram. Note: In the example, all Action Types are Assignment; all Action Qualifiers are Pulse, except for Action 2 in Step 2, which has an Action Qualifier of Non-stored. (The reason is that if Action 2 Step 2 were Pulse, it might not get set because it waits until the actual mode is Auto. It would fail on the first try and never be set.) Use the Connect Mode tool to connect the steps and transitions in order. Change the step and transition names by right-clicking, selecting Rename , and then typing the name listed in the following table. Be sure to read the table footnote for important information about statement syntax. Step/Transition Name Action Text or Condition Text* Description S1 STOP_AND_WAIT 'SP':='SFCCTRL:IDLE'; Inhibits startup sequence (until the user changes the SP to START). T1 WAIT_ UNTIL_START 'SP'='SFCCTRL: START' Waits until operator selects START. If SP is START, proceeds to the next step. S2 SET_FLOW_RATE A1: '//FIC-101/PID1/MODE. TARGET' := AUTO; A2: '//FIC-101/PID1/SP': = 50; (Action Qualifier is Non-Stored.) Sets the flow loop to AUTO. Sets the setpoint at 50 GPM. T2 WAIT_FOR_OUT_30 '//FIC-101/PID1/OUT' > 30 Waits for the regulatory valve to be 30% open. S3 OPEN_BLK_VLV '//XV-101/DC1/SP_D':=1; Opens the block valve. T3 WAIT_VLV_OPEN '//XV-101/DC1/PV_D'=1 Confirms that the block valve is open. S4 START_PUMP '//MTR-101/DC1/SP_D' :=1; Starts the pump. T4 WAIT_PUMP_START '//MTR-101/DC1/PV_D'=1 Confirms the pump started. * IMPORTANT: Assignment actions use the assignment operator ( :=) and end with a semicolon (; ). Transitions use an equals sign (=) to indicate that when the condition is true, the next step should be made active. Parameter values are enclosed in single quotes. The finished SFC looks like this.

title: Complete the recipe properties
body_text: Complete the recipe properties There are several fields you might want to complete to document the recipe. These fields are found on the Product tab of the recipe's Properties dialog. It is recommend that, at a minimum, you enter a version identifier and author. The version identifier can be used to manually track when changes have been made to the recipe or the formula. The Version field and Author fields are logged in the batch history file when a recipe is run. Right-click the Diagram View, and then click Properties to open the Properties dialog. On the Product tab, enter a Product name (Paint) and Product code (any string). Enter 1.001 (or any string) in the Version field and your name in the Author field. Click OK .

title: Configure an operation (OP_FINISH)
body_text: Configure an operation (OP_FINISH) Leave the first step and transition as they are on the screen. Add a new step by dragging a step icon from the palette to a spot below the first transition. Select Properties from the context menu to open the Properties dialog (or double-click the step). Browse for the phase class AGITATE (in the BlenderPhases category). Enter the description as Agitate blender. The Key Parameter field allows you to select one parameter that will display on the step when viewing the recipe in the Batch Operator Interface. For this tutorial, leave it as the default <none>. Click OK . Another dialog opens for you to select whether the recipe is to be class-based or unit specific. This only occurs on the first step in the recipe and sets the class or unit for the current recipe. Select Unit class , and then select the class BLENDER. Draw a line from the previous transition to the step. Add a transition and draw a line from the previous step to the transition. The following transition text is automatically created: 'AGITATE:1/BSTATUS' = '$phase_state:Complete' Add a step and modify it to use the phase class DRAIN. Enter the description as Drain blender. Draw a line from the previous transition to the step. Drag a termination below the step. Draw a line from the step to the termination. Click the Main button, click Save , and then name the operation OP_FINISH. The completed procedural function chart looks like the following:

title: Configure an SIS module
body_text: Configure an SIS module Configuring an SIS module is similar to configuring a control module. Open the SIS module in Control Studio. Drag the function blocks and parameters you need from the various SIS palettes to the diagram. Modify each block's extensible parameters, properties, and so on, as necessary. Wire the blocks, set parameter values as needed, and set the execution order of the blocks.

title: Configure an SLS 1508 logic solver
body_text: Configure an SLS 1508 logic solver The SLS 1508 logic solver card and logic solver are configured in different places in the DeltaV Explorer. After you create the logic solver assign it to the logic solver card. Navigate to a SIS Network Domain in the SIS Network in DeltaV Explorer. Right-click and select New Logic Solver . On the General page of the Properties dialog that opens, enter a name and description for the Logic Solver. The default name is SLS n , where n is the next unique number, beginning with 1. Select a Scan Rate from the drop-down list. Refer to the DeltaV SIS Safety Manual for guidelines on choosing the scan rate. If desired, select the Enable fast I/O updates to the DeltaV Controller check box . If you want secure parameters published by this logic solver available to logic solvers in other nodes, select the Publish secure parameters globally checkbox, then select whether to publish as SIS Network Domain globals or system globals. If you want to have this logic solver publish 16 secure parameters, select the High-Density Secure Parameters checkbox. On the Alarms and Displays tab, enter or browse for the displays to be used for the Primary Control, Detail, and Faceplate displays. On the Proof Testing tab, set the Proof Test Interval in years and days and set the Proof Test Reminder Alert in days. Note: For more information on proof testing, refer to the DeltaV SIS Safety Manual . Click OK . The Logic Solver now appears in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy under a SIS Network Domain in the SIS Network, but the icon is grayed until it is commissioned to a Logic Solver card. You can also create a Logic Solver by dragging and dropping a Logic Solver card from an I/O subsystem onto a SIS Network Domain (which assigns the Logic Solver as well). Right-click the Logic Solver and select Properties to complete the properties information.

title: Configure a physical SLS 1508 logic solver card
main_heading: Configure a physical SLS 1508 logic solver card
body_text: Configure a physical SLS 1508 logic solver card Create Logic Solver cards under controller I/O subsystems in the Physical Network. The cards can also be auto-sensed. Logic Solver card icons are different from other card icons. You assign a Logic Solver in the SIS Network to the physical Logic Solver card. Navigate to the I/O subsystem under a controller. Right-click and select New Card . Select SIS Cards as the card class. Logic Solver is the only choice in the SIS card class. Select the slot position, which should always be an odd number for Logic Solver cards. Note: The Logic Solver card occupies two slots for a simplex and four slots for a redundant Logic Solver. If the card is redundant, select the Card is redundant check box. Click OK .

title: Configure the charge and dump phase classes
main_heading: Configure the charge and dump phase classes
body_text: Configure the charge and dump phase classes Create the SFC logic diagrams for the CHG_COLOR and DUMP phase class running logic as shown in the following diagrams. In the DeltaV Explorer, assign the CHG_COLOR phase class to the BLENDER unit class. DUMP was previously assigned to the COLOR unit class. Click View > Refresh (or press the F5 key) and verify that the new unit phases (that is, CHG_COLOR in both UM_BLEND_500 and UM_BLEND_600) have been created on the appropriate unit modules. Select the new unit phases (both CHG_COLOR and DUMP) and mark them to be included in the download by selecting Controller as the Phase type on the Properties dialog.

title: Configure a CIOC placeholder
body_text: Configure a CIOC placeholder A CIOC placeholder is configured in DeltaV Explorer through its Properties pages. Rght-click the CIOC in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Select Properties . Click the Help button on each tab in the Properties dialog for information about the options on that page.

title: Configure communications failure modes for fieldbus valves
main_heading: Configure communications failure modes for fieldbus valves
body_text: Configure communications failure modes for fieldbus valves If a fieldbus valve loses air, or a fieldbus valve positioner loses power, the valve will either go fully open or fully closed. This state is determined by the valve itself and is often termed its shelf position or air fail position. This state is different from the Fault State parameter (FSTATE_VAL) of the Analog Output function block when it is assigned to a fieldbus valve. By default the Analog Output function block's FSTATE_VAL and FSTATE_TIME parameters are set to 0. This causes the block to hold the last value when communication on the fieldbus is lost. It is highly recommended that you configure the FSTATE_VAL parameter to correctly set the valve position if fieldbus communications to the valve cease for the time period that you configure with the FSTATE_TIME parameter. Communication to a device is lost when a fieldbus function block is downloaded. Follow these steps to configure these parameters in Control Studio: Assign the AO block to a fieldbus device. Note: This step is very important as the FSTATE_VAL and FSTATE_TIME parameters only appear in the parameter list after the block has been assigned to a fieldbus device. Double-click IO_OPTS and enable Fault State to value. Configure the FSTATE_VAL and FSTATE_TIME parameters.

title: Configure a CSLS LS CHARM
body_text: Configure a CSLS LS CHARM When a CSLS is created under the Local Safety Network, the LS CHARMs default to the Undefined channel type. You must then configure the LS CHARMs to define the type of I/O signal. Navigate to an LS CHARM in the CHARMs subsystem under a CSLS. Right-click, and then select Properties . Select a CHARM class . The Enabled check box is automatically selected. Fill in the Description and Cabling ID fields if desired. Select a CHARM hardware type . Select a CHARM functionality . The Device Tag field is blank at this point but if you click OK and reopen the dialog, the field contains the default DST. To select a Device Tag other than the default, click the Browse button next to the Device Tag field. Note: The Browse dialog displays the Unassigned I/O references of the appropriate type for the channel type. Select an I/O reference, and then click OK . If required, enter the HART Long Tag . Click OK in the LS CHARM Properties dialog.

title: Configure a dataset for VIM
body_text: Configure a dataset for VIM Each port can have as many as 16 datasets associated with it. These can all be configured for one device or you can have several devices with one or more datasets each. To create a dataset, right-click the device and select New Dataset . On the General tab of the Create dataset dialog: Enter a description, if desired. Select the Data direction . If you selected Output , enter an Output mode : 0 indicates the entire dataset is written to the PLC if any dataset register changes. 1 indicates only the value that has changed is written. If you want the output dataset to be read back into the Serial Card's input scan, select the Output read back check box. The values that are read back update the current output values. If this box is not checked, no output read back is performed. Open the DeltaV tab of the dialog. On the DeltaV tab: Select the DeltaV data type this dataset contains. Enter or browse to a Dataset Tag . A Dataset Tag , together with a specific register, is a Device Signal Tag (DST). You use DSTs to configure DeltaV control modules that read from or write to a serial device. This concludes the common configuration tasks. The following sections contain the instructions for completing the configuration of the three different device types.

title: Configure VIM Ethernet devices
body_text: Configure VIM Ethernet devices At this point you should have configured the serial cards, ports, devices, and datasets through the DeltaV tab of the Dataset Properties dialog. Open the PLC tab of the dialog. On this tab, specify the DF1 command type to be used to read/write the dataset: Enter a Device data type that matches the PLC you are communicating with. Enter a Data start address , specifying where in the PLC table where data is read. This can be any valid PLC specific table address. Enter a Number of values value. This parameter determines the registers read or written. The start address plus the number of values must not exceed the maximum table size. Open the Special data tab. Enter the value or values required by your application. Subtopics: VIM Ethernet device configuration data Related information VIM Ethernet device configuration data

title: Configure the external network
body_text: Configure the external network Note: If you will be communicating to devices other than computers, such as network printers, it is necessary to ensure these devices can communicate through the firewall. Refer to the device instructions to ensure they are configured correctly to communicate through the firewall. Navigate to Configuration > Network settings > External workstations. If Then static addressing is used enter the workstation names and IP addresses from the Worksheet for external workstation names and IP addresses . dynamic addressing is used you must be connected to the external network and the external network routing must be configured correctly for the firewall to obtain this address. There are two ways to establish routing: Use the route add command to configure a route in each external workstation Configure the router on the external LAN to route traffic for the DeltaV 2.5 network addresses to the external address of the firewall. Routing must be completed before testing communications on either side of the firewall In the firewall's web UI navigate to Configuration > Network settings and depending upon input from your IT department either select or deselect Allow users on the external interface to access through HTTPS (read only). Navigate to Configuration > Summary and ensure the information is correct. Navigate to Configuration > Internal workstations and if dynamic addressing is used for DeltaV workstations, ensure that these workstations are listed. If you do not see any or all of the DeltaV workstations that are connected to the firewall ensure that the network cables are connected properly and the workstations' NICs are set to Obtain an IP address automatically . Remember that if static IP addressing is used for the DeltaV workstations, the workstation name and IP address is entered directly into the firewall through the firewall's web UI. Related information Worksheet for external workstation names and IP addresses

title: Configure history collection in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading: Configure history collection in DeltaV Explorer
body_text: Configure history collection in DeltaV Explorer In DeltaV Explorer, complete the following steps to configure the collection of historical data: Right-click an Area or a module and select History Collection from the context menu. On the History Collection dialog, click the Add button to configure the history collection for that object. To modify or delete an existing history collection, select a parameter and click the Modify or Delete button. Fill in the Add History Collection dialog. Click the Help button on the dialog for specific instructions. Download the workstation.

title: Configure history collection for modules in Control Studio
main_heading: Configure history collection for modules in Control Studio
body_text: Configure history collection for modules in Control Studio Open a module and select History Collection from the File menu. On the History Collection dialog, click the Add , Modify , or Delete buttons to configure the history collection for that object. To modify or delete an existing history collection, select the parameter and click the Modify or Delete button. Fill in the Add History Collection dialog. Click the Help button on the dialog for specific instructions. Download the module.

title: Configure history collection for parameters in Control Studio
main_heading: Configure history collection for parameters in Control Studio
body_text: Configure history collection for parameters in Control Studio Open a module, select the desired function block and parameter. Right-click the parameter and select Add History Recorder from the context menu. Fill in the Add History Collection dialog. Click the Help button on the dialog for specific instructions. Download the module.

title: Configure the internal network
body_text: Configure the internal network You will need the information from the Worksheet for internal workstation names and IP addresses to configure the internal network. It is assumed that you have the firewall installed, powered up and the network cables correctly installed and the firewall is able to access the DeltaV workstations and the external network. In the firewall's web UI navigate to the Configuration > Network settings . Set up the internal network information from the Worksheet for internal workstation names and IP addresses . If you change the internal network address from 192.168.1.1 to another address the web UI will disconnect and you will have to log in again using the new address. If you use a different subnet from the firewall default, the PC will need a new address in its Network Interface Card (NIC) to access the firewall. The PC's NIC information is updated by the firewall if the firewall is set to automatically assign addresses. If not, you will have to set up the PC's NIC manually by editing its IPv4 properties. If the firewall is set to provide an address automatically you may need to force the firewall to update the computer. The easiest way is to unplug the network cable from the PC and wait a minute or two and then reconnect the cable. This will alert the firewall that there is a new device and it will assign a new address. If you are using static network addressing, use the information from the setup sheet to configure the NIC on the PC. The next step is to configure static addressing on DeltaV workstations. Related information Configure static addressing on DeltaV workstations Worksheet for internal workstation names and IP addresses

title: Configure a control module to perform a customized alarm roll-up
main_heading:
Configure a control module to perform a customized alarm
	 roll-up
body_text: Configure a control module to perform a customized alarm roll-up The Alarm Unit dynamo (HP_Alarms) shows alarm count information. This dynamo can be configured to perform alarm roll-ups in modules matching the normal breakdown of Area > Unit > Equipment Module > Module or in modules that do now match the normal breakdown of Area > Unit > Equipment Module > Module. The steps below show how to configure a control module to perform a customized alarm roll-up. Open the module in Control Studio. Add a CALC block to the module. Add these parameters at the module level: Parameter Description PRI Represents the module's highest alarm's priority. CUALM Represents whether the module's highest alarm is a new alarm. NALM Represents the highest alarm's current state. COUNT Counts the total number of annunciated alarms. That is, it counts all alarms that are Active/Unacknowledged, Active/Acknowledged, and Inactive/Unacknowledged. Add the following code to the module: Pn := 255; Cn := 0; Nn := 0; Count := 0; Pt := '//MODULE/ALARMS[1].PRI'; Ct := '//MODULE/ALARMS[1].CUALM'; Nt := '//MODULE/ALARMS[1].NALM'; IF ((Nt > Nn) OR (Ct * (Cn - 1) < 0) OR ((Nt = Nn) AND ((Ct != 0)=(Cn != 0)) AND (Pt > Pn))) THEN Pn := Pt; Cn := Ct; Nn := Nt; Count := Count + 1; ELSE IF (Nt > 0) OR (Ct > 0) THEN Count := Count + 1; END_IF; END_IF; '^/PRI' := Pn; '^/CUALM' := Cn; '^/COUNT' := Count; '^/NALM' := Nn; Replace MODULE with the module name. If you want additional modules included in the alarm roll-up, duplicate the following code for each module: Pt := '//MODULE/ALARMS[1].PRI'; Ct := '//MODULE/ALARMS[1].CUALM'; Nt := '//MODULE/ALARMS[1].NALM'; IF ((Nt > Nn) OR (Ct * (Cn - 1) < 0) OR ((Nt = Nn) AND ((Ct != 0)=(Cn != 0)) AND (Pt > Pn))) THEN Pn := Pt; Cn := Ct; Nn := Nt; Count := Count + 1; ELSE IF (Nt > 0) OR (Ct > 0) THEN Count := Count + 1; END_IF; END_IF; Replace each MODULE with the appropriate module name. Save the module. In DeltaV Operate Configure, open the HP_Alarms' Dynamo Properties dialog. Select the Custom radio button. Browse to the module's PRI, NALM, CUALM, and COUNT parameters. Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog. Related information High Performance Unit Alarms Indicator dynamo (HP_Alarms)

title: Configure a port for VIM
body_text: Configure a port for VIM In DeltaV Explorer right-click a card port and select Properties . On the Port tab, select the Enabled check box and enter a description, if desired. Note: Enable only the ports you are using. Do not enable unused ports. Open the Advanced tab. On the Advanced tab: In the Mode field, select Master . Select values for the Retry count , Message timeout , and Transmit delay fields. For most applications configure the port as shown above. Do not select the Send outputs on startup check box. Open the Communications tab. The fields on the Communications tab are not used. Accept the default values and click OK .

title: Configure the Remote Desktop client
body_text: Configure the Remote Desktop client The Remote Desktop client is the computer that will connect to the DeltaV workstation using Remote Desktop Connection by going through the Remote Desktop Gateway. You must have an SSL-compatible x.509 certificate that was exported from your Remote Desktop Gateway (RD Gateway) computer. If you do not have one, please return to the previous sections on the certificates. Configure the TCP/IP properties of the NIC that will connect to the Remote Desktop Gateway server (see table of network addresses you created earlier). Connect this NIC to the appropriate switch/hub/firewall (based on in your network map). Copy the Remote Desktop Gateway's server certificate to the RD Client computer and make note of where you copy it to. The certificate is exported from the RD Gateway server to the default location of c:\users\administrator\Documents\RDG-SRV.cer (where RGD-SRV is the name of our example Remote Desktop Gateway machine). Note: You can also install the certificate when the RD Client computer connects to the RD Gateway. Remote Desktop Connection informs the user that the certificate is not installed and prompts if you want to install it then. However, to be sure that the correct certificate is used, it is strongly recommended that you configure the clients with the appropriate certificate before connecting to the DeltaV node. Install and establish a root certificate trust for on the Remote Desktop client.

title: Configure the Remote Desktop Gateway server
main_heading: Configure the Remote Desktop Gateway server
body_text: Configure the Remote Desktop Gateway server This procedure describes how to configure a computer to be your Remote Desktop Gateway (RD Gateway) server. The Remote Desktop Gateway (RD Gateway) server computer is a non-DeltaV computer that resides outside of the DeltaV ACN network. Normally in the DMZ or PlantLAN (L3/L4) networks. Through this gateway, computers on non-DeltaV networks can access DeltaV (provided the credentials and certificates are valid). Install Windows Server (2008 R2 or higher) on the computer that will be your RD Gateway server and configure the network address. Using the Windows Server product disk, install the server operating system. This will require multiple reboots. Name the computer something relevant. For this example, we use the name: RDG-SRV . Configure TCP/IP properties so that RDG-SRV has an IPv4 static IP address. Refer to your table of IP addresses developed earlier. For this example we use the address: 10.0.0.11 . Connect the RDG-SRV to the appropriate switches/hubs/firewalls (based on your network map). Join RDG-SRV to the appropriate domain (if needed). Because the RD Gateway computer (RDG-SRV) is normally located outside of the Emerson Smart Firewall, you would connect to a non-DeltaV network in the DMZ or higher. Install the RD Gateway role on RDG-SRV (using Server Manager). This will also install any dependent roles, services, and features. Provide IIS with a certificate and export a certificate for RD Gateway. You can create this from IIS Manager for testing/evaluation purposes. The type of certificate (self-signed or CA) is the user's decision. However, for TLS (Transport Layer Security) to function correctly, you must install an SSL-compatible X.509 certificate on the RD Gateway server. Install the certificate on the RD Gateway Server (RDG-SRV) using the Remote Desktop Gateway Manager. Export the SSL certificate from the RD Gateway (RDG-SRV) using Remote Desktop Manager. This step is only required for self-signed certificates and certificates not already trusted on the Remote Desktop Client. In those two instances, the certificate will be installed on the Remote Desktop client computer.

title: Configure secure parameters
body_text: Configure secure parameters To transfer data from one SIS module to another, you must configure a Secure Parameter and a Secure Parameter Reference. This pair (parameter and reference) is required whether the SIS modules are assigned to the same logic solver or different logic solvers. Drag a Secure Parameter from the Special Items palette to the function block diagram for the SIS module. A Properties dialog appears with a parameter type of Boolean with status. Name the parameter, select a parameter category, change the value if desired, and click OK . Wire a Boolean parameter that you want to reference from another module to the secure parameter. Click the Main button, then click Save . Note: If the module is assigned to a logic solver, the database verifies that the logic solver has a secure parameter slot available, and assigns the slot for the parameter. The number of secure parameters than can be configured in a module depends on: The type of logic solver the module is assigned to. For SLS 1508 logic solvers, whether it is configured for high-density secure parameters. The number of remaining slots available in the logic solver. An unassigned module containing secure parameters can only be assigned to a logic solver that has enough slots available to contain the configured secure parameters. Related information Capacity limits for CHARMs Smart Logic Solver SIS systems Capacity limits for SLS 1508 SIS systems

title: Configure secure parameter references
body_text: Configure secure parameter references If you have a secure reference configured in an SIS module you can configure a secure parameter reference using these steps. Open a different SIS module. Drag a Secure Parameter Reference from the Special Items palette onto the function block diagram. A properties dialog opens for the secure parameter reference. Enter a name and select a parameter category. Click the Browse button. Browse to the Secure Parameter that you defined previously and click OK . Note: In SLS 1508 systems the database checks to make sure the Secure Parameter is in a Logic Solver on the local peer bus or in a Logic Solver publishing Secure Parameters globally. In CHARMs Smart Logic Solver systems the database checks to make sure the Secure Parameter is in a CSLS on the Local Safety Network. Multiple secure parameter references can refer to the same secure parameter. Click the Main button, then click Save .

title: Configure security options for OSIsoft PI Server
main_heading: Configure security options for OSIsoft PI Server
body_text: Configure security options for OSIsoft PI Server On the workstation where you installed OSIsoft PI Server, use the PI System Management Tools (PI SMT) application to complete the following steps: Navigate to Security > Security Settings , and then disable or set all security options to their lowest level. Navigate to Security > Mappings & Trusts > Trusts , select the Trusts tab, and then specify DeltaVAdmin for PI User or specify DeltaV for PI Groups . If you installed PI Server on a remote Application Station or a non-DeltaV workstation outside the DeltaV Area Control Network (ACN), navigate to Security > Mappings & Trusts , select the Mappings tab, and then create a mapping between the account under which the DeltaV Smart Connector is running on the Application Station (typically, the DeltaVAdmin account) and a PI User with write access to PI Server database, such as piadmin . To initiate communications using the new mapping, ensure that it is enabled in the PI System Management Tools, and then restart the Application Station where you installed the DeltaV Smart Connector.

title: Configure SIS alarm groups
body_text: Configure SIS alarm groups With the SIS module open in Control Studio, on the Home tab, in the Alarms group, click Alarm Groups Configuration . Click New to create a new alarm group. With the alarm group selected, click Modify . Modify the alarm group name and enter the primary control, detail and faceplate displays for the alarm group. The alarm group name must be unique within the DeltaV system. Create additional alarm groups as needed. If blocks are available in the module, you can assign them to the alarm groups. To do this, select an alarm group and click the Assignments tab. Select a block or blocks from the Available Items list that you want to assign to this alarm group. If blocks are not available, you can make the assignments at a later time. Click Assign . Click Apply . Click Close .

title: Configure SIS Controller Modbus port Data set mapping
main_heading: Configure SIS Controller Modbus port Data set mapping
body_text: Configure SIS Controller Modbus port Data set mapping This topic assumes you have already configured registers from the Modbus Port Properties dialog. You can map registers interactively from DeltaV Explorer using the Register mapping dialog. However, because of the potentially large numbers of register to map it is recommended that you use Bulk Edit to map registers initially. To map registers from DeltaV Explorer: Select the Modbus port. Right click and select Map Registers . On the Register mapping dialog, select a register to map and click the Map button. On the Map Register dialog, browse to the parameter to map the selected register to. Click OK to accept the mapping and close the dialog. Repeat steps t_configure_sis_controller_modbus_port_mapping.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_122__step_A72D8824F64A4A7C805E0E2C7BAFEE03 through t_configure_sis_controller_modbus_port_mapping.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_122__step_8CCD3662A82D46188849E7C2755CB1F0 for other registers you want to map. Click Close on the Register mapping dialog to accept your changes. Related information Bulk edit SIS Controller Modbus Port register mapping

title: Configure SIS module alarms
body_text: Configure SIS module alarms SIS module alarms are configured in the same way as control modules. With the SIS module open in Control Studio, right-click in the Alarm View and select Add . The Alarm Properties dialog appears. The only alarm types in the drop-down list are SIS alarm types. Select an SIS alarm type and priority. Enter or browse to an alarm parameter. If you select or enter a bitstring parameter such as SIF_ALERTS, the Mask button appears on the Alarm Properties dialog. Click the Mask button to open the Alarm Mask dialog. On the Alarm Mask dialog, select the bits you want to activate this alarm. If any of the conditions you select become active, the alarm becomes active. Close the Alarm Mask dialog. Close the Alarm Properties dialog.

title: Configure static addressing on DeltaV workstations
main_heading: Configure static addressing on DeltaV workstations
body_text: Configure static addressing on DeltaV workstations Use the Control Panel and navigate to Network and Internet > View network status and tasks > Change adapter settings . Select the plant LAN adapter, (not the DeltaV Control Network adapter), on the DeltaV workstation, click the right mouse button, and select Properties . Select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and click the Properties button. Select Use the following IP address and enter the DeltaV workstation's IP address and subnet mask. Set the default gateway to the internal address of the firewall so the PC can communicate with the devices on the external LANs. Select Use the following DNS server addresses . Leave blank the Preferred DNS server and Alternate DNS server entries for now. Click OK to save the settings.

title: Configure the first Application Station
body_text: Configure the first Application Station In DeltaV Explorer on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, right-click one of the existing pair of Application Stations that you intend to use for running an OPC client connected to a redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. Click Delete on the shortcut menu for the Application Station, and then click Yes when prompted to confirm that you want to delete this Application Station from the Control Network. In DeltaV Explorer, right-click the remaining Application Station that you intend to use for running an OPC client connected to a redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. Click Properties on the shortcut menu for the Application Station. You can optionally change the name of the Application Station on the General tab of the Properties dialog, but this is not necessary. However, changing the Application Station name is strongly recommended if it coincidentally ends with the characters _S. Important: As a general rule, do not specify an Application Station name that ends with the characters _S. When the DeltaV system creates a pair of Application Stations for redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server, it appends these characters to whatever name you specify as the base name for the Application Station. Having a pair of Application Stations named nodename _S and nodename _S_S could result in misleading or undesirable results while working with redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. On the Redundancy tab of the Properties dialog, check the Enable a redundant subsystem option, select the Assigned Modules option, and then select either the OPC Data Access Server option or the OPC Data Access Server and OPC Mirror option. Important: You cannot enable redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on a pair of Application Stations if you have already enabled any other subsystems, such as Batch Executive, Batch Historian, Continuous Historian, Campaign Manager, Alarms and Events, or Remote Network, for this Application Station. To enable redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on a pair of Application Stations, you must first disable any previously-enabled assigned modules for this Application Station. Enabling redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server You can optionally enable the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, if either of the Application Stations will be located in an unmanned facility, for example. Click OK to close the Properties dialog for the Application Station. When prompted to export a workstation configuration file for the Application Station, click Yes . Save the workstation configuration file either to removable media or to a network location that can be accessed from the Application Station you are configuring. You can use the default name for a workstation configuration file, DevData.cfg, or specify a different file name. On the Application Station that you did not delete in DeltaV Explorer, import the workstation configuration file by clicking Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Workstation Configuration on the Start menu. When the introductory DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog appears, click Next . For the Select Workstation Type option, select Professional / Operator / Application / Base / Inter-Zone Server , and then click Next . Specifying the type of workstation When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Importing the workstation configuration file Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with Redundant Assigned Modules has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? It is recommended that you respond to this prompt by clicking Yes when configuring the first of the two Application Stations. When you click Yes , the Application Station is given the name specified for it in DeltaV Explorer. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the configuration of the Application Station. Note: If you ever need to reconfigure either workstation in the pair, you should respond to this prompt by clicking Yes if it is the Application Station that you specified as the preferred active; otherwise, click No , if it is the workstation with the characters _S appended to the base Application Station name. Related information Configure the second Application Station Using the unattended reboot option Initiate a manual switchover Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server

title: Configure the second Application Station
body_text: Configure the second Application Station On the Application Station that you deleted in DeltaV Explorer earlier, import the workstation configuration file by clicking Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Workstation Configuration on the Start menu. When the introductory DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog appears, click Next . When prompted to choose your workstation type, select the Local Application Station option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier on the Professional PLUS workstation, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. In the DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog, select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with Redundant Assigned Modules has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? If you clicked Yes earlier when configuring the first Application Station, you must respond to this prompt by clicking No now. When you click No , the characters _S are appended to the name specified for the Application Station in DeltaV Explorer on the Professional PLUS workstation. Important: When the message appears, advising you that any historical database stored on this Application Station will be deleted, click Yes to continue with this procedure, if you have no historian data sets to protect. Otherwise, click No to discontinue this procedure until you have backed up or exported historian data sets. After backing up your historian data sets, restart this procedure of importing the workstation configuration file. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the second Application Station. Related information Finish configuring Application Station redundancy Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server Back up a historical data set Automated backup utility Export a historical data set

title: Configure VIM Modbus TCP/IP
body_text: Configure VIM Modbus TCP/IP At this point you should have configured the serial cards, ports, devices, and datasets through the DeltaV tab of the Dataset Properties dialog. Specify the Device data type. Open the PLC tab of the dialog. In this dialog you map DeltaV data types to PLC (or external device) data types. In the Data start address field specify where in the PLC to read the data. This can be any PLC specific address. Finally, open the Special data tab. The Special data 1 value is used when transferring data for Floating point, signed 32-bit integer and unsigned 32-bit integer registers. The Special data 2 value is used to indicate the number of registers used for Floating point and 32-bit integer values. Details of Special data usage are provided below. You can customize ModbusTCP communications and representation of data with the VIM firmware. Modification of data representation is typically only required when reading/writing Floating Point or Signed/Unsigned 32-bit Integer registers. However, in some cases, you may need to use Special data 1 for 16-bit byte swapping as well. To customize data representation in a data set, you can use the Special data 1 and 2 registers as flags. To customize communications for a specific data set, the Special data 3 and 4 registers are used. This is described below. Assume a Floating-point number 123.45, and its representation in IEEE 754 format as follows: Floating-point number Represented as 2 16-bit words Represented as 4 bytes 123.45 58982, 17142 230, 102, 66, 246 Configure the remaining datasets the device requires. Subtopics: VIM Modbus TCP/IP configuration data Related information VIM Modbus TCP/IP configuration data

title: Configure other workstations
body_text: Configure other workstations Perform the following steps on the other workstations: Open the Workstation Configuration application by clicking Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Workstation Configuration . Click Next on the opening screen. Select Other Workstation and then click Next to continue. The Workstation Configuration application guides you through the process of configuring the workstation. Remember to refer to the online help. This process may take several minutes to complete. You are instructed to restart your computer for the configuration changes to take effect. If you have more workstations to configure, repeat this procedure on each workstation using the same workstation configuration file. When you have finished configuring the workstations, you need to download each workstation's configuration. Related information Download the ProfessionalPLUS workstation

title: Configure the test parameters
body_text: Configure the test parameters To configure any download or report parameters do the following: Select Config > Download Params or Config > Report Params . Click the Add button on the dialog (if editing an existing parameter, click Modify ). Enter the parameter name, type and if required, default value. Click OK .

title: Configure the structure of external phases in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading:
Configure the structure of external phases in DeltaV
	 Explorer
body_text: Configure the structure of external phases in DeltaV Explorer The external phase referenced in this example uses the DeltaV Soft Phase server. Specific instructions for writing an external phase of type Syncade is covered in its documentation set. However, all external phases must be created in DeltaV Explorer under System Configuration/Control Strategies/External Phases , as described here. Create a phase class. (In this example, the DeltaV soft phase exe file will have the same name as this phase class, for example, CS_MANUAL_ADD.) Create a unit class, for example, TANKS. Associate the phase class with the unit class. That is, drag CS_MANUAL_ADD to TANKS. Create an external phase under Control Strategies. Associate the external phase with your phase class (CS_MANUAL_ADD in our example). Right-click the external phase and select Properties . Set the external phase server to SoftPhase. (If creating a Syncade external phase, select the Syncade option here.) Enter the soft phase node (that is, where the soft phase will run). (This step is only applicable for the phase server type of Soft Phase.) If left blank, the system defaults to the Batch Executive. Click OK . Create a process cell in an area. The process cell must be class based for the Batch Executive to recognize it. Either drag the process cell class down to the area, or select the area and right-click, selecting New > Process Cell . Create the unit module in the process cell. You can either drag the unit class (TANKS) down to the process cell or select the process cell and right-click, selecting New > Unit Module . Name the instance, for example, TANK_600. Expand the unit that will need to run the soft phase (TANK_600) and select the unit phase (CS_MANUAL_ADD). Right-click the unit phase and change the phase type to External Phase type. Select the external phase name. You can click Browse and select the external phase created previously. Assign the area to a Batch Executive. Download the Batch Executive. Assign the unit module to the appropriate node (controller) and download that node.

title: Configuring alarms on option bitstring parameters
main_heading: Configuring alarms on option bitstring parameters
body_text: Configuring alarms on option bitstring parameters DeltaV software supports alarming on individual bits of function block and module bitstring parameters such as MERROR. For example, to configure an alarm controlled by one or more bits of the MERROR parameter, do the following: With the module open in Control Studio, right-click in the Alarm View and select Add . The Alarm Properties dialog appears. Select an alarm type. Enter or browse to the module's MERROR parameter. Because MERROR is a bitstring parameter the Mask button appears next to the Browse button. Note: The Mask button appears only when a bitstring parameter that supports alarming on individual bits is selected. To select the bits that cause the alarm to become active click the Mask button. The Alarm Mask dialog opens. The Alarm Mask dialog contains check boxes for all of the bits of the currently selected parameter. Select the bits you want to activate this alarm. If any of the conditions you select become active, the alarm becomes active. Close the Alarm Mask dialog. Select a Functional classification for this alarm. If you want operators and other users to have access to alarm help, select the Enable alarm help check box. This check box adds an Alarm Help tab to the Properties dialog. On the Advanced tab, enter optional alarm message parameters and set the alarm shelving timeout. Setting the three alarm shelving timeout fields to zero (0) disables alarm shelving. Close the Alarm Properties dialog. Related information DeltaV Alarm Help

title: Configure the first channel on the first I/O card
main_heading: Configure the first channel on the first I/O card
body_text: Configure the first channel on the first I/O card In the DeltaV Explorer, select System Configuration > Physical Network > Control Network > CTLR1 > I/O . The right pane lists the I/O cards. Click the I/O configuration button on the toolbar (or right-click I/O , and then select Configure I/O from the menu). The I/O Configuration window opens, displaying a list of the eight channels available on all the I/O cards. The default channel names are CH01 through CH08. For the first card (C01), select CH01, the first channel. Double-click CH01 (or right-click, and then select Properties from the menu). The Channel Properties dialog appears. Select Enabled . Enter a description of the channel, for example, Level Transmitter. Enter a Device Tag in the Device Tag field, for example, LT-1. The Channel Properties dialog now looks like this: Click OK .

title: Configure the Advanced Continuous Historian
body_text: Configure the Advanced Continuous Historian Only one Continuous Historian subsystem can be enabled on each Application Station. However, you can install the Advanced Continuous Historian on more than one Application Station. To collect or display historical data with the Advanced Continuous Historian after installing it on an Application Station, you must complete the following configuration steps to set up the Continuous Historian subsystem and configure the Advanced Continuous Historian: Define history collection for module and node parameters. Assign modules to commissioned controllers or Application Stations. Note: If you do not assign the module to an Application Station or a commissioned controller, historical data will not be collected for the module. Download the controller or Application Station. In DeltaV Explorer, right-click the Continuous Historian subsystem under the Application Station, and then select Properties . In the Continuous Historian Properties dialog, enable the Continuous Historian subsystem for each Application Station where you installed the Advanced Continuous Historian and select the Use Advanced Continuous Historian option. Assign specific area folders and nodes to the Continuous Historian subsystem. In DeltaV Explorer, download the Application Station. Note: After the initial download of the history collection subsystem there may be a short delay before the overall integrity of the subsystem reports GOOD in DeltaV Diagnostics. Start the Windows Services application, and then complete the following tasks: Right-click the service named PIDeltaV_ACtr, and then select Properties . In the PIDeltaV_ACtr Properties dialog, click the Log On tab, change the service logon account to the DeltaVAdmin account, and enter the services password that you specified during Workstation Configuration. Restart the PIDeltaV_ACtr service. Right-click the service named Remote Application Monitor, and then select Properties . In the Remote Application Monitor Properties dialog, click the General tab, and then set the Startup type option to Automatic (Delayed Start) . Restart the Remote Application Monitor service. Note: To configure the parameters on the Advanced tab of the Continuous Historian Properties dialog, use the PI System Management Tools (PI SMT). After configuring the Advanced Continuous Historian, you must create a trust to view historical data on a remote system. Related information Historian installation The Continuous Historian subsystem

title: Configure Labeled Button tab
body_text: Configure Labeled Button tab A labeled button is used to change any writeable Logic Solver parameter to a value that is specified at configuration time. A typical use could be to reset a CEM Effect (that is, to write the .CV field of the Boolean RESETx parameter to 1). If no object is selected when the SIS Data Entry Expert is invoked and the Labeled Button tab is used, it creates a pushbutton with a text label on a picture and creates a click-event script for the pushbutton. Otherwise, the SIS Data Entry Expert creates a click-event script for the selected SIS object. If a non-SIS object is selected, this tab is not available. If Electronic Signature is enabled for the parameter, the Electronic Signature dialog appears when the labeled button is clicked in Run mode. When the Electronic Signature is successfully entered or if Electronic Signature is not enabled, the confirmation dialog is displayed. The operator must then confirm the write request. The SIS Data Entry Expert dialog prompts for the following: A text label (of up to 40 characters) for the button. This can be a string or a tilde character followed by the name of a variable object (disabled if an object is selected). The font of the text label can be changed. The foreground color of the text label and the foreground color of the button can also be changed and made dynamic. The color and font selections are applied immediately so that you do not need to switch to run mode to see the effect. The full path of the parameter to be written. The numeric value to be written. The Confirmation Information text displayed on the confirmation dialog. This can be a string or a tilde character followed by the name of a variable object. The string can be up to 300 characters and contain any keyboard character except double quote marks ("). Strings can also contain %P which is replaced in Run mode with the value from the %P Parameter. For example, Do You Want to Reset the %P?. When the string is displayed in Run mode, %P is substituted with the value of the parameter defined by %P. Use the browse button to select a variable. The full path of the %P parameter (optional). This option is used in the confirmation information field and is replaced in Run mode with the value of the %P Parameter. Select the Labeled Button tab on the SIS Data Entry Expert dialog to see the fields associated with the labeled button. After configuring the required fields, click OK on the SIS Data Entry Expert dialog to create the labeled button on the picture. Related information Electronic signatures

title: Configure SLS 1508 logic solvers in DeltaV SIS Simulate
main_heading: Configure SLS 1508 logic solvers in DeltaV SIS Simulate
body_text: Configure SLS 1508 logic solvers in DeltaV SIS Simulate The configuration of SLS 1508 logic solvers (under the SIS Network) is identical to that used in the physical system. To create logic solvers: Select the SIS Network in DeltaV Explorer. Select New Logic Solver from the context menu.
