title: Create a campaign
body_text: Create a campaign The procedure that follows outlines the basic steps for creating a campaign using the Create Campaign dialog, shown below: To create a campaign: Enter a name in the Campaign Name field. Enter a number in the Number of Batches field. Enter a number in the Maximum Active Batches field. Enter a description in the Description field. Click the Select button to select the base recipe, scale the batch, change unit bindings, and enter parameter values. Select Continuous Iteration (only available after selecting the base recipe) to have this campaign run continuously. When continuous iteration is enabled, the Campaign Manager continues to add batches to this campaign based on the base recipe. This allows the campaign to continue until continuous iteration is turned off. Once continuous iteration is turned off, the Campaign Manager runs all the remaining batches in the campaign (without creating more). This allows you to set a cleanup batch to be run after all other batches complete and are removed. Enter a Batch ID Prefix , Sequence , and Suffix or use the default value for any of these fields. Note: The Batch ID Prefix field defaults to the first 22 characters of the campaign name. The Sequence number is a required field. It is a counter with a default starting value of 00001; it can be changed to any integer. The Suffix field defaults to the first 22 characters of the base recipe. Commas are not allowed as part of the Batch ID . Click Setup Batch (or Cleanup Batch ) if you want to create a setup or cleanup batch for the campaign. On the Create Campaign dialog, click Create to create the campaign batches, including the setup and cleanup batches. If you wish to specify that completed batches should be automatically removed from the Batch Executive, open the Properties dialog for the campaign.

title: Create an alias name
body_text: Create an alias name In the DeltaV Explorer, under Library/Advanced Definitions/Unit Classes/Blenders , select BLENDER and right-click. Select New > Alias . A new alias, ALIAS1, appears in an edit box in the right pane, ready for you to rename. Rename ALIAS1 to TANKCAPACITY. Later, when the unit module UM_BLEND_500 is created, the path for the TANKCAPACITY alias can be bound by browsing to UM_BLEND_500/CAPACITY.CV. Alias names can also be derived automatically from the phase logic. (That is, if you make reference to a new alias in the phase logic, it will automatically be added to the unit class and to the Alias Resolution Table when the unit module is created.) An advantage to identifying the aliases when you create the unit class is that you can browse for them when you create the phase logic.

title: Create an Application Station
body_text: Create an Application Station On the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, create an Application Station in DeltaV Explorer by right-clicking Control Network under System Configuration > Physical Network , and then selecting New > Application Station . On the General tab of the Properties dialog, specify a name for the Application Station. Naming the Application Station Important: As a general rule, do not specify an Application Station name that ends with the characters _S. When the DeltaV system creates a pair of Application Stations for redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server, it appends these characters to whatever name you specify as the base name for the Application Station. Having a pair of Application Stations named nodename _S and nodename _S_S could result in misleading or undesirable results while working with redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. On the Redundancy tab of the Properties dialog, check the Enable a redundant subsystem option, select the Assigned Modules option, and then select either the OPC Data Access Server option or the OPC Data Access Server and OPC Mirror option. Important: Once a redundant subsystem is configured, you cannot concurrently enable any other subsystem (redundant or not) on that Application Station or its pair. If you select the OPC Data Access Server option rather than the OPC Data Access Server and OPC Mirror option, running OPC Mirror in a simplex configuration on the Application Station pair is not supported. You can optionally enable the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, if either of the Application Stations will be located in an unmanned facility, for example. Enabling redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server with OPC Mirror Click OK to close the Properties dialog for the Application Station. Export a workstation configuration file for the new Application Station. In DeltaV Explorer, select the new Application Station that you just created. Click File > Export > Workstation Configuration . Save the workstation configuration file either to removable media or to a network location that can be accessed from the Application Stations you will be configuring. You can use the default name for a workstation configuration file, DevData.cfg, or specify a different file name. Related information Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server Redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server Using the unattended reboot option Initiate a manual switchover

title: Create an area
body_text: Create an area In the DeltaV Explorer, click System Configuration/Control Strategies . Right-click, and then select New Area from the context menu. A new area, AREA1, is created. Rename the area EXTERIOR_PAINT.

title: Create an OPC UA server
body_text: Create an OPC UA server Note: This task describes how to create a DeltaV OPC UA server without security features. Refer to the related information for information on OPC UA security. Navigate to the OPC UA Server subsystem in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. The OPC UA server subsystem is under ProfessionalPlus workstations, Application workstations, and DeltaV PK controllers. This procedure is for an OPC UA server on a ProfessionalPlus workstation. Creating a server on a DeltaV PK controller is similar. Note: Make sure the node name does not contain a $ character. This is not a legal character in OPC UA applications with digital certificates. Select the OPC UA Server subsystem, right-click and select Properties . The system displays the OPC UA Server dialog. Click Enable OPC UA Server . Important: Enabling the OPC UA server can consume large amounts of memory (viewable in the FreMem parameter). This happens because OPC UA creates an address space for every parameter of every function block in each module in the controller. On the General tab, select an option under User Authentication . Refer to Related information for topics on security and user authentication. Use the Certificate tab to generate or import your certificate. The PK controller's OPC UA server has an Advanced tab. Use this to specify the primary and secondary port addresses. The endpoint URL is shown on the Advanced tab. Click OK . Right-click the OPC UA Server and select Download . Subtopics: Change the OPC UA server's port Related information DeltaV OPC UA server and client capacities Implementing security for a DeltaV OPC UA server Developing a digital certification solution for OPC UA

title: Create an SIS module
body_text: Create an SIS module Create SIS modules with the same tools and techniques that you use to create DeltaV control modules. In DeltaV Explorer, navigate to an area under System Configuration\Control Strategies . Right-click and select New > SIS Module . On the New dialog, enter a name of up to 16 characters. To start with a copy of an existing SIS module select Start From Existing and browse to an existing SIS module (or an SIS module template). Click OK to create the SIS module. You can now open the module in Control Studio and add SIS function blocks, set initial parameter values, and so on. You can also create an SIS module from Control Studio.

title: Create a class for OPC
body_text: Create a class for OPC There is some information that the client application needs to keep in order to work with the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server connection. In Barcode, you will create a class to hold this information. You will also add procedures to this class to complete various tasks associated with OPC. To add a class, select Class Module from the Project menu. Open the properties window of the new class module. Properties window of new class module Change the name of the class to "COPCServer". Add the following declarations: Option Explicit Public WithEvents AnOpcServer As OPCServer Public AnOpcServerBrowser As OPCBrowser Related information Connect to the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server

title: Create a DeltaV OPC UA client
main_heading: Create a DeltaV OPC UA client
body_text: Create a DeltaV OPC UA client Note: This task describes how to create a DeltaV OPC UA client without security features. Refer to the related information for information on OPC UA security. To create a working client, you need to know the endpoint URL of the associated OPC UA server. Record the server’s opc.tcp protocol URL before creating a client. To obtain the url of a DeltaV server: For DeltaV workstation servers, click the OPC UA Server subsystem in the left pane of DeltaV Explorer. The right pane displays the opc.tcp endpoint url. Right click the endpoint and click Properties . Copy the url from the dialog. For DeltaV PK controller servers, click the OPC UA Server subsystem in the left pane of DeltaV Explorer and right-click Properties . Click the Advanced tab and copy the endpoint url. Note: The endpoint URL is not contained in the OPC UA server's FHX file. To reconstruct the URL, you can use the node's information in this format: protocol://machine:port/path . For example, opc.tcp://192.168.1.2:4880/DVOpcUaServer (where 192.168.1.2 is the node's IP address. For workstation-based OPC UA servers, the hostname (the node's computer name) is valid in place of the IP address). For EIOC clients, the port protocol must be OPC UA . To set the protocol, open the EIOC port properties in DeltaV Explorer, click the Advanced tab and select OPC UA under the Protocol drop-down list. Navigate to the OPC UA Client subsystem in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. The client is under ProfessionalPlus workstations, Application workstations and EIOCs. This procedure is for a client on the ProfessionalPlus. The procedure for other client types is similar. Note: Make sure the node name does not contain a $ character. This is not a legal character in OPC UA applications with digital certificates. Select the OPC UA Client and right-click Properties . The system displays the OPC UA Client dialog. Click Enable OPC UA Client . Click the Certificate tab. Click OK . Select the OPC UA Client and right-click, New OPC UA Physical Device . The system displays the physical device (PDT) properties dialog. On the General tab, enter a description for the physical device. Physical devices correspond to OPC UA servers. You may want to include information in the description that identifies the server. On the Primary tab, enter the opc.tpc protocol URL for the server in the Endpoint Url field. Note: If the URL contains a hostname and not an IP address, you must have a DNS server configured that will resolve that hostname to a static IP address with a lease time set to infinite (so that the IP address will remain in the DNS table). If a dynamic IP address is used for your endpoint (such as one assigned by DHCP), you will have to update the DNS table with the new IP address every time it is reassigned. For redundant servers, enter the secondary opc.tcp protocol URL on the Secondary tab. This step is not required for simplex servers. Click OK . Select the physical device in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy and right-click, New OPC UA Logical Device . The system names physical devices PDT1, PDT2, and so on. Select the logical device and right-click Properties . The software displays the OPC UA Logical Device dialog. The system names logical devices LDT1, LDT2, and so on. On the General tab, enter a description to differentiate this from other logical devices. On the Subscription Settings tab, enter the Publishing Interval . The publishing interval is the interval at which the client pulls data from the server. Click OK . Click the OPC UA Client , then right-click Download . The system displays the Confirm Partial Download dialog. Click Yes . If you receive any warnings (for example, the primary connection for PDT1 does not have a server application certificate configured), click Download Anyway . Before creating signals in the client to read server data, test to make sure that the client can communication with the server. Related information DeltaV OPC UA server and client capacities Implementing security for a DeltaV OPC UA client Developing a digital certification solution for OPC UA Test OPC UA client-side communications

title: Create a display from scratch
body_text: Create a display from scratch Select the Graphics Explorer pane as the active pane in the Explorer view. On the ribbon's Home tab, in the Graphics group, click New > Display > Create New Blank Display . The display opens as a content tab and becomes available for editing in the content pane. Rename the display, if desired. Configure the display's properties in the Graphics Configuration pane. Add graphics elements to the display by dragging them from the Palette pane and dropping them on the content pane. Configure each element's properties in the Graphics Configuration pane. Click Save . Related information Displays overview

title: Create a display set
body_text: Create a display set Select the Graphics Explorer pane as the active pane in the Explorer view. On the ribbon's Home tab, in the Graphics group, click New > Display Set . The display set opens as a content tab and becomes available for editing in the Content pane. A new Display Set tab also appears in the ribbon. Rename the display set, if desired. Enter a title and description for the display set, if desired, in the Graphics Configuration pane. Add displays to the navigation hierarchy. Drag a display from the Graphics Explorer pane into the Navigation Hierarchy pane. When you see a tooltip showing the desired level, drop the display. Click the Save button. Tip: To change the level of a display in the display set, click Promote or Demote in the ribbon's Display Set tab. (The Overview level cannot be changed.) To move a display up or down within a display set, click Move up or Move down in the ribbon's Display Set tab. Related information Display sets overview

title: Create a formula for PRC_PAINT
body_text: Create a formula for PRC_PAINT To define the PRC_PAINT formula, complete the following steps: With nothing selected in the Diagram view, right-click in the lower right corner of the Formula view , and then select New Formula to open the Properties from the context menu. In the New Formula box, enter the name for the formula: LIGHT. The formula named LIGHT is created in the Formula view, with values set as the default values originally set in the definition of the phase input parameters for the three parameters. The default values are shown in angle brackets, (< >). Note: You may need to press the F5 key to refresh the screen to see the parameters. Right-click the value for AGITATE_TIME, and select Modify Value from the context menu (or double-click to open the Properties dialog, clear the Use default value check box and change the value to 50. Click OK . Note that you can easily reset the value to the default by selecting the Use default value check box. Change the remaining two parameter properties for the LIGHT formula, as shown in the following table. Then, add two more formulas--one for a MEDIUM batch (using the default values) and one for a DARK batch. Parameter Light Medium Dark AGITATE_TIME 50 <30> 40 PRC_BASE_AMT 180 <150> 130 PRC_COLOR_AMT <15> <15> 20 Save the PRC_PAINT formula.

title: Create a layout from a template
main_heading: Create a layout from a template
body_text: Create a layout from a template Select the Graphics Explorer pane as the active pane in the Explorer view. On the ribbon's Home tab, in the Graphics group, click New > Layout and select the desired template under Library . The layout opens as a content tab and becomes available for editing in the content pane. Rename the layout, if desired. Modify the layout as desired Click Save . Related information Layouts overview

title: Create a layout from scratch
body_text: Create a layout from scratch In the Graphics Explorer pane, right-click the Layouts root folder and select New > Layout from the context menu. The layout opens as a content tab and becomes available for editing in the Content pane. Rename the layout, if desired. Configure the layout's properties in the Graphics Configuration pane. Add screens to the layout by dragging screen elements from the Palette pane and dropping them on the Content pane. Add one screen for each physical monitor on the Operator Station for which this layout is intended. Arrange the screens to match the arrangement of the intended Operator Station’s monitors. Info: Each screen snaps together and becomes attached to another screen. Configure the properties for each screen. Add a display frame to each screen by dragging a display frame element from the Palette pane and dropping it inside a screen on the Content pane. The frame fills the screen's available space. Add additional display frames for each area of a screen you want to designate as a specific content region. Configure each display frame's properties in the Graphics Configuration pane. Click the Save button. Tip: Double-click a screen to zoom in on it. To zoom back out, click Fit To Window in the ribbon's View tab. Related information Layouts overview

title: Create a phase class and batch input/report parameters
main_heading: Create a phase class and batch input/report parameters
body_text: Create a phase class and batch input/report parameters Now we are going to create phase classes and their associated batch input and report parameters. After that, we will create the logic for the phase class. The input parameters will be used later when we create recipes. One of the report parameters will be used later to log a value to the Event Chronicle. In the DeltaV Explorer, select the TankPhases phase category. Right-click and select New Phase Class . Name it FILL. Create another phase class and name it DUMP. Select the phase class FILL , right-click and select New > Batch input/report parameter from the context menu. A Parameter Properties dialog opens. In the Parameter Properties dialog, enter the name FILL_AMOUNT and select the following choices from the drop-down boxes: Type: Real Category: Input (The ID field is used as an identifier that can be used to specify this parameter in phase requests. Phase requests are discussed later in this tutorial.) In the value boxes, leave 0 as the Low Limit , enter 100 as the Default Value and 500 as the High Limit , and select (type) gal for Engineering Units . Note: The Scalable option can be used to indicate that, if the batch recipe is scaled (for example, by 50 percent), this is one of the parameters that will be scaled by the given percentage. For example, you may want to be able to scale the amounts of the input ingredients by the same percentage, but you may not want to scale the mixing time by the same percentage. Therefore, you would not check scalable for the mixing time parameter. Click OK .

title: Create a phase class category
body_text: Create a phase class category The BlenderPhases category was created as part of the import of two phase classes, CHG_BASE and DRAIN, which were part of the Startup.fhx file. Now we will create another phase class category, TankPhases, to hold the phase classes associated with the color and base tanks. In the DeltaV Explorer, select Library/Advanced Definitions/Phase Classes . Right-click and select New Category from the context menu. Rename Category1 to TankPhases.

title: Create a procedure
body_text: Create a procedure In Recipe Studio, click the Main button, and then click New . Select Procedure as the recipe object type. Create the procedure as shown in the following diagram. Important: On the Properties dialogs for UP_COLOR and UP_BLEND, do not select the Acquire unit prior to starting unit procedure check box. This allows each unit procedure to be started individually as soon as the unit it needs is available. Right-click the Diagram view, then click Properties and fill in the other fields on the Properties tab. Save the procedure as PRC_PAINT. In DeltaV Explorer, assign the procedure recipe to the Batch Executive, and then download.

title: Create a process cell
body_text: Create a process cell In the DeltaV Explorer, click System Configuration > Control Strategies > EXTERIOR_PAINT . Right-click and select New > Process Cell from the context menu. Name the new process cell PAINT_BLEND. Check the Class Required box and browse for the process cell class PRODUCTION. (In the Browse dialog, double-click General and then double-click PRODUCTION to select it.) Note: An easier way to create a process cell from a class is to drag the PRODUCTION process cell class to the area, EXTERIOR_PAINT, which creates a process cell named PCELL1. You can then rename PCELL1 to PAINT_BLEND. From this point on, we will use the drag-and-drop method when available.

title: Create an SIS composite template
body_text: Create an SIS composite template If you have bit of logic that you intend to reuse, create an SIS Composite Template: From Control Studio create a new SIS Composite Template. Add the items required for your template Save the template. You are prompted for a name and a location within the SIS Composite Templates library. Protect the template if desired. You can now insert this composite block in any SIS module you create.

title: Create a unit parameter definition
body_text: Create a unit parameter definition In the Library section of the DeltaV Explorer, select the BLENDER unit class. Note: Every new unit class has unit parameters named FREMEM and NUMPHASES. The FREMEM value is the amount of the free memory available in a node, and the NUMPHASES parameter contains the number of phases currently loaded on the unit. Right-click and select New > Unit Parameter Definition from the context menu. In the PARAM1 Properties dialog, enter the parameter name (CAPACITY), parameter type (Floating point), and default value (1000). Leave the Parameter category field blank. Click OK to create the unit parameter. Repeat the steps to create the additional parameters listed in the table.

title: Create a view-only user account
body_text: Create a view-only user account A view-only user account is an optional account that enables the user to view alarms but does not allow the user to write values. (Can also be called zero span of control user.) This account may be appropriate as the default account associated with the screen saver for security purposes. Specifically, the account: Shows active alarms in the alarm banner (and other alarm displays) for specified plant areas. Does not allow the user write new values to parameters in most modules. Enables the user turn off the horn. Enables the user to use the disable horn button. Using the DeltaV User Manager application, designate one of the unused locks (for example, User Lock 10 ) for the view-only account. Right-click User Lock 10 and rename it to View Only . Create a new account and grant the View Only key. Download setup data for the appropriate workstation. The example below provides information about horn privileges. User account with view only and horn privileges A DeltaV NEWUSER account requires view-only privileges for alarms in plant areas AREA_A, AREA_B, and AREA_C. To grant the privileges: In User Manager, double-click NEWUSER . The software displays the properties dialog. Choose the Keys tab. Select View Only item in the list of all locks on the left. Click Grant Key . Select AREA_A and click OK. Grant the same key for AREA_B and AREA_C . This enables NEWUSER to see the alarms from plant areas AREA_A, AREA_B, and AREA_C in the alarm banner (assuming that these areas were also assigned to this workstation's Alarm & Events subsystem and that the areas were not turned off in the alarm area filtering display). If the horn was enabled, and sound files were configured for the alarm priorities, then the horn would sound. At this point, NEWUSER can not turn off an active horn. The default configuration is to attach the Control lock to the HORN parameter name. Since NEWUSER does not have the Control lock in plant area 0 (AREA_A), then an attempt to write that parameter would be prevented. To enable NEWUSER to turn off the horn it is necessary to change the lock assignment of the HORN parameter through DeltaV Explorer to the View Only lock. Refer to Explorer help for information about defining locks for module parameters. NEW USER can not disable the horn (the horn disable button writes the HENAB field of the HORN parameter). To enable NEWUSER to disable the horn, it is necessary to change the lock assignment of the HENAB field through DeltaV Explorer to the View Only lock. Refer to Explorer help for information about defining parameter field locks.

title: Create the BASE_HEADER module and complete the configuration
main_heading: Create the BASE_HEADER module and complete the configuration
body_text: Create the BASE_HEADER module and complete the configuration Modify the XV_BASE_500 and XV_BASE_600 modules to allow them to participate in equipment arbitration. Create a BASE_HEADER module similar to the COLOR_HEADER module that you created earlier. Modify BASE_HEADER to allow it to participate in equipment arbitration, and add the XV_BASE_500 and XV_BASE_600 to its equipment needed list. Note the equipment ID of the BASE_HEADER module to use in your CHG_BASE requests to acquire and release the resource. (In the example, we use 23 for the BASE_HEADER equipment ID. If necessary, change the phase logic to use the actual ID numbers in your database.) Assign BASE_HEADER to the controller or workstation. Assign the CHG_BASE and DRAIN phase classes to the unit class BLENDER and make the phase type for the corresponding unit phases Controller in both UM_BLEND_500 and UM_BLEND_600. Click Aliases under UM_BLEND_500, and then click View > Details . Double-click the alias BASE_OUT_FLOW and browse to UM_BASE_400 > FIC_BASE_400 . Double-click the alias BASE_OUT_PUMP and browse to UM_BASE_400 > MTR_400 . Download the controller or workstation and test the modules using the Batch graphic. Remember to manually clear any phase requests that appear in the CHG_BASE phase by setting them to 0. After testing, reset all phases to Idle and unload them. Related information Create the COLOR_HEADER control module

title: Create a CIOC placeholder
body_text: Create a CIOC placeholder A placeholder CIOC is used to configure a CIOC offline before you physically connect it to the control network. After you connect the CIOC to the network, you commission it by assigning it to the placeholder. The I/O Network must be enabled as a DeltaV System Preference before it is available to the DeltaV system. To enable the I/O Network, click Start > DeltaV Engineering > System Preferences . Right-click the I/O Network in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Select New > CHARMs I/O Card . A CIOC and its CHARMs container appears under the I/O Network.

title: Create the COLOR_HEADER control module
body_text: Create the COLOR_HEADER control module Now, you will create a control module called COLOR_HEADER in the PAINT_BLEND process cell and modify its properties to add XV_COLOR_500 and XV_COLOR_600 to its Equipment Needed list. In DeltaV Explorer, right-click the PAINT_BLEND process cell and select New > Control Module from the context menu. Name the new control module COLOR_HEADER. (Leave the Algorithm type as Function Block Diagram.) Open the COLOR_HEADER Properties dialog. On the Arbitration tab of the Properties dialog, select the Participate check box in equipment arbitration. Note the Equipment ID, which is 15 in the example below. You may have a different number, which you will need to substitute for 15. This ID will be used later in requesting the resource. In the Equipment Needed list, add XV_COLOR_500 by clicking Add and browsing in EXTERIOR_PAINT > PAINT_BLEND > UM_BLEND_500 for the control module. Add XV_COLOR_600 to the Equipment Needed list. On the Tools tab, assign the module to the node. Click OK to close the Properties dialog. Download.

title: Create a controller placeholder
body_text: Create a controller placeholder Open DeltaV Explorer on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. Select and right-click Control Network , then select New > Controller from the context menu. A new controller, named NODE1, is added under the Control Network. The name appears in the right pane in an edit box, ready for renaming. Note: A red X next to a controller means that the controller is not communicating. Rename the controller to something meaningful for your system. To do the tutorials in this guide, name it CTLR1.

title: Create a control module from a library template
main_heading: Create a control module from a library template
body_text: Create a control module from a library template In a previous procedure, you created a control module using DeltaV Explorer to copy a module template. In this procedure, you will create a control module using Control Studio to open a module template for a block valve. Open Control Studio. To choose a template from the library, click the Main button , and then click New . In the New dialog, select Start from Existing , and then click the Browse button. The Browse dialog appears. Click the Object Type field at the bottom of the dialog, and then select Module Templates . In the large center box that lists the contents of Module Templates, double-click Valves-Normally Closed. From the contents of Valves-Normally Closed, select VLVNC-11. (This name is automatically placed in the Object name field.) Click OK in the Browse dialog. Click OK in the New dialog. Control Studio now displays an untitled copy of the VLVNC-11 module. Subtopics: Modify the control module template

title: Create a control module and assign it to a controller
main_heading: Create a control module and assign it to a controller
body_text: Create a control module and assign it to a controller In DeltaV Explorer, select Library > Module Templates > Analog Control > PID_LOOP and drag PID_LOOP to the TANK-101 area. In the TANK-101 area, select PID_LOOP and rename it FIC-101 . Right-click FIC-101 and select Assign . In the Browse dialog box, select the controller and click OK .

title: Create a control module class category
main_heading: Create a control module class category
body_text: Create a control module class category In the Advanced Definitions section of the DeltaV Explorer Library, expand Control Module Classes. In addition to the default category, General, it contains two categories, AnalogControl and DeviceControl, that were imported as part of the Startup.fhx file. Right-click Control Module Classes, and then select New Category . Rename the new category AnalogInput. Subtopics: Create a control module class from a library template

title: Create a control module class from a library template
main_heading: Create a control module class from a library template
body_text: Create a control module class from a library template The batch system in the paint example contains a number of similar valves. Rather than create the module class from scratch, we will define a control module class for on-off valves using a preconfigured control module template in the DeltaV Module Template Library as the starting point. In the Module Templates section of the Library, open the Valves-NormallyClosed category. Select the module template VLVNC-11, and then drag it to the DeviceControl category under Control Module Classes. Rename the new class (VLVNC-11_1) to NC_VALVE (for normally closed valve).

title: Create custom rules when the ports and protocols are known
main_heading: Create custom rules when the ports and protocols are known
body_text: Create custom rules when the ports and protocols are known It is assumed that you have printed and completed the Worksheet for custom applications . Note: As you create each custom rule, check to see if the applications are communicating properly. Since these rules are not pre-tested you must exercise the applications to ensure they are communicating and working as expected. On the firewall's web UI navigate to Configuration > Applications and click the Add new application button. For each custom application on the Worksheet for custom applications , complete the information requested on the Add new application to the rules drop-down selection list page. On the Protection tab select either Inbound connections or Outbound connections and enable logging for each application. Troubleshoot the communication rules if the applications are not working as expected. When you complete the rules using the entries from the pre-built firewall application list, you can create another set of custom rules for applications with unknown ports and protocols or complete the configuration. Related information Troubleshoot a communication rule Discover ports and protocols to create custom rules Complete the firewall configuration Worksheet for custom applications

title: Create a datalink for the block valve
main_heading: Create a datalink for the block valve
body_text: Create a datalink for the block valve Click the Datalink Stamper button. (You will place this datalink in the bottom center of the picture.) Fill in the parameter reference as XV-101/DC1/PV_D.A_CV. If you browse for the parameter reference, the system will automatically supply .F_CV (for floating point) after PV_D. Edit the parameter reference to have .A_CV (for ASCII) after PV_D. In the Datalink dialog box, in the Data Entry group, select None for the Type . Click OK to let the application configure the remaining fields in the dialog. Place the new datalink in the bottom center of the picture. Use the text tool to add the label XV-101/PV.

title: Create a datalink for the loop output
main_heading: Create a datalink for the loop output
body_text: Create a datalink for the loop output Click the Datalink Stamper button. (You will place this datalink below the loop process value.) Edit the parameter reference to be FIC-101/PID1/OUT.F_CV. In the Data Entry group, select In-Place for the Type . In the Formatting group, select Numeric for the Type . Click OK . Select the datalink, and then click the DeltaV Data Entry Expert button on the Toolbox . Be sure that Numeric Entry is selected, and then click Fetch Limits from the Data Source . Click OK . Place the datalink below the loop process value. Use the text tool to add the label FIC-101/OUT.

title: Create a datalink for the loop process value
main_heading: Create a datalink for the loop process value
body_text: Create a datalink for the loop process value Click the Datalink Stamper button. (You will place this datalink below the loop setpoint.) Edit the parameter reference to be FIC-101/PID1/PV.F_CV. In the Formatting group, select Numeric for the Type . Click OK . Place the new datalink below the loop setpoint. Use the text tool to add the label FIC-101/PV.

title: Create a datalink for the loop setpoint
main_heading: Create a datalink for the loop setpoint
body_text: Create a datalink for the loop setpoint Click the Datalink Stamper button. Enter the new parameter reference as FIC-101/PID1/SP. If you use the Parameter Browser, click the Up One Level button to go up to the module level. The system changes the parameter reference to DVSYS.FIC-101/PID1/SP.F_CV. The default node for all parameter references is DVSYS. In the Data Entry group, select In-Place for the Type . In-place data entry enables operators to change the value from the workstation. In the Formatting group, select Numeric for the Type . Click OK . Tip: If you accidentally close the Datalink dialog before completing your selections, double-click the datalink on the picture to reopen the dialog. Place the datalink in the lower right quadrant of the screen. Use the text tool to add the label FIC-101/SP. (Remember, you access the Text tool by clicking Text button in the Toolbox.

title: Create a datalink for the motor setpoint
main_heading: Create a datalink for the motor setpoint
body_text: Create a datalink for the motor setpoint Click the Datalink Stamper button. (You will place this datalink in the bottom left quadrant of the picture.) Fill in the parameter reference as MTR-101/DC1/SP_D.A_CV. If you browse for the parameter reference, the system will automatically supply .F (for floating point) after SP_D. Edit the parameter reference to have .A_CV (for ASCII) after SP_D. Tip: Tip Select the Read/Write text data check box in the Browse dialog to make the default datalink A_CV. On the Datalink dialog box, in the Data Entry group, select None for the Type . Click OK to let the application configure the remaining fields in the dialog box. Place the new datalink in the bottom left quadrant. Select the datalink, and then click the Data Entry Expert button on the Toolbox . In the Entry Method group, select the Pushbutton tab. Uncheck Get Named Set at Runtime if it is checked. Type STOP in the Open Button Title(0) field. Type START in the Close Button Title(1) field. The operator can start and stop the pump motor by clicking the datalink in the picture. Click OK . Reposition the new datalink, if necessary, in the bottom left quadrant. Use the text tool to add the label MTR-101/SP. Select File > Close to save and close the picture. It is a good idea to save your picture file any time you do a significant amount of work on it.

title: Create a datalink for the tank level
main_heading: Create a datalink for the tank level
body_text: Create a datalink for the tank level Click the Datalink Stamper button in the Toolbox . The Datalink dialog appears. Click the ellipsis button to search for the parameter reference. The Expression Builder dialog opens. Select Browse DeltaV Control Parameters to open the Browse dialog. (This may take a few seconds.) If TANK-101 is not displayed in the Look in: field, click the Up One Level button to go to Control Strategies, and then double-click the TANK-101 area. You can use the Up One Level button to move up one level in the hierarchy. The contents of the selected level are displayed in the list box. A list of the modules assigned to the TANK-101 area is displayed. Double-click the module name, LI-101 . A list of function blocks and module-level parameters is displayed. Double-click the AI1 function block. A list of parameters is displayed for that function block. Double-click the PV parameter. A list of fields is displayed. Click the CV (current value) field, and then click OK . (Alternatively, you can double-click the CV field.) DeltaV Operate assembles the node, tag, and field information and enters it into the Expression Builder dialog. Click OK to return to the Datalink dialog. In the Datalink dialog box, in the Formatting group, select Numeric for the Type , and then click OK . If you have not assigned the module to a controller or if you set up a placeholder controller, you may get a message about the parameter reference not existing. Click Use Anyway to use this parameter reference for the tutorial. Note: DeltaV Operate reads the datalink and automatically configures the settings in the Datalink dialog. The stamper and datalink appear and "float" on the picture. Click the upper left quadrant to place the datalink on the picture. (Refer to the picture in the Creating Datalinks topic for the approximate location.) The datalink appears on the picture as #####.##, surrounded by handles. To label the datalink, click the text button in the Toolbox , click to the left of the datalink, and type LI-101/PV. Click anywhere to change the pointer back to an arrow. Tip: To move any object, you can select it and drag it to a new location. You can use the alignment tools to align objects horizontally and vertically. You can also use the arrow keys on the keyboard to make minor adjustments to the position of any selected object.

title: Create datasets for VIM diagnostics
body_text: Create datasets for VIM diagnostics On the General tab configure the data direction to be input or output, as required for your application. Next, click the DeltaV tab as shown below. In the DeltaV data type field, select 32 bit unit w/Status . Click OK . Open the PLC tab. Configure the Device data type . For VIM Diagnostics, enter the Device data type as 6. The Data start address is always 0. The Number of values is 30. Click OK to close the dialog. The Special data tab is not used for this dataset. A special case of this dataset is to control redundancy switching at the DeltaV Control Module level. This capability is enabled only if the VIM is configured as redundant. In this case, this dataset should be configured with Data direction as Output , and the Output read back check box should be checked as follows: Subtopics: VIM diagnostics dataset values Related information VIM diagnostics dataset values

title: Create a new database for the batch tutorial and set it to active
main_heading:
Create a new database for the batch tutorial and set it to
    active
body_text: Create a new database for the batch tutorial and set it to active Warning: This tutorial assumes you are using a DeltaV system that is offline - not one that is controlling a process. Do not perform any tutorial procedures that involve importing, installing, or downloading configuration information into an operational system without fully considering the impact of the changes. Note: If you are using a workstation that has an existing database, it is assumed that you can safely create a new database and set it to be the active database. Before creating a new database, you must delete the assignment of all modules from workstations, controllers, and Logic Solvers. You must also delete assignments of areas and recipes that to the Batch Executive. Finally, you must delete assignment of any areas to the Alarms and Events subsystem. If you do not delete the module, area, and recipe assignments, when you create a new database using the following procedure, all or portions of the current database will be copied into your new database. Review the preceding note for instructions on deleting any module assignments from workstations in the current database. If you are using a controller, decommission the controller you want to use in the new database. Create a new database by double clicking the Create Database tool in the Database Administrator ( Start > DeltaV Engineering > Database Administrator ). Name the database PaintTutorial (or TutorialComplete if you are importing the completed database) and click Next . Select Create New Database and then click Next . Select Preserve Network Definition and then select From the current active database . (This maintains your current workstation configuration information.) Click Finish . Click Yes in response to the question about where to create the database. Click No to all in response to the question about updating existing objects in the database. After the database has been created, click OK . Set the new database to active using the Set Active Database tool. Click Change and then click OK in response to the warning. The new database name appears in the Database name field on the Select New Active Database dialog. Click OK . Close the Database Administrator application.

title: Create a device placeholder
body_text: Create a device placeholder Device description support files must be installed before you can add a device to the segment or create a device placeholder. The DeltaV system includes built-in support for a number of fieldbus devices from different device manufacturers. The files necessary to support these devices are included in the DeltaV install image and are available in the DeltaV Explorer library ( DeltaV_System/Library/Fieldbus Devices ). If a fieldbus device is not included in the DeltaV install image, you must install a set of device support files for that device. Many device files that have been tested with the DeltaV system are available from the main DeltaV website under Resources. If the device files that you require are not available on the website, contact the device manufacturer. About device placeholders A device placeholder is an electronic representation of a device that exists in the DeltaV database with no associated physical device. You can use a placeholder to configure block parameters offline and have your control strategy in place prior to attaching the device to the segment. When you are ready, you can attach the device to the segment and use the DeltaV system to reconcile any differences between the placeholder and the device when you commission the device. Note: The use of placeholders is optional and depends on the size and requirements of your fieldbus application. However, it is recommended that you use placeholders for large applications. If you do not want to use placeholders, you can attach your devices directly to the segment. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > DeltaV Explorer to open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the fieldbus ports. The ports are under the H1 fieldbus card. The card is under the I/O subsystem. Right-click the port to which you want to attach the device placeholder and select New Fieldbus Device . The Fieldbus Device Properties dialog opens. Enter the appropriate information about the device in the dialog. The DeltaV system selects an address. You can customize this field, but it is not necessary. Select the device type and revision based on the type of device you want to add. The device properties must match the properties of the device you will commission later. Remember that DeltaV Explorer has extensive online help. Click the Help button on this dialog for help on any of the fields. fieldbus devices often provide error detection for a variety of device conditions. Select the Alarms and Displays tab in the Fieldbus Device Properties dialog to enable Device Alarms to be reported by the device. Note: The Alarms and Displays tab is only shown when supported by the DeltaV hardware. Device alerts are supported by Series 2 H1 cards. Each device can also be configured with a primary control display and faceplate. DeltaV software includes a standard device faceplate. Click OK to add the device placeholder to the segment. The device appears as a decommissioned device on the segment. When device alarms are enabled, alarms become visible in the right pane in DeltaV Explorer when you select the fieldbus Device Alarms icon for the device. Select an alarm and right-click Properties to enable or disable it or to change the alarm's priority. Related information Fieldbus device descriptions and methods Device alarms overview Configuring device alarms

title: Create a DVRead Function
body_text: Create a DVRead Function Select a cell in your workbook where you want the data to be displayed. Note: To display the call status and the parameter property, select two adjacent cells (horizontal or vertical). Select the Add-Ins tab. From the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and select Runtime Data > Configure Read Function . Enter (or browse to) the Parameter Path to the DeltaV parameter you want to read. Note: The DeltaV OPC .NET Server service must be running to be able to browse to the parameter. Click Paste parameter path to the left of result if you want the parameter path to be displayed next to the value. Select the Data Type for the specified DeltaV parameter. Select the Status Type . This is the data type of the returned status for the specified DeltaV parameter. Note: To display the call status and the parameter property, two adjacent cells must be selected first. Click OK . Related information DVRead and DVReadWithStatus Syntax Modify a function Read process data and the call status Set the update interval Update all read functions in a workbook

title: Create a DVWrite function
body_text: Create a DVWrite function Select a cell to hold the write value. Select the Add-Ins tab. In the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and then select Runtime Data > Configure Write Function . Enter (or browse to) the Parameter Path to the DeltaV parameter you want to write. Click Paste parameter path to the left of result if you want the parameter path to be displayed next to the value. Select the Value to Write for the specified DeltaV parameter. If the value is text, do not use quotes. The DeltaV Excel Add-in adds the quotes automatically for text values. Select the Status Type . Click OK . Note: In order to watch the results of the DVWrite function, create a DVRead or DVReadWithStatus function for the same parameter property. Related information DVWrite Syntax Execute a single DVWrite function Execute all DVWrite functions Execute selected DVWrite functions

title: Create the failure monitor logic
body_text: Create the failure monitor logic Open the AGITATE phase class in Control Studio. Double-click the Fail_Monitor to open it. It opens with one CALC block, named BLOCK1. Add four Condition blocks, one Boolean Fan In block, and one Calc/Logic block to the diagram, as shown in the previous topic. (Look on the Logical and Analog Control palettes for these items.) Rename the blocks as shown on the diagram. You can remove the display of the block template names by clicking click Diagram Preferences on the Diagram tab in the Layout group. Then, clear the Template Names check box. To change the number of inputs to the BFI1 block, select the block, select Extensible Parameters from the context menu, and change the number of connectors to 4. Tip: If you would like more detailed information about the BFI block, click the Books Online icon. To change the number of outputs and inputs on the FAIL_MESSAGE block to 1 each, select Extensible Parameters from the context menu, double-click the OUT (then the IN parameter), and change the number of connectors to 1.) Connect the blocks as shown in the following figure. For each condition block, select Expression from the context menu and modify the expression to check for the failure conditions. (We have shown the expressions on the diagram as a configuration aid.) Set the DISABLE parameter for each condition block equal to 1. This initially disables the conditions so that the expressions are not monitored. During execution of the phase, we will selectively enable any condition that we want to monitor. To disable a condition, display all parameters in the Parameter View by selecting all the filters (all boxes selected). Click one of the Condition blocks (for example, BASE_IN_OPEN). Double-click the Disable parameter and change the value to 1. Continue for all the Condition blocks. Create the following expression for the FAIL_MESSAGE calculation block: FAIL_MOD := IN1; OUT1 := 0; IF (FAIL_MOD = 1) THEN OUT1 := 'phase_failures:Inlet Valve Open'; ELSE IF (FAIL_MOD = 2) THEN OUT1 := 'phase_failures:Inlet Valve Open'; ELSE IF (FAIL_MOD = 4) THEN OUT1 := 'phase_failures:Outlet Not Closed'; ELSE IF (FAIL_MOD = 8) THEN OUT1 := 'phase_failures:Agitator Stopped'; ENDIF; ENDIF; ENDIF; ENDIF This expression determines which failure message should be displayed to the operator based on the first failure condition that was detected by the Boolean Fan In block. The failure message will later be written to the phase's FAIL_INDEX parameter.

title: Create a named set
body_text: Create a named set Open or restore DeltaV Explorer. Select System Configuration > Setup > Named Sets . Select and right-click Named Sets in the left pane, and then select New > Named Set . A new entry, NamedSet n (where n is the next number available), is added to the end of the list of existing named sets. The entry is in an edit box, ready to be renamed. Type the new name, SFCCTRL, and press Enter . Double-click SFCCTRL (or select and right-click SFCCTRL, and then select Properties from the menu). The Properties dialog appears. Type Sequence Control in the description box. Click Add . The State Properties dialog appears. Type IDLE in the Name box, and then click OK . Note: Named sets are case sensitive. You can define them using any combination of uppercase and lowercase characters, but all future references to a state must be as originally defined. To add another state, click Add . Type START in the Name box, and then click OK . The Properties dialog now has two named states, IDLE and START. Click OK to save the set and close the dialog. Minimize DeltaV Explorer.

title: Create a new module from scratch
main_heading: Create a new module from scratch
body_text: Create a new module from scratch In Control Studio, click the Main button, then click New. The New dialog box appears. Click OK to accept the default settings in the New dialog. Control Studio opens with a blank, untitled Function Block diagram.

title: Create OPC UA client signals
body_text: Create OPC UA client signals Each OPC UA client signal reads a specific node ID in the OPC UA server. In the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy, select the logical device and right-click New OPC UA Signal. The system displays the OPC UA Signal dialog. Click Browse Online next to the Node Id field. If you have established communication with the server, the system displays the Browse Nodes window. The window enables you to navigate the server’s address space. Items available to the client have a checkbox. Note: If your server supports off-line nodesets, the software enables you to browse offline as well. To use an off-line nodeset, click the Browse Offline checkbox and browse to the xml nodeset file through the Windows Explorer. Select the checkbox next to the item you want this signal to read. Note: The signal and node ID relationship is one-to-one. You can only select one checkbox per signal. Click OK . Click the physical device then right-click Download > OPC UA Physical Device . Note: If the OPC UA signal is mapped to a dynamic reference parameter, the signal returns the data type of the parameter to which the dynamic reference parameter is bound. For example, if the dynamic reference parameter is bound to a floating point parameter, the OPC UA signal returns a floating point data type. If the bound parameter is changed to another type, the signal goes bad because there is a mismatch. You must manually change the data type of the signal and download the OPC UA client to restore communications.

title: Create the operation OP_FINISH in Recipe Studio
main_heading: Create the operation OP_FINISH in Recipe Studio
body_text: Create the operation OP_FINISH in Recipe Studio The first operation you will create is one to agitate and drain the contents of a blender. You can create a recipe in DeltaV Explorer and then open it in Recipe Studio to configure it. You can also create a recipe directly in Recipe Studio, configure it, and save it. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > Recipe Studio . Recipe Studio opens with a single step and transition in the Diagram view. Click the Main button, and then click New . A New dialog opens. Accept Operation as the Object Type and click OK . Make sure Default Transition Conditions is selected so that transition conditions will be written automatically. On the Diagram tab, in the Layout group, click Diagram Preferences , and then select Condition under Transitions so that you can see the conditions on the diagram.

title: Create the parameters at the unit procedure and procedure levels
main_heading: Create the parameters at the unit procedure and procedure levels
body_text: Create the parameters at the unit procedure and procedure levels In the Hierarchy view, in the upper left corner, select the unit procedure UP_BLEND. In the Diagram view, click the OP_CHARGE step. Note: You may need to press the F5 key to refresh the screen to see the parameters. In the Parameter view, double-click the OP_BASE_AMT parameter to open the Properties dialog. Change the Origin to Defer and the Source to UP_BASE_AMT. Modify the OP_COLOR_AMT parameter to defer the source to UP_COLOR_AMT. Click the OP_FINISH step. Modify the AGITATE_TIME parameter to defer the source to AGITATE_TIME. In the Hierarchy view, select the procedure PRC_PAINT. To create the procedure level parameters, click the UP_BLEND step. Modify the UP_BASE_AMT parameter to defer the source to PRC_BASE_AMT. Modify the UP_COLOR_AMT parameter to defer the source to PRC_COLOR_AMT. Modify the AGITATE_TIME parameter to defer the source to AGITATE_TIME. Save PRC_PAINT. Download.

title: Create the phase messages
body_text: Create the phase messages In DeltaV Explorer, select the DRAIN phase class. Right-click, and then select New > Phase Message from the context menu. In the Phase Message Properties dialog, enter the message text as shown, and then click OK . Note that the message ID is automatically assigned number 1. Create message 2 using the following message text: How many gallons would you like to release?

title: Create ping rules
body_text: Create ping rules It is assumed that you have tested communications by establishing ping communications between the computers on the internal and external network. In the firewall's web UI navigate to Protection > Inbound/Outbound connections , select Add Inbound connection or Outbound connection to create the inbound and outbound ping rules to allow all of the ping communications you have established. On the Create Inbound/Outbound connection page, select Ping from the Application drop-down list. Select the DeltaV workstation and the external workstation from the drop-down lists. Select Enabled . Deselect Log . Click the Apply button. It will take a few seconds to build the rule and you will receive a message when the rule is successfully built. Continue to create the inbound and outbound ping rules for all of the pings that are currently running. Note: Connections only appear on the Dashboard Summary if actual communications are occurring through the firewall. If communications stop for some reason (such as the application is terminated or stops communicating) the connection entry will not appear on the Dashboard Summary . If the applications create multiple communications using the same rule you will observe multiple entries in the connections section. Related information Test communications between the internal and external network

title: Create a process cell class
body_text: Create a process cell class In the DeltaV Explorer Library, click Advanced Definitions/Process Cell Classes/General . Right-click, and then select New Process Cell Class . A new class, PCELLCLS1, is created. Rename the new process cell class PRODUCTION.

title: Create a push button to start the SFC
main_heading: Create a push button to start the SFC
body_text: Create a push button to start the SFC This procedure explains how to use the DeltaV Operate interface to create a push button to start the SFC. Another way to assign the Start command to the push button is to select and right-click the push button, select Edit Script , and then edit the Visual Basic script for the Push Button object. On the DeltaV Operate Configure menu bar, click Insert > Push Button . Move the push button to a blank area near the link named FIC-101/MODE. Click the Text tool on the Toolbox and type the text to appear on the button: Start Discharge. Resize the push button to accommodate the text label. To do this, click the box and drag its handles. Select the push button and click the Task Wizard button on the toolbar. The Task Wizard dialog opens. Select Command as the Task Category and scroll down to Write Value to Tag Expert in the Tasks list. Click the Perform Task button. The Write a Value Expert dialog opens. In the FIX Database Tag field, type or search for: DVSYS. SFC-START/SP.F_CV Click Numeric and type 1 in the Value field. This command sets the value for the SFC to 1, which was defined to be the START value in the SFCCTRL named set. Click OK , and then click Close on the Task Wizard dialog. Save TANK101. Quit DeltaV Operate.

title: Create communications rules in Allow all mode to not disrupt existing communications
main_heading:
Create communications rules in Allow all mode to not disrupt existing
	 communications
body_text: Create communications rules in Allow all mode to not disrupt existing communications Use this procedure if you are installing the firewall in an existing network and cannot interrupt communications. In this procedure the firewall is placed in Allow all mode. It is recommended that you create rules to keep critical communications working through the firewall in Allow all mode first and after testing these rules, switch to Normal mode and create rules for non critical communications. In the firewall's web UI navigate to Dashboard > Summary . Click the Allow all button. Navigate to Protection and select either Inbound or Outbound connections. Select a DeltaV application that is considered a critical communication from the Application drop-down list. Select the DeltaV workstation that uses this application. Enable logging on the rule. Continue to create rules for critical communications in Allow all mode. When all rules for critical communications are created, follow the instructions for troubleshooting a communication rule. This procedure explains how to use log data to review the rule settings and ensure the rules are correct for your system. When you are sure that the rules are correct, reset the mode to Normal, retest the critical communications to ensure they are correct, and then create and verify rules for any remaining communications. Related information Troubleshoot a communication rule

title: Create communication rules in normal mode
main_heading: Create communication rules in normal mode
body_text: Create communication rules in normal mode It is assumed that you have printed and completed the Worksheet for DeltaV applications and know the DeltaV workstation names and the external computer names. In the firewall's web UI navigate to Dashboard > Summary . Click the Normal button. Navigate to Protection and select either Inbound connections or Outbound connections . Select a DeltaV application from the Application drop-down list. Select the DeltaV workstation that uses this application. Enable logging on the rule. As you create each rule, ensure that the applications are communicating properly. These rules were tested with the DeltaV system and should communicate properly but it is always a good idea to exercise the applications to ensure they are communicating and the applications are working as desired. Continue to create and test the rules for DeltaV applications. When you have created all the required rules using the applications in the firewall's application list, you can create custom rules if required or complete the firewall configuration. Related information Troubleshoot a communication rule Create custom rules when the ports and protocols are known Discover ports and protocols to create custom rules Complete the firewall configuration Worksheet for custom applications

title: Create a serial card for VIM
main_heading: Create a serial card for VIM

If you can auto-sense the VIM it is not necessary to manually create the cards. On the Add card dialog do the following: Enter a description, if desired. In the Card class field, select Serial Cards . In the Card type field, select 2 Ports, Programmable, RS232|RS485 . In the Card series field, select Series 2 . Select the Card is redundant check box, if you are configuring a redundant card. Select the correct Slot position for the card. Click OK to accept your changes and close the dialog.

main_heading: Create a serial device for VIM

On the Properties dialog that appears: Enter a description, if desired. Specify the Device Address . The device address is the PLC device address. Click OK to accept your changes and create the device.

title: Create a Sequential Function Chart
body_text: Create a Sequential Function Chart Restore Control Studio by clicking its button on the Windows task bar. Click the Main button, then click New . In the New dialog, select Control Module or Template as the Object Type . Select Sequential Function Chart as the Algorithm Type , and then click OK . A new SFC diagram opens, with a single step, S1.

title: Create a step action in the SFC
main_heading: Create a step action in the SFC
body_text: Create a step action in the SFC In the Diagram View, select the step box named S1. Click the name, S1, and change it to STOP_AND_WAIT. In the Action View area of Control Studio, right-click anywhere and select Add . The Properties dialog appears. Enter Stop and Wait for the Description . For the Type , select Assignment . (This type assigns the result of an expression to a destination. This action assigns the value of 'SFCCTRL:IDLE' to SP.) For the Qualifier , select P Pulse . An action with the P Pulse qualifier is active only on the first scan when the step goes active. Thus, the assignment statement is evaluated and the assignment made on the first scan through the step actions when the step goes active. After the first scan, the assignment destination retains the assigned value; it is not rewritten for each scan. To set the setpoint to the IDLE state, type the following in the Action expression field: 'SP':='SFCCTRL:IDLE'; (remember: named sets are case-sensitive). Alternatively, you can click the Expression Assistant button and use the Expression Assistant to define the Action expression. (You used the Expression Assistant earlier to define the interlock conditions for the motor control module.) Click the Insert Named State button in the Expression Assistant and follow the prompts to define the Action expression. Click OK in the Properties dialog. Make any necessary corrections, and then click OK . Select the step action (A1) in the Step Action View, right-click, select Rename , and then change the name to SET_TO_IDLE. Giving the step actions meaningful names instead of A1, A2, etc., helps you identify a particular action you may later want to modify.

title: Create the AGITATE and CHG_COLOR phase classes
main_heading: Create the AGITATE and CHG_COLOR phase classes
body_text: Create the AGITATE and CHG_COLOR phase classes Perform the following steps according to the information in the above table: Create the phase class under the BlenderPhases category. Create the batch input/report parameter. In the Parameter Properties dialog, enter the parameter name. Select the type and category (either input or report). For batch input parameters, enter the range ( Low Limit and High Limit values), the Default Value , and the Engineering Units . For batch report parameters, enter the Engineering Units .

title: Create the BASE unit modules
body_text: Create the BASE unit modules Drag the BASE unit class to the PAINT_BLEND process cell. Expand the unit module to see its contents. Rename BASE_1 to UM_BASE_400. Rename BASE_OUT_FLOW1 to FIC_BASE_400. Rename BASE_OUT_PUMP1 to MTR_400.

title: Create the BLENDER_OUTLET equipment module class
main_heading: Create the BLENDER_OUTLET equipment module class
body_text: Create the BLENDER_OUTLET equipment module class Earlier we configured a control module called NC_VALVE. (We started from the VLVNC-11 control module template and added a valve setpoint, a deadtime block, and a PV output parameter.) Now we will add two copies of this control module class to the equipment module class to represent the two outlet valves. The resulting module blocks will be named PRODUCT_VLV and WASTE_VLV. We will also add the 2STATE_MTR control module class to be used as the OUT_PUMP. The 2STATE_MTR control module class was imported as part of the Startup.fhx file. First, create an equipment module class category of StateDriven under Equipment Module Classes in the Advanced Definitions section of the Library. Right-click StateDriven, and then select New Equipment Module Class . On the New Dialog, enter BLENDER_OUTLET as theObject name. Select Create New , and then select State-driven as the algorithm type. Browse for the named set outlet_state. Click OK to create the equipment module class. Drag the NC_VALVE control module class to BLENDER_OUTLET. Rename the resulting module block (NC_VALVE_1) to PRODUCT_VLV. Drag the NC_VALVE control module class to BLENDER_OUTLET and rename the new module block WASTE_VLV. Drag the 2STATE_MTR control module class to BLENDER_OUTLET and rename the new module block OUT_PUMP. Open the Properties dialog for BLENDER_OUTLET. On the Displays tab, browse for and select Process as the primary control display .

title: Create the BLENDER unit modules
body_text: Create the BLENDER unit modules Drag the BLENDER unit class to the PAINT_BLEND process cell under EXTERIOR_PAINT area in the System Configuration/Control Strategies section of the DeltaV Explorer. A unit module, BLENDER_1, is created. Expand BLENDER_1 and the contained equipment module, BLENDER_OUT_11, to see the contents. The unit module contains module blocks for four control modules (AGITATOR1, BASE_IN_VLV1, BLENDER_LEVEL1, and COLOR_IN_VLV1); the equipment module BLENDER_OUT_11 contains control modules OUT_PUMP1, PRODUCT_VLV1, and WASTE_VLV1. Rename BLENDER_1 to UM_BLEND_500. Rename AGITATOR1 to AGIT_500. Rename the remaining modules as shown below: To create the UM_BLENDER_600 unit module, drag another copy of the BLENDER unit class to the PAINT_BLEND process cell. Rename the resulting module instances as in steps 3 through 5 above, but substitute 600 for 500 in all the module names.

title: Create the class category and TOTALIZER equipment module class
main_heading: Create the class category and TOTALIZER equipment module class
body_text: Create the class category and TOTALIZER equipment module class First, create an equipment module class category named CommandDriven under Equipment Module Classes in the Advanced Definitions section of the Library. Right-click CommandDriven, and then select New Equipment Module Class . On the New dialog, enter TOTALIZER as the Object name. Select Create New , and then select Command-driven as the algorithm type. Browse for the named set totalizer. Click OK to create the TOTALIZER equipment module class. Drag the FLOW_CONTROL control module class to TOTALIZER. Drag the TOTAL_FLOW control module class to TOTALIZER. Click the + sign next to TOTALIZER to view the contents of the module class. Open the Properties dialog for TOTALIZER. On the Displays tab, browse for and select Process as the primary control display .

title: Create the COLOR unit modules
body_text: Create the COLOR unit modules Drag the COLOR unit class to the PAINT_BLEND process cell. Expand the COLOR_1 unit module and the contained equipment module, TOTALIZER_11 to see all the module instances contained within the unit module. Rename COLOR_1 to UM_COLOR_100. Rename the remaining modules under UM_COLOR_100 as shown in the figure below. To create the UM_COLOR_200 and UM_COLOR_300 unit modules, drag two more copies of the COLOR unit class to the PAINT_BLEND process cell. Rename the resulting module instances as in the figure below, but use 200 and 300 (for UM_COLOR_200 and UM_COLOR_300, respectively), in all the module names.

title: Create the control module class
body_text: Create the control module class Select Analog Input, right-click, and then select New Control Module Class . On the New dialog, name the class LEVEL_INDICATOR. Click Start From Existing , browse the module templates to Monitoring/Analog , and then click OK to create the class.

title: Create the link group LINK_COLOR
body_text: Create the link group LINK_COLOR In this exercise, you will create a link group called LINK_COLOR. The link group will allow phase messaging between DUMP and CHG_COLOR. In Recipe Studio, with PRC_PAINT open, on the Home tab, in the Algorithm group, click Link Group . Name the link group LINK_COLOR and enter a description. Click Add in the dialog. Browse for the CHG_COLOR phase (under UP_BLEND > OP_CHARGE ), and then click OK . Add DUMP to LINK_COLOR. (Browse under UP_COLOR > OP_COLOR .) Close the link group and save PRC_PAINT. We are almost ready to run batches in the Batch Operator Interface. However, before we can do that, we need to enable the workstation to run batch, initialize the DeltaV Batch Executive, assign the area to the Batch Executive, and download the workstation.

title: Create the outlet_state named set
body_text: Create the outlet_state named set Before creating the equipment module class, we will create the named set (outlet_state) that will be referenced by it. In the DeltaV Explorer, select Named Sets under System Configuration/Setup . Right-click and select New Named Set from the context menu. Rename NamedSet1 to outlet_state. Double-click outlet_state to open the Properties dialog. Click Add . In the State Properties dialog, type the name of the state, Closed , and change the value to 1. Leave the Visible and User selectable check boxes selected. Add the additional states of Draining (value=2), ReleasingProduct (value=3), InTransition (value=99) and Idle (value=255). When creating the Idle state, remove the check mark next to User selectable .

title: Create the totalizer named set
body_text: Create the totalizer named set In the DeltaV Explorer, select Named Sets under System Configuration/Setup . Right-click, and then select New Named Set from the context menu. Rename NamedSet1 to Totalizer. Double-click Totalizer to open the Properties dialog. Click Add . In the State Properties dialog, type the name of the state, Totalize_fast, and change the value to 1. Leave the Visible and User selectable check boxes selected. Add the additional states (Totalize_accurate, Reset, and Idle) and assign the state values as shown below. The two control module classes, FLOW_CONTROL and TOTAL_FLOW, were imported as part of the Startup.fhx file. They are both under the AnalogControl category under Advanced Definitions/Control Module Classes . FLOW_CONTROL is a PID loop that can be adjusted to control the flow into the color tank. TOTAL_FLOW is an integrator that keeps track of the total amount of color added to the tank.

title: Create a transition in the SFC
main_heading: Create a transition in the SFC
body_text: Create a transition in the SFC On the All SFC Items palette, click Transition , and then drag it to a point below the STOP_AND_WAIT box. A plus sign named T1 appears. Right-click the transition and select Properties (or double-click the transition). The Properties dialog appears. Enter Wait until Start for the transition description, open the Expression Assistant, and then build the following condition statement: 'SP' = 'SFCCTRL:START' Click Parse in the Expression Assistant, correct any errors, and then click OK in both dialogs. Rename the transition WAIT_UNTIL_START.

title: Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system
main_heading: Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system
body_text: Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system Explicit logins are not supported in the Advanced Continuous Historian. You must create a trust for the remote client by completing the following steps: Log on as Administrator to the system where the Advanced Continuous Historian is installed. Start the PI System Management Tools by clicking All Programs > PI System > PI System Management Tools . In the PI System Management Tools window, navigate to Security > Mappings & Trusts , and then select the Trusts tab. Start the Add Trust Wizard by right-clicking in the Trusts window, and then selecting New Trust on the context menu. In the Add Trust Wizard , complete the following steps: Specify a trust name. Enable the PI-API Application option. Specify either or both the computer name of the client or the name of the application running on the client. By using the Application Name and Client Connection options, you can set up a trust relationship for one or more application running on a specified client, for all applications running on the client, or for a specified application running on any client. To use the Application Name option, specify up to the first eight characters of the client application's executable file name. For example: specify PREDICTP instead of PREDICTPRO.EXE for the PredictPro client application; specify PREDICT. instead of PREDICT.EXE for the Predict client application; specify CHS.EXE for the Process History View client application. To use the Client Connection option, it is recommended that you specify one or both of the following: Network Path , specifying the computer name of the client or IP Address and NetMask for Trust #1 , specifying 10.4.x.x as the IP address of the DeltaV primary network and 255.255.0.0 as the network mask and IP Address and NetMask for Trust #2 , specifying 10.8.x.x as the IP address of an existing DeltaV secondary network and 255.255.0.0 as the network mask Note: If you do not specify the computer name of the client in Network Path , the trust using 10.4.x.x as the IP address of the DeltaV primary network only takes effect if the connection to the 10.8.x.x IP address of an existing DeltaV secondary network is unavailable. Specify piadmins as the PI User . Related information Client application support Map the security account for Advanced Continuous Historian

title: Create unit class categories and unit classes
main_heading: Create unit class categories and unit classes
body_text: Create unit class categories and unit classes In the DeltaV Explorer, select Library/Advanced Definitions/Unit Classes . Create a new category and name it Tanks. Select and right-click Tanks, and then click New Unit Class . Name the new unit class COLOR. Click OK . Under the Tanks category, create another unit class named BASE. Create a unit class category named Blenders. Within the Blenders category, create a unit class named BLENDER. When expanded, this part of the Advanced Definitions section under Library should look like this:

title: Create unit procedures (UP_BLEND and UP_COLOR)
body_text: Create unit procedures (UP_BLEND and UP_COLOR) In Recipe Studio, click the Main button, and then click New . Select Unit Procedure as the recipe object type. Create the unit procedure as shown in the following diagram. Select BLENDER as the unit class. Finish the unit procedure by filling in the Properties dialog. Save the recipe as UP_BLEND. Create a unit procedure named UP_COLOR. This unit procedure contains only one operation, OP_COLOR. Use COLOR for the unit class.

title: Create a workstation configuration file
body_text: Create a workstation configuration file If you do not create a workstation configuration file immediately after adding workstations to the system in DeltaV Explorer, you will need to create one later. Perform the following steps on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation to create a workstation configuration file. You can save the file to removable media or to an accessible network location. Open DeltaV Explorer if it is not already open. Select and right-click Physical Network . A context menu appears. Select Create Station Configuration File from the context menu. A dialog appears for you to specify the file name and destination. The default name for the workstation configuration file is DevData.cfg. Select a location to save the workstation configuration file, and then click Save .

title: Create a batch report
