body_text: Create a batch report The intent of this exercise is to demonstrate how to connect to the DeltaV Batch Historian and request data from the Historian's database. The specific data requested, along with how it is handled after retrieval from the database, is up to the individual user. The user may want to query data from other sources as well to include in the final report. Note: The example provided in this exercise reads a batch ID and prints out any parameters that were used during the batch, along with the associated parameter values. It uses Microsoft Word to format, output and save the report information. Comments to the code are shown here in green and are preceded by a single quote ( ' ). Define the variables that will be used by the program to generate the report. Create a way for users to request a batch report (e.g. an input dialog). Read the data entered by the user. Connect to a Batch Historian (using the DSN defined for that historian). Ask for a list of available batches (using SQL to query the historian's database). Open an application to use for outputting the data (e.g. Microsoft Word). Read some batch data (using SQL to query the historian's database). Format and output the data to the application. Save the report (optional). Subtopics: New report sample code

title: Create a custom calculation for the alarm
main_heading: Create a custom calculation for the alarm
body_text: Create a custom calculation for the alarm Custom alarm calculations must be associated with a parameter that has a value of either 0 or 1. A one (1) indicates an alarm condition, and a 0 indicates a non-alarm condition. Note: If you create your own alarm calculations you must use one of the function blocks that support expressions (for example, the Condition function block or the Calc/Logic function block). The following example shows how to add a custom alarm to a module using a Condition block. In this example, an alarm is triggered when the PV of the AI block is 70 or higher. Note: The custom calculation creates a Boolean parameter that still must be associated with the alarm. This step only sets up the calculation that is associated with an alarm. To create a custom calculation, perform the following steps: Drag an Analog Input block onto the diagram. The Analog Input block is in the I/O function block category. Drag a Condition block onto the diagram. The Condition block is in the Logical function block category. Right-click the Condition block. Select Expression . In the Expression Editor dialog, click Insert Internal Parameter . Browse to the AI block's PV parameter and CV field. Click OK . In the Expression Editor dialog, click the >= symbol. Enter the value 70. Click Parse . When the expression parses without any errors, click OK . This sets up an expression to see if the PV parameter is greater than or equal to 70. For this module, the value of the expression is the value of the OUT_D parameter.

title: Create a pump using a dynamo
main_heading: Create a pump using a dynamo
body_text: Create a pump using a dynamo From the system tree in configure mode, expand the Dynamo Sets folder, and then double-click PumpsAnim . The dynamo set opens at the bottom of your screen. Back in the system tree, expand the PumpsAnim folder, and then select PumpAnimVertA1 . The dynamo PumpAnimVertA1 is highlighted in the Dynamo Set at the bottom the screen. Select PumpAnimVertA1 and drag it onto the picture. (Alternatively, you can drag the dynamo name from the system tree onto the picture.) Because this dynamo has animation properties, you are asked if you want to animate the pump color. We will animate the pump color so it changes from red to green when the pump goes from Stop to Start. Select the Animate Pump Color check box. The Color By dialog opens. Browse for MTR-101/DC1/SP_D/CV as the Data Source (digital tag) for the pump. Select Exact Match . In the Color Threshold group, click the Delete Row button, and then delete all but two rows. Set the value in the first row to 0.00, click the color bar, and then select red. Set the value in the second row to 1.00, click the color bar, and then select green. Click OK in both dialogs. The pump is placed on the picture.

title: Create a tank using a dynamo
main_heading: Create a tank using a dynamo
body_text: Create a tank using a dynamo Now you will add a tank that, in run mode, is supposed to show the level of the product in the tank by changing color. (This will not actually happen, since we do not have a working system with I/O.) First, close the PumpsAnim dynamo set by selecting and right-clicking PumpsAnim in the system tree, and then selecting Close . Double-click the TanksAnim1 dynamo set in the system tree to open the dynamo set. Drag the tank labeled TankWDoorD1 to your picture, placing it a little above the motor, as in the figure shown earlier. On the Tank Dynamo dialog, browse for the following tag for the tank level. LI-101/AI1/PV/CV The system automatically adds .F_CV as the field. In the Input Ranges group, select Fetch Limits from Data Source . Click OK . The tank is placed on the picture. Close the TanksAnim1 dynamo set.

title: Create the softphaseuser on the non-DeltaV node
main_heading: Create the softphaseuser on the non-DeltaV node
body_text: Create the softphaseuser on the non-DeltaV node Creating the SOFTPHASEUSER on the Non-DeltaV Node On the DeltaV system, run Windows User Manager to set the privileges (if necessary) for the SOFTPHASEUSER. When DeltaV is in a domain, and the non-DeltaV node is in a workgroup, you must Create a local SOFTPHASEUSER account on the DeltaV node that you are connecting to. Make the password match the domain SOFTPHASEUSER account. Set any Windows privileges if needed for the local SOFTPHASEUSER. These should be the same as the domain SOFTPHASEUSER account has, but only on the local computer. Set the local SOFTPHASEUSER as a non-interactive user. That is, the user account cannot be used to log onto Windows. This can be set using GPOs or local policies (in a workgroup). When DeltaV is in a domain, and the non-DeltaV node is in a workgroup, you must create a local DeltaVAdmin account on the DeltaV node that you are connecting to. Log on to Windows as an administrator on this computer. Using Windows User Manager, create a local account named DeltaVAdmin. Assign it the same password as the domain DeltaVAdmin account. Make it a member of the local DeltaV group. Set this account as a non-interactive user. That is, the user account cannot be used to log onto Windows. This can be set using GPOs or local policies. On the DeltaV node, log on to Windows as an administrator and run DeltaV Security Administration. In a domain, log on to Windows as a domain administrator. In a workgroup, log on to Windows as a local administrator. Set the SOFTPHASEUSER account password. Note: This password must match between the DeltaV node (both local and domain accounts) and the non-DeltaV node. On the non-DeltaV machine, create the SOFTPHASEUSER account using Windows User Manager. Assign it any privileges needed. Set the account as a non-interactive user. That is, the user account cannot be used to log onto Windows. This can be set using GPOs or local policies. Set the password to be the same password that you created for this account on the DeltaV node. On the non-DeltaV node, create a local DeltaVAdmin account using Windows User Manager. Assign it any privileges needed. Set the account as a non-interactive user. That is, the user account cannot be used to log onto Windows. This can be set using GPOs or local policies. Set the password to be the same password that you created for this account on the DeltaV node. Add the DeltaVAdmin account to the local administrators' group. Alternately, you can add the DeltaVAdmin account in DCOM Launch and Activate.

title: Physically decommissioning controllers
body_text: Physically decommissioning controllers The controller hardware must be physically removed from its carrier to initialize it to its decommissioned state. Removing the controller from its carrier clears the controller's commissioning and cold restart data. Note: The ProfessionalPlus maintains a commissioning file for each controller in the database. If the node is not decommissioned in the database, it is possible for the ProfessionalPlus to automatically recommission the controller when it is reinstalled. This will not occur if nodes are decommissioned before exchanging databases. Decommission a simplex controller Remove the simplex controller from its carrier and wait for 10 seconds. Reinstall the controller on the carrier. Decommission a redundant controller pair Remove both the standby and active controllers from the carrier and wait for 10 seconds. Both controllers must be removed otherwise the standby will become the active node and the node will remain unavailable to the database. Reinstall the controllers on the carrier.

title: Physically decommission CIOCs and WIOCs
body_text: Physically decommission CIOCs and WIOCs Unlike controllers, the ProfessionalPlus is not used to recommission WIOC and CIOC nodes. CIOC and WIOC commissioning information is stored in the I/O Port’s (IOP) nonvolatile memory (NVM). When a CIOC/WIOC is powered up, its hardware address is compared to the stored commissioning information. If the IOP and the CIOC/WIOC recognize that they were last commissioned together, the node is restored. If a physical change is detected, the commissioning information is discarded and the CIOC/WIOC comes up decommissioned. Decommission a simplex CIOC or WIOC Remove the simplex WIOC or CIOC from its slot on the carrier. Install it in another slot on the carrier. If you want to install the CIOC/WIOC in a particular slot, repeat the above steps after the CIOC/WIOC has initialized. Decommission a redundant CIOC or WIOC pair Remove both CIOCs/WIOCs from the carrier. Swap the physical location of the CIOCs/WIOCs on the carrier.

title: Defer a parameter
body_text: Defer a parameter To defer the step parameter up to the procedure level, use the following steps: At the operation level, create the recipe parameter AMOUNT as a deferred parameter. Then access the recipe step assigned to phase XFER_IN and defer the phase parameter AMT_TO_ADD to the recipe parameter AMOUNT. Edit the unit procedure and create the recipe parameter ADD_AMOUNT as a deferred parameter. Then, access the step assigned to the operation configured above and defer the step parameter, AMOUNT to the ADD_AMOUNT recipe parameter. At the procedure level, you access the values for step parameters to which the above unit procedures are assigned and set the parameter values based on the specific recipe. Alternatively, you can create a top-level recipe parameter, and set the value at run time, with additional formulas if needed. By creating this chain of parameters, you pass desired values all the way down to the phase. This approach lets you incorporate generic operations that are shared by multiple master recipes into your control strategy. Note: Only parameters of the category Process Input can be deferred (to both input and report parameters).

title: Defer a phase parameter and create an operation level parameter
main_heading: Defer a phase parameter and create an operation level parameter
body_text: Defer a phase parameter and create an operation level parameter Open the procedure PRC_PAINT in Recipe Studio. In the Hierarchy view in the upper left corner, expand PRC_PAINT and UP_BLEND and select the operation OP_CHARGE. In the Diagram view, click the step named CHG_BASE:1 to select the phase. In the lower left corner of the Parameter view, right-click the phase parameter CHG_BASE:1/CHARGE_AMT, and then select Properties from the context menu. The parameter Properties dialog opens. Change the Origin to Defer and type OP_BASE_AMT as the operation-level parameter to be used as the source for the phase parameter value. Click OK when the system displays the following message about creating the parameter. Since you haven't created the parameter directly, the system will do it for you. Note that in the Parameter view, with the CHG_BASE phase selected, the Origin field for the CHARGE_AMT parameter is now set to Defer and the Value field specifies OP_BASE_AMT. To create a parameter for the charge amount for color, follow steps 3 through 7 above, except click the CHG_COLOR step and name the new parameter source for CHARGE_AMT to OP_COLOR_AMT. To create a parameter for the agitate time, follow steps 2 through 7 above, except select the OP_FINISH operation in the Herarchy view, click the AGITATE step, modify the AGITATE_TIME parameter, and name the new parameter source AGITATE_TIME. Now that we have the three process input parameters at the operation level, we need to create them at the unit procedure level and then the procedure level. We will do this the same way, by deferring the lower level parameters to the next higher level, which automatically creates the parameters at the higher level.

title: Define the Master Time Server node
main_heading: Define the Master Time Server node
body_text: Define the Master Time Server node The Master Time Server node broadcasts the system time to all workstations and controllers on the DeltaV Control Network. By default, the Professional PLUS workstation is the Master Time Server node. However, any physical DeltaV workstation on the DeltaV Control Network can be defined as the Master Time Server node. To define the Master Time Server node, complete the following steps: Navigate to System Configuration > Physical Network . Right-click Physical Network , and then select Properties . Click the Browse button on the System Time tab in the Physical Network Properties dialog, and then select a workstation on the DeltaV Control Network. You can also define the Backup Time Server node on the System Time tab in the Physical Network Properties dialog. Related information System time

title: Define a reserved list of users or nodes
main_heading: Define a reserved list of users or nodes
body_text: Define a reserved list of users or nodes The Administrator setting up the Remote Client session can specify that the session be made available to a reserved list of user names or node names. The same user/node names may appear on the reserved lists for more than one remote session. Reserved lists allow connection according to the following rules: If the reserved list has only one name, then only that user/node can connect through that remote session. If there are multiple names in the list for a particular session, then access is available to those users/nodes on a first-come, first-served basis. If there is no reserved list set up, then any DeltaV user/node will be allowed to connect under that remote session. Even though a user is able to begin the process of connecting to a Remote Client server from a node on the reserved node list, the user must still log in under a valid DeltaV user ID and password for the connection to be completed. Usage privileges are still as defined in the DeltaV User Manager. To add names to the Reserved for User (or Node) List: Open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the Remote Client server workstation. Right-click the Remote Client session for which you want to define a reserved user list and select Properties from the context menu. Select the Reserved for User List tab on the Properties dialog. Click Add to open a dialog where you can enter the user name or select the name from a pull-down list of available user names. You can also use this dialog to delete user names from the reserved list. Similarly, if you wish to reserve the remote session for specific nodes, click the Reserved for Node List tab. Then click Add to open a dialog where you can enter the node name or select the name from a pull-down list of all the node names in the local network.

title: Define CHARMs
body_text: Define CHARMs Defining a CHARM involves setting the CHARM's properties such as its class and type in the DeltaV Explorer. Defining a CHARM automatically enables it. After a CHARM has been defined, it can be assigned to an S-series controller. Select the CHARM and click Properties to access the Properties dialog. Refer to the help for the CHARM's Properties dialog for information on the various items on the Properties dialogs. Refer to the DeltaV S-series and CHARMs Hardware Reference manual for CHARMs wiring diagrams and specifications.

title: Define the alarm properties
body_text: Define the alarm properties Use the Alarm properties dialog to identify the parameter that you want to trigger the alarm and you associate that parameter with the alarm. Using the example in Creating a Custom Alarm Calculation (PV > 70), define the alarm properties by following these steps: Click the Condition block to select it. Right-click in the Alarms View window and select Add . In the Properties dialog, select an Alarm type . For this example, select Any Alarm . Select the Priority . The priority of Log only sends the event to the Event Journal and does not display anything to the operator. Note: This step sets the alarm presentation. In the Related Parameters section's Alarm field, browse to the Condition block's OUT_D parameter. Make sure the alarm is enabled and invert the alarm characteristics if desired. Use the Advanced tab to change the alarm message parameters (if available) and set the Alarm Shelving Timeout . Click OK . Right-click the alarm and select Rename . Rename the alarm appropriately. The alarm is now defined for the parameter OUT_D of the Condition block. When the AI block's PV > 70, the output of the Condition block is set to True and the alarm is triggered. Note: If the alarm was inverted, then the alarm is triggered when OUT_D of the Condition block is set to False.

title: Delete data from the main database
main_heading: Delete data from the main database
body_text: Delete data from the main database To delete data from the main database, perform the following steps: Select the archived batch and chronicle events, and then click Batches\Events > Delete . This frees up space in the main database for more batch and chronicle events. Verify the newly created space by selecting the DVHisDB database, clicking Database > Properties from the main menu, and looking at the Database Space tab. You should develop a structure and naming convention for your archive databases to help manage your historical batch information. The Batch Historian Administration Tool allows you to create folders for your archive databases. You can easily move the archive database containers to and from these folders.

title: Delete the update interval named range
main_heading: Delete the update interval named range
body_text: Delete the update interval named range Select the Formulas tab. In the Defined Names group, click Name Manager . Select the DVUpdateInterval which you want to delete. Click Delete . Note: DVUpdateInterval is a named range. To delete it, you must follow this procedure. Deleting the contents of the cell that contains the update interval only removes that value assigned to the update interval; it does not delete the named range itself.

title: Finish the demotion
body_text: Finish the demotion Assign licenses for the Application Station as needed. Enable the Batch Executive (or Campaign Manager, or both) on the workstation (previously the preferred active). Download the workstation. If keeping both computers on the DeltaV network, you will need to Add the second computer (previously the preferred standby) to the control network in DeltaV Explorer. Assign licenses, enabled subsystems, and assign areas, modules, and so on, to the workstation as needed. Export the configuration file. Run Workstation Configuration on the workstation. Download the workstation.

title: Remove the Redundant Batch subsystem
body_text: Remove the Redundant Batch subsystem In DeltaV Explorer, select the Application Station pair, right-click and select Properties . Select the Redundancy tab. Deselect the Enable a redundant subsystem option. Click OK to close the Properties dialog. Export the configuration file. Reboot both workstations in the pair. This will stop the services. Run Workstation Configuration on the preferred active node. Reference the newly exported configuration file. Note: The Direct Link connection's Ethernet card, if previously configured, will no longer be used.

title: Discover ports and protocols to create custom rules
main_heading: Discover ports and protocols to create custom rules
body_text: Discover ports and protocols to create custom rules Follow this procedure if you want to create custom rules but do not know the applications' ports and protocols. In this procedure, you create custom applications using both the TCP and UDP protocols and ports 1-65534 to allow communications on all ports. You can then examine the log to determine which ports and protocols are actually used. On the firewall's web UI navigate to Configuration > Applications and select Add new application . Create a new application called "test TCP ports" that uses the TCP protocol, and ports 1-65534, select Use for inbound connections and Use for outbound connections and click Apply . Select Add new application again and create a new application called "test UPD ports" that uses the UDP protocol, and ports 1-65534, select Use for inbound connections and Use for outbound connections and click Apply . Navigate to the Protection tab Inbound or outbound connections page and create a TCP and UPD rule between the computers that will be communicating using these applications. If you are unsure if the application needs an outbound or inbound rule, create both and use the information in the log to determine the proper direction. Enable logging on the newly created rules. Note: If other rules are enabled between these computers, disable logging on these rules so this is the only rule that is creating log entries for these computers. Run the applications on both computers using the application's full functionality. Allow the applications to run long enough to create sufficient log entries. Find the logs on the syslog server and search for all of the log entries matching the IP addresses of the computers that use the applications you just created. Find the applications' ports and protocols in the log. Document the ports and protocols on the Worksheet for custom applications . Delete and disconnect the test rules. Now that you know the ports and protocols, go to Configuration > Applications and add the custom applications. Then go to Protection > Inbound and Outbound connections to add the rules for the custom applications. Be sure to enable logging on the rules. Note: As you create each rule, ensure that the applications are communicating properly. Since these rules were not pre-tested, exercise the applications to ensure they are communicating and working properly. Related information Deleting rules and disconnecting communications Worksheet for custom applications

title: Disk check
body_text: Disk check Perform a disk check whenever Windows shuts down abruptly (without using the normal shutdown procedures). Use the following steps: Start the Windows Explorer by selecting Start > Programs > Accessories > Windows Explorer . Select the disk(s) where the DeltaV software and database reside. (If the software and database reside on two disks, perform these steps separately for each disk.) Right-click and select Properties . The Local Disk Properties dialog appears. Click the Tools tab. Then, click Check Now in the Error-checking pane. Select both check boxes, as shown in the following figure. A system message appears stating that you cannot get exclusive access to the disk and asking if you want to perform error-checking restart. Click Yes . Restart the computer. This runs the disk check.

title: Download a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver
main_heading: Download a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver
body_text: Download a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Navigate to a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver in the Local Safety Network under a SIS Controller. Right-click and select Download > CHARMs Logic Solver . If parameter values have changed since the last download, an Upload dialog appears listing the changes. Note: If you do not have the key for the SIS_UPLOAD_CONFIG function, click Cancel on the Upload dialog to continue with the download. Otherwise, you can select the changes to be uploaded, if there are any, and click OK . If you have the key for the SIS_UPLOAD_CONFIG function (by default, SIS Can Configure), select the parameter values you want to upload to the database and click OK . The Upload complete dialog appears. Click Close on the Upload complete dialog. The Confirm Download dialog appears. Click Yes on the Confirm Download dialog. If the Logic Solver is locked, the Logic Solver Locked Dialog appears. Click Unlock and Continue to proceed. The Exploring DeltaV dialog appears prompting you to confirm this unlock. Click Confirm to continue. If the physical keylock is enabled and it is not in the unlocked position an error message appears. Note: The Logic Solver remains unlocked after the download. The Downloading Selected Objects dialog appears, and the system performs pre-downloaded configuration checks. If errors are found, the Configuration Check Results dialog that appears informs you that the download cannot continue. At this point you can cancel the download, correct the problems found, and then re-download. The download proceeds to the Verifying Configuration phase. If verification errors are found, the download is not allowed to continue. If no verification errors are found, the download proceeds through the Generating and Downloading phases and the Download complete dialog appears. Note: If the configuration has changed since the last download, the Download dialog includes a message that a functional test may be required. For more information on using CRCs (cyclic redundancy checks) to determine if a functional test is required, refer to the DeltaV SIS Safety Manual . Click Close .

title: Download the SLS 1508 logic solver
body_text: Download the SLS 1508 logic solver Navigate to the Logic Solver in the SIS Network. Right-click and select Download > Logic Solver . If parameter values have changed since the last download, an Upload dialog appears listing the changes. Note: If you do not have the key for the SIS_UPLOAD_CONFIG function, click Cancel on the Upload dialog to continue with the download. Otherwise, you can select the changes to be uploaded, if there are any, and click OK . If you have the key for the SIS_UPLOAD_CONFIG function (by default, SIS Can Configure), select the parameter values you want to upload to the database and click OK . The Upload complete dialog appears. Click Close on the Upload complete dialog. The Confirm Download dialog appears. Click Yes on the Confirm Download dialog. If the Logic Solver is locked, the Logic Solver Locked Dialog appears. If the dialog appears click Unlock and Continue to proceed. An Exploring DeltaV dialog appears asking you to Confirm this unlock? Click Confirm to continue. Note: The Logic Solver remains unlocked after the download. The Downloading Selected Objects dialog appears, and the system performs pre-downloaded configuration checks. If errors are found, the Configuration Check Results dialog that appears informs you that the download cannot continue. At this point you can cancel the download, correct the problems found, and then re-download. The download proceeds to the Verifying Configuration phase. If verification errors are found, the download is not allowed to continue. If no verification errors are found, the download proceeds through the Generating and Downloading phases and the Download complete dialog appears. Note: If the configuration has changed since the last download, the Download dialog includes a message that a functional test may be required. For more information on using CRCs (cyclic redundancy checks) to determine if a functional test is required, refer to the DeltaV SIS Safety Manual . Click Close .

title: Download an SIS Controller
body_text: Download an SIS Controller You must have the privilege to perform DOWNLOAD_CONFIG to download an SIS Controller. You do not need the equivalent SIS privilege. Navigate to an SIS Controller in the Control Network. Right-click and select Download > SIS Controller . The Confirm Total Download dialog appears. Note: If you select any of the other Download options, a similar dialog appears. Click Yes to start the download.

title: Download the controller configuration
body_text: Download the controller configuration In DeltaV Explorer, select and right-click the controller, and then select Download > Controller from the menu. Read any messages that appear and select the appropriate responses. A window opens showing the progress of the download and providing information about any problems encountered. When the download is complete, click Close .

title: Download the modules
body_text: Download the modules Open (or restore) DeltaV Explorer and open System Configuration > Physical Network > Control Network > CTLR1 (or your controller name) > Assigned Modules . (This shows you all the modules you have assigned to the controller.) Select and right-click Control Network , and then select Download > Control Network . When asked, confirm that you want to proceed with the download. When asked, confirm that you want to check the configuration. A window opens to show you the progress of the download and to let you know when it is complete. When the download is complete, click Close . Quit DeltaV Explorer and any other DeltaV applications you have open.

title: Download the ProfessionalPLUS workstation
body_text: Download the ProfessionalPLUS workstation When you have finished configuring the workstation and assigning licenses, you need to download the configuration. Before you download, make sure the System Identifier has been connected to the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. Start DeltaV Explorer by clicking Start > DeltaV Engineering > DeltaV Explorer . Under Control Network , select and right-click the workstation, and then select Download > ProfessionalPlus Station from the menu. Read the message and, if you are sure that the workstation is not controlling a process, click Yes to acknowledge the message and accept the defaults in the Confirm Download dialog. A window opens showing the progress of the download and providing information about any problems encountered. Click Download Anyway if the Configuration Check Results message box appears. Because you have not assigned I/O, you will probably get some configuration messages. Click Close to close the Download dialog.

title: Download the workstation
body_text: Download the workstation Select and right-click the workstation you want to download. Click Download > ProfessionalPlus Station . Read the message and, if you are sure that the workstation is not controlling a process, click Yes to acknowledge the message. (Accept the default option to verify the configuration.) A window opens showing the progress of the download and providing information about any problems encountered. Click Close to close the dialog. We assigned area TANK-101 to the Continuous Historian and Alarms and Events subsystems, enabled history and events collection on the workstation, and downloaded the workstation. Now we will use the Process History View application to view the data. Related information DeltaV Explorer overview

title: Download the workstation setup data
body_text: Download the workstation setup data After you have made your changes in DeltaV User Manager, you need to download the workstation setup data. In DeltaV Explorer, select the workstation, right-click it, and select Download > Setup Data from the menu. Click Yes to confirm the download. A window opens to show the progress of the download and to provide information about any problems encountered. You have finished the Physical Network part of the system configuration and set up your user account. Now you are ready to start configuring the control strategy.

title: Draw and color a rectangle with a crosshatch appearance
main_heading:
Draw and color a rectangle with a crosshatch
	 appearance
body_text: Draw and color a rectangle with a crosshatch appearance Click the rectangle button on the Toolbox. The pointer changes to a +. Click and hold somewhere on the picture, drag the pointer to set the size of the rectangle, and release the mouse button. Select the rectangle, right-click, and then select Fill Style > Cross Hatch . For the remaining steps, make sure the rectangle is selected. Right-click, and then select Edge Style > Dash Dot . Right-click, select Color > Foreground , and then select yellow in the palette. Draw another rectangle. Note that none of the default colors, line style, or fill style have changed. Now you can add some basic shapes and text to your drawing using the rectangle, oval, line, polyline, polygon, and text tools. Try coloring, moving, and resizing the objects. (If you use the polyline or polygon tools, double-click to finish the object.) When you have finished, click File > Close and do not save the work you have done on the file. If you are ready to continue, open TANK101 from the Pictures folder in the system tree.

title: Edit documents
body_text: Edit documents After you have created your Documents folder hierarchy, populated it with documents, set the working folders, and retrieved the documents, you can edit documents. Edit documents only after you have checked them out or have determined they are already checked out to you. VCAT for documents allows you to open documents from DeltaV Explorer whether they are checked out to you, checked out to someone else, or not checked out at all, but you may not be able to check them in and could end up with three versions of a document: VCAT's copy, DeltaV Explorer's copy, and the copy in your working directory. It may take some effort to resolve such a situation. If you establish the habit of editing only documents checked out to you, you can avoid such situations. The most straightforward way to manage documents is: Make sure the folder containing the document has a working folder set. Check the document out of VCAT from DeltaV Explorer. Retrieve the document from DeltaV Explorer. Open the document from DeltaV Explorer. The document opens in its associated application. If the application is not found, you are prompted to select an application. Edit the document. Save the document in its application (this saves the document to the working folder) and close the application. An Exploring DeltaV popup appears saying the document has been modified and asking if you want to save it to the database now. Clicking Yes on this dialog saves the document to the DeltaV database. Clicking No does not save it to the DeltaV database and the versions of the document in the DeltaV database and in the working folder are now different. Check the document back in to VCAT.

title: Edit the NC_VALVE control module class
main_heading: Edit the NC_VALVE control module class
body_text: Edit the NC_VALVE control module class Open the NC_VALVE control module class in Control Studio. (In the DeltaV Explorer, right-click the class, and then select Open with Control Studio .) It contains a single DC function block. Click the DC1 function block. In the lower left pane, double-click the MODE parameter. On the MODE Properties dialog, select both Auto and Cascade as permitted modes. Set both the Normal mode and Target mode to Cascade . (The phase logic will be writing to the CAS setpoint, and the block must be in CAS mode to respond to CAS setpoint changes.) Add an input parameter from the Special Items palette, dragging it to the left of the DC block, as shown in the figure below. On the Parameter Properties dialog, name the parameter VALVE_SP, keep the parameter type as Floating point, and check the box marked Allow instance value to be configured . Draw a connection line between VALVE_SP and the CAS_IN_D parameter on the DC block. Show PV_D as an output parameter on the DC block. (To do this, right-click the DC block, select Show Parameter , browse for the PV_D parameter, and then select Output as the type of parameter.) Add an output parameter from the Special Items palette, dragging it to the right of the DC block. On the Parameter Properties dialog, name the parameter PV and keep the parameter type of Floating point. Draw a connection line between PV_D on the DC block and the PV parameter. Add a Deadtime (DT) block from the Analog Control palette, dragging it to the right of the DC block. Draw a connection line from the OUT_D parameter on the DC block to the IN parameter on the DT block. Draw a connection line from the OUT parameter on the DT block to the SIMULATE_IN_D parameter on the DC block. (The reason for looping back to the SIMULATE_IN_D parameter is that we will be using modules derived from this class during some simulation exercises.) In the Diagram View, right-click, and then select Properties . On the Displays tab, browse for and select Process as the primary control display. Save NC_VALVE. The completed function block diagram looks like the following. Note: Control Studio automatically depicts a feedback wire, such as the line between OUT on the DT block and SIMULATE_IN_D on the DC block, as a dashed line after you save a module or manually set its execution order. To manually set or remove a feedback wire, select the line, right-click, and then select Wire > Set as Feedback or Wire > Remove as Feedback . Whether the line is dashed or solid has no effect on the logic; it is simply a visual clue.

title: Edit the parameter setpoints
body_text: Edit the parameter setpoints Now we will edit the values in the table to specify the required value of each parameter setpoint for each of the defined states. (A value of 0 will send a closed setpoint to the item and a value of 1 will send an open setpoint to the item.) When you select an item's state, the item's name appears in the Items tab as shown. When the state is Closed, all setpoints should be 0. When the state is Draining, the outlet pump should be on (1) and the waste valve open (1). When the state is Releasing Product, the outlet pump should be on (1) and the product valve open (1). Double-click the value 0 in the Draining column for the OUT_PUMP_SP. On the OUT_PUMP_SP Properties dialog, change the value from 0 to 1. Change other parameter setpoint values so that the table looks like the following, save the file, and close Control Studio. We now have all the basic control module classes and equipment module classes that will be used for this application. Now we can create the remainder of the equipment hierarchy. This includes creating the unit classes in the Advanced Definitions section of the library and the unit modules in the System Configuration section. After that we will create the phase logic that will be assigned to the unit classes.

title: Configuring custom or array PLC tag definitions
main_heading: Configuring custom or array PLC tag definitions
body_text: Configuring custom or array PLC tag definitions Prerequisites: In the System Preferences application under Networking , select Ethernet I/P Integration with Tags . Export control tag definitions from the PLC. For Rockwell devices, this is a .L5X file. Copy the file you exported from the PLC to the ProfessionalPLUS. You can place the file anywhere on the workstation. When you configure the physical device later in the configuration process, the software copies it to the DeltaV\DVData\ControlTags folder. In DeltaV Explorer, navigate to DeltaV_System > Library > PLC Tag Definitions . Right-click Rockwell Logix , then click New PLC Tag Definition . The software displays the New Control Tag Definition dialog. Select the Tag Type (Custom or Array). Click Browse for file . Select a PLC definition file, then click Open . Click Browse for definition . The software displays the Add-on instruction definitions available in this file. Select a definition from the top selection box. The software displays the parameters for the selected definition in the bottom selection box. Select as many as 10 parameters (for a custom-type definition). Select one parameter for an array-type tag. Array tags can have one parameter with 2 to 64 elements (non-string data types) or 10 elements (string data type). Click OK on the selection dialog. Click OK on the New Control Tag Definition dialog. Tip: The New Control Tag Definition dialog also supports a manual Add button. This enables you to add a specific parameter if do not have a PLC definition file at this time but you know the valid parameter names. Browse to or create an EIOC. Make sure the EIOC port protocol is set to Control Tag Access and a physical and logical device are present. Right-click the EIOC's logical device, then click New Ethernet I/O Control Tag . The software displays the New Control Tag dialog. From the Tag Definition list, click the custom tag definition you created in this procedure. The software creates the definition tags, tag signals and device tags under the logical device. You can reference the device tags in your control logic. If you configured an L5X file, click the Browse button next to the Tag Name field to select a name. The software displays the tags of the selected type (if any exist in the file). Connect the PLC to the EIOC port. Download the EIOC card.

title: Electrical noise on the carrier
body_text: Electrical noise on the carrier Electrical noise on the carrier affects the communication between Series 2 redundant serial cards and causes them to switch over. To correct this issue: Determine if there is any electrical noise near the carrier and, if so, remove the noise source. Flashing red LEDs and loss of communication between the card and the carriers indicate the existence of noise. Noise can be caused by electrical activity (such as welding), the use of devices (such as 2-way radios), or natural causes (such as lightning), occurring close to the DeltaV installation. Reset the serial cards by removing each card from the carrier and then re-inserting it into its slot. Open DeltaV Diagnostics (click Start > DeltaV Operator > Diagnostics ). For each card, right-click the card, and then select Clear Saved Fault Information .

title: Enable a DeltaV Remote Client
body_text: Enable a DeltaV Remote Client ProfessionalPLUS workstations have Remote Client functionality enabled by default. To enable DeltaV Remote client on an Operator Station, the node must be running the server version of the operating system. To enable DeltaV Remote Client on an Operator Station to be used as a Remote Client server, complete the following steps: Open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the Control Network and right-click the Operator Station for which you want to enable Remote Client. Select Properties from the context menu. Select the check box next to Enable Remote Client Functionality . The Remote Client subsystem is added under the workstation.

title: Enable CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers
body_text: Enable CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers If you did not enable DeltaV SIS CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers when you installed DeltaV software, enable it now. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > System Preferences . Select the Enable CHARMs Logic Solvers check box. Click OK. A message appears saying that you must restart the DeltaV Database Server for the changes to take effect. Enabling CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers changes the DeltaV interface, particularly DeltaV Explorer and Control Studio. In DeltaV Explorer the changes include the addition of CHARMs Smart Logic Solver-related Library objects, and Setup additions in SIS Security, SIS Named Sets, and SIS Alarm Types. In Control Studio the changes include the ability to configure SIS modules, templates, and composite blocks. If your system has both SLS1508 Logic Solvers and CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers and you have enabled both in the DeltaV software, you must be careful not to inadvertently create SIS modules that will not run on the intended logic solver.

title: Enable DCOM on the PC
body_text: Enable DCOM on the PC Normally, DCOM is enabled on the machine when Windows is installed. However, if DCOM is not enabled, you can do so by following these steps on both the server and client machines: Run the executable file, dcomcnfg.exe. The Component Services window opens. In the left pane, open Component Services . A Computers folder appears. Open the Computers folder. The My Computer icon appears. Right-click the My Computer icon and select Properties . Select the Default Properties tab. Select the Enable Distributed COM on this computer check box. Changing this value requires a reboot. The EnableDCOM key in the Windows registry is set to "Y" when this check box is selected. If DCOM is not enabled, then all cross-machine calls are rejected (the caller, typically, gets an RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE return code).

title: Enable SLS 1508 Logic Solvers
body_text: Enable SLS 1508 Logic Solvers If you did not enable DeltaV SIS SLS 1508 Logic Solvers when you installed DeltaV software, enable it now. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > System Preferences . Select the Enable SLS 1508 Logic Solvers check box. Click OK. A message appears saying that you must restart the DeltaV Database Server for the changes to take effect. Enabling SLS 1508 Logic Solvers changes the DeltaV interface, particularly DeltaV Explorer and Control Studio. In DeltaV Explorer the changes include the addition of the SIS Network, SIS-related Library objects, and Setup additions in SIS Security, SIS Named Sets, and SIS Alarm Types. In Control Studio the changes include the ability to configure SIS modules, templates, and composite blocks. If your system has both SLS1508 Logic Solvers and CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers and you have enabled both in the DeltaV software, you must be careful not to inadvertently create SIS modules that will not run on the intended logic solver.

title: Enable DeviceNet I/O polling
body_text: Enable DeviceNet I/O polling Right-click the device and select Properties Select the Enable I/O Polling option to exchange I/O data between the device and the DeviceNet master. Note: In order for data exchange to occur, the VendorID , Device Type , Product Code , and input/output sizes must match. If there is no match, the connection breaks, and no data is exchanged. Also, the VendorID , Device Type , Product Code , and input/output sizes cannot be read from the device. The verification only identifies a match in these items, it does not read back the values. Disable I/O Polling and download the device, and then read back Vendor ID , Device Type , Product Code , and input/output sizes using DeltaV Diagnostics to troubleshoot communication problems.

title: Enable or disable a system preference
main_heading: Enable or disable a system preference
body_text: Enable or disable a system preference To enable or disable a function by using DeltaV System Preferences, complete the following steps: Click DeltaV Engineering > System Preferences on the Start menu. In the System Preferences dialog, select or clear the check box for the function that you want to enable or disable. Options on the System Preferences dialog are arranged in groups. You can enable or disable individual options or all options included in a group. Note: After changing a system preference option, it may be necessary to restart the affected DeltaV client application for the change to take effect. If enabling or disabling a function requires restarting the DeltaV Database Server, shut down and restart the server by completing the following steps: Click DeltaV Engineering > Database Administration on the Start menu. In the Database Administration window, select Shutdown Server on the File menu. On the Shutdown Server dialog, enable the Force shutdown even if clients are connected option. If a notification window appears for any application connected to the DeltaV Database Server, exit the application by clicking the Yes button. After the Shutdown Server command terminates, the message Database Server is shut down appears in the status bar of the Database Administration window. Select Connect to Server on the File menu. After the Connect to Server command terminates, the message Database Server is running appears in the status bar of the Database Administration window. Optionally, restart any application that you exited while shutting down and restarting the DeltaV Database Server.

title: Enable history collection in the workstation
main_heading: Enable history collection in the workstation
body_text: Enable history collection in the workstation Under the Workstation, click the Continuous Historian subsystem. Right-click, and then select Properties . The Continuous Historian Properties dialog opens. Click the Enabled check box if it is unchecked. Click the Advanced tab. This tab enables you to set the maximum size and time span for the historical database as well as the size of historical data sets. You can also set up automatic export of historical data sets by enabling that feature and then setting a valid directory path on the workstation, outside the DeltaV system. We will not make any changes on this tab. Click OK . Subtopics: Enable history collection from the Alarms and Events subsystem

title: Enable history collection from the Alarms and Events subsystem
main_heading: Enable history collection from the Alarms and Events subsystem
body_text: Enable history collection from the Alarms and Events subsystem Under the Workstation, click the Alarms and Events subsystem. Right-click, and then select Properties . The Alarms and Events Properties dialog opens. Click Enabled if it is not already selected. Click the Advanced tab. Set the Current Event History Data Set Total Storage Target to 250 megabytes. Click OK .

title: Enable the Mynah Integration web service
main_heading: Enable the Mynah Integration web service
body_text: Enable the Mynah Integration web service If you are using the Mynah Mimic application for simulation, you must enable the Mynah Integration web service. Note: The Mynah Integration web service is intended for use only in DeltaV Simulation systems. To enable and start the Mynah web service: Select Start > DeltaV Engineering > System Preferences . Select Enable Simulation Download . Click OK . Select Start > DeltaV Engineering > Database Administration . Close all DeltaV applications. Select File > Shutdown Server . After the Database Server shuts down, select File > Connect to Server . From DeltaV Explorer, open the ProfessionalPLUS workstation Properties dialog. Select Enable Mynah Integration Web Service . Click OK . Download ProfessionalPLUS setup data. It may take a few moments for the Mynah Integration web service to start. The Mynah Integration web service should now appear in the Gateway Administration application. After you enable the Mynah service the following services start on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation: Monitor Service Mynah Integration web service

title: Enable simulation on the NC_VALVE module class
main_heading: Enable simulation on the NC_VALVE module class
body_text: Enable simulation on the NC_VALVE module class Open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the NC_VALVE control module class under the DeviceControl category in the Advanced Definitions section. Right-click NC_VALVE, and then select Configure from the context menu. Select the Parameters tab. Click Add . Browse to DC1/SIMULATE_D, and then click OK . Select the DC1$SIMULATE_D parameter and click Modify to open the Properties dialog (or double-click the parameter name). Select Enabled under Simulate Enabled/Disabled. Click OK on the Properties dialog, and then close the Configure dialog.

title: Configure Windows firewall profiles on a DeltaV workstation
main_heading: Configure Windows firewall profiles on a DeltaV workstation
body_text: Configure Windows firewall profiles on a DeltaV workstation Important: Do not enable the Windows firewall profiles for any dedicated DeltaV networks; for example, the DeltaV Primary and Secondary ACNs , DLINK for Redundant Batch, and the Thin Client Primary and Secondary networks . Doing so could disrupt communications between DeltaV nodes. Login to the Windows desktop as an administrator. With the Windows firewall service started on the DeltaV workstation, open the Windows firewall utility. Note: These are the only supported paths for accessing the Windows firewall. This ensures that the Windows firewall is configured for the correct store. Do not access the Windows firewall in any other manner. Start > Windows Administrative Tools > Windows Firewall with Advanced Security Click the Windows Firewall Properties link. Important: Determining which profile you need to enable requires an understanding of each profile's definition, of what the network interface card is used for, and of how the DeltaV computer is using that card. It requires knowledge of what networks connect to that card, and what types of communication by what applications must be permitted on that card (so that the appropriate application rules allowing communication can be applied). Turn on the firewall for each profile as needed. In this procedure you must also select which network interface card to apply the enabled profile. Do not apply a profile to any of the dedicated DeltaV networks. Select a profile tab (Domain, Private, Public). Select On (recommended) for the Firewall state: option. For Inbound connections , select Block (default) . Note: This allows the inbound rules to apply. Do not select Block all connections as it will not apply the inbound rules you enable. For Outbound connections , select Allow <Default> . Click the Protected network connections Customize… button. Deselect all dedicated DeltaV network connections ; for example, DeltaV Primary DeltaV Secondary DLink Thin Client Primary Thin Client Secondary Note: Networks used to connect to the DeltaV system that are outside of the DeltaV network need to be evaluated for the Windows firewall. If any non-DeltaV traffic is allowed on the network connecting to DeltaV, then enable the Windows firewall on that NIC and use DeltaV Security Administration to select the correct rule to open the necessary ports. Select any non-DeltaV network connections where you need to regulate the external traffic coming into the DeltaV system. On the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security dialog, in the Settings section, click the Customize button. On the Customize Settings dialog, configure the settings as follows: Windows Server Profile Display Notification Allow Unicast Response Domain Yes No Private Yes No Public Yes No Windows Workstation Profile Display Notification Allow Unicast Response Domain Yes No Private Yes No Public No No Click OK . Click Apply and continue to another profile. When done with all the profiles, click OK . With the Windows firewall enabled, all default Windows firewall rules are applied. The DeltaV rules are in addition to the default Windows firewall rules. When complete, close the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security window. Open DeltaV Security Administration to apply the appropriate DeltaV firewall rules to allow necessary communication through the Windows firewall. Perform this entire task on all DeltaV workstations. Related information The Windows firewall and a DeltaV workstation

title: Enable and setup recipe authorization
body_text: Enable and setup recipe authorization The recipe authorization function is enabled and set up in Version Control Audit Trail. Version Control is accessed through the DeltaV Database Administrator application. Remember that Version Control must be installed and setup to use the recipe authorization function. The process of enabling Version Control can take a significant amount of time. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > Database Administrator , and then double-click the Version Control Configuration icon to open the Version Control Configuration dialog. Enable Version Control if not already enabled (the check box is selected). Click the Recipes must be authorized before downloading check box. Select Enable signature propagation to referenced recipes if you want signers to have the option of sending their signature to lower level (referenced) recipes. Click the Signers button to open the Recipe Authorization Signers dialog. Then click Add to add at least one signer (for example managers or supervisors). Note: When you add a new signer description, VCAT automatically unauthorizes all previously authorized recipes until the new signer approves them. When you delete a signer description, VCAT automatically authorizes all recipes that have approvals from all other remaining signers. Click OK on the Version Control Configuration dialog to enable Version Control (if not already enabled) and recipe authorization and to setup recipe authorization. If not already created, the DeltaV system creates a Version Control database and populates it with items in your current configuration database. If VCAT was already running, this procedure adds Recipe Authorization functionality to the SQL database. Related information Setting up and disabling Version Control

title: Enter data in user-changeable fields
body_text: Enter data in user-changeable fields Some of the data links on the TANK101 picture were set up to allow changes by the operator. When you move your pointer over these fields, they are highlighted in a box. To make a change, click the field, type in a new value, and press Enter. Click the value for the data link for the loop setpoint. The value is highlighted. Type a new value, such as 50, and press RETURN . If you used a placeholder for a controller to do the tutorial, you will not be able to change this value.

title: Excessive withdrawal of current causes hardware error
main_heading:
Excessive withdrawal of current causes hardware
    error
body_text: Excessive withdrawal of current causes hardware error Providing a constant 24 VDC without current limit protection to the inputs of a redundant AI card for long periods of time during normal operation of the DeltaV system can cause a hardware error on the card. The excessive current damages the card's internal components. To correct this issue: Replace the card with the blinking red LED as it is probably damaged. Use a multimeter or other measurement device to determine if any of the channels are drawing 24 VDC without current limit protection and fix this problem. Reset the cards by removing each card from the carrier and then re-inserting it into its slot. Open DeltaV Diagnostics (click Start > DeltaV Operator > Diagnostics ). For each card, right-click the card, and then select Clear Saved Fault Information .

title: Execute all DVWrite functions
body_text: Execute all DVWrite functions To execute all the DVWrite functions on the active worksheet: Make sure the active cell is empty. Select the Add-Ins tab. From the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and select Runtime Data > Execute Write Function . Click Yes when prompted to confirm the selection. Related information Create a DVWrite function Execute a single DVWrite function Execute selected DVWrite functions

title: Execute selected DVWrite functions
body_text: Execute selected DVWrite functions To execute functions in a range of cells: Select a range of cells containing the DVWrite functions you want to execute. Select the Add-Ins tab. From the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and then select Runtime Data > Execute Write Function . Click Yes when prompted to confirm the selection. Related information Create a DVWrite function Execute a single DVWrite function Execute all DVWrite functions

title: Execute a single DVWrite function
body_text: Execute a single DVWrite function Select the cell that contains the DVWrite function. Change the value (optional). Select the Add-Ins tab. From the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and then select Runtime Data > Execute Write Function . Click Yes when prompted to confirm the selection. Related information Create a DVWrite function Execute selected DVWrite functions Execute all DVWrite functions

title: Exit the soft phase tester
body_text: Exit the soft phase tester To exit the Soft Phase Tester, follow these steps: Stop the soft phase. Once the soft phase is in an idle state, click the Reset button. This removes the soft phase from the computer's memory. Simply exiting will not remove the soft phase from memory. Select File > Exit .

title: Export a Zone topology
body_text: Export a Zone topology From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation in each zone: If you have not already defined the local areas shared with other zones, do so now. Select the Inter-Zone Server. From the context menu, select Zones Topology Export . Select a location and name for the .fhx file, and then click Save . After you complete steps 1 through 4 for each connected DeltaV system, you will have topology .fhx files exported from each of the zones in your system.

title: Export an OPC UA client certificate
main_heading: Export an OPC UA client certificate
body_text: Export an OPC UA client certificate Export the certificate to share it with an OPC UA server. Select the OPC UA Client in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Export Certificate . The software displays the Save As dialog, enabling you to save the certificate anywhere on the ProfessionalPlus workstation. The default location is DeltaV\DVData\Import-Export . Related information Create a DeltaV OPC UA client

title: Export the SLS 1508 configuration from the real system
main_heading: Export the SLS 1508 configuration from the real system
body_text: Export the SLS 1508 configuration from the real system On the real system: Export the SIS Network on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. Save the export files with unique names to prevent overwriting previous export files. You do not need to export SIS modules or their containing areas. SIS modules and areas are exported as part of the SIS Network subsystem.

title: Export a historical data set
body_text: Export a historical data set Current and extended historical data sets can be exported. If only an active data set is available, you can use Create New Active Data Set to create a new active data set and convert the existing active data set to a current data set that can be exported. To export one or more current or extended data sets, the user must have the DeltaV security key for the HDS_EXPORT function, and then complete the following steps: Select the current data set(s) you wish to export. To select more than one data set, hold down the CTRL or SHIFT key while selecting. Click the Export History Data Set(s) icon on the toolbar or select Export Data Set(s) from the Tools menu. You can also right-click the data set and select Export History Data Set(s) from the context menu. On the Browse dialog, browse for the directory to which you want to export the data sets. It is recommended that you select a directory location on the current workstation, but outside the DeltaV system. The Export History Data Set(s) dialog shows the progress of the export. If you interrupt the process by clicking the Abort button, the export in progress is not completed; however, any data sets already exported are not affected. Click Close to close the Export History Data Set(s) dialog. Note that exporting data sets does not automatically delete them from Primary storage. The data sets that are exported are not deleted from the Primary storage area. If the data set is again exported to the same directory, the export is given a unique name, appending - n to the name. The newly exported data set does not overwrite the existing one. It is common for the size of exported data sets to be different from the size of the original data set.

title: Export the equipment hierarchy
body_text: Export the equipment hierarchy Equipment hierarchy information enables OSIsoft PI Server to store and display parameter values in the context of the DeltaV system equipment hierarchy. To export equipment hierarchy information, use the File > Export > Equipment Hierarchy command in DeltaV Explorer on the Professional PLUS workstation. To export the equipment hierarchy, you must have the Can Configure key. For more information about manually exporting an equipment hierarchy, refer to the online help for DeltaV Explorer.

title: Export a self-signed OPC UA server certificate
main_heading: Export a self-signed OPC UA server certificate
body_text: Export a self-signed OPC UA server certificate Export the server certificate to share it with OPC UA clients. Select the OPC UA Server in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Export Certificate . The software displays the Save As dialog, enabling you to save the certificate anywhere on the Professional Plus workstation. The default location is the DeltaV\DVData\Import-Export folder. Related information Create an OPC UA server

title: Export the simulated SLS 1508 SIS configuration
main_heading: Export the simulated SLS 1508 SIS configuration
body_text: Export the simulated SLS 1508 SIS configuration On the simulation system: Make sure all SIMULATE and SIMULATE_D parameters in the configuration are disabled. Make sure the ProfessionalPLUS workstation and all Application Stations are aliased to controllers in the real system. Verify that the configuration works as desired. Record SIS-related CRCs. Export the SIS Network subsystem. Save the export file. If your SIS configuration needs to change in the future you can import the configuration back into your simulation system and make the necessary changes, then export the modified configuration for import into the real system. You do not need to export SIS modules or their containing areas. SIS modules and areas are exported as a part of the SIS Network subsystem. As a result of the above steps you should have one export file for the SIS Network subsystem. Note: Exporting the entire SIS Network is the recommended method. You can export and import SIS Network Domains, but if you have System Global Secure Parameters you must be careful. If the configuration is not stable, exporting and importing domains may cause System Global Publishers to move between slots which changes the CRCs.

title: Extend CHARM power to other baseplates
main_heading: Extend CHARM power to other baseplates
body_text: Extend CHARM power to other baseplates When CHARM Baseplates in a 96 CHARM system are installed on multiple DIN rails, CHARM Column Extenders and cables are used to extend redundant 24 VDC power and communication busses to the baseplates. The bottom column extender can be connected to CIOC carriers or to baseplates depending upon the physical location of the carrier and the baseplate. The top column extender can be connected to baseplates only. For this procedure, it is assumed that at least one CHARM Baseplate is installed on a separate DIN rail from the other baseplates and CIOC carrier. CHARM Column Extender cables are available in three lengths: 0.5 meters (1.64 feet) 1.0 meters (3.28 feet) 2.0 meters (6.56 feet) A maximum of four extender pairs can be used and only one extender pair can exceed 0.5 meters (1.64 feet). The maximum bus length ( the total length from the CIOC to the CHARM Column Terminator) is 5.5 meters (18 feet). Example installations with CHARM Column Extenders Slide together the connectors on the extender with the connectors on the carrier or baseplate. The bottom column extender can be connected to CIOC carriers or to baseplates. The top column extender can be connected to baseplates only. Connect the cables between the extenders. Connect primary to primary and secondary to secondary.

title: Extend CHARM power to other I.S. baseplates
main_heading: Extend CHARM power to other I.S. baseplates
body_text: Extend CHARM power to other I.S. baseplates When I.S. CHARM Baseplates in a 96 CHARM system are installed on multiple DIN rails, CHARM Column Extenders and cables are used to extend redundant 24 VDC power and communication busses to the baseplates. The bottom column extender can be connected to CIOC carriers or to baseplates depending upon the physical location of the carrier and the baseplate. The top column extender can be connected to baseplates only. Be sure to install a Separation Wall on all baseplates and extenders. For this procedure, it is assumed that at least one I.S. CHARM Baseplate is installed on a separate DIN rail from the other baseplates and CIOC carrier. CHARM Column Extender cables are available in three lengths: 0.5 meters (1.64 feet) 1.0 meters (3.28 feet) 2.0 meters (6.56 feet) A maximum of four extender pairs can be used and only one extender pair can exceed 0.5 meters (1.64 feet). The maximum bus length (the total length from the CIOC to the CHARM Column Terminator) is 5.5 meters (18 feet). Example I.S. Installation with CHARM Column Extenders Install a Separation Wall on the bottom extender. Slide together the connectors on the extender with the connectors on the carrier or baseplate. The bottom column extender can be connected to CIOC carriers or to baseplates. The top column extender can be connected to baseplates only. Connect the cables between the extenders. Connect primary to primary and secondary to secondary. Related information Install a Separation Wall

title: Extend power from left to right 8-wide VerticalPLUS carriers
main_heading: Extend power from left to right 8-wide VerticalPLUS carriers
body_text: Extend power from left to right 8-wide VerticalPLUS carriers Be sure that the DIN rail stops are in place on both DIN rails. Refer to “Installing the DIN Rail Stop”. This procedure is for an installation with 6 carriers. Connect a left 1-wide VerticalPLUS carrier extender to the last 8-wide carrier on the left side (carrier 3) by sliding together the 96 pin connectors on the carriers. Connect a right 1-wide VerticalPLUS carrier extender to the first 8-wide carrier on the right side (carrier 4) by sliding together the 96 pin connectors on the carriers. Connect the 25 pin D-shell (male) connector on the extender cable to the D-shell connector labeled A on the left 1-wide carrier extender and fasten the retainer screws. Connect the 25 pin D-shell connector on the other end of the cable to the D-shell connector labeled A on the right 1-wide carrier extender and fasten the retainer screws. Related information Installing the DIN Rail Stop

title: Extending power from right to left 8-wide VerticalPLUS carriers
main_heading:
Extending power from right to left 8-wide VerticalPLUS
	 carriers
body_text: Extending power from right to left 8-wide VerticalPLUS carriers This procedure is for an installation with up to 8 carriers. Note: If a 4-wide SISNet Repeater carrier is installed on the top right, there is no need for a 1-wide carrier because power can be extended from the D-shell connectors on the SISNet Repeater carrier. Connect the left 1-wide VerticalPLUS carrier extender or SISNet Repeater carrier to the last 8-wide carrier on the right side (carrier 6) by sliding together the 96 pin connectors on the carriers. Connect the right 1-wide VerticalPLUS carrier extender to the first 8-wide carrier on the left side (carrier 7) by sliding together the 96 pin connectors on the carriers. Connect the 25 pin D-shell (male) connector on the extender cable to the D-shell connector labeled A on the right 1-wide carrier extender or SISNet Repeater carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Connect the 25 pin D-shell connector on the other end of the cable to the D-shell connector labeled A on the left 1-wide carrier extender and fasten the retainer screws. Power Extended from a Left to Right Carrier and Right to Left Carrier

title: Extend LocalBus power to other Carriers
main_heading: Extend LocalBus power to other Carriers
body_text: Extend LocalBus power to other Carriers When Carriers are installed on separate DIN rails, Left and Right Extenders and cables are used to extend the LocalBus power that runs through the carriers. For this procedure it is assumed that at least one 8-Wide I/O Carrier or Power / Controller Carrier is installed on a separate DIN rail from other 8-Wide I/O Carriers. The illustration in this topic shows an 8-Wide I/O Carrier connected to the Right Extender. However, the Right Extender can be connected to a Power / Controller Carrier containing an S-series controller and power supply or a VIM / VIM 2 card and power supply. Extender cables are available in the following lengths: 0.4 meters (1.3 feet) 0.8 meters (2.6 feet) 1.1 meters (3.6 feet) 1.5 meters (4.9 feet) 1.9 meters (6.2 feet) Extending LocalBus power Slide together the connectors on a Right Extender with the connectors on the right side of the last 8-Wide I/O Carrier or Power / Controller Carrier on the first DIN rail. Slide together the connectors on a Left Extender with the connectors on the left side of the first 8-Wide I/O Carrier or Power / Controller Carrier on a separate DIN rail. Connect the cables between the Left and Right Extenders. Typically, one D-shell cable is used to make the connection; however, two cables can also be used. Connect A to A for single cables and A to A and B to B for dual cables. Related information Extending the LocalBus 8-Wide I/O Carrier specifications Power/Controller Carrier specifications Left and Right Extender specifications

title: Extend CHARM power to other baseplates
main_heading: Extend CHARM power to other baseplates
body_text: Extend CHARM power to other baseplates When CHARM Baseplates in a 96 LS CHARM system are installed on multiple DIN rails, CHARM Column Extenders and cables are used to extend redundant 24 VDC power and communication busses to the baseplates. The bottom column extender can be connected to CSLS carriers or to baseplates depending upon the physical location of the carrier and the baseplate. The top column extender can be connected to baseplates only. For this procedure, it is assumed that at least one CHARM Baseplate is installed on a separate DIN rail from the other baseplates and CSLS carrier. Be sure to install a Separation Wall on extenders connected to I.S. Baseplates. CHARM Column Extender cables are available in three lengths: 0.5 meters (1.64 feet) 1.0 meters (3.28 feet) 2.0 meters (6.56 feet) A maximum of four extender pairs can be used and only one extender pair can exceed 0.5 meters (1.64 feet). The maximum bus length ( the total length from the CSLS to the CHARM Column Terminator) is 5.5 meters (18 feet). Example installations with CHARM Column Extenders Slide together the connectors on the extender with the connectors on the carrier or baseplate. The bottom column extender can be connected to CSLS Carriers or to baseplates. The top column extender can be connected to baseplates only. Be sure to install a Separation Wall on the extender if installing the extender on an I.S. Baseplate. Connect the cables between the extenders. Connect primary to primary and secondary to secondary. Related information Install a Separation Wall

title: Diagnosing fieldbus devices
body_text: Diagnosing fieldbus devices The DeltaV Explorer, Control Studio, and Diagnostics programs as well as the H1 card itself provide a great deal of diagnostic information on fieldbus devices. H1 fieldbus Card Communication information between the card and fieldbus devices is available from a visual inspection of the H1 card. The bottom two LEDs on the H1 card reflect communication between the port and fieldbus devices on that port. A blinking yellow LED indicates that the port is communicating with fieldbus devices but either a communication problem exists with an attached fieldbus device or no function blocks are configured on the segment. If the LED is off, either the port is disabled or the H1 card is not communicating with any fieldbus devices on the port. Use the DeltaV Explorer to enable and download the port and Control Studio to create and download configuration. A solid yellow LED indicates good communication between the port and devices on that port and at least one function block is configured on the segment. DeltaV Explorer Indicators in the DeltaV Explorer tell you if an H1 port or a fieldbus device needs to be downloaded or commissioned. The on an H1 port or device means that the port or device needs to be downloaded. Right-click the port or device, and then select Download to open a dialog that lists the fieldbus configuration information to be downloaded. The on a device means that the device needs to be commissioned. To commission the device, select it from the Decommissioned device list and drag it to either the port or device placeholder. Control Studio Use Control Studio in online mode to diagnose problems with modules running in fieldbus devices. You must assign and download a module before viewing it in online mode. Open the module in Control Studio. Click View > On-line to create an online (or debug) session in which you can examine module and block parameters. A red X on a function block parameter indicates a problem with the function block. CAUTION: Any online changes affect your process because the changes are made to downloaded modules in the controller. Use extreme care when changing values or stopping the execution of an algorithm. Select the block with the red X. The Parameter View window in Control Studio displays a full list of parameters for that block. Double-click a parameter in Parameter View to open the Parameter Properties dialog for that parameter. Diagnostics Use DeltaV Diagnostics to perform the following tasks: determine if the device is commissioned check integrity on the H1 card, backup Link Master device, and ports check overall port statistics and communication statistics for each device Open DeltaV Diagnostics and click View > Details or View > Compare to quickly see the device state. If the device is not commissioned, open the DeltaV Explorer and commission the device. Then, download the port and the device. If the device is commissioned, check integrity on the port and then check port and device communication statistics. Port Integrity Typically, integrity problems originate below the node and then rise to the node level. Integrity problems are indicated by the overlay. Start by looking for a controller with the overlay and, if found, expand the controller hierarchy until you find the root cause of the problem. If a fieldbus card has an integrity problem, expand the card to see which port has the problem. Select each port and look at the port's status. Possible port status values are: Good - Good basic communications with all devices on this port No Termination on Link - This port is not terminated. Check attached cable. Link Error - PCMCIA Card problem exists. Replace the H1 card. Duplicate Address on Link - Another device is currently communicating at this port's address. No Communications on Link H1 Card Problem - Replace the H1 card. One or more function block problems on link or device problem - Expand the port and check the state of each fieldbus device on the port. Any state other than Commissioned indicates a potential problem with that fieldbus device. Port Communication Statistics The Port Statistics command provides a broad view of communication activity on the port. Right-click the port, and then select Port Statistics . In the Port Statistics dialog, look for the following: Retries Invalid responses Stack errors Timeouts Note: If any of the port statistics and communication statistics are continually increasing, a potential communications problem could exist on this port.
