To isolate the problem, investigate the communication statistics on each fieldbus device. Refer to the following section for information. Next, look at detailed port statistics. Right-click the port, and then select Display Port Detail Statistics . In the Detailed Port Statistics dialog, look for the following: Identifies Initiates Aborts Tip: Clicking the Reset Stats button resets all values to 0 and makes it easier to read the statistics. Device Communication Statistics Finally, look at communication statistics for each device. Rght-click each device, select Display Communication Statistics , and look for the following: Aborts received and sent Initiates received and sent Pcr Timeouts Livelist appearances (the number of times the device showed up as new)

title: Assign blocks to fieldbus
body_text: Assign blocks to fieldbus Now we will assign the AI block to a fieldbus device. Remember that for fieldbus, blocks can run in either the controller or the fieldbus devices. The decision about where to run the blocks is based on your requirements, and there are pros and cons to each method. Right-click the block in Control Studio and select Assign I/O > To fieldbus . (To run the blocks in a controller, select Assign I/O > To Signal Tag .) Click the Browse button and find the device to which you want to assign this block. Navigate through the controller, I/O card, port, and device to get to the blocks. Some devices may have more than one AI block because the device may be capable of outputting more than one variable. In this image, the device, PDT2, has two AI blocks: FFAI1 and FFA12. Select one of the AI blocks and click OK . Now that the block has been assigned to a device, we will configure a parameter for the device. The Using InSight Tuning with fieldbus Devices topic has information on how assigning blocks to fieldbus devices affects loop performance and how you can achieve maximum performance. Related information Deciding where to run control function blocks Using Tune with InSight

title: Assign fieldbus strategy to a node
main_heading: Assign fieldbus strategy to a node
body_text: Assign fieldbus strategy to a node Now, you assign the strategy to a node to tell the DeltaV system where it will run. A strategy can be assigned to a workstation or a controller. Generally, control strategies run in a controller. Click the Assign to Node button on the Control Studio toolbar. Select the controller to which you want to assign the module and click OK .

title: Configure fieldbus block parameters
body_text: Configure fieldbus block parameters If it is not already selected, select the AI block, and you will see its default set of parameters listed in the parameter pane. In order for the device to work properly, you must configure the device's parameters. In Control Studio, double-click Filtered by at the top of the parameter list. This opens the Parameter Filtering dialog. Click the Select All button to make all parameters visible to you. The CHANNEL and XD_SCALE parameters must be correctly configured for AI and AO blocks or a configuration error will occur when the device is downloaded. Let's take the CHANNEL parameter as an example of how to configure a parameter. Because each device may be capable of more than one measurement, when you configure an AI block, you specify which measurement you want the block to process. The value for the CHANNEL parameter tells the block which measurement to process. Double-click the CHANNEL parameter to open the Properties dialog for this parameter. The device manufacturer publishes valid values for the channels, and much of this information is available in DeltaV Books Online. Enter that value in the Value field and click OK . Now you know how to configure a parameter for a block. Experiment with Control Studio and open the Properties dialogs for other AI parameters or drag another block onto the diagram and look at its parameters. When you are ready, configure the other blocks in your control strategy. Consult the device documentation for recommended parameter values. Then, connect all inputs and outputs, assign the strategy to a node, and save and download the strategy.

title: Confirm a module's operation
body_text: Confirm a module's operation Control Studio's On-line mode is a powerful tool for confirming a module's correct operation and for diagnosing module problems. You must assign and download a module before you can view it in On-line mode. Open the module in Control Studio. On the Home tab, in the Diagram Mode group, click On-line to create an online session in which you can examine module and block parameters. If the module is operating correctly, the outputs are displayed next to the block. If there is a problem with a function block, a red X appears on the function block. To determine the source of the problem, perform the following steps: Check the BLOCK_ERR parameter (double-click a parameter to edit it) and determine if the block is out of service (OOS) or if it has a block configuration error. Among the problems that can cause a block to be out of service are misconfiguration, bad sensor input, and problems with the download. Check the status of the block's input and output parameters. For example, a status of BadNoCom indicates that information is not being sent to the block's inputs. If the block has a bad PV, verify that the correct XD_SCALE, UNITS, and RANGE are transferred. If the data has intermittent bad status, check the required macrocycle and the module execution rate. The module execution rate should be >= 2 times the actual macrocycle. Remember that if you make any changes in On-line mode, the changes are not saved in the database. Use Control Studio or Explorer to upload the changes to the database.

title: Connect fieldbus block inputs and outputs
main_heading: Connect fieldbus block inputs and outputs
body_text: Connect fieldbus block inputs and outputs Algorithms that determine how information is exchanged between devices run in the background in Control Studio. You wire the blocks together in Control Studio to create the algorithms that describe how you want the blocks to execute. The output of one block flows into another block as an input. In our example control strategy, the output of the AI block flows into the PID block as input, the output of the PID block flows into the AO block as input, and so on. To wire blocks together in Control Studio: Click the connection point where you want the wire to begin. The cursor turns into a . Hold the left mouse button down and drag the cursor to the end point. Release the left mouse button at the end point and the line is drawn between the two points. If you have trouble drawing the connections, use the Connection tool on the toolbar.

title: Download fieldbus block configuration and strategy
main_heading: Download fieldbus block configuration and strategy
body_text: Download fieldbus block configuration and strategy You have assigned the strategy to a node, saved it, reconciled differences between the device and placeholder, and commissioned the device. The changes you have made are stored in the DeltaV database but have not yet been written to the device. The DeltaV system places a blue triangle next to the device in DeltaV Explorer to indicate that the device needs to be downloaded. In DeltaV Explorer, right-click the device and select Download > fieldbus Device . DeltaV software informs you if items subordinate to this one also need to be downloaded and can verify the configuration if you choose. Make sure the modules associated with the devices on the segment have been downloaded. The module information must be sent to the H1 card before devices are downloaded. Read the important Warning and if you are sure you want to download, click Yes . When the download is complete, the blue triangle disappears from the device. There may be other blue triangles in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Download those items if you are comfortable doing so or read the DeltaV Explorer help on downloading for more information. The Express fieldbus Download option is available for faster downloads of fieldbus ports and devices during plant startup and commissioning. One port or multiple ports can be downloaded from the Express fieldbus Download dialog. Related information Downloading fieldbus segments during plant startup and commissioning

title: Save a fieldbus strategy
body_text: Save a fieldbus strategy Once you have created your control strategy and assigned it to a node, you must save it. A strategy is saved as a module. Click the Main button in Control Studio, and then click Save . In the Look in box, select the location (Area) where you want the strategy to run. Name the module and click Save .

title: Select fieldbus blocks
body_text: Select fieldbus blocks In Control Studio, click the down arrow in the list box at the top of the palette and select IO . This makes the I/O function blocks available to you. Drag the Analog Input function block from the palette to the diagram pane to create a generic AI block. The handles around the AI block indicate that it is selected. At this point, you may want to rename the AI block to make it meaningful to you. Right-click the block and select Rename .

title: Finish the FIC-101 module
body_text: Finish the FIC-101 module You have already named the module and assigned it to the controller. Open the Properties dialog for the module. On the Displays tab, enter TANK101 in the Primary Control field. The TANK101 picture does not exist yet. You will create it later. Save the module.

title: Finish configuring the MTR-101 module
body_text: Finish configuring the MTR-101 module Assign the MTR-101 module to the primary control picture TANK101. (Remember, you enter the name of the primary control picture on the Displays tab of the Properties dialog for the module. Also remember that the TANK101 picture does not exist yet. You will create it later.) Note that this module has two predefined pictures: DL_DT8 is the detail display and DL_FP is the faceplate. Change the Detail to DL_DT3 to match the number of conditions. (Remember, in a previous topic you removed the five unused condition blocks.) Assign the control module to the controller. Save the control module by clicking the Save button. (The module has already been named.) Minimize Control Studio by clicking the Minimize button in the upper right corner.

title: Finishing the process picture
body_text: Finishing the process picture For other parts of the picture, use the dynamos in the following table and arrange them as shown in the earlier illustration of the process graphic. Be sure to read the table footnotes for the block valve and regulatory valve. The topic on creating a pump using a dynamo explains how to animate the color for the regulatory valve if you have forgotten how to do so. Item Parameter Reference for Dynamic Properties Dynamo Set Dynamo Pipes No dynamic properties Pipes As needed Block valve XV-101/DC1/PV_D/CV ValvesAnim ValveHorizontalOnOff1 Regulatory valve FIC-101/PID1/PV/CV ValvesAnim ValveHorizontalControl1 You can resize a pipe by selecting the pipe, dragging one of its resizing handles, and releasing the mouse button. In fact, you can resize any graphic object, including text, by dragging the side or corner handles. Subtopics: Add the remaining dynamos to the process picture Related information Create a pump using a dynamo 1 In the Valve Dynamo dialog for the block valve, choose Animate Valve Color , and set two colors, as you did earlier for the Pump Dynamo. 2 In the Valve Dynamo dialog for the regulatory valve, choose Animate Valve Color . In the Color By dialog, choose Color by Current Value . Under the Color Threshold , select Range and set the colors as follows: 0-50 is red; 50-100 is green.

title: Finish configuring Application Station redundancy
body_text: Finish configuring Application Station redundancy Assign licenses for the Application Stations and redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server, as needed. Note: There is no reason to assign licenses to the Application Stations for DeltaV software components that are not designed to coexist with the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server feature. For example, you should not license subsystems such as Batch Executive, Batch Historian, Continuous Historian, Campaign Manager, or Remote Network on the Application Stations, because they cannot be enabled simultaneously with the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server feature. In DeltaV Explorer on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, download the Application Station. Note: If you selected the OPC DA Server and OPC Mirror option on the Redundancy tab of the Properties dialog for the Application Station, the current version of OPC Mirror must be installed on each Application Station. If a previous version of OPC Mirror is already installed on the existing Application Station, uninstall it before installing the current version on both the existing and new Application Stations. Related information Redundant DeltaV OPC Mirror

title: Finish configuring the SFC module
body_text: Finish configuring the SFC module Assign the SFC module to the primary control picture TANK101, which you will create later. Click the Assign to Node button on the toolbar and assign the SFC module to the controller. Click the Save button, and then save the SFC module as SFC-START. Quit Control Studio by clicking the Close button in the upper right corner.

title: Finish the unit modules
body_text: Finish the unit modules There are a few more things we need to do to finish the unit modules for the color tanks. For each unit module, we will perform the following tasks: Change the phase type to Controller for phases assigned to the unit module. (This will be demonstrated in a later chapter, after we create phases and assign them to units.) Assign the unit module to a node (usually the controller, but, for simulation, it may be the workstation). The easiest way to assign unit modules to a node is to drag the entire area to the node. To assign individual unit modules, there are several different methods that can be used. In the DeltaV Explorer, assignment can be done on the Tools tab of the Unit Module Properties dialog. It can also be done using the context menu ( Assign > Unit and All Contained Modules to Node ) or using the drag-and-drop method. In Control Studio, on the Home tab, in the Module group, click Assign to Node . Assign the area (EXTERIOR_PAINT) to the Alarms and Events subsystem under the workstation. This is necessary because the batch operator is only allowed to operate modules that are assigned to the Alarms and Events subsystem for the particular Operator Station. This prevents an operator from inadvertently causing an alarm condition on a module that cannot be viewed on the operator's workstation. Download the controller or workstation. To finish the unit modules, complete the following steps: Drag the EXTERIOR_PAINT area to the controller or to Assigned Modules under the Workstation in the Control Network. All the contained modules will automatically be assigned to the node. Drag the EXTERIOR_PAINT area to the Alarms and Events subsystem under the Workstation. A message appears to remind you to download the workstation's Setup Data. Click Yes to confirm that you want to assign the area. Download the node. (You may need to download the controller, the workstation, the Control Network, or the Physical Network, depending on the download status of the network elements.) At this point all the equipment entities have been defined. Now we will move on to configuring the phase logic that will be used in the process.

title: From the SOA Gateway (Application Station)
body_text: From the SOA Gateway (Application Station) Install DeltaV software as a local application station. When prompted, select Professional / Operator / Application / Base / Inter-Zone Server . Click Next . Browse to the location of the workstation configuration file you created earlier and select it. Select the application station name in the list that appears. Click Next . Complete the installation. Return to the ProfessionalPLUS workstation and download the SOA Gateway application station. The following services are installed on the SOA Gateway: Campaign Manager Web Service Recipe Exchange Web Service Monitor Service

title: From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation
body_text: From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation To set up the SOA Gateway you must first configure the application station that is going to be designated as the gateway: Open DeltaV Explorer on the DeltaV system's ProfessionalPLUS workstation. If you need to create an application station to use as the gateway, select Control Network, and then select New > Application station from the context menu. In the Properties dialog, name the application station and select other options as desired, and then click OK . Select Physical Network, and then select Properties from the context menu. In the Properties dialog, select the Gateway tab. Browse to or enter the name of the application station you want to be the gateway, and then click OK . Select File > Export > Workstation Configuration . Save the workstation configuration file.

title: Getting Started with DeltaV Hardware
body_text: Getting Started with DeltaV Hardware This section provides a brief description of the steps required for system installation. Specific information on installation steps 1–7 is included in this chapter. Specific information on step 8 is included in the topic "Checking Out and Troubleshooting Your DeltaV System". The appendices in this manual include product specifications and detailed information. The following steps for installation are listed in the most common order. You can elect to perform these steps in another order that is more convenient for your project. CAUTION: The DeltaV I/O Cards and Controller must be mounted vertically on the horizontal carrier for cooling purposes. Install the DIN rails and DeltaV Carriers. Install the DIN rails. Install the power/controller carrier and I/O interface carrier on the DIN rails. Install the DeltaV I/O Interface. Check the key settings on the I/O terminal blocks and install them on the I/O interface carrier. Connect field wiring. Install the I/O cards on the I/O interface carrier. Install the DeltaV Controller. Install the controller on the power/controller carrier. Install the DeltaV System Power Supply. Install the system power supply on the power/controller carrier. Connect the supply inputs. Install the DeltaV Workstation and Servers. Follow the instructions supplied with your workstation and Server. Install the system identifier. Follow the instructions supplied with your printer and UPS Set up the DeltaV Control Network. Install the hub or switch. Install the network cables between nodes. Connect power to the system and power up. Install the bulk power supply and connect the supply inputs. Power up the system. Check out the installation. Check cable connections. Check power supply voltages. Check indicators on the devices and cards. Test field wiring connections. Read the manual Getting Started with your DeltaV Digital Automation System for information on the software applications for the DeltaV system. Related information DeltaV Vertical Carriers Checking Out and Troubleshooting Your DeltaV System System Power Guidelines Installing Your DeltaV System

title: Grant softphaseuser permissions to the installed Soft Phase directories
main_heading: Grant softphaseuser permissions to the installed Soft Phase directories
body_text: Grant softphaseuser permissions to the installed Soft Phase directories Granting SOFTPHASEUSER Permissions to the Installed Soft Phase Directories You must grant the SOFTPHASEUSER access to the Soft Phase directories as installed on the non-DeltaV machine. On the non-DeltaV machine, run Windows Explorer. Right-click on the top-level Soft Phase directory (the 'root directory' where you installed the Soft Phase environment). Select Sharing and Security from the context menu. Click the Security tab. Add the SOFTPHASEUSER to the list of users with permission to access this folder. Give the SOFTPHASEUSER the Read & Execute and Write permissions. Click the Advanced button on the Security tab. Select the check box for Inherit from parent the permission entries that apply to child objects. Include these with entries explicitly defined here . Note: This last option gives Read & Execute permissions to the subdirectories of the 'root' Soft Phase directory (where you installed the Soft Phase environment). Click OK until all dialogs are closed.

title: Grant login permission
body_text: Grant login permission For security reasons, the Administrator needs to grant DeltaV users permission to log in to a Remote Client server. This is done through the DeltaV User Manager. To grant DeltaV users permission to log in to the server Open the DeltaV User Manager application. Select a user name, right-click, and select Properties from the context menu. In the Properties dialog, under Account Type, select the check box next to Allow Remote Desktop Logon . Click OK .

title: Hide an item's internal structure
body_text: Hide an item's internal structure Open DeltaV Explorer. Select the item (Composite Template, Control Module Class, Equipment Module Class, and Phase Class). Choose Hide Internal Structure from the context menu. Enter a password, confirm the password, and click OK .

title: Create the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller
main_heading: Create the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller
body_text: Create the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller This procedure creates the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller (either primary or additional domain controller) for use with a DeltaV domain-based system. Before starting the installation, consider the following: The built-in administrator account cannot be used when creating the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller. The network cards should all be named to match your DeltaV ACN, like DeltaVPrimary and DeltaVSecondary. This will simplify selecting the network cards later. Log on to the computer as a local administrator that is not the built-in administrator. Insert the DeltaV installation media. Select Set Up Independent DeltaV Domain Controller from the menu. If the menu does not appear, browse to the DeltaV media's DV_Extras\IDDC folder. Right click and select Run as administrator from the context menu. Fix any issues found (for example, a pending reboot needed). Cancel setup. Fix the errors. Restart setup. Select one of these choices: Add a new forest - Select this when you are creating the first domain controller for the DeltaV domain (the domain will not exist until the primary domain controller is established). Add a domain controller to an existing domain - Select this when you are creating an additional (backup) domain controller and adding it to the existing DeltaV domain. Click Next . Complete the information needed. When creating a new domain, you are providing to the setup application the information about what to name the domain and what network cards to configure. A fully qualified domain name. This names the domain. The format is DeltaV system name.System.company name.local (Where DeltaV system name , System , and company name are names you provide). When joining an existing domain (for the additional domain controllers), you are giving the software the location of the existing domain controller (as a fully-qualified domain name) and what network cards to configure. Important: Only select the DeltaV ACN network cards for your domain. Click Next . An estimate of the time is given. Click Continue to start the configuration and installation of needed components. If you do not click Continue , the installation will start in the time listed (counted down). Enter the Directory Services Restore Mode (DRSM) password. Note: The Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) password is required to be able to perform a safe mode boot option on your domain controller. DSRM allows an administrator to repair or restore an Active Directory database. Once promoted to a domain controller, a restart is required. Click Restart Now . Log in using the domain administrator. This is the same account name prefaced with the domain name ( myDomain \ MyUserName ). The account you logged in as to run the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller setup application was promoted to be a domain administrator when the computer was promoted to a domain controller. A time estimate is displayed. Click Continue to proceed with the remaining steps. Once the accounts are created, a restart is required. Click Restart Now . Log in as the same domain administrator. Enter a password for the DeltaV Services account. This sets the password for the account and click OK . The setup application continues setting the NTP services and installing any operating system updates. Once complete, review the results and click Close on the setup window. You can now create additional domain controllers or install DeltaV workstations and join them to this domain.

title: Create a DeltaV workstation in an Independent DeltaV Domain Controller environment
main_heading:
Create a DeltaV workstation in an Independent DeltaV Domain Controller
	 environment
body_text: Create a DeltaV workstation in an Independent DeltaV Domain Controller environment This procedure highlights the steps required when creating a DeltaV workstation in an Independent DeltaV Domain Controller environment. When the domain controller is an Independent DeltaV Domain Controller you must select the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller during Workstation Configuration. This will join the workstation to the existing domain. This means the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller must be configured and the domain created before you can join any DeltaV node to the domain. The first workstation you usually install is the ProfessionalPLUS. All other DeltaV workstations require that the DevData.cfg file be exported from the ProfessionalPLUS database. However, multiple DeltaV workstation installations can occur concurrently. You will simply pause at the Workstation Configuration step until the DevData.cfg file is available. Because the ProfessionalPLUS is the first workstation to complete the process, it is used as the example DeltaV node here. Tip: When installing DeltaV, you must be logged in as (at the least) a local administrator (even in a domain environment). However, if you want to use the domain administrator credentials, you can, if (and only if) the computer is already a domain member. If the computer was not joined to the domain prior to running Workstation Configuration, you are only able to log in as a local administrator. Workstation Configuration prompts you for domain administrator credentials at the point it needs to join the computer to the domain. The user who ran the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller setup application is added to the domain DeltaV Admins group. When running Workstation Configuration, at the time you are logging into the domain for the first time (after it has joined to the domain and a reboot has occurred), log in using the same user that created the IDDC (the first domain DeltaV Admins group member). Insert the DeltaV installation media into the drive on the ProfessionalPLUS computer. Select the DeltaV workstation type to install. ProfessionalPLUS ProfessionalPLUS as Remote Client Server When Workstation Configuration runs at the end of the installation, select Domain: Independent DeltaV Domain Controller . Enter or select (if the list is available) the root domain name from the FQDN you entered when creating the Independent DeltaV Domain Controller. The root domain name format adheres to Domainname.xxx ; where xxx is either com, or org or another valid domain name extension. You can verify the computer has been added to the domain by going to the domain controller and running Active Directory Users and Computers. The computer's name will be listed under DeltaV Workstations . After installation and Workstation Configuration completes, download the ProfessionalPLUS. Once the ProfessionalPLUS is created and downloaded, configure the remaining DeltaV nodes in the database, create the DevData.cfg file and use that file to finish the installation of the other workstations.

title: Identify the primary control picture associated with the control module
main_heading:
Identify the primary control picture associated with the control
	 module
body_text: Identify the primary control picture associated with the control module Three types of operator pictures are associated with control modules: the primary control picture, the faceplate, and the detail display. In Control Studio, click the Main button, point to Module , then click Properties . The Properties dialog appears. On the Displays tab, enter TANK101 in the Primary Control field. TANK101 will be the primary control picture associated with this control module. You will create TANK101 later. Note: Picture file names must be alphanumeric and cannot contain the hyphen character, begin with a number, or use a Visual Basic reserved word. Note that the fields for the detail display and faceplate are already filled in. All the control module templates in the library have pre-defined detail displays and faceplate s associated with them. Click OK . Related information Creating operator pictures in DeltaV Operate - overview

title: Implement exception reporting
body_text: Implement exception reporting When a group is added, the application can request to be notified when items in that group change value or quality. This request is made by simply setting an attribute in the an OPCGroup object and creating an event handler to process the data change. It is possible to handle these events on two levels, the OPCGroups or OPCGroup level. For this example, we will process data change notifications on the OPCGroups (OPCGroup collection) level. Make sure events are enabled by double-checking that our definition of MyGroups contains the "WithEvents" declaration. In the declaration section of the COPCServer class module, MyGroups declaration should be: Dim WithEvents MyGroups As OPCGroups Create a public function that turns on data change notification for a specific group. Public Function Subscribe(GroupName As String, Optional Status As Boolean = True) As Integer Dim TargetStatus As Boolean Dim anOPCGroupHandle As Long Subscribe = False On Error GoTo ErrorHandler 'Look up group anOPCGroupHandle = LookUpGroup(GroupName) If anOPCGroupHandle <= 0 Then MsgBox "Error - Group Not Found" Exit Function End If 'Set the group's subscribe status appropriately. Default to "True". MyGroups(GroupName).IsSubscribed = Status Subscribe = True Exit Function ErrorHandler: MsgBox "Subscribe: Error!" & vbCrLf _ & "Err.Number = " & Err.Number & vbCrLf _ & "Err.Description = " & Err.Description & vbCrLf _ & "Err.Source = " & Err.Source & vbCrLf End Function Create a private subroutine in the COPCServer class module. Private Sub MyGroups_GlobalDataChange(ByVal TransactionID As Long, ByVal GroupHandle As Long, ByVal NumItems As Long, ClientHandles() As Long, ItemValues() As Variant, Qualities() As Long, TimeStamps() As Date) Dim i As Integer 'Step through items in DataChange array For i = 1 To NumItems If Qualities(i) > 0 Then If GroupHandle = gStepHandle Then 'Put current step in Status Bar gStatusBar.Panels(1).Text = "Current Step: " & ItemValues(i) gStep = ItemValues(i) 'Check to see if its time to print the label If ItemValues(i) = DRYADD_STEP Then gDryAddTime = DateAdd("h", -6, TimeStamps(i)) End If End If End If Next i End Sub The GlobalDataChange procedure steps through the given array of items. If the Quality is good and the item is the Step of the SFC then the value is written to the status bar to let the user know the current step. In the case that the step is "DRY_ADD" the application needs to do more work. It is not allowed to call a DeltaV OPC Data Access Server function within the OnDataChange. It is also good practice to limit the length of time the OnDataChange executes. To accomplish these requirements, a timer object was added to the Main form. The timer function reads the target information and pops up a message asking the user to add the ingredient (refer to the Visual Basic Help - Timer object). You have already added the code to read the target values when the timer fires. Now add the code to check if its time to add the dry ingredient. Related information Use exception reporting in the application

title: Import a Zone topology
body_text: Import a Zone topology Now that you have collected an export .fhx file of each zone's Shared Local Areas, you must import these topologies in every system. From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation in each DeltaV system: Select File > Import > Standard DeltaV Format . Select and import a zone topology .fhx file exported from another DeltaV system. This step adds Remote Zone Areas under the Remote Zone whose topology you imported. These Remote Zone Areas correspond to the Local Shared Areas defined in the DeltaV system whose topology you imported. If a remote zone area's name you are importing duplicates an existing local or remote zone area name, a number is appended to the name to make it unique in this DeltaV system. Repeat steps 1 and 2 for every other remote DeltaV system (zone).

title: Import a CA-signed certificate and assign it to the client
main_heading: Import a CA-signed certificate and assign it to the client
body_text: Import a CA-signed certificate and assign it to the client To assign a CA-signed certificate to the server, you must send a certificate signing request to a third-party certificate authority. After receiving the signed-certificate from the CA, import it to the server. The DeltaV\DVData\Import-Export folder is the default folder for importing certificates. Select the OPC UA Client in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click the Certificate tab. Click Import . The software displays the Open dialog. Select the .pfx certificate files or browse to the correct location. The software assigns the certificates to the client. Trusted certificates are in .cer or .der format. Related information Create a DeltaV OPC UA client

title: Import a CA-signed certificate and assign it to the server
main_heading: Import a CA-signed certificate and assign it to the server
body_text: Import a CA-signed certificate and assign it to the server You import CA-signed certificates as .pfx files. Make sure the CA certificate files (.pfx files) are available on the Professional Plus workstation. DeltaV\Data\Import-Export is the default folder for importing certificates. Select the OPC UA Server in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click the Certificate tab. Click Import . The software displays the Open dialog. Select the certificate files or browse to the correct location. The software assigns the certificates to the server. Related information Create an OPC UA server

title: Import a revocation list
body_text: Import a revocation list Revocation lists identify digital certificates that have been revoked by the certificate authority. The DeltaV software enables you to import revocation lists to automatically untrust revoked certificates. Perform this procedure when you receive a revocation list from the certificate authority. Put the list in the DeltaV\DVData\Import-Export or to another location where it is available to the ProfessionalPlus workstation. Revocation lists have a .crl extension. Select the OPC UA client or server from the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click the Revocation List tab. Click Import . Browse to and select the revocation list. Then click OK .

title: Import client certificates for an OPC UA server
main_heading: Import client certificates for an OPC UA server
body_text: Import client certificates for an OPC UA server To communicate with an OPC UA client, the server needs client certificates. The certificates you import are automatically trusted by the server, enabling communication with the clients. You can import self-signed client certificates or CA-signed issuer chains. After importing a CA-signed issuer chain, any client signed by the issuer is trusted. By default, DeltaV looks for certificate files in the DeltaV\DVData\Import-Export folder. Select the OPC UA Server in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click Clients and Issuers . Click Import . Browse to the certificate files (.cer and .der). Click the certificate file and then click Open . The software adds the certificate to the Clients and Issuers list and trusts them. Related information Create an OPC UA server

title: Import the SLS 1508 configuration from the real system
main_heading:
Import the SLS 1508 configuration from the real
	 system
body_text: Import the SLS 1508 configuration from the real system On the simulation system: Set up the ProfessionalPLUS workstation and assign licenses for multi-node simulation. Create Application Stations as needed to simulate the controllers in the configuration. Set the controller alias names in Simulated Logic Solvers subsystem on the ProfesionalPLUS workstation and Application Stations to match the real system controller names. Create logic solver cards in the correct slots in the Logic Solvers subsystem. Import the SIS Network subsystem you exported from the real system (default export file name is SIS Network.fhx). Areas and SIS modules are created as required and the modules are assigned to logic solvers. Commission the logic solvers. Download the logic solvers. The DownloadProgress.log file includes the message that the logic solver download was different from the last download.

title: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solvers
body_text: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solvers This section outlines how to bulk edit Logic Solvers, which exist in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy under the SIS Network. The general procedure to bulk edit Logic Solvers is: Create and configure one Logic Solver, including the hardware alarms. Use the Logic Solver.fmt format specification file to export the Logic Solver or create your own format specification file. Copy and edit the exported Logic Solver in the bulk edit Excel template as required. Import the edited data. You must at least provide unique names in the logic_solver column for each Logic Solver. To create assigned Logic Solvers the node_name column must contain the name of a node that already exists in the database and the card_slot column must contain a node slot number that contains a Logic Solver card. To create unassigned Logic Solvers enter <NULL> in the node_name and card_slot columns. Subtopics: SLS 1508 logic solver object syntax table Related information Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver cards

title: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver cards
main_heading: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver cards
body_text: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver cards SLS 1508 logic solver cards do not have card-level parameters so you can use the Card.fmt format specification file included with the DeltaV software to export and import Logic Solver card data. If you do create your own format specification file, note that the Object type you specify is card (the standard fields for Logic Solver cards are the same as for Local I/O cards). When you create Logic Solver cards with bulk edit, remember that they use two slots (four for redundant cards) and that they must start in an odd-numbered slot. To successfully import bulk edited cards, the node to which you are assigning the cards must be defined in the database. The general procedure to bulk edit Logic Solver cards is: Create one Logic Solver card. Use the Card.fmt format specification file to export the card or create your own format specification file. Format Specification Files can allow existing card configurations to be overwritten in the database but you can prevent this by specifying information that must exist. Edit the cards in the bulk edit Excel template. Import the cards. Subtopics: SLS 1508 logic solver card object syntax table Related information Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solvers

title: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver channels
main_heading: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver channels
body_text: Bulk edit SLS 1508 logic solver channels This section outlines how to export a Logic Solver channel of one subtype, copy and edit the exported data, and then import the edited data. Because there are several Logic Solver channel subtypes that have unique fields, create a separate format specification file for each subtype you use so you can bulk edit channel parameters and alarm parameters. The general procedure to bulk edit Logic Solver channels is: Create and configure one Logic Solver. Configure one channel of each type you want to bulk edit. For each channel type, create a format specification file and export the channel. For each set of exported data, copy and edit the exported Logic Solver channel in the bulk edit Excel template as required. Import each data file. The logic_solver column must contain the name of an existing Logic Solver. The channel_slot column must not duplicate any other channel_slot value for the Logic Solver. The ls_channel_type column must contain the channel type for which the specification file was created. The device_signal_tag column must contain a unique tag. The other columns and their values depend on the type of channel you are configuring. Subtopics: SLS 1508 logic solver channel object syntax table Valid SLS 1508 logic solver channel types

title: Create a format specification file
body_text: Create a format specification file The format specification file defines the object to export and import, including the order of the data fields. The specification also defines the comment character, separator character, and the use of blank lines and columns. When you export data the output .txt files follow the field order specified in the .fmt files. Note: Format specification files from a previous release, both those provided with the software and those that you have created, should be reviewed before using them in this release of DeltaV software. The fields available for bulk editing configuration objects may change between releases. The content of sample format files may also change. To create or modify a format specification file, follow these steps: From DeltaV Explorer, select File > Format Specification . Then, select New or Edit . If you selected Edit , select a format file to edit from the Open Format Specification dialog, then click Open . The Format specification - General dialog opens. Select or verify the filename of the format specification file you are editing. Then, set the other options on the dialog as desired. Click Next . The Format specification - Select fields dialog opens. Set or verify the Object type . For the following object types a Subtype field appears: Card object - Browse to an instance in the database of the card type you want to bulk edit. Channel object - Subtypes are channel types: 100 mv input, discrete input, discrete output, and so on. The channel type must be valid for the card type you are bulk editing. Formula object - Subtypes are formulas in Procedures, Unit Processes, or Operations. HART Device object - Subtypes are Non-SIS HART device (Wired), Non-SIS HART Device (Wireless), SIS HART Device (Wired). Module object - Subtypes are either module templates or modules based on module templates. Module objects require that you enter a subtype so that information on the blocks within the module are exported and imported. If you do not correctly specify the module subtype, importing creates empty modules. For other object types specify a subtype if you need to export information specific to the subtype. The fields that appear in the Field names area depend on the object type and subtype selected. Note that for each of the object types, there are required fields (that is, fields the import file must contain to be successfully imported). The tables in the sections that explain how to bulk edit various configuration objects define the valid syntax and field values for the transferable objects. Each table has three columns: Field -- The field name as it appears in the Format Specification wizard and exported data files Valid Values -- The syntax of valid field values or a list of valid values Required for Import -- Indicates whether a field must be included in the format specification file and contain a value in the bulk edit spreadsheet for the data to be successfully imported Note: When you are editing the text files do not enclose field values in quotes. Note: You can include fields that are not required for import in your format files. However, for some objects some fields are interdependent. That is, if a field exists in the format and text import files, other related fields must also be included and must contain valid values in the import file or the import fails. Choose the fields to include in the format file. Note: Because Excel limits the number of columns in a spreadsheet, you cannot select more than 255 fields. If your module is large or complex, select only the fields you must be able to bulk edit. You must at least include the fields that are required for import. You can include other fields you need. Note that some objects have object-level parameters and alarms that you can include in the format specification file if you need to. Click Next . The Format specification - Field order dialog appears. Order the fields if you desire. If you are creating the format specification to import an existing data file, order the fields and insert skip columns as required to match the existing data. Use skip columns as placeholders if your import file contains data that you do not want or need to import. The number and order of fields in the format file must match the import data file exactly. If they do not match, importing the data results in errors. Click Next . The Format specification - Must exist dialog appears. Depending on the object for which you are creating a specification file, there may be one or more fields listed in this dialog. Select a field to allow imports only when data in the selected fields already exist in the configuration database. Click Finish . The software saves the format file.

title: Install the Bulk Edit Excel Add-in
main_heading: Install the Bulk Edit Excel Add-in
body_text: Install the Bulk Edit Excel Add-in Note: The Bulk Edit Excel Add-in requires Excel 2013 software and Visual Basic for Applications. Open Excel. Select File > Options . Click Add-Ins . Make sure Excel Add-Ins is selected in the Manage field, and then click Go . On the Add-Ins dialog, click Browse and navigate to \DeltaV\DVData\BulkEdit . Select BulkEdit_Support.xla and click OK . Click OK on the Add-Ins dialog. Close and relaunch Excel. Loading the add-in creates the Bulk Edit menu command and the DeltaV Bulk Edit toolbar on the DeltaV group on the Excel Add-Ins tab. The BulkEdit menu has the following selections: Select Entry — Select from list of valid entries. Header Comments — Display header comments. Open Data File — Open a user-defined text export file. Save Data File — Save the current worksheet as a tab-delimited text file. Bulk Edit Help — Open the Bulk Edit help file. The DeltaV Bulk Edit toolbar buttons invoke the same commands as the menu. You can edit the data files in a text editor, but the Bulk Edit Excel Add-in has several features that simplify bulk editing. Note: The output data .txt files from the User-Defined Export utility are in Unicode. The sample .txt files in the BulkEdit directory are plain ASCII. The User-Defined Import utility accepts both Unicode and ASCII files. Though you can edit the Unicode data files in a text editor, it is much easier to open and edit the text files from the Bulk Edit Excel Add-in. If you use a text editor be sure to use one that is Unicode compliant on the data files you export. Preserve the field separators in the data and save the file with Unicode encoding.

title: Import an OPC UA server certificate to the client’s list of issuers
main_heading:
Import an OPC UA server certificate to the client’s list of
	 issuers
body_text: Import an OPC UA server certificate to the client’s list of issuers To communicate with an OPC UA server, the client needs one or more trusted server certificates. At the client level, import the certificate chain. Issuer certificates enable trust of all servers from that issuer. You can import a specific self-signed certificate from the client’s physical device. By default, DeltaV looks for certificate files in DeltaV\DVData\Import-Export . Select the OPC UA Client in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click Issuers . Click Import . Browse to the certificate file (.der or .cer). Click the certificate file and then click Open . The software adds the certificate to the Issuers list. Related information Create a DeltaV OPC UA client Import a self-signed server certificate to the client physical device

title: Import a self-signed server certificate to the client physical device
main_heading:
Import a self-signed server certificate to the client physical
	 device
body_text: Import a self-signed server certificate to the client physical device Select the client physical device (PDT) from the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click the Primary tab (or Secondary tab for a redundant client). Click Import . This is the file you exported from the server and saved to DVData\Import-Export . Browse to the certificate file. These files have a .cer or .der extension. Click the certificate file and then click Open . The software displays the name, valid dates and thumbprint of the certificate on the Primary or Secondary tab. Related information Create a DeltaV OPC UA client

title: Import the simulated SLS 1508 SIS configuration
main_heading: Import the simulated SLS 1508 SIS configuration
body_text: Import the simulated SLS 1508 SIS configuration On the real system: Create controller placeholders if they do not already exist. Create logic solver cards in the correct place in the controllers if the cards do not already exist. Import the SIS Network subsystem you exported from the simulation system (default export file name is SIS Network.fhx). Areas and SIS modules are created as required and the modules are assigned to logic solvers. Commission controllers if they are not already commissioned. Download the controllers. Commission logic solvers. Download the logic solvers. The DownloadProgress.log file includes the message that the logic solver download was different from the last download. Record SIS-related CRCs and verify they are identical to the CRCs recorded in the simulation system. Perform a functional test on the real system. Note: An explanation of Functional Testing is beyond the scope of this topic. Functional Testing is covered in the DeltaV SIS Safety Manual.

title: Import the Startup.fhx and Simulation.fhx files
main_heading: Import the Startup.fhx and Simulation.fhx files
body_text: Import the Startup.fhx and Simulation.fhx files The following procedure describes how to import the Startup.fhx file, which contains the simulation control modules, three control module classes, and two phase classes. Importing the Complete.fhx file is similar, but involves a few additional considerations, which are detailed in additional steps after the procedure. Start DeltaV Explorer. The new database opens. Import the Startup.fhx file using the File > Import > Standard DeltaV Format command. Browse to the DeltaV\Samples\BatchTutorial directory and select the Startup.fhx file. (If importing Complete.fhx, refer to the additional steps.) A message may appear stating that the database already contains an object with the same name and asking if you want to update that object with the one from the import file. Click No to All so that the latest database object names are used. Import the Simulation.fhx file. Note: Some of the imported phases and modules contain references to named sets and other modules that we will create later in the tutorial. Ignore the warnings in the import log that refer to these import errors. Also ignore any warnings about import of the workstation name not being successful. If you are using a controller, commission the imported controller, CTLRnn, by clicking Decommissioned Controllers, selecting the controller you want to use, and dragging that controller from the right pane to CTLRnn. (If you have I/O cards, click NO when asked to autosense them.) Download the configuration by selecting Physical Network, right-clicking, and then selecting Download > Physical Network from the context menu. If you check the configuration, there might be several messages that refer to some modules not having any blocks, and so on. Click Download anyway. Related information Additional steps after importing Complete.fhx

title: Improve batch archiving speed
body_text: Improve batch archiving speed The speed at which batches are archived can be affected by the number of entries in the AdminLog table in the DVHisDB database. The AdminLog table contains records of batches, campaigns, and events that have been archived or deleted and records when the Batch Historian has stopped or started. Periodically check the number of entries in the AdminLog table. If the number of entries is greater than 20,000, export and delete all admin data to improve archive performance. The time it takes archive batches rises exponentially with the number of entries in the AdminLog. Check the number of entries in the Adminlog table in DVHisDB Start SQL Server Management Studio. Connect to the Batch Historian Server node. Expand the Historian server node name. Expand the Databases folder below the Batch Historian SQL Server. Expand the DVHisDB folder. Right-click on the dbo.AdminLog and click Open Table . The application displays the number of entries. Export the AdminLog table entries from DVHisDB Start SQL Server Management Studio. Connect to the Batch Historian Server node. Expand the Batch Historian server node name. Expand the Databases folder below the Batch Historian SQL Server. Right-click DVHisDB database and click Tasks , then click Export Data . Select the SQL Native Client date source and DVHisDB as the database. Select the Destination preference (for example, Excel) and a file path to store the file. Click Copy data from one or more tables or views . Select Source Table [DVHisDB].[dbo].[AdminLog] by checking the appropriate box. Click Execute immediately , and then click Finish . Locate the output file and make sure the export was created successfully. Delete old entries in the Adminlog table for DVHisDB Run the following sql query to delete records that have been exported. The example below deletes all records in the last three months. delete from AdminLog where occurTime < dateadd(month, -3, GETDATE ())

title: Improve MQ, MX, PK, SX, SQ, or SZ controller or Ethernet I/O card performance
main_heading:
Improve 
	 MQ, MX, 
	 PK, SX, SQ, or SZ controller
		or Ethernet I/O card performance
body_text: Improve MQ, MX, PK , SX, SQ, or SZ controller or Ethernet I/O card performance The Controller Performance dialog helps identify potential performance issues in MQ, MX, PK , SX, SQ, and SZ controllers or Ethernet I/O cards (EIOC) . To open the Controller Performance dialog, right-click a controller, and then select Time Utilization Chart from the shortcut menu. Performance Tips Control Control performance represents the amount of load on the controller as a result of module execution. Control loading can be reduced by lowering module execution rates. For example, a module that executes at a scan rate of 200 ms will result in five times the control load as a module configured with a scan rate of one second. Verify that modules are not executing faster than they need to be, based on process characteristics. Comms Communication performance represents the amount of controller resources consumed to transmit and receive data over the controller’s Ethernet networks. This includes both the primary and secondary active control networks. For the SZ controller model, this also includes the Local Safety Network and the MODBUS port, if enabled. Communication loading can be reduced by removing parameters from displays, eliminating controller-to-controller references, and setting the scan rate appropriately, based on process characteristics, for all types of remote network I/O, such as Zone 1 and Zone 2 I/O or CHARMs I/O cards.

title: Include OPC constants
body_text: Include OPC constants The opcconst.txt file declares constants for Visual Basic that are defined in the OPC specification. They are provided as part of this example. As the specification is revised these constants are subject to change and should be reviewed accordingly. To add a text file to the project, select Add File from the Project menu. Change the file type to All Types (*.*) Select the opcconst.txt file, and then click Open . The project window shows a new module named OPC Constants. To save the new project, select Save Project from the File menu. Related information OPC constants for Visual Basic Create a class for OPC

title: Increase the space allocated for Version Control data files
main_heading: Increase the space allocated for Version Control data files
body_text: Increase the space allocated for Version Control data files The data files that support the Version Control Database are configured to automatically grow as needed with unrestricted file growth. However, it is possible in some circumstances for the file space requirements to increase so quickly that the files are not automatically grown to meet the need. The Timeout expired message is a possible indication of this condition. If you receive a Timeout expired message, check the file size and increase it if necessary using the following procedure: Click Start > Programs > Microsoft SQL Server > SQL Server Management Studio . Browse to the Version Control database (for example, VCAT_DeltaV_System). With the database name selected, right-click and select Properties . On the Files page, review the space allocated to vcat_data, vcat_data2 and vcat_data3. To increase any of the file sizes, click the Space allocated (MB) field. Enter a file size twice the original size shown in the Space allocated column. Click OK to exit the dialog and save your changes. Close SQL Server Management Studio.

title: Initiate a manual switchover
body_text: Initiate a manual switchover From DeltaV Diagnostics, a user with the Diagnostic Key can initiate a manual switchover, in which the standby assumes the role of active DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. To manually initiate a switchover, select the Application Station with DeltaV OPC Data Access Server, and then click Redundancy Switchover on the Tools menu. After a switchover event that occurs when the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option is disabled, the standby DeltaV OPC Data Access Server will take over as the active DeltaV OPC Data Access Server, but the other DeltaV OPC Data Access Server will not re-establish itself as the standby DeltaV OPC Data Access Server until the Application Station where it runs is restarted. This is true for a manual switchover, as well as for an unplanned switchover. To bring the other DeltaV OPC Data Access Server into error-free, standby status, you must restart the Application Station where the red Error light is flashing in the DeltaV Status window. Related information Using the DeltaV Status Window on the Application Stations Using the unattended reboot option

title: Inject field power to LS CHARMs
main_heading: Inject field power to LS CHARMs
body_text: Inject field power to LS CHARMs The baseplates' injected power bus that supports 24 VDC or 120/230 VAC can be used in installations with many isolated LS CHARMs. This bus receives power through the CHARM Address Terminal. If 24 VDC power is used, connect two separate bulk power supplies to a redundancy module to create a redundant common power distribution bus for redundant power to field devices. Connect the AC power that is feeding the bulk power supplies to surge suppression/filter devices as shown in the following image. Connect the common redundant power distribution bus to the Address Terminal through a 10 A fuse to create a 12-channel, system-powered baseplate. Field power injection for LS CHARMs Ground the connections as shown in the image.

title: Inserting System Power
body_text: Inserting System Power To decide when to use external system power, calculate the power used per position on the carrier. Add these values to determine if they exceed the power supply’s capabilities. If the calculation at a given position exceeds the power supply’s capabilities: Locate the power jumper that is just before this position (count from the power supply end). Insert additional power at this node. If multiple power supplies are used, be sure they are grounded at the same point. Remove the jumper. Warning: Removing the jumper removes all 12 VDC power to all cards on all downstream carriers. When 12 VDC power is removed, cards are unable to hold the last value. Insert 12 VDC power: + to the center terminal - to the - terminal Remove Jumper to Insert Additional System Power

title: Installing the 2-Wide Power Controller Carrier
body_text: Installing the 2-Wide Power Controller Carrier To install the 2-wide power/controller carrier Refer to 2-Wide Power/Controller Carrier Installation . Install the DIN rail at the appropriate location. Connect each power/controller carrier to any adjacent carriers by sliding the 48-pin connectors on the sides of the carriers together. Turn the screws counter-clockwise on the power/controller carrier to disengage the latch. Place the carrier on the rail and tighten the screws clockwise to latch. Note: The middle two screws are for G-rail mounting and the upper and lower screws are for T-rail mounting. 2-Wide Power/Controller Carrier Installation Note: 2-wide carriers should be installed to the left of any 8-wide carriers.

title: Installing the 4-Wide Power Controller Carrier
body_text: Installing the 4-Wide Power Controller Carrier No tools are required to install the P-series 4-wide carrier on the DIN rail. The orange locking device (seen along the top and bottom of the carrier) holds the carrier in place. When the orange locking device is exposed along the top of the carrier, the carrier is unlocked and can slide along the carrier. Install the DIN rail at the appropriate location. With the carrier lock open (orange tab at the top of the carrier should be up), place the carrier onto the DIN rail. Connect each power/controller carrier to any adjacent carriers by sliding the 48-pin connectors on the sides of the carriers together. When in place, push the orange carrier lock down to lock the carrier in place on the DIN rail.

title: Installing the 8-Wide I/O Interface Carrier
body_text: Installing the 8-Wide I/O Interface Carrier To install the 8-wide I/O interface carrier 8-Wide I/O Interface Carrier Installation Install the DIN rail at the appropriate location. Turn the screws counter-clockwise on the I/O interface carrier to disengage the latch. Place the carrier on the rail and tighten the screws clockwise to latch. The middle two screws are for G-rail mounting and the upper and lower screws are for T-rail mounting. If you are installing I/O interface carriers on separate rails, connect them with the LocalBus cable from the 48-pin connector on the right side of one carrier to the 48-pin connector on the left side of the next carrier. title: Install an 8-Wide I/O Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install an 8-Wide I/O Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install an 8-Wide I/O Carrier on the DIN rail The 8-Wide I/O Carrier holds up to eight simplex or four redundant S-series I/O cards. It has connectors for providing separate primary and secondary 24 VDC field power to redundant cards and other connectors for providing 120/230 AC and 24 VDC field power to individual cards. If the carrier has been installed and then removed from the DIN rail, turn the two screws on the front of the carrier counter-closewise to reengage the latch before reinstalling the carrier. The 8-Wide I/O Carrier installs on horizontal T-type DIN rails. No screws are required to install the 8-Wide I/O Carrier on the DIN rail. Connectors on both sides of the carrier connect with adjacent carriers to form the LocalBus. Installing an 8-Wide I/O Carrier Align the carrier against a T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place. Connect the carrier to any adjacent carriers by sliding together the connectors on the sides of the carriers. Connect the shield ground bar on one carrier to chassis ground. The carriers pass the shield on to adjacent carriers. There is no need to make more than one shield ground connection.

title: Wire the System Power Supply's alarm relay contact
main_heading: Wire the System Power Supply's alarm relay contact
body_text: Wire the System Power Supply's alarm relay contact The System Power Supply's alarm relay contact is closed during normal operation. Wire the alarm relay contacts as shown in the following image. Note that this image shows the alarm relays in the unpowered (shelf) condition.

title: Install and connect a Pepperl+Fuchs Field Barrier
main_heading: Install and connect a Pepperl+Fuchs Field Barrier
body_text: Install and connect a Pepperl+Fuchs Field Barrier The following image shows the connectors on the Field Barrier. Field Barrier for four devices Securely attach the Field Barrier at the desired location. For the trunk segment connection: connect the positive (+) segment wire to the positive, connect the negative (-) segment wire to the negative, and connect the segment shield (S) to the S. Remove the shorting jumpers (1B, 2B) so that the trunk (S) shields are isolated from, not connected to the Field Barrier case. For each device connection: connect the positive (+) spur wire to the positive, connect the negative (-) spur wire to the negative, and connect the shield wire (S) to the S. The spur (S) shields must be connected to the Field Barrier case and isolated at the device in the field. The best way to ground the output shields at the barrier is with a mechanical connection through a metal gland or bar at the barrier. If this Field Barrier is at the end of the segment, the terminator switch S1 should be in the On position. If this is not the end of the segment, ensure that the terminator switch S1 is in the Off position. If the segment continues and connects to another Field Barrier, continue the trunk segment by connecting the trunk out connections to the next Field Barrier and proceed with steps 3, 4, and 5. Ensure that the shorting jumpers (1B, 2B) are removed on all Field Barriers, so that the trunk (S) shields are isolated from, not connected to, the Field Barrier case. If this Field Barrier is the end of the segment, ensure that the terminator switch S1 is in the On position. Verify the installation with the segment checkout procedure. Related information Using the segment checkout procedure to verify the installation Example Intrinsically Safe application with the Field Barrier

title: Install the I/O cards on the carrier
main_heading: Install the I/O cards on the carrier
body_text: Install the I/O cards on the carrier The I/O cards install in the slots labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4 on the carrier. Each slot has four keys labeled A, B, C, and D that are used to configure the slot to allow only a specific card type to be installed. In hazardous locations the I/O cards should not be removed or inserted into the carrier unless the input power has been de-energized for at least one minute. Card slot and key on the carrier Locate the slot into which you want to install the I/O card. Break off the appropriate keys with a screwdriver. Keying assignments Card Carrier keys to be removed Zone 1 Discrete I/O B and D Zone 1 Analog I/O A and C Note: A key replacement kit is included with each carrier to reconfigure the slots. Align the connectors on the back of the I/O card with the connectors on the carrier and push to attach the I/O card to the carrier. Tighten the two mounting screws on the card with a 3 mm hex-head wrench.

title: Install the carrier
body_text: Install the carrier Zone 1 Carrier dimensions Use four mounting screws to mount the carrier to the back plate of an enclosure suitable for your application. The mounting screws are not supplied by Emerson. Refer to the document 12P3292, DeltaV Type KJ7000 Series Zone 1 I/O System Installation Instructions for enclosure requirements. This document can be found on the DeltaV Documentation Library DVD. This document is in Portable Document Format (PDF). A letter (A-Z) is appended to the filename and is incremented for each release of the document. Related information Zone 1 Enclosure specifications

title: Install CHARMs
body_text: Install CHARMs CHARMs install in terminal blocks on the CHARM Baseplate. Installing a CHARM Note: Although CHARMs can be installed in any location, it is good engineering practice to separate low voltage DC signals from high voltage AC signals. To ensure a safe working environment, it is recommended that you wire AC signals to a different enclosure from DC signals . Open the latch on a terminal block. Insert a CHARM into the terminal block and push the CHARM until the latch closes. Note: Most CHARM terminal blocks are automatically keyed to the first CHARM installed. However, the CHARM Thermocouple mV Terminal Block has a fixed key setting and cannot be reset.

title: Install a CHARM I/O Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install a CHARM I/O Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install a CHARM I/O Carrier on the DIN rail The CHARM I/O carrier holds redundant CHARM I/O Cards (CIOCs). It has redundant 24 VDC connectors for providing power to the CIOCs, to the CHARMs, and to the field devices, redundant (primary and secondary) ethernet ports for connection to the control network, and redundant (primary and secondary) cascade ports for daisy-chaining up to 16 CIOCs. No tools are required to install the CHARM I/O carrier on the DIN rail. A latch on the back of the carrier snaps it into place on the DIN rail. Connectors on the bottom of the carrier connect with connectors on the first CHARM Baseplate. Installing a CIOC Carrier Align the carrier against a T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place.

title: Install the Control Network Cables
body_text: Install the Control Network Cables Make and test the required Control Network cables. See the section, "Control Network Specifications" for cable guidelines and specifications. Select the appropriate cable type on the cable test tool and follow the detailed instructions in the test tool’s manual. You must connect the test equipment to both ends of the cable to test it properly. The testing tool checks each cable based on its type and issues a Pass or Fail reading. Make sure the cable passes each test. The tests supported by the Microtest PentaScanner testing tool include the following: Cable mapping Length Crosstalk Attenuation Attenuation-to-crosstalk ratio Impedance Loop resistance Capacitance CAUTION: Substandard cables can create serious communication problems. Make sure all cables meet the specifications listed in the "Control Network Specifications" section. If you have a simplex Control Network, connect the unshielded end of a network cable to the twisted pair port on the primary Network Interface Card (NIC) and connect the shielded end of the cable to the primary hub as shown in the following figure. Simplex Control Network Cable Connections Note: For hub-to-hub connections, one end of the cable must have unshielded connectors. For redundant Control Networks, be sure to verify the NIC binding order to differentiate between the primary and secondary NICs. If you have a redundant Control Network, connect the unshielded end of a network cable to the twisted pair port on the workstation’s primary NIC and connect the shielded end of the cable to the primary hub as shown in Redundant Control Network Cable Connections . Connect another cable from the twisted pair port on the workstation’s secondary NIC to the secondary hub. It is helpful to identify the Control Network cables with color-coded boots. Emerson recommends the following conventions: a yellow color-coded boot for the primary Control Network cable and a black color-coded boot for the secondary Control Network cable. Note: Make sure you are consistent in your primary and secondary network connections so they are not crosswired. Redundant Control Network Cable Connections Note: For hub-to-hub connections, one end of the cable must have unshielded connectors Connect network cables from the hub(s) to the RJ45 connectors on the bottom of each controller. The front connector is for the primary Control Network and the rear connector is for the secondary Control Network. Refer to the following figure to locate the connectors. Control Network Cable Connections for a Simplex Controller

title: Install the CPU on the carrier
main_heading: Install the CPU on the carrier
body_text: Install the CPU on the carrier In hazardous locations the CPU should not be removed or inserted into the carrier unless the input power has been deenergized for at least one minute. Locate the slot labeled CPU on the carrier. Align the connectors on the back of the CPU with the connectors on the carrier and push to attach the CPU to the carrier. Tighten the two mounting screws on the CPU with a 3 mm hex-head wrench.

title: Installing the DeltaV Controller
body_text: Installing the DeltaV Controller For simplex controller systems, the controller mounts on the right slot of the 2-wide power/controller carrier. Note: Refer to the DeltaV Power and Grounding manual for information on proper configuration of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) to back up the controller power during short-term power outages. The UPS allows the controller to continue operating and to maintain current process data even when AC main power is down. Refer to the UPS manufacturer’s specifications for all other UPS information. Align the connectors on the back of the controller with the connectors on the right slot of the 2-wide power/controller carrier and push to attach. Tighten the mounting screw. Controller Installation Related information Controller Specifications Controller Redundancy

title: Installing the DeltaV System Power Supply
main_heading: Installing the DeltaV System Power Supply
body_text: Installing the DeltaV System Power Supply The system power supply takes line power or power from a bulk power supply and converts it to 12 VDC power to drive the controller and I/O cards. The system power supply mounts on either slot of the 2-wide power/controller carrier. For mounting on a 4-wide power/controller carrier refer to Appendix M DeltaV Vertical Carriers. This section describes the connections for a simplex system power supply. Refer to Appendix E System Power Supply Specifications for system power supply specifications and for details on redundancy. Refer to the figures following the steps for more information. Connect the input supply wires to the input power connection on the top of the system power supply. Figure 2-15 shows input supply wiring for the system power supply (AC/DC). Simplex Wiring Diagram for System Power Supply (AC/DC) shows the input supply wiring for the system power supply (Dual DC/DC). If you have secondary system power supplies, connect the input supply drops to each system power supply as shown in Appendix E System Power Supply Specifications. Warning: Always remove input power to the supply before connecting or disconnecting the input power connection. The connector should not interrupt current flow and could be damaged if actuated under a load condition. Refer to Appendix J Power Guidelines for more information. Simplex Wiring Diagram for System Power Supply (AC/DC) Redundant Wiring Diagram for System Power Supply (AC/DC) Note: If you are using a Two-Wide Power Carrier and redundant AC-to-DC power supplies, connect only one of the power supplies to protective earth. Refer to Appendix J Power Guidelines for power supply and grounding overviews. Simplex Wiring Diagram for System Power Supply (Dual DC/DC) Note: Do not connect the ground terminal on the power carrier when powering the dual DC/DC system power supply from a 12 VDC supply. Install alarm contact wiring as shown in the following figure. System Power Supply Alarm Contact Wiring (Unpowered Condition) Note: The alarm relay contact is closed during normal operation. The alarm relay is shown open (unpowered condition) in the following figure. Align the system power supply with the connector on the 2-wide power/controller carrier and push to attach, as shown in the following figure. Tighten the mounting screw. System Power Supply Installation Related information DeltaV Vertical Carriers System Power Supply Specifications Power Guidelines

title: Installing the DeltaV Workstation
body_text: Installing the DeltaV Workstation To install the DeltaV Workstation, connect the workstation components, install the DeltaV System Identifier (one per system), install the printer (if used), and install the UPS (if used). Connect the workstation and its associated peripherals to one power distribution and system ground. After hardware installation, refer to the DeltaV media pack installation pamphlet for information on installing DeltaV software on the workstation. To install the workstation Follow the instructions supplied with your workstation to connect the monitor, keyboard, and mouse to the central processing unit (CPU). Refer to the documentation supplied with your workstation for details on the I/O ports If the DeltaV label is not installed on your workstation monitor, apply it to the lower right corner of the monitor faceplate. Install the system identifier on the Universal Serial Bus (USB). Workstation Installation Refer to the documentation supplied with your printer for hardware installation information.
