title: Installing the DIN Rail Stop
body_text: Installing the DIN Rail Stop Vibration will cause the vertical carriers to slip down on the DIN rail and disconnect from the carrier above it. Before installing the carriers, install a DIN rail stop to prevent the carriers from slipping. The stop should be at the lowest position on the DIN rail. The DIN rail stop (KJ4010X1-BS1) can be purchased from Emerson. DIN Rail Stop Be sure the arrow on the front of the stop is pointing upward towards the device. If the arrow is pointing downwards away from the device, the screws on the DIN rail stop could damage pins extending from the device. First hook the end with the deeper notch over the DIN rail and then hook the end with the more shallow notch over the other side of the DIN rail. Screw the stop onto the DIN rail being careful not to overtighten the screws. Be sure that both sides of the DIN rail stop are properly secured. The torque limits are specified on the DIN rail stop.

title: Install a DIN Rail Stop
body_text: Install a DIN Rail Stop Vibration may cause baseplates to slip down on the DIN rail. Install a DIN Rail Stop after the Column Terminator to prevent slippage. DIN Rail Stop Be sure the arrow on the top of the DIN Rail Stop is pointing upwards. This prevents potential damage from the screws on the stop. Hook the end with the deeper notch over the DIN rail and then hook the end with the more shallow notch over the other side of the DIN rail. Screw the stop onto the DIN rail being careful not to overtighten the screws. Be sure that both sides of the DIN rail stop are properly secured. The torque limits are specified on the DIN rail stop.

title: Installing Extender Cables
body_text: Installing Extender Cables This section applies to horizontal and Legacy Vertical carriers. For VerticalPLUS carriers, refer to “Extending LocalBus Power to Other Carriers.” When carriers are installed on separate DIN rails, extender cables are used to extend LocalBus power. Extender cables connect to one-wide carriers on the left and right sides of the 2-wide and 8-wide carriers. Note: The 8-wide carriers must be left-aligned when using extender cables. A standard installation uses one extender cable; however, dual extender cables can also be used. The following procedure is for a standard installation that uses one carrier extender cable. To install carrier extender cables Install the right and left-side one-wide extender cable carriers by sliding together the 48 pin connectors on the sides of the carriers. Connect the 44-pin D-shell (male) connector on the extender cable to the top D-shell connector labeled A on the right-side carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Connect the 44-pin D-shell connector on the other end of the cable to the top D-shell connector labeled A on the left-side carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Related information Extending LocalBus Power to Other Carriers

title: Install the Fieldbus Power Hub components
main_heading: Install the Fieldbus Power Hub components
body_text: Install the Fieldbus Power Hub components Fieldbus Power Hub with four redundant segments and a Diagnostics Module Attach the top latch of the fieldbus motherboard onto the DIN rail and push it into place. Tighten the two DIN rail latching screws until the motherboard is held securely onto the rail. Plug the Fieldbus Power Supply Modules (FBPS-1.23.500) and the Diagnostic Module on to the motherboard. Secure the modules to the motherboard by depressing the two latching levers on each module.

title: Install the first CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the first CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail
body_text: Install the first CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail The first CHARM Baseplate holds Address Plug one and a bank of 12 CHARM Terminal Blocks. The first CHARM Baseplate connects to a CHARM I/O Carrier on the DIN rail. No tools are required to install a CHARM Baseplate onto the DIN rail. For this procedure it is assumed that a CHARM I/O Carrier is installed on the DIN rail. Installing the first baseplate Hold the first CHARM Baseplate beneath the CHARM I/O carrier installed on the DIN rail and notice how the connectors on the top of the baseplate interlock with the connectors on the bottom of the CHARM I/O carrier. Align and fit the connectors together as you snap the CHARM Baseplate onto the DIN rail. A latch on the back of the baseplate snaps it into place on the DIN rail.

title: Installing the 8-Wide Legacy Vertical I/O Interface Carriers
main_heading: Installing the 8-Wide Legacy Vertical I/O Interface Carriers
body_text: Installing the 8-Wide Legacy Vertical I/O Interface Carriers Refer to the following figure when performing these steps. 8-Wide Legacy Vertical I/O Interface Carrier Installation Mount the DIN rail at the appropriate location. Connect each 8-wide carrier to any adjacent carriers by sliding the 96-pin connectors at the top or bottom of the carriers together. Hold the carrier in position to ensure that it does not fall. Turn the screws counter-clockwise to disengage the latch. With the carrier on the rail, tighten the screws clockwise to latch. Note: The middle two screws are for G-rail mounting and the outer screws are for T-rail mounting. If you are mounting 8-wide carriers on separate rails, use the bottom cable extender for a left-to-right bridge and the top cable extender for a right-to-left bridge. Install ground wiring as shown in the following figure. For a good connection, use a signal ground cable and a block spade terminal, sized for AC/DC system power. Ground Wiring for System Power Supplies Related information Cables for Legacy Vertical Systems

title: Install and uninstall the Campaign Manager Operator Interface
main_heading:
Install and uninstall the Campaign Manager Operator
	 Interface
body_text: Install and uninstall the Campaign Manager Operator Interface To install the Campaign Manager Operator Interface, insert the DeltaV installation disk #1 and browse to DV_Extras\Campaign Manager Operator Interface folder. Run Setup.exe. Note: When installing CMOI on a non-DeltaV node, a minimum of Windows 7 or Windows Server 2008 is required. To uninstall the Campaign Manager Operator Interface, go to Programs and Features on the workstation where the application is installed. Select Campaign Manager Operator Interface from the list. Click Change/Remove and follow any dialogs presented. Note: Campaigns will continue to run; however, you cannot control any campaigns (for example, start or stop a campaign) from this workstation until you have reinstalled Campaign Manager Operator Interface. Batches can be controlled using DeltaV Operate or Batch Operator Interface.

title: Installing a Redundant Controller
body_text: Installing a Redundant Controller Note: A simplex controller cannot be made redundant by using the following steps after VCAT is enabled. Assign an appropriate redundancy license to the simplex controller you want to make redundant in DeltaV Explorer. Plug in a second 2-wide carrier to the left of the current 2-wide carrier. Ensure that it has the correct pins and supports redundancy. Insert the appropriate power supply in the left slot of the left 2-wide carrier and plug in the power cord to supply power. Insert a controller (the controller type should match what is already in the right 2-wide carrier) into the right slot of the left 2-wide carrier. The added controller's Power LED should turn on and the Error LED should blink for a few seconds. Then, all 6 of the LEDs should turn on for about 2 seconds, followed by the LEDs turning off except for the Power LED, which should always remain on. At this point, the Standby LED and the two communications LEDs should start to blink (Standby Controller becomes commissioned). Observe that the LEDs behave as described; the LEDs are the controller's tell-tales. Download the ProfessionalPLUS workstation in DeltaV Explorer. Download the setup data to the controller. The two communications LEDs should continue to blink for a few minutes and the Standby LED should turn on solid (Standby Controller becomes configured). The Standby Controller is now ready to take over if the Active Controller fails.

title: Install the Batch Historian software
body_text: Install the Batch Historian software To install the Batch Historian server and the Historian Administration Tool, complete the following steps: Insert the DeltaV Installer disk into the drive. From the DeltaV installation menu, select Other DeltaV Products . If the menu does not appear, select Start > Run , navigate to the \DV_Extras\BH_Server folder on the DeltaV Installation disk #1, and run the setup.exe program. From the next screen, select Batch Historian Server . Accept the defaults for the dialogs that appear during the installation. Microsoft SQL Server Standard is required to run the Batch Historian server. If not already installed, you are prompted to install it. To install Microsoft SQL Server Standard, insert the SQL Server Standard disk into the drive. When done, the SQL installation program reboots the system. After the system restarts, repeat t_installingthebatchhistoriansoftware.html#t_installingthebatchhistoriansoftware__step_C48A264467194113A502A3AD6EF2F9F2 through t_installingthebatchhistoriansoftware.html#t_installingthebatchhistoriansoftware__step_F92DD7258D9B43329DB663A53BC93D57 above. After the Batch Historian software has been installed, click Yes to reboot the system. During the installation of Batch Historian Server, the status of the workstation to which modules are assigned (the Virtual Controller) shows "No Configuration", even if modules are assigned. After rebooting, the Virtual Controller is restored. Note: When renaming a Batch Historian workstation, you must synchronize the new DeltaV workstation name (changed using Workstation Configuration) and the SQL server name as shown in SQL Server Management Studio. Related information Renaming workstations

title: Install the Soft Phase environment
body_text: Install the Soft Phase environment The DeltaV Soft Phase environment consists of three elements: the Soft Phase Broker, the Soft Phase DLL and the user written Soft Phase application (the executable file). To install the DeltaV Soft Phase environment, follow these steps: Close all applications. Insert the DeltaV installation disk #1. Open the DV_Extras\SoftPhaseTemplates folder. Double-click Setup.exe. This initiates the DeltaV Soft Phase installation program. The installation defaults to C:\DeltaV\SoftPhases . When the installation is complete, click Finish to restart the computer. When running soft phases on a non-DeltaV node, you must register the DVBSPBrokerPS.dll and DVBSPSps.dll (regsvr32 DVBSPBrokerPS.dll and regsvr32 DVBSPSps.dll). When registering the DLL(s) on a 64-bit operating system, you must use the 64-bit version of regsvr32.exe. This can be found at C:\Windows\SysWOW64\regsvr32.exe . Note: Installing the Soft Phase environment on non-DeltaV nodes requires a minimum of Windows 7 or Windows Server 2008. The DeltaV installation adds the SOFTPHASEUSER account to your system. This user is created without privileges and is a DeltaV User account. If your soft phase requires specific privileges, you must assign those privileges to the SOFTPHASEUSER account through the Windows User Manager application. The SOFTPHASEUSER account password is pre-assigned in your system. Never change the SOFTPHASEUSER account password from Windows User Manager. For DeltaV computers, use the DeltaV Security Administration to manage the password. On non-DeltaV computers, use the ServPwd.exe utility (found in the DeltaV\bin directory and copied to the non-DeltaV computer) for changing this password. Important: Only change the SOFTPHASEUSER account password using DeltaV Security Administration or the ServPwd utility. Subtopics: Running Soft Phases on a non-DeltaV node Uninstall the Soft Phase environment Related information DeltaV Soft Phases

title: Installing the Cables
body_text: Installing the Cables Use the bottom cable extender to connect a left Legacy Vertical I/O carrier to a right Legacy Vertical I/O carrier at the bottom of the DIN rails. Use the top cable extender to connect a right Legacy Vertical I/O carrier to a left I/O carrier on the opposite side of the cabinet at the top of the DIN rails. Note: Be sure that the bottom cable extender exits in a downward position and the top cable extender exits in an upward position. CAUTION: Be careful when inserting sockets and plugs. The connectors are fragile and bend easily. Ensure that the pins are straight before connecting the cable ends. Connect the plugs and sockets on the carriers. Tighten the two mounting screws on each cable end.

title: Installing VerticalPLUS Carriers
body_text: Installing VerticalPLUS Carriers Position the carrier on the DIN rail and push it against the DIN rail to snap it into place. Slide the carrier down on the DIN rail until it meets the DIN rail stop. Snap the next carrier onto the DIN rail following the instructions in Step 1. Connect each carrier to the adjacent carrier by sliding together the pins on the ends of the carriers. Connect ground wiring as shown in the following figure. Connect only one ground wire for each group of carriers on a DIN rail. Ground Wiring for System Power Supplies

title: Installing an I/O Card
body_text: Installing an I/O Card Warning: Before installing a card in a carrier slot, ensure that the bussed field power voltage at the slot matches the field power requirements for the card. Card damage can result during installation if there is a mismatch between the field power voltage at a carrier slot and the card installed in the slot. Refer to I/O Card Installation . Locate the assigned slot on the I/O interface carrier. Warning: I/O cards are designed to be installed on terminal blocks. If you temporarily install a card on the carrier without a terminal block, be sure to carefully align the pins on the card with the connector on the carrier to prevent damage to the pins. Align the connectors on the I/O card with the connectors on the I/O carrier and the I/O terminal block and push to attach Tighten the mounting screw. I/O Card Installation

title: Install I/O cards onto an 8-Wide I/O Carrier
main_heading: Install I/O cards onto an 8-Wide I/O Carrier
body_text: Install I/O cards onto an 8-Wide I/O Carrier S-series I/O cards snap onto S-series terminal blocks installed on an 8-Wide I/O Carrier. Warning: I/O cards are designed to be installed on terminal blocks. The terminal block guides the card as the retention latch engages. Installing I/O cards Place the bottom of the card on the terminal block and align the top of the card with the card housing on the 8-Wide I/O Carrier. Push the card to snap it into place.

title: Installing an I/O Card
body_text: Installing an I/O Card Warning: Before installing a card in a carrier slot, ensure that the bussed field power voltage at the slot matches the field power requirements for the card. Card damage can result during installation if there is a mismatch between the field power voltage at a carrier slot and the card installed in the slot. Refer to I/O Card Installation . Locate the assigned slot on the I/O interface carrier. Warning: I/O cards are designed to be installed on terminal blocks. If you temporarily install a card on the carrier without a terminal block, be sure to carefully align the pins on the card with the connector on the carrier to prevent damage to the pins. Align the connectors on the I/O card with the connectors on the I/O carrier and the I/O terminal block and push to attach Tighten the mounting screw. I/O Card Installation

title: Installing an I/O Terminal Block
body_text: Installing an I/O Terminal Block Check the key settings on the corresponding I/O card, and set the keys on the I/O terminal block to match. Locate the assigned slot location on the I/O interface carrier. Place the tabs on the back of the I/O terminal block through the slots on the carrier and push the I/O terminal block up to lock it into place as shown in the following figure. I/O Terminal Block Installation Connect field wiring for the I/O terminal block as shown in I/O Terminal Block Channel Assignments or in the I/O card wiring diagrams in the "Interface Specifications" section. Note: Field wiring connections are specific to the I/O card type associated with the I/O terminal block. I/O Terminal Block Channel Assignments Note: The channel assignments in the preceding image pertain to the I/O terminal block, the fused I/O terminal block, and the 4-wire terminal block. Related information I/O Interface Keying Interface Specifications

body_text: Installing an I/O Terminal Block Check the key settings on the corresponding I/O card, and set the keys on the I/O terminal block to match. Locate the assigned slot location on the I/O interface carrier. Place the tabs on the back of the I/O terminal block through the slots on the carrier and push the I/O terminal block up to lock it into place as shown in the following figure. I/O Terminal Block Installation Connect field wiring for the I/O terminal block as shown in I/O Terminal Block Channel Assignments or in the I/O card wiring diagrams in the "Interface Specifications" section. title: Install I.S. CHARMs
body_text: Install I.S. CHARMs I.S. CHARMs install in I.S. CHARM Terminal Blocks on the I.S. CHARM Baseplate. Installing an I.S. CHARM Open the latch on an I.S. Terminal Block. Insert an I.S. CHARM into the terminal block and push the I.S. CHARM until the latch closes. Note: Most I.S. CHARM Terminal Blocks are automatically keyed to the first I.S. CHARM installed. However, the I.S.CHARM Thermocouple mV Terminal Block has a fixed key setting and cannot be reset.

title: Install local peer bus extender cables
main_heading: Install local peer bus extender cables
body_text: Install local peer bus extender cables Notice that the local peer bus extender cable has black and white boots. The cables connect black-to-black (D) and white-to-white (C). Place the cable end onto the BNC connector on the one-wide carrier. One-wide carriers Push and turn to lock the cable into place.

title: Install and connect Megablocks
body_text: Install and connect Megablocks Refer to the following image for the location of the connectors on the Megablock. Megablock Spur Guard for 8 devices Notice that the trunk connectors are black and the spur connectors for the devices are gray. Attach the top latch of the Megablock onto the DIN rail and push the unit into place. For the trunk connector (black): connect the positive (+) segment wire to the positive, connect the negative (-) segment wire to the negative, and connect the segment shield (S) to the S. For each device connector (gray): connect the positive (+) spur wire to the positive, connect the negative (-) spur wire to the negative, and connect the shield wire (S) to the S. If this Megablock is the end of the segment, connect a terminator (Relcom FCS-MBT) at the end of the trunk and at a ground connection. Use a properly sized ground wire to reduce the risk of a surge affecting the segment. If the segment continues and connects to another Megablock, continue the trunk by connecting it to the next Megablock and make the connections described in steps 2 and 3. At each device, ensure that the shield is isolated and not connected to the device. If this Megablock is the end of the segment, connect a terminator (Relcom FCS-MBT) at the end of the trunk and at a ground connection. Use a properly sized ground wire to reduce the risk of a surge affecting the segment.

title: Install the other CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the other CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail
body_text: Install the other CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail CHARM baseplates connect to each other on the DIN rail. Up to eight baseplates can be installed under a CHARM I/O Carrier on a DIN rail. The baseplates and CHARM I/O Carrier connect together to form a redundant power and communication bus. This procedure assumes that a CHARM I/O Carrier and first CHARM Baseplate are connected together on the DIN rail. Installing other baseplates Fit together the connectors on the top of the baseplate that you are installing with the connectors on the bottom of the installed baseplate as you snap the baseplate onto the DIN rail. Install up to eight baseplates under the CHARM I/O Carrier. Subtopics: Remove a CHARM I/O Carrier or Baseplate from the DIN rail CHARM I/O Carriers and CHARM Baseplates are removed from the DIN rail in the same way.

title: Install the I.S. CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the I.S. CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail
body_text: Install the I.S. CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail Up to eight I.S. baseplates can be installed under a CHARM I/O Carrier on a DIN rail. The I.S. baseplates and CHARM I/O Carrier connect together to form a redundant power and communication bus. This procedure assumes that a CHARM I/O Carrier is already installed on the DIN rail. Important: I.S. CHARM Baseplates can also be installed under the same CIOC as standard (non I.S .) CHARM Baseplates. When I.S. CHARM Baseplates and standard CHARM Baseplates are installed under the same CIOC Carrier, standard baseplates must be installed between the CIOC Carrier and the I.S. CHARM Baseplate. A Separation Wall must be installed on every I.S. baseplate and every component, such as extenders and terminators after the I.S. baseplates. The following figure shows a standard baseplate (non-I.S.) installed between the CIOC Carrier and I.S. baseplates. A standard baseplate installed between the CIOC Carrier and an I.S. CHARM Baseplate Refer to Installing I.S. Baseplates Insert a Separation Wall into the notches on the top of the I.S. CHARM Baseplate. Fit together the connectors on the top of the I.S. baseplate that you are installing with the connectors on the bottom of the installed CIOC Carrier as you snap the baseplate onto the DIN rail. Install up to eight I.S. baseplates under the CHARM I/O Carrier. Be sure to install a Separation Wall on each I.S. Baseplate. Installing I.S. Baseplates Related information Install a Separation Wall

title: Install a Power / Controller Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install a Power / Controller Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install a Power / Controller Carrier on the DIN rail The Power / Controller Carrier holds an S-series System Power Supply (24 VDC) and S-series controller or two S-series System Power Supplies (24 VDC) if power injection is required. When a Power / Controller Carrier holds a power supply and controller, it installs to the left of an 8-Wide I/O Carrier. Refer to the DeltaV S-series and CHARMs Hardware Reference manual for information on injecting power to the I/O. If the carrier has been installed and then removed from the DIN rail, turn the screw on the front of the carrier counter-closewise to reengage the latch. The Power / Controller Carrier installs on a horizontal T-type DIN rail. No tools are required to install the Power / Controller Carrier on the DIN rail. Connectors on both sides of the carrier connect with adjacent carriers to form the LocalBus. Installing a Power / Controller Carrier Align the carrier against a T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place. Connect the carrier to any adjacent carriers by sliding together the connectors on the sides of the carriers.

title: Install the power supply on the carrier
main_heading: Install the power supply on the carrier
body_text: Install the power supply on the carrier In hazardous locations the power supply should not be removed or inserted into the carrier unless the input power has been deenergized for at least one minute. Locate the slot labeled PS on the carrier. Align the connectors on the back of the power supply with the connectors on the carrier and push to attach the power supply to the carrier. Tighten the mounting screws on the power supply with a 3 mm hex-head wrench.

title: Install a redundant controller
body_text: Install a redundant controller A redundant controller requires an additional Power / Controller Carrier. Do not mix controller types in a redundant controller pair. Use two SX controllers, two SD Plus controllers, or two SQ controllers. For this procedure, it is assumend that a simplex S-series controller and System Power Supply (24 VDC) are installed on a Power / Controller Carrier. Installing a redundant controller Connect a Power / Controller Carrier to the left of the existing Power / Controller Carrier holding a System Power Supply 24 (VDC) and S-series controller. Snap a System Power Supply (24 VDC) into the left slot of the Power / Controller Carrier. Snap an S-series controller of the same type as the redundant partner into the right slot of the Power / Controller Carrier.

title: Installing a Redundant I/O Card
body_text: Installing a Redundant I/O Card A redundant I/O card consists of two Series 2 cards installed in a redundant terminal block. Read “DeltaV Series 2 I/O” before installing a redundant I/O card. Locate the assigned slots on the I/O interface carrier. Align the connectors on the I/O card with the connectors on the I/O carrier and the redundant I/O terminal block and push to attach. Tighten the mounting screws. Related information DeltaV Series 2 I/O

title: Installing a Redundant I/O Card
body_text: Installing a Redundant I/O Card A redundant I/O card consists of two Series 2 cards installed in a redundant terminal block. Read “DeltaV Series 2 I/O” before installing a redundant I/O card. Locate the assigned slots on the I/O interface carrier. Align the connectors on the I/O card with the connectors on the I/O carrier and the redundant I/O terminal block and push to attach. Tighten the mounting screws. Related information DeltaV Series 2 I/O

title: Installing a Redundant Terminal Block
body_text: Installing a Redundant Terminal Block Read the information in “DeltaV Series 2 I/O” before installing a redundant terminal block. Check the key settings on the corresponding Series 2 cards and set the keys on the terminal block to match. Refer to “I/O Interface Keying” for information on key settings. Locate the assigned slot location on the I/O interface carrier. Remember that the lower slot number must be odd and the upper slot number must be the next higher even number. Place the tabs on the back of the I/O terminal block through the slots on the carrier and push the I/O terminal block up to lock it into place. Connect the field wiring for the redundant I/O terminal blocks as shown in the Series 2 card wiring diagrams and redundant terminal block figures in the "Interface Specifications" section. Related information I/O Interface Keying Interface Specifications DeltaV Series 2 I/O

title: Installing a Redundant Terminal Block
body_text: Installing a Redundant Terminal Block Read the information in “DeltaV Series 2 I/O” before installing a redundant terminal block. Check the key settings on the corresponding Series 2 cards and set the keys on the terminal block to match. Refer to “I/O Interface Keying” for information on key settings. Locate the assigned slot location on the I/O interface carrier. Remember that the lower slot number must be odd and the upper slot number must be the next higher even number. Place the tabs on the back of the I/O terminal block through the slots on the carrier and push the I/O terminal block up to lock it into place. Connect the field wiring for the redundant I/O terminal blocks as shown in the Series 2 card wiring diagrams and redundant terminal block figures in the "Interface Specifications" section. Related information I/O Interface Keying Interface Specifications DeltaV Series 2 I/O

title: Install and connect the Fieldbus Segment Protector
main_heading: Install and connect the Fieldbus Segment Protector
body_text: Install and connect the Fieldbus Segment Protector Segment Protector for eight devices Securely attach the Fieldbus Segment Protector at the desired location. Choose a location that minimizes the length of the spur cables. For the trunk segment connection: connect the positive (+) segment wire to the positive; connect the negative (-) segment wire to the negative; and connect the segment shield (S) to the S. For each device connection: connect the positive (+) spur wire to the positive, connect the negative (-) spur wire to the negative, and connect the shield wire (S) to the S. The two shorting jumpers must be repositioned so that the trunk (T) and spur (S) shields are connected together and not connected to case. Jumper T to S and Gnd to Gnd. If this Segment Protector is at the end of the segment, the terminator switch S1 should be in the On position. If it is not at the end of the segment, ensure that terminator switch S1 is in the Off position. If the segment continues and connects to another Segment Protector, continue the Trunk segment by connecting the Trunk Out connections to the next Segment Protector and proceed with the connections described in steps 2, 3, and 4. For all Segment Protectors, ensure that the two shorting jumpers are repositioned so that the trunk (T) and spur (S) shields are connected together and not connected to case. Jumper T to S and Gnd to Gnd. At each device ensure that the shield is isolated and not connected to the device. If this Segment Protector is at the end of the segment, ensure that the terminator switch S1 is in the On position. Verify the installation. Related information Using the segment checkout procedure to verify the installation

title: Install a simplex controller
body_text: Install a simplex controller A simplex S-series controller installs in the right slot of a Power / Controller Carrier. Align the thick plastic tab on the bottom of the controller with the opening on the right slot of the Power / Controller Carrier and align the top of the controller with the housing on the right slot of the Power / Controller Carrier. Installing a simplex controller Push the controller to snap it onto the right slot of the Power / Controller Carrier.

title: Install a System Power Supply (24 VDC)
main_heading: Install a System Power Supply (24 VDC)
body_text: Install a System Power Supply (24 VDC) The System Power Supply (24 VDC) takes power from a bulk power supply and converts it to 12 VDC power to power controllers and I/O cards. The System Power Supply (24 VDC) installs on the left slot of the Power / Controller Carrier. Always remove input power to the Power / Controller Carrier before installing or removing a power supply from the carrier. Align the thick plastic tab on the bottom of the power supply with the opening on the left slot of the Power / Controller Carrier and align the top of the power supply with the housing on the left slot of the Power / Controller Carrier. Installing a power supply Push the power supply to snap it onto the left slot of the Power / Controller Carrier. Subtopics: Wire the System Power Supply's alarm relay contact The System Power Supply's alarm relay contact is closed during normal operation.

title: Install terminal blocks onto an 8-Wide I/O Carrier
main_heading: Install terminal blocks onto an 8-Wide I/O Carrier
body_text: Install terminal blocks onto an 8-Wide I/O Carrier Terminal blocks provide screw terminations for field wiring. S-series I/O cards snap onto S-series terminal blocks. Set the key on the terminal block before installing the card on the terminal block. Simplex terminal blocks can be installed in any slot on the 8-Wide I/O Carrier. Redundant terminal blocks occupy two slots and must be installed in slots 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, 7 and 8. That is, the lower slot in a redundant pair must be an odd number. Installing terminal blocks Locate the slots for the terminal block on the 8-Wide I/O Carrier. There are three slots for each simplex terminal block. Locate the tabs on the back of the terminal block. There are three tabs on each simplex terminal block. Place the tabs on the terminal block in the slots on the carrier and push the terminal block down to lock it into place. Connect the field wiring to the terminal block.

title: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail
body_text: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail The Column Terminator terminates the redundant bus. It installs after the last CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail. Installing the Column Terminator Locate the last CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail. Typically, this is the baseplate with Address Plug 8. Ensure that the lock on the Column Terminator is in the locked position. Insert a screw driver into the lock and turn it counter-clockwise to engage the lock. Align the connectors on the Column Terminator with the connectors on the last baseplate and snap the terminator onto the DIN rail. After installing the Column Terminator you can install a DIN Rail Stop and then wire your field devices to the terminal blocks on the baseplates. Refer to the specifications for the CHARM Terminal Block and CHARM Injected Power Terminal Block in the DeltaV S-series and CHARMs Hardware Reference manual for information on the terminal block connectors. After wiring your devices, perform all standard field wiring checkout procedures.

title: Set up a DeltaV workstation and install the system identifier
main_heading: Set up a DeltaV workstation and install the system identifier
body_text: Set up a DeltaV workstation and install the system identifier Setting up a DeltaV workstation involves connecting its components, installing the DeltaV system identifier, and optionally installing an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS). The system identifier gives each DeltaV system a unique identification that allows you to download changes to the system. Follow the instructions supplied with your workstation to connect the monitor, keyboard, and mouse to the central processing unit (CPU). Refer to the documentation supplied with your workstation for details on the I/O ports. Install the system identifier on the parallel printer port or Universal Serial Bus (USB). Connect the workstation and its associated peripherals to one AC power distribution and system ground.

title: Install CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers onto the carrier
main_heading: Install CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers onto the carrier
body_text: Install CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers onto the carrier CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS) install in the CSLS Carrier. Align the shallow opening on the bottom of the CSLS with the tab on a carrier slot and align the top of the CSLS with the housing on a carrier slot. Push the CSLS to snap it into the slot. Install two CSLS for redundancy. To remove a CSLS, depress the button on the top of the CSLS and pull it out of the slot.

title: Install a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carrier on the DIN rail The CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carrier holds redundant CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS) and redundant Power Modules. The CSLS and Power Modules receive 24 VDC input power through the carrier. The Power Modules generate 6.3 VDC power for the LS CHARMs. The carrier houses primary and secondary ethernet ports for connections to the Local Safety Network. No tools are required to install the CSLS Carrier on the DIN rail. A latch on the back of the carrier snaps it into place on the DIN rail. Connectors on the bottom of the carrier connect with connectors on the first CHARM Baseplate. CSLS Carrier Align the carrier against a T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place.

title: Install the DeltaV Excel Add-in
body_text: Install the DeltaV Excel Add-in The DeltaV Excel Add-in can only be installed by the local administrator or by a user in a group with administrator privileges. Prior to installation, you must start Microsoft Excel at least once to create Registry keys required by the DeltaV Excel Add-in. Important: Any additional user who wants to use the DeltaV Excel Add-in on the workstation where it has been installed must also complete the steps in Set up an additional user below. These steps are also required for a user account on a Remote Desktop Services system, including the user who installed the DeltaV Excel Add-in. To install the DeltaV Excel Add-in, complete the following steps: Log on as a user with administrator privileges. Start and exit Microsoft Excel. In Windows Explorer, navigate to \DeltaV\bin\ExcelAddInRuntime , and then double-click setup.exe . If the Excel AddIn Runtime dialog appears, prompting you to install additional required items, click the Install button. If a prompt appears, indicating that the installation of the DeltaV Excel Add-in needs to restart the computer, click the Yes button. When the Customer Information dialog appears, enter the name of your organization in the Company Name field, select the Anyone who uses this computer (all users) option, and then click the Next button. When the Ready to Install the Program dialog appears, click the Install button. Following installation, you can select DeltaV Excel Add-in options by navigating to DeltaV > Runtime Data on the Add-Ins ribbon of Microsoft Excel. Related information Uninstall the DeltaV Excel Add-in Set up an additional user To set up an additional user on the workstation where the DeltaV Excel Add-in has been installed or for a user account on a Remote Desktop Services system, including the user who installed the DeltaV Excel Add-in, complete the following steps: Open Microsoft Excel. Click the File tab, and then click Options . In the Excel Options dialog, click Add-Ins . In the View and manage Microsoft Office Add-ins window, select Excel Add-ins from the Manage list, and then click the Go button. In the Add-Ins dialog, click the Automation button. In the Automation Servers dialog, highlight DeltaV.ExcelAddIn.Functions.Functions, and then click the OK button. Close the Add-Ins dialog by clicking the OK button. Exit and restart Excel.

title: Install DeltaV on the first Application Station
main_heading: Install DeltaV on the first Application Station
body_text: Install DeltaV on the first Application Station Using the DeltaV installation disks, run the setup program on one of the Application Stations. When prompted to choose your workstation type, select the Local Application Station option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Specifying the workstation configuration file Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with Redundant Assigned Modules has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? When configuring a pair of Application Stations for the first time, you must respond to this prompt by clicking Yes when configuring one of the two Application Stations, and click No when configuring the other Application Station. When you click Yes , the Application Station is given the name that you specified when creating it in DeltaV Explorer on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation; when you click No , the characters _S are appended to the Application Station name. Note: If you ever need to reconfigure either workstation in the pair, you should repond to this prompt by clicking Yes if it is the Application Station that you specified as the preferred active; otherwise, if it is the workstation with the characters _S appended to the base Application Station name, click No . Specifying an Application Station as preferred active Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the Application Station. Related information Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server Install DeltaV on the second Application Station

title: Install DeltaV on the new Application Station
main_heading: Install DeltaV on the new Application Station
body_text: Install DeltaV on the new Application Station Use the DeltaV installation disks to run the setup program on the new Application Station where you intend to run an OPC client connected to a redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. When prompted to choose your workstation type, select the Local Application Station option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. In the DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog, select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with Redundant Assigned Modules has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? If you clicked Yes earlier when configuring the existing Application Station, you must respond to this prompt by clicking No now. When you click No , the characters _S are appended to the appended to the name specified for the Application Station in DeltaV Explorer. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the new Application Station. Related information Finish configuring Application Station redundancy Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server

title: Install DeltaV on the second Application Station
main_heading: Install DeltaV on the second Application Station
body_text: Install DeltaV on the second Application Station Using the DeltaV installation disks, run the setup program on the remaining Application Station. When prompted to choose your workstation type, select the Local Application Station option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with Redundant Assigned Modules has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? If you responded to this prompt by clicking Yes when configuring the first of the two Application Stations, click No now. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the second Application Station Related information Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server Finish configuring Application Station redundancy

title: Install DeltaV OPC Mirror
body_text: Install DeltaV OPC Mirror You can install OPC Mirror on a DeltaV workstation or a non-DeltaV system. To install the OPC Mirror application, run the Setup.exe file located in the DV_Extras\OPCMirror folder on the DeltaV installation disk #1. The OPC Mirror help file contains information about system requirements when installing on a non-DeltaV workstation. Important: During installation, you can specify the directory where OPC Mirror is installed. The default location is C:\Program Files (x86)\FRS\OPC Mirror . Because OPC Mirror runs as a service in Windows, it must be started by a user whose security permissions are set to Full Control for this directory. After installing OPC Mirror, complete the following steps: Assign the appropriate OPC Mirror licenses. Note: If the OPC Mirror installation program finds an OPC Mirror configuration database file from a previous installation, you are prompted to import the database file into the current installation. If the previous installation of OPC Mirror licensed more OPC Data Access Servers than you are licensing for the current installation, it is possible that errors may appear in DeltaV Diagnostics in the event that OPC Mirror attempts to reestablish more connections than allowed for the current installation. Start the OPC Mirror service by right-clicking the OPC Mirror icon in the System Tray, and then selecting Start OPC Mirror Service from the shortcut menu. (You can also start the OPC Mirror service by using the Computer Management program in Windows.) Note: If the OPC Mirror setup program initiates a system restart during installation, you do not need to manually start the OPC Mirror service, because it starts automatically on system startup, by default. Start the OPC Mirror Configuration program to add OPC servers and items and to define server monitoring specifications. To start the OPC Mirror Configuration program, right-click the OPC Mirror icon in the System Tray, and then select Configure from the shortcut menu, or select Programs > OPC Mirror > OPC Mirror Configuration on the Start menu. Uninstall OPC Mirror Before uninstalling OPC Mirror, you must first complete the following steps: If the OPC Mirror Configuration program is running, exit it by selecting Exit on the Pipe menu. If the OPC Mirror Diagnostics program is running, exit it by selecting Exit on the File menu. Stop the OPC Mirror service by right-clicking the OPC Mirror icon in the System Tray, and then selecting Stop OPC Mirror Service from the shortcut menu. Close the OPC Mirror Tray program by right-clicking the OPC Mirror icon in the System Tray, and then selecting Close from the shortcut menu. You can then uninstall OPC Mirror by using Windows Control Panel.

title: Install DeltaV Reporter
body_text: Install DeltaV Reporter DeltaV Reporter can be installed on a DeltaV workstation or on an office computer capable of connecting to the Continuous Historian or Event Chronicle node. DeltaV Reporter users must have a valid DeltaV user account. You must install .NET Programmability Support before you install DeltaV Reporter. See the following procedures for information on installing .NET Programmability Support and DeltaV Reporter. Install the .NET Programmability Support Use the Control Panel in Windows to open Programs and Features . Select Microsoft Office, and then click Change . Note: The version number for Microsoft Office might be included in the item, for example, Microsoft Office 2016. In the Office Setup dialog, select Add or Remove Features , and then click Continue . Expand Microsoft Excel on the list of Microsoft Office programs. Click the down arrow on .NET Programmability Support. Select the Run from My Computer option, and then click Continue . After the configuration process concludes, click Close . Close the Programs and Features window. Install DeltaV Reporter Insert the DeltaV installation disk #1 in the drive, and then navigate to the DV_Extras\DeltaVReporter folder. To run the DeltaV Reporter Setup Wizard , double-click the setup.exe program. If you are prompted to install the Shared Add-in Support Update for Microsoft .NET Framework, click Install . On the Welcome screen, click Next . On the .NET Programmability Support screen, click Next . On the Select Installation Folder screen, click Next to accept the default directory for installation. On the Confirm Installation screen, click Next to start the installation. After the installation concludes, click Close . By default, DeltaV Reporter is installed in the C:\Program Files (x86)\Emerson Process Management\DeltaV Reporter folder. During the installation of DeltaV Reporter, important sample Excel workbook files are copied to the C:\DeltaV Reporter\Definitions folder. You can use these as examples of using the DeltaV Reporter worksheet functions and as templates to create report definition files for automatically generating scheduled reports from the Event Chronicle database. The .NET Programmability Support must be installed before Excel is used with DeltaV Reporter. If Excel is started without .NET Programmability Support, you should follow the steps above to add the required support and then reactivate DeltaV Reporter by running the ExcelAddIn.reg file from the installation folder (by default, C:\Program Files (x86)\Emerson Process Management\DeltaV Reporter ). Note: Refer to the Release Notes KBA for compatibility information. Office Service Packs and Microsoft Office updates may be required for proper operation of Excel. DeltaV Reporter must be uninstalled and reinstalled with each upgrade of the DeltaV System to a new version. You can uninstall DeltaV Reporter by either using the Programs and Features applet in Control Panel or by rerunning the DeltaV Reporter setup.exe program in the DeltaV\bin\DeltaVReporter folder and selecting the Remove option.

title: Install the Dual Universal Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the Dual Universal Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install the Dual Universal Carrier on the DIN rail The Dual Universal Carrier holds simplex or redundant Ethernet I/O cards (EIOCs). The carrier provides redundant 24 VDC power to the EIOCs. The Dual Universal Carrier installs on horizontal T-type DIN rails. No screws are required to install the carrier on the DIN rail. Dual Universal Carrier on a DIN rail Align the carrier against a T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place.

title: Install a Dual Universal Safety Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install a Dual Universal Safety Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install a Dual Universal Safety Carrier on the DIN rail The Dual Universal Safety Carrier holds redundant Local Safety Network Bridges (LSNB) or SZ controllers. The carrier provides redundant 24 VDC power to the LSNBs or SZ controllers. The Dual Universal Safety Carrier installs on horizontal T-type DIN rails. No screws are required to install the carrier on the DIN rail. Align the carrier against a T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place.

title: Install Ethernet I/O Cards on the Dual Universal Carrier
main_heading: Install Ethernet I/O Cards on the Dual Universal Carrier
body_text: Install Ethernet I/O Cards on the Dual Universal Carrier Ethernet I/O Cards (EIOC) install on the Dual Universal Carrier. Installing EIOCs Align the shallow opening on the bottom of the EIOC with the tab on a carrier slot and align the top of the EIOC with the housing on a carrier slot. Push the EIOC to snap it into place. Install two EIOCs for redundancy. To remove an EIOC, depress the button on the top of the EIOC and pull the EIOC out of the slot.

title: Install the EnTech Toolkit
body_text: Install the EnTech Toolkit After installing DeltaV, you can install one or more application modules from the EnTech Toolkit on any DeltaV workstation. To install an application module, complete the following steps: Insert DeltaV installation disk #1 in the drive. The DeltaV Install dialog appears. Note: If the Windows Autorun feature is disabled, preventing the DeltaV Install dialog from appearing when you insert the DeltaV installation disk #1 in the drive, run Autorun\DVAutorun.exe . Click the Other DeltaV Products button. Click the EnTech Toolkit button. Click the EnTech Collect , EnTech Tuner , or EnTech Analyse button for the application module you want to install. Important: Do not install the EnTech Toolkit License Manager program on a workstation within a DeltaV system. The License Manager program is only required to install and register licenses for the EnTech Toolkit on a non-DeltaV system. Accept the default for each dialog that appears during installation. Note: If you are prompted to restart your computer, select the Yes, I want to restart my computer now option, and then click the Finish button. Repeat the preceding steps for each application module from the EnTech Toolkit to be installed. For additional information about using the EnTech Toolkit, see the application help for each application module and the documentation files listed in the following Start menu locations: Start > EnTech Toolkit > Collect Start > EnTech Toolkit > Tuner Start > EnTech Toolkit > Analyse Related information Convert .fhx DeltaV configuration files to .mdb database files Uninstall the EnTech Toolkit Uninstall one or more application modules from the EnTech Toolkit using the following steps: Select Control Panel > Programs and Features . In the list of applications, select the module you want to uninstall. Analyze Collect Tune Right click and select uninstall . If prompted that this will uninstall the application, click OK . Click Finish when the process completes. Continue uninstalling other EnTech modules. When done uninstalling, close Control Panel.

title: Install the first CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the first CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail
body_text: Install the first CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail The first CHARM Baseplate holds Address Plug one and a bank of 12 LS CHARM Terminal Blocks. The first CHARM Baseplate connects to a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) Carrier on the DIN rail. No tools are required to install a CHARM Baseplate onto the DIN rail. For this procedure it is assumed that a CSLS Carrier is installed on the DIN rail. Installing the first baseplate Hold the first CHARM Baseplate beneath the CSLS carrier installed on the DIN rail and notice how the connectors on the top of the baseplate interlock with the connectors on the bottom of the CSLS carrier. Align and fit the connectors together as you snap the CHARM Baseplate onto the DIN rail. A latch on the back of the baseplate snaps it into place on the DIN rail.

title: Install I.S. Baseplates
body_text: Install I.S. Baseplates I.S. CHARM Baseplates install exactly like CHARM Baseplates except that a Separation Wall must be installed on every I.S. Baseplate and every component such as Column Extenders and Column Terminators, installed after the baseplates. Important: I.S. CHARM Baseplates can also be installed under the same CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) as standard (non I.S.) CHARM Baseplates. When I.S. CHARM Baseplates and standard CHARM Baseplates are installed under the same CSLS Carrier, standard baseplates must be installed between the CSLS Carrier and the I.S. CHARM Baseplate. A Separation Wall must be installed on every I.S. Baseplate and every component, such as extenders and terminators after the I.S. Baseplates. The following figure shows a standard baseplate (non-I.S.) installed between the CSLS Carrier and I.S. Baseplates. A standard baseplate installed between the CSLS Carrier and an I.S. CHARM Baseplate This procedure assumes that a CSLS Carrier is already installed on the DIN rail. Insert a Separation Wall into the notches on the top of the I.S. CHARM Baseplate. Fit together the connectors on the top of the I.S. baseplate that you are installing with the connectors on the bottom of the installed CSLS Carrier as you snap the baseplate onto the DIN rail. Install up to eight I.S. baseplates under the CSLS Carrier. Be sure to install a Separation Wall on each I.S. Baseplate. Installing I.S. CHARM Baseplates Related information Install a Separation Wall

title: Install LS I.S. CHARMs
body_text: Install LS I.S. CHARMs LS I.S. CHARMs install in I.S. CHARM Terminal Blocks on the I.S. CHARM Baseplate. Installing an LS I.S. CHARM Open the latch on an I.S. Terminal Block. Insert an LS I.S. CHARM into the terminal block and push the LS I.S. CHARM until the latch closes. Note: Most I.S. CHARM Terminal Blocks are automatically keyed to the first LS I.S. CHARM installed; however, the I.S. CHARM Thermocouple mV Terminal Block has a fixed key setting .

title: Install LS CHARMs
body_text: Install LS CHARMs LS CHARMs install in terminal blocks on the CHARM Baseplate. Installing a CHARM Note: Although LS CHARMs can be installed in any location, it is good engineering practice to separate low voltage DC signals from high voltage AC signals. To ensure a safe working environment, it is recommended that you wire AC signals to a different enclosure from DC signals. Open the latch on a terminal block. Insert a LS CHARM into the terminal block and push the LS CHARM until the latch closes. Note: Most CHARM terminal blocks are automatically keyed to the first LS CHARM installed. However, the following CHARM terminal blocks have a fixed key setting: CHARM Thermocouple / mV, LS DVC (simplex and redundant), LS Redundant DTA Relay, LS Redundant ETA Relay.

title: Install Local Safety Network Bridges or SZ Controllers on the Dual Universal Safety Carrier
main_heading:
Install Local Safety Network Bridges or SZ Controllers on the Dual
	 Universal Safety Carrier
body_text: Install Local Safety Network Bridges or SZ Controllers on the Dual Universal Safety Carrier Redundant Local Safety Network Bridges (LSNB) or SZ Controllers install on the Dual Universal Safety Carrier. You must install either LSNBs or SZ Controllers on the carrier. You cannot install one LSNB and one SZ. Align the shallow opening on the bottom of the LSNB or SZ Controller with the tab on a carrier slot and align the top of the LSNB or SZ with the housing on a carrier slot. Installing LSNBs or SZ Controllers Push the redundant LSNBs or SZ Controllers to snap them into place. To remove a LSNB or SZ Controller, depress the button on the top of the LSNB or SZ and pull it out of the slot.

title: Install Microsoft Windows Server and Remote Desktop Services
main_heading: Install Microsoft Windows Server and Remote Desktop Services
body_text: Install Microsoft Windows Server and Remote Desktop Services Microsoft Windows Server (the version supported for this release) must be installed and Microsoft Remote Desktop Services (formerly Terminal Server) must be installed and the RDS role enabled on the server machine before the DeltaV software is installed. Multiple reboots of the computer are required for this process. Note: For complete information on configuring the Windows operating system to support the Remote Desktop Services role and Remote Clients, refer to the Emerson Knowledge Base Article for your operating system. Install Windows Server (the version supported for this release) on the server machine per the instructions found in the Emerson Knowledge Base Article for that operating system. Add the Remote Desktop Services role per the instructions found in the Emerson Knowledge Base Article for the operating system. Note: When adding the role, be sure to select Audio and video playback to allow operators to hear alarm sounds. When installing the DeltaV software, use one of three choices as the workstation type for the server: ProfessionalPLUS as a Remote Client Server Operator Station as a Remote Client Server Simulate for standalone laptop or workstation Important: During installation of the DeltaV software, the correct workstation type must be selected to designate the workstation as a Remote Client server. After installing the DeltaV software, you must configure the Windows Server operating system properties to enable remote access. From Administrative Tools, select Services. Right-click the Routing and Remote Access service and select Properties . Set the service to enable automatically. Click OK to close the dialogs. Open the Systems Properties dialog by clicking Start > Control Panel > System & Security > System . Select the Remote Settings link. Select Allow remote connections to this computer . Click OK if prompted with security message. Click Select Users... to configure the users. Enter the users that will have remote access. Click Add to add the user. Click OK when done adding users Click OK to close the System Properties dialog. Close the remaining open windows. On the remote node (the machine that connects remotely to the DeltaV system) you must install the appropriate Microsoft licenses. DeltaV licenses for remote use are assigned in DeltaV Explorer and are based on the existing license structure for DeltaV workstations. Related information Administrator functions: adding users

title: Install OPC Mirror for redundancy
body_text: Install OPC Mirror for redundancy To install OPC Mirror as a redundant subsystem, you must first set up a pair of Application Stations by creating an Application Station in DeltaV Explorer, and then enable the Enable Redundancy for Assigned Modules option on the Redundancy tab of its Properties dialog. Also, you must select OPC DA Server and OPC Mirror from the pull-down list for the Redundant OPC option. Redundancy tab in Application Station Properties dialog After setting up the Application Station pair, install OPC Mirror on each Application Station, run the Setup.exe file located in the DV_Extras\OPCMirror folder on the DeltaV installation disk #1. Important: To be used redundantly on a pair of Application Stations, OPC Mirror must be installed in the same directory path on each workstation in the pair. By default, OPC Mirror is installed in C:\Program Files (x86)\FRS\OPC Mirror . If you specify a different location when installing OPC Mirror on one of the Application Stations, you must also specify the same installation directory path on the other Application Station. Because OPC Mirror runs as a service in Windows, it must be started by a user whose security permissions are set to Full Control for this directory. After installing OPC Mirror, complete the following steps: Assign the appropriate OPC Mirror and OPC Mirror Redundancy licenses to the Application Stations. Note: If the OPC Mirror installation program finds an OPC Mirror configuration database file from a previous installation, you are prompted to import the database file into the current installation. If the previous installation of OPC Mirror licensed more OPC Data Access Servers than you are licensing for the current installation, it is possible that errors may appear in DeltaV Diagnostics in the event that OPC Mirror attempts to reestablish more connections than allowed for the current installation. Start the OPC Mirror service by right-clicking the OPC Mirror icon in the System Tray , and then selecting Start OPC Mirror Service from the shortcut menu. (You can also start the OPC Mirror service by using the Computer Management program in Windows.) Note: If the OPC Mirror setup program initiates a system restart during installation, you do not need to manually start the OPC Mirror service, because it starts automatically on system startup, by default. Important: After setting up OPC Mirror for redundancy and downloading the Application stations, if the value of the MirLic (OPC Mirror Redundancy Enabled) or MirPAvail (OPC Mirror Partner Application Available) parameters in DeltaV Diagnostics is NO, stop the OPC Mirror service (if necessary), and then restart it on both Application Stations. Start the OPC Mirror Configuration program to add OPC servers and items and to define server monitoring specifications. To start the OPC Mirror Configuration program, right-click the OPC Mirror icon in the System Tray, and then select Configure from the shortcut menu, or select Programs > OPC Mirror > OPC Mirror Configuration on the Start menu. Related information DeltaV OPC Mirror

title: Install the other CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the other CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail
body_text: Install the other CHARM Baseplates onto the DIN rail CHARM baseplates connect to each other on the DIN rail. Up to eight baseplates can be installed under a CSLS Carrier on a DIN rail. The baseplates and CSLS Carrier connect together to form a redundant power and communication bus. This procedure assumes that a CSLS Carrier and first CHARM Baseplate are connected together on the DIN rail. Installing other baseplates Fit together the connectors on the top of the baseplate that you are installing with the connectors on the bottom of the installed baseplate as you snap the baseplate onto the DIN rail. Install up to eight baseplates under the CSLS Carrier.

title: Install PI AF Client support for embedded trend objects in DeltaV Operate
main_heading:
Install PI AF Client support for embedded trend objects in DeltaV
    Operate
body_text: Install PI AF Client support for embedded trend objects in DeltaV Operate If you are using the Advanced Continuous Historian or an OSIsoft PI Server enterprise historian and configure an Embedded Trend object to display a trend chart of historical data in DeltaV Operate, you must install PI Asset Framework (AF) Client software on each DeltaV workstation where an Embedded Trend object is configured. To install the PI AF Client, complete the following steps: Log on as a user with Windows Administrator account privileges. Insert the Advanced Continuous Historian installation disk in the drive. Click Start > Run . After the Run dialog appears, click the Browse button. Navigate to the Advanced_Continuous_Historian\AF Client folder. Select the PI-AF-Client_2016-R2-SP1_.exe setup program, and then click the Open button. In the Run dialog, click the OK button. In general, you can accept the defaults during the installation of the PI AF Client; for example, notification symbols related to the availability of optional PI AF Client features can typically be disregarded. When the Default Servers dialog appears, specify the name or IP address of a system where the Advanced Continuous Historian or PI Server is installed in the Default Data server field. If needed, you can specify additional systems from which to retrieve historical data for an Embedded Trend object in DeltaV Operate by using the PI SDK Utility to add them to the known servers table. To start the PI SDK Utility, click Start > PI System > PISDKUtility . When the Customer Experience Improvement dialog appears, read the scrolling text in the information window, and then select whether or not to participate in this program sponsored by OSIsoft. For additional considerations, consult with your system administrator.

title: Install PI AF Client support for embedded trend objects in DeltaV Operate
main_heading:
Install PI AF Client support for embedded trend objects in DeltaV
    Operate
body_text: Install PI AF Client support for embedded trend objects in DeltaV Operate If you are using the Advanced Continuous Historian or an OSIsoft PI Server enterprise historian and configure an Embedded Trend object to display a trend chart of historical data in DeltaV Operate, you must install PI Asset Framework (AF) Client software on each DeltaV workstation where an Embedded Trend object is configured. To install the PI AF Client, complete the following steps: Log on as a user with Windows Administrator account privileges. Insert the Advanced Continuous Historian installation disk in the drive. Click Start > Run . After the Run dialog appears, click the Browse button. Navigate to the Advanced_Continuous_Historian\AF Client folder. Select the PI-AF-Client_2016-R2-SP1_.exe setup program, and then click the Open button. In the Run dialog, click the OK button. In general, you can accept the defaults during the installation of the PI AF Client; for example, notification symbols related to the availability of optional PI AF Client features can typically be disregarded. When the Default Servers dialog appears, specify the name or IP address of a system where the Advanced Continuous Historian or PI Server is installed in the Default Data server field. title: Install Power Modules onto the carrier
main_heading: Install Power Modules onto the carrier
body_text: Install Power Modules onto the carrier Power Modules install in the CSLS Carrier. Open the latch on the Power Module slot on the carrier. Align the Power Module in one of the slots. Push the Power Module to snap it into the slot. The latch closes when the Power Module is properly installed. Install two Power Modules for redundancy. To remove a Power Module, open the latch and pull it out of the slot.

title: Install redundant I/O cards
body_text: Install redundant I/O cards A redundant I/O card consists of two Series 2 cards installed in a redundant terminal block. Make sure that 24 VDC field power is provided to the carrier. Locate the assigned slots on the I/O interface carrier. Align the connectors on the Series 2 card with the connectors on the I/O carrier and the redundant I/O terminal block and push to attach. Tighten the mounting screws.

title: Install redundant I/O terminal blocks
body_text: Install redundant I/O terminal blocks The DeltaV system supports redundant Analog Input, Analog Output, Discrete, H1, and Interface terminal blocks. (Follow the Related information links for specifications.) Make sure that 24 VDC field power is provided to the carrier. Check the key settings on the corresponding Series 2 cards and set the keys on the terminal block to match. Locate the assigned slot location on the I/O interface carrier. Remember that the lower slot number must be odd, and the upper slot number must be the next higher even number. Place the tabs on the back of the redundant terminal block through the slots on the carrier and push the terminal block up to lock it into place. Connect the field wiring for the redundant terminal blocks. as shown in the Series 2 card wiring diagrams and redundant terminal block figures. Related information Redundant Analog Input Terminal Block Redundant Analog Output Terminal Block Redundant Discrete Terminal Block Redundant H1 Terminal Block Redundant Interface Terminal Block I/O Interface Keying DeltaV Series 2 Redundant I/O

title: Install and set up the Secure SOA Server
main_heading: Install and set up the Secure SOA Server
body_text: Install and set up the Secure SOA Server If you need access to web services on computers outside of the area control network (ACN), both the DeltaV system and the external system must be in domains, not workgroups. The SOA web services do not support workgroup-to-workgroup communication. You must install the web services software on a computer in the external domain to create a Secure SOA Server. The prerequisites for installing the Secure SOA Server are: Set up the SOA Gateway in the DeltaV ACN as explained above. If you are using a firewall between the domains, make sure it has been configured correctly. Configure a two-way domain trust between the DeltaV domain system and the external domain. Configure the domain name system (DNS) for both domains. To install the Secure SOA Server software in the external domain: Run the setup.exe program on the DeltaV installation disk #1 in the DV_Extras\Secure SOA Server folder. A progress dialog appears, then after a few moments the DeltaV External Gateway - InstallShield Wizard dialog appears. In the Receiver field enter the fully-qualified domain name of the SOA Gateway configured within the DeltaV network. This is the domain that contains the DeltaV application station configured as the SOA Gateway in DeltaV Explorer. For example: AppStation1.MyDeltaVDomain Enter the port number the SOA Gateway (the application station) uses for the service EmersonProcess.Web.Services.MonitorHost.exe. Click Next. A dialog appears in which you select and verify an installation path for the web service software. Click Next . A dialog appears that summarizes the installation settings you have made. Click Next . Installing the Secure SOA Server creates the Windows user account DeltaVAdmin. A dialog appears in which you can change the password of this account. This is the account used by the Gateway web services. You can change this password or accept the default password. Click Next . The setup continues until the InstallShield Wizard Complete dialog appears. Click Finish . The following services are installed on the Secure SOA Server: Campaign Manager Web Service Recipe Exchange Web Service Monitor Service You can verify their existence from the Windows Task Manager or the Windows Services application. You can view service logs from the DeltaV SOA Gateway Administration application. After the Monitor Service is activated, the other web services attempt to start using their default port numbers. If the default ports are already in use, the services do not start. The Windows Event Viewer contains information on whether the services started or not. For information on resolving port conflicts refer to the topic Troubleshooting SOA Web Services. Note: SOA web service client programs in the external domain must point to the Secure SOA Server, not the SOA Gateway within the DeltaV system domain.

title: Install the SmartPlant Excel Add-in
body_text: Install the SmartPlant Excel Add-in The SmartPlant Instrumentation Excel Add-in works with Excel 2013. For specific requirements refer to the DeltaV Compatibility Chart in the Release notes KBA for this release. In addition: The add-ins must be installed and run on a DeltaV ProfessionalPLUS or Professional node to connect to and transfer data between the DeltaV database and SPI software. The add-ins should only be used with the version of DeltaV software that provided them. Note: Excel 2013 supports all of the SPI features that DeltaV software requires. If you use other features of SPI software, refer to its documentation for versions of Excel that it supports. To install the add-ins: Open Excel. Select File > Options . Click Add-Ins . Make sure Excel Add-Ins is selected in the Manage field, and then click Go . On the Add-Ins dialog, click Browse and navigate to \DeltaV\DVData\SmartPlant\Instrumentation\Deltav_Xl_Spi.xla . On the Add-Ins dialog, click Browse and navigate to \DeltaV\DVData\SmartPlant\XLSupport\Deltav_Xl_Support.xla . Click OK on the Add-Ins dialog. Loading the add-ins creates the DeltaV menu command under the Excel Add-Ins tab and creates the I/O Support and SPI Interface menus below it. Important: If you are upgrading to a newer release of Excel be sure to remove the add-ins before you upgrade and reinstall the add-ins after the upgrade.

title: Install the SmartPlant Intergraph components
body_text: Install the SmartPlant Intergraph components Note: To move data from the DeltaV system to the SmartPlant Instrumentation application you must have a SmartPlant Instrumentation version specified in SmartPlant Excel Interface. When you install DeltaV software as recommended on a PC that does not include the SPI software, then you will need to install these Intergraph components. If DeltaV software and SPI are on the same machine then SPI installs these components as part of a major SPI software release. SPI does not install the schema with a service pack. It is recommended that you install the Intergraph components on the same computer that has DeltaV software installed. The Intergraph SmartPlant Instrumentation components require MSXML 4.0 SP2. If it is not installed you can obtain it from the Microsoft website. To install the Intergraph components: From Windows Explorer navigate to \DVData\SmartPlant\Foundation\v2014 . Double-click the setup.exe file. In the Intergraph install dialog accept the defaults. The following message may appear. Ignore this message and click No to continue. From Windows Explorer navigate to \DVData\SmartPlant\Foundation\Client\v2014 . Double-click the setup.exe file. In the Intergraph install dialog accept the defaults. The Intergraph components are installed as choices on the Windows Start menu. Note: To install newer versions of the Intergraph components, you must first uninstall the existing components. From Control Panel select Programs and Features. Related information SmartPlant Excel Interface

title: Install SZ Controllers onto the carrier
main_heading: Install SZ Controllers onto the carrier
body_text: Install SZ Controllers onto the carrier SZ Controllers install in the SZ Controller Carrier. Align the shallow opening on the bottom of the controller with the tab on a carrier slot and align the top of the controller with the housing on a carrier slot. Push the controller to snap it into the slot. Install two SZ Controllers for redundancy. To remove a controller, depress the button on the top of the controller and pull the controller out of the slot.

title: Install an SZ Controller Carrier on the DIN rail
main_heading: Install an SZ Controller Carrier on the DIN rail
body_text: Install an SZ Controller Carrier on the DIN rail The SZ Controller Carrier holds redundant SZ Controllers. It has redundant 24 VDC connectors for providing power to the controllers, redundant (primary and secondary) ethernet ports for connection to the Area Control Network, and redundant (primary and secondary) ethernet ports for connection to the Local Safety Network. No tools are required to install the SZ Controller Carrier on the DIN rail. A latch on the back of the carrier snaps it into place on the DIN rail. SZ Controller Carrier Align the carrier against a vertical T-type DIN rail and push it to snap it into place.

title: Install the Continuous Historian Data Conversion utility
main_heading:
Install the Continuous Historian Data Conversion

body_text: Install the Continuous Historian Data Conversion utility To install the Continuous Historian Data Conversion utility, complete the following steps: Insert the DeltaV installation disk #1 in the drive of the computer where the Legacy Historian is installed. title: Install a Separation Wall
body_text: Install a Separation Wall A Separation Wall must be installed on every I.S. baseplate and every component, such as Column Extenders and Column Terminators, installed after the baseplates. Locate the notches on the top of the I.S. Baseplate, Column Extender, or Column Terminator. Locate the connector on the Separation Wall. Snap the connector on the Separation Wall into the notches on the baseplate, extender, or terminator. Installed Separation Wall
