title: Connect power to I.S. CHARM I/O
main_heading: Connect power to I.S. CHARM I/O
body_text: Connect power to I.S. CHARM I/O Redundant 24 VDC power is delivered from bulk power supplies to I.S. CHARM I/O through the CHARM I/O Carrier. For this procedure, it is assumed that redundant bulk 24 VDC power supplies are already installed. Note: In the following image, the power supplies and CHARM I/O Carrier are installed in a Hazardous, Div. 2 or Zone 2, Group A, B, C, D location. Powering and grounding I.S. CHARM I/O Connect the bulk power supply to the power terminals on the CHARM I/O Carrier shown in the preceding image. Install a 20 A fuse between the bulk power supply and the CHARM I/O Carrier. The fuse must have a breaking capacity greater than 1500 A and a Um rating of 40 V. The fuse and fuse holder must meet IEC60079-11 requirements. The fuse and fuse holder can be purchased from Emerson. Use the following model numbers to order the fuse and fuse holder: SE4610T01: Fuse Holder and Fuse Assembly for 24VDC Power Supply of CHARM I/O Card KL4510X1-FA1: Replacement Fuse for SE4610T01 Fuseholder Assembly KL4510X1-GA1: Replacement Fuseholder for SE4610T01 Fuseholder Assembly Ground the connections as shown in the image.

title: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail
body_text: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail The Column Terminator terminates the redundant bus. It installs after the last I.S. CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail. Installing the Column Terminator Locate the last I.S. CHARM Baseplate on the DIN rail. Install a Separation Wall on the Column Terminator. Ensure that the lock on the Column Terminator is in the locked position. Insert a screw driver into the lock and turn it counter-clockwise to engage the lock. Align the connectors on the Column Terminator with the connectors on the last baseplate and snap the terminator onto the DIN rail. After installing the Column Terminator you can install a DIN Rail Stop and then wire your field devices to the terminal blocks on the baseplates. Refer to the specifications for the I.S. CHARM Terminal Block in the DeltaV S-series and CHARMs Hardware Reference manual for information on the terminal block connectors. After wiring your devices, perform all standard field wiring checkout procedures. Related information Install a Separation Wall

title: Connect power to LS I.S. CHARM I/O
main_heading: Connect power to LS I.S. CHARM I/O
body_text: Connect power to LS I.S. CHARM I/O Redundant 24 VDC power is delivered from bulk power supplies to LS I.S. CHARM I/O through the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) Carrier. Note: In most cases, removing a CHARM from the CHARM baseplate removes power from any connected field device. However, CHARM type, terminal block type, and external power distribution can affect whether removing the CHARM removes power from a field device. Note: In the following image, the power supplies and CSLS Carrier are installed in a Hazardous, Div. 2 or Zone 2, Group A, B, C, D location. Powering and grounding LS I.S. CHARM I/O For this procedure, it is assumed that redundant bulk 24 VDC power supplies and surge suppression/filter devices are already installed. Connect the AC power that is feeding the bulk power supplies to surge suppression/filter devices. Connect the bulk power supply to the power terminals on the CSLS Carrier as shown in the preceding image. Install either a 10 A or a 20 A fuse between the bulk power supply and the CHARM I/O Carrier. If your installation contains any standard, non-I.S. CHARMs, you must use a 20 A fuse. A 10 A fuse is suitable for use only in exclusively I.S. installations. The fuse must have a breaking capacity greater than 1500 A and a Um rating of 40 V. The fuse and fuse holder must meet IEC60079-11 requirements. You can purchase a 20 A fuse and fuse holder, for use in non-ATEX, non-IECEX applications, from Emerson. Use the following model numbers to order the fuse and fuse holder: SE4610T01: Fuse Holder and Fuse Assembly for 24VDC Power Supply of CHARMs Smart Logic Solver KL4510X1-FA1: Replacement Fuse for SE4610T01 Fuse Holder Assembly KL4510X1-GA1: Replacement Fuse Holder for SE4610T01 Fuse Holder Assembly Ground the connections as shown in the image.

title: Reset the keying mechanism on an I.S. CHARM Terminal Block
main_heading: Reset the keying mechanism on an I.S. CHARM Terminal Block
body_text: Reset the keying mechanism on an I.S. CHARM Terminal Block The keying mechanism on most I.S. CHARM Terminal Blocks is in a neutral position when shipped from the factory. In most cases, installing an I.S. CHARM sets the keying mechanism. For most I.S. CHARMs you can reset the keying mechanism if you need to remove the I.S. CHARM from the terminal block and install an I.S. CHARM of a different type. However, the I.S. CHARM Thermocouple mV Terminal Block has a fixed key setting to allow only an I.S. Thermocouple / mV input CHARM. I.S. Terminal block latch and release button Insert a small screwdriver into the release button to the left of the terminal block's latch, depress the release button, and remove the terminal block from the baseplate. Flip the terminal block 180° and notice the two small keying posts protruding from the bottom of the terminal block. Push the two keying posts completely in to return the posts to the neutral position. You will hear a click when the posts are completely pushed in. Verify that the posts are in the neutral position. In the neutral position, the ends of the posts sit slightly inside the bottom face of the terminal block. That is, the keying posts are sub flush to the bottom face of the terminal block. If the keying posts are flush with the bottom face of the terminal block, the keying posts are not yet in the neutral position. In this case, use your fingers to push the keying posts to the neutral position. Snap the terminal block back into the slot on the baseplate. You can now install an I.S. CHARM of a different type into the terminal block.

title: Label the CHARMs installed on each baseplate
main_heading: Label the CHARMs installed on each baseplate
body_text: Label the CHARMs installed on each baseplate The CHARM labeling component consist of a label support that holds a label and its protective plastic cover. Remove the label support from the baseplate before writing or typing the CHARM IDs on the label. Note: The image shows the labeling component on a CHARM Baseplate. If you are labeling I.S. CHARMs, install the labeling component on an I.S. CHARM Baseplate. CHARM labeling component Press the label support at the top hinge and remove it from the hinge post. Lift the support off of the bottom hinge post. The label support is now free of the baseplate. Slide the protective plastic cover off of the label being careful not to bend or fold it. Slide the label from the label support being careful not to bend or fold it. Write or type the CHARM IDs in the preformatted areas on the label. Slide the completed label back into the support from the top, being sure that the label passes under the label retainers and is properly seated under the top and bottom corner tabs. Repeat the previous step and insert the protective plastic cover over the label. Reattach the label support to the baseplate.

title: Link the TANK101 picture with the Overview
main_heading: Link the TANK101 picture with the Overview

title: Load licenses
body_text: Load licenses From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation: Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > DeltaV Explorer to open DeltaV Explorer. Insert the license disk into the drive. In DeltaV Explorer, select File > Licensing > Load License File . The Load License dialog opens. Select the license file to load, and then click Open . Tip: You can also select System Configuration > Setup > Licenses in the left pane of the Explorer, right-click, and then select Load License File . Read the information in the Terms and Conditions dialog and, if you agree, enter the requested information, and then click Next . If you do not agree, return the license disk and System Identifier to Emerson. Fill in the User Contact Information dialog, and then click Next . Fill in the End User Company Information dialog, and then click Next . Read the information in the Registration dialog, and then click Finish . The licenses are loaded into the License folder. Select System Configuration > Setup > Licenses to view the licenses. Now you can assign the licenses to nodes. Consider creating a backup copy of the license file. Select File > Licensing > Create License File to create a backup copy of the licenses. Note: Your licenses are exported if you completely export your DeltaV system.

title: Locate assigned CHARMs in DeltaV Explorer
main_heading: Locate assigned CHARMs in DeltaV Explorer
body_text: Locate assigned CHARMs in DeltaV Explorer The Goto commands provide a fast and easy way to find an assigned CHARM in the controller's hierarchy or a physical CHARM under the I/O Network. To find a CHARM assignment, right-click the configured CHARM under the I/O Network and select Goto CHARM Assignment . To find a configured CHARM, right-click the assigned CHARM and select Goto CHARM .

title: Locate a specific batch alias
body_text: Locate a specific batch alias This is the recommended procedure for locating a specific batch alias that you want to clean out of the database. Open the DeltaV Explorer (click Start > DeltaV Engineering > DeltaV Explorer ). Select Library/Advanced Definitions/Unit Classes . Select the Unit Class that has the alias. Select and right-click the alias, and then select References .

title: Locate and configure a connected controller
main_heading: Locate and configure a connected controller
body_text: Locate and configure a connected controller (These are general instructions and are not part of the tank process tutorial. If you have a controller and I/O connected, they are not likely to match the hardware specifications for the example.) In DeltaV Explorer, select System Configuration > Physical Network > Decommissioned Nodes . Select the decommissioned controller in the right pane. Drag the decommissioned controller to Control Network or to a specific controller placeholder. You can also commission a controller by selecting Commission from the Control Network context menu or the controller's context menu. If you drag the decommissioned controller to Control Network , a Properties dialog opens for you to enter a name for the controller. Then you will be asked if you want to auto-sense the I/O cards. For a new controller, for which you have done no configuration, you would normally click Yes . If you drag the decommissioned controller to a placeholder, such as CTLR1, you will be asked if you want to auto-sense the I/O cards. If you have already configured I/O cards for the placeholder controller (which you will learn how to do in the next section), click No . If you click Yes , the auto-sensed cards will be compared to the ones configured, and any mismatches will be displayed. You can replace any empty slot with an auto-sensed card. To replace mismatched cards, you must delete the configured cards. Tip: You can identify a decommissioned controller and confirm that it is communicating by selecting and right-clicking the controller, and then selecting Properties . Select the Controller tab, and then select Flash lights to make the controller's lights all flash at the same time. You can then select Stop flashing and click OK to close the dialog. Important: You can decommission a controller by selecting and right-clicking the controller, and then selecting Decommission . The left pane still shows the controller name. This placeholder still contains configuration information, such as I/O Device Tags and assigned modules. Do not delete the controller placeholder. Deleting a controller placeholder will also delete the I/O configuration, including any Device Tags assigned to the controller's I/O.

title: Lock and unlock the SLS 1508 Logic Solver
main_heading: Lock and unlock the SLS 1508 Logic Solver
body_text: Lock and unlock the SLS 1508 Logic Solver The Lock and Unlock functions launch the Secure Write Mechanism. This mechanism verifies the operator has the correct security key (SIS Can Download) and guarantees that the value sent cannot be corrupted in the process of sending it to the logic solver. The Logic Solver must be unlocked to commission, decommission, download, or debug SIS modules. Locking also prevents a user-initiated logic solver switchover. From DeltaV Explorer or Diagnostics, navigate to the logic solver in the SIS Network. Right-click and select Lock or Unlock . On the confirmation dialog, click Confirm to make the change. Locking or unlocking a logic solver generates an event in the event log.

title: Lock and unlock the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver
main_heading: Lock and unlock the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver
body_text: Lock and unlock the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver The Lock and Unlock functions launch the Secure Write Mechanism. This mechanism verifies the operator has the correct security key (SIS Can Download) and guarantees that the value sent cannot be corrupted in the process of sending it to the logic solver. The Lock and Unlock functions launch the Secure Write Mechanism. This mechanism verifies that the operator has the correct security key (SIS Can Download) and guarantees that the value sent cannot be corrupted in the process of sending it to the logic solver. The Logic Solver must be unlocked to commission, decommission, download, debug SIS modules or allow HART write commands. Locking also prevents a user-initiated logic solver switchover. The Unlock function can be inhibited with a physical key switch on the CSLS or the SIS Controller. If Enable Key-lock has been selected on the properties dialog for this CSLS, the physical inhibit key switch on the CSLS must be in the unlocked position to proceed. If the SIS Controller associated with this CSLS includes a Keylock EIP, the physical key switch on the SIS Controller must be in the unlocked position to proceed. From DeltaV Explorer or Diagnostics, navigate to the logic solver under the Local Safety Network under a SIS Controller. Right-click and select Lock , Unlock or Unlock (Timed) . Unlock (Timed) enables you to unlock for a time you specify. When the time expires, the CSLS returns to the locked state. On the confirmation dialog, click Confirm to make the change. Locking or unlocking a logic solver generates an event in the event log. Related information Logic Solver Lock and Unlock functions

title: Connect power to LS CHARM I/O
main_heading: Connect power to LS CHARM I/O
body_text: Connect power to LS CHARM I/O Redundant 24 VDC power is delivered from bulk power supplies to LS CHARM I/O through the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver (CSLS) Carrier. Emerson recommends connecting the bulk power supply to a surge suppression/filter device. Note: In most cases, removing a CHARM from the CHARM baseplate removes power from any connected field device. However, CHARM type, terminal block type, and external power distribution can affect whether removing the CHARM removes power from a field device. Powering the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Carrier For this procedure, it is assumed that redundant bulk 24 VDC power supplies and surge suppression/filter devices are already installed. Connect the AC power that is feeding the bulk power supplies to surge suppression/filter devices. Connect the bulk power supply to the power terminals on the CSLS Carrier. Ground the bulk power supplies as shown in the image.

title: Remapping secure parameters
body_text: Remapping secure parameters As a configuration evolves some secure parameters may no longer be referenced so the database automatically removes them from their assigned LSNB publisher slots without changing or affecting the mapping of the remaining secure parameters. Logic solvers that are unaffected by the removing of secure parameter references therefore do not require downloading. Any secure parameters added to the database later are placed in the empty slots. It is also possible to manually remap secure parameters by selecting the Enable remapping check box. CAUTION: Manual remapping of secure parameters may be required in rare circumstances and should be performed only by experienced personnel. Manual remapping affects all modules referencing the remapped secure parameters. It is possible to manually move secure parameters to free slots. That is, you can reassign a currently mapped reference to an open publisher slot in the same LSNB. For example: LSNB1 exists on an LSN which has CSLSs with several secure parameters referenced by other LSNBs on the Global Safety Network, so that LSNB1 has at least two publishers. One of these publishers has had secure parameters deleted from it so that it has at least one free slot. Another publisher has a secure parameter of the same type (Boolean or non-Boolean) as the free slot, so that it can be remapped there. The Secure Parameters dialog for LSNB1 is open. To remap secure parameters manually: Select the Enable remapping check box The Show references to parameters check box is automatically selected and then grayed out. The Secure Parameters dialog refreshes. References appear and remain visible as long as remapping is enabled. Select a secure parameter to be remapped from the list. This makes the Remap button selectable. Click the Remap button. The Remap Secure Parameter dialog opens. The Remap to… area lists all publishers in the LSNB that the selected secure parameter can be remapped to. The first of these publishers is selected. If there are no publishers that the secure parameter can be remapped to, the display of the Remap Secure Parameter dialog closes and an error message appears. Select a different publisher to remap the secure parameter to or select Cancel to close the dialog. Click the OK button. A confirmation dialog appears that lists the SIS modules and CSLSs that contain global references to the secure parameter and explains that the remap changes their CRCs so that they will need to be revalidated and re-downloaded. Click Yes to confirm the remap of the selected secure parameter. The Remap Secure Parameter dialog disappears and the Secure Parameters Dialog reappears. Remap additional secure parameters as needed. Uncheck the Enable remapping checkbox in the Secure Parameters dialog. The Show references to parameters checkbox becomes selectable. Uncheck the Show references to parameters check box. The Secure Parameters dialog no longer displays references.

title: Make the formula available to an operator to load
main_heading: Make the formula available to an operator to load
body_text: Make the formula available to an operator to load Before you can use the formula in a batch, you need to make it available to an operator to load. To open the Properties dialog for the formula, use one of the following two methods: Select and right-click one of the values in the formula, and then select Formula Properties from the context menu. Select and right-click the formula in the DeltaV Explorer, and then select Properties from the context menu. To make the formula available to an operator, complete the following steps: Open the Properties dialog for the DARK formula. Select the Operator can load check box, and then click OK . Repeat steps 1 and 2 for the LIGHT and MEDIUM formulas. Save and download the recipe. Note: Whenever you make changes to a recipe, you need to save and download it before you can use it.

title: Manage the firewall application rules
body_text: Manage the firewall application rules Before you can apply any of the rules found in DeltaV Security Administration , you must enable the Windows firewall for the appropriate profiles and network interface cards (NICS). Important: The Windows firewall profiles should not be enabled without fully understanding the potential impact on communications between DeltaV and any applications external to DeltaV on the either the DeltaV 2.5 network or applications in networks above the 2.5 network. With the Windows firewall enabled, all default Windows firewall rules are applied. The DeltaV rules are in addition to the default Windows firewall rules. Important: Do not edit the DeltaV rules. If you need a specific rule, you must create a new rule and configure it as needed. Any rules created by you are your responsibility to test and validate with your DeltaV system. You can create a new rule by copying the existing DeltaV rule and modifying it. Open the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security application and select the DeltaV rule (for example, OPC: OPC UA Server). Copy and paste the rule and rename it to something meaningful. Edit the rule's properties to change what is needed; for example, a different default OPC UA Server TCP port to match what you have configured in DeltaV Explorer (for that protocol). Enable the new rule as an incoming rule on non-DeltaV networks. You are still responsible for testing and validating this change works in your DeltaV system. Open the DeltaV Security Administration application. Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Security Administration . From the DeltaV Security Administration application, expand the Windows Firewall for DeltaV Workstations item in the hierarchy. Select Manage Firewall Rules . Select (place a checkmark for) any rules you want to enable. Unchecked - not enabled; that is, inbound communication for this port is blocked. Note: The rules are applied by port, so if a rule is not selected, then inbound communication on the port is blocked, unless another rule has that same port open. Checked - enabled as an allow rule; that is, communication for this port is allowed. Click Apply Firewall Rules button. The selected rules are now applied to the enabled Windows Firewall profiles for the network cards specified (in the Windows Firewall Advanced Settings).

title: Manage Telnet communications through the firewall IPD
main_heading: Manage Telnet communications through the firewall IPD
body_text: Manage Telnet communications through the firewall IPD To increase protection from network intrusions that can be caused by Telnet packets, you can configure the firewall IPD to drop all incoming packets that contain the Telnet protocol. This ensures that Telnet connections cannot get through the firewall IPD. However, disabling Telnet prevents the use of one DeltaV diagnostic function. If Telnet is disabled, you may see a message similar to the following: Could not open connection to the host. Connect failed The message indicates that DeltaV is attempting and failing to determine network connectivity to the controller. You can use the Multicast Ping option to detect the controller. Alternatively, you can temporarily enable Telnet on the firewall IPD and then disable it again if necessary. Complete the following steps to disable Telnet. Log on to the firewall IPD from the Management station. Launch HiView (version 3.0 or later). Enter the IP address of the firewall IPD in the URL field. On the firewall IPD login screen, enter the administrator credentials. The default user name is Admin and the default password is Emerson1. However, this should have been changed when you initially configured the firewall IPD. Expand Network Security in the hierarchy and select Packet Filter/Incoming Packets . Scroll down through the Incoming IP Packets rules until you find the two rows that have Telnet in the Description column with the Source IP column showing a DeltaV primary IP address (10.4.0.0) and a DeltaV secondary IP address (10.8.0.0). The Destination Port is 23 for both. Note that both Telnet rows initially show accept in the Action column. Select drop in the Action column for each of the two Telnet rows. There is a difference between drop and reject . Drop silently discards the incoming package. Reject results in an ICMP error or TCP Reset being returned. Find the two rows labeled Diagnostics with a Destination Port of 18550 . Select drop in the Action column for each of the two Diagnostics rows. Save this configuration. Click the Set button at the bottom of this screen. On the Load/Save screen, click New . Enter no_telnet when prompted for a name. Click OK . The firewall IPD will now drop all incoming packets containing the Telnet protocol. Save the running configuration to Non-volatile memory and AutoConfiguration Adapter by clicking the Save to NVM+ACA button at the bottom of the Load/Save screen.

title: Manually copy DeltaV Operate displays into a system with Version Control enabled
main_heading: Manually copy DeltaV Operate displays into a system with Version Control enabled
body_text: Manually copy DeltaV Operate displays into a system with Version Control enabled There are times when you will need to copy a display file from one DeltaV system to another DeltaV system (for example, when creating DeltaV Zone capable displays). To do this when Version Control for Displays is enabled, follow these steps: Important: You cannot rename any DeltaV Operate files using Windows Explorer. All files must be renamed from within DeltaV Operate using the Save As function. Renaming using Windows Explorer or any method other than DeltaV Operate makes that graphic unusable by DeltaV Operate. Copy the file from the source workstation to the destination workstation using Windows Explorer (you may need to use a storage device such as a memory stick if the two systems are not connected). Paste the file into the DeltaV\DVData\DisplayWorking\Pic folder on the destination workstation (the one that has VCAT for DeltaV Displays enabled). Open DeltaV Operate on the destination workstation. From the DeltaV Operate system tree in the Pictures folder, open the picture that was just pasted into the DisplayWorking\Pic folder. Close the picture. Version Control for DeltaV Displays adds that picture to the VCAT database. Continue with all pictures you added to the destination workstation so they are added to the VCAT database. You can then download your workstations to propagate the displays to the Operator Stations.

title: Manually decommission and unassign a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver
main_heading: Manually decommission and unassign a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver
body_text: Manually decommission and unassign a CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Performing these manual steps resets the CSLS and the non-volatile memory within the Safety Network Ports to the default unassigned state. Unplug the primary and secondary Safety Network Ports from the carrier. Remove both CSLSs from the carrier and install them in the opposite slots: move the CSLS in the right slot to the left slot and the CSLS in the left slot to the right slot. Wait one to two minutes for the CSLS to boot up. Plug the primary and secondary Safety Network Ports into their original locations. Note: This procedure can be useful in the rare case that a new database has been brought online or the CSLS has been removed from one Local Safety Network and placed on another Local Safety Network before it was unassigned.

title: Manually decommission an EIOC
body_text: Manually decommission an EIOC Performing these manual steps resets the EIOC and the non-volatile memory within the Ethernet Isolation Ports to the default decommissioned state. Unplug the primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports from the carrier. Remove both EIOCs from the carrier and install them in the opposite slots: move the EIOC in the right slot to the left slot and the EIOC in the left slot to the right slot. Wait one or two minutes for the EIOC to boot up. Plug the primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports into their original locations. Note: This procedure can be useful in the rare case that a new database has been brought online or the EIOC has been removed from one Area Control Network and placed on another Area Control Network before it was decommissioned.

title: Manually decommission a SZ Controller
body_text: Manually decommission a SZ Controller Performing these manual steps resets the SZ Controller and the non-volatile memory within the Ethernet Isolation Ports to the decommissioned state. Unplug the primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports from the carrier. Remove both SZ controllers from the carrier and install them in the opposite slots: move the SZ controller in the right slot to the left slot and the SZ controller in the left slot to the right slot. Wait one or two minutes for the SZ to come up. Plug the primary and secondary Ethernet Isolation Ports into their original locations. Note: This procedure can be useful in the rare case that a new database was brought online before the SZ controller was decommissioned.

title: Manually decommission a virtual EIOC
body_text: Manually decommission a virtual EIOC If a database is changed when a system is in flux such as during development or when it is used to create a training scenario, it is possible that the database could get out of synch with the commissioned state of the vEIOC. Follow these steps to decommission a vEIOC. Select the vEIOC in DeltaV Virtual Studio. Click Turn Off. Create and configure a new vEIOC in DeltaV Virtual Studio. Refer to the DeltaV Virtualization media for more information on DeltaV Virtual Studio.

title: Manually proof test input LS CHARMs
main_heading: Manually proof test input LS CHARMs
body_text: Manually proof test input LS CHARMs The following procedure should be used for manually proof testing input LS CHARMs. Appropriate steps should be taken in the SIS module and/or the process to ensure a trip does not occur when proof testing. The LS CHARM can be manually reset only when the CSLS is Unlocked. Select the CSLS in Diagnostics Explorer. If the value of the Locked parameter is Yes in the contents pane, right-click the CSLS and select Unlock . Click Confirm on the Secure Write Confirmation dialog. Right-click the LS CHARM and select Force Proof Test Reset . When prompted, click OK in the Exploring DeltaV Diagnostics dialog. Then click Confirm in the Secure Write Confirmation dialog. Drive the input to appropriate values as determined by the proof test of the input device and observe the correct value changes in the SIS module containing the input.

title: Manually proof test output LS CHARMs
main_heading: Manually proof test output LS CHARMs
body_text: Manually proof test output LS CHARMs The following procedure should be used for manually proof testing output CHARMs. Appropriate steps should be taken in the SIS module and/or the process to ensure a trip does not occur when proof testing. The LS CHARM can be manually reset only when the CSLS is Unlocked. Select the CSLS in Diagnostics Explorer. If the value of the Locked parameter is Yes in the contents pane, right-click the CSLS and select Unlock . Click Confirm in the Secure Write Confirmation dialog. Right-click the LS CHARM and select Force Proof Test Reset . When prompted, click OK in the Exploring DeltaV Diagnostics dialog. Then click Confirm in the Secure Write Confirmation dialog. For a DTA LS CHARM, observe that the Final element changes state either at the device or via feedback into the SIS module. Important: Safety outputs are de-energized during proof testing. Be sure to take appropriate precautions before proceeding. For redundant DTA LS CHARMs, it is necessary to observe that the Final element changes state for both LS CHARMs. You can either force a proof test one one LS CHARM and observe that the Final element changes state while the LS CHARM is in its proof test cycle (then repeat for the partner) or unplug one of the pair and observe that the Final element changes state (repeat for the other LS CHARM in the pair). Important: Safety outputs are de-energized during proof testing. Be sure to take appropriate precautions before proceeding. For an ETA LS CHARM, drive the value in the SIS module to ensure the final element can be energized. Important: Safety outputs are energized when driving the value ON from the SIS module. Be sure to manually isolate the process before proceeding. For redundant ETA LS CHARMs, it is necessary to ensure that either of the LS CHARMs can energize the final element when required. You can either force a proof test on one LS CHARM and drive the output from the other while the LS CHARM is in its proof test cycle (then repeat for the partner) or unplug one of the pair and drive the value in the SIS module to ensure the final element can be energized (repeat for the other LS CHARM in the pair). Important: Safety outputs are energized when driving the value ON from the SIS module. Be sure to manually isolate the process before proceeding.

title: Manually proof test redundant CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS)
main_heading:
Manually proof test redundant CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers
	 (CSLS)
body_text: Manually proof test redundant CHARMs Smart Logic Solvers (CSLS) The procedure for a redundant CSLS allows the proof test to be done online without adversely affecting the running process. The logic solver can be manually reset only when the CSLS is Unlocked. Select the CSLS in Diagnostics Explorer. If the value of the Locked parameter is Yes in the contents pane, right-click on the CSLS and select Unlock . Click Confirm on the Secure Write Confirmation dialog. Right-click the CSLS and select Force Reset on Standby . Click Confirm on the confirmation dialog. Wait for the Standby card to complete power-up tests and become configured by the Active card. The Partner Not Available maintenance alert goes inactive when the Standby card is fully configured. Right-click the CSLS and select Switchover . Click Confirm on the confirmation dialog. The previously reset Standby card becomes the new Active card and the new Standby card goes through power-up tests and is configured by the new Active card. The proof test timer is 0. There will be event records for the user reset and switchover commands and for the CSLS cards, confirming that power-up tests completed successfully.

title: Map the security account for Advanced Continuous Historian
main_heading: Map the security account for Advanced Continuous Historian
body_text: Map the security account for Advanced Continuous Historian On the Application Station where you are running the Advanced Continuous Historian, you must use the PI System Management Tools (PI SMT) application to complete the following steps: Under Collectives and Servers , select the server or collective. In the System Management Tools pane, click Security > Mappings and Trusts . Click the Mappings tab. Open the Add New Mapping dialog by clicking the New button in the toolbar. In the Windows Account field, specify an Active Directory principal or a local Windows group or user account (typically, the DeltaVAdmin account). To specify the account, complete either of the following tasks: Click the Browse button, and then select the account. Type the account name in the Windows Account field. After typing the account name, click the Resolve SID button to verify that this is a valid account. If the account is valid, a Security Identifier (SID) appears in the field. Otherwise, an error message appears. In the PI Server list, select the server where you want to create the mapping. In the PI Identity field, enter a PI identity, group, or user (typically the piadmins Group or piadmin User). Click the Browse button to open the Select PI Identity , PI Group , or PI User dialog. Use the Type option to filter the choices, and then select a PI identity, PI group, or PI user from the list. Click the OK button. Click the OK button to create the mapping and close the Add New Mapping dialog. Related information Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system

title: Migrate CHARM I/O Cards (CIOCs) online
body_text: Migrate CHARM I/O Cards (CIOCs) online Verify that the LEDs on the current active and standby CIOCs are green and steady. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows no Bad Integrity on the current CIOC's redundancy subsystem and on the standby CIOC. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows that the standby CIOC is present and available for switchover. Replace the current standby CIOC with the new model standby CIOC. Use the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility to upgrade the CIOC to the correct version of the DeltaV software. Wait for the migrated standby CIOC to become reconfigured and its LED to go to steady. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows no Bad Integrity on the current active CIOC's redundancy subsystem and on the standby CIOC. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows that the standby CIOC is present and available for switchover. Manually initiate a CIOC switchover from DeltaV Diagnostics. The newly replaced standby CIOC becomes the new active CIOC. Replace the new standby CIOC with the new model CIOC. Use the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility to upgrade the new CIOC to the correct version of the DeltaV software. Launch DeltaV Explorer and ensure that the controller model displayed within controller properties have updated to the correct model for both cards. If the cards' models in DeltaV Explorer have not updated then download the Setup Data for the CIOC.

title: Migrate controllers online
body_text: Migrate controllers online Verify that the Active and Standby LEDs on the current active and standby controllers are steady. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows no Bad Integrity on the current controller's redundancy subsystem and on the standby controller. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows that the standby controller is present and available for switchover. Replace the current standby controller with the new model standby controller. Use the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility to upgrade the controller to the correct version of the DeltaV software. Wait for the migrated standby controller to become reconfigured and its LED to go to steady. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows no Bad Integrity on the current active controller's redundancy subsystem and on the standby controller. Ensure that DeltaV Diagnostics shows that the standby controller is present and available for switchover. Manually initiate a controller switchover from DeltaV Diagnostics. The newly replaced standby controller becomes the new active controller. Replace the standby controller with the new model controller. Use the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility to upgrade the new controller to the correct version of the DeltaV software. Launch DeltaV Explorer and ensure that the controller model displayed within controller properties have updated to the correct model for both controllers. If the controllers' models in DeltaV Explorer have not updated then download the Setup Data for the controller.

title: Migrate from the DeltaV Continuous Historian to OSIsoft PI Server
main_heading:
Migrate from the DeltaV Continuous Historian to OSIsoft PI
    Server
body_text: Migrate from the DeltaV Continuous Historian to OSIsoft PI Server After upgrading DeltaV on a system where you have been using the DeltaV Continuous Historian, you can migrate to OSIsoft PI Server by completing the following steps: Upgrade DeltaV on the Application Station where you were using the DeltaV Continuous Historian. If you plan to run PI Server on the Application Station in the DeltaV Area Control Network (ACN), complete step t_migrate_dvch_to_enterprise_pi_server.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_54__substep_1E31FAD4A5D64F35B495B46FDF44CF6C below. If you plan to run PI Server on a remote Application Station or a non-DeltaV workstation outside the DeltaV ACN, complete step t_migrate_dvch_to_enterprise_pi_server.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_54__substep_62182FB947084AB3A612A2C134B02973 below. Install and configure PI Server and the PI Asset Framework (PI AF) Server on the Application Station in the DeltaV ACN according to the documentation provided by OSIsoft. Install and configure PI Server and the PI AF Server on the remote Application Station or a non-DeltaV workstation outside the DeltaV ACN according to the documentation provided by OSIsoft. Install the DeltaV Smart Connector on the Application Station in the DeltaV ACN according to the documentation provided by OSIsoft. Enable PI Server in DeltaV Explorer by right-clicking the Continuous Historian subsystem under the Application Station where you installed the DeltaV Smart Connector, and then selecting Properties . On the General tab, select the Enabled check box, and then select the Use Enterprise Historian option. Download the Application Station where you installed the DeltaV Smart Connector. The configuration of the DeltaV Continuous Historian that you were previously using on the Application Station is preserved and migrated to the new installation of PI Server. Important: Any historical data previously collected with the DeltaV Continuous Historian is not merged into the PI Server database. For more information, refer to the DeltaV Historian Upgrade Planning Guide white paper on the Emerson web site, also available from your Emerson field sales office or local business partner. Related information Historian installation The Continuous Historian subsystem

    to OSIsoft PI Server

title: Modify the AGITATE phase restarting logic
main_heading: Modify the AGITATE phase restarting logic
body_text: Modify the AGITATE phase restarting logic Change the restarting logic according to the figure below. Save the AGITATE phase. Download. Do not select any on-line changes.

title: Modify an alarm
body_text: Modify an alarm Alarms have been set up in the PID_LOOP template, which we used as the basis for the FIC-101 module. Only three of the alarms, HI_ALM, LO_ALM, and PVBAD_ALM, are enabled. For the example, you will modify HI_ALM slightly to change the value from 95 to 90. This means that an alarm will be activated if the flow goes above 90 gallons per minute. In the Alarm view, double-click HI_ALM (or right-click it and select Properties ). Change the Limit value from 95 to 90, and then click OK .

title: Modify a function
body_text: Modify a function When using the DeltaV Function Wizard to edit existing DeltaV functions, select the same range of cells that the formula originally used (that is, one cell for DVWrite, one cell for DVRead, two cells for DVReadWithStatus). The DeltaV Function Wizard will then fill in the fields with the existing function information, and be ready for editing. Related information Create a DVRead Function Create a DVWrite function Modify the update interval Set the update interval

title: Modify the control module
body_text: Modify the control module In the left pane of DeltaV Explorer, under TANK-101, double-click FIC-101 to open the module. If necessary, click the List button to display the contents of the right pane as shown in the next figure. Select PID1 (the PID loop function block) and make the following changes to the parameters in the right pane. Double-click IO_IN . In the Properties box, enter the Device Tag of FT-1. Double-click IO_OUT , and then enter the Device Tag of FY-1. Double-click GAIN , and then change the value from .5 to 1. Double-click RESET , and then change the value from 10 to 3 (that is, 3 seconds per repeat). Double-click PV_SCALE , and then change the Engineering unit to GPM (gallons per minute).

title: Modify the control module template
body_text: Modify the control module template The module template is fairly simple, consisting of only one function block. To customize the module for the tank application, all you need to do is identify the Device Signal Tags for the input and output. (Device Tags are assigned to the I/O channels as part of the I/O card configuration process.) In the Diagram view, click the Device Control function block, DC1. Four small black squares (called "handles") appear at the corners to indicate that this block is the currently selected item on the diagram. Select and right-click a parameter in the Parameter view, and then select Filter Parameter List . The Parameter Filtering dialog opens. In the System group, select Common configuration to display the parameters most commonly used for configuring process control, and select On-line to display the parameters most commonly used for operating a process. Deselect any other boxes that may be checked, and then click OK to close the dialog. In the Parameter View, select IO_IN_1 . You may have to scroll down the list to find it. Double-click IO_IN_1 to open the Properties dialog. In the Device Tag field, enter LSC-1. (LSC-1 is the Device Tag used in our tank example for Limit Switch-Closed.) The Device Tags for the tank application are listed in the table in Control modules used in the tutorials . The IO_IN_1 parameter is given a value of FIELD_VAL_D. (You can click the Parameter field to see this value. It also appears in the Parameter view.) LSC-1, together with the FIELD_VAL_D parameter define the Device Signal Tag (DST). (If you have configured placeholders for the I/O cards, you can browse for the Device Tags. Clicking the Browse button opens a dialog that lists all the configured I/O card channels and their assigned Device Tags. You can scroll down the list, select the appropriate Device Tag, and then click OK . Click the Alphabetic tab to alphabetize the list and scroll past the entries beginning with COxx to get to the Device Tag names such as LSC-1.) Click OK . In the Parameter View, double-click IO_OUT_1. The Properties dialog appears. In the Device Tag field, enter XV-1, and then click OK . XV-1 is the Device Tag used in our example for the Block Valve. The DST is given a default parameter value of OUT_D. The Parameter list should now look like this: Related information Configuring the hardware Control modules used in the tutorials

title: Modify the expression for the Monitor block
main_heading: Modify the expression for the Monitor block
body_text: Modify the expression for the Monitor block Select BLOCK1 and change the name to MONITOR. Right-click, and then select Expression from the context menu. Modify the text of the expression, using the Insert Internal Parameter and Insert Named State buttons as necessary to match the logic shown below: IF (( '/+/WDOG_STATE.CV' = '$phase_wdog_states:FAILED' ) AND ('/+/FAIL_INDEX.CV' = 0)) THEN '/+/FAIL_INDEX' := 'phase_failures:PLM Watchdog Failed'; ELSE; IF (( '/+/SWITCHED_OVER.CV' = TRUE ) AND ('/+/FAIL_INDEX.CV' = 0)) THEN '/+/FAIL_INDEX' := 'phase_failures:Controller Switchover Detected'; '/+/SWITCHED_OVER.CV' := FALSE; ELSE; IF (('^/BFI1/OUT_D.CV' = 1) AND ( '/+/FAIL_INDEX.CV' = 0 )) THEN '/+/FAIL_INDEX' := '^/FAIL_MESSAGE/OUT1.CV'; ENDIF; ENDIF; ENDIF; Click Parse to check the expression and make any corrections necessary. Save the AGITATE phase class. Download the controller or workstation so that changes to the AGITATE phase logic as well as changes to the phase_failures named set are sent to the node. Do not accept the online values for uploading.

title: Modify module properties to allow equipment arbitration
main_heading: Modify module properties to allow equipment arbitration
body_text: Modify module properties to allow equipment arbitration First, you will modify the properties of the control modules (XV_COLOR_500 and XV_COLOR_600) that control the color inlet valves to allow them to participate in equipment arbitration. In the DeltaV Explorer, select the module XV_COLOR_500 under System Configuration/Control Strategies/EXTERIOR_PAINT/PAINT_BLEND/UM_BLEND_500 . Right-click and select Properties from the context menu. On the Arbitration tab of the Properties dialog, select the Participate in equipment arbitration check box . The Equipment ID is automatically assigned the next available number. Note: The equipment IDs in the examples may not match those in your system. Whenever they are referenced in the phase logic, you need to substitute the ID numbers used in your system. Leave the Maximum Owners value at 1 and click OK . Repeat this procedure for module XV_COLOR_600 (in UM_BLEND_600).

title: Modify the phase_failures set
body_text: Modify the phase_failures set In the DeltaV Explorer, select Named Sets under System Configuration/Setup . Double-click the phase_failures set to open the Properties dialog. Click Add . In the State Properties dialog, type the name of the new failure state, Inlet Valve Open, and accept the assigned value of 4. Make sure that the Visible and User selectable check boxes are selected. Add the failure states Agitator Stopped and Outlet Not Closed. The phase_failures set should now look like the following: Click OK to save the named set.

title: Modify the FEED_FLOW parameter
body_text: Modify the FEED_FLOW parameter In DeltaV Explorer, select TOTAL_FLOW_100 under the unit module UM_COLOR_100. Right-click the FEED_FLOW parameter in the right pane and open the Properties dialog. Browse for the following External parameter path: UM_COLOR_100/EM_TOTAL_100/FIC_COLOR_100/PID1/PV Repeat the above steps for the FEED_FLOW parameters in UM_COLOR_200 and UM_COLOR_300, substituting 200 (or 300) where appropriate in the names.

title: Modify the LEVEL_INDICATOR class
body_text: Modify the LEVEL_INDICATOR class Open LEVEL_INDICATOR in Control Studio and select the AI block. Select the tuning parameter SIMULATE, and then open the Properties dialog. Select Enabled , check the Allow instance value to be configured box, and then click OK . Select the I/O parameter OUT_SCALE and open the Properties dialog. Change the 100% scale to 1000 and the Engineering unit to gallons (gal), and then check the Allow instance value to be configured box. Select the L_TYPE tuning parameter, and then change the named state to Direct . Select the HI_ALM parameter in the Alarm Parameters window, and then open the Properties dialog. Change the Limit value to 950, and then click OK . Open the Properties dialog for the module class and, on the Displays tab, browse for and select Process as the primary control display . Save the module, and then close Control Studio.

title: Modify the update interval
body_text: Modify the update interval There are two ways to modify the update interval. Related information Create a DVRead Function Create a DVWrite function Modify a function Set the update interval Using the Configure Update Interval dialog Open the Configure Update Interval dialog. Select the Add-Ins tab. In the DeltaV group, select Runtime Data > Configure Update Interval . If the named range containing the update interval exists, the cell address is shown in the Named Range Location text box. This can be changed by clicking the Selected button. Enter the update interval. Click OK. Manually updating the interval Select the cell that contains the update interval. To find the cell that contains the update interval, Select the Home tab. In the Editing group, select Find & Select > Go To... Select DVUpdateInterval . Click OK . Type a new value. If the value is not valid (must be a whole number between 1 and 65), the default rate of 10 seconds is used.

title: Modify and add an action to the FILL running logic
main_heading: Modify and add an action to the FILL running logic
body_text: Modify and add an action to the FILL running logic Double-click the step. In the S1 Properties dialog, enter the step description: Close outlet. Rename the step to CLOSE_OUTLET. (Click S1 in the step box to rename it.) With the CLOSE_OUTLET step box selected, select and right-click Step Actions View . Select Add to add an action. The Action Properties dialog opens. Enter the description (optional) as "Ensure that the color tank outlet valve is closed," leave the Type as Assignment , and leave the Qualifier as Pulse . Click Expression Assistant to open the Expression Editor. Click Insert Alias . Browse under Tanks > COLOR for the desired alias. Note that COLOR_OUT_VLV may appear in the Browse list as both a module block ( ) and a simple alias ( ). Double-clicking the module block lets you browse to the module parameter for VALVE_SP, whereas selecting the simple alias allows no further browsing. The first part of the expression should be defined as shown in the following: '//#COLOR_OUT_VLV#/VALVE_SP' Next, click the Assignment button or type := . Then, click Insert Named State . In the Browse dialog, select the valve setpoint named state (vlvnc-sp) and the state of CLOSE. The completed expression now appears in the Expression Editor: '//#COLOR_OUT_VLV#/VALVE_SP' := 'vlvnc-sp:CLOSE' Click Parse to check the expression. If the parsing completes without errors, click OK . Otherwise, correct the expression as needed. The expression now appears in the Action Properties box. Click OK . The action text appears in the Step Actions View. Rename the step action, A1, to CLOSE_OUT_VLV.

title: Monitor MQ, MX, PK , SX, SQ, or SZ controller or Ethernet I/O card performance
main_heading:
Monitor 
	 MQ, MX, 
	 PK 
	 , SX, SQ, 
	 or SZ controller 
	 or Ethernet I/O card 
	 performance
body_text: Monitor MQ, MX, PK , SX, SQ, or SZ controller or Ethernet I/O card performance To monitor the performance of MQ, MX, SX, SQ, PK or SZ controllers ; or, Ethernet I/O cards (EIOC) performance, open the Controller Performance dialog in DeltaV Diagnostics by right-clicking the controller, and then selecting Time Utilization Chart from the shortcut menu. MQ, MX, SX, SQ, PK and SZ controller and EIOC resources are partitioned and allocated for control and communication. The Controller Performance dialog shows a graphical representation of the controller's runtime performance based on an indexed value from 1 to 5. Specifically, the meaning of each index value is: Index Performance indicated 1 An overloaded condition 2 A heavily loaded but supported condition 3 or 4 A moderately loaded and supported condition 5 A lightly loaded and supported condition The gray bar for each of the following performance indices turns progressively more purple in color if performance heads in the direction of the "Requires Attention" value of 1: Control Performance Index (CONTROL_INDEX) is an indicator of controller module execution. Included in this metric is the amount of CPU time spent executing control for the high, medium, and low priority modules. Comms Performance Index (COMMS_INDEX) is an indicator of the data that is transmitted and received by the controller. This metric takes into account bandwidth comparisons in terms of the average amount of data sent and received as compared to the maximum bandwidth that is supported for the controller, solicited and unsolicited data transfers, the amount of Remote I/O data sent and received, and the depth of the communications queue. System Performance Index (SYSTEM_INDEX) is an all inclusive indicator of the controller processor's total free time. Free Memory Index (FREMEM_INDEX) is an all inclusive indicator of the controller's free memory. In addition, the Overall Performance Index , located on the right, compares the smallest value of the Control Performance Index , the Comms Performance Index , and the System Performance Index . The Overall Performance Index listed is always equal to the controller's Perf_Index diagnostic parameter.

title: Move and resize the toolbox
body_text: Move and resize the toolbox Click the Toolbox title bar, hold the mouse button down, drag to a new location, and release the mouse button. Point to any corner or side of the Toolbox . The pointer changes to a two-sided arrow. Hold the mouse button down and drag to reshape the box. Release the mouse button when the Toolbox is in the desired shape. Repeat the moving and resizing steps as needed to suit your personal preferences.

title: Move the simulation modules to the process cell
main_heading: Move the simulation modules to the process cell
body_text: Move the simulation modules to the process cell In the next exercises, we will be testing the FILL phase. Before we do this we need to move the simulation modules that we imported as part of the Startup.fhx file to the PAINT_BLEND process cell so that they will be available for our testing and simulation activities. Click SIMULATION in the left pane of the DeltaV Explorer (under System Configuration/Control Strategies ). In the right pane, select all the simulation modules. Drag the simulation modules to the PAINT_BLEND process cell. Assign the simulation modules to the workstation or controller. Download.

title: Create an Application Station
body_text: Create an Application Station In DeltaV Explorer, create a single Application Station by right-clicking Control Network under System Configuration/Physical Network , and then selecting New > Application Station . Note: This will be the preferred active node. The preferred standby is created by enabling the redundant subsystem in the Properties dialog of this workstation. Do not create two Application Stations in DeltaV Explorer. On the General page of the Properties dialog, specify a name for the Application Station. Important: As a general rule, do not specify an Application Station name that ends with the characters _S. When the DeltaV system creates a pair of Application Stations for redundant subsystems, it appends these characters to whatever name you specify as the base name for the Application Station. Having a pair of Application Stations named nodename _S and nodename _S_S could result in misleading or undesirable results. On the Redundancy page of the Properties dialog, select the Enable a redundant subsystem option, and then select the Batch option. Important: After enabling the redundant subsystem feature on a pair of Application Stations, you cannot also enable any other subsystems, either redundant or simplex on this Application Station. Before enabling the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, read the topic, Operational Considerations for Redundant Batch Subsystem. You can optionally enable the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, if, for example, either of the Application Stations will be located in an unmanned facility. Select Enable Direct Link for Batch Synchronization if you are connecting the pair with a direct connection. Click OK to close the Properties dialog for the Application Station. Export a workstation configuration file for the new Application Station. (Click File > Export > Workstation Configuration ). Save the workstation configuration file to removable media or to a network location that can be accessed from the Application Stations you will be configuring. You can use the default name for a workstation configuration file, DevData.cfg, or specify a different file name. Related information Operational considerations for Redundant Batch subsystem

title: Finish the installation
body_text: Finish the installation Assign licenses for the Application Stations and Redundant Batch, as needed. Note: There is no reason to assign licenses to the Application Stations for DeltaV software components that are not designed to coexist with the redundant subsystem feature. For example, you should not license subsystems such as Continuous Historian on the Application Stations, because they cannot be enabled simultaneously with Redundant Batch. In DeltaV Explorer, enable the Batch Executive (and Campaign Manager, if needed) on the Application Station pair. In DeltaV Explorer, download the Application Station pair. Go to DeltaV Diagnostics and verify that all communications and statuses are good.

title: Install the DeltaV software on the primary Application Station (the preferred active)
main_heading: Install the DeltaV software on the primary Application Station (the preferred active)
body_text: Install the DeltaV software on the primary Application Station (the preferred active) Using the DeltaV installation disks, run the setup program on one of the Application Stations. When prompted to select your workstation type, select the Local Application Station option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier in DeltaV Explorer, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with a Redundant Subsystem has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? As this is the FIRST application station (the preferred active), click YES . Important: When configuring a pair of Application Stations for the first time, you must respond Yes to this prompt when configuring one of the two Application Stations, and respond No when configuring the other Application Station. When you respond Yes, the Application Station is given the name that you specified when creating it in DeltaV Explorer; when you respond No, the characters _S are appended to the Application Station name. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the Application Station.

title: Install the DeltaV software on the secondary Application Station (the preferred standby)
main_heading: Install the DeltaV software on the secondary Application Station (the preferred standby)
body_text: Install the DeltaV software on the secondary Application Station (the preferred standby) Using the DeltaV installation disks, run the setup program on the secondary Application Station. When prompted to select your workstation type, select the Local Application Station option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier in DeltaV Explorer, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with a Redundant Subsystem has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? As this is the SECOND application station (the preferred standby), click NO . Important: When configuring a pair of Application Stations for the first time, you must respond Yes to this prompt when configuring one of the two Application Stations, and respond No when configuring the other Application Station. When you respond Yes, the Application Station is given the name that you specified when creating it in DeltaV Explorer; when you respond No, the characters _S are appended to the Application Station name. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the second Application Station

title: Open the Batch graphic and module phase faceplates
main_heading: Open the Batch graphic and module phase faceplates
body_text: Open the Batch graphic and module phase faceplates Start DeltaV Operate ( Start > DeltaV Operator > DeltaV Operate ). Open the Batch graphic by clicking the Open folder button and selecting Batch from the list of graphics available. (Click Skip All for any messages warning about parameters not being configured, since we haven't configured many of the unit modules referenced in this graphic.) The Batch graphic opens. Click the name UM_COLOR_100 to select the unit module and open the faceplate. Click the button next to Load a Phase at the bottom of the faceplate. Enter the phase name FILL (all uppercase) in the dialog. When the phase has been loaded, it is listed under Active Phases on the unit module faceplate. Click the Faceplate button next to the phase name FILL to open the phase faceplate. The phase is listed as UM_COLOR_100/P1 on the faceplate title, meaning it is the first active phase loaded. Note that the phase owner is listed as External. Click the button next to Phase Command to open the list of phase commands that are valid for the current state. Click the Pushpin button at the top left of the command list to keep the list open. Note: The Pushpin button appears when multiple faceplate capability has been enabled in UserSettings.grf. When multiple monitor capability has been enabled, a display selector appears to the right of the Pushpin button. Click the Process Graphic button at the top of the graphic to replace the Batch picture with the Process picture. Click Skip All on any warning messages .

title: Open channel fault on DO card
main_heading: Open channel fault on DO card
body_text: Open channel fault on DO card Occasionally, during setup or normal operation of the DeltaV system, one or more channel wires can become loose and cause an open channel fault. Open channel faults cause a switchover in Series 2 redundant DO cards. To correct this issue: Open DeltaV Diagnostics (click Start > DeltaV Operator > Diagnostics ). Select the card from the I/O subsystem in the left pane in Diagnostics. In the right pane, read the Status and OInteg parameter values for all channels to determine if there is an open connection. Look for values, such as Status = Bad – Hardware Error and OInteg = Bad, Pair Status – Possible Field Problem. Fix any wiring problems on the card. In Diagnostics, right-click each card, and then select Clear Saved Fault Information .

title: Open DeltaV Operate in configure mode
main_heading: Open DeltaV Operate in configure mode
body_text: Open DeltaV Operate in configure mode Let's get started now with DeltaV Operate in configure mode. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > DeltaV Operate Configure . DeltaV Operate in Configure mode opens with a blank drawing. In addition to the menu bar and toolbars, the window is made up of a system tree and the work area. The system tree shows a hierarchical view of the files on the local node and all objects associated with each file. The system tree can be resized, moved, or hidden. Opening and closing folders in the system tree is the same as opening and closing folders in Windows Explorer: click a plus sign (+) to open a folder and see its contents; click a minus sign (-) to close a folder and hide its contents. Take a few minutes now to become familiar with the system tree. Open a folder and double-click a file to open the file in the work area. Click the plus sign (+) next to the file and select an object associated with the file. Notice how that object is highlighted on the picture in the work area. Select File > Close to close the file, or right-click and then select Close . Continue to explore the system tree, and when you are ready, continue to the next section. Subtopics: Open the main picture template

title: Open DeltaV Operate in run mode
main_heading: Open DeltaV Operate in run mode
body_text: Open DeltaV Operate in run mode Click Start > DeltaV Operator > DeltaV Operate Run . DeltaV Operate opens in run mode, displaying the DeltaV startup screen. Tip: If your picture does not line up correctly with the Toolbar and Alarm Banner, click the Reset Layout button to fix the layout.

title: Open the DeltaV User Manager
body_text: Open the DeltaV User Manager If you are the very first user after the workstation has been installed with DeltaV, log into Windows desktop as either Administrator (on server class computers) or Emerson (on workstation class computers). When prompted to log into DeltaV, use the same administrator-level account as used for the Windows login. Select Windows Desktop from the Flexlock application. Click Start > DeltaV Engineering > User Manager . The initial screen of the User Manager application appears. There are a number of default interactive user accounts, including Administrator (or Emerson on workstation class machines), Configure, Operator, Supervisor, Maintainer, SIS_Configure, and Guest. Only Administrator (Emerson) has full privileges. To learn more about User Manager, particularly the specifics of how to limit access to plant areas and grant configuration/download privileges, read the online help for this system.

title: Open and edit the module in Control Studio
main_heading: Open and edit the module in Control Studio
body_text: Open and edit the module in Control Studio Select FIC-101 in DeltaV Explorer. Right-click, and then select Open > Open with Control Studio from the context menu. Control Studio opens with module FIC-101 preloaded. Resize the individual views as necessary.

title: Open a faceplate and a detail display
main_heading: Open a faceplate and a detail display
body_text: Open a faceplate and a detail display Click the link for FIC-101/SP. Note that the currently selected link is now displayed in the upper right corner of the picture. Click the Faceplate button to open the faceplate for the module. At the bottom of the faceplate, notice that the Detail button has a blinking line under it. This indicates there is a problem with the module (in this case, there is no I/O). Change the mode to Auto by clicking the AUTO button on the faceplate. Change the setpoint by moving the slider bar (large white triangle) to a new value. Close the faceplate. Tip: The Trend button at the bottom of the faceplate opens the prebuilt, module-specific trend display for any module created from a DeltaV Library template. Open the detail display by clicking the Detail button on the faceplate or the main picture. On the detail display, the operator can change tuning parameters (such as gain and reset), change high and low limits, and enable or disable alarms, if these have been configured as changeable. Close the detail display.

title: Open the main history list
body_text: Open the main history list The Main field in the Toolbar lists the name of the current picture. Operators can go quickly to another picture by clicking its name in the Main History list. Click the arrow next to the Main field. This opens a list of the pictures recently visited. Click the Pushpin button in the top left corner. Tip: The Pushpin button at the top of the Main History list is a toggle switch for keeping the Main History list open after a selection is made. The Lock button locks the list, and the Close button closes the list. You can predefine a Display History list and lock it using the UserSettings file. Click DeltaV . Click TANK101 to return to the process graphic. Related information Developing a picture hierarchy

title: Open pin fault on Series 2 redundant H1 card
main_heading: Open pin fault on Series 2 redundant H1 card
body_text: Open pin fault on Series 2 redundant H1 card Some of the pins that connect Series 2 redundant H1 cards to the terminal block can bend or break during installation or through improper handling and cause an open pin fault. An open pin can cause problems on one or both of the ports. To correct this issue: Open DeltaV Diagnostics (click Start > DeltaV Operator > Diagnostics ). Scroll through the parameters for the standby card and determine if there is a port problem. Remove the redundant cards and check for bent or broken pins. Straighten any bent pins and re-insert the card into its slot on the carrier. If a pin is broken or bent beyond repair, replace the card. For each card, right-click the card, and then select Clear Saved Fault Information .

title: Open the Process History View application
main_heading: Open the Process History View application
body_text: Open the Process History View application Click Start > DeltaV Operator > Process History View . Select File > New . Click the E +Chart button in the New dialog. The Configure Chart dialog opens. Click the Add button, and then click the Browse button in the Parameter Reference Entry dialog. Select Module Parameters in the Object Type field, and then browse in the TANK-101 area for FIC-101/PID1/PV.CV to plot the value of the outlet flow. Click OK in the Parameter Reference Entry dialog. In the Configure Chart dialog, click Add , and then browse for LI-101/AI1/PV.CV to plot the value of the tank level in the tank process. Click OK . Click the New Axis check box for LI-101/AI1/PV.CV. Click the Multiple Y-Axes tab. Click the down arrow and select 50/50 in the Axis styles box to create two Y scales to plot the data values. Click the Configure Chart tab, and enter MYGRAPH as the Graph Title. Click OK to close the Configure Chart dialog. The graph appears, showing module trends for the two parameter references, as well as the events in area TANK-101. The Process History View application has numerous graph configuration options and event filtering options that are described in the Online Help. Tip: Click Trend > Plot Method to change the line style. Quit the Process History View application. Save if you are prompted to do so.

title: Open the TANK-101 module
body_text: Open the TANK-101 module In Control Studio, click the Main button, and then click Open . The Browse dialog appears. For Object Type , select Modules . If TANK-101 is not in the Look in field, click the pull-down list, and then select Control Strategies . In the large center box that lists the contents of Modules , double-click TANK-101 . Select MTR-101 , and then click Open . The MTR-101 module is displayed in the Diagram view. Enlarge the Control Studio application window to its full size by clicking the Maximize button in the upper right corner. Select the Logical palette so you can easily access the descriptions for the individual blocks. Remember, you can select and right-click a palette item or a function block on the diagram, and then select Help to open DeltaV Books Online for information about the selected item.

title: Open the FILL running logic and select the Running composite block
main_heading: Open the FILL running logic and select the Running composite block
body_text: Open the FILL running logic and select the Running composite block In DeltaV Explorer, select Library/Advanced Definitions/Phase Classes/TankPhases/FILL . Right-click and select Open with Control Studio from the context menu. Control Studio opens with the standard State Transition Diagram in the diagram window, ready for editing. Double-click Running . (Other options are to right-click Running , and then select Drill Down from the context menu or to click RUN_LOGIC in the Hierarchy view). A sequential function chart with one step and one termination opens.

title: Open the main picture template
body_text: Open the main picture template In the system tree, click the plus signs next to the Pictures folder to expand its contents, and then click the plus sign next to the Templates folder to expand its contents. Double-click the main template picture. The main template and the Toolbox open in the Work Area. (If the Toolbox is not visible, select Toolbars from the Workspace menu, select Picture as the toolbox owner, and then click DeltaV_Toolbox .) Notice how a plus sign appears next to the main picture. Click the plus signs to see the objects that make up the main template. The main template has instructional text, including descriptions of the five buttons in the upper left corner. In your system, the background color may be gray rather than white, as shown in this document. Later, we will tell you how to change picture background color, as well as object colors. Read the information on this template. Then delete the text by clicking near the center of the page, right-clicking, and then selecting Delete . (Alternatively, you can click near the center of the page and then press the Delete key). Select File > Save As . The Save As dialog appears. Click the Up One Level button to go to the Pic folder. Enter the File Name as TANK101, and then click Save . (Be sure the picture is saved in the Pic folder.) Note: Picture file names must be alphanumeric and cannot contain the hyphen character, begin with a number, or use a Visual Basic reserved word, such as "new".

title: Open the DeltaV Workstation Configuration application
main_heading: Open the DeltaV Workstation Configuration application
body_text: Open the DeltaV Workstation Configuration application When you start up a workstation for the first time, the DeltaV Workstation Configuration application opens automatically. If you elect not to configure the workstation right away, then you will need to open the application from the DeltaV program group when you are ready to perform the configuration. You cannot do any work with the DeltaV system until the workstation is configured. The Workstation Configuration application guides you through the process of configuring the ProfessionalPLUS. Remember to refer to the online help for complete information on configuring the ProfessionalPLUS workstation. The Workstation Configuration application sets up the workstation's network settings and creates the initial database to hold the DeltaV system configuration. This process may take several minutes to complete. You are instructed to restart your computer for the configuration changes to take effect. Important: If your workstation has already been configured, do not repeat this procedure. Click Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Workstation Configuration . The initial screen appears. Click the Help button to familiarize yourself with the application. When you are ready to begin the configuration, click Next . Select ProfessionalPLUS workstation , and then click Next .

title: Connecting Power to the System for P-series
main_heading: Connecting Power to the System for P-series
body_text: Connecting Power to the System for P-series The method of connecting power to the DeltaV system depends on your existing power supply, power distribution scheme, and grounding techniques. Refer to the DeltaV Power and Grounding manual for recommended power and grounding techniques for a DeltaV system. Related information System Power Guidelines

title: Install the Control Network Cables
body_text: Install the Control Network Cables Make and test the required Control Network cables. See the section, "Control Network Specifications" for cable guidelines and specifications. Select the appropriate cable type on the cable test tool and follow the detailed instructions in the test tool’s manual. You must connect the test equipment to both ends of the cable to test it properly. The testing tool checks each cable based on its type and issues a Pass or Fail reading. Make sure the cable passes each test. The tests supported by the Microtest PentaScanner testing tool include the following: Cable mapping Length Crosstalk Attenuation Attenuation-to-crosstalk ratio Impedance Loop resistance Capacitance CAUTION: Substandard cables can create serious communication problems. Make sure all cables meet the specifications listed in the "Control Network Specifications" section. If you have a simplex Control Network, connect the unshielded end of a network cable to the twisted pair port on the primary Network Interface Card (NIC) and connect the shielded end of the cable to the primary switch as shown in the following figure. Simplex Control Network Cable Connections For redundant Control Networks, be sure to verify the NIC binding order to differentiate between the primary and secondary NICs. If you have a redundant Control Network, connect the unshielded end of a network cable to the twisted pair port on the workstation’s primary NIC and connect the shielded end of the cable to the primary switch as shown in Redundant Control Network Cable Connections . Connect another cable from the twisted pair port on the workstation’s secondary NIC to the secondary switch. It is helpful to identify the Control Network cables with color-coded boots. Emerson recommends the following conventions: a yellow color-coded boot for the primary Control Network cable and a black color-coded boot for the secondary Control Network cable. Note: Make sure you are consistent in your primary and secondary network connections so they are not crosswired. Redundant Control Network Cable Connections Connect network cables from the switches to the RJ45 connectors on the front of the carrier. The left side ports are the primary ports and the right side are the secondary ports (for use with redundant networks).
