The ports must be enabled on the controller's Properties page in DeltaV Explorer. Control Network Cable Connections for a P-series Controller

title: Installing Extender Cables for P-Series Hardware
main_heading: Installing Extender Cables for P-Series Hardware
body_text: Installing Extender Cables for P-Series Hardware When carriers are installed on separate DIN rails, extender cables are used to extend LocalBus power. Extender cables connect to one-wide carriers on the left and right sides of the 2-wide, 4-wide, and 8-wide carriers. Note: The 8-wide carriers must be left-aligned when using extender cables. A standard installation uses one extender cable; however, dual extender cables can also be used. The following procedure is for a standard installation that uses one carrier extender cable. To install carrier extender cables Install the right and left-side one-wide extender cable carriers by sliding together the 48 pin connectors on the sides of the carriers. Connect the 44-pin D-shell (male) connector on the extender cable to the top D-shell connector labeled A on the right-side carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Connect the 44-pin D-shell connector on the other end of the cable to the top D-shell connector labeled A on the left-side carrier and fasten the retainer screws.

title: Installing a Redundant Controller
body_text: Installing a Redundant Controller Note: A simplex controller cannot be made redundant by using the following steps after VCAT is enabled. Assign an appropriate redundancy license to the simplex controller you want to make redundant in DeltaV Explorer. Insert the power supply module into the right power module slot in the P-series carrier. Insert a matching controller into the right slot of the P-series carrier. The controller type must match what is already installed. The added controller's Power LED should turn on and the Error LED should blink for a few seconds. The newly inserted controller must go through its power on self test. Download the ProfessionalPLUS workstation in DeltaV Explorer. Download the setup data to the controller. The LEDs will flash appropriately. Wait for all LEDs to return to a steady green light. The Standby Controller is now ready to take over if the Active Controller fails.

title: Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system (PI Server)
main_heading:
Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system (PI
    Server)
body_text: Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system (PI Server) Explicit logins are not supported in OSIsoft PI Server, beginning with version 3.4.380. You must create a trust for the remote client by completing the following steps: Log on as Administrator to the system where PI Server is installed. Start the PI System Management Tools (PI SMT) by clicking All Programs > PI System > PI System Management Tools . In the PI System Management Tools window, navigate to Security > Mappings & Trusts , and then select the Trusts tab. Start the Add Trust Wizard by right-clicking in the Trusts window, and then selecting New Trust on the context menu. In the Add Trust Wizard , complete the following steps: Specify a trust name. Enable the PI-API Application option. Use the Application Name and Client Connection options to set up a trust relationship for one or more application running on a specified client, for all applications running on the client, or for a specified application running on any client. Application Name option To use the Application Name option, specify up to the first eight characters of the client application's executable file name. For example: specify PREDICTP instead of PREDICTPRO.EXE for the PredictPro client application; specify PREDICT. instead of PREDICT.EXE for the Predict client application; specify CHS.EXE for the Process History View client application. Client Connection option for an embedded PI Server historian (PI Server installed on an Application Station) – specify one or both of the following: Network Path : the computer name of the client. or IP Address and NetMask : Trust #1 – 10.4.x.x as the IP address of the DeltaV primary network and 255.255.0.0 as the network mask and IP Address and NetMask. Trust #2 – 10.8.x.x as the IP address of an existing DeltaV secondary network and 255.255.0.0 as the network mask. Note: If you do not specify the computer name of the client in Network Path , the trust using 10.4.x.x as the IP address of the DeltaV primary network only takes effect if the connection to the 10.8.x.x IP address of an existing DeltaV secondary network is unavailable. Client Connection option for an integrated PI Server historian (PI Server installed on a non-DeltaV workstation) – specify the following: Network Path : the computer name of the client. Specify DeltaVAdmin as the PI User . Start the PI Software Development Kit (SDK) by clicking All Programs > PI System > PI-SDK Utility . In the navigation pane of the PI-SDK Utility window, select Connections , and then click File > Connections > Options . In the Specify Authentication Procedure area, move PI Trust to the top of the Protocol order list, followed by Windows Security, and then click the OK button. Related information Client application support Specify the historical data server in Process History View

title: Plan your system for using Remote Desktop Gateway with DeltaV
main_heading: Plan your system for using Remote Desktop Gateway with DeltaV
body_text: Plan your system for using Remote Desktop Gateway with DeltaV This procedure outlines the steps needed before installing any software. The first steps to using the Remote Desktop Gateway (RD Gateway) are to map where all the computers are that will access the DeltaV system, determine where you will locate the Remote Desktop Gateway, and obtain the certificates needed. Create a map of the relevant networks. These networks include: Locate the remote computers; that is, the computers that will use Remote Desktop Client to access the DeltaV node. Record their domain (or workgroup) membership, their computer name, and IP addresses. Map the connections from remote computers to the RD Gateway (switches/hubs/firewalls to traverse). The appropriate ports will need to be open to allow RDP traffic to the RD Gateway. Map the connections from RD Gateway to the DeltaV Remote Desktop Server. Normally, the RD Gateway will be in the DMZ with a firewall between it and the DeltaV Remote Desktop Server. Create a table of the network addresses being used for remote access for the following computers: DeltaV Remote Desktop Server RD Gateway Remote computers Determine the type of certificate you will use and get the certificate created. All certificates must be SSL-compatible X.509 certificates. The following are the valid types of certificates: Internally created/maintained stand-alone or enterprise CA (not self-signed) Externally created certificate purchased from a public CA that participates in the Microsoft Root Certificate Program Members program. A self-signed certificate. (only supported for testing and evaluation of the RD Gateway)

title: Practice docking the toolbox
body_text: Practice docking the toolbox Click Workspace > Toolbars . Click Picture , and then click the Customize button. Select DeltaV_Toolbox . Select Enable docking for selected toolbar , and then click Close . Move the toolbox to the top edge of the screen and notice how the toolbox "docks" to the edge rather than floats over the screen. Disable or enable docking to suit your personal preferences.

title: Practice using the Toolbars dialog
body_text: Practice using the Toolbars dialog Click Workspace > Toolbars . The Toolbars dialog appears. By default all the workspace toolbars are displayed. Make sure that Show Screen Tips on toolbars in the lower left corner is selected. With Screen Tips enabled, when you pause the pointer over a tool in the Toolbox, its name will pop up. Uncheck and recheck the various toolbars to see the buttons that belong to each toolbar. (Watch the toolbar across the top of the window and see which buttons disappear and then reappear.) Click the Customize button and use the online help to familiarize yourself with the Customize Toolbars dialog. Later, when you are more familiar with the tools, you can add and remove buttons and toolbars to suit your needs. Click Close on the Customize Toolbar dialog. Click Workspace > Toolbars to reopen the Toolbars dialog, and then select Picture in the Owner field. Select DeltaV_Toolbox if it is not already selected. The DeltaV_Toolbox is a group of toolbars assembled in one box. It saves space on your picture because you do not have to keep several toolbars open. By default, docking is not enabled for the DeltaV_Toolbox and it floats regardless of its position on the screen. The DeltaV_Toolbox contains everything from simple drawing tools for creating lines, rectangles, and circles to complex charting tools. In the Toolbars dialog, select DeltaV_Operating_Experts if it is not already selected. Click Close in the Toolbars dialog.

title: Prevent users from running unauthorized software
main_heading: Prevent users from running unauthorized software
body_text: Prevent users from running unauthorized software In domain environments, Microsoft's software restriction policies can be used to prevent certain software programs from running under any circumstances. In domains, software restriction policies are created for a particular GPO. The policies are enforced against users associated with that GPO. A software restriction policy consists of a default rule about whether programs are allowed to run and exceptions to that rule. The default rule can be set to Unrestricted or Disallowed; that is run or do not run. Setting the default rule to Unrestricted allows an administrator to define exceptions; for example, the set of programs that are not allowed to run. A more secure approach is to set the default rule to Disallowed and specify only the programs that are known and trusted to run. For complete information on software restriction policies, refer to the Microsoft TechNet article named Using Software Restriction Policies to Protect Against Unauthorized Software . The Microsoft Management Console is used to create software restriction policies. You can download this utility from the Microsoft Download Center . After downloading the Microsoft Management Console, follow these steps to access it and use its online help to create software restriction policies: Log onto the domain controller with an Administrator account. Click Start > Run , type gpmc.msc in the Run dialog, and click OK . The Group Policy Management Console opens. Click Help > Help Topics . In the left pane of the Microsoft Management Console online help, find Group Policy Object Editor Extensions under Concepts and select the link for the Security settings topics. Use the help topics under Software restriction policies for information on how to create policies.

title: Define the Master Time Server node
main_heading: Define the Master Time Server node
body_text: Define the Master Time Server node The Master Time Server node broadcasts the system time to all workstations and controllers on the DeltaV Control Network. By default, the Professional PLUS workstation is the Master Time Server node. However, any physical DeltaV workstation on the DeltaV Control Network can be defined as the Master Time Server node. To define the Master Time Server node, complete the following steps: Navigate to System Configuration > Physical Network . Right-click Physical Network , and then select Properties . Click the Browse button on the System Time tab in the Physical Network Properties dialog, and then select a workstation on the DeltaV Control Network. You can also define the Backup Time Server node on the System Time tab in the Physical Network Properties dialog.

title: Configure an SLS 1508 Logic Solver Channel
main_heading: Configure an SLS 1508 Logic Solver Channel
body_text: Configure an SLS 1508 Logic Solver Channel When an SLS 1508 Logic Solver is created under the SIS Network, the channels default to the Undefined channel type. You must then configure the channels to define the type of I/O signal. Navigate to a channel in the Channels subsystem under a Logic Solver. Right-click, and then select Properties . In the Properties dialog, select the Enabled check box to enable this channel. Enter a description for the channel. Select a channel type. To select a Device Tag other than the default, click the Browse button next to the Device Tag field. Note: The Browse dialog displays the Unassigned I/O references of the appropriate type for the channel type. Select an I/O reference, and then click OK . Click OK in the channel Properties dialog.

title: Start a recipe at any specific point with active step changes (ASC)
main_heading:
Start a recipe at any specific point with active step changes
	 (ASC)
body_text: Start a recipe at any specific point with active step changes (ASC) Use the following procedure to start at any point in the recipe. You must accommodate recipe logic where parallel PFC branches exist. When changing the active step to a part of the recipe that has not yet become active (an operation or phase in a non-active unit procedure, for example) you have to activate the higher recipe level first and then drill into the new active step and perform active step changes from there, down to the recipe level you want to run. In effect, you are performing multiple active step changes (without starting the steps) until you reach the final step you want to run. Important Considerations When performing an active step change, you cannot have any two steps active at the same time that wouldn’t be active during the normal course of the recipe. The logged in user must have the Batch_Active_Step_Change key. The step you are performing the active step change from must be in a terminal state; that is, Complete, Stopped, Aborted, Stopped_NC, or Aborted_NC. If it is not, the execution of the ASC will issue a STOP to any steps marked as Deactivate. The parent steps of the one you are changing from must be in one of the following states: Held, Running or Ready. The active step change cannot be performed if the batch or the parent step is in a terminal state (Complete, Stopped, Aborted). However, the operator can reset the batch into the Ready state if the batch is in a terminal state (and the operator has the appropriate key) To activate a step in a part of the recipe that is not yet active, follow these steps: Perform an active step change so that the part of the recipe containing the step you want to run is active. For example, active step change to the unit procedure that contains the operation that you want to run. Then, perform the active step change within the newly activated step for the next level down, making sure you follow the path to the step you want to run. Continue doing this until you have activated the step (an operation, for example) you want to run. Select that step (which will show as Ready) in the step list, and then click the Start Step button. To complete these actions and get the recipe to fully automatic condition, select each ready step (should all be in O-AUTO mode). Then start each step by clicking the Start Step button. Select the top level of the recipe, and then click the Auto mode button to place the entire recipe in AUTO mode. If you have started steps as required by the recipe logic, it should complete automatically (unless interrupted by failure or operator action).

title: Perform an active step change (ASC)
body_text: Perform an active step change (ASC) Important Considerations When performing an active step change, you cannot have any two steps active at the same time that wouldn’t be active during the normal course of the recipe. The logged in user must have the Batch_Active_Step_Change key. The step you are performing the active step change from must be in a terminal state; that is, Complete, Stopped, Aborted, Stopped_NC, or Aborted_NC. If it is not, the execution of the ASC will issue a STOP to any steps marked as Deactivate . The parent steps of the one you are changing from must be in one of the following states: Held, Running or Ready. The active step change cannot be performed if the batch or the parent step is in a terminal state (Complete, Stopped, Aborted) . However, the operator can reset the batch into the Ready state if the batch is in a terminal state (and the operator has the appropriate key). Note: The rules for active step change also apply to re-running a step. Select the batch on the batch list. Click the Procedure as PFC button on the toolbar to open the PFC screen. Select the step for the active step change using one of the following methods (based on the Batch Application Manager Advanced setting, Allow Implicit Mode Change ). Allow Implicit Mode Change Procedure Yes Select the recipe level where you will perform the ASC. Click the Active Step Change button from the PFC command bar. Acknowledge the prompt to change to MANUAL mode. The mode for the recipe level above the one selected is changed to Manual. The active step change buttons are now visible. No Select the recipe at the level above the step you wish to change. Place that level in MANUAL mode. If the recipe is not in MANUAL mode, you will not be able to complete the active step change. That is, if you are performing the step change on an operation, select that operation’s unit procedure and place it (the unit procedure) in MANUAL mode. On the PFC block diagram, drill into the recipe block where the active step change will take place. Note: If you are at the top level of the recipe, you can skip this step. Click the Active Step Change button from the PFC command bar. The active step change buttons are now visible. Important: When you execute the ASC, a STOP is issued to the steps marked as Deactivate that are not in terminal states (that is, Complete, Stopped, Aborted, Stopped_NC, or Aborted_NC). Select the steps. For Procedure Active step change Select the Deactivate button and the cursor changes to . Move the cursor to the currently active step(s) that you want to remove (deactivate). Select the Activate button and the cursor changes to . Move the cursor to the step(s) that you want to add (activate). Rerun a step Click the Rerun button (the cursor changes to ). Click any active step(s) you wish to rerun. Note: The click must be made with the cursor’s point in the center of the step, not along the top or bottom as these are reserved areas even when blank. For example, on the Rerun cursor , the cursor is the tip of the arrow. Click the Execute ASC button. This validates your choices (to rerun or change steps), accepts them and returns you to the PFC View for the level above the step change. Note: If you cancel (that is, do not execute the ASC or step rerun), the step remains in MANUAL mode and you are required to place it back in AUTO mode using the PFC command toolbar. Select the step where you were working in the recipe level (from the Recipe List on the left side of the display). Place that step in AUTO mode (click the Auto Mode button ). Click the Start Step button.

title: Proof test the SIS Relay module for AC wiring
main_heading: Proof test the SIS Relay module for AC wiring
body_text: Proof test the SIS Relay module for AC wiring Measure the voltage at the AC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 11). The voltage at these points should match the input voltage. Slide the switch labeled Test 1 down to toggle it and then measure the voltage at the AC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 11). The voltage at these points should be 0 when toggled. Release the toggle and re-measure the voltage. Slide the switch labeled Test 2 down to toggle it and then measure the voltage at the AC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 11). The voltage at these points should be 0 when toggled. Release the toggle and re-measure the voltage. Slide the switch labeled Test 3 down to toggle it and then measure the voltage at the AC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 11). The voltage at these points should be 0 when toggled. Release the toggle and re-measure the voltage.

title: Proof test the SIS Relay module for DC wiring
main_heading: Proof test the SIS Relay module for DC wiring
body_text: Proof test the SIS Relay module for DC wiring Measure the voltage at the first DC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 10). The voltage at these points should match the input voltage. Slide the switch labeled Test 1 down to toggle it and then measure the voltage at the DC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 10). The voltage at these points should be 0 when toggled. Release the toggle and re-measure the voltage. Slide the switch labeled Test 2 down to toggle it and then measure the voltage at the DC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 10). The voltage at these points should be 0 when toggled. Release the toggle and re-measure the voltage. Slide the switch labeled Test 3 down to toggle it and then measure the voltage at the DC field device's + and - connections (screw terminals 9 and 10). The voltage at these points should be 0 when toggled. Release the toggle and re-measure the voltage. If you have a second DC field device, perform steps 1-4 by measuring the voltage at pins 11 and 12.

title: Protect a library category
body_text: Protect a library category Open DeltaV Explorer. Select the library category and select Protect from the context menu. Note: You cannot protect the items that contain categories (Composite Templates, Module Templates, and so on). Enter and confirm a password. Click OK . Items in protected categories cannot be modified, deleted, moved, or overwritten and new items cannot be added to a protected category. Note: In addition to protecting library items, you can hide the internal structure of some library items (and their instances). The Hide Internal Structure command cannot be applied to an item in a protected category. To hide an item in a protected category, first hide the item and then protect the category to which the item belongs. Related information Hiding intellectual property

title: Protect a parameter in a class-based template
main_heading: Protect a parameter in a class-based template
body_text: Protect a parameter in a class-based template Protect a parameter in a class-based template from the class. There are two ways to do this; both have the same result: Method 1 Open DeltaV Explorer. Select the parameter in the class on which the template is based and select Properties from the context menu. Make sure the Allow instance value to be configured check box is not selected. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for other parameters as desired. Method 2 Open DeltaV Explorer. Select the class on which the template is based and select Configure Instance from the context menu. Open the Parameters tab. Click, CTRL+click, and SHIFT+click to select the parameters to protect. Click Remove . This sequence of actions has the same effect as opening the Properties dialog of each parameter and deselecting the Allow instance value to be configured check box. It is not possible to remove the protection in instances of the module made from the template. Protection is not automatically preserved during a manual database export and import. To preserve protection when manually exporting and importing a database, check the Include the data for a DeltaV software upgrade check box. Note that you can only do one online upgrade import. However, protection is automatically preserved when a DeltaV installation is upgraded with the DeltaV Upgrade Wizard .

title: Provide power to the system
body_text: Provide power to the system In hazardous locations the power supply should not be removed or inserted into the carrier unless the input power has been deenergized for at least one minute. Power connections Locate the three power terminals on the side of the carrier. The terminals are labeled +24V, RETURN, and ground ( ). Connect the 24 VDC power supply's +24 VDC and return connectors to the corresponding terminals on the carrier. Connect the power supply's return connection to earth ground. Connect earth ground to the terminal labeled on the carrier.

title: Provide power to the Logic Solvers
main_heading: Provide power to the Logic Solvers
body_text: Provide power to the Logic Solvers Note: Read the Caution in the Providing power topic before proceeding. Locate the removable 24 VDC screw terminal connectors on the top of the Logic Solver. Connect power supply positive (+) to the positive (+) connector on the Logic Solver and power supply negative (-) to the negative connector on the Logic Solver.

title: Provide power to SISNet Distance Extenders
main_heading: Provide power to SISNet Distance Extenders
body_text: Provide power to SISNet Distance Extenders Note: Read the Caution in the Providing power topic before proceeding. Locate the removable 24 VDC screw terminal connectors on the top of the SISNet Distance Extender. Connect power supply positive (+) to the positive (+) connector on the SISNet Distance Extender and power supply negative (-) to the negative (-) connector on the SISNet Distance Extender.

title: Provide power to SISNet Repeaters
body_text: Provide power to SISNet Repeaters Note: Read the important Caution in the Providing power topic before proceeding. Locate the removable 24 VDC screw terminal connectors on the top of the SISNet Repeater. Connect power supply positive (+) to the positive (+) connector on the SISNet Repeater and power supply negative (-) to the negative (-) connector on the SISNet Repeater.

title: Put a CIOC in simulate mode
main_heading: Put a CIOC in simulate mode
body_text: Put a CIOC in simulate mode Select the CIOC in DeltaV Explorer. Select Properties from the context menu. Enable Simulate CHARMs , and then save and close the CIOC Properties dialog. Download the CIOC's setup data. Notice that the CIOC's icon changes to indicate it is in simulate mode.

title: Installing the DeltaV P-Series Controller
body_text: Installing the DeltaV P-Series Controller For simplex controller systems, the controller mounts on the left controller slot of the P-series power/controller carrier. Note: Refer to the DeltaV Power and Grounding manual for information on proper configuration of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) to back up the controller power during short-term power outages. The UPS allows the controller to continue operating and to maintain current process data even when AC main power is down. Refer to the UPS manufacturer’s specifications for all other UPS information. Simplex installation: Align the connectors on the back of the controller with the connectors on the left slot of the P-series carrier and push to attach. There should be a firm click into place. The LEDs on the controller (when powered) will go to an appropriate state when properly seated. Tighten the mounting screw. Redundant installation: Align the connectors on the back of the 2nd controller with the connectors on the right slot of the of the P-series carrier and push to attach. There should be a firm click into place. The LEDs on the controller (when powered) will go to an appropriate state when properly seated. Tighten the mounting screw. Related information P-series Controllers PK controller LEDs Controller Redundancy

title: Read a dataset value using an AI block
main_heading: Read a dataset value using an AI block
body_text: Read a dataset value using an AI block Create a module containing an Analog Input block. Double-click the IO_IN parameter. To select a device tag, click Browse . In the Object Type field select All . This shows all the Device Tag names including the dataset tag name you want to read. Double-click the dataset tag that contains the parameter (register) that corresponds to the dataset value that you want to read. Select the parameter from the pull down list. If desired, scale your input value using the Analog Input block's XD_SCALE, OUT_SCALE, and L_TYPE parameters.

title: Read a dataset value using an internal read parameter
main_heading:
Read a dataset value using an internal read
	 parameter
body_text: Read a dataset value using an internal read parameter Create a module containing an Internal Read parameter (located on the Special Items palette). Modify the properties of the Internal Read parameter by specifying a parameter type of External Reference. For the External parameter path field, click Browse . In the Browse dialog, select System Configuration in the Look in field. Select DST Parameters in the Object Type field. Starting at Physical Network, drill down until the dialog contains DSTs. The list includes dataset tags. Double-click the dataset tag that contains the parameter (register) that corresponds to the dataset value that you want to read. Double-click the parameter. If desired, scale your input value using the Analog Input block's XD_SCALE, OUT_SCALE, and L_TYPE parameters.

title: Read process data and the call status
main_heading: Read process data and the call status
body_text: Read process data and the call status Select two adjacent cells in your workbook. The cells can be in the same row or the same column. Select the Add-Ins tab. From the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and then select Runtime Data > Configure Read Function . Enter (or browse to) the Parameter Path to the DeltaV parameter you want to read. Note: The DeltaV OPC .NET Server service must be running to be able to browse to the parameter. Click Paste parameter path to the left of result if you want the parameter path to be displayed next to the value. Select the Data Type for the specified DeltaV parameter. Select the Status Type . This is the data type of the returned status for the specified DeltaV parameter. Click OK . Related information Create a DVRead Function Modify a function Set the update interval

title: Read or write display serial data using a serial dataset DST
main_heading: Read or write display serial data using a serial dataset DST
body_text: Read or write display serial data using a serial dataset DST Open a display for editing. Click the Data Link tool from the graphics toolbox. Enter the dataset's DST name followed by the register number in the tagname field (for example: CTLR101010101/R40101). You can also use the Parameter Browse feature to browse for the DST and register name. Set the other Data Link parameters to their desired values and click OK . Drag the Data Link to the desired location on the display. You can use serial device data in control modules. For example, use serial data as the I/O reference in standard function blocks or create module-level parameters that reference the Dataset Tag and parameter associated with the register with which you want to work. The following specific examples describe how to read from and write to serial devices using a control module and a control module reference.

title: Configure the primary Application Station (the preferred active)
main_heading: Configure the primary Application Station (the preferred active)
body_text: Configure the primary Application Station (the preferred active) In DeltaV Explorer, right-click the remaining Application Station that you intend to use as the primary Application Station in the redundant pair and select Properties . You can optionally change the name of the Application Station on the General page of the Properties dialog, but this is not necessary. However, changing the Application Station name is strongly recommended, if it coincidentally ends with the characters _S. Important: As a general rule, do not specify an Application Station name that ends with the characters _S. When the DeltaV system creates a pair of Application Stations for a redundant subsystem, it appends these characters to whatever name you specify as the base name for the Application Station. Having a pair of Application Stations named nodename _S and nodename _S_S could result in misleading or undesirable results. On the Redundancy page of the Properties dialog, select the Enable a redundant subsystem option, and then select the Batch option. Important: To enable a redundant subsystem, you must first disable any previously-enabled subsystems for this Application Station. After enabling the redundant subsystem feature on a pair of Application Stations, you cannot also enable any other subsystems, either redundant or simplex, on this Application Station. You can optionally enable the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, if, for example, either of the Application Stations will be located in an unmanned facility. Important: Before enabling the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, see Operational Considerations for Redundant Batch Subsystem for more information . Select Enable Direct Link for Batch Synchronization if you are connecting the pair with a direct connection. Click OK to close the Properties dialog for the Application Station. When prompted to export a workstation configuration file for the Application Station, click Yes . Save the workstation configuration file either to removable media or to a network location that can be accessed from the Application Station you are configuring. You can use the default name for a workstation configuration file, DevData.cfg, or specify a different file name. On the Application Station that you did not delete, run Workstation Configuration ( DeltaV/Installation/DeltaV Workstation Configuration ). When the introductory DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog appears, click Next . For the Select Workstation Type option, select Professional / Operator / Application / Base / Inter-Zone Server , and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with a Redundant Subsystem has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? Respond Yes to this prompt when configuring the primary Application Station (the preferred active). When you respond Yes, the Application Station is given the name specified for it in DeltaV Explorer. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the configuration of the Application Station. Related information Operational considerations for Redundant Batch subsystem

title: Configure the secondary Application Station (the preferred standby)
main_heading:
Configure the secondary Application Station (the preferred
    standby)
body_text: Configure the secondary Application Station (the preferred standby) On the Application Station that you deleted in DeltaV Explorer earlier, apply the workstation configuration file by clicking DeltaV/Installation/DeltaV Workstation Configuration on the Start menu. When the introductory DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog appears, click Next . When prompted to select your workstation type, select the Professional / Operator / Application / Base / Inter-Zone Server option, and then click Next . When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made in DeltaV Explorer, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. In the DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog, select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with a Redundant Subsystem has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? Respond No to this prompt now. When you respond No, the characters _S are appended to the name specified for the Application Station in DeltaV Explorer. Important: When the message appears, advising you that any historical database stored on this Application Station will be deleted, click Yes to continue with this procedure, if you have no historian data sets to protect. Otherwise, click No to discontinue this procedure until you have backed up or exported historian data sets. After backing up your historian data sets, restart this procedure of importing the workstation configuration file. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation of the second Application Station. Related information Back up a historical data set Automated backup utility Export a historical data set

title: Delete one of the existing Application Stations
main_heading: Delete one of the existing Application Stations
body_text: Delete one of the existing Application Stations In DeltaV Explorer, right-click one of the existing Application Stations. This should be the workstation that you intend to use as the secondary Application Station (the preferred standby) in the redundant pair. Select Delete on the context menu for the Application Station Click Yes when prompted to confirm that you want to delete this Application Station from the Control Network. Note: Only one Application Station per pair is displayed in DeltaV Explorer. The secondary (or preferred standby) is created in the database by enabling a redundant subsystem on the Properties dialog of the primary Application Station.

title: Finish the installation
body_text: Finish the installation Assign licenses for the Application Stations and Redundant Batch as needed. Note: There is no reason to assign licenses to the Application Stations for DeltaV software components that are not designed to coexist with the redundant subsystem feature. For example, you should not license subsystems such as Continuous Historian on the Application Stations, because they cannot be enabled simultaneously with Redundant Batch. In DeltaV Explorer, download the Application Station.

title: Reference OPC in your project
body_text: Reference OPC in your project Start Visual Basic. From the File menu, click Open Project , and then select the Barcode.vbp file in the \DeltaV\samples\Opc\Start directory. Barcode.vbp is a project file to use as a starting point. The Microsoft Comm Control is the only Custom Control option selected. To open the References dialog, select References from the Project menu. If OPCAutomation 2.0 is in the list, skip to step 7. If OPCAutomation 2.0 is not on the list, click Browse to find the OPCDaAuto.dll file. Select the OPCAutomation 2.0 check box. To accept the settings in the References dialog, click OK . All of the OPC objects are now available to your project. You can find a specific object and its methods and properties in the Object Browser. Note: In Visual Basic 5, the Object Browser shows the object name for the default interfaces instead of the interface name. For example, IOpcItemMgtDisp shows up as Group and IOpcItemDisp shows up as Item. The IOPCItemMgtDisp is the default interface for the Group object. The IOpcItemDisp is the default interface for the Item object. Related information Include OPC constants

title: Refer a parameter
body_text: Refer a parameter To refer parameter up to a higher (containing) recipe level, use the following steps: On the phase, create a batch parameter of category Report (for this example, CAPACITY). At the operation level, select the phase step. In the Parameter View, select the phase parameter (CAPACITY) and double-click. On the Properties dialog for the phase parameter (CAPACITY), set the Destination field to Refer . This creates a recipe parameter with the same name (in the Target field). You can rename the parameter once it has been created (for this example, rename it to OP_CAPACITY). Note: You can also first create the parameter at the operation level and then refer the phase report parameter to it. From the unit procedure, select the operation step. In the Parameter View, select the operation's recipe parameter (OP_CAPACITY) and double-click. On the Properties dialog, set the Destination field to Refer . This creates a recipe parameter with the same name (in the Target field). You can rename the parameter once it has been created (for this example, rename it to UP_CAPACITY). Note: You can also first create the parameter at the unit procedure level and then refer the operation report parameter to it. From the procedure, select the unit procedure step. In the Parameter View, select the unit procedure's recipe parameter (UP_CAPACITY) and double-click. On the Properties dialog, set the Destination field to Refer . This creates a recipe parameter with the same name (in the Target field). You can rename the parameter once it has been created (for this example, rename it to PROC_CAPACITY). Note: You can also first create the parameter at the procedure level and then refer the unit procedure report parameter to it. The parameter value for PROC_CAPACITY is set based on the value of the phase parameter CAPACITY. Note: Only parameters of the category Process Report can be referred (to other report parameters).

title: Remove a CHARM I/O Carrier or Baseplate from the DIN rail
main_heading: Remove a CHARM I/O Carrier or Baseplate from the DIN rail
body_text: Remove a CHARM I/O Carrier or Baseplate from the DIN rail CHARM I/O Carriers and CHARM Baseplates are removed from the DIN rail in the same way. Push the latch tab on the right side of the carrier or baseplate to the unlock position. You will hear a click when the latch opens. Slowly pull the carrier or baseplate straight towards you as you slightly rock the carrier to disengage the bus connectors to the adjacent carrier. Reengage the latch before reinstalling the carrier on the DIN rail.

main_heading:

title: Remove a Dual Universal Safety Carrier from the DIN rail
main_heading: Remove a Dual Universal Safety Carrier from the DIN rail

Slowly pull the carrier towards you and off of the DIN rail. Reengage the latch before reinstalling the carrier on a DIN rail.

main_heading: Remove a Dual Universal Carrier from the DIN rail

title: Remove excess blocks from a module template
main_heading: Remove excess blocks from a module template
body_text: Remove excess blocks from a module template Having unused condition blocks on the Function Block Diagram does not affect operation, but deleting them improves the appearance of the diagram. Place the mouse pointer outside the upper left corner of CND4. Click and hold the left mouse button, then drag to include the lower right corner of the CND8 box. Boxes CND4 through CND8 should now be selected. If not, click a blank spot and try again. Press the Delete key to delete the selected items (or right-click, and then select Delete from the context menu.) Click Yes when asked to confirm the deletion. Another way to delete multiple blocks is to select them while holding down the Shift key, and then press the Delete key.

title: Removing VerticalPLUS Carriers
body_text: Removing VerticalPLUS Carriers Use the largest flat blade screw driver that will fit through the latch access holes on the carrier. Turn the latch cam approximately one quarter turn to the right as indicated on the graphic printed on the carrier top.

title: Rename a workstation
body_text: Rename a workstation Log in to Windows on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation as a user with Administrator privileges. Log in to DeltaV as a user with Administrator privileges. From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation open DeltaV Explorer. Select the node being renamed, right-click, and then select Rename . If this node has Alarms and Events enabled, you are prompted to disable Alarms and Events prior to renaming the workstation. To disable it, expand the workstation in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy and right-click the Alarms and Events item. Select Properties from the context menu. Uncheck the box and click OK . Enter the new workstation name. On the popup dialog that appears, click the Yes button to create a workstation configuration file. On the workstation you are renaming, log in to Windows as a user with Administrator privileges. Stop all DeltaV programs. Run DeltaV Workstation Configuration. From DeltaV Workstation Configuration, click Next , Next , Browse , and select the correct workstation name from the list in the workstation configuration file. Restart the computer when prompted by DeltaV Workstation Configuration. After the computer has restarted, log in to Windows as a user with Administrator privileges and let DeltaV Workstation Configuration complete. From the ProfessionalPLUS workstation use DeltaV Explorer to download all the nodes (you can either download them individually or as a group) on your DeltaV network. If you rename any workstations that are SQL servers (such as the Batch Historian, or Version Control machines), you must shut down and restart the workstation or restart the SQL Server. For more information about renaming a server, refer to the SQL Server online help. If you are renaming a workstation on a domain, you must verify the name and IP address of the newly renamed workstation has been updated in Active Directory and also on the DNS server. Go to the workstation that was promoted to domain controller first and verify that Active Directory is updated. Go to the DNS server (also on the first domain controller), right click the My Computer icon (this icon may have been renamed to the actual computer's name) and select Properties . Verify the IP address for the newly renamed workstation is updated. Workstation Configuration creates a new IP address for the workstation when it is renamed. If you are renaming a Continuous Historian workstation, you will need to export your datasets and import them after the rename. This is due to Continuous Historian using the workstation name as part of the data source name. Historical data collection will be stopped during the renaming process. Related information Downloading data

title: Rename module class parameters to avoid revealing parameter paths
main_heading: Rename module class parameters to avoid revealing parameter paths
body_text: Rename module class parameters to avoid revealing parameter paths For Module Class parameter shortcuts, (parameters that have the "Allow instance value to be configured" option enabled), the Hide Internal Structure command does not conceal the parameter path in instances of the Module Class. If you do not want parameter paths revealed in instances of the class, you must rename the parameters before using the Hide Internal Structure command. Select the Control or Equipment Module Class at the Library level and select Configure from the context menu. Select the Parameters or I/O tab in the Configuration dialog. Select the parameter and click the Rename button. Enter a parameter name that will not reveal the path and click OK . Close the Configuration dialog. Now select the Control or Equipment Module Class and click Hide Internal Structure .

title: Rename the Continuous Historian workstation
body_text: Rename the Continuous Historian workstation On the Continuous Historian workstation, select Start > Settings > Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Services . Stop the DeltaV services (including DVCHScan.exe, DVHistorianserver.exe andDVHistorianserver_2.exe. Run the Continuous Historian Administration application. Create a new Active dataset. This allows you to export the currently Active dataset. Export all Current and Extended datasets to the local drive. Close the Continuous Historian Administration application. Rename the workstation. Note: Restarting the workstation after running DeltaV Workstation Configuration will restart the DeltaV services on this computer. Stop the DeltaV services again. Rename the existing Continuous Historian database directory (for example, DeltaVHistory to DeltaVHistory-old). Copy the C:\DeltaV\fdbhist directory and paste it as the new D:\DeltaVHistory . Open a Command Prompt window and run the following Objectivity command to register the new database for use: C:\ooinstallfd -nocheck -standalone -lockserverhost COMPUTERNAME X:\DeltaVHistory\DvCHdb.hdb where COMPUTERNAME is the new name of the Continuous Historian workstation and X: is the drive where the \DeltaVHistory folder exists. Reboot the machine. Run the Continuous Historian Administration application. Restore all the exported datasets. Related information Rename a workstation

title: Replace the DeltaV Operate opening pictures
main_heading: Replace the DeltaV Operate opening pictures
body_text: Replace the DeltaV Operate opening pictures On slow connections, DeltaV Operate may take several minutes to open. (As noted above, enabling bitmap caching may significantly improve subsequent access.) For applications where slower remote connections are common, it may be useful to replace the opening DeltaV Operate pictures (DeltaV and Startup) with simpler versions (DeltaV.BLANK and Startup.BLANK). The replacement pictures are stored in the same directory as the originals. The DeltaV.grf and DeltaV.BLANK files are in the D:\DeltaV\DVData\Graphics-iFIX\Pic\ directory. The Startup.grf and Startup.BLANK files are in the D:\DeltaV\DVData\Graphics-iFIX\Pic\Standard\ directory. To preserve the original Startup.grf and DeltaV.grf files, rename them to new names, for example, Startup.original and DeltaV.original. Then rename the "blank" pictures (Startup.BLANK and DeltaV.BLANK) to Startup.grf and DeltaV.grf. This procedure is detailed below. To replace the DeltaV.grf and Startup.grf files Exit DeltaV Operate on the Server and any connected remote sessions. Log on to the Server machine as a privileged user. Open Windows Explorer. Go to the \DeltaV\DVData\Graphics-iFIX\Pic directory. Right-click the DeltaV.grf file and select Rename . Type the new file name, DeltaV.original, and click OK . Click OK to the warning and/or confirmation messages. Right-click DeltaV.BLANK and select Rename . Type the new name, DeltaV.grf, and click OK . Click OK to the warning and/or confirmation messages. Repeat the process for Startup.grf (rename to Startup.original) and Startup.BLANK (rename to Startup.grf) under \Pic\Standard . Restart DeltaV Operate.

title: Reset the keying mechanism on a CHARM Terminal Block
main_heading: Reset the keying mechanism on a CHARM Terminal Block
body_text: Reset the keying mechanism on a CHARM Terminal Block The keying mechanism on most CHARM Terminal Blocks is in a neutral position when shipped from the factory. In most cases, installing a CHARM sets the keying mechanism. For most CHARMs you can reset the keying mechanism if you need to remove the CHARM from the terminal block and install a CHARM of a different type. However, the CHARM Thermocouple mV Terminal Block has a fixed key setting and cannot be reset. Terminal block latch and release button Insert a small screwdriver into the release button to the left of the terminal block's latch, depress the release button, and remove the terminal block from the baseplate. Flip the terminal block 180° and notice the two small keying posts protruding from the bottom of the terminal block. Push the two keying posts completely in to return the posts to the neutral position. You will hear a click when the posts are completely pushed in. Verify that the keying posts are in the neutral position. In the neutral position, the ends of the posts sit slightly inside the bottom face of the terminal block. That is, the keying posts are sub flush to the bottom face of the terminal block. If the keying posts are flush with the bottom face of the terminal block, the keying posts are not yet in the neutral position. In this case, use your fingers to push the keying posts to the neutral position. Snap the terminal block back into the slot on the baseplate. You can now install a CHARM of a different type into the terminal block.

title: Reset a locked switch
body_text: Reset a locked switch If you are working with a switch that was previously commissioned and you are unsure of its status or configuration or the switch has locked up, you can connect to the switch through the serial port and reset the switch to the factory defaults. If a switch was previously in service, resetting the switch enables the Network Device Command Center to locate the switch and list it under Decommissioned Switches. Follow the steps in Establishing a serial port connection to a switch . At the Emerson prompt ( (Emerson NNNN > ), where NNNN is a switch type such as RM or MD, enter DeltaV default and press Enter . The switch responds with: Clearing configuration will interrupt switch operation for about 10 seconds. Are you sure you want to clear the configuration? (y/n) Press Y to clear the configuration.

title: Reset CHARM I/O Cards
body_text: Reset CHARM I/O Cards If the CHARM I/O Card (CIOC) assembly ( CIOCs, CIOC carrier and I/O Ports) was removed without being decommissioned, the CIOCs must be reset before they can be installed and commissioned to another system. CIOCs that were moved to another system without being properly decommissioned can interfere with communications to an existing node that has the same IP address. Remove both CIOCs from the carrier. Install the CIOCs in the opposite slots: move the CIOC in the right slot to the left slot and move the CIOC in the left slot to the right slot.
