title: Reset the FILL phase
body_text: Reset the FILL phase When the tank finishes filling, the phase automatically goes to Complete. Send a Reset command to place the phase in the Idle state. Unload the phase by clicking the Unload button on the UM_COLOR_100/P1 faceplate. Click the Reset Color Tanks button on the Process graphic to reset the tank. Minimize DeltaV Operate. You might want to repeat the exercises for testing the FILL phase until you are comfortable with the procedures. Later, in the Verifying Phase Coordination topic, you will use the Batch picture for stepping through equipment arbitration and phase messaging.

title: Reset Wireless I/O Cards
body_text: Reset Wireless I/O Cards If the Wireless I/O Card (WIOC) assembly ( WIOCs, WIOC carrier and I/O Ports) was removed without being decommissioned, the WIOCs must be reset before they can be installed and commissioned to another system. WIOCs that were moved to another system without being properly decommissioned can interfere with communications to an existing node that has the same IP address. Remove both WIOCs from the carrier. Install the WIOCs in the opposite slots: move the WIOC in the right slot to the left slot and move the WIOC in the left slot to the right slot.

title: Resolve a unit alias
body_text: Resolve a unit alias Unit aliases are resolved at the instantiation of the unit module. Expand the unit module (under Control Strategies in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy). Select the Aliases object. In the right pane, right-click the specific unit alias. Select Properties . Complete the Path field by browsing to the appropriate parameter (the module parameter or the parameter designated for history collection). Note: Modifying the resolution of a unit alias requires downloading the unit module.

title: Restore the security settings
body_text: Restore the security settings Follow this procedure to restore security settings from a previously created backup. The following procedure requires the MMC snap-in (Microsoft Management Console), and it only applies to workstations and servers in a domain environment. You must have privileges to write to the file system where you are storing the backed up settings. Note: Re-running Workstation Configuration does not re-apply the default settings; therefore, you must restore the settings from an archive/backup to return to the DeltaV default installed settings. Go to Start > Run and type Group Policy Management Console . Press Enter. The application can also be launched by typing GPMC at the command prompt (CMD.exe) and then press Enter. In the Group Policy Management Console (GPMC) console tree, go to the forest and domain containing the Group Policy object (GPO) you want to restore and expand the GPO. Right click the GPO and select Import Settings . Follow the instructions in the Import Settings Wizard .

title: Restoring the Batch Historian data
body_text: Restoring the Batch Historian data Restoration of the Batch Historian database can only be performed using the SQL Server Management Studio. All Batch Historian applications must be shut down before restoring data. Open the SQL Server Management Studio. Connect to the local SQL server. Expand Databases. Right-click the DVHisDB database. Select All Tasks . Select the Restore Database menu option. CAUTION: If the main database is restored, the database will only contain the data present at the time of the backup. All data added to the main database since that backup will be overwritten and potentially lost. If the data still exists in the form of Batch Executive .EVT files or still exists within the Event Chronicle, it will be added to the main database again. Restore any active archives by selecting and right-clicking the archive, selecting All Tasks , and then clicking the Restore Database menu option. Note: If you restore only the archive, there can be a mismatch between what is actually in the archive and what the main database shows is in the archives. Restore the main database and the archives together.

title: Restrict operator access in run mode
main_heading: Restrict operator access in run mode
body_text: Restrict operator access in run mode Security settings enable you to secure the run-time environment and restrict or prohibit specific operator actions. For example, you can prohibit the operator from closing the current picture and switching to another application. Note: The User Preferences dialog provides the means to define the DeltaV Operate start environment. To ensure security in your plant, it is very important that you carefully develop your security scheme before making changes to the start environment. Refer to the online help and Books Online for more information before making changes to the User Preferences dialog. Click Workspace > User Preferences , and then select the Environment Protection tab. Select the Enable Environment Protection check box, and then select the options that you want to enable.

title: Resume workbook updates
body_text: Resume workbook updates From the File tab, select Options > Formulas . In the Calculation options section under Workbook Calculation, select Automatic . Click OK . Note: This procedure causes all DeltaV read functions in the workbook to execute. Related information Stop workbook updates

title: Resync the base recipe
body_text: Resync the base recipe When a change is made to the base recipe and the recipe is downloaded to the Batch Executive, you need to resync the Campaign Manager's copy of that recipe with the Batch Executive's copy of that recipe. Refer to the Campaign Manager Operator Interface online help for the procedure.

title: Return to the state transition diagram
main_heading: Return to the state transition diagram
body_text: Return to the state transition diagram You have completed the running logic for the FILL phase logic. To return to the state transition diagram, you can do either of the following: Right-click anywhere on the SFC, and then select Back Out from the context menu. Click the phase class name, FILL, in the Hierarchy view. Save the FILL phase class and close Control Studio.

title: Rewire a WIOC or CIOC carrier installed with a copper IOP with fiber-optic cable
main_heading:
Rewire a WIOC or CIOC carrier installed with a copper IOP with
	 fiber-optic cable
body_text: Rewire a WIOC or CIOC carrier installed with a copper IOP with fiber-optic cable The I/O Ports (IOPs) on the CHARM I/O Carrier (CIOC) and the WirelessHART I/O Carrier (WIOC) are removeable to allow either copper or fiber-optic cabling between carriers and switches. Remove the network cable (copper) from the standby WIOC or CIOC's secondary control network port. Remove the copper IOP from the standby WIOC or CIOC's secondary control network port by depressing the button next to the IOP and pulling the IOP out of the carrier. Install a fiber IOP in the standby WIOC or CIOC's secondary control network port. Connect fiber-optic cable between the fiber IOP and a DeltaV Four Port Fiber switch. Refer to the DeltaV TM M-series Hardware Installation and Reference manual for information on the DeltaV fiber switches. Connect copper cable between the DeltaV Four Port Fiber switch and the secondary control network switch. Remove the network cable (copper) from the standy WIOC or CIOC's primary control network port. Remove the copper IOP from the standby WIOC or CIOC's primary control network port by depressing the button next to the IOP and pulling the IOP out of the carrier. Install a fiber IOP in the standby WIOC or CIOC's primary control network port. Connect fiber-optic cable between the fiber IOP and a DeltaV Four Port Fiber switch. Connect copper cable between the DeltaV Four Port Fiber switch and the primary control network switch.

title: Run Chkdsk
body_text: Run Chkdsk To aid in Windows, file system, or hard drive failure prevention or early warning, it is recommended that you run Chkdsk periodically and reinstall the supported service pack each time a software change is made to the system. Chkdsk is Windows' built-in file system error detection and repair utility. Running it scans the physical drive surface, checks each file, and looks for problems on the hard drive. Run Chkdsk periodically to safeguard against data loss. Running Chkdsk includes restarting a Windows workstation. Before performing this procedure, make sure of the following: All DeltaV applications on the workstation are closed. Your process is either properly shut down or being controlled by another node. You have adequate time to complete the procedure. If you are performing this procedure on a ProfessionalPLUS workstation, close all of the DeltaV Engineering Tools on all workstations on your DeltaV network. If you are unsure about any of the above requirements, call Technical Support. To run Chkdsk, perform the following procedure: Click Start > Programs > Accessories > Command Prompt . From the command prompt, enter the following: CHKDSK c: /f /r A message appears stating that Chkdsk will run the next time that the system is restarted. Restart the workstation. Upon restart, during the blue screen portion of the process, Chkdsk will run. Chkdsk can take five minutes or longer if problems are found on the drive. Once you are finished, log on to Windows. Click Start > Settings > Control Panels > Administrative Tools > Event Viewer . If the top line of the Event Viewer windows does not read, "Event Viewer - Application Log on \\ computer name" , click Log > Application . An entry labeled Autochk appears in the log that correlates to the last boot process. Double-click the entry to view the results of the Chkdsk. If no errors are reported in the log, you are finished. If errors are reported in the log, perform this process again. If an error occurs the second time you run Chkdsk, you might have a hard drive media problem. Call Technical Support immediately. If no errors occur the second time you run Chkdsk, Chkdsk has successfully corrected any problems it found.

title: Run the Barcode client application
body_text: Run the Barcode client application This chapter describes the steps necessary to run the Barcode application with DeltaV software. To run the application, you must first configure DeltaV software with the sample configuration. This configuration contains a few Named Sets and one module. After these have been imported and downloaded to a DeltaV controller, the application can connect and interact with the OpcSample SFC. Import the OPC-SAMPLE area using the DeltaV Explorer: In Explorer, select Import from the File menu. Select the file barcode.fhx, and then click OK . Assign the module, OPCSAMPLE in the area OPC-SAMPLE to a controller and download it. Once the OPCSAMPLE module is running in a controller the Barcode application can connect to the defined items and interact with the SFC. The SFC will loop through the recipe continuously. In Visual Basic, select Make EXE File.. from the File menu. Run the Barcode.exe file. The application may take a few seconds to start up the first time. The DeltaV OPC Data Access Server does not run automatically when the DeltaV system starts up. The DeltaV OPC Data Access Server will start when the first OPC client application issues a CreateObject call. The DeltaV OPC Data Access Server runs as a background process (no window) and will continue to run until DeltaV services are shut down. To see if the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server is running, open the Task Manager in Windows and look at the Process tab. The name of the executable is frsopcdv.exe.

title: Run the Controller Load Estimator
body_text: Run the Controller Load Estimator Run Setup.exe from \_Support\tools\LoadEstimator and follow the instructions in the setup program. When the setup program is complete it adds the DeltaV Controller Load Estimator application to the Start > Programs menu. Note: Be sure to read the Load_Estimator_Readme.txt file before running the Controller Load Estimator Tool.

title: Run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a DeltaV workstation
main_heading:
Run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a DeltaV
    workstation
body_text: Run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a DeltaV workstation To run an OPC client on a DeltaV workstation connected to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on an Application Station pair set up for redundancy, run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on the DeltaV workstation. Important: You must be logged on to the workstation as an administrator with privileges to write to the registry (to register the application) on the local machine to run this application. To start the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program, run RedDeltaVOPC.exe (located in the DeltaV\bin folder), or click Start > DeltaV Installation > Redundant DeltaV OPC Server . Then complete the following steps: In the Application Station pair field, enter the name of the Application Station where you selected the Redundant OPC option after enabling the Enable Redundancy for Assigned Modules option. Alternatively, click Browse to locate and select the Application Station. Important: Be sure to specify the name of the Application Station where you selected the Redundant OPC option—do not specify the name of its partner Application Station, which has the same name, but with the characters _S appended to it. Specifying an Application Station with a redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server After specifying the name of the Application Station in the Application Station pair field, click Validate . After the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program validates the Application Station, click Add . After clicking Add , the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server for the specified Application Station appears in the Redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access servers field as ROPC. nodename .1, where nodename is the name of the Application Station. Specifying an Application Station with a redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server

title: Run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a non-DeltaV workstation
main_heading:
Run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a
    non-DeltaV workstation
body_text: Run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a non-DeltaV workstation To run an OPC client on a non-DeltaV workstation connected to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on an Application Station pair set up for redundancy, run the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on the workstation. Important: You must be logged on to the workstation as an administrator with privileges to write to the registry (to register the application) on the local machine to run this application. To start the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program on a non-DeltaV workstation, complete the following steps: Install the OPC Remote application on the remote workstation by running the setup.exe program located in the DV_Extras\OPCRemote folder on DeltaV installation disk #1. The version must be the same as the installed version of the DeltaV software. Note: To uninstall OPC Remote, go to Programs and Features in Windows Control Panel and select OPC Remote from the list. Click the Change/Remove button and follow any dialogs presented. Connection to the DeltaV OPC Server is not available from the workstation when OPC Remote is uninstalled. When the Default DeltaV OPC Server dialog appears, click the Redundant OPC button. When you click the Redundant OPC button, the OPC Remote installation program runs the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program. In the Application Station pair field of the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program, enter the name of the Application Station where you selected the Redundant OPC option after enabling the Enable Redundancy for Assigned Modules option. Alternatively, click Browse to locate and select the Application Station. Important: Be sure to specify the name of the Application Station where you selected the Redundant OPC option—do not specify the name of its partner Application Station, which has the same name, but with the characters _S appended to it. After specifying the name of the Application Station in the Application Station pair field, click Validate . After the Redundant DeltaV OPC Server Configuration program confirms the Application Station, click Add . After clicking Add , the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server for the specified Application Station appears in the Redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access servers field as ROPC. nodename .1, where nodename is the name of the Application Station.

title: Save the configuration
body_text: Save the configuration You can save this configuration for when you want to retest the soft phase. However, if you change the soft phase, you may need to adjust the configuration. For example, if you add or remove report parameters in the soft phase, you need to do so in the Soft Phase Tester configuration file. Select File > Save As and enter a filename.

title: Save a snapshot of the firewall
main_heading: Save a snapshot of the firewall
body_text: Save a snapshot of the firewall If Emerson support asks for a snapshot of the entire firewall setup, you can save it to disk as well. To save a snapshot to disk: Open the Management station's web browser and enter the firewall 's IP address, for example https://10.5.128.18:443. The Security Alert dialog opens. Read the information on this dialog and click Yes . The Connect to dialog opens. Enter admin as Username and the default password if these have not changed from the factory settings. Otherwise, enter your Username and Password and click OK . The firewall's Welcome page opens. Find the Support folder on the left side of the Welcome page and expand it. Select Snapshot under the Support folder. Click Download on the Support Snapshot page. A Download dialog opens. Click Save to save the file as snapshot[1].tar. This file can be sent to Emerson support for analysis. Related information Verify the firewall configuration

title: Save the module
body_text: Save the module Click the Save button on the Quick Access Toolbar . The Browse dialog opens. In the Objects Type box, select Modules . In the Look In field, select Control Strategies , and then double-click TANK-101. MTR-101, the module you created earlier in DeltaV Explorer, is in the list of modules. In the Object Name box, type XV-101 as the name for this module, and then click Save .

title: Secure the DeltaV Operate environment
body_text: Secure the DeltaV Operate environment Environmental security protection is used to create a secure environment in DeltaV Operate that prevents the operator from navigating to unauthorized applications or from performing unauthorized actions. You can use the Environment Protection dialog in the Configure mode of DeltaV Operate to secure the environment. (You must have Configure privileges in order to access Configure mode.) All of your pictures share the same environment settings. Protected actions in DeltaV Operate are as follows: starting other tasks opening unauthorized pictures switching to unauthorized tasks closing the current picture exiting DeltaV Operate restarting the computer using CTRL+ALT+DEL Note: After installing the DeltaV software, restart the operating system before attempting to use environment protection for the first time. To secure the DeltaV Operate environment: Click Workspace > User Preferences . The User Preferences dialog opens. Click the Environment Protection tab. Environmental Protection tab for DeltaV Operate The following table describes the behavior of the Environment Protection settings. Setting Description Applications/desktops affected Disable title bar and menu bar Does not display the title bar or the menu bar. Removes the Minimize , Maximize , and Close buttons from the title bar Disabled for DeltaV Operate only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Disable menu bar Does not display the menu bar Disabled for the operator's interface only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Disable the Workspace pull-down menu Disables all entries in the Workspace menu selection in Run mode Disabled for DeltaV Operate only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Disable CTRL+ALT+DEL CTRL+ALT+DEL is ignored Disabled on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops as long as DeltaV Operate is running on either desktop Disable task switching ALT+TAB is ignored. Removes Minimize , Maximize , and Close buttons from the title bar ALT+TAB is disabled on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops as long as DeltaV Operate is running on either desktop Title bar is only affected on DeltaV Operate Disable VBE access Disables access to the Visual Basic Editor in Run mode Disabled for the DeltaV Operate only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Disable Workspace File menu accelerators Disables the menu accelerators that exists for the entries under the File menu Disabled for DeltaV Operate only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Disable Open accelerator Disable the CTRL+O accelerator Disabled for DeltaV Operate only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Disable Print accelerator Disable the CTRL+P accelerator Disabled for DeltaV Operate only on both the Windows and DeltaV desktops Establish the settings in the Environment Protection dialog. You can disable the menu bar and the title bar based on your own preferences. Task switching does not need to be disabled because operators can only switch between DeltaV applications made available from FlexLock, provided that Autoswitch Desktop is enabled. However, you might want to disable task switching if you want to display the title bar and menu bar in DeltaV Operate without allowing operators to have access to the Minimize , Maximize , and Close buttons. The following settings are recommended: Disable <Ctrl><Alt><Del> to provide a secure operating environment . The only resulting loss of functionality from the engineering environment will be the ability to change passwords or lock the workstation while DeltaV Operate is running. If you do not select this setting, an operator can log off, shut down, or lock the workstation from the Windows Security dialog. Invoking the task manager from the Windows Security dialog launches the task manager on the Windows desktop rather than the DeltaV desktop. Therefore, an operator is still unable to switch to or launch another application. Do not enable the menu bar . Emerson recommends that you not change this setting. Note: While running DeltaV Operate, operators can access other DeltaV system software applications through the buttons in the Toolbar window. If the currently logged-in operator does not have the privileges to run the application or to perform the function that is accessed by the button, the button is enabled but the system does not allow the operation. Related information DeltaV FlexLock

title: Select a base recipe for a campaign
main_heading: Select a base recipe for a campaign
body_text: Select a base recipe for a campaign Before you click the Create button on the Create Campaign dialog, you need to specify a recipe to be used as the base production recipe for the campaign. To select a base recipe, click Select on the Create Campaign dialog to display the Select Recipe dialog, shown below. You can scale the batch, change the unit bindings, view the unit alias resolution, load a formula and change parameter values from this dialog. When the recipe is configured as needed, click Select to set it as the base recipe for the campaign.

title: Select which alias to use on a unit module
main_heading: Select which alias to use on a unit module
body_text: Select which alias to use on a unit module A unit alias can be used on one unit module and not in another. Therefore you can create all the aliases that the unit class will use and, at the unit module, select which unit aliases are not to be used by selecting the Ignore option. Note: Only unit aliases that you create at the unit class can be set to Ignore . Unit alias that are created in the unit class (and inherited at the unit module) from control or equipment modules cannot be ignored. Expand the unit module (under Control Strategies in the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy). Select the Aliases object. In the right pane, right-click the specific unit alias. Select Properties . Select the Ignore check box. You do not have to select a parameter path when the alias is set to Ignore . Important: Leaving the parameter reference path blank without selecting the Ignore check box will result in errors when verifying the unit module. When downloading the unit module, the download occurs even when the Path and Ignore fields are blank.

title: Send a file to a printer
main_heading: Send a file to a printer
body_text: Send a file to a printer Most print to file functions save the file in PostScript format and will require a PostScript-compatible printer to print the file properly. Open a command prompt. Navigate to the directory where file is stored. Type: copy filename\\PrintServerName\printername (where PrintServerName is the print server and printername is the PostScript printer name as configured on the computer's Printer settings.)

title: Set a local policy for the softphaseuser on the non-DeltaV node
main_heading: Set a local policy for the softphaseuser on the non-DeltaV node
body_text: Set a local policy for the softphaseuser on the non-DeltaV node Setting a Local Policy for the SOFTPHASEUSER on the Non-DeltaV Node You must add the SOFTPHASEUSER to one local policy (Log on as a batch job). On the non-DeltaV node where the Soft Phase environment is installed, open Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Local Security Policy . Expand Local Policies . Select User Rights Assignments . Double-click the Log On As Batch Job policy. Click the Add User or Group button. Add the SOFTPHASEUSER. Click OK until all dialogs are closed.

title: Setting up an event chronicle
body_text: Setting up an event chronicle To record events in a workstation's Event Chronicle database: Drag the areas for which you want to record events and alarms to the Alarms and Events subsystem using DeltaV Explorer. Right-click the Alarms and Events subsystem and select Properties . Check the Enabled box. Under the Advanced tab, define how the system manages the event history data sets. Download the workstation.

title: Setting up each Batch Operator Interface
main_heading: Setting up each Batch Operator Interface
body_text: Setting up each Batch Operator Interface Operators can use the Batch Operator Interface to schedule and run batches. Typically, the Batch Operator Interface runs on an Operator Station, separate from the ProfessionalPLUS and Batch Executive workstations. When setting up each Batch Operator Interface, you need to follow these steps: Setup the workstation using DeltaV Workstation Configuration application ( Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Workstation Configuration ). Note: You must create a workstation configuration file from your ProfessionalPLUS workstation and use that for installing the Workstation Configuration on the Batch Operator Interface computer. Verify the Batch Operator Interface workstation is communicating on the DeltaV network. Start the Batch Executive (using the Application Manager). Start the Batch Operator Interface. Select the Batch Executive node to connect to. You can now run a batch using the Batch Operator Interface.

title: Setup the Batch Historian
body_text: Setup the Batch Historian Before starting the Batch Historian, do the following: Enable the Batch Historian. Choose the Batch Executive and Event Chronicle(s) from which the Historian will read data. Define the output locations the Historian will use to store batch data. Related information Enabling the Batch Historian Input configuration Output configuration

title: Set DCOM services on the non-DeltaV node for Soft Phases
main_heading: Set DCOM services on the non-DeltaV node for Soft Phases
body_text: Set DCOM services on the non-DeltaV node for Soft Phases Setting DCOM Services on the Non-DeltaV Node for Soft Phases If your soft phase connects to other DCOM services, you might need to configure the DCOM launch and access permissions for those applications to allow the SOFTPHASEUSER launch and access rights. In addition, you will need to set the DCOM Identity property for the DeltaV Soft Phase Broker application. Launch dcomcnfg. Open the DCOM Config folder and select the DeltaV Soft Phase Broker. Right-click and select Properties . Select the Identity tab. Select the This User radio button. Set the user to SOFTPHASEUSER with the same password as found on the DeltaV node. Click OK until all dialogs are closed. Close the DCOM Config application.

title: Set up a redundant DeltaV Control Network
main_heading: Set up a redundant DeltaV Control Network
body_text: Set up a redundant DeltaV Control Network A redundant DeltaV Control Network uses primary and secondary communication cables between controllers and workstations. Make and test the control network cables. Connect the unshielded end of a network cable to the twisted pair port on the workstation's primary Network Interface Card (NIC). Connect the shielded end of the network cable to the primary switch Connect the unshielded end of a network cable to the twisted pair port on the workstation's secondary Network Interface Card (NIC). Connect the shielded end of the network cable to the secondary switch. It is helpful to identify the control network cables with color-coded boots. Emerson recommends a yellow boot for the primary control network and a black boot for the secondary control network. Connect the network cables from the switches to the control network connectors on the bottom of the controller. Use shielded connectors at the controller. The front connector is for the primary control network and the rear connector is for the secondary control network.

title: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA PK controller server with third-party clients
main_heading:
Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA PK controller server with
	 third-party clients
body_text: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA PK controller server with third-party clients Note: User Certificate logon requires that application certificates are trusted. Note: Connecting to third-party clients that are external to the DeltaV network is a security risk. In DeltaV Explorer, navigate to the PK controller's OPC UA server subsystem and right-click Properties . Select the Certificate Logon checkbox. Click View Certificate . The software displays the View User Certificate dialog. Make sure there are values in the Name , Valid Until and Thumbprint fields. If these fields are blank, click Generate . Then, click Close . Click OK . Download the OPC UA server. Enter the password and click Export . The software exports a .pfx file. Third-party clients need this file for certificate Logon. Enter a password. This password will be used later when splitting the certificate into .der and .pem files or when importing the .pfx file.

title: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA PK controller server with DeltaV clients
main_heading:
Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA PK controller server with
	 DeltaV clients
body_text: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA PK controller server with DeltaV clients Note: User Certificate logon requires that application certificates are trusted. User certificates will not work if OPC UA clients are DeltaV clients (EIOC or Workstation) in the same DeltaV system as the PK controller. DeltaV OPC UA clients and the PK controller OPC UA server must be in separate DeltaV systems. In the DeltaV system that includes the OPC UA client, open User Manager. Click File > New > User . Enter a name in the Name field. Enter and confirm a password. In the Account Type section, select the OPC UA User checkbox. Click Certificates . The software displays the User Certificate dialog. Make sure there are values in the Name , Valid Until and Thumbprint fields. If these fields are blank, click Generate . Select Private + Public key (.pfx) , enter and confirm a certificate password, then click Export . The password specified during export will be required to import the certificate into another OPC UA device. Specify the export location of the newly created user certificate and click Save . Click Close to exit the User Certificate dialog box. Click OK to exit the User Properties dialog box. The DeltaV system may inform you that a download is necessary if changes have been made. Close User Manager. Right click on the physical device (PDT) of the OPC UA client and click Properties . In the Primary tab, click User Certificate from the Authentication drop-down list. Enter the username of the OPC UA enabled user. Download the EIOC PDT if prompted. In a different DeltaV system that includes the PK controller OPC UA server, open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the PK controller OPC UA server subsystem and right-click Properties . Select the Certificate Logon checkbox. Click View Certificate . The software displays the View User Certificate dialog. The user certificate exported from the system with the DeltaV OPC UA client will be imported into the PK controller using this dialog box. Click Import and locate the user certificate. Enter the certificate password when prompted. Click Close . Download the PK controller OPC UA server if prompted.

title: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA workstation server with third-party clients
main_heading:
Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA workstation server with
	 third-party clients
body_text: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA workstation server with third-party clients Note: User Certificate logon requires that application certificates are trusted. Note: Connecting to third-party clients that are external to the DeltaV network is a security risk. Open User Manager. Click File > New > User . Enter a name in the Name field. Enter and confirm a password. In the Account Type section, select the OPC UA User checkbox. Click Certificates . The software displays the User Certificate dialog. Make sure there are values in the Name , Valid Until and Thumbprint fields. If these fields are blank, click Generate . Then, click Close . Click OK . Open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the workstation's OPC server subsystem and right-click Properties . Click Set Users . Select the user that you created earlier in this procedure. Click Add . Click OK . Select the Certificate Logon checkbox. Click OK . Download the OPC UA server subsystem. Open User Manager and double-click the user you created earlier in this procedure. The software opens the Properties For User dialog. Click Certificates . The software displays the User Certificate dialog. Click Private + Public key (.pfx) . Enter a password. This password will be used later when splitting the certificate into .der and .pem files or when importing the .pfx file. Click Export . The software exports a .pfx file. Third-party clients need this file for Certificate Logon. Make sure application certificates are trusted between clients and the server.

title: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA workstation server with DeltaV clients
main_heading:
Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA workstation server with
	 DeltaV clients
body_text: Set up Certificate Logon for a DeltaV OPC UA workstation server with DeltaV clients Note: User Certificate logon requires that application certificates are trusted. Open User Manager. Click File > New > User . Enter a name in the Name field. Enter and confirm a password. In the Account Type section, select the OPC UA User checkbox. Click Certificates . The software displays the User Certificate dialog. Make sure there are values in the Name , Valid Until and Thumbprint fields. If these fields are blank, click Generate . Then, click Close . Click OK . Close User Manager. Open DeltaV Explorer. Navigate to the workstation's OPC UA server subsystem and right-click Properties . Click Set Users . Select the user that you created earlier in this procedure. Click Add . Click OK . Select the Certificate Logon checkbox. Click OK . Download the OPC UA server subsystem. Navigate to the physical device under the OPC UA client subsystem and right-click Properties . Click the Primary tab. In the Authentication section, select User Certificate from the drop-down list. Enter the username that you created earlier in this procedure. Click OK . Download the OPC UA client subsystem. Make sure application certificates are trusted between clients and the server. Note: User Certificate logon requires that application certificates are trusted.

title: Set up OSIsoft PI Server with a new DeltaV system
main_heading: Set up OSIsoft PI Server with a new DeltaV system
body_text: Set up OSIsoft PI Server with a new DeltaV system To install and set up OSIsoft PI Server with a new DeltaV system, complete the following steps: Install DeltaV and set up an Application Station. Important: When the Select Historian dialog appears, select the Enterprise Historian option. If you plan to run PI Server on the Application Station in the DeltaV Area Control Network (ACN), complete step t_setup_enterprise_pi_server_new_deltav_system.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_53__substep_ADBBD4809A6D4731943AF51851B2E2C6 below. If you plan to run PI Server on a remote Application Station or a non-DeltaV workstation outside the DeltaV ACN, complete step t_setup_enterprise_pi_server_new_deltav_system.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_53__substep_B3E21B98D3D646DBBE35B983F6D84681 below. Install and configure PI Server and the PI Asset Framework (PI AF) Server on the Application Station in the DeltaV ACN according to the documentation provided by OSIsoft. Install and configure PI Server and the PI AF Server on the remote Application Station or a non-DeltaV workstation outside the DeltaV ACN according to the documentation provided by OSIsoft. Alternatively, you can use existing PI Server and the PI AF Server software that meets all version requirements. Install the DeltaV Smart Connector on the Application Station in the DeltaV ACN according to the documentation provided by OSIsoft. Enable PI Server in DeltaV Explorer by right-clicking the Continuous Historian subsystem under the Application Station where you installed the DeltaV Smart Connector, and then selecting Properties . On the General tab, select the Enabled check box, and then select the Use Enterprise Historian option. Important: You will not be able to successfully download the workstation unless you selected the Enterprise Historian option in the Select Historian dialog, as instructed in t_setup_enterprise_pi_server_new_deltav_system.html#task_51B674B970AF4F56901608D74F08397E_unique_53__step_980B47629C8F486D8CBC8D5532223503_unique_43 . Download the Physical Network containing the Application Station where you installed the DeltaV Smart Connector. Note: To configure the parameters on the Advanced tab of the Continuous Historian Properties dialog, use the PI System Management Tools (PI SMT). Related information Historian installation The Continuous Historian subsystem

title: Access the Emerson Smart Firewall's web UI
main_heading: Access the Emerson Smart Firewall's web UI
body_text: Access the Emerson Smart Firewall's web UI This topic explains how to access the firewall's web user interface. The web user interface has an extensive online help system. Note: If the security level of the Internet Explorer browser is set to High, it is likely that you will need to add the firewall's IP address to IE's list of trusted sites. Refer to Adding the Smart Firewall to Internet Explorer's trusted sites . Note: Both Ethernet ports on the Smart Firewall are 10/100 auto-speed sensing and full/half duplex auto-negotiating. Do not configure any PC or switch port to either a fixed speed or duplex setting if it is to be directly attached to the Smart Firewall ports. Always let the connected devices auto-negotiate both speed and duplex with the Smart Firewall. Otherwise, communications could be negatively impacted and possibly stop. Read the Safety instructions for the Emerson Smart Firewall before connecting or using the firewall. Attach both of the included power cords to the AC mains. If the Power LED does not illuminate, ensure that the power feed is good (breakers, outlet strip switches/breakers). Refer to the troubleshooting topic for the location of the power LEDs. Attach a Cat. 5(e) Twisted Pair (TP) Ethernet cable with RJ45 connectors (100 meters/328 feet maximum) between the site's plant Ethernet switch or a plant network PC and the Smart Firewall's EXT (External/left side) port. Attach a Cat. 5(e) TP cable with RJ45 connectors (100 meters/328 feet maximum) between the DeltaV INT (right side) port of the Smart Firewall and the LAN Ethernet switch that is used for the DeltaV workstations' plant connections (sometimes called the third NIC). If there is only one DeltaV workstation communicating through the Smart Firewall, the Smart Firewall's DeltaV port can be directly connected to the workstation's third NIC. Verify all equipment is powered up. On the DeltaV PC that is connected to the Smart Firewall's INT port, open the Network Connections dialog from the Control Panel and select the third NIC. Set the third NIC's Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) properties to DHCP ( Obtain an IP address automatically ) and save this setting. This setting causes the Smart Firewall to assign the PC an IP address from its IP address pool. Note: It may be necessary to restart the PC or to run the ipconfig/release and ipconfig/renew commands from a command prompt in order for it to obtain an IP address from the Smart Firewall. On the same PC (the PC connected to the firewall's DeltaV port), open Internet Explorer, enter 192.168.1.1, (the firewall's default IP address) in the address area, and click the green arrow or press Enter . If the certificate error security warning appears, select continue to open the Smart Firewall's web user interface (UI). The certificate error security warning appears because the Smart Firewall uses HTTPS for communications and does not currently provide security certificates for these communications. Log in to the Smart Firewall's web UI using the default credentials: user: admin and password: Emerson1. The admin password can be changed later. Refer to Smart Firewall's web UI online help for information on changing passwords. Note: After 10 failed log in attempts, the firewall will block any log in attempts for one minute. Use the web UI's online help to assign a static IP address to the Smart Firewall's EXT (left side) port.

title: Set or change the system time
main_heading: Set or change the system time
body_text: Set or change the system time Setting the system time while the Advanced Continuous Historian or PI Server is running may cause unexpected results, because they track time according to the Windows clock, including the time zone and Daylight Savings Time (DST) settings. If the system clock is incorrect, historical data cannot be time-stamped accurately. Before setting the time or changing the time zone in DeltaV or on a non-DeltaV workstation where the Advanced Continuous Historian or PI Server is installed, refer to the OSIsoft PI Server System Management Guide for more information on time specifications and considerations. Note: OSIsoft recommends that you check the system clock regularly. If you need to make an adjustment, adjust the clock only in small increments: one second per minute, for example. Keep a record of all adjustments you make. Related information Historian run-time processes System time

title: Set DCOM access and launch permissions
main_heading: Set DCOM access and launch permissions
body_text: Set DCOM access and launch permissions In order for the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server service to run, the DCOM access and launch permissions must be set on the server machine. Most permissions are set when DeltaV software is installed. However, you must manually set permissions for anonymous logon. To confirm DCOM permissions and to set permissions for anonymous logon, complete the following steps: Run the executable file, dcomcnfg.exe. The Component Services window opens. In the left pane, open Component Services . A Computers folder appears. Open the Computers folder. The My Computer icon appears. Right-click the My Computer icon, and then select Properties . Select the COM Security tab, and then click the Edit Limits button in the Access Permissions group. From the Group or user names list, select ANONYMOUS LOGON , and then enable the Allow option for both Local Access and Remote Access permissions. Important: Neglecting to enable the Allow option for Remote Access permissions prevents an OPC client on a non-DeltaV workstation from being able to connect to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on an Application Station pair set up for redundancy. Open the My Computer icon. Several folders appear. Open the DCOM Config folder. Right-click FrsOpcDv in the list that appears, and then select Properties . Select the Security tab. The Access permissions should include the accounts that need to connect to the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. The SYSTEM account is the only account with Launch permission. The System account will also have Access permission. The accounts that need to connect are the ones that will actually be running the client application. If these are not Domain accounts then the user name and password must match on both the server and client machines for Windows to recognize the users as the same account. The user name must also be a DeltaV user on the server machine (defined by running DeltaV User Manager). Note: After the server is running, the launch permission setting is not used. The only user that launches the server is SYSTEM. Any other client accessing the server bypasses launch permissions and requires Access permission only. Select the Identity tab. The This user option should have been selected and DeltaVAdmin should be the user name. This tells COM how to launch the server. There are three options: Interactive User - Server is launched as user who is currently logged on the machine. If nobody is logged on, launch fails. Launching User - Server is launched with account running the client application on the other machine. This user/User - DCOM logs on the specific User in the background and starts server using caller's token. This is the setting needed for the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. Related information Configuring user accounts for OPC server and clients

title: Set DCOM security
body_text: Set DCOM security On both the server and client machines, DeltaV OPC Data Access Server must have the correct properties. Run the executable file, dcomcnfg.exe. The Component Services window opens. In the left pane, open Component Services . A Computers folder appears. Open the Computers folder. The My Computer icon appears. Right-click the My Computer icon, and then select Properties . Select the Default Properties tab to view the default DCOM security levels. The Default Authentication Level should have been set to Connect. The Default Impersonation Level should have been set to Identify. Once access is permitted, COM will check security for each call. There are two categories, AuthenticationLevel and ImpersonationLevel. The authentication level dictates how secure the communication is between the client and the server. The negotiated authentication level is the highest of client and server. It can not be RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_NONE if the callee wants to know who is calling him. The impersonation level is set up by the caller for how much it trusts the callee.

title: Set the DeviceNet device address
body_text: Set the DeviceNet device address An address configured for a DeltaV Explorer placeholder must match the MAC ID of the device you intend to place on the network. (Address 63 is reserved for new devices and address 62 is reserved for diagnostic purposes. Do not use these addresses.) You can set the address: On the device using switches and device specific parameters. With DeltaV Diagnostics if the device supports the standard method of addressing through setting the MAC ID parameter of the DeviceNet Object. Follow these steps to set the device address: Disable I/O Polling for the device in DeltaV Explorer and download the DeviceNet card. Open DeltaV Diagnostics. Right-click the device in the left pane, select Set Device Address , and enter an address. Enable I/O Polling and download the card in DeltaV Explorer to resume data exchange. Note: Set the address before you put the device on the network if the port is operational. Do not attach the device if you do not know the address or baud rate.

title: Set TANK101 as the next picture for the Overview picture
main_heading: Set TANK101 as the next picture for the Overview picture
body_text: Set TANK101 as the next picture for the Overview picture Open the Overview picture (Ovw_ref.grf) in the Pictures folder in the system tree. (Do not make any changes on this picture.) Save the file as My_Ovw_ref. Double-click the Next and Previous picture button. For the Next Picture, enter TANK101, and click OK. Save and close the My_Ovw_ref picture.

title: Set the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server
main_heading: Set the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server
body_text: Set the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server On the server machine, the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server application must be set to run on the local machine. Run the executable file, dcomcnfg.exe. The Component Services window opens. In the left pane, open Component Services . A Computers folder appears. Open the Computers folder. The My Computer icon appears. Open the My Computer icon. Several folders appear. Open the DCOM Config folder. Right-click FrsOpcDv in the list that appears, and then select Properties . Select the Location tab. On the client machine, the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server application must be set to run on the server machine. Related information Verify the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server

title: Set the update interval
body_text: Set the update interval Select the cell (or cells) where you want to store and display the update interval. Select the Add-Ins tab. From the Menu Commands group, click DeltaV and then select Runtime Data > Configure Update Interval . Click the Selected button to fill in the Named Range Location field. Select an update interval. You can select a number between 5 and 65. While you can enter intervals lower than 5 seconds, the lower numbers can, in some cases, adversely affect performance. Notes: The update interval applies to all read functions in the workbook. If multiple workbooks are open, you must define the update interval for each one with the same value. To determine whether an update interval named range has already been defined, select the Home tab. In the Editing group, click Find & Select > Go To and select DVUpdateInterval . Related information Resume workbook updates Set the update interval directly in Excel Stop workbook updates

title: Set the update interval directly in Excel
main_heading: Set the update interval directly in Excel
body_text: Set the update interval directly in Excel Select the cell where you want to store and display the update interval. Select the Formulas tab. In the Defined Names group, click Define Name and then select Name > Define Name ... Type DVUpdateInterval . Select the scope (workbook or a worksheet) and click OK . Enter the update interval in the cell. Note: To determine whether an update interval named range has already been defined, select the Home tab and, in the Editing group, click Find & Select > Go To . Then select DVUpdateInterval . Related information Resume workbook updates Set the update interval Stop workbook updates

title: Set up a new project
body_text: Set up a new project Creating an OPC client application in Visual Basic means creating an OLE Automation client. Using OLE Automation, you can borrow the functionality of other applications by controlling their objects from within your Visual Basic application. If the object is an OLE Automation object, you can use its properties and methods in code. To start this application, open the VB project, Barcode, and add references to the OPCDisp library. This gives you project access to all of the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server interfaces and their properties and methods. Use the References dialog to make another application's objects available in your code. This dialog allows you to set a reference to the other application's object library. Also included with the project is a TrueType bar code font called 3of9.ttf. To load this font, go to Control Panel, Fonts. Select Install New Font from the File menu. Select the file, \DeltaV\samples\Opc\Start\3of9.ttf , and then click OK . Related information Reference OPC in your project

title: Enable historical data collection
body_text: Enable historical data collection The Continuous Historian subsystem must be enabled on each workstation that will be used to collect, store, and retrieve historical data. The Continuous Historian subsystem exists under the workstation in DeltaV Explorer. You can enable the DeltaV Continuous Historian on a Professional PLUS workstation , an Application Station, or an Operator Station. No more than one Continuous Historian subsystem can be enabled on a single DeltaV workstation. Within the DeltaV network, only the DeltaV Continuous Historian, the Advanced Continuous Historian, or OSIsoft PI Server can be enabled to run on an Application Station. You can also, however, install PI Server on a non-DeltaV workstation outside the DeltaV network. Complete the following steps to set up the Continuous Historian subsystem: Configure history collection for module and node parameters. Assign the modules. Note: Historical data for modules can only collected if the modules are assigned. Download the controllers or workstation to which the modules are assigned. Enable the Continuous Historian subsystem for the workstation(s) that collects historical data and configure the historian properties. To enable the Continuous Historian subsystem on a Professional PLUS workstation or an Operator Station, right-click the Continuous Historian subsystem under the workstation in DeltaV Explorer on the Professional PLUS workstation, and then select Properties from the context menu. On the Continuous Historian Properties dialog, select the Enabled check box. To enable the Continuous Historian subsystem on an Application Station, right-click the Continuous Historian subsystem under the workstation in DeltaV Explorer on the Professional PLUS workstation, and then select Properties from the context menu. On the Continuous Historian Properties dialog, select one of the following options in the Continuous Historian Selection field: Use DeltaV Continuous Historian Use Advanced Continuous Historian Use Enterprise Historian Important: You will not be able to successfully download the workstation unless the historian that you enable matches the historian selected in the Select Historian dialog while installing the DeltaV Application Station or the historian selected in the Continuous Historian box of the DeltaV Upgrade Wizard configuration dialog while upgrading the Application Station. Assign specific area folders and nodes to the Continuous Historian subsystem. Download the workstation. Note: After the initial download of the history collection subsystem there may be a short period of time before the overall integrity of the subsystem reports GOOD. Related information Configure the Continuous Historian subsystem properties Configure history collection in DeltaV Explorer Historian installation

title: Set up the existing Application Station
main_heading: Set up the existing Application Station
body_text: Set up the existing Application Station Connect the new Application Station to the DeltaV network. In DeltaV Explorer on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, right-click the existing Application Station under System Configuration > Physical Network > Control Network . Click Properties on the shortcut menu for the Application Station. You can optionally change the name of the existing Application Station on the General tab of the Properties dialog, but this is not necessary. However, changing the Application Station name is strongly recommended if it coincidentally ends with the characters _S. Important: As a general rule, do not specify an Application Station name that ends with the characters _S. When the DeltaV system creates a pair of Application Stations for redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server, it appends these characters to whatever name you specify as the base name for the Application Station. Having a pair of Application Stations named nodename _S and nodename _S_S could result in misleading or undesirable results while working with redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server. On the Redundancy tab of the Properties dialog, check the Enable a redundant subsystem option, select the Assigned Modules option, and then select either the OPC Data Access Server option or the OPC Data Access Server and OPC Mirror option. Important: You cannot enable redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on a pair of Application Stations if you have already enabled any other subsystems, such as Batch Executive, Batch Historian, Continuous Historian, Campaign Manager, Alarms and Events, or Remote Network, for the existing Application Station. To enable redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server on a pair of Application Stations, you must first disable any previously-enabled subsystems for this Application Station. You can optionally enable the Unattended Workstation Reboot on Failover or Manual Switchover option, if either of the Application Stations will be located in an unmanned facility, for example. Enabling redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server with OPC Mirror Click OK to close the Properties dialog for the Application Station. When prompted to export a workstation configuration file for the existing Application Station, click Yes . Save the workstation configuration file either to removable media or to a network location that can be accessed from the Application Station you are configuring. You can use the default name for a workstation configuration file, DevData.cfg, or specify a different file name. On the existing Application Station, import the workstation configuration file by clicking Start > DeltaV Installation > DeltaV Workstation Configuration . When the introductory DeltaV Workstation Configuration dialog appears, click Next . For the Select Workstation Type option, select Professional / Operator / Application / Base / Inter-Zone Server , and then click Next . Specifying the type of workstation When prompted to provide the workstation configuration file that you made earlier on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation, click Browse , navigate to the exported workstation configuration file, and double-click it. Importing the workstation configuration file Select the workstation name, and then click Next . The following message appears: A node with Redundant Assigned Modules has been selected. Is this the preferred active Application Station? It is recommended that you respond to this prompt by clicking Yes when configuring the existing Application Station. When you click Yes , the Application Station is given the name specified for it in DeltaV Explorer. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the configuration of the Application Station. Note: If you ever need to reconfigure either workstation in the pair, you should respond to this prompt by clicking Yes if it is the Application Station that you specified as the preferred active; otherwise, click No , if it is the workstation with the characters _S appended to the base Application Station name. Related information Install DeltaV on the first Application Station Connecting to the redundant DeltaV OPC Data Access Server Using the unattended reboot option Initiate a manual switchover

title: Set up Username/Password logon for an OPC UA PK controller server
main_heading:
Set up Username/Password logon for an OPC UA PK controller
	 server
body_text: Set up Username/Password logon for an OPC UA PK controller server In order for Username/Password logon authentication to work on a DeltaV PK controller server, you must trust the OPC UA client certificate. Using DeltaV Explorer, select the PK controller OPC UA Server and right-click Properties . Click Set User . The system displays the Set Username and Password dialog. Enter a user name. You are defining the name at this point. This is not an existing name. Enter a password. Click OK . Click OK on the OPC UA Server dialog. Using DeltaV Explorer, download the PK controller OPC UA subsystem. Download the workstation’s OPC UA subsytem. Select the OPC UA client physical device (PDT) and right click Properties . Click the Primary tab. In the Authentication section, select Username from the drop down list. Enter the username and password you created previously. Download the physical device. Test the OPC UA client-side communications. Related information Test OPC UA client-side communications

title: Set up Username/Password logon for an OPC UA workstation server
main_heading:
Set up Username/Password logon for an OPC UA workstation
	 server
body_text: Set up Username/Password logon for an OPC UA workstation server In order for Username/Password logon authentication to work on a DeltaV workstation server, you must trust the OPC UA client certificate. Go to Start > DeltaV Engineering > User Manager . In User Manager > File > New > User . Select OPC UA User . Enter a user name. You are defining the name at this point. This is not an existing name. Enter a password. Click OK . The software displays the user name you created. The software displays a message asking you to perform a full download and log on again. Click OK . In the Authentication section, select Username from the drop down list. Enter the username and password you created previously. Download the physical device. Test the OPC UA client-side communications. Related information Test OPC UA client-side communications

title: Set up a workstation to run Batch Executive
main_heading: Set up a workstation to run Batch Executive
body_text: Set up a workstation to run Batch Executive In DeltaV Explorer, select System Configuration/Physical Network/Control Network , and then click the + next to the workstation name. Select and right-click Batch Executive , and then select Properties from the context menu. On the General tab of the Properties dialog, click Enabled to enable this workstation for batch. You will be reminded that you will need to download the workstation. Fill in the fields on the Server tab as follows: Revision - leave as is Maximum event file age - 15 Restart behavior - Query User Hold propagation limit - UOP (operation level) Allow manual phase history to be combined with other batch history - leave as is Click OK . Download the workstation.

title: Set working folders
body_text: Set working folders Before you can store documents in VCAT and work on them from DeltaV Explorer, you must create a folder hierarchy in DeltaV Explorer and move the documents you want to store in VCAT into that hierarchy. The folder hierarchy you create can be arbitrarily complex, consisting of as many subfolders as you need. You can explicitly set a different working folder for each folder in DeltaV Explorer. Alternatively, You can create a working folder structure that mirrors the folder hierarchy in DeltaV Explorer. A simple way to do this is: Select the Documents folder, and then select Set Working Folder from the context menu. If the working folder has not been previously set, the Browse For Folder dialog appears as shown. Navigate to the location where you want to create a working folder structure, and then click Make New Folder . A new folder appears in the dialog. Select Rename from the context menu and enter the name you want for the working folder (VCAT_WORK, for example) as shown in the following figure. Click OK to accept the name and close the dialog. Note: Each user must set working folders on each workstation. The working folders can be different for each user and each workstation. Create the DeltaV Explorer folder hierarchy you need. Select the Documents folder (or folders you created), and then select New > Document Folder from the context menu. Folders are created named Document Foldernn . You can rename the folders. Add documents to the hierarchy in DeltaV Explorer. There are several ways to add documents to the hierarchy in DeltaV Explorer: Select a folder and then select New > Text Document . You can rename the document after you created it. Select a folder, and then select Add Documents . The Add Documents dialog appears. Navigate to documents, and then click Add . Drag documents of any type from Windows Explorer to a folder in DeltaV Explorer. Creating subfolders and adding documents to them in the DeltaV Explorer Documents folder adds them to the DeltaV database and the VCAT database. When you add documents they are automatically checked out of VCAT. Before you edit a document you must set the working folder for the directory the document is in and retrieve the document. You can set the working folders for the entire Documents folder hierarchy in DeltaV Explorer and retrieve all the documents in the hierarchy at one time as follows. Select the Documents folder, and then select Retrieve from the context menu. The Retrieve Documents dialog appears with the working directory you previously set for the Documents folder. Select Recursive on the dialog. Click OK . Because you have not set a working folder for the subfolders, the following dialog appears: Click Yes All to create all of the subdirectories in the working folder and retrieve all the documents in the hierarchy. If you subsequently add subfolders, working folders are set to the appropriate place in the working folder structure. You must still retrieve new folders and any documents you add, to new folders or existing folders, before you can edit these documents. Note: If you change a folder name in DeltaV Explorer after setting a working folder for it, the links to the working folders are retained. The following figure shows an example folder hierarchy consisting of two subfolders below the Documents folder. The SOPs directory contains an Excel workbook and three text documents. The Contents pane contains information about the documents in the current folder. For example: dsts.xls is checked in (no check mark) and was last modified by user U1. SOP1.txt is checked out to the current user (red check mark). SOP2.txt is checked in (no check mark) and was last modified by ADMINISTRATOR. SOP3.txt is checked out to another users (blue check mark), U1 in this case.

title: Show statistics on a trend line
main_heading: Show statistics on a trend line
body_text: Show statistics on a trend line You can show statistical markers on the graph for selected trends. Available statistics for each trend include its minimum and maximum values, time-weighted average, and totalized value. The following steps explain how to show statistics for the minimum, maximum, and time-weighted average on the trend line. Click Chart > Configure Chart . In the Configure Chart tab, select the Show Statistics check box next to each parameter reference for which you want to show statistics. The trend's minimum value, maximum value, and time-weighted average are shown on the trend line. To modify which statistics are shown on a trend line, select a trend and click Details . Deselect the check box for any values ( Min , Max , Time Average ) you do not want to show on the trend line. If you want to show the totalized value on the trend line, select the Total check box. Enter the Multiplier and Engineering unit to use for the totalized value. Click OK .

title: Simulate phase logic
body_text: Simulate phase logic You can specify a phase for simulation only. This enables you to run the phase logic in the Recipe Simulator (instead of in the controller) to test the recipe without affecting the plant. To mark a unit phase for simulation, Select the unit phase in DeltaV Explorer. Right-click and select Properties . Check the Simulate check box to enable simulation. Click OK . To mark a phase logic module for simulation, Open the module in Control Studio. Click inside the Diagram View area. Right-click and select Properties . Select the Simulate check box. Unit Phase Properties with Simulate Enabled Once the Simulate check box is selected, any time the phase logic is used as a phase in an operation, the Batch Executive accesses the Recipe Simulator for information about the phase rather than looking at the phase logic in the controller. The Batch Operator Interface displays DVBSIM in the status bar. This indicates to the operator that some simulation is in effect and recipes might not be in control for some phases. However, the phase logic running in the controller is not affected by the Simulate function. It is still downloaded to the controller and can still be operated by setting its OWNER parameter to external. The operator can then control the phase manually from a faceplate on the operator's workstation. Whenever you change the phase logic to or from Simulate, you must download the workstation on the Batch Executive node. Run the Recipe Simulator on the same machine as the Batch Executive to simulate the phase logic. Related information The Batch Executive properties Recipe Simulator

title: Install carrier extender cables
body_text: Install carrier extender cables A standard installation uses one carrier extender cable; however, dual carrier extender cables can also be used. The following procedure is for a standard installation that uses one carrier extender cable. Install the right and left-side one-wide carriers by sliding together the 48 pin connectors on the sides of the carriers. One-wide carriers Connect the 44 pin D-shell (male) connector on the carrier extender cable to the top D-shell connector labeled A on the right-side carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Connect the 44 pin D-shell connector on the other end of the cable to the top D-shell connector labeled A on the left-side carrier and fasten the retainer screws.

title: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail
main_heading: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail
body_text: Install the Column Terminator onto the DIN rail The Column Terminator terminates the redundant bus. It installs after the last baseplate on the DIN rail. Installing the Column Terminator Locate the last baseplate on the DIN rail. Typically, this is the baseplate with Address Plug 8. If the baseplate is an I.S. Baseplate be sure to install a Separation Wall on the baseplate. Ensure that the lock on the Column Terminator is in the locked position. Insert a screw driver into the lock and turn it counter-clockwise to engage the lock. Align the connectors on the Column Terminator with the connectors on the last baseplate and snap the terminator onto the DIN rail. After installing the Column Terminator you can install a DIN Rail Stop and then wire your field devices to the terminal blocks on the baseplates. Refer to the terminal block specifications in the DeltaV SIS™ CHARMs Smart Logic Solver Hardware Reference manual for more information. After wiring your devices, perform all standard field wiring checkout procedures. Related information Install a Separation Wall

title: Add a static route to a workstation
main_heading: Add a static route to a workstation
body_text: Add a static route to a workstation The route add command is used to add a route to a computer's routing table. This topic presents basic information about the format of the route add command. Before using this command, consult with your IT department or network administrator for the correct network addresses and subnets used in your organization and for more information on using the route add command. Note: The route add command is effective on computers that are one hop from the firewall. If your computers are more than one hop from the DeltaV 2.5 LAN then you should consult with your IT department to ensure the proper routing is set up for these computers to access the firewall. Open a command prompt and enter route add -p Destination mask Netmask Gateway. Route add: adds the route to the routing table in the computer. -p: makes the specified route persistent on the computer so the route survives a reboot. Destination: the address of the network on the other side of the firewall to which this computer needs to communicate. mask: the subnet mask of the Destination network. Gateway: The gateway to the Destination network. For the Smart Firewall this is the IP address of the external port on the firewall. Related information What is the 2.5 network?

title: Configure Emerson Smart Firewall remote logging using its WebUI
main_heading:
Configure Emerson Smart Firewall remote logging using its
    WebUI
body_text: Configure Emerson Smart Firewall remote logging using its WebUI This procedure uses the Smart Firewall's WebUI to configure the Smart Firewall for use with a syslog server. There are many types of syslog server software packages available, from no cost, open source versions to more costly private versions. If your IT department does not have a syslog server preference, we suggest that you install a simple syslog server, such as the free KIWI Syslog Server and use it to collect and archive firewall logs for security analysis. Note: Users are responsible for acquiring the syslog daemon and must install and run the syslog daemon per the manufacturer's instructions. Emerson provides no support or warranty for any syslog daemon. The KIWI Syslog Server has been tested to work with the DeltaV system and the Emerson Smart Firewall. The free KIWI Syslog Server for Windows is available at http://www.kiwisyslog.com/ . Refer to the Emerson Smart Firewall's WebUI help for any additional information. Connect to the firewall from a browser using the firewall's IP address. Open the Configuration tab and choose Logging . Select the Logging facility for UI events. This is the category assigned to firewall events. It is a label only and does not affect how events are logged. The default facility is User . You might change this if User is already assigned to a different group of events in your system log. Select Enable to turn on remote logging. Enter the name or IP address of the remote server (normally on the DeltaV 2.5 LAN) to which the log will be saved. This is the same computer as where the syslog server is installed. Select the minimum priority level for events that are sent to the remote log. It is recommended this be set to Debug . Click Apply . Close the web browser when all changes are complete and applied/saved.

title: Configure DeltaV Smart Switch remote logging using the switch module
main_heading:
Configure DeltaV Smart Switch remote logging using the switch
    module
body_text: Configure DeltaV Smart Switch remote logging using the switch module Switch events can be written to a standard reporting format log file that is then saved to a remote server as historical data. A syslog server application must be installed on the computer accepting the logging information and that computer's IP address must be known and accessible to the switch. There are many types of syslog server software packages available, from no cost, open source versions to more costly private versions. If your IT department does not have a syslog server preference, we suggest that you install a simple syslog server, such as the free KIWI Syslog Server and use it to collect and archive firewall logs for security analysis. Note: Users are responsible for acquiring the syslog daemon and must install and run the syslog daemon per the manufacturer's instructions. Emerson provides no support or warranty for any syslog daemon. The KIWI Syslog Server has been tested to work with the DeltaV system and the DeltaV Smart Switch. The free KIWI Syslog Server for Windows is available at http://www.kiwisyslog.com/ . Open DeltaV Explorer. Select the switch module. There are two methods to setting the SYSLOG_IP_ADDR parameter's value. At the class level - to do this, select the switch module class (under Libary > Advanced Definitions > Control Module Classes > Switches . At the instance level - to do this, select the instance of the switch module in the area. The module class must have the Allow instance value to be configured option selected. Tip: When managing switches on multiple networks, select the Allow instance value to be configured option in the module class. This allows you to configure different IP addresses for each switch, as not all switches will be able to connect to the same syslog server because the subnets will be different on the switches. Right click the SYSLOG_IP_ADDR parameter and select properties. Note: This parameter is only visible in the switch module instance if the module class has the Allow instance value to be configured option selected. Enter the IP address of the syslog server computer in the Value: field. Click OK. Download the switch. If configuring the module class and no switches are commissioned yet, the download during commissioning will set this address. Related information General parameters (Smart Switch) Commissioning and monitoring DeltaV Smart Switches Smart Switch module classes

title: Specify that a parameter is configurable
main_heading: Specify that a parameter is configurable
body_text: Specify that a parameter is configurable In Control Studio, select the DC block on the NC_VALVE module class. The parameters for this block are listed in the lower left pane. (If necessary, check the various filter boxes so that all the parameters are visible in the list.) Click the Categorized tab. In the Tuning category, select DELAY_TIME as the parameter you wish to make configurable at the instance level and open the Properties dialog. Check the box Allow instance value to be configured. The default value for DELAY_TIME for all instances created from this class is 0, but the value can now be changed for particular instances. Note that the Properties dialog can also be opened in DeltaV Explorer to make this kind of change. Save the class and close Control Studio. Later, when instances of the valve have been created in the System Configuration section of the DeltaV Explorer, we can select the DC block on any of those valve control modules, open the Properties dialog, delete the check mark from the box Use default value from library object, and then change the parameter value for that instance. Thus, if we wanted to add a delay of 10 seconds to the opening of a particular valve, the Properties dialog for the DELAY_TIME parameter on its DC block would look like the following:

title: Specify the DSTs for MTR-101
body_text: Specify the DSTs for MTR-101 In the Function Block diagram, click DC1 , the Device Control function block. In the Parameter window, double-click IO_IN_1 , the parameter for the run status signal. In the Properties dialog, type XI-1 in the Device Tag field, and then click OK . If you have configured the controller hardware and I/O channels, you can browse for the Device Tag under the controller. The parameter field is automatically set to the correct parameter, FIELD_VAL_D. Double-click the IO_OUT_1 parameter. (This is the output signal from the Discrete Loop block to the field device.)
