In the Properties dialog, type ZX-1 in the Device Tag field, and then click OK . The parameter field is automatically set to OUT_D. Related information Configuring the hardware

title: Specify the historical data server in Process History View
main_heading: Specify the historical data server in Process History View
body_text: Specify the historical data server in Process History View To view historical data with Process History View, you must specify the node where PI Server is running in the Historical Data Server field on the Continuous Historian tab of the Set Default Data Servers dialog in Process History View. If the node where PI Server is running does not appear on the drop-down list—for example, in a DeltaV Zones environment or when an integrated PI Server is installed on a non-DeltaV workstation—you can enter the node name in the Historical Data Server field explicitly. Tip: To improve performance when opening a chart for historical data, enable the Connect to Advance Continuous Historian Server option on the Continuous Historian tab of the Set Default Data Servers dialog. For more information, refer to the application help for Process History View. Related information Create a trust to view historical data on a remote system (PI Server) Change the data source for historical data

title: Specify the unit parameter value for UM_COLOR_100
main_heading: Specify the unit parameter value for UM_COLOR_100
body_text: Specify the unit parameter value for UM_COLOR_100 Select UM_COLOR_100. In the right pane, double-click the unit parameter CAPACITY to open the Properties dialog. Change the Value to 600.

title: Create partial controller data in SmartPlant Instrumentation and retrieve it to the DeltaV database
main_heading: Create partial controller data in SmartPlant Instrumentation and retrieve it to the DeltaV database
body_text: Create partial controller data in SmartPlant Instrumentation and retrieve it to the DeltaV database It is possible to create a partial configuration in SmartPlant Instrumentation, retrieve it into the Excel worksheet, and save it into the DeltaV database. For example, you may need to add more instruments and their configuration information to an existing controller: Create the configuration in SmartPlant Instrumentation. Publish the configuration. In Excel, select DeltaV > SPI Interface > Retrieve from SPI . Browse to and select the file you published from SPI. The Select Load Format dialog appears. Select any required columns that are not already selected and click OK . The workbook containing the data appears. Enter the word Partial in the value column of the node row, overwriting any text already in the cell. Select DeltaV > I/O Support > Data Manager . Because you have told the software that this is a partial controller configuration, you cannot load or save the workbook, you can only reconcile the workbook against an existing controller. Click Reconcile . The Excel add-in merges the information you retrieved from SPI with the information from the DeltaV database. Items that are different from the database are flagged as comments. Review the changes and if you are satisfied, save the merged information to the database. Note: The Partial Controller Reconcile feature assumes that all existing objects in the DeltaV Database should remain. Any object that is in the DeltaV database which is not found in the file retrieved from SPI is simply fetched in to the Excel worksheet. Do not attempt to rename or delete any objects when working with a partial controller.

title: Adding Visual Basic for applications and .NET programmability support
main_heading:
Adding Visual Basic for applications and .NET programmability
    support
body_text: Adding Visual Basic for applications and .NET programmability support There are two features you must add to Microsoft Office to ensure that the add-ins work correctly. To add the features: Select Start > Settings > Control Panel . Double-click Programs and Features. Select the version of Microsoft Office Professional Plus installed on the computer. Right-click and select Change . On the dialog that appears, select Add or Remove Features. Click Continue . Under Microsoft Office Excel, click .NET Programmability Support and select Run from My Computer . Under Office Shared Features, click Visual Basic for Applications and select Run from My Computer . Click Continue . Wait for VBA to be configured, and then click Close .

title: Retrieving data from SmartPlant Instrumentation
body_text: Retrieving data from SmartPlant Instrumentation After you have configured instrument data in the SmartPlant Instrumentation application and have published it to an xml file, you can retrieve the data into an Excel worksheet. If you have not previously generated the libraries you are prompted to do so before you can continue. It is recommended that you regenerate the libraries once at the beginning of each session unless you are sure that there have been no changes to the database since your last session. Select the SPI Interface > Retrieve from SPI option to load the xml file. After selecting the file, the Select Load Format dialog appears. By default all the columns necessary for the SmartPlant Instrumentation interface are selected. Note: Do not change the default selections in the Select Load Format dialog. Modifying the selections may cause errors when you attempt to save configurations created in SmartPlant Instrumentation to the DeltaV Database. If errors appear during retrieve do not save the data to the DeltaV database. Make a note of the errors and close the worksheet without saving it. Return to SmartPlant Instrumentation, correct the errors, and re-publish the data. SPI now has the capability to add user-defined rules in its Rule Manager. Contact your database administrator to get appropriate rules added for working with DeltaV. Click OK to load the data into the worksheet. At this point you can edit the information in the workbook—configure items that are configurable, bind instrument data to I/O channels, and so on. After you have completed your edits, open the Data Manager dialog ( DeltaV > I/O Support > Data Manager ) to save the data in the workbook to the DeltaV database. Related information Editing instrument and signal data in Excel

title: SPI: Retrieving multiple XML files
body_text: SPI: Retrieving multiple XML files If you have multiple XML files you need to retrieve and work with in Excel, you must work on one file at a time. This is a limitation of Excel and add-ins. To work with multiple XML files, follow these steps: Start Excel. Retrieve from SPI. Work on data. Open Data Manager. If Data Manager is already open, close and reopen it to refresh the Excel column of the Controllers list. Save your work to the DeltaV database from the Data Manager. If you need to work on additional xml files retrieved from SPI to work on, close Excel and begin again at step 1.

title: SPI: set up SmartPlant software
body_text: SPI: set up SmartPlant software In addition to installing the add-ins and the Intergraph components there are other setup tasks to perform: The administrator may choose to add rules to SPI to make it more useful for DeltaV configuration. The administrator must choose a tag convention that is compatible with DeltaV software and make the tag conventions for instruments, fieldbus devices, and control system tags (CSTs) and so on conform to it. Create a new user environment variable: EFCommonFileMode=1 To create the variable, open System Properties from the Control Panel, open the Advanced tab and click Environment Variables . In the Environment Variables dialog, click the New button under the User variables pane, and then enter the variable name and value. There are two additions the administrator must make to the INtools.ini file (located in \Program Files\SmartPlant\Instrumentation ): The administrator must choose a tag separator for SPI to parse instrument tags on. For example, "-", "_", or "$." In the [API] section of the INtools.INI file add the following line: NameSpacesReplacement=$ In the [database] section of the INtools.ini file, add the following line: LOCK=RC In SPI select Tools > Interfaces > DeltaV to open the DeltaV Interfaces dialog. Select Retrieve DeltaV definitions as shown below. Then click OK and browse to the definitions source path. Then click OK again. Note: It is recommended to retrieve the fieldbus definitions first, then retrieve the HART definitions. The files should retrieve successfully. Note that this process is additive. Old definitions are not deleted automatically, because they may be in use. However, if you publish objects with obsolete definitions for the target DeltaV system, then Retrieve into DeltaV will have errors. DeltaV provides an Enumerations file, SPIDefinitional.enum.xml, loaded into the SPI database to populate the custom enumerations required to interface with DeltaV. See the SPI help topic Synchronize an Enumerated List. When publishing from DeltaV and before retrieving into SPI it is recommended that the Administrator sets up a Device Type Profile for each combination of Device and Tag Mnemonic that has been used in fieldbus. For example, FE and Flow Transmitter xxxx. Add DeltaV Default Instrument Manufacturer and Model types to the list of SPI Instrument Types. To add manufacturers, select Index > Tables > Instrument Manufacturers , and then add the new manufacturer. To add model types, select Index > Tables > Instrument Models , and then select the default manufacturer and add new model data. To add instrument types, select Index > Tables > Instrument Types , and then select Process Function and add the new instrument type. For more information see the topic DeltaV Default Instrument Manufacturer and Model . Related information SPI: default DeltaV instrument manufacturer and model

title: Start and test the FILL phase
main_heading: Start and test the FILL phase
body_text: Start and test the FILL phase Click Start on the command list to send a Start command to the phase. The inlet valve on the Process graphic changes to open and the tank data link shows the tank filling. The tank will fill to approximately 100 gallons, the amount specified by the batch input parameter FILL_AMOUNT in the FILL phase. Click the FILL_AMOUNT parameter on the Batch picture and change the value to 75 in the Data Entry box.

title: Start the Batch Executive
body_text: Start the Batch Executive Click Start > DeltaV Batch > Application Manager . The DeltaV Batch Application Manager dialog opens. Under the Administer section of the Batch Executive tab, click the Start button. Select Cold on the Choose Boot Method dialog. You are given this choice because we selected User Query as the restart method in the Batch Executive Properties dialog. Wait for a few seconds until the Batch Executive is running and the phase server status is good. Click Verify Phases . The Batch Executive checks that all items specified in the batch configuration (phases, phase parameters, and so on) are available. There should be no Bad Phases. (If there are bad phases, first try clicking Verify Phases again. If there are still errors, go to the DeltaV Batch log file to find the errors. In Windows Explorer, go to DeltaV\DVData\Batch\Logs ). If there are bad phases, you need to correct them in your configuration. Another thing to check (on the unit phase Properties dialog) is that the unit phases all have an assigned phase type of Controller. (Unit phases are the assigned phases in each blender and color unit module in the PAINT_BLEND process cell.) Verify the number of Bad Phases is 0 before proceeding. Click File > Exit . The Batch Executive will continue running in the background. If you need to stop it, open the Application Manager dialog (from the Start > DeltaV Batch menu), and then click Stop .

title: Start the Batch Operator Interface and run the batch
main_heading: Start the Batch Operator Interface and run the batch
body_text: Start the Batch Operator Interface and run the batch Launch the Batch Operator Interface by clicking Start > DeltaV Operator > Batch Operator Interface . If necessary, select the workstation for the desired Batch Executive. The Batch List screen opens. Click the Add Batch button . Select OP_FINISH from the list of available recipes. Only those recipes specifically assigned to a Batch Executive will appear in this list. The Batch Creation dialog opens. The default Batch ID is the date and time. You can leave it as is or edit the ID by typing an appropriate Batch ID (alphanumeric). Since this is a class-based recipe, the Bound Unit has a drop-down list from which you can select the blender you want to use. Select UM_BLEND_500. Click Create to add this batch to the batch list. Select the pending operation you just created, and then click the Start Batch button . Click OK when asked if you want to start the batch. Verify from the Batch List that the batch state indicates RUNNING. Click the Procedure as PFC button on the toolbar to see how the batch is progressing. Click the Phase Control button to see the information on this view. On the Phase Control screen, click Display Process Cells, then click Display Units, and then click the UM_BLEND_500 unit to view the details on this screen. Return to the Batch List display by clicking the first button on the toolbar and confirm that the operation goes to Complete. Tip: If you encounter a failure, make sure that none of the failure conditions have been tripped. Fix the condition that caused the failure, clear the failure, and restart the batch.

title: Start the Continuous Historian Data Conversion utility
main_heading:
Start the Continuous Historian Data Conversion
    utility
body_text: Start the Continuous Historian Data Conversion utility Before you start the Continuous Historian Data Conversion utility, the Legacy Historian must be installed on the system and its services must be running. In addition, the offline Legacy Historian archive data that you wish to convert must be loaded into the online Legacy Historian system before data conversion can be done. To start the conversion utility, navigate to the Program Files\HistorianDataConversion folder and double-click HistorianDataConversion.exe.

title: Start the OPC .NET Services
body_text: Start the OPC .NET Services The OPC .NET services are named OPC .NET Server and OPC .NET Discovery in the Services dialog. Make sure the DeltaV service is running Open the Windows Component Services application. Right-click DeltaV OPC .NET Server , and then click Start . Wait until the service has started. Right-click DeltaV OPC .NET Discovery , and then click Start . Wait until the service has started. Note: You must shut down the OPC .NET services prior to shutting down the DeltaV service. Related information OPC .NET technical overview

title: Steps to recipe building
body_text: Steps to recipe building Building a recipe is a straightforward process and requires the following steps: Open Recipe Studio. A new PFC is automatically opened. If Recipe Studio is already running, click the Main button, click New , and then select the type of recipe (operation, unit procedure, or procedure). Define the steps. Assign the individual units, unit classes or unit aliases (if in procedure level recipe) to the step you are creating. Add transitions to move the recipe from one step to another. Write specific expression logic or use the default transition feature. Set the values for the step parameters. If the step is a phase, the parameters are inherited from the phase class. You can leave the default value, change the default value, set the Origin to Operator (default applies also), set the Origin to Defer and the Source as one of the recipe parameters, or set the Destination to Refer (for report parameters) and set the Target to one of the recipe parameters. Create recipe parameters. You can define type, low and high limits, default value, engineering units, scalability, and category for each parameter. Note: When deferring or referring a step parameter value, the recipe parameter is created when you set the Origin and Destination on the step parameter. The category and type of the recipe parameter must match the category and type of the step parameter in order to defer/refer the value. If this is a recipe that you will use as a top-level recipe, define any recipe formulas needed. These formulas override default values of the recipe parameters. If this is not a top-level recipe, the recipe parameters at this level can be considered step parameters at the next level up. You can then create recipe parameters and recipe formulas at that next level. Complete the recipe properties. This step is required to verify the recipe. The following fields must be completed: Version Author Equipment If this recipe is the top-level recipe and needs to be available to the operator to run, assign the recipe to a Batch Executive. Do not assign lower level recipes. Save the recipe. Each recipe must have a name. This allows you to reference the recipe easily in higher levels and allows the operator to easily select the recipe to run. Verify the recipe. Verifying the recipe ensures the recipe is defined correctly. If it is not, Recipe Studio identifies the problems so you can correct them.

title: Setup equipment for dynamic unit allocation
main_heading: Setup equipment for dynamic unit allocation
body_text: Setup equipment for dynamic unit allocation This is a relative order of how to configure your equipment. That is, equipment train classes can be created before unit classes, however you will have to go back to the equipment train class once the unit classes exist to associate the unit aliases with a unit class. Create the process cell class. Class-based process cells are required for the Batch Executive. Create the process cell and areas under the process cell. Define the unit classes (assigning phase classes as appropriate). Create unit modules (the instances of unit classes) in the appropriate process cells. Define the downstream units for each unit module. Create unit selection policies. Create equipment train classes. Define unit aliases in each equipment train class. Note: If switching from not using an equipment train to using an equipment train, the unit aliases defined in the equipment train must be typed exactly as they are used in the recipe. Associate each unit alias with a unit class. Select the downstream unit aliases for each unit alias in an equipment train class (optional, downstream unit aliases are not required.) The use of a unit selection policy for determining the resolution of the unit alias to a unit is optional; however, when using a unit selection policy, you must specify the policy (regardless of the initial selection mode). If using a unit selection policy, set the initial selection mode. Create individual equipment trains (instances of equipment train classes) under Control Strategies. Set the appropriate unit selection options (use all units or use selected units) for each unit alias in each equipment train. Order the selected units. The order is used when determining the First Available priority choice. In the Procedure Recipe Properties dialog, on the Unit Alias tab, select the Use Equipment Train option. Note: The unit alias names used here and the unit aliases in your recipe must be the same. Select the equipment train class on which this procedure will run. Choose whether the procedure can run on all trains in the class, or only on specific trains. If running on specific trains, select those trains. Verify that the unit classes in this train are appropriate for this recipe. Associate unit aliases with the unit procedures (steps) in the procedure. It is recommended that each unit alias within the train be assigned to at least one step in the recipe. Assign all areas and recipes to the appropriate Batch Executive. Download the Batch Executive. Subtopics: Configuring downstream units Configuring downstream unit aliases in the equipment train class Important equipment configuration notes for dynamic unit allocation

title: Stop alarm and event logging for unused Profibus DP devices
main_heading: Stop alarm and event logging for unused Profibus DP devices
body_text: Stop alarm and event logging for unused Profibus DP devices Alarms and events for unused Profibus DP devices that are left on the segment but scheduled to be powered-down are continuously logged in the DeltaV Historian. Follow these steps to prevent logging of alarms and events for unused Profibus DP devices. Disconnect both the green and red communication cables from the unused Profibus DP device. Note that logging continues if even one of the communication cables is connected. Verify that no alarms or events are being logged in the Historian. If alarms and events are still being logged, double-check that both communication cables have been disconnected from the Profibus DP device. Power down the devices that are to be removed from the Profibus DP segment.

title: Stop workbook updates
body_text: Stop workbook updates Select the File tab. Select Options and then click Formulas . In the Calculation options section, under Workbook Calculation , select Manual . Make sure the Recalculate workbook before saving option is not selected. Click OK . Note: This procedure does not disconnect the data server; rather, it simply prevents the read functions from reading at the update interval you established with DVUpdateInterval. Tip: This procedure stops updates for existing cells. If you create a new read function in manual mode, it will read process data once when you click Finish . The existing cells will not be updated. To retrieve data while in manual calculation mode, press F9 . Related information Resume workbook updates

title: Swap CHARM configurations
body_text: Swap CHARM configurations Suppose that your design changed, and as a result either the wiring to a CHARM or a CHARM's configuration must change. The Swap CHARMs Configuration command provides a fast and easy way to respond to late design changes or mistakes in configuration or installation by swapping configuration between two CHARMs. In the DeltaV Explorer, select the CHARMs container under the CIOC. The CIOC's CHARMs are listed in the right pane. Select the two CHARMs to swap and click Swap CHARMs Configuration from the context menu. Download the changes

title: Switch between configure and run modes
main_heading: Switch between configure and run modes
body_text: Switch between configure and run modes Click Workspace > Switch to Run or press CTRL+W . To return to configure mode, right-click anywhere in the workspace and select Quick Edit . (Alternatively, you can press CTRL+W .)

title: Synchronize time stamps after changing the time zone
main_heading:
Synchronize time stamps after changing the time
    zone
body_text: Synchronize time stamps after changing the time zone After you change the time zone you must stop and restart the DeltaV Database Server to ensure that time stamps in the system are correct. From any workstation: Close any DeltaV applications Select Start > DeltaV Engineering > Database Administrator . The DeltaV Database Administrator dialog opens. Select File > Shutdown Server to stop the Database Server. Click OK on the Shutdown Server dialog that appears. Wait until the text in the status line of the Database Administrator dialog is Database Server is shutdown , then select File > Connect to Server to restart the Database Server. If time stamps are not correct after completing these steps it may be necessary to restart the workstation.

title: Synchronize time with an external network
main_heading: Synchronize time with an external network
body_text: Synchronize time with an external network This section explains how to synchronize the time on your DeltaV System with an external network--a plant-wide network for example. Requirements: The workstation that is to synchronize with the time server must have network access to that server. For example, if the time server is only accessible via the plant LAN, the workstation must have a plant LAN connection. The time source must adhere to Network Time Protocol (NTP). To set up the network, follow these steps: From DeltaV Explorer, select Remote Network under the ProfessionalPLUS workstation or Application Station. From the context menu, select Properties . The Remote Network Properties dialog appears. Note: It is not necessary to select Enable Remote Network for time synchronization to work. Select the Advanced tab on the Remote Network Properties dialog. Enter the IP address of the plant-wide master into the Master Time Server field. If your network has a backup time server, enter its IP address in the Backup Time Server field. Open the properties dialog for the Physical network. On the System Time tab Master Time Server field, browse to the DeltaV node configured to communicate with the plant-wide Master Time Server. This is the ProfessionalPLUS or Application workstation whose Remote Network you selected in step 1. If you are using a backup time server, browse to it in the Backup Time Server field. Download the changed setup data on the ProfessionalPLUS workstation.

title: Connect power to SZ Controllers
body_text: Connect power to SZ Controllers Redundant 24 VDC power is delivered from bulk power supplies to SZ Controllers through the SZ Controller Carrier. It is recommended that the bulk power supply is connected to a surge suppression/filter device. For this procedure, it is assumed that redundant bulk 24 VDC power supplies and surge suppression/filter devices are already installed. Powering the SZ Controller Carrier Connect the AC power that is feeding the bulk power supplies to surge suppression/filter devices. Connect the bulk power supply to the power terminals on the SZ Controller Carrier. Ground the power supplies as shown in the image.

title: Temporarily block new connections
body_text: Temporarily block new connections Sometimes it is necessary for the administrator to prevent remote users from initiating a session. This may be the case when system maintenance is being performed and it is necessary to keep all non-critical usage to a minimum. To temporarily block new connections, complete the following steps: From the Windows taskbar, select Start > Control Panel > System . On the System Properties dialog, click the Remote tab. Clear the Enable Remote Desktop on this computer check box. Click OK .

title: Test a soft phase
body_text: Test a soft phase After writing the soft phase, you can test it using the Soft Phase Tester application. Start the Soft Phase Tester and select File > New . Enter the name of the soft phase (without the .exe extension) that you are testing. If you already have the configuration saved for this phase, select File > Open and select the Soft Phase Tester (.SPT) file. Under the Commands section, click the Start button to begin the phase. All phases start with a 1000 request. Click the Ack Request button to acknowledge that request and any time you are prompted with a request. Respond to operator prompts by entering the value in the Prompt Info fields and clicking Ack Request . The Messages field lists the text of the message or any debug message that you have programmed into the soft phase. The batch commands (stop, abort, hold, clear failure, and restart) are issued through the Soft Phase Tester by clicking the appropriate button. Test the Watchdog by clicking the Disconnect button. This simulates a communications failure between the Soft Phase Server and the Batch Executive. Change the parameter values (once the parameters are configured) by selecting the parameter, entering the new value, and clicking the Ack Request button. Use the Prev and Next buttons to flip through the pages of parameters (if your list exceeds 10 parameters). Note: The Reset button removes the soft phase from the computer's memory and should be used before exiting the Soft Phase Tester or starting the soft phase again. Tips Keep a list of Phase Request Codes to refer to. The Phase Request Codes are found in the DeltaV Batch Book Online. Write debug messages in your soft phase, especially for the operator prompts. These debug messages display in the messages display. Your operator messages are not available to you in the Soft Phase Tester because the Batch Executive is not being used. Periodically clear the messages display by clicking the Clear button.

title: Test the AGITATE running logic
body_text: Test the AGITATE running logic Verify the running logic by modifying the AGITATE_TIME parameter and then manually running the AGITATE phase for UM_BLEND_500. Open the Batch display in DeltaV Operate. Click UM_BLEND_500 to open the unit module faceplate. Load the AGITATE phase. Click the AGITATE_TIME parameter data link and enter a value of 20. Open the faceplate for the AGITATE phase and the command list. Send a Start command. Go to the Process display. When the phase goes to complete, send a Reset command to return the phase to the Idle state. Unload the phase. Note: After testing, the phase must be reset to the Idle state before it can be unloaded. It must then be unloaded so that it will be available later for Batch Executive control.

title: Test communications between the internal and external network
main_heading: Test communications between the internal and external network
body_text: Test communications between the internal and external network Pinging is used to verify communications prior to creating rules in order to simplify troubleshooting. In the firewall's web UI navigate to Dashboard > Summary and click the Allow all button to open the firewall so you can easily ping between computers or devices. On each DeltaV workstation, open the command prompt and type ping -4 -t xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx (the external workstation's IP address) to create a persistent ping to each external workstation that will be communicating with a DeltaV workstation. Troubleshoot any non-working pings by checking that the routing is correct, the DeltaV workstation's NIC configuration is correct, and the IP address is correct. Verify that all computers and devices are communicating before setting up the protection rules for each application. Related information Setting up communication rules

title: Test OPC UA client-side communications
body_text: Test OPC UA client-side communications From the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy, select the OPC UA Client . Right-click Diagnose . The software launches DeltaV Diagnostics. From the DeltaV Diagnostics hierarchy, select the physical device (PDT) of the OPC UA Client. Right-click Test Endpoint Connection . If successful, the software displays a message indicating that the OPC UA server connection is established. Related information Troubleshooting communications between OPC UA clients and servers

title: Test recipe formulas
body_text: Test recipe formulas Now that you have created three recipe formulas, you can go to Batch Operator Interface to see how they can be used in a batch. Open the Batch Operator Interface. (Remember to start the Batch Executive first if it isn't already running in the background.) Click the Add Batch button, and then select PRC_PAINT from the list of recipes that have been assigned to a Batch Executive. In the Unit Binding section, select UM_BLEND_500 for UP_BLEND and UM_COLOR_100 for UP_COLOR. In the Batch Creation dialog, click Load Formula , and then select the LIGHT formula. The formula values for the LIGHT formula are listed. You can accept the values you originally entered for this formula, or you can modify any value by double-clicking and editing it. If you modify values, notice that the formula name changes from LIGHT to CUSTOM FORMULA. Click Create to add the batch to the batch list. Select the batch on the batch list and click the Start Batch button. When the batch has completed, close the Batch Operator Interface.

title: Test the revised DRAIN phase
body_text: Test the revised DRAIN phase Open the DeltaV Explorer and navigate to the Assigned Recipes object under the Batch Executive. Make sure that OP_FINISH has been assigned to this Batch Executive so we can select it from the available list of recipes in the Batch Operator Interface. Stop the Batch Executive (if running). Download the controller or workstation. This will download all changes to the phases. Start the Batch Executive and verify phases. Open DeltaV Operate to the Process picture. If there is not any level in the blender, you may need to run the CHG_BASE phase. Make sure all the valves are closed. Open the Batch Operator Interface. Click Add Batch , and then select OP_FINISH from the list of recipes assigned to the Batch Executive. Bind to the Blender UM_BLEND_500. Select the batch, and then click the Start button. When the DRAIN phase starts, the Unacknowledged Operator Prompts button in the button bar starts to flash. Click the Unacknowledged Operator Prompts button. A new screen opens with a list of unacknowledged operator messages (which should only contain one message). Double-click the message line to open a dialog to enter a response to the Send this batch to Product (YES) or Waste (NO)? message. Select Yes . After another prompt appears to ask the number of gallons to drain, type the number of gallons you want to drain. Make sure that this number is less than or equal to the level in the blender. At this point, you may want to go to the Process picture to watch the draining of the blender. If the blender is not empty, you can run OP_FINISH again and send the rest of the batch to waste to verify that portion of your logic.

title: Troubleshoot decommissioned CHARM I/O Cards
body_text: Troubleshoot decommissioned CHARM I/O Cards If the CHARM I/O Card (CIOC) assembly (CIOCs, CIOC carrier and I/O Ports) was previously installed and commissioned, it could have been removed without being properly decommissioned. As long as the CIOCs are still in the same slots with the same I/O Ports, they retain their IP address even if power is removed from the carrier and can interfere with communications to an existing node with the same IP address. If you suspect that the CIOCs were not properly decommissioned, the CIOCs must be reset before the assembly is installed and commissioned to another system. Follow these steps to troubleshoot the status of the CIOCs. If the CIOCs are commissioned, reset the CIOCs. Confirm that the CIOCs are correctly installed in the carrier. Check the LEDs on the CIOCs to determine if the CIOCs are decommissioned ( Power LED is constant green, Error LED is flashing red, and the Primary and Secondary ACN LEDs are flashing yellow). Check the LEDs for other conditions: If no LEDs are lit, confirm that the CIOC carrier has been supplied with 24 VDC power. If the network LEDs are not flashing, confirm that the I/O Ports are correctly installed. If the LEDs on the I/O Ports are not flashing, they are not communicating on the network. Ensure that the network cable is properly connected at the I/O Port and the switch. If the LEDs indicate that the CIOC is commissioned but the CIOCs have not been commissioned on this system, the CIOC is still in a previous commissioned state and must be reset. Related information CHARM I/O Card LEDs Reset CHARM I/O Cards

title: Troubleshoot decommissioned Wireless I/O Cards
body_text: Troubleshoot decommissioned Wireless I/O Cards If the Wireless I/O Card (WIOC) assembly (WIOCs, WIOC carrier and I/O Ports) was previously installed and commissioned, it could have been removed without being properly decommissioned. As long as the WIOCs are still in the same slots with the same I/O Ports, they retain their IP address even if power is removed from the carrier and can interfere with communications to an existing node with the same IP address. If you suspect that the WIOCs were not properly decommissioned, the WIOCs must be reset before the assembly is installed and commissioned to another system. Follow these steps to troubleshoot the status of the WIOCs. If the WIOCs are commissioned, reset the WIOCs. Confirm that the WIOCs are correctly installed in the carrier. Check the LEDs on the WIOCs to determine if the WIOCs are decommissioned ( Power LED is constant green, Error LED is flashing red, and the Primary and Secondary ACN LEDs are flashing yellow). Check the LEDs for other conditions: If no LEDs are lit, confirm that the WIOC carrier has been supplied with 24 VDC power. If the network LEDs are not flashing, confirm that the I/O Ports are correctly installed. If the LEDs on the I/O Ports are not flashing, they are not communicating on the network. Ensure that the network cable is properly connected at the I/O Port and the switch. If the LEDs indicate that the WIOC is commissioned but the WIOCs have not been commissioned on this system, the WIOC is still in a previous commissioned state and must be reset.

title: Troubleshoot a communication rule
body_text: Troubleshoot a communication rule In the firewall's web UI navigate to the Protection tab and based on the type of rule you are creating select either Inbound connections or Outbound connections . Click the Add connection button. Select Custom from the Application drop-down list. Select the DeltaV workstation and the external workstation that will be communicating. Select TCP from the Protocol drop-down list. Enter 1-65534 in the Ports area to allow communications on all ports. Check Enabled to enable logging and click Apply . Repeat the above steps and create another rule using UPD as the protocol. On the Protection tab, Inbound connections and Outbound connections pages, disable logging on any other rules between the DeltaV workstation and the external workstation for which you created the custom rules and click Apply . This causes the log to contain only data from the custom rules making it much easier for you to analyze the data. Exercise a test application on the DeltaV workstation and external computer. Use the application's full functionality including the functions that may not be working correctly. Run the application long enough to create log entries. Open the log on the syslog server and search for all of the log entries matching the IP addresses of the computers using the application you are troubleshooting. Compare the ports and protocols in the log with the ports and protocols in the rules you originally created for the application. You can use the Configuration audit page on the Administration tab or the Applications page on the Configuration tab to view the ports and protocol information. Follow these steps if a port or protocol used by the application is not configured in the original rule: Navigate to Protection Inbound or Outbound connection and disable the test custom rules you created. Navigate to Dashboard > Summary and disconnect any communications that were created by the custom rule. Create a new rule with the custom application using the missing ports and protocols and test the application to see if it resolves the issue. You may have to create both TCP and UDP rules. If creating a rule with the missing port and protocols resolves the issue, create a new application in the firewall's application list using the revised ports and protocols to allow the application to work. Do not revise the original application as you might need this for future rules. Consider using the word custom in the new application's name (for example OPC:Custom- OPC.NET Client Read/Write for xxxxxxx) Use the new application to revise the original rule you created for this application. Delete and disconnect any custom rules that you created. Related information Deleting rules and disconnecting communications

title: Trust, untrust or remove an OPC UA certificate
main_heading: Trust, untrust or remove an OPC UA certificate
body_text: Trust, untrust or remove an OPC UA certificate Select the OPC UA client or server from the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click the Issuers or Clients and Issuers tab. Select the certificate. Click Trust , Untrust or Remove .

title: Uninstall the Batch Historian software
body_text: Uninstall the Batch Historian software The Batch Historian Server is uninstalled separately from the standard DeltaV software. Go to Control Panel > Add or Remove Programs . Select the Batch Historian from the list of programs to uninstall. Select Remove . You are presented with two options: Uninstall Batch Historian Server only . This option only removes the executable files, leaving Microsoft SQL and the historical database intact for future use. This option should be used when upgrading from one version of the DeltaV software to the another. Complete Un-installation of Batch Historian Databases . This will result in the loss of all historical data and should only be used when the data is no longer needed. Note: When reinstalling the Batch Historian, it is possible that you will not receive any campaign data. This is due to the campaign journal file (dvbcmjrnl.seq) located in DeltaV\DVData directory becoming out of step with the Batch Historian Database. Rename the dvbcmjrnl.seq file and allow it to be recreated. All the campaign data will now be collected successfully.

title: Uninstall the Soft Phase environment
body_text: Uninstall the Soft Phase environment Follow these steps to uninstall Soft Phase Environment. Go to Programs and Features. Select Soft Phase Environment from the list. Click Change/Remove . Follow any dialogs that are displayed. Note: With the Soft Phase Environment uninstalled, DeltaV Soft Phases will not run on this workstation.

title: Uninstall the Advanced Continuous Historian
body_text: Uninstall the Advanced Continuous Historian Completely uninstalling the Advanced Continuous Historian requires that you also uninstall DeltaV from the Application Station. You can then reinstall DeltaV, at which time you can elect to: Reinstall the Advanced Continuous Historian Install a different historian by enabling the DeltaV Continuous Historian , Advanced Continuous Historian , or Enterprise Historian option in the Select Historian dialog while reinstalling DeltaV. To uninstall the Advanced Continuous Historian, complete the following steps: Back up the Advanced Continuous Historian database. Navigate to Control Panel > Programs and Features . On the Uninstall or change a program page, select and uninstall all OSIsoft PI Server software. Delete any of the following folders that exist on the C: or D: drive: D:\PI C:\Progam Files\PI C:\Progam Files\PIPC C:\Progam Files (x86)\PIPC C:\ProgamData\OSIsoft C:\Progam Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL12.ADV_CONT_HIST D:\MSSQL2K\MSSQL12.ADV_CONT_HIST Note: Deleting the MSSQL12.ADV_CONT_HIST folder uninstalls the ADV_CONT_HIST SQL Server Instance associated with the Advanced Continuous Historian. Navigate to Control Panel > Programs and Features . On the Uninstall or change a program page, select and uninstall DeltaV. Related information Historian installation Uninstall a historian

title: Uninstall the DeltaV Excel Add-in
body_text: Uninstall the DeltaV Excel Add-in The DeltaV software and the DeltaV Excel Add-in versions must match. Therefore, you must uninstall the DeltaV Excel Add-in whenever you uninstall or upgrade DeltaV. You can then reinstall the DeltaV Excel Add-in after you reinstall or upgrade DeltaV. Tip: Uninstall the DeltaV Excel Add-in before uninstalling or upgrading DeltaV and deleting DeltaV folders. Open Control Panel , and then select Programs and Features . From the list of installed programs, select ExcelAddInRuntime . Click Uninstall . Related information Install the DeltaV Excel Add-in

title: Uninstall the SOA server from a non-DeltaV computer
main_heading: Uninstall the SOA server from a non-DeltaV computer
body_text: Uninstall the SOA server from a non-DeltaV computer To uninstall the SOA server from a non-DeltaV computer, follow these steps. Note: You do not need to use this procedure on a DeltaV computer. The DeltaV uninstall will remove the Secure SOA server from the DeltaV computer. Navigate to Programs and Features. Select Secure SOA Server from the list. Click Change/Remove . Follow any dialogs that are displayed. The DeltaV system and the web services (Campaign Manager Web Service, Recipe Exchange Web Service, and Monitor Service) will not be able to communicate through this server when the SOA server software is uninstalled.

title: Unlock the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver for a specified time
main_heading: Unlock the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver for a specified time
body_text: Unlock the CHARMs Smart Logic Solver for a specified time Note: This functionality is only supported by the Major Revision 2 (or higher) CSLS. The Lock and Unlock functions launch the Secure Write Mechanism. This mechanism verifies the operator has the correct security key (SIS Can Download) and guarantees that the value sent cannot be corrupted in the process of sending it to the logic solver. The Lock and Unlock functions launch the Secure Write Mechanism. This mechanism verifies that the operator has the correct security key (SIS Can Download) and guarantees that the value sent cannot be corrupted in the process of sending it to the logic solver. The Logic Solver must be unlocked to commission, decommission, download, debug SIS modules or allow HART write commands. Locking also prevents a user-initiated logic solver switchover. The Unlock function can be inhibited with a physical key switch on the CSLS or the SIS Controller. If Enable Key-lock has been selected on the properties dialog for this CSLS, the physical inhibit key on the CSLS must be in the unlocked position to proceed. If the SIS Controller associated with this CSLS supports key switch functionality, the physical key on the SIS Controller must be in the unlocked position to proceed. From DeltaV Explorer or Diagnostics, navigate to the logic solver under the Local Safety Network under a SIS Controller. Right-click and select Unlock Timed . The software displays the Unlock Timed dialog. Enter the duration of the unlocked state. After this time expires. the CSLS returns to the locked state. Locking or unlocking a logic solver generates an event in the event log. Related information Logic Solver Lock and Unlock functions

title: Update all read functions in a workbook
main_heading: Update all read functions in a workbook
body_text: Update all read functions in a workbook To update all read functions in a workbook by recalculating all formulas that have changed since the last calculation (including all formulas dependent on them), press F9 . Related information Resume workbook updates Set the update interval Stop workbook updates

title: Upgrade redundant CIOCs
body_text: Upgrade redundant CIOCs Using the DeltaV Controller and I/O Upgrade Utility, upgrade the standby CIOC. Once the upgrade is complete, use DeltaV Diagnostics to monitor the standby CIOC OINTEG until it becomes GOOD (this can be 3 minutes on a fully loaded CIOC). Select the other CIOC in the redundant pair and start the upgrade.

title: Upload DeviceNet device parameters
body_text: Upload DeviceNet device parameters Uploading parameters reads all configurable parameters from the device and stores the values in the database. Right-click the device and select Upload Parameters .

title: Use the CHARMs Simulate application
body_text: Use the CHARMs Simulate application Once a CIOC is in simulate mode, you can use the CHARMs Simulate application. Select Charms Simulate from the Start menu's DeltaV Engineering folder ( Start > All Programs > DeltaV > Engineering > Charms Simulate ). The CHARMS Simulate application opens. The left pane of the CHARMS Simulate dialog lists the CIOCs in simulate mode. Select a CIOC in the left pane to list its CHARMs in the right pane. Double-click a CHARM to open the Update CHARM dialog. Use this dialog to modify the simulated CHARM's pattern, status, and value. Pattern - Use this option to turn a waveform pattern (for example, Sawtooth or Square) On or Off for the selected CHARM. The pattern is based on the CHARM's signal type. Note that Pattern must be Off to write a value. When the Pattern is turned on, the CHARM's value increments by 1. Status - Use this option to change the selected CHARM's status. The numbers in parenthesis represent the status values. Possible values for CHARM Status are: Good (128) Uncertain (64) Unknown (20) Bad (0) Value - Use this option to write a simulated value to the selected CHARM. Pattern must be Off to write a value. Note: Simulated writes to Value and Pattern are not supported for output CHARMs (AO and DO). Simulated writes to Status are supported for output CHARMs. Related information Function block status information

title: Use exception reporting in the application
main_heading: Use exception reporting in the application
body_text: Use exception reporting in the application Now that the support is in place for exception reporting you can add the code to create a group, request exception reporting and display the results to the user. In the Barcode module, add the global variables for keeping track of the step of the MIXTANKS SFC. 'OPC Exception Reporting Global gStepHandle As Long Global gStepItemHandle As Long Global gStep As String In the sub Main of the Barcode module, add the following code before the frmMain.Show command: 'Add group for receiving notices from the DeltaV System gStepHandle = gOpcServer.AddGroup("Notify", 1000) If gStepHandle <= 0 Then MsgBox "Unable to add group Notify" Exit Sub End If 'Add items to track in Notify Group - save handles for callbacks gStepItemHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("Notify", "OPCSAMPLE/STEP_COUNT.CV", VT_BSTR) gOpcServer.Subscribe ("Notify") In the declarations section of the Barcode module, add a global variable for flagging the time to add dry ingredients: Global Const DRYADD_STEP = "DRY_ADD" Global gDryAddTime As Date In the Timer1_Timer function of the form frmMain, add the following: If gDryAddTime <> 0 Then Beep MsgBox "Add " & txtTargetIngAmt & "kgs of " _ & txtTargetIngName & " to product and Scan in the bar code" gDryAddTime = 0 End If Related information Write back to the DeltaV system

title: Install intrinsically safe cards in a DeltaV SIS system
main_heading: Install intrinsically safe cards in a DeltaV SIS system
body_text: Install intrinsically safe cards in a DeltaV SIS system DeltaV I.S. cards used with DeltaV SIS hardware Install a right one-wide carrier onto the 8-wide carrier installed with DeltaV SIS components by sliding together the 48 pin connectors on the carriers. Install a left one-wide carrier onto the 8-wide carrier to be installed with DeltaV I.S. cards by sliding together the 48 pin connectors on the carriers. Terminate the right one-wide carrier. Connect the 44 pin D-shell (male) connector on the one-wide carrier extender cable to the top D-shell (female) connector on the terminated, right one-wide carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Connect the 44 pin D-shell connector on the other end of the cable to the top D-shell connector on the left one-wide carrier and fasten the retainer screws. Install a LocalBus Isolator and I.S. Power Supply on the 8-wide carrier holding the DeltaV I.S. cards to separate standard DeltaV cards from DeltaV I.S. cards. Refer to the DeltaV TM M-series Hardware Installation and Reference manual for information on installing DeltaV I.S. components. Related information Terminate the local peer bus

title: Use reserved pictures
body_text: Use reserved pictures For quick picture call up, it is recommended that you use Reserved Pictures. You can reserve up to three pictures. The picture data is fresh and always available to the operator. To reserve pictures: Open DeltaV Operate in Configure Mode. In the Pictures/Standard folder, open User_Ref.grf and follow the directions to save the picture as UserSettings.grf. Right-click in UserSettings.grf, select Edit Script , go to the section called "Reserved Picture Initialization," and then follow the directions to reserve your pictures. Important: Every picture listed in the Reserved Pictures list is open (but not visible) in DeltaV Operate run mode. The picture is resident on the machine and the datalinks are actively being updated, allowing for faster access to data when the operator opens one of these pictures. It is important to understand that the pictures on the Reserved Pictures list place a burden on the system's resources by keeping those datalinks updated. Therefore, testing is required to validate that the system is behaving as expected (for example, datalinks are updated at the configured scan rate, FreMem is at an acceptable level, and so on).

title: Use the new class
body_text: Use the new class The next step is to use the OPCServer class by declaring a variable of the class and calling its methods. In this application, you will define a global variable, OPCServer of the type OPCServer. You need two groups for this application. The first one holds items for the target ingredient and target amount that need to be added to this recipe. It also holds the actual ingredient and amount and a Done flag to send back to the DeltaV system. The second group contains the step of the MIXTANKS SFC (Sequential Function Chart). The step will pause at "DRY_ADD" waiting for the user to manually add the ingredient. This second group needs to request OnDataChange notifications. The OnDataChange procedure in the application can display the current step and react when the step is "DRY_ADD". When an application needs to manipulate a group or item, it makes the request with a handle. This handle is returned from the server when the group or item is first created. In addition to adding global variables for each of the values needed, it is also necessary to have a variable to hold the server handles for those variables. In the code window for the Barcode module (Barcode.bas), set the Object to "General" and the Proc to "Declarations". Add the following declarations, after the Option Explicit: 'Variables for OPC Global gOpcServer As New COPCServer 'OPC Server Handles Global gTargetIngHandle As Long Global gTargetIngStrHandle As Long Global gTargetAmtHandle As Long Global gActualIngHandle As Long Global gActualAmtHandle As Long Global gDoneHandle As Long The Target Ingredient has two handles. The first is for the numeric value of the target ingredient. The second is for the text value of the target ingredient. In the DeltaV system, the ingredient has been defined by a Named Set (also referred to as an enumeration). This is a value from 0 to 255 that displays an assigned text message. This application needs to display both values to the user. To accomplish this, you will add two items with the only difference being the data type requested (string vs. integer). In the Sub Main, add the following code before the line frmMain.show: 'Connect to OPC Server If Not gOpcServer.OpenServer Then MsgBox "Server didn't open" End End If 'Add group for reading and writing to DeltaV System If gOpcServer.AddGroup("IngredientInfo", 1000) <= 0 Then MsgBox "Unable to add group IngredientInfo" End If The group IngredientInfo is added with an update rate of 1000 milliseconds or 1 second. This is the fastest update rate possible with OPC. Since this application requires very few data points, maintaining the best possible rate is not a performance issue. For large amounts of data, it would be important to separate items in groups that require different update rates and therefore reduce loading. In the Sub Main, add the following code before the line frmMain.Show: 'Add items to IngredientsInfo group gTargetIngHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("IngredientInfo", _ "OPCSAMPLE/TARGET_DRYINGR.CV", VT_I4) gTargetIngStrHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("IngredientInfo", _ "OPCSAMPLE/TARGET_DRYINGR.CV", VT_BSTR) gTargetAmtHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("IngredientInfo", _ "OPCSAMPLE/TARGET_DRYAMT.CV", VT_R4) gActualIngHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("IngredientInfo", _ "OPCSAMPLE/ACTUAL_DRYINGR.CVI", VT_UI4) gActualAmtHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("IngredientInfo", _ "OPCSAMPLE/ACTUAL_DRYAMT.CV", VT_R4) gDoneHandle = gOpcServer.AddItem("IngredientInfo", _ "OPCSAMPLE/DRY_ADDS_DONE.CV", VT_BSTR) In the call to AddItem, the ItemID is a string representing the path of the item in the DeltaV system, for example: "OPCSAMPLE/TARGET_DRYINGR.CV". In the sample DeltaV configuration there is a module named OPCSAMPLE. This module has a module level parameter named TARGET_DRYINGR. The ".CV" indicates the field of the parameter. The Current Value (CV) is the default field if none is specified. The defined fields depend on the parameter type. Note: One easy way of determining the path of an existing parameter is to use the Excel add-in in the DeltaV system. The add-in includes a wizard that allows you to browse for the item to the field level. Select the Paste parameter path to left of result check box to see the full parameter path. Related information DeltaV parameter types and field definitions Add reads and writes to the opcServer class

title: Using netstat
body_text: Using netstat When the SOA Gateway is activated by downloading the DeltaV application station, the first service to get activated is the Monitor service. This service supports the Gateway Administration application. The Monitor service default port is 49301. Use the Windows netstat command to determine the port the other services are using and, if needed, find unused ports. netstat -a -b Look for instances that include the word LISTENING. For example, the Recipe Exchange service appears in the command output looking similar to: TCP DVPROPLUS1:49201 DVPROPLUS1.DOMAIN:0 LISTENING 4088 [EmersonProcess.Web.Services.RecipeExchange.RExWindowsServiceHost.exe] Depending on where you are running the netstat command, there may be instances of the service appearing in the output other than the port number (49201) shown above, but they will not include LISTENING so you can ignore them.

title: Verify the AGITATE holding and restarting logic
main_heading: Verify the AGITATE holding and restarting logic
body_text: Verify the AGITATE holding and restarting logic Download UM_BLEND_500. If asked, do not accept the online values for uploading. Click Select None , and then proceed with the download. Go to the Batch picture in DeltaV Operate. Open the UM_BLEND_500 unit module faceplate. Load the AGITATE phase and open the phase faceplate and command list. Go to the Process picture. Send a Start command and wait for AGIT_500 to begin agitating (phase shows Running). Send a Hold command to the AGITATE phase. Verify that the phase goes to the Held state and that AGIT_500 stops. Send a Restart command to the AGITATE phase. Verify that the phase transitions back to the Running state and that AGIT_500 resumes agitating. When the phase completes, reset the phase to Idle and unload it.

title: Verify the AGITATE phase failure conditions
main_heading: Verify the AGITATE phase failure conditions
body_text: Verify the AGITATE phase failure conditions Now we will verify that when a condition is tripped, it is detected by the Fail Monitor. To create a failure condition, we will open the XV_BASE_500 valve while the agitator is running. To do this, we will first put the XV_BASE_500 module in AUTO mode to allow us to open the valve. Open the Batch picture in DeltaV Operate. Open the faceplate for the unit module UM_BLEND_500, load the AGITATE phase, open the AGITATE faceplate, and open the command list. In Control Studio, open the UM_BLEND_500 unit module. On the Home tab, in the Diagram Mode group, click On-line . Drill down into the AGITATE > FAIL_MONITOR block. Enable monitoring for BASE_IN_OPEN by changing its DISABLE parameter to 0. Go to the Process picture in DeltaV Operate. Click the tag XV_BASE_500 to open the faceplate for the module. Change the mode to AUTO. Start the AGITATE phase. After AGITATE has started, open XV_BASE_500 by clicking the word CLOSE next to the XV_BASE_500 valve icon and clicking the OPEN button on the dialog. The AGITATE phase should go through the holding state to the held state. On the faceplate for UM_BLEND_500/P1, click the Details button at the bottom of the faceplate to open the detail display. The Failure State at the bottom of the display should read Inlet Valve Open . Return to Control Studio. The OUT_D parameter on the BASE_IN_OPEN block temporarily changes to 1 and is sent to the BFI block's IN_D1 parameter. This value passes through the BFI to the FAIL_MESSAGE block using the FIRST_OUT parameter. The OUT1 parameter on the FAIL_MESSAGE block changes to 4, which reflects the numeric value associated with the named state Inlet Valve Open in the phase_failures named set. To test another condition, you need to reset XV_BASE_500 to Closed in DeltaV Operate. Clear the failure by clicking Clear Failures at the bottom of the command list. Then, click the STOP and RESET commands. Remember to enable failure monitoring for the condition block you want to test by setting its DISABLE parameter to 0. Note: When you test the condition, AGIT_STOPPED, the phase should fail immediately because the agitator will not be running when the phase starts. When you are finished testing, return the mode for all the modules to CAS, unload the AGITATE phase, and close the faceplates. Note: If you forget to unload a phase, it will remain in external (manual) mode. Later, when you try to run recipes, you will get errors about the phase being under external control.

title: Verify and save the recipe
body_text: Verify and save the recipe To finish the recipe, you should verify and then save it. On the View tab, in the Recipe group, click Verify Recipe . The Verify Recipe dialog appears. Keep the default settings and click Verify . If any errors are found, correct them. Save the recipe.

title: Verify failure monitoring for AGITATE
body_text: Verify failure monitoring for AGITATE Since the AGITATE_TIME parameter is set to only 30 seconds, you may want to increase this a little to allow yourself more time to trip the failure condition before the phase goes to complete. In Control Studio, open the UM_BLEND_500 unit module. On the Home tab, in the Diagram Mode group, click On-line . Drill down into the AGITATE > FAIL_MONITOR block. Open the Batch picture in DeltaV Operate. Load and start the AGITATE phase for the unit module UM_BLEND_500. Trip a failure condition by opening XV_BASE_500 (in the Process picture). (XV_BASE_500 must be in Auto mode.) In Control Studio, verify that the FAIL_INDEX parameter is set and that AGITATE goes to Held. (XV_BASE_500 closes as part of the Hold logic FAIL_SAFE instructions.) Clear the failure by clicking the Clear Failures button on the command list. Send a Restart command. Verify that the AGITATE phase transitions from the Restarting state to the Running state. When the AGITATE phase goes to Complete, send a Reset command. You can verify other failure conditions using the same general procedure. When you are finished, reset the phase to Idle. Unload the AGITATE phase.

title: Verify the module configuration
body_text: Verify the module configuration Click the Main button, point to Module , and then click Properties . The Properties dialog opens. Click the Tools tab. Click the Verify Now button. A message is displayed; it may contain minor warnings due to I/O references. Click OK to close the message box, and then click OK in the Properties dialog. You now have two control modules, one for the motor and one for the block valve.

title: Verify the phase coordination
body_text: Verify the phase coordination Download. Launch DeltaV Operate and open the Batch graphic. Open the faceplate for unit module UM_COLOR_100. Load the FILL phase, open its faceplate, and start the FILL phase. The color tank fills to approximately 100 gallons. When complete, send a Reset command and unload the FILL phase. Load the DUMP phase for UM_COLOR_100 and open its faceplate. Open the command list, and then click Start . The DUMP phase state changes to Running. The REQUEST parameter changes to 5501, indicating it is waiting for the first message. Load and start the CHG_COLOR phase in unit module UM_BLEND_500. The CHG_COLOR state changes to Running and waits with a 40nn (such as 4027) request to acquire the color header resource. Clear the 40nn request in CHG_COLOR by clicking the number and entering 0 in the Data Entry dialog. This gives control of the two valves in the color header to the CHG_COLOR phase.A new request, 5201, appears. This request synchronizes with the 5501 request in the DUMP phase. Clear the 5201 request and the 5501 request. Two new requests, 5202 and 5502, are written to DUMP and CHG_COLOR, respectively. The outlet valve XV_OUT_100 from the color tank opens. Clear 5202 and 5502. Request 5503 is written to the DUMP phase. Inlet valve XV_COLOR_500 opens, and UM_BLEND_500 starts filling. Open the Process graphic so you can see UM_BLEND_500 fill. (The default charge amount, 15 gallons, was specified earlier, in the phase class definition.) When the tank stops filling, return to the Batch graphic. When the tank charge is complete, Request 5203 (to close the inlet valve XV_COLOR_500) is written to the CHG_COLOR phase. Clear 5503. On the faceplate for DUMP, the state goes to Complete, and outlet valve XV_OUT_100 closes. Clear 5203. Valve XV_COLOR_500 closes. Request 42nn is written to the CHG_COLOR phase to request release of the color header. Clear 42nn. On the faceplate for CHG_COLOR, the state goes to Complete. Send a Reset command to CHG_COLOR and unload the phase. Send a Reset command to DUMP and unload the phase. Close any open faceplates and close DeltaV Operate. Tip: If you want to rerun the modules a few times, you need to be able to drain the blender. Since we don't have a drain phase yet, you can click the RESET BLENDERS button on the Process graphic. This resets the blender tank level to 0.

title: Verify the firewall configuration
body_text: Verify the firewall configuration For troubleshooting purposes, Emerson support personnel may ask for the firewall's configuration file. To obtain this file, use the Management station's web browser such as the Internet Explorer to log into the firewall and download the configuration text file DELTAV DEFAULT 1-311. The following instructions explain how to save the configuration text file to a disk on the Management station: Open the Management station's web browser and enter the firewall 's IP address, for example https://10.5.128.xx:443 (where xx is the IP address you assigned using the serial port. The Security Alert dialog opens. Read the information on this dialog and click Yes . The Connect to dialog opens. Enter admin as Username and the default password if these have not changed from the factory settings. Otherwise, enter your Username and Password and click OK . The firewall's Welcome page opens. Find the System folder on the left side of the Welcome page and expand the folder. Select Configuration-Profiles to open the System Configuration Profiles page. In the Name column, find DELTAV DEFAULT x-xxx (where x-xxx is the version number) and click Download . A File Download dialog opens. Read the information on this dialog and click Save . The Save As dialog opens. Chose a file name and location and click Save . This is the file that can be sent to Emerson support for analysis. If the Download complete dialog opens, click Close .

title: Verify the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server
main_heading: Verify the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server
body_text: Verify the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server On the client machine, the DeltaV OPC Data Access Server application, FrsOpcDv, must be set to run on the server machine. This is set up automatically when OPC Remote is installed, and can be verified by completing the following steps: Run the executable file, dcomcnfg.exe. The Component Services window opens. In the left pane, open Component Services . A Computers folder appears. Open the Computers folder. The My Computer icon appears. Open the My Computer icon. Several folders appear. Open the DCOM Config folder. In the list of applications, right-click FrsOpcDv , and then select Properties . Select the Location tab. The Run application on the following computer check box should be selected and the name of the server machine should be listed. Related information Set the location of the DeltaV OPC Data Server

title: Verify the SFC
body_text: Verify the SFC The DeltaV system provides a tool to help you check the completeness (not the logic) of your sequential function charts. It checks the syntax of the step actions and transition conditions and verifies the existence of any modules or parameters referenced in the logic. It also checks to see if all the steps and transitions have been connected in a legal form. On the View tab, in the SFC group, click Check SFC . If the SFC passes the syntax checks, the following message appears: If you get an error message, go back and fix the SFC as needed.

title: View a recipe's authorization signatures
body_text: View a recipe's authorization signatures Select the recipe that you want to authorize, right-click, and then select Version Control > Authorization . The Recipe Authorization dialog displays listing each signature.

title: View controller properties
body_text: View controller properties (These are general instructions and are not part of the tank process tutorial. If you have a controller and I/O connected, they are not likely to match the hardware specifications for the example.) In DeltaV Explorer, select System Configuration > Physical Network > Control Network > controller placeholder . From the context menu, select Properties . The Controller Properties dialog appears. Select an area to associate alarms and events with, and select the check boxes required for your installation. You do not need to set any values in the Model/Software Revision group of the dialog box. Accept the defaults. When you download, the DeltaV system updates the values in this group to reflect the controller model and software revision in your system.

title: View license details
body_text: View license details Select and right-click the node for which you want to see license details. Select Properties from the context menu, and then click the Licensing tab. The Licensing Properties page shows the assigned license features and the number of features (DSTs, items, and devices) configured on the node. Click the Licensing Details button to see details on the license features included on each license. There are two other ways to assign licenses: Open the Licenses folder (under System Configuration > Setup ), drag a license from the list, and drop it onto a node. When you drag a license from the licenses folder onto a node, you must choose the license from the entire license pool. Select and right-click the Licenses folder (under System Configuration > Setup ), and then use the license's context menu to assign the license to a node. When you assign a license using the license's context menu, you are given a list of compatible nodes for the license. Now that you have assigned your licenses, you can download the configuration for your workstations and controllers.

title: View only defined CHARMs
body_text: View only defined CHARMs It is possible to see only those CHARMs that have been defined rather than all 96 CHARMs when you expand the CHARMs container under a CIOC. Right-click the CHARMs container under the CIOC. Select Show Only Defined CHARMs .

title: View OPC UA certificate details
body_text: View OPC UA certificate details Select the OPC UA client or server from the DeltaV Explorer hierarchy. Right-click Properties . Click the Certificate tab. Click Details . The software displays the following information about the certificate: Name Valid dates Issuer name Key size Signature algorithm Thumbprint

title: View the picture in run mode
main_heading: View the picture in run mode
body_text: View the picture in run mode Click Workspace > Switch to Run or press CTRL+W . Click the Open Main Display button and select TANK101. If you have a controller configured, the datalinks appear as numbers. The numbers are not realistic because you do not have any real I/O devices configured. If you have a placeholder for a controller, the numeric datalinks appear either as symbols (such as @ or &) or as specified in the User Preferences dialog. Return to configure mode either by right-clicking anywhere in the background of the picture and then selecting Quick Edit , or by pressing CTRL+W .

title: View SIS module references
body_text: View SIS module references SIS modules can refer to other module's parameters and have parameters that are referenced by other modules. You can display a list of database objects that reference or are referenced by an SIS module. In DeltaV Explorer, navigate to the SIS module under either the Logic Solver or the plant area. Right-click and select References . A References dialog appears, displaying a list of all the database objects that reference the module or that are referenced by the module. Click Close .

title: View the data conversion log
body_text: View the data conversion log You can click View Log to see details of the data conversion process, including any errors that may have been encountered. The LogView dialog includes a Print button so that you can print the log details.

title: Autosense VIMs
body_text: Autosense VIMs From DeltaV Explorer, navigate to the I/O folder under a controller associated with the VIM cards. Right-click and select Auto-sense I/O cards . The VIMs appear as serial cards in the controller card slots you configured in the VIMNet software.

title: Configure VIM serial cards and ports
main_heading: Configure VIM serial cards and ports
body_text: Configure VIM serial cards and ports The following are the instructions for configuring serial cards, ports, devices, and datasets. These instructions are the same for Ethernet/IP, Generic Ethernet/IP, and Modbus TCP. For each VIM module, you must configure four Programmable Serial Cards in DeltaV Explorer. A maximum of two VIM modules can be used with each DeltaV controller. Redundant serial cards must be configured in pairs in slots 57/58, 59/60, 61/62, and 63/64. Simplex cards must be configured in slots 57 through 60 or 61 through 64. You can also create cards by auto-sensing them from DeltaV Explorer. You must configure all four cards even if not all are used. In addition, disable all unused serial card ports. Subtopics: Create a serial card for VIM Configure a port for VIM Create a serial device for VIM Configure a dataset for VIM

title: Install and launch VIMNet software
body_text: Install and launch VIMNet software Install the VIMNet software on a computer connected to the PLC network. To install the VIMNet software: Insert the DeltaV installation disk #1 into a drive on the target computer. Navigate to \DV_Extras\VIMNetExplorer . Double-click the .msi VIMNet installation file. Follow the instructions on the dialogs that appear. If the DeltaV installation disk #1 is not available, you can copy the .msi VIMNet installation file from the \DeltaV\bin\VIMNetExplorer directory on any DeltaV workstation. To launch the VIMNet software select Start > All Programs > Mynah > VIMNet Explorer . If you installed it on a DeltaV Professional or ProfessionalPLUS workstation, you can launch it from DeltaV Explorer from the Applications menu or from the Launch VIMNet Explorer button on the toolbar. Now use the VIMNet software to create and commission VIMs using the VIMNet documentation as a guide. Uninstall VIMNet Explorer software To uninstall the VIMNet Explorer software: Open Control Panel > Programs and Features > Uninstall a program . Select VIMNet Explorer from the list. Right click and select Uninstall . When the uninstall completes, close Control Panel's Programs and Features window.

title: Connect the MTL NI power supplies to the hazardous area
main_heading: Connect the MTL NI power supplies to the hazardous area
body_text: Connect the MTL NI power supplies to the hazardous area Refer to the following image for the location of the hazardous area connectors on the power supply. Connectors on the MTL 9111 and 9112 NI power supplies Connect the NI area fieldbus segment positive (+) wire to pin 7. Connect the NI area fieldbus segment shield (S) wire to pin 8 and to a shield ground connection. Connect the NI area fieldbus segment negative (-) wire to pin 9.

title: Connect the MTL NI power supplies to the safe area
main_heading: Connect the MTL NI power supplies to the safe area
body_text: Connect the MTL NI power supplies to the safe area Refer to the following image for the location of the safe area connectors on the power supplies. Connectors on the MTL 9111 and 9112 NI power supplies Connect the primary power supply positive (+) wire to pin 1. Connect the primary power negative (-) 24 V return to pin 2. Connect a secondary power supply positive (optional) (+) wire to pin 3. If using a primary and secondary 24 VDC power supply, be sure to connect the power supply returns together. Connect the host segment negative (-) to pin 4. Connect the host segment shield to pin 5. Connect the host segment positive (+) .

title: Connect the MTL IS power supplies to the hazardous area
main_heading: Connect the MTL IS power supplies to the hazardous area
body_text: Connect the MTL IS power supplies to the hazardous area Refer to the following image for the location of the hazardous area connectors on the power supply. Connect the IS area fieldbus segment positive (+) wire to pin 7. Connect the IS area fieldbus segment shield (S) wire to pin 8 and to a shield ground connection. Connect the IS area fieldbus segment negative (-) wire to pin 9.

title: Connect the MTL IS power supplies to the safe area
main_heading: Connect the MTL IS power supplies to the safe area
body_text: Connect the MTL IS power supplies to the safe area Refer to the following image for the location of the safe area connectors on the power supplies. Connect the primary power supply positive (+) wire to pin 1. Connect the primary power negative (-) 24 V return to pin 2. Connect a secondary power supply positive (optional) (+) wire to pin 3. If using a primary and secondary 24 VDC power supply, be sure to connect the power supply returns together. Connect the host segment negative (-) to pin 4. Connect the host segment shield to pin 5. Connect the host segment positive (+) to pin 6.

title: Write an AI value to a specific dataset register
main_heading: Write an AI value to a specific dataset register
body_text: Write an AI value to a specific dataset register Create a module containing an Analog Input block. Double-click the IO_IN parameter, and then click Browse to select a specific analog input channel. If desired, scale the analog input value using the XD_SCALE, OUT_SCALE, and L_TYPE parameters. Add an Internal Write parameter to the diagram. The Internal Write parameter is on the Special Items palette. Modify the properties of the Internal Write parameter by selecting a parameter type of External Reference. For the External parameter path field, click Browse . In the Browse dialog, select System Configuration in the Look in field. Select DST Parameters in the Object Type field. Starting at Physical Network, drill down until the dialog contains DSTs. The list includes dataset tags. Double-click the dataset tag that contains the parameter (register) that corresponds to the dataset value to which you want to write. Double-click the parameter. Wire the AI block's Out parameter to the Internal Write parameter.
